As most owners of Android phones, especially the 4G versions, have learned, all of a sudden the battery is drained. I started to look for a backup battery to keep me from ending up with a dead phone just when I needed it. I liked the specs for the New Trent iTorch IMP52D 5200 and also liked how it looked. Amazon's price couldn't be beat so I went for it. So far I am very pleased with my choice, knowing I can go anywhere without worrying about my phone. This backup is a nice size for portability. Only two wishes, 1. I would like to be able to recharge it more quickly, and 2. being able to turn off the LEDs would be nice, they are very bright. Maybe New Trent could just use dimmer bulbs in the future as there is no need for such bright ones. Bought this for the axillary backup power, and I guess I will find a need to use its LED flashlight capability. If I come across a need for the Laser Pointer, I will let you know in a future review. Also as this unit is still new to me, I will write updates as I put it through its paces.
summary: Convenient, eliable backup for my Droid Charge

reviewText: charges quickly, is small and is s very attractive device. does exactly what it's supposed to do.docked a star because the cable it came with was faulty out of the box. used one of my own cables and everything's great.

I really, really like the unit. I have only owned it for a week or so but have had some good usage from it already. I previously owned a Zagg Sparq, and I did not like that it didn't hold a charge well, and the size. Even though the battery was almost twice the size of this one, it didn't seem to charge as well as this.I am a little confused with the flashlight and laser. I would prefer just a battery, and the only reason for me is easy-Sometimes I hold the button down too long and the light comes on. Getting that off and getting back to just the battery is kind of tedious, but I will get used to it.The size of the unit, awesome. I really like how it feels, very well constructed. I also like how easy it works with all of my devices. Flexibility is a real selling point, I love being able to use it on so many devices.

I had the opportunity to take the iTorch with me this past week Camping.  Its a very nice product, easy to hang on too and small enough to fit in a pocket with ease.  The LED flashlight is a handy feature.  It's not overly bright but it worked well in a pinch in a tent.  I managed to get about 2 charges out of the iTorch for my phone.  I used it during some of the charging time so, I might have been able to get more out of it had the phone been off.  This would be quite handy for a photographer who uses their phone as a Geotagging device when taking pictures.  I have been to Maine in Acadia State Park a few times and turned Geotagging on my phone.  It certainly eats through battery.  My only problem with the device is that between charging, turning the LED or Laser on or off.  It can get a little difficult.  It was pretty easy to shut the battery pack off when turning on or off the LED and a few times the LED came on when I just wanted the battery pack on.  It could be because of my lack of time with the device, but a separate button to turn on the LED or Laser would make this a 5 star device.

Picked up this battery charger when Amazon had it on sale for around 30 bucks. Device came attractively packaged and fully charged. The battery life on this is amazing, and the 2A output port charged my phone and my 3DS completly during a recent road trip, and still had enough charge for another round. The input to charge the device is Micro-USB, which is pretty much the standard now a days. It does come with a 3' USB to Mini-USB cable, but it will accept any USB cable (especially those proprietary Apple USB cables) as output. Embedded into the device is a red laser pointer, which can be used to get your cat out of the room, and a flashlight to look for your cat when his scared little butt runs and hides under the sink after a thunderstorm or a vaccuum attack. Simply holding down the button cycles through turning the device on, then the flash light on, then the device off. A quick press ignites the laser pointer.The unit doesn't feel cheap, is moderately weighted according to appearance, and has a really nice smell to it.

The IMP52D (iTorch) is a very sleek cool looking back-up power source for my iPhone. It is about the size of a swooshed Twinkie, perfect to grab and go. I needed to purchase a short USB lightning cable to use it, but it was inexpensive and makes this a great backup power source. I loan it to others in need almost as often as I use it. It is a great design with a great feel. I have a cigarette lighter charger from an old phone that I sometimes use to recharge my iTorch when I am in my car. It charges fast and can boost my phone to 100% even when it is dead, and it still has some juice to spare. I rarely use the flashlight or laser pointer, but they are cool little features that could come in handy. Great price well made, very cool external charger. The only thing that could make it cooler would be some kind of retractable lightning cable for charging an iPhone or Droid. The AmazonBasics 4" cable is the perfect complement, but I wish Trent devices came with short cables for charging.IMP52D is a great back-up power source for my IPhone. I also need the short USB lighting cable but it is no problem. Great design, integrated flashlight and laser pointer big pluses.
summary: Cool looking very functional power source

reviewText: After having received my new charger just in time for a weekend camping trip with the family and lots of charging to be done as my phone is my primary source of taking photos.  So off we went without worry as I had a new charger and while you may think that 5,200 mAh may not be enough for a weekend getaway it was definitely sufficient.I was able to not only charge my phone twice (once for each day camping) but I got to play with another nifty feature that comes with this little charger which is the laser pointer.  It has quite the range on it and relatively no affect on the battery as I played with it for some time.  It really didn't serve me any purpose other than just something to play with but would make great for business persons in need of something to not only charge their mobile device as well as have something for a presentation in their business meetings.  The battery will shut off automatically if you don't plug something into it and once charged and you unplug you device it will also shut down automatically as well.  Also shutting off manually is quite easy compared to some other external batteries and will shut down in a few seconds whereas some take 10 - 15 at least to shut down.With this nice little charger you not only get your typical USB charger cord but you also get an adapter for the Galaxy Tab and beyond that you get a very nice felt carrying bag to make not only keeping everything together but makes carrying everything so much easier.  Like other New Trent products it also comes with easy to read LED indicators showing how much battery is left on the charger in 25% increments.  Altogether I have to say I am very pleased with the iTorch and it served me well as I see it serving me well for much longer.
summary: Great little charger for a weekend getaway!

reviewText: I really loved this when I first got it. It charged well and the battery lasted a long time. When I went to charge it a second time it would not charge. I do not know if mine was just defective or what but I had to return mine.

The physical properties (size, weight, feel) are perfect for the battery capacity, and it seems to hold a charge as expected. Charging over USB (for both of these units) is a really nice feature that many other chargers are missing. I like the fact that there is a laser pointer as well as the LED flashlight.

I'm a heavy power user when it comes to my phones and tablet. Unfortunately, my daughters are taking after me. I have not been disappointed in buying them this great little unit. We often take long car rides and this battery has saved me from quite a few rides where my kids have drained their phones. By way of stress relief alone, it has paid for itself a few times over. Great and reliable battery.

I got this for someone that had needed a mid-day mobile charging solution. However, it is too bulky to fit in the small purse she carries, so, now it sits mostly unused in her car. The price was decent, but it is just a bit too big for ladies' small handbags. Later I purchased a lipstick sized 2600mAh battery that does fit her intended use.EDIT: Now there are Batteries this size with much more capacity thanks to advancements in battery technology.

New Trent IMP52D charger is sleek and well designed. The smaller size makes if convenient to carry in a briefcase, purse or "go bag" for emergencies or daily use. It would be well suited for the business traveler with the onboard laser pointer and the white LED. Don't be fooled by the smaller size. This charger does the job intended. I have owned and used a Mophie in the past and found the New Trent much quicker and longer lasting than the Mophie.In addition to the good looks and size the IMP52D charges quickly with a wall charger and does a great job extending the battery in my iPhone. I am in the first duty cycle and finding the IMP52D adds about 1% charge to my iPhone per minute. As expected the IMP52D takes additional time to charge my iPad, but with the extra amperage draw needed to charge the iPad the extra time is not unreasonable.The iTorch has a great hand feel. Immediately out of the box I noted the different from the other chargers I have used. The smaller design with smaller LEDs makes it not only functional, but aesthetically pleasing to both touch and sight. I look forward to the ability to keep my devices charged and ready by using this well made product.

Great as a backup to carry around. I think it would be better if it was flatter/thinner.LED light may or may not be useful but why not. New Trent offers great deals if you purchase more than one of their products on amazon.

I was mistaken in my previous review, this charger will work with the iPad, but you must not use the standard sync/charge cable from Apple.  You can only use the included cable and adapter.So, while the product works for iPad, it does not use the standard technology, slightly limiting the usefulness of the product overall.

This external battery is perfect! Exactly what I was looking for. I love my IMP1000 (old 2010 model of the newer IMP120D)...but I found myself not bringing it with me as often as I'd like due to it's larger size.I've only had this for a short while, so I'll update my review when I've had more time with it.So far, first impressions are:*PROS*- Small, compact, and lightweight. Perfect for travel and everyday use.- Feels extremely well-made. Durable. I really like the weight. It's nottoo heavy, but you can tell it's great quality.- Lasts a long time. Can easily keep my iPhone 5 juiced up when travelinghome during the week.- Handy laser pointer and flashlight. Though not necessary, it's a niceadd-on.- This is a big one. The charging cable is the SAME cable to charge boththe device itself, as well as charge my other devices. No more AC wall adapter.Can't stress enough how great it is to only carry one cable.- Carry-case included. Awesome!*CONS*- Probably haven't had the iTorch long enough...but so far, no complaints!
summary: Top notch! Compact, well-made, great design.

reviewText: The New Trent iTorch is the smallest and lightest 5200mah external battery pack you will find anywhere.  It feels sturdy and solidly built.  This is a must have for anyone who finds themselves needing to charge their phone all the time.  I hate walking out the door with 40% left of battery life on my iPhone5 and having to not use my phone like I would like to in order to save battery.  Now I can use my phone when and where I want without worrying about the battery dying.The only issue I have is the battery pack might not store as much juice as advertised.  I get about 1 full charge on my iPhone5 - it is advertised to provide 2-3 full charges.  I don't see that happening ever!  But this is still light, compact and easy to carry around all day in your pocket just in case you need some added power to your phone or other device.
summary: Great size and weight - not as powerful as advertised?

reviewText: I purchased this item to use while on travel to Israel for two primary reasons.  First, since I was on a formal tour, we would be out of range of electric outlets from 8-9 hours every day.  With this item, I did not have to worry about my iPhone (used for taking pictures and email) running out of juice.  The second reason was that some electronics can be a bit temperamental when charging them in other countries and can be easily fried/damaged.  With this item (I have 2 of these devices), I would charge this item via the local outlet then use it to charge my other devices.  If this device was fried, it was relatively inexpensive when compared with the cost of an iPhone. Fortunately, this charger worked flawlessly.  In terms of size, while I generally carried it in my backpack, it was small/light enough to carry in the leg pocket of my cargo pants.  Nice!  This product is dual voltage so no transformer is required when traveling to Israel; only adapters. This product recharged within a reasonable amount of time and subsequently charged my electronics (iPhone, Blackberry, iPod Nano) fairly quickly.  The only annoying feature was the method by which the flashlight and laser pointer are turned on/off (X number of clicks to turn on and another X number of clicks to turn off).  But, certainly tolerable and not a deal breaker. Overall, this item is well worth the investment.

Although I did not buy this for myself, I did purchase them as Christmas gifts. Perfect size for people on the go and I thought they were great gifts, everyone can use an extra battery for their phones.

I have nothing but good things to say about this little unit!  It does exactlly what it claims to do.  I have used this product on my iPhone 3GS as well as my boyfriends iPhone 4.  A friend told me about this product after I told her how my iPhone always dies when I am at Disneyland and that I would have to look for an outlet and sit and charge my phone.  I wish is would come in more colors.
summary: Finally a way to make my phone last all day!

reviewText: I picked up the iTorch as a 'just in case' gadget. I am glad I did. The family went camping this weekend and we were out in the middle of no where in a tent. We had cell coverage, but no way to charge iPhones without going back to the car. The IMP52D came worked out perfectly. It was able to recharge an iPhone 4 twice and a Kindle Fire with 1 charge. I cant be totally exact on how long the charges kept because the kids kept plugging their devices into the iTorch, then taking them off 30 minutes later.All in all, buying the iTorch will be the best move you can make if you are looking for a portable external power source for multiple devices!

I love love love this unit, and make sure to bring it with me whenever I know I'm going to be out and about for the day, and my phone is not going to survive.  It's absolutely essential on plane flights, long days at the beach, etc. I cannot recommend this or some other type of external charging highly enough.  It's hard to be without your phone, so having this unit is a no brainer.  You can plug it in and put it in your pocket.  Easy
summary: Great to have battery charging on the go

reviewText: I go on a lot of camping, hiking, and backpacking/trekking trips where no electricity is available. For months, my friend brought his Energizer external battery pack to charge his iPhone, and friends' phones on our return home. The gadget person I am, I set out to purchase my own. However, reviews of the Energizer pack and other brands were not favorable, until I came across New Trent's products.I decided to buy the IMP500 for its great look (love the blue accents and rounded/bezeled edges/corners) and excellent reviews. It claims to charge a smartphone several times before running out of juice, and it was the right size for me to take on a backpacking trip.I took it on my 2-week trip to Peru: a 4-day Inca Trail trek to Machu Picchu, and a 1-week stay at the Peruvian Amazon Forest lodge, Inca Terra, and was never once disappointed. It charged my Samsung Galaxy S II smartphone, and 2 iPod Touch devices.Comes with a cloth pouch to store the battery pack, but there was no way to include the charging cable without scratching the battery pack's glossy interior. Which now brings me to the biggest issue with the product:The charging cable is proprietary. One end is USB, and the other is proprietary. I wish it was micro-USB based on the proprietary end so that in the event I lose the charging cable, I could use my smartphone's cable.Another improvement suggestion would be to allow you to manually turn off the battery pack -- currently, you have to leave it on and let a timeout shut it off. Perhaps New Trent could allow the user to long-hold the power button to manually force shut off?With that said, a 2-device charging version came out weeks after I purchased the product, and seeing how well the IMP500 works, I wish that I would have bought the 2-device version instead. Either way, I'm very happy with this product and would recommend it to anyone. I may purchase the more powerful 11,000mAH sibling in the future (which also allows charging of tablets like the iPad), but have no need for it right now.UPDATE 1/8/2014: After 2 years, the product still works GREAT! It has not yet failed on me and still is one of the few items I take with me wherever I go.
summary: Great quality, reliable performance, great look

reviewText: Been out for a long day and your phone's running low? This thing fits in your pocket. (or purse ladies), and will get you through the night. Actually, I put it in my daughter's purse as she headed off to prom - that was 3 weeks ago, and I haven't seen it since. Proves it was the right purchase as she kept her Samsung Galaxy SIII going strong all night.

I'm a huge fan of external batteries.  The iPhone is a great device, but one of its obvious imperfection is its very subpar battery life.  It's hard to notice day-to-day, but if you have to travel with it (as I often do), that imperfection is jarring.  For iPhone owners who travel, an external battery is almost a must.I bought the New Trent IMP70D (the old one, not the upgraded one) and last year and it's permanently in my luggage for when I travel.  In my review of it, I noted the one drawback was that it was a bit bulky.  While understandable given the juice that it provides, the bulk ensure that I never carried it outside the hotel room.Along comes the IMP52D.  It does not provide as much power as the IM70D.  However, it is significantly smaller and, more importantly, small enough for me to think that I will be able to carry outside the hotel room.  It's actually smaller in many respective than many phones although much thicker.Size aside, this product does exactly what it says it does and does it well.  The battery charges fast and it charges my iPhone 4S and iPad (original) fast.  5 star.

The NewTrent iTorch IMP52D is a must have for tech geeks and casual electronics users alike. I love my Motorola Photon 4G but the thing is a battery sucker, that's where the IMP52D comes in. This little gizmo will charge my phone from dead to full three times on one charge. I also use it to charge my girlfriends Iphone 4, the kid's Ipods and Kindle fire and just about any electronic device you can think of.  I searched on Amazon and found many other external battery charges, most of which seemed to be cheap Chinese products, produced under many different brand names but all bearing the same exact look. I was pleasantly surprised to find this gem from NewTrent.The IMP52D comes in sleek packaging that includes simple to follow instructions, a retractable USB cable and micro and mini USB plugs to connect to various devices, and a velvet type drawstring pouch to hold it all.The product features a USB port which will accept all Apple charging cables and cables for many other devices. Added bonuses on this product are the built in laser pointer and LED flashlight. The product is very sleek in design and feels very solid in your hand. There are also blue LED lights indicating the battery level and status of charge and an easy to use, single button that performs all functions.I originally purchased this product to use during an upcoming Disneyland vacation. We will spend many long days at the park and use our phones to find info about the park and check on wait times for rides. I know this will exhaust the batteries on our phones and I feel confident that the IMP52D will be a life saver on this trip. I will update this review after putting the product through its paces there. But until then, the product has already proven very handy. I work in a field which requires me to work 24 hour shifts, often on the go, and the IMP52D has already rescued my phone from the abyss of dead batteries several times.  The product charges at a fast rate but does so safely without overheating itself or you device.I will be looking forward to purchasing NewTrent products in the future.
summary: Incredible convenience in the palm of your hand!

reviewText: Been using it as a backup battery on the go for Iphone 5 and 4s, works fantastic, really easy to use and lightweight, highly recommended!
summary: Excellent backup Battery for almost any electronics!

reviewText: The primary reason I purchased the New Trent iTorch was for use with my iPhone 5.  Although I have several other devices,  I have not attempted to recharge them with this external battery.  With the iPhone, I've only used it a few times, but based off of my experiences thus far I can say I really like this product!Fully charged, the New Trent iTorch took my iPhone 5 from 17% to 100%.  The second time I used it, the iTorch recharged the iPhone from about 36% to 100%.  The third time, my phone was about 17% and the iTorch charged it to about 46% before the iTorch itself was drained.  Based off of this, it seems that the iTorch may charge my completely empty (0%) iPhone twice.Recharging the iTorch via wall charger (using a separate wall adapter to connect via USB cable) seems to take about 4+ hours, when it was completely drained. This seems to be a bit excessive, but I plan to just recharge the device at night, no big deal.I previously purchased the Mophie Juice Pack Air, which added so much bulk and weight to my phone and was a true pain to get off, which I did not like any of that and consequently returned.  The iTorch is not heavy at all.  One recommendation or nice addition would be if New Trent added a short charging cable to accompany the charger (similar to GO-TRONIX 3 in 1 USB 2.0 Connect to Lightning 8 Pin, Micro USB and apple 30 Pin Connector for iPhone 4 4S Samsung Galaxy Note 2 iPhone 5, iPad 4/Mini ipod touch 5G Nano 7th).  This may drive the cost up a tad, but it covers most any device type and would be beneficial as to not need to walk around with a cord that is longer than necessary when trying to travel / be mobile. Amazon does sell shorter cables for only lightningAmazonBasics USB A to Lightning Compatible Cable (4 inch/10 CM)or mini usb as well. I would recommend ordering one of those to accompany this.  Even without that, this product is highly recommended!

I bought this charger because I occassionally leave my phone in my purse overnight without charging.  It's nice having the iTorch in my purse as well so that I can just take out the cable and charge it while I'm on the go, in meetings, at the mall, etc.  I had my phone 25% charged, and pulled out the iTorch.  I fully charged the iTorch about three weeks ago, so I wasn't sure if it was going to work.  I was presently surprised to see that it charged pretty quickly and was at full capacity after 1.5 hours.  Totally took the charge out of the iTorch but I can easily charge that again later.It has a USB port and also another port that fits my blackberry and GPS unit.  It also has a laser pointer on it.  I haven't had much use for the laser pointer, but it's small enough that it doesn't make a difference.  I like that it's nice and small and fits well in my purse without much bulk.The only con I can think of is that I wish the charger would indicate how much the battery is charged.  I know it's written in the directions somewhere, but I'm pretty bad about keeping track of where I put that sort stuff.  Totally recommend this product for charging phones and ipods.

This battery pack will charge your iphone several times.  It is compact and easy to carry in your briefcase.  It doesn't plug directly into the iphone so you will need to also carry a charging cord.  The unit is very solid and I would recommend it.
held good charge and would charge my phone 2 full cycles, however after 3 months and outside of the return period, it died...
summary: Was great while it lasted for 3 months

reviewText: Everything about this charger is awesome. The flashlight is great, the laser pointer is very powerful, and it holds a good charge.My only issue is it was a little bit bulkier than I expected, it doesn't fit in my pocket with my phone too well. The external charger my girlfriend has is a lot slimmer, and fits very well. But that's my fault for not looking at the specifications.Either way, love it, very useful, and totally worth it!

The itouch is perfect for me since I travel and do presentations. Its got a led pointer which is great for presentations and the battery also charges my iphone. What's great is that it is a 3-in-1 (charger, flashlight and led pointer). The extra benefit is that it is compact and small eough to fit in my suit pocket. Great product..

Fits perfect in a pocket, backpack, purse, etc. My wife loves having a sleek and stylish battery to keep her iphone charged all day. It's nice to be on vacation, or a "staycation" at Disneyland and not have to make the whole trip come to a screeching halt having to charge mobile devices. With the iTorch we were able to keep moving without having to be tethered to an electrical outlet and waiting for phones to charge. The flashlight and laser pointer come in handy as well. Got a lot of jealous looks from other tourists wishing they had one to charge their phones.

Initial impression on the battery charger (IMP52D, iTorch external battery): The plastic casing is thick and sturdy. It seems pretty solid and well crafted. I found the manual useful. It was also helpful to have the extra cord and case. I was able to get three full charges for my Sansa Fuze mp3 player before I had to recharge the battery. I used my new Trent wall charger to charge the battery and all worked well (nothing felt warm). A side note, you could label the ports on the wall charger.Could improve: Have some sort of cover or cap for the usb ports to keep dust, lint, etc. out of ports. See if there is anything that can be done so products won't heat up on first charge.Issues: Upon the first charge it heated up my mp3 player when I charged it. I did charge it though and I used it again with supervision. The mp3 player doesn't feel warm when charging via usb wall charger. The 2nd and 3rd charge of my mp3 player went better; it did not heat up. On the second cycle (after recharging the IMP52D, iTorch external battery) the same thing happened - 1st charged warmed up my mp3 player (2nd, 3rd, ok). But this time I set my mp3 player on a cold sandstone coaster and it didn't seem to heat up as much. I set it on a glass table other times and that seemed to help as well. You might also recommend taking the product you are charging (if it has one) out of its case so it can cool easier.All in all I think it is a good charger. People just need to be careful that the first charge doesn't heat up their product too much. Setting the item on something that will conduct heat away (marble counter, sandstone coaster, glass table, etc.) will help with that issue somewhat. As will taking it out of its case.

As I was unpackaging the product, I was already pleased by it.  The construction was very well and felt of very high quality.  The battery charger was not as heavy as I would have imagined and I knew it would not be a problem to carry around.  What was also a plus side on convenience was that I would still be able to use my original phone holsters and cases which I saw may become a problem with using one of those rechargeable cases.  This charger holds a good amount of juice and in one instance I was able to not only charge my phone but another persons as well with the charger still having some energy left for another phone to be charged, not to mention it seems to charge just as fast as using a wall charger.This charger also has the features of a red laser pointer, which is great for presentations and an LED light which always comes in handy.  I do however, wish that there were separate buttons or switches for these lights and that It would be not shared with the button to turn on the charger for actual charging.  The holding down of the button to go through the different features can get a bit annoying when I am just trying to charge my phone.Overall, I give this product a 5/5 rating.  It works GREAT, holds lots of energy for charging, charges very fast and is very well constructed.

The iTorch IMP52D is a great device to supply additional power to a portable device when your battery runs out.  It is very easy to charge, and the operation of the device is very intutive.  It works with USB cord charger that comes with your device (iPhone, iPad).the device is compact and fits easily in a briefcase.

I only had the device for several days now but so far I am extremely happy with the IMP52D.  I received the IMP52D the day before I left for vacation so I had a chance to use it extensively for several days now.  I purchased the unit for it's generous 5200mAh capacity, competative price, attractive looks, and most of all from the experience I had with other NewTrent products I own.  I am a little bit of a mobile electronics junkie.  Never traveling withour my iPhone, iPad, laptop, and camera.  I also use electronic cigarettes which charge via usb chargers.  A backup battery or several backup batteries is a must.  I have tried several of them.  Because I wanted the flexability of charging several devices from different manafacturers I did not consider iphone or ipad cases that snap on and extend the battery of that specific device.First impressions when opening up the box was that it is smaller then what I expected.  It's over an inch shorter and over a 1/2 inch less wide then my iPhone 5.  It is a little bit thicker then the iPhone 5 with my Otterbox Defender case on it.  It's a very attractive unit.  Black of course with a chrome bezel around the front.  There's a single flush button on the front with four blue leds above it.  The flush button is nice as it prevent it from getting caught on something and accidently turned on.  There's a micro and regular usb ports on the top along with a laser pointer light and an led light.  The device can easily fit in a shirt or pand pocket and it rather light.  The unit appears very well built.  The package contained 2 usb cables.  One with a micro usb on one end and a regular usb on the other used for charging and android based phones.  The other is a Galaxy Tab charging cable. Also included were an instruction manual, and a nice drawstring pouch to keep it in.  The pouch is a nice addition to keep the attractive unit from getting banged up and scratched.  These devices are very simple to use and because I get excited with every new device I get in my hands started charging it right away.  I plugged the included micro usb into the IMP52D and the other into an Apple cube type usb/ac adapter.  The indicator lights show the charging progress with flashing and solid leds.  The solid led indicates the current level and the flashing one is the level it's working on.  Total initial charging time was 2.5 to 3 hours.  Note that the leftmost led only illuminates when the device it connected to (charging) another device.So far the device has charged everything I threw at it.  Charged my iPhone 5 without an issue.  Note to iPhone 5 users...if you recently got one or are waiting for yours a backup battery is a necessity.  I haven't figured if I could change some settings on it but it chews through the battery much faster then my iPhone 4 did (and the 3GS for that matter).  I've been using the maps app quite a bit so that may be the cause but it's really taxing the battery.  I was able to fully charge my iPhone 5 and also put a decent charge on my iPad 2 and charge one of my cigarette batteries.The included led flashlight and laser pointer are an added benifet as well.  Haven't had a chance to use the laser pointer other then to play with my dog (he loves chasing it on the floor) but the led flashlight already came in handy on a couple occasions.As far as product improvements there is nothing really major but would love to see the following.1. The user manual is sufficient but most functions are explained via pictures.  Including pictures and text would be better.2. The led flashlight could be stronger.3. A single button operates the laser pointer, the led flashlight, and turns the unit on and off.  Having separate buttons would be better.  I do not like having to hold buttons for different durations of time to turn features on and off.Separating the unit on light from the battery capacity lights (I would think most people think all 4 leds represent the battery life and when charging the unit the first one is off)Overall I think the unit is excellent and highly recommend it.

This small battery backup charger easily fits into the palm of my hand and is not bulky in my pocket. The itorch charged my iphone in what seemed like record time.My iPhone contained 2% battery life when I plugged in the iTorch and began charging. Also, they could increase the capacity to 7000+mAh.  All in all, solid product.
I bought this as Christmas gifts for my co-workers and myself.  It's a perfect gift since everyone uses cell phones.

I got this item for a trip to Peru.  I used this to charge my phone while on the plane, and in airport and while in Peru and not near power.  It work great.  you won't get more then a few charges out of it though. reviewText: I bought the iTorch to charge my iPhone while on the Appalachian Trail. I have gotten 2+ charges to 95-100% so well worth the weight since it can be a 5-10 days between places to charge on AT. The unit is easy to use, the blue lights keep you informed of the charge available and the red LED light is an added bonus.  I am very pleased with the quality!  I did contact New Trent with a question and they were very quick to respond and were most helpful.  If you need a lightweight battery charge, the iTorch is an excellent choice.

Have a Droid Razr which is always hungry.  Bought the New Trent IMP500 and it fit the bill perfectly.  Easy to use, can nearly get 3 full charges of my Razr out of one charge of the New Trent IMP500.  Nice.

I am a graduate student and I also work part time. Often I get in a situation where my battery is low, but I can not plug my phone in to charge. I bought the iTorch to ensure my phone didn't die during the day. I can plug my phone into the iTorch and stick it in my backpack. The iTorch has great capacity. reviewText: Very convenient to charge my Apple phone & mp3 player. No hassle compact design and a large capacity charger. No need to look for electrical source to charge my devices.

It comes with a soft bag case, but I find I never use those.Occasionally the LED or the laser would turn on, in my pocket, but the good thing is they auto-shutoff after about 30 seconds.After about 3 weeks of use, my device would not charge anymore. reviewText: I already owned an external battery from this company.  Had it two years and it's still working great so when I saw they had a smaller unit, I bought two.  These are smaller than my iPhone and iPod Touch and fits perfect in my travel purse.Likes-Portablity, comes with a small black drawstring bag.-Size, fits in my smallest purse, easy to tavel with.-Battery standby life on this battery is awesome.-Charges my iPhone and Galaxy Player faster than the computer and car charger.-Charges my dead iPhone 2x's while using the phone, probably more if I didn't use (surfing, talking, etc) it while charging.Dislikes-Power button easily depressed when in my purse, so I found a cushioned case to keep that from happening.-Adapters, charges with a micro usb cable, it ships with that and cables but there not dedicated, there's an adapter included for that. reviewText: The product arrived and I read the instructions and charged the battery for the recommended time. Product did not work, It had no charge.  I charged it again, andthen same issue.  I was only offered a refund and not a replacement.  The product in my book is suspect.  Be advised that you may have to go through multiple purchases and shippings in order to receive a functional device.

I've had similar products to this, but this is both the most compact and most reliable I've used.  It's a great size for putting in my computer bag, and so handy when traveling not having to worry about a dead iPhone battery.

The imp 52 gave me just about 3 dead to full charges which was to be expected based on the MAH of my cell phone battery, and the capacity of the power pack. The pack is very small and portable with curved edges making it very pocket friendly.The included laser pointer and flashlight were very handy and useful add ons, though as a minor complaint, it would be nice if those were on the opposite end of the pack from the usb port/charging port. But since you can quickly disconnect it to use it as a flashlight thats an extremely minor complaint.My friend's iphone got wet (a wine bottle broke in her purse containing the phone) and experienced some kind of a battery short where the battery could no longer hold a charge. We were able to use my imp52 to keep it powered and continue to use it without issue while connected to the newtrent power pack. When we took the phone to the apple store to get repaired/replaced and even the apple staff assisting us was impressed with the imp52 and asked questions about it, and couldnt believe its capacity or how we were using it.The only problem I had with it, and its a minor issue, is that the led indicator lights are a little hard to see to gauge charging levels, especially from a distance.I genuinely find myself charging my phone less at home knowing I have my newtrent power pack with me

reviewText: I have had the New Trent IMP52D iTorch for about 3 weeks now and I love it.It's a small enough package that it fits in your pocket for charging onthe go. Perfect for the quick charge of your phone when there aren't anyoutlets or USB plugs around. Also the added convenience of a laser pointeris very handy during presentations or product demonstrations. I thoughtthe light was weak but when used in a dark room it works perfectly. I evenuse the iTorch when on the road. The iTorch even kept a full charge after a week of nouse, and topped off my phone in minutes! Great product and the perfectaddition to my road warrior gear.
summary: You need this if you travel at all!

reviewText: I received the IMP52D iTorch external battery, on Sept 21st - fast shipping.  The packaging is great, very easy to open and get to the product.  The included cables are good, but I have been using a retractable micro usb.  It just keeps things neat I think.  I like the laser pointer and used it a few times to point something out.  I think the flashlight is extremely bright, and has come in handy a few times.  I have been charging my phone for the past week with it, instead of the wall plug, and have got 5 charges out of it before it seemed like it was going to die, HTC evo 4g.  I like the blue light indicator of remaining charge, very clean looking.  I wish it could charge a Xoom, but I guess that requires a higher voltage.  The build is solid and looks like quality material.  Kind of reminds me of a block phone like a Nokia.  It is small enough to carry without really noticing you have it in your pocket.  Very good for someone who travels and needs some extra charge on a long flight or even a weekend camping.  I am bringing it with me this weekend on a long flight and am confident it will get me through six hours of video on my phone.  Overall it gets a 5 out of 5 from me.  Hope this review helps. - Ryan

I have been using the iTorch as my sole means of charging a few separate devices since I received it. Namely, an iPod touch 5th Gen, a Verizon MiFi Jetpack, my Blackberry Curve, and an older iPod Touch (2nd Gen). The iTorch has delivered exactly what I was looking for in terms of allowing me to not have to find an outlet to recharge any of my devices. The capacity of the iTorch completely recharged my iPod 5th Gen twice, as well as recharging the older iPod Touch completely, and the iTorch still had some power remaining. This is more than adequete to get me through the day.In terms of design and functionality, I find the physical dimensions and design to be very pleasant. It slips VERY easily into any pocket, and is less bulky than some of the other battery chargers I have.The single-button implementation of enabling the various functions (battery on, laser pointer on, flashlight on), while efficient, takes a bit of getting used to. I'm the type of person who simply assumes that I can figure out how most things work without needing to read the manuals, and most of the time that's true. I had to check the manual in order to figure out how to turn the flashlight on, but that's not really a big deal, as once I learned how to do it, I haven't had to look at the manual again. Ultimately, though, the primary function of this device is to serve as a backup battery, and getting it to work in that regard is a no-brainer, and it works flawlessly for that.Overall, I think the iTorch has a great physical design, more than adequate capacity for a single-user to get through the day, and the performance meets my expectations. The added bonus features of the flashlight and laser pointer may come in handy.
summary: Great charging companion with bonus features

reviewText: When I bought my wife an HTC One X, it was the first phone we had owned that did not have a removable battery. I did some research, read many reviews, and bought the iTorch, IMP52D.Am I ever glad I did.It is small enough to fit into my wife's purse (without complaining about the size or weight) and packs enough juice to charge the phone a few times over, before the iTorch needs to be recharged itself.I've even "borrowed" her iTorch when I don't want the hassle of changing out batteries when my Galaxy S3 gets low on power.The LED light and laser pointer are nice extras. The LED has enough light to see things I've dropped in the movie theater!I would definitely buy this little workhorse again!
summary: Great for Phones without Removable Batteries

reviewText: I love using this product. I got it with the intentions of using it when i'm on the go, but I actually enjoy using it around the house just as must as when i'm out. Before I would plug my iphone or iPad into the nearest wall outlet, but when I moved to a different room, i'd have to move the plug, the cable, find an available outlet.... Now I keep the IMP52D plugged into my gadget, and I can move around easily without losing a charge.For example, i'm at my computer now typing this. If I want to go to the kitchen for 10 minutes, normally i'd have to unplug my phone and take it. Then i'd probably forget to plug it back up when I got back to my computer and i'd have dead phone life. Since its charging now on this device, I can just take the whole thing into the kitchen and my charge lives on!There are many things to like. The small size makes it very easy to grab and move around with. It fits in my pocket or messenger bag easily. Even though its small, it still feels solid and well built. Sometimes you can feel a piece of equipment and tell that it's not well designed. This is not the case with this product. It doesn't feel cheap - it looks and feels very dependable.Even though the features are minimal, you can tell much thought went into the design of these features. The USB outlets are on the same side and close to each other. The product itself has a nice curve and shape to it. The power button is small but prominent - i like how it sits flush with the product so that it doesn't accidentally get pressed, but its also easy to find and press if the device is in a bag or in the dark.The battery life is good for a product of this size. It charges my devices quickly, and the device itself does not take too long to charge.The flashlight and red laser are nice extra features, especially the flashlight. I frequently had this product by my side during the past week, and I found myself being happy that I had a quick flashlight on hand. Before I would have to pull out my cell phone and use the flashlight, and my phone is a little sluggish at its older age, so it's always a hassle to unlock it, find the icon for the flashlight, blah blah blah... it was nice to have something that could provide a quick light.I also have the NT70T from New Trent, which is a little bigger and has more charging ports, etc. I really like that product as well, but i found myself using it as more of an emergency option for power. I didn't want to use it often in case I needed the extra power in a pinch. The IMP52D however crossed the line into every day usage, which I didn't think would happen with an external battery charger.I definitely recommend it to anyone looking for some extra juice for any kind of USB chargeable device.

Pros:-Very small compaired to other battery packs I had in past with similar milliamps.- Two extra features that I use very often. Laser and LED light-Same cable for my android phone is used to charge the iTorchCons:- None at allThe iTorch is a great every day accessory for anyone with a cellphone or a tablet who finds themselves always running low on battery power when a wall charger is not accessible.Where I work I can not plug in my smart phone and find it running low on battery life by 3pm. The iTorch is small enough to fit in my pocket with my phone.It is a must have if you own any electronic device. It makes a great holiday gift for anyone male or female.
summary: Super Compact battery pack that packs a punch

reviewText: The IMP52D, iTorch external battery is a nice option from NewTrent for backup battery for your smartphone. I personally have an iPhone 4S and my wife as an iPhone 4. It will also charge tablets as well (only at 1A so its can seem to take a little while to do so). Since the capacity is 5200mAh, it won't fully charge an iPad 4th generation but it does come in handy when you need a least 2 or more charges on your phone. The device is compact and is smaller than most smartphones (it is thicker but width and length are smaller) and is easy to carry around with you. The capacity would be enough to get your through some heavy phone usage on a long flight or a few days of camping if the phone was used sparingly.The iTorch also has a LED light and laser pointer option on it as well, making it a potential replacement for an emergency light and laser pointer for presentations. This would allow you to leave a couple other devices at home and increase this chargers usefulness especially when space may be tight. The light is fairly bright, think good pen light, which is all you need in an emergency or if you just need a small light for those times when working in a dark area (under a desk or behind something). I haven't gotten to test the laser pointer fully, but it seems adequate for using in a presentation/meeting.Pros:- Multiple functions: light, laser pointer, external battery- small size and good power (5200mAh)- charges an iPhone 4S more than twice before needing to be rechargedCons:- none really...maybe since it doesn't come with a charging cord for Apple products, it would be nice to offer one especially since its called "iTorch"Summary:I'd give this product a 5 out of 5 stars as it meets or exceeds all my expectations for a good, reliable battery backup for my iPhone. It is easy to pack with you and has some nice bonus features that one doesn't expect to find on an external battery backup device. I would definitely recommend to anyone wanting battery backup/external pack for extending the life of your phone.
summary: Great backup/external battery with bonus features

reviewText: I have used this charger during and after school and it works. I love how it has a flashlight and a laser built in. I bought it for $24.95 plus 2 free car chargers, and they came the next week on Monday when I ordered them on Thursday. Another bonus is that it includes a velvet pouch. I really wish it had a lightning adapter so that I could keep my charger plugged into my outlet.

I have found the external battery to be amazing and soooo handy! I do construction for a living so have to be able to keep in touch with clients a lot. Many times I have not been able to use my phone when I wanted to for fear of running my battery down when expecting an important call - had to save the charge so my phone would be good when the call came through. This external will enable me to answer all calls and not worrying about missing a business opportunity and still being able to receive the important call!!! This is a great product!!!

IMP52DGood: There are a lot of things that I like about this battery pack. The main thing is how fast it charges my iPhone 4s. It appears to charge it faster than my home computer, work computer and even the wall plug. This is obviously very nice when you don't have the time or want to keep it plugged into whatever device you are charging. The size is also really nice, I was expecting it to be larger than it is. Weight wise it really doesn't weight that much but kind of feels like it weighs more than it should. I think this is because for its size it is hefty. This isn't a bad thing though it is still plenty light enough that if you have it in your pocket it doesn't feel like your pants are being pulled down.  It also comes with a small felt bag which I think is a really nice add on. It obviously allows you to keep it with its charging cable all together in one spot. There is also enough room to fit in the standard Apple charging cable.Not so good: The button to switch between the laser pointer, LED light and turning it on / off is a bit of a pain. You have to hold the button for varying amounts of time to get the result you want. The laser is easy since it is just click once, I have turned it on a couple of times by accident and then almost shined it in my eye. :\
summary: Nice little power back up option

reviewText: Worked perfectly for me when I needed to use it and lke that it includes a carry pouch with it.  The combination of button presses to get the laser pointer / flashlight / battery charge is a little confusing.  Maybe they could make the laser pointer / flashlight on a slide switch option?  Other than this, this is one great little charger.  Easily fits in a pocket or  small space in a backpack.  Works great for a long weekend trip.
It works great & it charges my iPhone 5 fairly quickly.  It's small enough to fit in a pocket but still has enough power to charge a dead phone.

I would give this product a 4.5 / 5 stars.Gave it a 5 because its only negative is that it has added bells & whistles which aren't necessary.PROS:- Very compact. Put it in a pocket and don't even realize it!- Aesthetic design w/ nice finish- Easy to operate- Universally compatible- Holds charge for many days when unusued- Reasonably priced- Reputable brand w/ growing customer base (See Facebook)CONS:- Button pressing can be a bit confusing at first- Still need to hook up your phone/tablets respective charging cable- No direct/built-in wall plug to recharge the iTorch- Laser Pointer & Torch (I prefer simplicity...but I'm sure this can fall under PROS for others.)I've been using this almost daily. At the locations I travel to often times I can not find a power outlet and nor do I have time to sit around and wait for a phone to charge 5% at each corner. My iPhone 5 gets heavy usage on the go and with LTE, it naturally burns through the battery and I'm usually phone-less by the end of the day. That changed after buying the iTorch. Very happy with my purchase and the price point is truly reasonable considering how much of a headache it can be to not have a phone when you need it most.A couple of things I'd like to see improved on a future update:- If it can be made even more lightweight/compact (I think thats a common goal with any small electronics over time.)- Possible addition of a dual-port. One on each end. (I like that the iDual has this feature.)- Add a "wall plug" but have it as a foldable option. (There is an iPhone charger on Kickstarter which has this feature. It is a case with a built-in / fold-out wall plug. I think a Trent which could charge from a wall outlet, without a wired USB plug, would earn a 5/5 unanimously)- Make a simpler version without the laser pointer or torch. They actually slow down the usage of the product because you click quick once for the laser pointer. Click and hold for the charger to turn on, click and hold for the torch, click and hold AGAIN to turn the torch and charger off and put it into standbye.If you need a RELIABLE external battery pack (from a reputable company)...then look no further, this is the one.EDIT/Update:1. I've noticed that this charges my iPhone 5 faster than my wall charger does. No idea how, but it does. Pleasantly surprised.2. The laser pointer turms on with the short click. NewTrent will have to weigh on TSA guidelines and whether it is deemed safe for use in-flight.
summary: This is the one! Finally...one that actually works.

reviewText: Slim and solid build. Chargers my phone multiple times. laser pointer and led light are useful. I bought another to give as a gift.

actually really liked this product. Overall the item is really portableand the design is very slick. Also the LED light and laser pointer make itreally ideal for the person to carry it around at the office or to work.Also it would be great to store in your car since sometimes i would dropcoins or a pen in my car at night and need to find it and the LED lightwould be perfect for that. The product also can charge my s3 and ipad tofull before it is drained. Also works for the new iphone 5 and ipad withretina display. The charge time is also fairly short which makes it idealfor if you're on the move and short on time. I would recommend this product.

I don't write many reviews, but the New Trent product line deserves a shout-out.A small, well-built battery charger that is reliable and powerful. Uses a standard 110 wall outlet to charge, and my Droid Razr was completely recharged almost 3  times.Comes with a USB cable for Droids and a cable for the Samsung Galaxy.The bells and whistles, i.e. the laser pointer and the LED flash, are handy.The bright blue 4 bar LED charge counter (lo, med, med-hi and full) allow you to check with a touch.I went with New Trent because I couldn't find a negative review, and I can see why.

reviewText: My recent purchase of the iTorch external battery IMP52D has presented itself to be a great buy (under $37). This external battery is smaller than my HTC thunderbolt phone and packs a good amount of charge.What is neat about this particular external battery pack is that it also has a useful laser pointer for my job and to drive my cat crazy.I have been using this charger at work to watch my Hulu shows and while I'm in line trying to checkout at the grocery store, otherwise my phone would die before end of day.It works on iPads,but for those who own an ASUS Tablet it requires 15V and there is no battery pack that would support that.The box includes a Micro USB cable, cloth pouch for storage, and an instructions sheet.So a quick summary of the +'s and -'s:Pros:* Very sleek and compact size for EASY storage in one's purse,briefcase,or pocket* Fairly light for a backup battery (only 4.6 ounces)* Sturdy product and the plastic is not flimsy* Able to completely charge my HTC thunderbolt about 4 to 4.5 times before the iTorch runs out of juice* Laser pointer very useful for presentations at work or school. (makes this a great gift for a colleague or teacher)* There is one button that controls all three features.(pressing for 1 second gives you laser pointer,2 seconds battery charge,3 seconds LED light light* Auto shut off after 10 minutes if light left on or battery no longer connected to device being charged (The only thing that doesn't shut off after 10 mins is the laser pointer in case you're still using in a presentation)Cons:* The torch (LED light) is useful when some light is needed to findsomething in your car or in a dark room real quick but it is not extrabright to brighten yourwhole room. (I know it's not meant for heavy duty but the current light could be a little brighter)
summary: Great power pack,easy to carry, and plenty of juice

reviewText: Can't go wrong with tossing this is your bag before a trip or a conference where you need juice! Laser pointer is fun to mess with the cat with but the pack itself is too bulky to be used as a dedicated laser for meetings, etc. I guess it would work as a backup in a pinch but don't buy this for the pointer. The same can be said about the flashlight.The battery pack works great but you need to make sure your phone is good enough on 1A. Otherwise, this pack will drain faster than it can "re-fuel" your device. If that is the case, like say for my ATT S4 which needs 2.1A to rightfully charge, the best way to use it is with the phone turned off and charging, say mid-flight. Worked much better back on my S2 or my Fiancee's S3 (no our last name won't be Samsung).

Nice device. Fits in my pocket. Charges my smartphones, powers my usb lights and fans.But it needs improvement.It does not stop charging. It just shows that its full and continues to charge. Has anyone had it stop charging when full? Or does it just overcharge?

This is the perfect size portable charger! There is an adapter for charging tablets. It looks like a little usb extension but somehow charges the tablet. I have used this to charge an asus tf700, samsung galaxy note 10.1, and the nexus phone. Charges fast and is very portable. There is also a nice little carry case that comes with this as well. I'm not sure why there is a laser pointer and led light on this, but it sure doesn't take anything away from the product. The laser is nice and it is a good thing to have just i case you need it. Definitely worth the money!!

I purchased this for my son who has an Android phone which he is constantly plugging in to recharge.  I thought this would prevent him from carrying a cord all of the time.  He has decided to keep it semi- permanently attached to his phone 24/7.  He seems to enjoy using it in this matter and he constantly has available power.
summary: Great for that extra boost of power

reviewText: I brought this product with me during a 4 day convention earlier this month. It only took about 8 hours to bring it to a full charge before using. I also noticed that it took at least 2 days before the battery pack fully drained, which was great. What I like about this product, other than its range for charging my devices is the portability and ease of use. It works with practically all of my electronic devices that can be charged via a USB cord, and I would highly recommend it for travel or everyday use. This would be a great alternative on saving not only time on juicing up your electronics, but also with spending extra money on extra batteries for your products.

I received my iTorch very quickly after ordering it and had the opportunity to test it right away.  Our family has several pieces of electronics that we use on a daily basis and we always seem to have a bottleneck charging them.  We have ipads of many sizes, itouches, iphones, digital cameras, kindles etc.  This little charger proved to be able to handle quite a demand.  We charged the iphones, kindle, ipads easily and very quickly.  I have found that the New Trent Products charge faster than the wall outlet and since it is portable it is quite comfortable and convenient to be charging the electronic while still using it or at least away from the wall. The size and shape of the iTorch is very convenient to carry, it is light and ergonomically comfortable in your hand. it also fits easily in a small purse or even pocket.  I also have the New Trent IMP120D  12000mAh and I can say with certainty, that on a daily basis I will use the iTorch, but on travel I will take the IMP120D. It charges easily and quickly to take on the go for a day's use, especially as fast as the batteries drain from electronics it is always nice to have some back up.  I have not had use for the flashlight or laser but I did test them and they worked well.  Ultimately, I would highly recommend this product to anybody with electronics! and kids, who aways seem to say their phone died and that's why they didn't answer. It is extremely versatile since it charges basically anything that uses a USB cable.  I have read some complaints about it not coming with a DC charger cable, but the fact that it is 100% compatible with the apple cable is good enough for me.  Actually, it is nice to not have too many cables.  You only need one at a time and with today's electronic waste- it find it unnecessary to provide something you already have.  Less to carry and less waste.

Review for IMP52D (iTorch)This external Battery has a 5200mAH capacity and an output of 1amp.The 1amp output is generally recommended for cell phones and Bluetooth devices.It comes with a usb micro cord and a second adapter cord for charging a Samsung Galaxy tablet.The battery is approximately the size a small closed flip phone and slightly heavier.It fits nicely in the palm, has a single button on the front, and a bulb on either side of the input and output ports on top.Device includes a built in red laser and led lights, and comes with a carrying pouch.It took about 5 hours to charge initially. When plugged in there are four blue lights, three of which continue to race until charged. Although it can be used when any of them are lit, once the three lights stops blinking it's fully charged. I recommend charging overnight the first time or when fully discharged. In a pinch, you can also charge your phone while charging the battery, just be sure to turn the battery on.Once you plug a device into the output port, the fourth blue light illuminates. Device was tested on Samsung Galaxy S2, Samsung Infuse, and an ATT Go phone. All charged quickly and without incident. With the included adapter, I've read that it reverses cord polarity, we were also able to charge a Samsung Galaxy 7in Tablet. Since the output of this battery is 1amp, vs. the 2amp Samsung charger, this was not completed as quickly.While the red laser and super bright led lights on the device might come in handy in certain situations, since I wanted battery for charging my phone, I probably won't use them and deplete the battery for lighting very often.I'd highly recommend this small powerful battery to anyone with the need to charge a phone or device where there is no power available.

After browsing through all kinds of portable battery chargers, I chose the New Trent iTorch battery charger. Not because it starts with an "i" but it looked attractive and ultra portable. It is a little heavy, but it was expected with a 5200 mAh battery. The day I received it, it came with more than 75% charge, which I used on a dead HTC one. After giving it a full charge, it was still not off, working like a hero! I like how the indicators show you how much charge is left on the device. Plus it comes with a USB cable which you can use to charge it and then to charge your phone. You can just put it in your pocket with your phone while charging it and you won't even know it's there! I don't really use the laser and flashlight on it but it's a must have while you're out camping or just when you need to use your phone without having to worry about a dead battery.

This is a great external battery to have and is convenient to have when you need a little extra juice.I've had other batteries, but one thing I love about this one is its size. It is much smaller than a lot of other ones yet provides ample power for my devices. I don't feel like I need to make extra space in my gadget bag for this and its portability may be the best thing about it.I also love the added laser pointer. I'm not one to use a laser pointer often, but I have needed one on a few occasions and having this ability straight from this device really works well in a jam.This is must-have item if you ever are traveling or anywhere where power supplies are limited. I highly recommend this product.

This slim design portable charger is good to carry in pants or a jacket pocket for someone on the go who may need to recharge a smart phone or tablet (or both). It has enough juice to get you through a busy day. The flashlight and laser pointer are nice extras but this is best for its size.

First the battery arrived 3 days ahead of schedule. A very nice surprise.The battery came with an almost full charge so I played with it for a while before charging. The laser pointer goes about 1/4 a mile before not being useful. The flashlight is very bright and very handy. The carry bag holds the battery and included retractable usb cord. The instructions were easy to read andnunderstand.What I found was it takes a few tries to get the timing right to turn on the battery and not the flashlight.Since the day it arrived I have found it charges all my families cell phones, Kindle Fire, Kindle Touch, Blu electronic cigarette charger pack, wifes Tom Tom, portable lte mifi, and  several bluetooth earpieces. I'm not saying it will fill them all on 1 charge, just that it charges them while powering them. I'm sure there are other devices I just haven't tried to plug in yet.It powers,  without charging, my Galaxy Tab 10.1 and wifes ipad1.It came with all the cords I'd need for many devices and the usb end of the specialty plugged ones work just fine so there's no need to buy any cords if yours plugs in to a usb plug on 1 end.The quality of the entire package is top notch and feels like it will last longer than the warranty.For families like mine that have lots of portable electronics and someone undoubtedly needs a charge and left their charger at home this is an almost must have and at the price it was a no brainer for me.If you get this you'll be surprised at how useful it can become in little to no time.
summary: I'd give more than 5 stars if I could
Good backup power when you need it

reviewText: For what the product is supposed to do, it does it flawlessly.There is a one-button-does-all (similar to Apple products) that is on the device. Initially I thought that I might accidentally hit it a few times, but its actually quite fine in that regards.The laser and torch are nice additional features, and both function as a "real" add on--not a last minute afterthought that the company slapped on.The torch isn't exceptionally bright, but it will get the job done.The design is sleek and feels like high quality--the entire casing seems to be entirely higher quality plastic.When charging, it charges my phone at about the same rate as the wall plug. This is very useful for anybody who may need more than one charge per day (as I do, because I always use pandora one/my iPhone 4 battery is slowly losing its capacity)The charger does not get hot -- only mildly warm, emphasis on this--when used. The temperature is hard to describe, but I could personally hold it in my hand all day without discomfort, it gets no hotter than the iPhone does when it is used.This product does what it promises to do, and you can charge it at night for the same time that your phone would take. The only con to this is that it does not have its own usb-wall plug, but that isn't so bad because most people buying this would already have an iPhone/iPod/Android adapter anyways.

My iPhone 4S tends to go through the battery fairly fast.  I am on 4G often (work wifi is bad), so I tend to need a lot of juice.  The iTorch IMP52D certainly has that.  I started with the NT52D, which is a lot larger (pack of cigarette sized) and had the same capacity (5200 mAh), so the size of this one is nice (more like a big lighter).  It fits in my pocket better, or in the side pouch of my backpack.  When I do that, I can have the backpack on and have the phone on a 6-foot cord, charging as I use it.  Very tech-geeky.The flashlight has come in handy a few times.  When I was in the hotel room and dropped something behind the bed, the light came in handy.  It's a tad dim (perhaps upgrading it to what the iphone itself has, or maybe even a cree light, would be better), but it is a great idea.  The laser pointer is even neat, although I do not need it for presentations, but if it did, it would be useful.I have not tried this with my ipad, but when the iPhone plugs in, it says it puts out 1000 mAh.  It charges up the phone quite fast, and at the end of the night, it has charged my phone a couple of times and still has juice left.  I just plug it into my dual USB charger and leave it overnight, and it's good to go.About the blue LEDs on the side.  It may be nice if when the battery is charged, if the light turned off and maybe would turn on when you turned the unit on to show the power level.  As it is, that LED is bright in the bedroom, stays on as long as it's plugged in, and I had to put the unit in the enclosed case while plugged in to dim the light so I could sleep.  It is quite bright in a dark bedroom.The other feature I'd like to see is the on/off switch changed.  As it is, I plug the phone in, then turn the unit on to wake it up.  It turns itself off after the phone is unplugged a short while.  I'd like to see it maybe turn itself on automatically when the iphone is attached to charge (like the NT600C does).  And, maybe have a built-in plug like the NT600C as well.  The unit is so compact, but having to remember a separate USB cord and power supply is a pain.All in all, I like the unit.  It is definitely more compact than the NT52D, and has the pointer and LED light as well.  Much better for travel.  I'd say of the 3 that I do have (NT52D, NT600C, and this one), I'd buy this one if I was only going to get one of the three.  If it had the extra features like the NT600C as well, it would be perfect.
summary: over-all, best of the New Trent charger products

reviewText: Since I started using my iPhone 4, I have been searching for a compact battery that can keep it going. I spend large amounts of time away from home and needed a battery that would not break the bank. After using an equally expensive battery from anther company, I did some research and came across this battery from New Trent. I have not been disappointed with this product.Not only is it designed well and fits great in my hand, but it has performed as necessary. My iPhone 4 is topped off very quickly and I no longer have to worry about using it too much during the day. The included charging cable works great and I normally charge it from my laptop while working at the office. The laser pointer is adequate, nothing special.My only question is about the light on the unit. When compared to my Photon LED keychain, it is not as bright. With 5200mAh at your disposal, why not put a brighter LED in the battery pack? It seems like an after-thought to include a flashlight at all, I would like to see it brighter or done away with completely. Then again, I did not buy this for the flashlight so it will get minimal use from me.As a portable battery pack, this performs excellently and has helped me and my coworkers equally as well. I take it everywhere and has performed marvelously. I will be looking to New Trent first when I need another battery backup.
summary: If you need a battery, look here first

reviewText: After receiving my iTorch, I decided a good first use would be a music festival I was headed to over the weekend. The music festival was the perfect environment to test out the iTorch:-I needed my phone at all times in order to meet up with friends at the festival-We were camping and I had no other way to charge my phone-The flashlight would get a good workout while looking for my stuff in the darkInitially, I was concerned that the iTorch would not be compatible with my Samsung Galaxy S3, but after checking the electrical specs, I knew the iTorch would work fine with my phone. The iTorch performed admirably over the weekend; by day 3, almost everyone else that I saw had a dead battery in their phone, whereas I had no concerns with constantly taking pictures and videos with my S3 as I knew that I would be able to charge it as needed.I was quite surprised that I was able to fully charge my phone twice using the iTorch, and even then, the internal iTorch battery was not depleted!Pros:-Extremely compact: I put the iTorch in my front pocket and basically forgot it was there-High battery capacity: Charged a Galaxy S3 (2100mAH capacity) twice and still had a charge left in the iTorch-USB charger means that I can charge up the iTorch while I'm on the go in my car.-Flashlight provides nice bonus functionality. I do a lot of camping and it's nice to have my phone charger and flashlight all in one.Cons:-iTorch took a fair amount of time to charge, which I would estimate at 3-4 hours. Even then, it may just be that I'm use to a much smaller capacity phone battery which would inherently mean it takes longer for the iTorch to charge.-While the device is extremely easy to use, the included instructions were a little confusing. I would suggest that a native English speaker go through the instruction and fix the grammar and spelling errors.Suggestion:-The Galaxy S3 should be listed in the compatible devices list on the Amazon listing. As one of the premiere Android phones, I could see people being a little nervous buying the iTorch for their Galaxy S3 since it's not listed. From what I could tell, the iTorch was 100% compatible with the S3.

The iTorch IMP52D External Battery Pack is an Awesome product! I love thatthis product comes with the extra laser pointer & the LED flashlight. I nolonger have to sit next to an outlet just to charge my phone. It is a veryreasonable price & charges my Samsung Galaxy S-III super fast. It chargedmy phone three times before having to plug the battery pack in to rechargeit. I rate this item 5 stars & would recommend it to family & friends.

I recently used this battery on at a 4-day long music festival where there is no access to any type of power outlets. Batteries like these are key to use since they are ultra portable, and charge your phone almost enough for once a day.The added plus to this item is its sleekness (ability to comfortably fit in hand or pocket). I would go as far to consider this "an executive tool" -- since it also includes a built in flash-light and red laser pointer (also all very nifty for a camping experience).New Trent continues to impress with quick charging, sleek, and multi-functional tools for the on-the-go user.***** (5/5 STARS)used this product with Samsung Galaxy S2 / iPhone 4S / iPhone 4 / Kindle / iPad 3

I have used this charger primarily for my Nexus devices and they have been performing well so far. I charge Nexus 4 and Nexus 7 using this charger when I am traveling or there is no power outlet available. According to my approximate estimates, this charger charges Nexus 4 completely (starting with no charge left) within 2 hours 45 minutes and there will still be almost half the charge left in the charger's battery pack. It charges Nexus 7 up to 83% (starting with no charge left) within 7 hours. So far so good and I intend to keep using New Trent products in future.If you have to travel internationally, these things are a lifesaver. Instead of using travel adapters directly with your electronic devices, it might be better to use these to charge your devices. Just my two cents.
If you always want to make sure that you will never be without a charged phone than this is a great item to buy

From the beginning, I could feel the excellent design quality. It doesn't feel cheap, doesn't have parts that come off, which is a plus, and it also has a nice weight to it. I found that I could charge my HTC One X in 1 hour and 30 minutes, and my PlayStation Vita could be charged in the same time. Of course, I made sure the battery was completely dead before trying to charge just to get the most accurate results. The ports feel solid and don't wiggle around. The charging portion of this product is indeed well worth the money. I found myself taking this product with me to school and during my errands. I found it very useful even walking around the house. It is convenient to be able to charge my devices away from a wall, which can sometimes limit the use of your devices. One thing I did notice that was surprising was that one of the LED's stopped working within the first week. Although I still can tell the battery level, it would be nice to see that fixed in a later model. The laser pointer was a useful feature. My cats love it and its useful to show people things during class. It could be very useful during presentations and other applications. I believe this unit has a flashlight, although I couldn't figure out how to enable it. Maybe a separate button should be added in the future for each function. I don't think that it would take away from the elegance of the design. Overall, this is definitely worth every penny. I was searching for a portable battery for a while, and I'm glad I ended up getting this one because it's come in handy many times already and i've only had it for about a week or so. If you're trying to decide which portable battery to get, your search is over!
summary: Ends the search for portable power!

reviewText: This gives me about one and half charges.  I like the small size, but prefer more power and two USB outputs.
