reviewText: First off let me say that I am a member of the club "I Don't Wear My Headset When I Am Not Using It", or Club IDWMHWIANUI for short.  These days when I am walking around the grocery store I feel like I am in a Star Trek movie watching all the various people walking around with devices de jour sticking from their ears.But when I do use headsets, this Jabra EXTREME has been one of the better ones I have used.  The last headset I had was difficult for me to synch with my phone, this Jabra synched for me right away.  The last headset I had didn't stay on my ear that well, this one does.  The last headset I had was weak on battery life, this one has good battery life.  The last one did have good sound/talk quality at least, and so does this Jabra.So overall, I have no complaints about this product so far...5 stars.  Since it has been comfortable to wear I just have to be extra careful (as a member of Club IDWMHWIANUI) to take off the headset when I am not using it!
summary: One of better headsets I have used...

reviewText: I've heard good things about Jabra so was excited to give this Extreme headset a shot. It's not half bad, but definitely not the best I've tried.Call Quality:People tell me I sound clear with good vocal tone when using this headset, and I don't have to speak very loud to be heard -- that's the benefit of dual mics at work -- they do a good job of picking up my voice while eliminating background noise.My first foray into dual mics was the BlueAnt V1, and to this day, it remains the best headset I've used by far. At the time, I predicted dual mics would become standard in all headsets due to their superior ability to separate noise while maintaining natural voice quality. The concept is similar to seeing with two eyes or hearing music in stereo -- dual mics just do a better job than one mic alone. Inferior noise canceling headsets filter noise at the expense of voice quality, but the dual mics help this Jabra do a decent job in the noise canceling department.On the flipside, listening to people speak to me through this Jabra is slightly less stellar. People sound slightly muffled, as if they're inside a box. Its not horrible, but certainly could be better.No Annoyingly Huge LEDs:I hate headsets with huge LEDs that scream, "HI EVERYONE, I'M ON THE PHONE!" It's minor, but I sure love that this headset only has one tiny LED. Lately, I've been developing a pet peeve with electronics that have needlessly large LEDs. It's as if every little piece of technology out there needs to declare its own self-worth via a blinking--flashing--glowing, something or other. Or more accurately, most tech developers seem to think big, shiny, sparkly luminescence will attract us to their products like hapless primates mesmerized by their first glimpse of flame. Thankfully, the Jabra Extreme just has the one tiny LED -- plenty big for anyone with eyes to see, yet small enough to be subtle.Comfort and FitThe Jabra Extreme feels comfortable in my ear and came with several different earpieces, which is always nice. It also came with two sizes of ear loops, though I was hoping I wouldn't need them. I've often eyed people who wear their headsets without an ear loop but never felt confident enough to try it myself. I imagined I'd constantly be adjusting the fit or worrying about losing my headset. But when I read the manual for this Jabra, I saw it came with a special earpiece that apparently made it possible to wear the headset without an ear loop. The headset is definitely small and light, so I figured it was worth a shot. At first, it stayed in my ear just fine without the ear loop -- well, at least while I was home. Unfortunately, the concept didn't hold up in a real world setting. As I went about my day, I constantly had to fiddle with the fit to keep the headset from falling off. I don't know about you, but I have more important things to do than constantly futz with my headset. It drove me nuts and I couldn't wait to get back home so I could put the ear loop back on and forget about it.Simple On/Off SwitchAnother thing I really appreciate about this Jabra is that it has a hard on/off switch -- and I don't mean the switch is hard to use, I mean it's an actual switch that clicks on, then clicks off. Anyone else noticed how such a simple thing has become a scarcity with electronics? Everything has a multifunction button -- tap once to do this, hold for 3 seconds to do that, tap twice for the other thingy..... I've come to appreciate a simple switch like the one on this Jabra that just clicks on and off -- and no flashy lights or anything either -- just a red mark showing when it's off and a green mark showing when it's on -- simple, efficient, easy and unmistakable -- perfect!Button SpacingThe call answer button and volume buttons are a bit cramped and can be tricky to operate when wearing the headset. I often thought I accidentally hung up on someone when I was just trying to adjust the volume. But I got accustomed to the layout the more I used it and rarely change the volume much, so it shouldn't prove to be an issue very often. Just be aware if you have big fingers or aren't good with spatial awareness, these buttons aren't going to work well for you. And as far as I can tell, there's no way to reassign the volume up and down buttons, so if you wear your headset on your left ear instead of your right, as I do, then your volume buttons will be upside-down -- volume up will be on the bottom and volume down on the top -- intuitively reverse. Placing the volume buttons side by side or allowing them to be remapped would have been better.AttachmentsThis Extreme comes with a car charger, a wall outlet charger and a USB charger for your computer. I thought it was a nice touch to include all three methods. And as I mentioned, it also comes with multiple earpiece attachments and 2 ear loops.Easy To Open Packaging:It's also worth mentioning that this Jabra is packaged well and is easy to open. If you've ever bought something that seems hermetically sealed and is near impossible to open, you'll appreciate the simple packaging of this Jabra.Bottom Line:This Jabra Extreme is pretty good, but I still give my 18 month old BlueAnt V1 the edge over every other bluetooth headset I've tried -- you just can't beat the BlueAnt's talking menus and superior noise canceling. But if you want a totally pared down yet reliable bt headset, this Jabra will serve you well.
summary: Extreme(ly) Good - But BlueAnt V1 is still the Best

reviewText: This bluetooth really does what it says.  I use this mainly when driving in the car, and with previous bluetooths, the person on the other end always said that it was noisy while driving.  Not with this model! There is a unique noise cancellation feature on this headset that blocks out all other noice! I havn't received any complaints since I've been using this bluetooth.  Additionally the buttons on this bluetooth are very easy to use and doesn't feel crowded like some others that I've tried. Give this bluetooth a try if you want to sound like you're on a "regualr phone"

I moved to this headset from a Plantronics Voyager 510, which I liked in spite or its proprietary connector to recharge (wall mounted only), rubber pieces that required regluing every few months and limited volume. When I started looking for a new Bluetooth headset I was concerned. It sounded as if the only acceptable units put all the functions of a smartphone in your ear. Personally - I use my headset to talk to people. This headset does that - and it does it well.In addition to making conversations simple - it has the A2DP functions - so navigation is clearly heard through your headset, not your speaker on the dash a few feet away from you. It allows me to put my phone in a great spot for navigation, and clear visibility, and still hear directions clearly. Sure A2DP can be used for music, and that's nice, but it's really the connection to a few specific apps that I use it for.Sometimes I get a bit jealous that other headsets have loads of options and store your contacts, but I don't need those. Sometimes I wish I had a headset that read my texts and emails for me - then I remember how many I can get in a day.The Good:* Fit is very comfortable for me without the 'earhook' - though it's good to have as a backup option* The options for charging are fantastic!- the car charger adapter- 'ratcheting' USB connector (for car adapter or computer)- wall plug* Connects/Reconnects quickly* Range is very good* Smaller than expected (much less intrusive than my old Plantronics unit)* Buttons seem well placed and easy to access for me ( though I have fairly large hands)* Battery Life - unsure. I haven't run out yet. Love that it stops charging itself when it's finished* A2DP for easy navigation (even with the windows down)The bad:When I think about it... nothing for me.There are a few subjective things that you may or may not find annoying or pleasing. The fact that it doesn't blink incessantly was initially troublesome. I wasn't sure it was working - turns out it's great, especially at night. I also found the lack of tones for some functions was initially off-putting. Now I realize it's also great. I don't need it to send me a tone - I need to hang up, call someone back, answer a call or whatever it is that I'm asking it to do. I never realized having a unique tone for all of these was annoying until I discovered the only reason I needed them with my old set - was because it so frequently didn't do them.
summary: Does the job well with no surprises or gimmicks.

reviewText: The name of the product is just ridiculous. "Extreme" labels on skateboards, snowboards, and BMX bikes are sensible. On bluetooth earpieces, a whole lot less so.Still, it's not a bad bluetooth earpiece. I found it to be quite comfortable, nicely sized, and easy to use. The noise cancellation was pretty good, but sometimes produced "boomy" artifacts while I was driving. (Maybe from trying to cancel some wind noise when the sunroof was open? Not sure.) This is a big step up in earpieces for me, my previous one was a no name brand item that cost a quarter of the amazon price for this one. If I had paid for the unit, I might be a bit more critical, it isn't cheap, but that's a very subjective matter.
summary: Comfortable and reasonably good noise cancellation

reviewText: I've been using a Plantronics Voyager 510 headset the last few years.  It gets the job done and the sound was always adequate.  I've used other headsets such as various Motorola sets but never found one that gave me enough improvement to justify changing sets.  I had the opportuntiy to give the New Jabra Extreme a try and my first reaction was....who's Jabra!When I got the set I was surprised at how small it is.  My Plantronics is rather bulky and would definitely not win any "best looking" awards.  The Extreme, on the other hand, is very sleek.  after I opened it I immedately hooked it up to the chrager which was a wall plug on one end and a usb on the other.  It comes with several connectors so I beleive it can be charged from your computer as well.After it was charged I began the pairing process with my Iphone.  I decided to NOT read the instructions to see if I could figure it out on my own. I set my phone to serach for new devices and then held the + button on the headset (hey, it worked with my older headset!).  Sure enough, my phone detected it and was then paired.  I did not have to enter a passcode so that seemed a little weird.  I will check on that later when I finally get around to reading the directions!I called a friends on my Iphone using just the phone and taked for a while.  Ended up needing to call him back a bit later and decided to give the headset a try.  It fits very comfortably and looks a lot better than my Plantronics.  When my friend answered, he came through loud and clear on my end.  I asked him how I sounded and he said the same as before.  He could not tell that I was using a headset.  I never got that response with my old headset as people could always tell.We spoke for about 45 minutes and never had a signal issue.  I was moving around my house with my phone on my counter in my kitchen.  The signal remained strong no matter where I was so this has great range.Later, I used it in my car and again, the sound was amazing.  I received a call and easily found the button on the side to answer it.  My old headset was bit more dificult to find and it didn't always work.I have Bluetooth through my built in GPS but this headset actually sounded better to me. I drive a Jeep so, let's just say that it's not the quietest vehicle one could own!  By using the headset with the way the earpiece is designed, it helped cover up the loudeness of my Jeep.Overall I am very happy with this headset.  My only concern is the size.  Due to its small size, special care will be required not to lose it!

Update 3/5/2010:There *is* a little lag, but nothing like what I had on my old blue tooth when I am listening to the navigation commands on my phone, and so little that I hadn't noticed it when I first tried it out. Audio is good. It connects and disconnects very quickly. The buttons are easy to use. Nobody has complained about hearing an echo. The microphone is pretty strong though, and outside noise is readily apparent to the person on the other end. Also, because of the outside noise, it is sometimes impossible for me to use the voice commands on my phone. The headset is comfortable but just does not feel secure and I always feel like I have to adjust it to hear better. It has NOT come off or fallen off, bit it just feels like it might. I would like to have had the chance to have a smaller ear bud piece that could be used with the earloop, I think that would have made all the difference. If I could I *might* drop it to 3.5 stars, but no way can I justify 3 stars so I left my star rating as is. I am still happy to have it and enjoy using it, but the honeymoon's over.I just got the Jabra EXTREME and I love it. Let me tell you, pairing it was no problem. Changing the attachment to better fit on my ear was easy. It came charged and ready to use. Instruction booklet is short and sweet and easy to use! It is not the most comfortable headset, however, that is really the only negative, and that is why I did not give it 5 stars....but this is easily 4.5 stars. I love all that comes with this, USB charger, car charger, AND wall charger. Some are not happy with the short cord of the AC charger, however, I like it, as it keeps it close by and less likely to be stepped on or otherwise damaged. The sound quality is excellent and there is no lag. I have a Dare and with my old Plantronics, there was a lag that would make me miss the first word the phone would say. This was EXTREMELY  bad when using the navigationi function! No such problem with the Jabra. Also, I should note that nobody has complained of an echo while I used this. Again, this was a problem with my Plantronics. I do wish there were different sized ear buds that came with the unit that worked with the over-the-ear attachment. There are two different size attachments for over the ear, as well as two different sized buds that fit into the ear (I don't feel they would hold as well). So far, I am VERY happy with this!
summary: Loving it!....Updated after some more use.

reviewText: Manufacturers are really getting hung up on the word "Extreme" these days.  Electronics products seem to be plagued with this word the most, as everyone wants people to think their product is one step above excellence.  Well Jabra makes some really impressive headsets, this product included, but I have yet to find one Bluetooth headset that is even close to being worthy of the word "EXTREME!"With that being said, I have been using the Jabra EXTREME Bluetooth Headset now for almost a month and I can honestly say that it is one solid performer.  Sound quality (incoming) is pretty good, although not the greatest, and people who have called me claim that my voice sounds very crisp and clear.  However, they also claim that they can still hear a fair amount of background noise.  In fact, one caller described the noise as being rather "focused," as if certain sounds were muted but other sounds were being amplified.  So for noise cancelling I would say it is on par or slightly better than some of the other dual mic., noise cancelling headsets that I have tested from Motorola and Plantronics.  I do not consider slightly better as being "Extreme."The one thing I have never really liked about many headsets out there is the ear-gels they use for holding them in your ear.  I realize that fit and feel are a matter of preference, but I find that I must fidget with them way too much to get them in my ear properly.  Meanwhile I might be driving down the road and spending way too much time playing around with my headset.  If they made a type that fit in your ear, in a similar fashion to ear bud style music headphones, I think I would be far happier.  But for now my favorite design is the kind that sits over my ear instead of in the ear.  That way I can pop the headset on and off in seconds, without any fiddling around.  But again, this is strictly a matter of personal preference.  As far as how good the Jabra Extreme feels, I can only say that it is extremely light, very small, and the ear-gels are on par with just about all other Jabra headsets to date.  I think the ear hook should be flared out just a bit on the end, so that you don't poke your ear with it when putting it on.So overall I would break down my rating of this device as follows:Visual Appeal  =  4-starsFit & Feel  =  3-starsNoise Cancelation  =  4-starsSound Quality  =  4-starsControls / Ease of Use  =  3-starsWireless Communication (between headset and phone)  =  4-starsI would say the Jabra EXTREME Bluetooth Headset is a solid 4-star device, which puts it above average in my book.  But the only that I would consider "extreme" about this headset is the teeny size of the control buttons.  I can barely feel them when trying to adjust the volume.  I do recommend this headset, as I feel it is a quality built device that is a step above most other headsets in this price range.  However, I think Jabra, as well as every other manufacturer out there, should not just throw around the word `extreme' so loosely.  I they can produce a product that is truly excellent in nearly every manner, then by all means call it Extreme.  Eventually the word `extreme' will mean nothing to consumers, as we will eventually define the word, mentally, as "better than average."

I love this  gadget! It is comfortable enough to wear for long periods of time and the sound quality is great. It doesn't pick up excessive amounts of background noise. When I would wear it while outside, noone complained about the noise or the wind which was unfortunately blowing like crazy at times. My cell phone alone always picks up the wind and the person on the other end can hear it, but this headset seemed to eliminate all of that. It does feel a little weird at first while wearing it, but I wasn't used to wearing something like this. I quickly got used to it and have no complaints. It was not irritating or heavy or anything. It stayed in place even while doing housework and other chores and generally being active/physical. It didn't make my ear sore or uncomfortable and I could just go about my business and gab away. The charge lasts pretty long too, which is nice because I tend to have really long conversations lol. I love that it came with a car charger. This is hands down one of my favorite gadgets now!

The package includes a lot of accessories, and they are all well packaged.The headset is very comfortable and includes a variety of ear hooks and ear pads.  I have used a Jawbone headset in the past and this one is lighter and more comfortable.Charging is easy to do with the THREE included chargers.  First there is a wall charger, the cord is a bit short, but works well.  Second in a car charger, I don't use this one much, but its nice to have in the car just in case.  Third is a USB charger, I use this one the most because I plug my phone into my laptop to sync at night anyways.  The charging port is a micro USB port, and it works with ALL the micro USB chargers I have in my house.Pairing it with my iPhone was easy, just like any other headset.  Call quality is mid-range, and you get some of the clipping that always comes along with noise suppression.I've also paired it to my laptop and used it for Skype chats and web conferences for work.  Just as easy to pair, and similar voice quality.Overall it is worth the price and feels well built.

After an extensive search for the best headset for my husband to use in noisy conditions (delivery truck), we finally found the Jawbone Prime, which is perfect for him.My situation is more typical, I just needed something that would sound decent with regular car background noise for the occasional on-the-road phone call.Not willing to spend another $100+ for the Jawbone, I was happy to see this tiny Jabra Extreme.After spending a few weeks with it these are my conclusions:Good:+ Ultra-compact design: fits anywhere.+ Includes car charger: Most require you to purchase this separately. Charger style is also nice and small.+ Real on/off switch: No wondering and waiting to see the light to be sure the unit is powered down.+ Pairs quickly and easily with my Motorola W385 and works with the phone's voice recognition.+ Fits my ear comfortably. I have small ears, and the smaller in-ear loop is so comfortable, I forget I'm wearing it.+ Sound quality on my end is good, and loud enough in the car even at 1/2 volume.Bad:- Microphone requires very loud speaking voice for the other party to hear you.- Tinny, annoying-sounding voice quality your poor callers have to deal with.- Didn't fit my husband's ear, no matter what configuration he tried.----------In the end, no matter how nice the features are on a bluetooth headset, it all comes down to what it sounds like - to you and the person you're calling - and this headset fails at both.

I have used a number of Bluetooth headsets in the past (Motorola H700, LG HBM-730, Jabra BT-350, Plantronics Explorer 320, Motorola HS850, and Jabra BT-250), but I had larger given them up in favor of myMotorola T305 Bluetooth Portable Car Speaker(see my review).  However, Bluetooth headsets have come a long way in the last two and a half years so I decided that it was worth having a look at the Jabra EXTREME.  I base my evaluation of the Jabra EXTREME on the following criteria:  pairing, sound quality, ease of use, comfort, and extras.Pairing:  This is an area that headset makers (and Bluetooth device makers in general) have improved over the years.  After completing the initial charge the headset automatically goes into pairing mode when turned on as indicated by the purple/blue sequence of the indicator light.  All I had to do was have myBlackBerry Curve 8330 Phone, Silver (Verizon Wireless)(see my review) search for new Bluetooth devices.  It found the Jabra EXTREME without issue, and the two were paired after punching in the standard "0000" code.Sound Quality:  I had pretty high expectations for the EXTREME based on the product description.  However, I didn't find it to be substantially better than my prior Jabra headsets or my Motorola speakerphone.  On my end, callers sounded as clear as they do when not using a headset.  This is not groundbreaking though.  Unfortunately and to my disappointment callers reported that the EXTREME did not sound substantially different than my prior Bluetooth devices.  It seems that it is still a mystery for device makers to create a transparent experience for callers on the other end.  My wife reported the usual cut-in cut-out crackling as I would begin to and finish talking.  I would have expected more based on both the midrange price point and the technological advancements.Ease of Use:  This was the area where I noticed the most progress over prior Jabra devices.  Jabra has realized that a separate power button is a necessity.  I never liked having to hold down the multi-function button for an extended period to power devices on and off.  I would either fail to turn the device on or wind up redialing the last number called rather than turning it off.  The multi-function button is also more tactile in being both smaller yet more pronounced in the amount it is raised from the surface.  The one area users may have trouble with is the volume buttons.  These are fairly small, and users with bigger fingers could find them hard to operate.  However, I found the default volume to be sufficient for my liking so this was a non-issue.  Your mileage may vary.  One final note, the included instruction manual is quite brief.  While it is sufficient for getting started, users may have to go online to get the detailed manual if they run into any problems.  This is a cost saving measure, but it may frustrate Bluetooth neophytes.Comfort:  Jabra has gone out of their way to accommodate a variety of users by including two different sized earhooks along with left and right eargels designed for "hookless" use.  While the variety is thoughtful, the earhooks are a pretty major failure.  Their makeup is similar to the sock hangers used to hang up a pair of dress socks in a department store.  However, the earhooks may actually be less flexible than the sock hangers.  Unless one of these earhooks happens to fit the shape of your ear perfectly, you are not likely to find the earhook a viable option.  At this point I was rather concerned as I had never used a headset without an earhook.  So I changed out the default eargel for the right eargel and situated the EXTREME in my right ear.  I was pleased that it fit fairly comfortably and securely.  I shook my head up and down as well as left and right, but the headset never hinted at falling out.  I even jumped up and down to try to force it loose, but it didn't budge.  I have found this manner of wearing to be sufficiently comfortable during commutes of 30-60 minutes.  However, I left it in for a little over two hours when working from home one morning, and I exceeded the limits of comfort.  While it didn't bother me prior, my ear was quite sore once I removed the headset.  It did not linger, and two hours might be beyond the reasonable amount of time to expect to wear a headset in comfort anyway.Extras:  This is another area where Jabra was quite thoughtful.  In addition to the variety of wearing options, Jabra has included both wall and car chargers for the EXTREME.  The car charger is actually in two pieces with a USB connector.  This allows for the adapter to also be used in a PC USB port.  Given the midrange pricing of the EXTREME, users will expect some level of extras, and it is good that Jabra included these.Conclusion:  The Jabra EXTREME is a competent Bluetooth headset, but it doesn't quite set itself apart as much as its description might suggest.  If you are already happy with another Bluetooth headset, you will be better served waiting until it is time for a replacement.  Users in the market for a new headset will find that the EXTREME performs sufficient for inclusion in the midrange class of headsets.  If you have demanding requirements for sound quality, you may be better off going into the upper tier of headsets from other manufacturers such as Jawbone.  Please feel free to ask questions in the comments section below.
summary: Good Choice In Midrange Priced Headsets

reviewText: Summary: My three favorite BT headsets are the Plantronics Voyager ProPlantronics Voyager PRO Bluetooth Headset, Aliph Jawbone (original version) and now the Jabra Extreme. All of them have their pluses and minuses, but I think i would give the slight nod to the Jabra at this point due to its ease of use.Pros:* Rapid paring and quick response to all controls. It's quick enough that I never find myself waiting for it to connect, disconnect, turn on/off, etc. Pairing with my Blackberry Tour (Verizon) and Macbook Pro (15.4", OSX 10.5.8) went without a hitch of any kind. With multiple device connection, I can use my cell and VOIP at the same time. Very cool!* A "real" on/off switch. It's tiny, but the unit has a small slider switch with positive stops for on/off. I like this a lot better than units that need you to hold a button down for a certain length of time to turn on/off or signal pairing. The JE just turns on and off. Seems like a small thing, but it's really big to me, especially since I am red/green color blind.* Range is good. I didn't test it to disconnect, but I could go to the next room in my house (about 20' and a wall) away from my BB and maintain connection.* Small and decent looking. Fit and finish are great and the packaging makes it all seem special. Feels high quality.* The buttons are clearly labeled. I can also actually hit them with my nominally size fingertips.* The best power/charger accessories I have seen for a BT headset. The units comes with a tiny USB converter plug that has a full sized USB on one end and a micro-USB on the other. You can then plug this into the supplied car charger, which has a USB plug on the end, or plug it into your PC. Very cool. One reviewer mentioned that the AC cord is too short, but for my setup it was about right because I have a 12 plug power bar running across the top back of my desk (not too stylish, but effective), and a long cord just gets in the way. Altogether, I thought this was all well thought out and well done, especially at the price.* The aforementioned charger system plugs into Micro USB, which is becoming very common and thus makes it a non-disaster if you forget the charger.* The sound is on par with my other high end headsets at half the price. I have found, as another reviewer did, that listening to single ear music is OK, and the sound from the JE is defiinitely "Better than nothing" when it comes down to waiting in lines, etc.* Comfort is OK, probably a solid "good".Cons* My Voyager Pro is more comfotable. For me, the "around the ear" loops of the JE do not work well. My best combo is the in-ear rubber gel with no ear hook. Definitely need to try all the combos to get a good one.* The instruction manual is just a little bit too sparse for comfort. For instance, it doesn't detail how to change the ear gels. I figured it out, but took longer than I should since it was not apparent that the ear gels just peel off instead of having an interlock and twist like the Jawbone or the PVP. Also, the manual was written by someone who had English as a second or third language. This doesn't keep the experienced user from succeeding, but it might mean that some of us may not get to all the neat features right away, or ever. I think they could have spared a couple more pages of explanation for multiple pairing, use with a PC, and the procedure for changing the earpiece. Since they already had pictures in the manual, a couple more sentences is all that is needed.* The aforementioned beloved power slider switch does not have a label to tell you which dicrection is on or off. Seems like a screwy omission. You figure it out quickly, but it did mess me up the first couple times out since "down" is on and "up" is off. On/Off or "0" "1", please.ConclusionI like it and it has become my new primary headset over the Voyager Pro and the Jawbone original. Smaller, faster, but slightly less comfortable, it's my new favorite.
summary: Tied for my favorite BT headset

reviewText: I tried several headsets before which some were good and most were useless. This is my first experience with Jabra and I chose the extreme because it can hold two Phones simultaneously. Simply this device is excellent with all aspects.

If you look closely under a lens the tiny writings on the device reveals that this isJabra BT 530 Bluetooth Headsetin disguise.The JABRA Extreme has nice industrial look and blends in well in my ear, the sound quality is pretty good and paring was very easy with myNokia 6085 ATT Cell PhoneComes in a display plastic box which is attractive looking but beware that it is hard to get the headset out unless you push a plastic tab see the pictures that I have posted on Amazon to give you an idea of what to expect.The Jabra Extreme has typical features like hands free answering calls of course that is what the headset is supposed to do :-), also ending, and rejecting calls, voice dialing support, last number redial, call waiting support, placing a call on hold, It also has a couple of advanced features like multipoint technology, which is the capability to connect the headset with two different devices, and A2DP compatibility, which allows for streaming music.I have music files on my Nokia 6085 and as soon as the paring is done with the headset the music starts to play automatically. If a call comes in the music is interrupted and I was able to accept calls and once the call is complete the music starts to play back again! - Cool!The call quality is pretty good but on the louder side, I tried it in a busy street intersection and I was able to hear things clearly, the others reported that my voice is coming thru' loud and clear. The usage of Jabra in my old noisy car proved good use of the noise cancellation technology, Even though the caller on the other side was able to distinguish that I was taking inside my car they had no problem in hearing my voice - Good!PROS:[+] Nice looking tiny Bluetooth headset[+] Car Charger included which is a bonus![+] Very good noise isolation[+] Mono Music streaming is possible.[+] Dedicated ON/OFF switch to save battery![+] Comparatively cheaper with loaded featuresCONS:[-] Volume is too loud even when turned down to minimum[-] Music quality is not that great
Great sound, long battery life, good range, very comfortable.  As long as under 30 bucks, a good value in a crowded field of junky options.  Pairs without fail.

No body could hear me or understand what I was saying.  That is using the Jabra in my office at home with no background noise.  It went right back to Amazon.  Save for time and money.  I like the Plantronics Margue 2. Crystal clear on both ends
This product did not come in retail packaging but it is what I wanted, it also came with the skype software which id nice to have.

I really like this headset.  I'm finding sound quality to be excellent, both for me and for folks I'm talking to.  My friends are surprised to find I'm talking through a headset when I use it.I love the on/off switch.  The switch makes it so easy for me to see when it's on and when it's turned off.  I have several headsets and on a couple of them, I think I've turned it off, but no...it thinks I want to send my cell phone a voice command.  That annoyance had been eliminated with the Jabra Extreme.The size is nice, too.  I like that it doesn't touch my face at all and stays right by my ear.One problem, though: I can't get it in my ear quickly no matter how many times I've tried.  I struggle every time, trying to get it in my ear and to have the little over-the-ear piece fit right.  Grrrrr....  I certainly can't do it on the fly and one handed.  I need to totally stop what I'm doing, and fit this thing with two hands.  Ok, maybe it's just me and I'm not coordinated enough.  But, I don't have any problems with myPlantronics Voyager 510 Bluetooth Headset.  I can take the Plantronics on and off quickly and easily and with one hand!Over all though, I really like this headset.  Once it's in my ear, it stays put and works great.

Hard to be unimpressed by the packaging, love it or hate it- they say you only get one chance to make a first impression- and since, to me at least, most diminutive Bluetooth headsets look pretty mush alike at a distance, the Jabra is presented like a museum piece- held up for display on a clear plastic pedestal, and enclosed in a clear plastic display case. All that was missing were pin spots, it must certainly stand out on a retail shelf. But I must add- do we need the plastic already? Once it's out of the box, I am seriously not going to put it back on display every night. How about a postpaid recycling envelope?Included in the package is the AC charger, as well as a 12v automotive adapter- I like this part- it plugs directly into the lighter socket, an adjustable elbow then connects to it and allows the headset to be plugged in to standby via a standard micro-USB charging connector. It's a little awkward to try to get it off and in your ear in time to catch a call, but it's a great way to keep it charged and handy. The AC adapter has a one foot cord, which also seems to be a love/hate thing. I love it; most of the time I charge on a bathroom counter so it's perfect.The set comes with both over-the-ear hooks or inserts for in-ear, the unit is light enough to not require very much external support. They refer to them as "Ultimate-fit ear gels" but to my eyes (and ear), they're just a flexible rubber or silicon cap.I do not like driving with any more distractions than already available and am not inclined (or use the phone enough) to keep the thing on all the time- so it is important to be able to have it in place and comfortable quickly- especially while wearing glasses. The Jabra is great at this, although using one of the in-ear pieces that have a small hook, it is a little more difficult to insert, with a chance you will press one of the controls. I am sure with time this can be forgotten. It's also small enough that if you did choose to leave it in, and have even moderately long hair, it's barely visible.Controls are simple and easy to access, effective, virtually no learning curve. The power switch is a raised slider and always easy to find and hit should the need arise.I have to say I am under-impressed by the "dual microphone noise canceling" as advertised, the quality is great but certainly, at least as I have so far used it, not exceptional. I should add: field testing an audio device of any kind is highly subjective and there are just too many variables to come to any sort of controlled conclusion. But recipients of calls made did not find anything worthy of note in the quality.Using my older Nokia phone, the instructions mention voice activation can be operated from the answer/end button, but this was not the case for my phone.The manual  is bare bones, but you don't really need much more. They state in the book that "online user manuals" can be found at their website, the Jabra website is very accessible and any additional information you seek may be found there. But, do not expect a detailed downloadable PDF- the information is there but in a more casual way. This device is so simple to operate, I can't really see how much more information you'd need .I checked out their tutorial about pairing to see if my phone would even work with it- and discovered that my previous phone, RIP, was also listed as compatible- when in fact it had no Bluetooth capability. So, if you use that feature to check your phone, be careful- although I doubt anyone these days would purchase a unit like this unless they already knew it would work.

I had a BT530 Jabra for a year worked GREAT! Lost it and use this to replace...after two months started getting noisy. Jabra will replace but wonder like cars and everything made in China if quality has gone down.

Jabra Extreme is very low profile and good looking headset with some great qualities, strongest being very good noise cancellation. I tried it with iPod Touch 2G, iMac & Motorola Droid. It's PROS & CONS are as follows.PROS1. Excellent noise suppression: the party at other end could not hear loud blaring music or wind noise.2. Low profile.3. Nice finish and construction quality.4. Good ergonomics with well placed controls.5. Can pair 8 devices to this headset, and connects to 2 simultaneously.6. Very clear sound.7. Easy to pair: I paired with Motorola Droid, iPod Touch 2G and iMac without any hitch.8. Ubiquitous mini USB charger, and the headset comes with both car and wall charger.9. Automatic adjustment of volume.10. Comes with two ear gels (one for each ear) and ear hooks.11. Long lasting battery charge.12. Range of about 20 feet.13. You can receive and reject calls. I have not tried voice dialing.14. Works flawlessly with Skype on iMac (but not on iPod Touch).15. Comes with wall and car charger although micro USB cable is very short. But retractable micro USB cables are not very expensiveAmzer Micro USB Retractable Data Cable (Black).CONS1.  Sometimes it does not connect automatically on turning it on, with Droid or iPod Touch and I have to go into Bluetooth settings to establish the connection. This happens about 20-30% of time and for me is the biggest glitch in this headset.2.  Relatively expensive because you can get Bluetooth headsetsMotorola H270 Bluetooth HeadsetandMotorol H500 Bluetooth Headset (Silver) [Amazon Frustration-Free Packaging] for about twenty bucks. And you can get stereo New Samsung  WEP870 Mono + Stereo BT Headset for thirty five bucks.3.  Cannot fast forward or skip music tracks. This headset is made mainly for the cell phones. Although you can use it with MP3 players like iPod touch, it lacks the music navigation capabilities found in many stereo A2DP headsets/headphones.4. Takes a minute or two to fit it in the ear, but very comfortable once it is placed. After a while, you forget that you are wearing headset.5. Comes with big clear plastic storage box, what is needed is really a small pocketable storage bag.6. There are some other glitches and I am not sure who is at fault there, the headsets or the gadget or app software. For example it works great with Motorola Droid phone part but not the Music app that comes with the phone, an app called Recorder (just the microphone) and sometimes not even with Listen, the Google podcast app. Similarly with iPod Touch: works fabulously with music and podcasts but the Jabra Extreme microphone does not work with Skype & Recorder apps. So far, I have been unsuccessful in fixing these snags by playing around with settings.7. The earhooks keep falling off and are easy to loose. A pack extra gels and hooks is avilable only at the JABRA website for ten bucks with ten buck shipping!Except for these glitches, this is one of the best Bluetooth headsets I have used when it comes to noise cancellation. Although there are other less expensive Blutooth headsets, I am not sure if they have such good noise suppression and clarity of sound that thisJabra EXTREME Bluetooth Headsethas.
summary: Excellent Noise Suppression but Spontaneous Reconnection Glitch & Expensive

reviewText: I'm no fan of Bluetooth headsets - but I've managed to become the kind of person that only uses my headset when I need it, so you won't find me walking through the mall or airport with my headset on, waiting for a call.The Jabra EXTREME has a lot to live up to, especially with its name and list of features. Thankfully it delivers - sound quality on both ends of the call is exceptional. The noise blocking features really do cancel out quite a lot of background noise, without reducing call quality too much.One of the best parts of this headset is the included assortment of accessories. Included in the box is a car charger, USB adapter, wall adapter and some replacement ear hooks.This headset makes it an easy choice to skip those $100 "fashion headsets" and go for something reliable and affordable - good job Jabra!
summary: Not only an impressive headset - but also an impressive array of included accessories

reviewText: This headset's noise canceling ability and its unobtrusive design make it worth the purchase.First, in testing out the noise canceling capability, I put this device to the ultimate test: I called my mother... in the car... with the radio on... and the window down.  No problem whatsoever.  Mom heard me loud and clear and I spent most of the call trying to convince her that I was using a headset.  She was convinced I had my phone right up to my face.  Please note, at no time did I have to talk above an average voice.  In fact, I kept talking softer and softer, trying to test the limits of the device, but not once did she have an issue hearing me.  This has been the case with other calls I've made using this headset.  So far, I haven't found a condition where my voice has been drowned out by outside noise.It should also be said that my voice is coming through with quality, and on the receiving end, I can hear those I'm talking to without any issues.  Just as importantly, while using this device when I have other people in the car with me, I have found that they cannot overhear any part of the persons comments coming through over the line.  In fact, when I'm using this headset and have the car radio on, the other people in the car can't really hear what I'm saying either (because I'm able to talk at a reasonably low volume without losing quality), so I can virtually have a private conversation and not bother those around me.Second, the unobtrusive design of this device should be noted.  For whatever reason, I'm adverse to big or flashy headsets, and so this device is near perfect for me.  It's extremely light and small.  It fits in my ear securely, and nothing I do is going to shake it out.  Just as nice, it comes out of my ear easily when I want to take it out.  It's small enough and sleek enough to where not only do I not feel self-conscious wearing it, but I usually forget I have it in.  I have not found any major discomfort while wearing it.  With that said, I have not worn it for any stretch over 30 minutes, and I sometimes have experienced a few seconds of discomfort immediately after taking it out.  I have this issue with other devices, so this may be more a quirk with me than a knock on the headset.As a final note on the design, I appreciate the intuitive layout of the buttons.  Each one gives you a definite "click" when you press it and they are laid out in such a way where you always know which one you are pressing.  These are very helpful features when you have a device in your ear that you are trying to adjust on the go.If I have any complaints about this headset, they are minor.  For instance, why did they include a wall charger that has a ridiculously short cord?  It's honestly an eight or ten inch cord at most, but, like I said, this is a minor complaint.  Certainly, I did not find any reason to dock this device a star.  Considering the sound quality and sleek design offered by this headset, it's a great option at a fair price.

There are some things I really like about this bluetooth headset, but unfortunately there are also some things I don't like.First, the good.  It is fairly comfortable and comes with two sizes of ear loops.  I had to replace the smaller loop with the larger loop, and then it fit quite well.  There is also an option to just stick it directly in your ear, with no loop, but I did not try that option.  I previously had a larger Motorola headset, and I like the smaller size of this Jabra.One of my complaints with the Motorola was that it was too hard to hear, even with the volume at max.  This one has a much better speaker, and I found both the volume and quality of the sound from the other person to be excellent.  Unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the quality of my voice to the other person, but I'll get to that.I also liked that it was very easy to pair with my iPhone, as the headset goes into automatic-pairing mode the first time you turn it on.  You just ask the iPhone to find it, and voila!When you first put this headset on and start using it, it seems fantastic.But then I did a test of my voice quality by leaving myself several voice mail messages and then playing them back.  I like doing this since it lets me hear my voice from the headset immediately after my voice from the greeting, so it's easy to compare.  This test failed miserably.  Even though I was speaking loudly into the headset, my voice played back to me sounded like I was in a room speaking into a speaker phone and far away from that speaker phone.  It was tinny and hard to hear.  If the caller on the other end doesn't have good volume on his/her end, he/she may not be able to hear you.  On the other hand, it's not much worse than speaking into a Bluetooth hands free car kit, but I expect better from an ear-mounted unit than from my car's built-in mic.My other complaints are minor compared to the quality and volume of how other callers hear me.First, the length of the included power cord is quite humorous.  To give you an idea of how short it is, I plugged it into a household wall outlet, and the cord is so short, that the headset doesn't even hit the floor when hanging down from the outlet!  Imagine if you need to charge this via an outlet in a typical office, you will have to have the headset dangling from an outlet under your desk!  Hopefully, you have an outlet up on our desk.The good news, however, is that it includes a USB adapter, so you can simply charge it from your computer instead.  Still, I got a laugh out of the world's shortest power cord.  Not sure what they were thinking.If you care about the environment, you will be alarmed at the product's packaging.  It is irresponsibly packaged inside a large, clear hard-plastic case that will never break down.  When you buy this headset, you are sticking a large plastic casing into a landfill.  I had no idea that companies were still using this type of packaging in the 21st century.Bottom line is I still haven't found a Bluetooth headset that provides as good of quality as using the iPhone's wired earbuds.  And that's a shame, since it would be great to ditch the wires.This one provides you with good audio, but not the other way around to your caller.
summary: Good audio for you, bad for the other person

reviewText: Sure there are a million bluetooth headsets in the market today and Jabra makes quite a few of them.  However, they have been in the business long enough to know how to make a good headset with noise cancellation.  Now I cannot give this 5 stars because the noise cancellation is not as great as the product would lead you to believe....it is however comparable to the others in the market.I have used this headset with the iPhone 3gS and a Blackberry Bold 9700.  It works great on both of my phones and calls while driving with the windows open or from a noisy stadium have all been clear and loud with the other end saying that they could barely hear the noise.Its a great headset and a great value as compared to other units similar to it.  4/5 for me...
summary: Jabra is the way to go for great Sound quality....

reviewText: I had low expectations of this headset. Every time I have tried to use a headset, the person on the other end complains that they can't hear me as well, and I have to switch back to my phone. With this headset, they could tell that I was using one, but they could hear me loud and clear. It's very comfortable for me as it is, but it comes with a couple of different clips to adjust the fit if you need. The volume was high enough for my slight hearing loss, but easily adjustable for lower levels for those who need it. It's light weight and after a few minutes I forget I have it on.The cord for the wall charger seems awfully short; I would rather not leave the headset on the floor while charging. However, it comes with a car charger AND an attachment to charge through any USB port on a computer! I love that I can put the USB charger in my purse, go anywhere, and not worry about losing power because I can charge it through my netbook or my computer at work. It was very easy to set up & connect to mySamsung Rant. When a call comes in, all I have to do is tap the button on the side of the headset, and when I dial out, it automatically connects.With so many other headset choices out there, it's hard to decide what to get. I highly recommend this headset for ease of use, EXCELLENT quality of sound and the three compact charging options included in the package. I am very pleased with it and I think you will be as well.

It is a great headset automatically pairs with my Playstion 3! It also has A2DP which means you can listen to music through these and not all bluetooths have this feature. Only setback is it does not charge while your talking on the phone. So great bluetooth but not being able to charge while you talk a major flaw in design.

I was very impressed with this headset.  I've had two Plantronics that I liked, but wanted something less bulky.  The "Ultimate-fit eargels" do fit great.  I can shake my head violently and it does't come out.  I've also worn it for several hours without fatigue.  I've never had voice clarity issues or echo.  I find the volume to be acceptable.  The volume buttons aren't the easiest to use when in your ear, but I always have it on high anyways.  I like that it charges via USB micro, so I can charge my phone and headset with the same chargers.  Battery life has never been an issue and it recharges really fast.  Unquestionably worthy of 5 stars.

This headset launched at 2010 CES.  Improvements are great.  I had a few older Jabra sets, including wired pieces, and this one is by far the best and most comfortable.  Features noise cancellation, which works well.I'm using it when holding bridge conference calls from home.  I don't have a wire home phone and use my iPhone for conferences.  I also like to get up and walk around, and so far I have had no complaints from callers and bridge attendees.  They hear my and I hear them... a joy!Fairly lightweight, with good ear balance.  I'm usually very picky about any sets hanging on my ear, but this one is pretty comfortable.  There's two ear hooks and ear gels.  I usually go to large hook and small gel. There's a built-in light and two volume buttons, which are pretty small, but usable.  Tapping either button gives you battery life status.Battery life is really good, I can average 3-4 calls a day, each about 45min to 1 hour each.
summary: Great Battery Life, Works EXTREMEly Well during Bridge Conference Calls when paired with iPhone 3G

reviewText: This here Bluetooth is among the best that I've owned to use with my cellphone.  And I've owned plenty of them (see my reviews on Plantronics, Motorola, etc.)The negative I'll get out of the way first as one is totally absurd to me (as to why a company would do the first) is the length of the charging cord.  From the actual AC charger that plugs into the wall to the adapter which plugs into the Bluetooth the cord is around six inches!!!  So most likely you'll need an extension cord and/or long power strip.  Now if you have an outlet in an open area then this is not a problem.The last I'll call a negative/positive, is the size of the Bluetooth itself.  The size is so small (and it's powerful in picking up your voice and battery life), but with that comes it being difficult to touch the right buttons, especially if you have large fingers or are wearing it and want to turn the volume down/up.Now keep in mind this is a VERY small bluetooth headset.  Lightweight.  Small so that it's easy loose if you're not careful.  And if you have puffy cheeks the bluetooth will not hit your cheeks and muffle the sound.  So small that many will not notice you are wearing it as it does not protrude along the side of your face.The over the ear part is a small wire, and that's great if you wear glasses as it does not bother the stem of the glasses.  However the first few times you wear it over the ear it'll be difficult to put on and feel strange.  However that feeling goes away after a few times.  And it's very easy to change the wire for Left/Right ear. It comes fit for the right ear and I like wearing them on my left ear.And there is a in ear piece that helps the speaker stay in your ear. With both wire behind the wear and the in ear piece (you don't notice this) you have a true fit bluetooth that does not wiggle around as you move.Pairing was easy.  The on/off button bluetooth is a simple slide up/down.  Range of the bluetooth is a good 20 feet depending on conditions (if you have walls in between or floors or are in an open area, etc.  Battery life is among the best I've seen.Sound quality is very clear.  And callers can hear me clear.Charging has a color system and when it turns green on the headset it's fully charged.  Red means it needs to be charged. Yellowish color means it's in between full/empty.There is also an extra wire for behind the ear.  Extra ear piece.  And a DC car charger.  Having a small bag would of been nice to include, but I'm sure everyone could find something or purchase a small bag to keep it in.Even with the small wire (I can't understand why Jabra would give such a small wire)I'm giving this full stars.  Jabra has a real nice bluetooth here!And again, if you wear glasses or sunglasses, then you will be very happy with this bluetooth as the behind the ear piece is very small and does not bother the stem of your glasses.

I have used many, many iphone covers.  Got this one for my new 3GS.  Yes, it fits perfectly.1.  The material is very high quality.  It's shinny and translucent, but at the same time feels durable.  It gives your iphone a beautiful red gloss.2.  A great fit.  All the buttons line up.  Does not make your phone look bulky.3.  A great price from Amazon.4.  If you have the white iphone, you have to go for the translucent colors.

reviewText: This case is perfect - fit is great & great protection.  Will probably buy in another color.  Is see-thru though - not solid like it looks, but that makes it look cool too.

I've received more positive feedback from friends about this iPhone "skin" then any other case, cover or skin I've previously owned. The rubber type material is very high quality, nicely thin enough to not feel bulky, and does a good job of fitting properly and staying in place once it's on the phone.  The only reason I rated it 4 instead of 5 is that I think it's priced a bit above it's worth. I'd easily recommend this product at $19.99 or so, but $25 is a bit high in my opinion. It's not an amazing protection to the phone as it's on the thinner side, so I think the price your'e paying is because it's uniquely transparent yet not hard plastic.Because this is very rubbery, I think that the case will probably last a long time. When hitting a hard surface it will more likely bounce rather than crack like a hard plastic case. It is more difficult to slip in and out of my jeans pocket because it is a bit rubbery, but on the upside you won't lose grip of your phone with this case, ever.
summary: Translucent colored rubber, good protection, great style!

reviewText: Nice and sleek but a bit slippery. I would not buy it again but then I am very hard to please.

What I really didn't like about this case was 1) the way it recesses the controls so they are harder to push, and 2) the difficulty with which the case goes on and off the phone. I prefer the Elago case -- easier controls and easier to put on and remove, but not as much protection as this. Very thin cases such as this and the Elago are for keeping a good grip on a slippery phone, not protecting it in a fall.
summary: An OK case but I'd pick another one

reviewText: This covers a little bit less than I realized, but it does cover the essential parts of the phone, and it is thin, so it doesn't add any extra bulk.  It does the job.

I knew before I purchased this that the SHIELD case wouldn't provide much protection for the front of the phone, but I didn't realize how much of the front silver lining of the phone was left uncovered. I changed my case from the iCase Slider to this in the morning, and five hours later I tripped with my phone in my hand and scratched up the bottom corner of the phone. There's a big scratch along the edge of my phone now, because the SHIELD left so much unprotected, and unfortunately my sleek new iPhone is now a scratched up iPhone.I guess for the much more careful, this is a fine case to buy. It covers most of the back and provides a firmer grasp on the phone when you're using it. For me, it always feels like the phone is going to slip right out of my hand when I don't have a case or cover on it, so this was a good case in that aspect since it doesn't add any bulk. However, don't count on much protection for your phone, even on the back where the Apple logo is exposed -- one wrong move with your car keys in your purse or pocket and you'll end up with a big scratch along the back too.I've since changed my case out to something with more coverage, and I'm happier using that instead.

I have been using this product for my Iphone 3G for almost a month. So far I like it. It seems to be made of good quality material, gives a very good feeling when holding the phone. Easy to take out and put on. I saw another Red color after I bought my black one so I might get that one too.

I had to replace my inCase cover for my iPhone as it had cracked - not pleased, but when I searched for a new case, I found this one. I received it in good order and it is an excellent case. Will it be THE case for me forever? Only time will tell:- very slim design - adds very little bulk to the phone, unlike other cases- snaps right on - no sliding, no multiple parts- great form and fit - feels good in the hand - rubberized material appears to be a good design for the function of the case- I am concerned that the cutouts for the buttons/switches are oversized - not sure why that is- Case does not wrap all the way around like other cases - the silver on the 3G is exposed in places and the case does not cover the top and bottom (in between the corners) of the phone - it DOES cover all corners, so I feel it will be OK - but again, time will tell.Overall I really like it so far. I just hope it will stay that way.

I would be $100 richer if I purchased this cover first. I purchased ivyskins, this and that, plus two others I can't remember the names of before trying this case. This case does the job without costing a mint plus it feels and looks perfect on the iphone.

I love this case for the iPhone. It fits snugly around the edges of the phone. There's no worry of it coming off unexpectedly. This case is thin enough that the phone + case still fits in my holster nicely. The case has a rubberized feel to it that is nice. All of the ports are accessible and best of all is the Apple logo is readily visible.

I just got a new 3GS iphone. This is my 2nd iPhone, the fist being the 2G. For 2G I used Corzip and was going to order a same brand for the new 3GS. However I saw several reviews on the SHIELD and liked the photos.  I am very happy I went with SHIELD. Here is my reasons. 1. It kept my iphone slim. 2. The grip is sticky enough to hold but slippery enough for my pants pockets. 3. It molds onto the iphone perfectly and both side are black, not painted over as in my previous Corzip skin. and 4. the edges are rounded, unlike Corzip.  It's hard to explain but take a look and compare the two and you will understand.  I would highly recommend this to anyone who has the iphone 3GS.Note, this does not come with a screen protector so you will have to purchase a separate item. I know iphone advertised that it's scratch proof and all that but better safe than sorry.

reviewText: This is the perfect iPhone 3G case you are looking. It has- Perfect fit. Fit's snugly without unnecessay covering. The top portion of the phone is fully exposed and the back is well covered.- The black colour of the case is also nice.- The apple logo is shown which enhances your ownership.- The quality if casing is good and will protect the phone.- Finally the looks are just pefect without compromising protection.Just get it, you will love it.

The case fits extremely snug, considering how little it wraps around the top edge of the phone.  Most of the chrome is exposed, so it does not provide protection there.  However, I personally like this because that's part of the look of the iPhone, so why cover it up.  Sure, if you cover it, it won't get scratched, but you don't buy a sports car to keep it in the garage so it doesn't get a rock chip!  If I wanted the chrome covered, I would have purchased a different case.The volume and vibrate buttons are slightly (and I stress slightly) harder to access due to the shield going across both sides of the buttons, but they are also protected from accidental pushing.What I like best about this case is the feel.  It's got a nice grippy texture without being overly rubbery.  It easily slides in and out of my pocket, but allows better grip than a naked iPhone (I was always afraid my phone would slide out of my hand, it's so slippery).  Excellent material.Great case.  With a quality screen protector, I think this will keep my iPhone well protected while still showing of the sleek and eye catching design of the phone.  Highly recommended.

reviewText: I really love this iPhone cover. Just now I got back from a trip and I got compliments from 2 separate people telling me how nice it looked. One even told me that I needed to get a case for my iPhone - this product is so sleek that you can't even tell that the cover is on and is protected. He was so impressed with it when I showed it to him.It's got all the cutouts necessary to give you full access to all the controls, and it even has a very cool circular cutout on the back that enables you to see the Apple logo.It's extremely form-fitting and tight, and incredibly lightweight. I have dropped my phone and nothing was damaged.But, here's the thing - the cover fits around and protects the phone in the back, and on the sides. It does not protect the screen if you should happen to drop the phone on its face. The wrap-around protection does not extend to the front, and it doesn't even come completely flush with the screen.Even so, I still recommended. This is very aesthetically pleasing cover, and it's light and sturdy.  Just don't expect it to safeguard your phone from a direct impact to the screen.
summary: Excellent product - but don't expect protection for the screen

reviewText: I purchased the Blackberry Bold 9000 in hopes of a great smartphone that would work out well with my prepaid phone plan. Well, this phone came in a protected package, no damage at all, worked great upon first time installing my sim card and memory card.  Contacts and all switched right over to the Blackberry from my sims card and I was able to read everything stored on my memory chip. I wanted to learn more about the phone and remembered the tutorial, then I added some free apps to the phone. With all of the adventures that I have taken this phone on I can honestly say no problems at all, great purchase for an awesome price. Very recommendable.

I initially purchased this device in 2008 from AT&T when it just came out and changed 3 of them since that time. First had a problem with trackball after couple of months of use. The other one had dead pixels on the screen. So I am on my third device now.  My primary aim for this device is usage of chat software(IM+), emails and internet browsing (Opera Mini). This is by far is one of the best and user friendly devices I have used. It is not laggy as windows mobile devices, The menus can be accessed quickly with no delays. And especially multitasking (which iphone lacks) is a very nice feature that has been helping me a lot while chatting, making a phone call, and watching a video or listening to the music at the same time. Of course I had to update it with the latest firmware update. Before that, I had some java errors and spontaneous reboots, but not anymore. Since the last update I can confirm that I had NO problems whatsoever. I have few complaints though which in my opinion are minor ones and I can live with them. First is the battery life. If I am not using internet very often it may last a day and a half but when I am browsing with Opera Mini or chatting on IM+ the battery drains very quickly so I have to carry another battery with me. Another thing I would prefer to have is a nice youtube player which I can't find anywhere (I tryed a couple of them). And the youtube that plays with a native browser is just garbage, which is kind of sad because other phones like Iphone and HTC touch pro 2 can play youtube quite nicely. And last but not least is the camera. Outdoors, on the bright light you can get more or less decent pictures but if you will try to shoot a video it will come out as a total crap, pixelated with distorted lighting. And the flash isn't helping much either. Unlike for example with Nokia n97 which takes pretty decent pictures and videos. But like I said these things are minor ones and since this phone is being oriented more for a business user you can't expect to have it all. Especially I like the ability to operate this device with one hand only, which comes in handy in many situations, unlike some other phones with larger keyboards I have tried. Of course another nice feature is a multilanguage support which you can not have in windows mobile phones (e.g. convert device and keyboard interface in spanish, german or other language at no charge) Now I am only expecting the release of OS 5.0 which I will immediately install on my device. So let's see how that goes. I definitely recommend Blackberry Bold for someone who is searching for a device with push email, chatting and light internet use.

I've been using Blackberries since a blackberry was thought to be something you would find in a muffin. The 8800 was the one I was using until I was given the Bold and, up until then, I thought of it as the best Blackberry ever. Then, the Bold came and it is probably safe to state that the Bold is now the last and the best classic Blackberry ever because the Storm, lacking a physical keyboard, probably deserves its own class.When the Bold and the 8800 are placed next to each other, what's striking is the similarities between the 2. The exact same size, similar keyboard, buttons placement, including the now familiar trackball. Even the ports are more or less the same, the same weight. Mine came with its own holster but I could have used the 8800's with the Bold.Then, it's the display. The Bold is what it says it is: bright, clear, vivid. You see it and you now know that it's an evolutionary step up on the ladder. In addition, you get the camera that shoots both pictures and video and the ability to add more memory means that you scan store more video and more music if you want to use your Blackberry as an iPod lite. The operation seems to be a bit faster, the battery life is more or less the same, the quality of the speaker phone is better but, overall, it's your familiar Blackberry, having learned a few new tricks and with a bright face.I am happy with the Bold because I am happy with Blackberries in general. I like the unlimited email and Internet browsing plan, the ability to use Wi-Fi when available and the security it provides. My Blackberry is tied into my company's email environment and it is now very much an extension of my office while I'm away. The Bold, with its high resolution screen and the same solid, functional build is a good tool, now with more 'fun' stuff (camera, video playing) added to it.
summary: The Best and Possibly the Last Classic Blackberry (with a real keyboard)
