reviewText: I've used several brands of Stereo Bluetooth headsets from Jabra to Plantronics to Motorola. I was mostly obsessed with getting ear bud style bluetooth headsets and did not want to give the over the ear ones a try. I thought they would get more sweaty at the gym or cause me to feel uncomfortable with the bulk but I was wrong!  These light weight S305's are fantastic.  The sound is about as good as bluetooth headsets can get. I do 45 minutes to an hour of weight training and 30-40 minutes of cardio in these and I often forget I'm wearing them.With my old ear bud style ones I would constantly have to re-adjust them during my workout. I would have a hard time skipping tracks and adjusting volume because the the buttons were so small and hard to use. With these S305's the button placement is excellent and easy to use and the only time I have to adjust them is when I do incline bench press but even that got easier to deal with after a few workouts.I have taken a few phone calls with these and those sound great too. The other party can hear me clearly and I can hear them clearly. I will say that if you are outside taking a phone call and there is a some wind the other party will hear the wind noise and it can become annoying on longer calls.  This is a minor complaint since I mostly use these for music and if I take a call with them I'm usually at home not outside.Overall I highly recommend these Motorola S305's. The price is excellent at $30-35 and they seem durable. I've been using them for over a month now and I will not go back to earbud style headphones again.QUICK TIP: If you sweat in them DO NOT charge them right away. When you get home let them sit for several hours (or overnight) before you charge them. Charging them after you sweat in them is a great way to fry the battery and burn them out.  The battery life is excellent and you should be able to get at least 3-4 workouts with them before they need charging.Edit: Well after 3.5 months the unit broke. The volume button stopped working on them. Too late to return them to Amazon but Motorola is going to replace them. I just have to pay to ship it back to them.  If the replacement breaks I will probably look to buy the Kinivo BTH220.  They seem sturdier than these Motorola's. I am a little disappointed that these don't cut out any outside noise at all (like zero noise cancelling). The foam pads barely touch my ears so I can hear all outside noise. The guy next to me was stomping as he ran on the treadmill and I could barely hear my own music.
summary: Started out great but broke after 3.5 months

reviewText: After trying out about four different sets of earbuds (which either hurt my ears, made my ears ring or sounded tinny and cheap), I took a shot at these, figuring the sound couldn't be any worse, and the discomfort certainly couldn't.  If I were to like them, the wireless feature would be a bonus.  Having said all that, though, I was highly skeptical.  I expected weak sound, spotty bluetooth and about an hour of battery life, tops.  In fact, I kept all the original packaging pristine to prepare for their return.  I'm happy too say I was proven wrong on all counts.  They're quite lightweight and comfortable, for starters (though if you're wearing a hoodie or something high up on the back of your neck, they can be a bit clunky -- admittedly, this is nitpicking);  Stunningly, the sound is crisp with full bass that put every earbud I tried to shame;  battery life is a non-issue, as they last for hours on a single charge; and, most amazingly, the bluetooth feature is smooth as silk.  The only time I could get it to skip was when I was across my house with the phones from the actual music player -- and then it was still mostly uninterrupted.  While I obviously can't guarantee you'll have the exact same result and response, I can highly recommend these phones -- I've been really surprised and delighted -- and the ability to answer phone calls has been effortless (I use a Droid X) and something I hadn't even thought of.  I will say that the controls on the earphone are a bit tricky to master without looking at when you use them -- but I had 'em down after a few days' use.  Overall, a great product from Motorola that I'd eagerly recommend.
Really bad battery life, connection was lost more often that i liked. Will not buy this thing again. What's more, i'm not sure i will buy Bluetooth headsets again.

Im not sure if the pair which I received became warped or if that is how they were intended to be designed, but they do not fit well at all. They wrap around the head as advertised, but the back of the wrap hits the bottom of my neck, and the earphones are not rotated as far as they should be. this causes the forward (>>) button to be not pointing forward towards my face, but pointing down towards my chin. This strange setup also causes the headphones not to sit flat against the ears, but are awkwardly angled slightly outwards.I really hope that this was just a defected pair that I received, but based on mine I would not recommend this product to anyone with a normally sized and shaped head. Maybe Shaq would like them.

Weird it seems as if Motorola is buying stuff and placing their name on it and calling it good.  These are horrible at reception, I couldn't even put my phone in my pocket without having spotty coverage.****I own another Bluetooth headset that I would recommend Rocketfish RF-MAB2 $60 at Bestbuy $35 on Ebay.  Owned for more than 1 year, excellent range and battery life****

After less than 3 months of use they quit working.  I looked into fixing them, but seemed easier to just replace them.  The sound was fantastic, and when they worked they were great for phone calls.  Not good for fitness, at least not for me - too fragile.  I didn't like how easy it was to hit the buttons on the side of the ear phones, so you could accidentally fast forward, re-dial, etc.  They were nicely priced and I read others had much better luck than me, but I'm done with them for now.
summary: Great at first, but broke early

reviewText: I bought these with the intention of using them predominantly for my work outs. I can run on the treadmill and not have to worry about knocking the wires out of my iPhone anymore or the headsets ever feeling like they're going to fall off. The money I paid is worth this benefit alone.Music sounds good; I put the EQ on flat as the music from my phone usually sounds best that way. Answering calls is simple as well. The only thing I would say that would make this better than they already are is if they would announce calls as my BT phone headset did. That would, of course, change the product from just a music headset to BT phone headset but it could happen!Comfort is good as they  fit snugly over the ears and the band connecting the earphones wraps around the back of the neck without any trouble at all.All in all it is a Motorola product and they continue to deliver great technology at competitive pricing. Way to go Motorola!!!Very pleased!!!

Previous to this headset I had purchased the Plantronics BackBeats and while having great sound, the connection between my phone (Droid Incredible) and the headset sucked.  The connection was fine as long as I placed the phone within line of site and no more than 2 feet from the headset.  Any variation from those parameters resulted in the headset cutting in and out.Anyway, enough of my previous bad experience....I was in the market again for another set of headphones so I started my research and found these.  I figured for the price, why not try them and let me tell you...I am glad I did.  They are great!!  I have had none of the previous problems described above. I can have the phone on my belt and the connection never get's interrupted, in fact in the last week since I have had these I have not had one instance where the connection has dropped due to interference!!  Woohoo!!  Sound quality is acceptable and so are the phone calls.  I use the headset for music and audio books but make the occasional phone call.  I am extremely pleased with the headset and would buy another pair in an instant!!

I got these for my dad and they are fantastic... My gf got them for me the year before and they were perfect for using at the gym, they sound great and last for at least 3hrs before a charge of full use.  There are all sorts of functions they can do, such as answering calls and manuvering around the phone with buttons on the ears, however I do not use any of those functions myself, I just use them as a bluetooth headset at the gym.

These are awesome.... Conferable, sounds great, light weight, no wire, no static, better than my iPhone ear buds, and definitely a very nice price for the quality. I use these mostly at work for listening to music 5+ hours at a time. Works excellent for music and calls. I am very impressed and these are the best bluetooth headphones/headset I've ever owned. Very highly recommended!Update: 7/1/2011 -- READ READ READThis is an update to the above review. I recently started going back to the gym and used these headphones about 3 times and now they stopped working. They will not charge or turn on. So, I am going to say these headphones do not hold up to perspiration. If you plan on using these headphones at the gym or any activity that will cause you to sweat then don't get these. They will die.If you have no plans of using these while working out or activities that will cause you to sweat these are still awesome headphones. I really liked them and was sad when they stopped working. Hopefully Motorola will stick by their product and warranty it.Update: 7/27/2013 -- Update READ!I'm still using these headphones. Although I don't use them at the gym they work great for when I am working in the office. I am upgrading the rating to 4 star from 1.
summary: Awesome!!! Must Buy! (not so much now!)

reviewText: These sound great, have good range, rarely disconnect due to interference, have a surprising battery life, and didn't cost much.  Took me a bit to get used to the buttons.  Works with my iPhone 3GS, and bought a second pair to hook to the home computer for VOIP conference calls to work.
summary: As near perfect as I'm likely to find.

reviewText: i have two pair of these since i am kind of a motorola fan....  i have a razr maxx hd phone and xyboard 10.1 tablet, so these are a perfect pairing with my devices.The only reason you should have signal issues is due to your bluetooth device you connect to.  My old droid bionic almost always had to be in eyesight, while my razr maxx hd can be over 35 ft away and behind a wall.  My xyboard 10.1 has decent range, maybe 15 ft.

I needed a replacement for an S9 that would begin beeping after about 45 minutes (low battery?).  Since I make several conference calls a day, the beeping was unacceptable.  The S305 keeps going and going.  The sound is good.  The microphone picks up my voice better also.  As someone else noted though, you cannot wear this jogging - they bounce off.

I purchased these after reading several reviews here that they were good for working out.I've managed to break 2 pairs of these after only using them maybe 5-10 each.Why?Sweat.First off, these things will keep your ears definitely warm.  After breaking the first pair, I made it a point to continually wipe down my ears and the headphones every couple of minutes and still, they broke.  Also, repeatedly wiping the ears off might make you remove the pads on your ears and there is absolutely no way to put them back in.However, these headphones are surprisingly clear and crisp.  If I didn't use these for working out, then I would recommend these hands down.  I actually use them as my PS3 headphone/mic now.Ups to Motorola for the RMA to replace the original pair, but I wish I never read any of the reviews here.I just wanted to add that I've broken a pair of Jaybird's that are supposed to be 100% sweatproof.  I'm probably just a freak of sweating nature.
summary: Good for working out...if you "glow" and not sweat.

reviewText: I use these paired to a Motorola Droid-X to listen to music while walking, riding the bus/subway etc.  I had my reservations about them as they were so inexpensive, however let me allay your fears, they sound incredible (and I am coming from expensive wired headphones), can take and make calls.  They are more than loud enough and produce acceptable music quality.  If I had three thumbs I would give these three thumbs up.

When I first got this headset I was very pleased, but then I started having a lot of problems with the battery that don't last long. Now it's not working at all, every time I charge it, use it for a little while then turn it off, the next time I tried to use it, it's dead and I have to recharge it again... So basically now I have to charge it every time I want to use them...I don't recommend this product... bad quality...

i have a bluetooth motorola earpiece that is over 3 yrs old and still works like day one (one reason i gave this motorola product a try) i wanted a bluetooth stereo headset for the gym or sitting poolside while listening to music w/o the hassle of a cord. i do not like the in-ear style which is why i choose this style. it fits comfortably and i have found the sound to be excellent. it handles all ranges well. i do not listen at max volumes since i do not want to cause hearing damage. i can still hear things going on outside of these headphones which i prefer. the controls are on the right ear side. your options are north, south, east & west. it lets me pause, skip forward or backward on music tracks. if you are listening to music and the phone rings, it will pause the music. after your call, the music resumes. i had a 30 minute call with a friend and the sound was fine. i never mentioned that i was on this new toy and he never indicated that he could not hear me. it comes with a wall charger. you have to charge it out of the box and it will take a cpl hours. it also has an soft color light that glows red while charging. once it's green - you're good to go. the headband sticks out an inch from the back of your head. that is fine for me but if you are against a pillow it might need some adjusting. for the money, this is a great buy - quality sound & very fair price. i highly recommend for the casual user who doesn't want to spend a fortune.

I have owned blu-tooth headsets in the past, and because I just gave one of my daughters my old Motorola BT head phones, I needed to replace them. I chose these S305"s. I am glad I did. I link mine to my iPad mostly, and on occasion with my iPhone , either way they work beautifully.  The sound produced is clean and these really reproduce the bass tones and power better than most wired head phones.  Amazon never surprises me , the quality of products and low prices make buying from them always a smart decision.  Their customer service is very responsive when you need help or adjustment.Motorola is one of the oldest and best trusted name in electronics i.e. communications, wireless technology etc.You can't go wrong by purchasing one of these headsets.
summary: Blu-tooth is great, and the bass rocks

reviewText: The only reason these headphones didn't get five stars is  because of the relatively cheap build quality, this comes with the price point but doesn't interfere with the integrity of the product. The headphones sit comfortable over the ear and with a little bit of manuvering, will fit on your ears with glasses. All the weight is carried on the ears which makes it so  these headphones don't bounce up and down (a characteristic oif many behind the neck headphones). The functionality of the controls are great though a direct push on the icons is needed to have the function correctly registered. The pairing process is effortless and the 'phones will last about 6 workouts before having to be recharged. The recharging takes about  45 minutes and the 'phones will probably last longer if you don't have the internal volume cranked up as I  do. Though i do this so I can simply control the volume from my iPhone. The sound quality was surprisinglky good, with many instruments coming through that I usually don't hear with inexpensive headphones. If you like bass in your music  these headphones will not dissapoint as the 30mm drivers provide nice bass. While not perfect in an audiophile sense these 'phones are great for the casual listener and more than adequate for gym use. A very satisfying purchase.
summary: Comfortable headphones with very good sound  quality

reviewText: The headset is comfortable while wearing.  Problem is that they lose signal a lot while using and every now and then break up.

These are nice - they work great for a headset for music; however, on phone calls, people complain that they hear everything in the background.  This is more of a speakerphone that goes directly on your ears, but the music quality is great.
summary: Works great as headphones for music

reviewText: I've had this headset for almost a year and it works great.  The side buttons work perfect with Skype and VLC media player.  I only have a few complaints.  The plastic that goes over your ear to hold it in place is sometimes uncomfortable.  There's a groove in it for the wire that goes between the two speakers and that groove sometimes digs into my ear.  They could have designed this piece better.

These headsets pair easily, and have good battery life. However Bass response is low unless you jack up the bass with an equalizer (using it with Android) and being a non adjustable behind the neck design, you can't enjoy them while laying down on a pillow as the ear pads will rise up above your ears. Next time I would get an over the head pair.
I bought this for myself originally. I gave it to my son because he loves it too. I may purchase another like it.

I found these headphone nice, however they didnt work for me.  The problem I have is if you wear glasses, any headphone that wrap around your ear never quite fit right and are sometimes painful.  Pairing was easy, they looked very well constructed, but the volume was a little low for me, great for a jog but no loud enough to compete with the lawnmower.

I had one pair break after a few months use, so far the next pair have been holding up okay. They sound good but I am not an audiophile. When used for calls clarity was generally quite good and people generally didn't know I was on a Bluetooth headset. I have some concerns about durability after the first pair died so quickly. The headphones generally linked reliably with a Galaxy Nexus and Motorola Triumph. I didn't track battery life too closely but it seemed about in line with the specs. Any questions just ask.
summary: Okay headphones but don't pay too much for them.

reviewText: I just got these headphones today and I have to say that I was expecting more. Don't get me wrong, they sound fine, good bass and the treble is not high, it is well balanced.What I don't like is that the stereo is not as wide as I thought it was going to be, since I own the regular headphones that came with my Galaxy Note 3 and they sound awesome, although the treble is higher with them, the sound I think is much clearer and wider.I also have a Plantronics Gamecom 780 with 7.1 sorround sound, and I think I am being unfair comparing them with any other not 7.1 capable headphones, but the sound they delivered are great, just wanted to tell that I consider the sound coming from the Note 3's are almost as good as them, just not so wide and with less bass, then this Motorola S305 are well balanced in sound but not as wide.They are a good choice for the price, I have not had any bluetooth headset before so I cannot compare them with any other, I am not an Audiophile so I don't go spending hundreds of dollars in these things since I basically use them while on the bus and at work.Overall, pretty good, the material is very classy, not fancy at all, they are smaller than I thought, they fit perfectly in my little head and although they don't eat your ears, they cover them well enough to stop the surrounding noise from being listened.At very high volume, they have a very little of distortion, but that may be because I tweaked the volume of my phone to be higher than normal and since you can make the volume go higher than what the phone can, it creates this bit of distortion.I have to try it with calls, I am not very social so I don't have lots of people calling me or I ever have so much of a necessity calling anyone, but I will give them a try.These headphones have a battery life of around 6.5 hours of constant audio playback, I am not sure about how long will it last for phone calls, in stand-by is said to last for days.It is a good device, it paired easily with my computer and Note 3, so there it has my 4 stars.I will be updating this review after trying a call.
summary: Good, not so wide stereo, though.

reviewText: The product worked as descibd, and you also able to make phone calls and accept calls and once yuo done with the call it goes back to the music. it is lovley sound quality is great. i love the product
summary: Perfect, That is what i have been looking for and more

reviewText: Sound quality - 8/10Battery life - 9/10Control - 5/10Call quality - 6/10Noise rejection - 1/10Asthetics - 2/10These bad boys sound pretty good and function well on a call in a quiet environment. There is however a reason why no-one has uploaded a picture wearing them... They fit well, but stand off the ears a full inch. You end up looking like princess leia. Not a great look. I'll wear them at my desk listening to music, but wouldn't necessarily want to be walking around in public with them. They also use a omni-directional microphone which picks up EVERYTHING. There is no use using the call function in anything but the quietest settings.

I bought this item for my dad's birthday a week ago. He loves them and says they are great. I tried them with my Nokia E71x and they sounded fantastic. Battery life is great(6.5hrs). Although the headband looks like it could snap anytime, it actually holds up pretty good. It depends on how you handle them. It clearly says that on the manual. Overall, these headphones are amazing, stylish, and awesome. Would definetly recommend them to anyone who wants a set of bluetooth headphones. Will update more on this fun toy as time goes by.

Sound quality is good for listening to spoken word things, such as TV shows and podcasts.  It does not have a great range for action movies or music.  Volume range is sufficient, I often use this in the kitchen so I don't have to turn my speakers on excessively loudly.  It's a good value if you do not need high quality sound.I have this connected to an Android phone and a Win7 PC.  Both were simple to set up.

These things are awesome - I use them all day streaming music from about 8am to 9pm. Battery life is great. I have only ever heard them beep for low battery once and that was before i had broken the battery in. Now I put it on the charger when I go to bed and 4 hours later when I wake up they last me all day. They far exceeded my expectations in this field. I figured they'd be dead after about 6 hours - they over double that.For the most part, they are relatively comfortable but once in a while, the band does start to cut into my ears.It could be that they are turned to an odd position but 95% of the time it's not a problem.If you have ever worn the old Sony headphones with the same relative design - they do not have guards that keep them comfortably lifted and the plastic is thicker so it does take some getting used to.Ive never had a problem using these with my phone. In fact, they love each other.The button positions are easy to use and [imo] intuitive.They do have their own volume controls are operated separately from the device which is a plus.Connection has a wide range. I can leave my phone at my desk and remain connected in the bathroom approximately 40 feet away.At home, my phone stays in my bedroom and i have reception from all corners of my 1700 square foot house. Range is great.Some people with the iphone commented on the reciever cutting off if your body is in the way - I'm not sure if they increased the strength of the transmitter but it has never been a problem for me.In calls I'm told it sounds like I'm not even using a headset and the soundquality is great for both music and calls.I love them so much, 3 of my friends purchased them on my recommendation and every one loves them.---Edit 23 April 2013---Somewhere around a year into owning these the plastic began to inexplicably fray.Not a huge deal, but something to know. They still work FLAWLESSLY (sound great, still pair easily.) and I will love them til they fall apart, but I am looking for another set that is lighter weight as it is time to replace these.I guarantee these things do not disappoint. Very solid motorola product.

I bought these headphones because they are bluetooth which means the wire wouldn't snag on the barbells when I work out and don't get in the way when I run.  So far, so good.  They are light and I can wear them comfortably for about 45 min to 1 hr, then they start to hurt the top of my ears a bit.  I take them off and reposition them, and I get used to it.  Overall though, they are pretty comfortable and you really don't notice them.The fit is good on the rest of my head (I'm 5'9", about 175 lbs) and I have no issues wearing them.They get pretty loud, but not loud enough to drown out everything around you in a very noisy environment.The music sounds pretty good.  I've spent a lot of time DJing in the past and have great headphones and cheap ones.  For me, these are just fine and pick up the tones quite nicely.Ratings (1=low, 5=highest)Comfort: 4Loudness:  4Cost:  4Ease of connection:  5fit:  5sound: 4I pad $40 on amazon, and they are good for workouts and running since they have no wires and they stay in place.  They can be a little uncomfortable on the ears after about 45 min, but you get used to it.NOTE:  I only used them with my ipod touch 2G, not a phone.  I tried them briefly with a BB bold, and they worked fine, but I had to unpair it then pair it again to use them with my ipod.I recommend them, you should get them, you won't be dissapointed.

These paired easily enough with my Samsung Galaxy S4.  Call sound and mic functioned well.  Music wasn't bad.  But after less than a half hour, these things were hurting my ears - right where they wrap up and over the ear.  Guessing they aren't for people with bigger heads.
These worked for a few months and went dead. I liked them while they worked. I wish they lasted longer tho.

These are extremely clever headphones.  They cram many, many features into a tiny package.  They are, unfortunately poor on two key counts if you're interested in using them to listen to music.  The first is that the bluetooth feature for listening to music just didn't work well and was easily disrupted, either by moving around in relation to the source of the bluetooth broadcast or, when using my iPad or iPhone, if I were using any other apps on the device.The comfort of these headphones was also poor and the behind the neck placement irritating if I were sitting.  The headphones pinched too tightly on my head and the grip or tension was not adjustable.  After a relatively short time, the pressure on my ears was unacceptably painful.  The behind the head placement of the loop connecting the individual earpieces is nominally a good idea, but because the loop of the headset is fairly large, it sticks out behind and down the neck.  This doesn't work for sitting in a chair or reading propped up in bed - the headphones are jammed forward by the loop or levered up, depending on how the loop hits the chair or bedframe and pillow.  Either way, not comfortable, not workable.
summary: Great sound, lousy bluetooth, lousy comfort

reviewText: These headphones not only sound great but are lightweight and very rarely loose the signal with your device. Great for the active person.

i love this. i use this with my iphone and it accepts my incoming calls. i can hear the other party without problems and they can hear me. music sounds great too. i like the fact that i dont trip on any cords nor do i have to wade through them.update:1. when accepting calls from the unit. You can hear the other party clearly but they cant hear you that well.2. since the loop in the back is solid(non flexible or retractable), it becomes irritating or is hanging so far when your head is average to small.otherwise, it is still a great headphone, i still use it when i run and it still wont fall off.update:11/2011its probably been a year now and it is still working perfectly
summary: Love it. I walk around the office with them

reviewText: I purchased these headphones because I am really hard on the corded kind, and I find myself needing to replace them every year or two. A bluetooth headset seemed like the way to go. Unfortunately, it did not turn out to be the case. Sound quality is decent, and charge time is okay, but sadly, this thing cannot maintain the Bluetooth connection with my iPhone. Every few minutes, the connection weakens, and sound stutters and even cuts off for a few seconds. Given that I keep my phone in my shirt pocket, the distance from the phone to the headphones is less than 2 feet, yet the connection fails. Not what I'd call a reliable product. I would definitely not buy this again. Total waste of money.

After reading all of the incredibly positive reviews about this product I figured I'd give it a shot and buy a pair. After a couple weeks with it and using it mainly to pair with my Motoactv on workouts I can say that they are just OK. The sound quality is very good, the ease of use is high, and they feel very comfortable. The biggest issue I'm encountering is while I'm out on runs the audio will skip or cut out for seconds at a time and then come back. This happening once or twice an hour would be fine, but this is happening once or twice per song which is unacceptable. If I had to guess I'd say that the erratic playback is due to sweat causing problems with the headset since there is minimal to no issues when they're dry. The Motoactv shows no signs of issue with a wired headset during these times too, so I don't think that's the problem. I'll give them another week before saying goodbye and trying a different product. It's a shame too, these guys are solid otherwise.UPDATE: 12/27/2012: Returned these and went with the Moto S11's and won't be looking back. They are far superior for workouts than these headphones. These have better audio, but didn't serve the purpose I needed them for. Because of that I will keep my rating as is and not knock it because it wasn't the perfect fit for me. They are still a solid product.

I read most of the reviews on here before buying. Given that I wasn't going to use it for extreme sports, I launched for the purchse. No regrets!!! I paired it with my BB 9500 (Storm2) and works PERFECT!!! I walk to work, so it serves me to hear music or voice AND if a call comes in, music gets paused, you hear a ring on the headset and with one touch,(on the ear piece)woila!! called answered! One downfall is in windy conditions. Since, the mic hole is facing straight out, if it's windy the person on the other side of the line will hear lots of wind. no biggie for me!!Confortable and lightweight on your ears.Great sound quality.Love the buttons on the actual ear piece.Working perfect with my BB Storm2.

I bought this with the intention of using it with my HTC Thunderbolt mobile phone to listen to music and take phone calls wirelessly via Bluetooth. For that purpose alone the S305 is perfect. I have to admit I felt a little awkward at first trying to wear them on my head correctly but I got the hang of it quickly.  From my phone I get excellent quality music playback and stereo quality phone calls.  People say they can hear me just fine which is a nice surprise since the microphone is nearly impossible to detect.  I'm also surprised at the excellent battery life.  I don't think the battery is replaceable but on average I've been listening to music about 3 hours per day and use it for about 30 minutes of phone calls.  It hasn't ran out of battery power yet and is fully recharged in 10-30 minutes.  I have tried pairing it with a PC and a laptop.  So far no luck.  That could be something I'm doing wrong or incorrect drivers perhaps but since I really only wanted it to work with the HTC Thunderbolt that's what I'm rating it on for 5 stars.
summary: On the HTC Thunderbolt Love it

reviewText: My Dad liked them so much, he took my pair and bought me another set.  He was leaving for a 12 hour flight.
summary: Sound quality is great, battery life is great, but they bother the top of my ears if not properly placed.

reviewText: I was excited when I first saw these headphones. More and more I've been using my iPhone to listen to music, but the Apple headphones were less than great and I'm terrible about wired stuff. A few times a day during my work I rip the headphones out of my ear or send the phone onto the floor while reaching for something on my desk.When I got these phones they paired immediately with my phone, no messing around!The sound was ok, but not terribly loud, and thats saying something because I don't blast my music.But I could learn to live with this.The one thing thats a deal breaker for me is the fact that these are "behind-the-head" earphones.I think I was a little blinded by the price that I didn't really take notice of that fact.If you're planning on lying back in bed or an easy chair for a nap with your new headphones, forget it. Incredibly uncomfortable trying to put your head on a pillow. This was very disappointing for me, but absolutely my fault.They would have gotten a 5 star if it weren't for this one thing.All-in-all I'd recommend them but remind about that one caveat.

This headset worked great for a couple of months.  I was able to control my iTunes on my iPhone 4.  Unfortunately they stopped working for me.  It may have been too much sweat/moisture as I was using them while running.  I'm not sure, but I'm now in the market for another bluetooth headset, and I will not be getting these again.
summary: Worked great for a couple months

reviewText: after a few months they stopped accepting the charge. The sound quality is good but i expected them to last longer

I wanted a pair of behind-the-head headsets for comfort reasons. These fit okay, but the user ergonomics are not to my liking.The volume controls are not tactile marked: I can't tell when I am on the + or - volume controls by touch. And, to make matters worse, when the mode changes, so does the volume. These headphones are capable of a high level so you can unexpectedly wind up having your ears blasted - without, in my case, the means to quickly adjust the volume.I wanted to use these with Skype and have the freedom to walk away from the computer when necessary. You don't get far with these: I managed about 10 feet away from the computer in repeated tests before the Bluetooth connection was lost.The audio feed from my music source did not shut off when I initiated a call. In fact, as soon as the call started ringing, the volume of the music shot up to its highest level.Overall, this unit offered the comfort level and fit that I was looking for - but none of the really useful things I need. Your experience may vary.Jerry

For the money, this set is hard to beat. I paid I believe 27 dollars shipped to my door.These things sound great for BT headphones and paired right up with both my Mytouch4G and Amaze4G cell phones. They have great highs without being overbearing and also decent bass. I mean they won't be Dre Beats, but these fit the bill according to price. If you want crazy bass, look elsewhere though.They fit well over my big melon head, that and I go to the gym quite a bit and do various exercises, from elliptical to busting butt on the bench and whatever else. They don't lose a beat......unless.....you leave them in your gym bag in cold weather. Seems it takes a minute for them to warm up or something. If not, they skip for whatever reason.I am actually really stoked about this purchase. One of the better ones of the past year. I mean I only have been rocking them about a month, but been great! See how they stand the test of time. I know they get a lot of bad reviews due to working out in them and sweat getting into them and shorting them out. I don't have that issue as of yet and I sweat pretty bad.Also all the controls work well, even calls when using the headphone switch. Microphone comes in well to boot. I have used it a few times with no issues.I highly recommend them.

reviewText: i've used about a dozen stereo bluetooth headsets.  my stupid dog eats them somewhat regularly.  these were ok, but subpar and not worth the price.this was my favorite of the 4 motorola stereo BT headsets i purchased over the years, although i found off-brand options that were better:Kinivo BTH240 Bluetooth Stereo Headphonei also used the s9, s9hd, and s10 headsets from motorola.  these were all ok, above average sound quality, but they would constantly come out my ears enough to lose all the bass response: plus if you're wearing those in-ear designs while out walking you're as good as deaf: at least with these over the ear ones you can hear the outside world if you keep the volume at a reasonable level.
summary: motorola stereo bluetooth headsets aren't worth the cost.

reviewText: the cheap plastic band that goes behind your head is huge and sticks out like a wing behind your neck.  if you look up, it hits your neck and moves the heaphones.  the band is not adjustable - big design flaw.also, the max volume level is horrible - you can easily hear noise around you with it turned all the way up.

reviewText: I am shocked and dissappointed in the sound quality from these headphones! They sound cheap and tinny. The device works fine and has a beautiful appearance, but they sound like something found in the dollar bin at Dollar General. I have the Motorola SD-10 bluetooth headphones, and love them. i love my headsets there my favorite thing i own i take them everywhere i go they do fit my head tho

For the price, ya can't beat what you get here.  It seems like the battery life is not as good as I would like, but I tend to keep my things charged.  I'm very happy with this, exactly what I was looking for.

Bluetooth pieces are falling off the market like flies off a baker's apron.  But this piece is probably one of the worst sound quality devices you can wrap around your ears.  The Bluetooth makes a very poor connection to your cell phone device and looses and regains connection strength as you are using it.  The result is a very poor sound quality experience. I had always wanted a pair of bluetooth headphones, but could never get myself to spend the money on them myself. I received a different pair as a gift for Christmas and loved how they could be applied to my daily life, but they were an in-ear variety that had poor sound quality and was simply uncomfortable to wear.So, i returned them & began shopping around for a decent mid-range over-ear set when I found these. The reviews were glaringly positive & I see why.Sound Quality--I'm a musician, so I have fairly well trained ears. I certainly didn't expect studio quality sound from a $40ish pair of bluetooth headphones. However, the performance and sonic quality of this item greatly exceeded any of my expectations. They sound fantastic and are perfectly acceptable for any casual listener.Microphone Recording Quality--I use Siri quite a bit on my phone & haven't had any problems related to poorly received voice commands. In voice calls the worst people have said is "You sound a little different, but you sound fine." Again, perfectly acceptable for my standards.Weight--Very light weight. Zero complaints.The Fit--This is wildly different on an individual basis, so I can only relate my experience. I have a bit of a large head and wear glasses. Naturally the concern for anyone with glasses is feeling like you have a pile of stuff pulling down on your ears. These absolutely DO NOT interfere with my glasses. However, I have rather thin framed specs so it allows for plenty of extra room on my ear. That being said, even with thick emo style frames I think these would continue to work without bothering you. I even wear them with glasses while jogging on the treadmill without problems.Cell Phone Integration-- I absolutely love how well this headset works with my phones. I actually use an iPhone 5, but also have an older Evo 4G on hand. It works extremely well with both phones. It syncs quickly and easily, and the right-earphone has 4 well-disguised buttons for call/accept call, skip forward, skip back, and play/pause. All functions worked perfectly on both android and apple platforms. As a pleasant surprise I tapped the call button on my iphone while it was in a standby state. I was delighted to hear the little Siri sound blip in my ear & mic channel open to accept a voice command.Battery Life-- I've used this headset for roughly a half hour a day for a week & still going strong. It advertises 4-6 hours of use & I am inclined to believe it. It seems perfectly acceptable given the fact that this lightweight set of headphones cannot have a large battery in them weighing them down.Range-- Once again I was blown away by the performance. Last night I let my daughter play on my phone upstairs while I played with these downstairs. When I powered them on I was shocked when they connected to my phone 20 yards away through an entire floor's layer of construction. I can basically leave my phone anywhere in my house and simply keep my headset on. VERY nice for those times when you forget to stuff your phone in your pocket before walking away.Final Impressions-- I think what will make or break the use of this product for someone is simply the question of "Does it fit your head?" Beyond that, there's really nothing more you could possibly ask for given the dollars you'd be spending. I am sure there's a pair out there with slightly better sound or an extra button or two, but for the money you simply can't beat these.

I was looking for an option that would allow me to workout without the restrictions of wires. I FOUND SO MUCH MORE! These headphones have become my daily drivers & I do mean DAILY! I rock them from sun up to sun down because the BATTERY LIFE & STANDBY TIME is SUPER! The sound quality is super for a non in ear, non noise cancellation option! I listen to a tone of music and have tested a tone of headphone options. WHY DO THESE SOUND BETTER THAN ALL THE IN EAR OPTIONS I'VE TRIED!? What takes the cake is that they have great sound, but they don't cancel out the noise around you so if you like to ride your bike in the city like me, you can mind your surroundings. The Bluetooth radius is true to specifications as long as you don't have a major object blocking the connection like multiple walls. The microphone is excellent at picking up your voice for hands-free calling and voice to text which also works better than most! As for what I bought them for, LOL they work flawlessly at the gym. Running, lifting, riding, basketball you name it, they are right there with you! There is a slight discomfort after about 45 minutes, but I have found that after about a month you get used to it or in my case it seems like it has adjusted to my head so I don't feel it. *Kanye Shrug* I wear them all day because when not in use I just lay them around my neck. Often times I forget I'm wearing them and they're not so bulky that they're unfashionable. I don't usually write reviews this long, but I really am a fan of this product! I highly recommend it!

I made the mistake of upgrading from these headphones to LG's headphones. By far, these headphones are better due to their over-the-ear design, allowing the headphones to sit comfortably on the user's ears, and not block out external noises. This means you can exercise outside while wearing them and not be in danger of not hearing your surroundings. Also, you don't have any loose bits flying around, or thin wire and a lousy storage system for the earbuds, which is just annoying.The S305 offers beautiful sound for being an earlier bluetooth headset, and is basically a wireless upgrade from its more popular wired cousin, which I also believe is one of the best budget wired headsets one can buy for their money.The buttons are clear and intuitive, after a short while one can learn to control their devices with very little thought, though of course communicating with the device in my experience, has been a bit of a headache. Yet the S305 has managed to do this moreso reliably than compared with the LG. My device can at least be in my pocket while I am walking, and I will be able to play music with little to no interruptions.If you are torn between the S305 and LG's sad attempt at making a headset, definitely do go for the S305. It is cheaper, more practical and just plain works better.

I wanted a pair of BT headphones to use at work to replace a pair of wired earbuds. I researched several models and this one stood out based on positive reviews and price. I've used them a few days now and they seem to be living up to their claim. They are fairly lightweight, comfortable, and the sound is impressive for their cost. I was surprised to see the various controls available on the headphones. Besides the obvious on/off and volume controls, it has remote control capabilities such as previous/next track, rewind/ff, play/pause, and stop - all conveniently located on the outer ring of the right headphone. The unit can also be used as a hands-free headset when connected to your phone. This is a definite winner!
I didn't think these headphones would work as good as they do but I'm a believer now. Only thing is it'd be nice if they came with some additional way to protect the ear pieces or spare covers

The distortion was coming from my other phone, not the headphones.For $45 headphones these little guys have some kick-butt audio, I can put them on put my phone in the kitchen and clean my entire house(about 3500sqft) and I rarely loose connection or have it cut-out. I've had them for almost a year and they still work perfectly. They are extremely durable, even if they don't feel like they are.. I haven't exactly taken good care of them and they still sound and feel great.Also, I wear glasses, so finding over-the-ears headphones is hard for me, the back on these is thin enough to fit under glasses and not move them around.The only complaint is that they are "one size fits all" and aren't adjustable, so if you lean back and rest your head on a chair, they will probably come off if you have a small head.Charging only takes about 25mins and they stay charged for days.

I have tried a few headphones, wireless and otherwise, to listen to my book on tapes. This is the one that I like the best. It has a good sound quality and works great with my iphone5c. It holds a charge for quite a few hours of listening, so I don't have to charge it as much. I can exercise with it and it stays on securely. It has a pretty good range, so I can walk around my house and leave my phone in its charger, without losing the signal. I would recommend this item.

reviewText: I bought this headset back in January 2009 and it is still working great!  I mostly use it paired with myApple iPod touch 8 GB (4th Generation) NEWEST MODEL.  I did find that my newest pair of eyeglasses and the headset don't really fit as well. My previous glasses has thin metal bows whereas my new pair has thicker plastic. By moving the ear pieces around a bit, I can get it everything to fit okay though.  It's worth not having a headset cord so that I can get up and do a few things in my cubicle or borrow something from a co-worker. I keep the power cord at work and charge the headset overnight. I also happen to have a Motorola cell phone so I can use the same cord to charge my phone during the day. Would I buy these again? Definitely. (Although if I could find a little earbud Bluetooth headset, I'd like to try that.) :)

I am using these with my iphone 4 and my ipad 1 and I am really very happy. Syncing with 2 devices is not a prob as long as you read the directions. As you can see from the tons of positive reviews, these are clearly the best on the market for the price range. I'd say they are probably worth far more than the listed price.Pro's:Very simple set up & operation. Just follow the docs.Sound quality is very good for BT wireless headphones.Very few (if any) drop outs. I walk the dog all day and they never skip or pause.Works great with Apple products (you knew know right?).Battery life seems great - I have used them for several hours on end for music and never ran into low battery warnings. They recharge fast.Hands down the BEST wireless BT headphones I have tried. I list the con's only out of full disclosure. None are a show stopper.Con's: (really pretty minor ones actually)Volume and operations buttons feel loose and flimsy. It would be nice to have more solid buttons as you will press them to often. Button placement takes a little getting used to.The max volume is a little low. This is probably to save battery life. While driving on the highway (or somewhere there is a lot of external noise) I have to turn them all the way up and even so it could be louder. For instance, trying to listen to classical music with soft passages or an audiobook is "iffy" on these if you have a lot of external noise.Lots of sound bleed - my wife tells me she can hear the music quite clearly even when I have them at half volume. I think this is a double edge thing - on the plus side the "open-ness" lets me hear sounds in the environment very clearly. The down side is everyone can hear the music and of course you aren't ever going to get "isolation" with these if that's what you are looking for.Lastly, they tend to hurt my ears after a few hours of wearing them. Maybe too tight? But then I do have a big head.
summary: Amazing value and a really darn great pair of BT headphones.

reviewText: I love bluetooth technology, after working in the tech industry for ten years anything that doesn't require wires brings a smile to my face.That said, these are fantastic headphones, I've only used them on a call once, but the performance was equally superb. They produce a beautiful sound, I am not saying it's 100% perfect and that some overly critical audiophile won't find a flaw in them... But for jamming out on a bus, or while jogging, or at a gym, or just walking around the house while your significant other is asleep they are fantastic.The only reason I dropped a star off, is that they are fragile, not in the general construct, but the about the volume buttons, the first unit I had I left in my car one too many times during the summer and the heat actually loosened the bonding material that fastens the volume up/down buttons; so that when I went to adjust the volume it just... "fell off". I send an email to the seller, as I was bit disgruntled and had only had them 3 months... Never got a response, bought a different pair think "**** you too!" which turned out to be just terrible and came running right back to a second pair of these.I highly suggest them, just be wary of how/where you store them.

I have purchased two sets of these and I would give the battery charge, ease of connection/use and range all an A++ rating.  However, I was using these at the gym where I do sweat a lot.  The first pair lasted me about 4 months but the second pair only about 60 days until they died.  Only thing I can think of is the sweat is killing them??  Great if you want to use in office or sitting at home doing nothing but if you are looking for some you can use while working out/running I would like to another product it might be worth getting a new pair every 4 months but every 2 months?  More trouble than they are worth at that rate.
summary: Great Battery life, easy to use but dies quickly

reviewText: I initially set out searching amazon specifically for Bluetooth sport headphones with a mic for use jogging with my Blackberry curve 8900. My first impression was that there did not seem to be the best selection of models to choose from, I had it in my mind what I wanted but had never used any similar products. I had previously used a set of wired sport headphones and the wire was an absolute pain while jogging! Competing models seemed to be more expensive than these, ranging up around $75 and the reviews weren't all that satisfying.When I saw these Motorola S305, the form was exactly what I had in mind and the price ($33 shipped) seemed fantastic to me. I liked the fact that there were so many positive reviews as well. I purchased them from Amazon and received them with in 2-3 days with free super saver shipping; I live in Washington state...Durability: I had a little concern ordering these based on a review that stated the build quality was a bit weak; I don't find that to be the case at all; these appear to be very well designed and built.  I had also read that some other brands had issues with sweat and rain which made some concern; I am not "heavy sweater" but I defiantly do a fair share of perspiring when exercising and I have also worn these in the rain, they have not missed a beat.Battery Life: I charged these up which I think took about 2-3 hours for the first full charge. I used these for almost a week at 30-40 minutes per use on a single charge, I'd estimate that I got about 4 hours of continuous music play which I think is amazing considering the battery must be tiny because these are so light weight. They started beeping when the battery went low and I was just about to run so I put them on the charger for about 10 minutes which was enough juice to keep them going for the next 40 minutes without beeping at me (very pleased!). They seem to be smart in that they shut off if no connection is present, I like that feature.Sound quality: My main use for these is listening to music while exercising. I am a huge music enthusiast but I am not super picky about sound coloration and such. I specifically wanted an over-ear phone, not an in-ear bud, so that I could still hear my surrounding environment. Sure in-ear buds have impressive bass response but I also have found that the cords tend to pick up and transmit a lot of noise which is very annoying to me. I would imagine that a set of Bose would out-perform these but honestly, as I mentioned I am very in to music and these sound great. I don't crank them too high so I'm not sure if they would distort but for normal listening, I couldn't be happier.Bluetooth connectivity: As mentioned, I use these with my blackberry curve 8900; they were very simple to do the initial set up and the pair/ un-pair without issue every time.Control Features: When previously using my wired headphones connected to my blackberry which I had in an arm band, it was very difficult to control the music player. For example, when a song comes on that I don't like it really messes up my running rhythm and I want to fast forward but it was difficult with the blackberry in the armband. The controls on the headphones were one of the main features that attracted me and they are VERY EASY TO OPERATE; I couldn't be happier. The buttons are spaced out enough to easily control the function you intended and there is a nice audible feedback beep when you adjust the volume (different for up/down).Phone: I mainly wanted these for wireless music while jogging but the ability to answer the phone was a bonus as well. The control button on the headphone is very easy to use and supports voice dialing or last number redial. Operation is fantastic and the microphone seems to work well. I tested by speaking softly and a little less clearly than normal and the other party had no issue hearing me at all. On the other hand, the received voice signal from the other party oddly enough is not very clear; it is defiantly usable but I am surprised in the low quality of the signal.Comfort: For about the first 3 days of use, I felt a little pressure on the back of my right ear where the rigid band rests, I would say it was slightly discomforting but I dealt with it. By about the 4 time using these, my ear had gotten used to it and the discomfort had gone away. These are very light and now that the initial discomfort has gone away I almost can't even tell these are on my head.Potential concern: I haven't checked availability but I would assume at some point the foam pads will need to be replaced and I'm not sure if they are replaceable. I'm not going to discount these headphones yet based in this as I haven't checked in to it but it is a consideration.Packaging: This is the only item that I give a huge FAIL. These were in the most user un-friendly packaging I've seen in a long time. The display plastic packaging was molded close to the item and the seam seal around the edge was very strong making for a work-out just getting them out of the packaging... Come on Motorola, get with the game on this one.Summary: I am so excited about these headphones, they meet my needs and expectations at a great price. I was so pleased that I just purchased another pair for my wife.
summary: So pleased I've bought my wife a set too. Fantastic!

reviewText: You need an average cranium, the sound is not super, the microphone is tinny and people had a hard time hearing me. You can go a long way from the phone and retain connection though!

So I got these along with the Sennheiser MM100's and Motorola S9-Hd's from a store going out of business (I'll be reviewing both at a later date). My test-bed was an iPhone 3Gs.The first pair I tried was the S9-HD's. These sounded pretty good and the fit was nice.The second pair I tried were the Senns and wow. These were pretty impressive. I thought there was no way a pair of bluetooth 'phones could compete with wireds, but alas, I was wrong. While not acoustically perfect (slightly anemic bass), these sound amazing.This brings me to the S305's. These look nicer than the Senns, but that's where the overtaking positives end. The sound is quite flat with a slight tinnyness to it, and has very little bass. The bass gets a little better if you press the phones against your ear, but who wants to do that? I tried every single eq setting and none made a difference. That being said, the iPhone is noted for having a relatively flat response, but the Senns offer decent bass response. Heck, even the S9-HDs have a relatively good low end. So there's no reason this particular set doesn't. And I'm not talking bass-head low end. I'm talking enough to provide a balance fill. The second issue I take with these, is they aren't particularly comfortable and make my ears sore after just a few minutes of use.Don't get me wrong, these aren't terrible. But not something to rave about either. There are better headsets for the price. (i.e. if you don't mind in-ear, the Moto S9-HD's are a good bet).

I received these as a gift, from my Amazon wish list. I also own a set of theMotorola MOTOROKR S9 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones. I wanted these to replace the in-ear bud of the S9's which was terribly uncomfortable after listening for a couple of hours.
