They both serve separate purposes though, the SuperFi's of course have excellent noise reduction capabilities, 26dB!The S305 headphones do also tend to get uncomfortable along the ridge in the over the ear support bar. It feels literally like they are cutting into your ear after a couple hours of use.The phone functions are on par with the S9's. Sound is excellent, and the microphone is decent. A bit "tinny" on the receiving end from what I've been told.The S305's pair easily with my Blackberry Storm, and also have the same micro USB charger which is where the industry is currently headed so that was a nice bonus!

Got the largest capacity microSD card I could find, and now my BB has replaced my mp3 player.Pros:-Very light weight, can use it at the gym-Works great with my BB-Works great as both A/V remote and for phone calls-Good quality audio, even with bassCons:-Hard plastic wrap-around hurts after a while-Can't wear like a regular pair of headphones orbluetooth headset for too long-Controls on the right hand side only-Can't always reach all buttons on the headset whilewearing it - have to take it off to turn it on/off

These things rock.  Battery life is good, the pair easily with iphone4, sound good (the left speaker is lower and it's made that way, they are not defective, it's just how they had to be built), work pretty well on phone calls, no complaints from people I'm talking to.  They can wear on your ears after 4 or five hours, so don't leave them on that long if you can help it.  Totally worth the price, I just need to find some speaker covers for when these foams wear out from use.In the last six months I've gotten way more than $40 out of these.  If you're looking for a pair, these are pretty good.

This BT headset does exactly what I wanted. It readily connects to any of my BT devices and the phone quality is good. Not as good as my Plantronics headset,but certaintly good enough for the times I am listening to music. The music sound quality is excellent. If you are expecting the quality of a $500 Sennheiseer, you have to be dreaming. But for general istening and where I am not expecting to hear Synphony Hall quality, they are great. And given the low quality of music that people listen to, the headset should be more than adequate. They are not real comfortable for listening beyond about two hours, but I don't listen to music more than that at one time.If they give out in a few months I will post another review, but for now they are 5 stars.

I decided to buy this headset, because it has over 1000 reviews, mostly positive. However, these are my points of assessment:Comfort: I don't know what most people consider to be "comfortable", but this set does not fit for me. It feels awkward, with its ark at the rear of my head, and it does not hug my ears snugly enough. When I lean back against my high sofa seat or pillows, the beam behind my head gets in the way and pushes the set off my ears, since it is not precisely snug around the rear of my head.I also wear reading glasses, and the bow of the set gets into a room crisis/conflict with the branches of my glasses right behind and above my ears. There is room for one of those, but not for the both.I wanted to use it for two things: as my speaker system for the laptop and at the same time, to use as the blue-tooth for my iPhone-4. The sound quality for music and sound files played from my laptop is poor, compared to the Plantronics DSP 400 I have been using until now. For my iPhone, I tried to pair it 3 times. I turned it off, then on again, to be discovered. It signaled that it was paired for phone calls, but upon testing it by calling my husband's iPhone-4, I never got to hear anything in the headset. I had to turn to the phone's speaker system instead. Maybe it needs that separate adapter that they also mention (although they claim it works with the iPhone "guaranteed".For all these poor performance reasons, it goes back into the box and returned for a refund.

I last owned a pair of Bluetooth A2DP headphones a few years ago -- they were a high-end Sony unit. The sound was never quite perfect on them, but cutting the cord made it worthwhile. I purchased these on a lark, as they are quite inexpensive (compared to what I paid for the Sony's), and I wanted that convenience again. I was surprised at the quality of the sound; I really can't tell the difference between these and wired headphones. They work great with both my Windows Mobile phone and my Ubuntu 9.10 workstation. The AVCHD controls work perfectly, which is great - no more fumbling around to flip to the next song or pause, just press the button on the headphones. Glad I made the purchase!

I own all sorts of headphones and ear buds.  My best are Etymotic ER-4 microPro ear buds, fabulous, and Grado SR80s, good.  For work I have been using Koss's Porta-Pro folding headphone and can easily recommend them for the cost.  I consider the PortaPro the best headphones for under $50.  I am most certainly NOT an audiophile as any true audiophile would scoff at the cans I use.  However, I do not like so-so audio quality either.The Motorola S305 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones were bought hoping I could use them to listen to music from various sources I have at the office.  And they fill that bill.  I also wanted a decent set of cans.  Nothing great, just good enough to keep me un-annoyed.  And they seem to do that although getting them to work cleanly with Amarok on my Fedora 16 desktop took some fiddling.  They now work and sound as good with my Linux box as with any other box or OS.The S305s work with my Droid Bionic (Android 2.3.4), my Samsung RF511 (Windows7), my Dell 6410(WindowsXP.Pro), and my Dell desktop (Fedora16).  It syncs and holds sync well with all of them.  The cans are a little dull and bassy sounding.  Not horribly so, well OK horribly so when compared to my ER-4's; but otherwise OK compared to my Koss Porta-Pros.  Their quality, however, is not as good as the Porta-Pros.  For that sort of quality in Bluetooth headphones I suspect one will have to spend $100 or more.Sounds like I might not like them.  That's the wrong idea.  They are OK for the price.  I have walked 60+ feet away from my desk in a cubicle office environment with a high concentration of electronics and they still work.  They connect to Asus BT21 Bluetooth dongles or my Bionic.  60 feet isn't shabby at all.They are generally comfortable.  If you wear glasses with thick ear pieces and don't have a fat-head (like I do) you will get along with the S305s.  Fortunately I have thin ear pieces with my glasses and can adjust the phones to be comfortable enough.My only wish is that I had experience with other Bluetooth headphones so I could judge these better.  I don't think you'll hate these headphones; but, I think you'll want to move up as soon as you can afford to.

Pros: light weight, Micro USB charger, controls are easy to use.Cons:Uncomfortable - The loops that go around your ear are hard plastic and dig into the side of my head, I wear a 7-1/4 hat size.  The loop that goes behind my head sticks straight out about an inch off the back of my head so with a high back chair I'm always bumping the back of the headset.Does not work as advertised - This is supposed to connect to two devices at a time but it doesn't work with a phone and computer or two phones.  Even if I set the phone for calls and the computer for audio it still won't stay connected to both at the same time which is really disappointing since that's exactly why I got it.

I like this headset a lot. I was a little nervous at first because of the mix reviews, but I tried it out and let me tell ya, the sound quality is really good. It has a nice ammount of bass, wonderful for music. It also works very well for calls, the only thing that i would do to improve is add padding to the plastic piece that goes around your ears other than that it's perfect. O and the battery hasn't died on me yet but I got about 6 hours of talk with it today.

For under $35, I was very impressed. This headset easily connects to my iPhone and my computer for wireless music and telephone calls. I was hesitant to buy a headset that didn't have a separate extended microphone piece but nobody has ever even asked me if I'm on a headset or not because they can hear me just fine. Having the ability to turn the speakers up so loud during phone calls is priceless, too. I mostly bought these so that I could talk hands free in the car and have a stereo headphone set for other times. This accomplishes both beautifully and people can hear me just fine.Also, I have an older 2G iPhone. By default the, headset works fine with this phone as a phone only, not as a stereo headset. I was able to download the A2DP app (Google it) and could then listen to my music from my older iPhone. It works beautifully. If you find yourself needing to do this, keep in mind two things: 1) The iPhone must be jailbroken to get this app. If you have a 3G or later, you don't need it - these will work perfectly with no modifications. 2) You have to start your music on the phone then press the play button on the headset in order for it to recognize it as a music player.The battery life is great on these headphones - it seems to last as long as I want. I did run out of battery once but it was one of the first times using it when the battery hadn't ever been fully charged.My only dislike on this is that after a while the headset can get uncomfortable and it's not a perfect combination with sunglasses because it uses the top of your ears to hold the weight, as do the sunglasses. Not a big deal and certainly no deal breaker.All in all, I really enjoy this headphone/headset combo.Buy them. You'll be happy you did.
summary: Great Headset, Great Headphones, Great Battery Life

reviewText: I was looking for the the most convenient earphones to use while watching videocasts on my Macbook while doing housechores.  I have several sets of earphones but they are either bulky or requires to hook up a power adapter and audio cables.My current favorite before this purchase is an IR line of sight Sony.  It uses one "AA" battery which lasts for a very long time.  Another bonus is that the transmitter that you plug to the audio source also works as battery charger.  I also have a 900 Mhz Senheiser.  A lot of reviewers seem to like this but I found it too heavy and bulky.  The interference is too much for me that I hardly use it anymore.Anyway, I mentioned an IR, a 900 Mhz, but this time it is a bluetooth headphone.  They all work in differently.  The bluetooth will only work if you have a bluetooth device.  For my purpose, this is excellent as you don't have any power adapter and audio cables to attach.  The 30-35 ft in the spec is accurate.  I did wander beyond 50 ft but the connection starts to fail at that point.  And when I turned across the corner, the music signal finally stopped.It has the power button, forward, volume control (- and +) located on the right ear.I also tried it on my iPhone and it works fine.  The music will stop when you get a call and just a push of a button to accept.  After hanging-up, your music continues where you left off.It also works great with my iPhone while exercising on the elliptical machine.  Now I don't have to strap my player and worry about hacking the earphone cord with a wayward motion of my arms.Cons:- I really like to have an option of a replaceable battery.  If this goes dead in the middle of whatever I am listening to, there is no choice but to plug it via USB and wait a few hours before I can use it again.  A  triple "A" battery would be nice.- It is hard to tell if it is on because the LED light  is hardly visible.  But I think is what you want if you want to use it as a phone accessory instead of just a music and podcast listening device..There is another Motorola Bluetooth set of earphones that is even smaller yet a bit more expensive, the S9-HD.
summary: I use it to watch on my notebook - very convenient.

reviewText: ALl I can say is don't listen or pay attention to any of the bad reviews you see or hear. I got this headset about 5 months ago and they are STILL going strong. They are light weight, cause no pain what so ever to the ear and a VERY durable! Will never trust any other Brand except Motorola as far as headsets go because they clearly know their stuff!

Overall the Motorola S305 is a very good B/T Stereo Headset. I have had it for almost a year now. It paired very easily with Windows Mobile and Android Phones (Samsung, Motorola, HTC); as well as my B/T equipped laptop (HP).Wearibility-wise, although it caused the some annoying discomfort in back of my right ear, it rested well over the ears. Perhaps a softer (rubberized?) padding around the plastic band would have helped.The audio/call control buttons are placed intuitively. I found the B/T range to be excellent. A very nice feature is that with my phone set to mute, I could receive the various audible notifications (email, text message, incoming phone call) on the headset.The sound quality is very good although not as good as in high-frequency range an "in-ear" set might provide but this IMHO is a trade-off (as most in-ear sets don't have very good low-frequency reproduction). The volume range is excellent which compensated very well for the muted highs.I have worn this headset while working-out and had no issues. Over time, as sweat accumulated on the foam covers it lost its softness. I finally figured out that removing and replacing the foam pieces after cleaning them was a cinch.I highly recommend this B/T Stereo Headset from Motorola.
summary: Very good B/T Stereo Headset from Motorola

reviewText: I enjoy them. They work great. They connect easy and interface well with my phone or PC. When a phone call comes in it transitions well. Also clear on the phone.

Pros: Reliably syncs to my Motorola Z6m phone, keeps the connection for listening to audiobooks, pretty comfortable, easy to use, good volumeCons: Buttons are a little loose sometimes depending on activity, microphone for phone conversations is weak and with no noise/wind suppressionOverall, this are excellent for the price.  The Motorola S9-HD, S9, and S-10 versions are far, far, far worse than this LESS expensive model!  If you're looking for a motorola bluetooth stereo headset, these are a great deal and MUCH better than the more expensive models in motorola.
summary: 'Way better than more expensive S9 or S10 version

reviewText: These are simply the best bluetooth headphones I have ever had.Build Quality: Motorola has spent some years mastering these bluetooth stereo headphones and this set is proof in that development process. The headset is much lighter than they appear and can easily fit a wide array of heads. The comparitive in-the-ear model made by Motorola can be quite uncomfortable for those with a large head. I wear a 7-3/4 hat size and this pair is perfect.Sound Quality: This is a mixed review for sound. The sound quality is quite good and has excellent range. I most often use these headphones for watching movies and TV shows on my tablet and laptop and in these instances, I would rate them a 9/10. For music, they are closer to a 7.5 as they are not perfect in this area.Call Quality: Considering these are made by Motorola, it should not come as a surprise that these headphones have excellent call quality.Battery life: These headphones seem to last forever on a single charge. I have not directly measured the number of hours, but I use them frequently and seem to charge them once or twice a week max.Overall: This is actually my second pair of these headphones and I didn't really realize how much I used them until my pair was lost. I like to pair them with my tablet or laptop and then fire up a movie or catch up on some TV shows while working around the house. Being able to plant my tablet on the table and freely move about without cables is what makes these so special. You can also do the same connected to your phone.I simply love these headphones and with this price, it is an empeccable buy.

I primarily bought this headset for using with my iPad on the treadmill in the gym to watch podcasts.It does have good sound and is very easy to pair and use.However, it is very cheap quality. The shining part looks like metal but is really metallized plastic....you know like the one in cheap products.Also, another issue is that if you use it for jogging or while working out, your ears sweat and the sweat gets on the foam ear muffs. Well you cannot remove the foam to rinse once in a while as you can with some standard headphones.If you don't mind these issues it is really good value for money.
summary: Good sound, bad design, cheap quality

reviewText: received package within a week.  no problem pairing with my samsung phone.  sounds clear and fits my big head comfortably.  thinking about purchasing another one for work.  will wait to see if it works in a few months.

These head phones are great!  I have had them now for about 6 Months.  The charge holds very well, you can use any cell phone charger to charge these.  The sound quality is awesome even at very high levels.I haven't had any connection problems between my Droid 2 (android phone.) When you are running the head phone stay right in place, and its awesome when you are lifting, pushups, pullups, etc because no wires get in your way.  Also when i work out at home i can set my phone down on the other side of the room and move all around with my head phones.The only con i have which really doesn't bother me, the band that wraps around the back of your head is one size fits all, but i figured out a way to make it work i just tilt it upward a little bit.I high recommend this product, i have had 3 people buy from my recommendation.  And at the price its the best on the market.

I bought this brand new for about $30. At this price it is a bargain. The sound quality is amazing. Treble is crisp and clear and bass is alright. It also has a built in mic. You can use this for skype, games, music, etc. This mic is decent in terms of audio fidelity. The battery life is amazing. It lasts me hours 3 to 4 hours of gaming which is what I use it mostly for. I'd like to also note that you can charge this head set while using it. So if you don't have a pair of wired headphones, you can just connect the Motorola via Bluetooth and charge it at the same time. Charging to full battery is pretty fast. The led will be orange when it is being charged. It will switch to green when it is fully charged.The headphones are great for workout and fits comfortably on my head. However, prolong use of this headset will hurt your hears. I would say after 2 hours of use, you should take it off before your ears get sore.
summary: Painful after prolonged use. Excellent sound

reviewText: I purchased the Motorola S305 mainly for my iPod Touch. I disliked wired systems because I found the tangling of the wires annoying. The freedom of Bluetooth makes my iPod more enjoyable to use with my music and other apps. I also purchased a Bluetooth dongle (Medialink - USB Bluetooth Adapter) for my netbook with the intention of using the headset.Each transmitting Bluetooth device needs to be paired correctly with the headset. Pairing was straightforward with both my iPod Touch and my netbook. Once paired, the headset worked well with both devices.Note that the Motorola S305 is a headset (as opposed to just headphones) as it includes a microphone. It works very well with Google Voice, Voice Memo, and Skype on my iPod. The sound is excellent and the microphone produces very clear sound.I've never used a behind-the-neck headset before and only had over-the-head headsets. It took a while getting used to but once I did, I found them just fine. They are not adjustable for size but they me fit well and the pressure on the ears is not too great. I find however, that after about a half-hour, I need to take them off.They have built-in ear cushions and I'm not sure how they will wear over time. They also seem a bit fragile and I'm not sure how they will hold up. The manufacturer says that if the frames become bent they can be straightened out by carefully bending them. A feature that would have been nice is if they folded flat so that they could be stored in my netbook case.All in all I found it to be a very good headset.

reviewerName: Radical Technoid "We know we're right, we hav...
reviewText: I like these lightweight headphones. They rest comfortably on the ears and, for $40 headphones, sound decent. They paired with my Blackberry Torch perfectly and control it just fine. My only grip is the way they handle paring to more than once device.If they are paired to anything other than a phone then when you pair them to a phone you don't get the stereo audio profile, only the hands free. The idea is that you can listen to music from an MP3 player and receive phone calls from your phone. What I wanted to do was either use them with my tablet or with the phone. Other than that, they are fine.

Solid quality product that works perfectly with multiple phones and Bluetooth devices I've paired them with.  Light on your ears and plenty loud.  I've used these at the gym, while hiking and driving and found them comfortable and long lasting.  These are especially great in the car, as I can use the same charger as my phone to top them off.  Due to the open design, you will hear what is going on around you -- these do not reduce ambient noise -- and if you crank them up, your neighbors will be jamming with you, but at normal volume your conversations or tunes will be yours alone.
summary: Great product and quality build at a great price, with fast shipping

reviewText: These headphones work well and have quite good sound for the price. Had no connection problems with a variety of devices. The problem was that they are far and away the most uncomfortable headphones I have ever had. Tried to get used to it. Couldn't.

I used these for about a month of running, during which I ran about 50 miles.  The sweat and light mist from that month (never did I run in the rain) caused these to go out.  Don't buy these with the expectation they are even somewhat rugged.  I don't know what else somebody would use them for if not exercising...

I love how lightweight these are, and how easily they paired with my phone.  I use them several times a week at the gym, and also at my office (it gets loud in CubeLand).  Battery life is great - even when that I use them at the gym and then almost a full day at the office, I can usually get away with a day and a half (or so) between charges!  Recharge is quick too, usually I can go from completely dead to completely recharged in about an hour.

I'll address the reason this is only 4 stars right now- sound quality on phone calls. Sound quality to the headsets is fantastic- I love to hear conversations with both ears. However, Call quality to the caller, not so good; I've heard from many people that I cannot be understood on the call. Obviously, this is a microphone or software deficiency and something that Motorola should address.To the positive- everything else on these headphones works, as it should. Ilove that they pair easily, sound quality is great, and it's easy to switch from one device to another. I've tried a couple other headsets and come back to these.The predecessors to the 305's were the HT820- much larger, and I used them for 3 years before upgrading. I bought my original 305's from an e-tailer and the audio on one side went out within a month of purchase. I contacted Motorola who replaced them (with my return shipment) promptly. Since then,it's bliss.I charge 2x per day, about 15 minutes a piece (not charging after about 6 hours of use leads to a dead battery on my commute home- I literally wear these about 11 hours a day, 5 days a week).As long as you're buying new, you'll have these headphones for a good, long time.

I bought these primarily to listen to music on my iPhone while cycling. While the sound quality doesn't compare to myGrado iGrado Headphones, for bluetooth headphones at this price, it's good enough for casual listening and has exceeded my expectations.  The range is pretty poor and I've had a few instances of brief stuttering with my iPhone 4 in my jeans pocket (in its case); however, those intermittent issues are an acceptable trade-off for wireless convenience when working around the house or yard.  With the latest version of the iOS, all the playback controls  (play\pause, skip fwd & rev) on the headphones work. Call quality is very good and people have no idea I'm on a headset.Overall, these are fantastic for cycling as there are no wires to get in the way, at a reasonable volume the headphones allow in enough outside noise to hear traffic, and, with the phone in a jersey pocket or bike mount, the phones are close enough not to have any issues with range. On the bike, you will get a bit of wind noise. The neck band sits comfortably below a helmet so they are comfortable on long rides. For cycling these headphones are a great in combination withRAM Mounting Systems RAP-274-1-AP6U EZ ON/OFF Handlebar Mount for Apple iPhone 3G & 3GS. Battery life is good - my iPhone seems to run down faster when using bluetooth and GPS; good for at least 3-4 hours just listening to music.Pros- sound quality better than expected (decent, not great)- good call quality for phone- completely compatible with iPhone 4 and latest iOS- reasonably comfortableCons:- build quality- not particularly loud- very limited range (10' open air, 3' in a pocket)Ratings (1-5):Sound quality music: 3Sound quality calls: 4Build quality: 3ease of use: 5comfort: 4Value: 5
summary: Good for the price, good for cycling

reviewText: They easily connect to devices (have them connected to my macbook, ipad and galaxy note phone)I give them an 8 out of 10 on the sound scale (could use a little more bass). But they still sound better than any earbuds i've owned.Extremly durable - I've had them over a year, toss them in my gym bag, ran marathons with them, and do yard work with them...these things have taken a beating & still work as good as day 1.They fully charge within 45min...and that charge will last a good solid 6hrs of playback time. I maybe charge them twice a week maybe.can make phone calls with them, can control your music through your phone with them. Very convienent for runners.The one con in my opinion is they feel a little on the cheap side. But that only took like 2 or so weeks for me to get used to.overall - this is a solid purchase.
I bought these to use with my Galaxy tab, and i am not impressed, the sound is ok, but for what i paid for, I was expecting a lot more.

I like this headset.  The only thing detracting from 5 stars is the buttons are hard to find when the headset is worn.  Maybe this just takes some time to get used to.  But overall, these were a good buy for me.

As someone who bought other versions of Motorola's bluetooth headphones:Motorola 89307 MOTOROKR S9-HD Bluetooth Stereo Headsetand I can say this unit right here gets the job done.  ALL THE FUNCTION BUTTON WORK!!!!! (at least with my iphone 3gs) which is a problem with most bluetooth headsets. These things are light and comfortable to wear, priced very,very nice ($34). Minus one star because the sound quality of the unit is somewhat lacking.Im very please overall with this model..but buy beware, stay away from Motorola's S9, S9HD, and the new S10HD models, they neither work like they are supposed to and they are not moisture proof (despite they are advertised as being so).

I just bought these to use with my Xoom, and so far so good. I was listening to Dark Night of the Soul (ASIN: B003TJ3OY8) within 2 minutes of getting them out of the packaging and charged up (Motorola, what were you thinking on the packaging? I had to take a box cutter to the packaging to free them!). Sound quality is great, controls are easy to find by touch. I'll update later if I have any issues.
summary: Seems to be a good value for the price

reviewText: I'm impressed with the sound quality of this Bluetooth headset, mostly because it's Bluetooth. I haven't had great experiences regarding sound quality on Bluetooth devices. This one is different. The sound embodies crisp highs and full lows. Some headsets are mid-range only, but I'm happy to report these rein in the full scope of sound.They seem to have one small drawback: the volume. It's too low. At their loudest, they're just below where I usually listen to music. Not good for lawn mowing or anyplace where there is ambient noise. I hear conversations from the patio next door when I have them on at full blast. One weird little quirk about that: I like them for bike riding. With my Bose ear buds, they're very loud and I can't hear car traffic, but with the Motorola S305 on, I can hear the music pretty well while also detecting oncoming cars.Battery life is good, functionality is good, sound quality is good less the volume issue. It's very lightweight and flexible. Easy to use and quick to charge. I don't have any real issues with this unit except the volume. I would still recommend them for use with theApple iPod touch 32 GB (4th Generation) NEWEST MODEL.

I purchased the Motorola S305 in January 2013.  In November 2014 the battery no longer holds any charge.  I don't think I ever got "6 hours" of use out of it.  The most was a little over two hours.  In the past 3 months the unit was running one hour at most, and steadily declined.  It got down to 15 minutes, now no more.  Less than two years.Phone call quality is fair to poor.  Indoors in a quiet place call quality is good.  Fair means that people on the other end of the line might mention about the call quality and background noise.  Poor means people say they can't  understand the call.I'm not a great judge of sound quality, my hearing is not good, I do wear behind the ear hearing aids at times.  One thing I like is that this headset does fit with the hearing aids on or off.  And I also wear glasses.  The unit fits with or without any combination of glasses, hearing aids.  Music, speech and other audio sound very good with or without the hearing aids -- the unit sounds much better that sound from the various Thinkpad and Mac laptops I use.  After an hour+ with the hearing aids, glasses however my ear tips do feel a pinch.The headphones fit my big 7 5/8+ size head.  I have worn them for intense workouts in the gym and during active yard work on hot days.  A lot of sweat doesn't seem to bother them.I have had no problem syncing these with my Android phones, and with my Panasonic Bluetooth DECT 6.0+ home wireless phone base station.  I also have used these iPod Nano 6, with a bluetooth adaptor.  The Nano  was only able to drive the micro adaptor for a little over a hour though.  Functionality with the nano and the adaptor was good, pause, fwd/rev, all controllable via the headphone buttons.  Syncing with my Macbook Pro was tricky and  in the end not really reliably functional mainly due the Mac's poor Bluetooth handling of units like this headset with a mix of both Stereo-playback  and phone-headset bluetooth protocols.I like the buttons all on the right ear piece.  It took a few days of use to get the button positions down, but now I find they come easily, naturally.I have just ordered a different manufacturer's model as a replacement.
summary: Not good enough.  Battery life way overstated.  Phone call quality fair-to-poor.

reviewText: So the purchase I'm reviewing is actually my second set. I bought my first set just about a year ago and they crapped out after about 6 months of use. I wanted to write a really angry review about it but in reality, these were like $30 and for that $30, they did a hell of a job.I mostly wear these for my pedestrian/bus/train commute to work. The audio quality is great for both calls and audio. It's definitely much better than many $20 price range headsets/earbuds but it's probably not audiophile quality either. I don't know because I'm not that hardcore into sound quality. I'm told the mic picks up quite a bit of background noise but none so bad that I can't complete my calls. I'm not sure if my phone or the headset is to blame, but you see lots of Bluetooth interference on busy streets resulting in skipping. Certainly nothing so bad I can't deal with it though.Micro USB ports and easy pairing also make this a plus. They're great for my purposes but I think my last ones crapped out due to sweat from walking during my commute so I definitely wouldn't recommend for workouts. Otherwise, these are almost certainly worth the $30.
summary: Great Bluetooth Headphones (as long as you don't expect them to last)

reviewText: After reading all the good reviews on Amazon, I finally decided to buy this headphone because I have an iTouch (with the latest 3.1.2 firmware) and I wanted a wireless headphone for the freedom that it offers. I got it in a day after ordering using Amazon's prime shipping. Charged the headphone completely (until the green light came) and also paired easily with my iPod and also my laptop. But very soon into my hearing experience, I started getting pauses between listening to my iTouch. The audio lagged so many times even after a full charge that I was so disgusted and I am returning back this product. Also the ear fit is very uncomfortable and I doubt if anyone can wear this product for 30 mins or more. All in all, a very poor product that has disappointed me.

I wanted a pair of Bluetooth headphones for wearing while working around the house, on the car, in the yard, etc. I wanted to be able to pair with my phone for music and calls as well as with my computer for music and video. I settled on the S305s based on the price and other reviews. Here are my impressions so far:Pros:-Easily connects with my Galaxy Nexus and 2010 MacBook Pro and can have both connected simultaneously.-Decent sound quality (Mac owners search for Terminal command to improve bitrate.)-Reasonably small and light.-Micro USB charger.-Battery life is decent, I get between 7-8 hours on a charge.-Range seems decent but there are a lot of other variables (other device, wireless interference, walls, etc.)-I wear glasses and these do not interfere.-Works pretty well while running or cycling, not sure about sweat resistance though-Calls sound ok through the headphones, but callers reported that I sound better than usual when using the built-in mic.-Price seems reasonable for the performance.Neutral:-Volume controls don't seem all that easy to press, the other buttons are however-If you experience lag when watching video on your computer, consider using a program like VLC Player so you can control the audio delay to properly sync things up again. Not the headphones fault, but worth mentioning.Cons:-Neck loop is large for my head and just hangs in the back. This makes leaning your head against anything awkward. That's just the way some universal fit things are I suppose.-There is some "sound bleed". So if you're in a quiet environment such as a library you might disturb your neighbors with moderate to high volume.-Not really that comfortable in my opinionOverall these do the important things right and I am pleased with the performance (especially for the price). I'd recommend these to anyone who needs a decent of Bluetooth headphones without breaking the bank.
Easy to pair, and produce decent sound.  Controls are easy to use.  They are fairly comfortable, but not so good when wearing glasses.
summary: These work well, but do not play well with glasses.

reviewText: I'm using it with a Samsung Galaxy S3. The gain of the microphone when connecting earbuds, either those supplied with the phones or others, is very weak and people were constantly complaining that they had a hard time hearing me, so I was hoping a bluetooth device would work better.I've been using this one for about a month and so far I'm loving it...Pros:* Very comfortable to wear, even with sunglasses (thin temples) and a bike helmet.* Sound quality is very good. I really enjoy listening to music on the go* Holds a good charge* Charger is standard 5V thin USB, so you can use your Android phone outlet or USB adapter to charge it from either an electrical outlet or a computer (supplied adapter is outlet only)* microphone quality is pretty good, as long as I'm in fairly quiet surroundings, people report hearing me well* I can drive or ride a bike with them as the external sounds are not completely blocked* No wires! earbuds cables which constantly got tangled used to drive me crazy. No more!* Low price - great value for the moneyCons:* No charge level indicator - I need to guess. Even three leds for >80%, <20% would have been great* Takes some practice to get them connected to my phone. Bluetooth connectivity has always been a black art. The best way for me is to turn off bluetooth on the phone, and then turn it back on as I turn on the device.* Sometimes cuts in and out. I assume this is due to interferences. It rarely gets to a point where it is a real nuisance, but it does happen. For example, walking down the Chicago loop (downtown), it was cutting in and out so much that it was unusable, but in general works fine* Takes some time to get used to the controlsAgain, overall a great buy. If I'd lose it, I would buy it again without thinking twice.
summary: Excellent way to listen to music & audiobooks, and to talk on the phone

reviewText: I was very disappointed. This item did not work right out of the retail box. The charge light came on red and never changed to green. The headphones would not power on. I was looking forward to these. I processed a refund (and was grateful for the Amazon process). I will not reorder because I see from other reviewers, and from somebody I know that bought the same headphones, that the overall product quality is poor and my experience was not uncommon.
summary: Did not work right out of the box

reviewText: It's rare to find a product that meets your expectations; no more, no less. There are no bells and whistles. This is a bluetooth stereo headset, plain and simple. The music quality is amazing, it's SUPER easy to use, and all the buttons are in the right places. They are so intuitive that you actually don't even need to read the manual to know what each button does, it just feels natural. It's comfortable, I wear mine on average about 2 hrs a day and I often forget they are even on my head. I like wearing this to listen to podcasts and music while riding my bicycle. Often, someone will call my cell while I'm riding. I don't have to stop or get my phone out of my bag, I can just git the button and this headset will automatically stop my music and connect me with the call. Even more amazing, I can be riding at 15 mph and I can hear the caller perfectly, and she/he does not notice any windy noises. As soon as they hang up, I don't have to hit any buttons, the headset automatically start my music where it left off. I can also control my music with the headset (pause, next song, previous song, volume, etc...). The battery life is amazing. I've never had it die on me, so I'm actually not sure how long it lasts. I've used it for 2 hr long phone calls, and use it to listen to music on long runs/bike rides/while doing the dishes. I charge it about once to twice a week. It takes like 15 mins to charge too. I highly recommend this, especially if you want to use it while riding your bicycle!

I sleep fine in any bed, with (or without) any pillow.  I never send back dishes at restaurants.  I've never had a bad taxi driver.  I've never cried over a haircut, or even withheld a tip.  I'm really not a whiny person.But these headphones sure as hell don't fit my head comfortably.  The earpiece covers my ears at a strange angle.  The plastic bar piece that goes over the ear is bulky and uncomfortable.  The back part that's supposed to "hover" over your neck is weird fitting and looking.Maybe if I had giant ears that stuck out from my head and pointed forward...
summary: I must have a weird head...

reviewText: I used this moderately, about 45 minutes a day M-F for running and they worked awesome for the first couple months, now all of a sudden they wouldn't turn on, fiddled with that for a while, then the pause play button doesn't work now either.  Pretty disappointing that these headphones can't last even 90 days.  They have a one year warranty so I'll return them and hope the next unit works at least a year.

This is probably the third set of bluetooth headphones I have bought. The first one was theLogitech FreePulse Wireless Headphoneswhich had problems with the head band breaking and wore fingers out waiting for the headset to pair up with the provided bluetooth adapter.  However, this set paired up at once with my 4th gen iphone, my Entourage Edge and my Samsung netbook.  The sound is ok.  However, they get uncomfortable after an hour or so.

EVER.  I have owned these for about 3 years and they're still kicking.  Pairs easily, very durable, great battery life.  Sound is not super-loud or overly bassy--just pretty even.  Not great in a loud situation, but perfect for at home.  I use them on my commute, if it's cold out--keeps my ears warm !  I would highly recommend these--I own these and a pair of Backbeat Go2's, for when it's warm out.  Two of the best out there.

I wanted these for one thing.. to stay on my ears during a run.  They do just that.  Reception is what you'd expect from bluetooth headphones today, and they arent the most comfortable pair out there, but they wont move around once they're on your head.  Good value

I bought this as a gift for my husband who wanted bluetooth headsets to listen to music while working out at the gym.  They had the best reviews so I bough them and now my husband loves them so much I'm going to get a pair for myself.  Quality is incredible and he synced it in seconds.  Charge life isn't bad either.

These Bluetooth earphones are a good value for the price.  I use them with my Blackberry Storm2, primarily at the gym and in my home office.Pros:* Pair easily and reliably with my device.* Good sound quality.  They are not the same as a Bose over-the-ear wired headset - but they do cost 1/6 the price.* Construction seems fine.  I carry them around in my gym bag and in my car.* Battery life is fine.. Somewhere between 4-6 hours of use and recharges quickly.* Very lightweight.Cons:* Occasional skips, especially when the device is far away (more than about 15 feet) or in my pocket.* Design is a bit bulky, which is typical for over-the-ear styles.* Buttons are on the small side and somewhat hard to distinguish from each other.  However, I have seen much less usable button styles on other headsets.* Comfortable to wear for about 90 minutes, then the headband tends to become uncomfortable around my ears.For $35, I would purchase these again... or until someone produces a Bluetooth headset with a slimmer profile or equal or better sound quality.
summary: Good value in a low cost headset

reviewText: bought these for my wife after she liked using mine - they are great for twice the price, work very well for Audiobook on our Samsung & Apple players and a breeze to pair with either.

I absolutely love this headset! I have a Droid X, and can fully control music, phone calls, and text messages (with the help of a voice-text app) directly from the headset.  And with the huge range, I've actually misplaced my phone while cleaning my apartment, yet still being able to listen to music, and answer all calls and texts!

I work in a cubicle environment which can get noisy, so I often listen to music.  I was constantly forgetting I had my earbuds in and would move to the other side of my desk which would yank them out.  I also would get caught in the cord as I worked.  My husband bought me the Motorola S305 headset for my birthday and I love them!  I can move around my desk freely now.  In fact, I can go quite some distance from my desk and the sound quality is as good as when I'm sitting right next to my iPhone.  The earpieces slip over the top of the ears which I thought would be uncomfortable, but I wear them for hours with no problems.  Most of my co-workers don't even know I have them on since my hair covers them completely. My only complaint is I can't seem to find a carrying case for them.  I take the train to work and have them in my tote bag when they aren't in use.  They don't seem to be of the sturdiest constructions, so I am concerned they might get damaged without a protective case.

These little headphones do sound very good for inexpensive phones, good strong bass and clear treble. Being free of connecting wires seems wonderful, I must admit. The fit is very comfortable for me also. I was dissapointed that with my new 3rd generation iPod Touch 64 Gb, the phones will not advance to the next song or go back to the previous song with the push controls as they are supposed to do. I later found that the issue here is that Apple does not support the S305's particular Bluetooth profile (AVRCP). Neither will my iPod recognize the phones built in microphone for voice recording as a result of this same issue. The phones themselves are great, but for anyone expecting to use them with their iPods, this is definitely a problem to consider.
summary: Great Sound but Doesn't Work Right With iPod

reviewText: The Motorola S305 surprisingly does not sound as good as the Kinivo BTH220 (also sold under other names). The Kinivo also consistently had an easier time connecting to my iphone. However, the Motorola S305 looks and feels better than the Kinivo, and appears to be more durable.I would have given the S305 4 stars, but after three months of ownership, the + volume button has completely broken. The - button works fine. I experienced a similar problem with another Motorola model, but that problem took over a year to manifest. No, I did not drop or abuse these headphones. I hardly even used the volume buttons since controlling the volume with my phone is usually sufficient.These headphones are going in the trash.

I was excited opening the package. After reading the directions, I plugged the unit in to charge, and waited, and waited, and waited.  The unit never charged.  Sent it back. Gave it one star - bad quality control - disappointed.

My current Go Blue Beat EXS is running it's course and I was hoping this Motorola s305 would replace it. Though This s305 is lighter and feels nice on my head the sound quality (bass, mid, treble) is no way as good as my Blue Beat. This is saying alot considering this from a name brand over an off brand. I'm going to give this a try for a week to see if it's worth the keep.
summary: Not as good as my off Brand Go Blue Beat EXS

reviewText: Ok first of all, if you have a crappy, tinny sound being produced from these head phones, Step #1- get a different blue tooth adapter or update the drivers.  My phone (HTC G2) and the blue tooth adapter I boughtIOGEAR USB 2.1 Bluetooth Micro Adapter GBU421work AWESOME.  However the blue tooth adapter that's incorporated into my work laptop (IBM Thinkpad T410) absolutely sucks in terms of the sound quality I receive.The reviews that say these feel cheap - no cheaper than the $10 wired headphones.  Which lets face it, if you're spending this sort of money on a wireless set, yup, they're going to feel cheap.Range, microphone quality, fit, all very acceptable.  The set is slightly tight around my ears but I'm uncertain if its because I never wear an over the ears headset or if its the headphones.  I wear a 7.75" hat to give you an idea for sizing.100% recommend these.

My husband had been looking at various bluetooth headphones and really liked these but they were a little pricey at our local store. I found them on Amazon at a more reasonable price. My husband loves them. One caution though, if you have a DVD player that can access Bluetooth be careful. One night while I was watching tv my husband turned off his headphones and his cell phone 'high jacked" the DVD player and his music was playing on the tv!

I haven't taken the time to read the directions but these things are usually self explainable.  This one must have a learning curve. But once it works, it has good sound and comfy. Better than the last set by another maker I owned.

My family and I have three of these, and they work, but there are better products for the money.. This one does not fold up, does not fit the ear real well as it uses those foam pads which get hot and sweaty... The Artic Cooling is a better choice for your money... I have both. I use the Artic all the time, and it comes with its own case and charging cord. Buy the Artic.

Still like new after many years of use.Looking for an "Over the ear" near perfect Bluetooth headset for phone calls or listening to music during your workout? Look no further!Charge holds for many hours. All around great product.

I bought this headset for use with my iPad 2 for when I want to watch a movie or play Angry Birds and don't want to disturb anyone.  I thought that I would use them when I wanted to hear music or a soundtrack to a movie when I am at home, but I never do that for a few reasons which I will cover soon.  Here is what I like about this headset:*  It syncs with my iPad 2 pretty easily and I can walk to the other side of the house and it still works.*  They are really lightweight.*  The sound is pretty decent for a lightweight, Bluetooth headset, (even the bass is acceptable.)*  The price is pretty reasonable.Here are some of the things that I am not to crazy about:*  I really don't like the way that it fits.  It is difficult to keep in the right place over my ear and I don't like the way the headband has to go behind my head.*  When I am listening to music, a movie, or even the spoken word a person sitting next to me (like on an airplane) can hear what I am hearing enough to tell what is being said.  I have to really turn it down low to keep that from happening.*  Recharging it is kind of a pain.  I really have to look close to be sure that it is charging.That being said, I seldom use these except for when I am traveling mostly because of the way it fits.
summary: I use these with my iPad 2 when I am on a plane or waiting at the airport

reviewText: I have this headset connected to my Macbook Pro and iPhone. I can be listening to audio from my Macbook and take a call from my iPhone at the same time. They are also good for running and I don't have to take my iPhone out of my pocket because all the controls are on the side of the headset.
These are no Beats By Dre headphones, but they sound great. I've had these for a few years now and they work fantastic. Not to mention that you can hear your phone conversation in Sterio.

The head set band twists in the back and the ear cups separate away from my ears. The band also goes behind the ears and presses into the back of my ears and is very uncomfortable. This one may have been molded really bad. It keeps disconnecting from the phone and the phone is only 2 feet away. Keep shopping around.

The sound is great. But forget the microphone. I used the headset with VOIP to call a landline, and there was a noticeable delay of at least 2 seconds at both ends. My headset received good sound with the annoying delay, and the landline got a delayed tinny voice from me. (Ordinarily, my VOIP connection is crystal clear, so I don't believe it was the culprit.)
Bought these a couple years ago and work great with my ipod touch, Samsung tablet, and now my HTC One phone.  Whenever I break these, I will buy another set.

I really like these headphones. I am about to buy my fourth pair in two years. They have decent sound quality, plenty sufficient for my primary use of listening to audiobooks and podcasts, and talking on the phone. Since I am not an audiophile, they are okay for music but I prefer to use good headphones for "real" music. They have very good call quality. They are my go-to bluetooth headphones for most activities and very handy to be able to listen to music and be able to take or make calls.The downside is that the average life of them is six months before they start flaking out and they won't turn on any more. Usually before this happens the light won't go out on them even when they are turned off and they burn through the battery quickly. Yes, I am well aware of the battery reset process, which usually stops working after three or four months.But I can't be too hard on them since I wear them for exercise and outdoor activities and I sweat a lot, so the foam cushions get soaking wet. This is probably why they don't last too long for me since this likely affects the inner electronics and/or battery which is why they have such a short life for me. And it used to make me mad that they gave up the ghost so quickly. But, once the price dropped to around $30, I started considering them disposable and a 6 month lifespan was acceptable. I certainly would not pay more than $30 for them, though.These headphones also meet two other absolute requirements I have - they sit on top of the ears and don't completely cover it up, or stick in my ear like earbuds, which would lead to even more sweating - plus I get ear infections when using either one of these. And they charge with any micro-usb cable so can be used with any of the dozen chargers I have lying around at home or work. I really ought to give them five stars for just these features alone since there are very few other headphones that meet these two criteria, but with the short life span of them, I really can't.Edit, 6 months later: Here I am looking for another pair since the ones I have are about to go. But I won't buy them this time since the price has risen to $40, granted that's the price including shipping since I have Prime. But they don't last long enough to justify that cost. So I am off to buy the Inland equivalent of these, the ProHT, since they _are_ $30 at my local Microcenter. The buttons are not as convenient and it charges with a mini instead of the preferable micro usb, but I can't bring myself to spend $40 on disposable headphones.
summary: Best disposable bluetooth headphones I own

reviewText: I researched and thought a lot before getting these headphones. They were like most selling blutooth headphones around with very mixed reviews. But when I finally got them and used them...I never had a moment of regret. They work great, sits good on my long ears and looks cool around the neck. I do have some hiccups sometimes like problems pairing with my phone, but no big deal. I like the sound quality for both music and calls. They are very efficient and highly sensitive for calls especially. The people on other side can hear everything clearly, even some sounds which I don't notice. I am happy with these.

CONS: These headphones HURT to wear. The reason being is there is no padding whatsoever on the part that actually rests on your ears. The best way I can describe it (which you cannot see in the picture) is imagine a long rectangular piece of plastic, now fold that in half so you now have a long u-shaped piece of plastic. Now form that piece into the curve shape you see in the picture. Now strap this around your ears with the weight of both sides (granted they are pretty lightweight) supported solely by the tops of your ears. Keep in mind, you have a two plastic edges sitting on top of each ear. After about 15 minutes of running I have to take them off. No amount of re-positioning helps. A better design would have made the headband part a solid cylinder so there are no edges, or placing a small section of padding on the part that actually rests on the ears.PROS: For the money, they sound like you would expect. I have no complaints in that department. For my 2nd Gen IPOD touch, the volume works, play/pause, but the track forward/reverse buttons do not work.All in all, I wish I would have gotten something else :(

I was skeptical about Bluetooth headphones, and have stayed away from even trying them mostly because of the price. But the Motorola S305's cost half what other Bluetooth headphones have in the past so I decided to give them a try. Mostly I've been very impressed with these, though I do have a few problems.First, the sound quality is very good - on par with a decent set of wired headphones of similar price. I haven't found there to be any static, though occasionally (and inexplicably) the sound will cut out for a half second, which can be annoying. It doesn't happen that often though. The range on these is remarkably good - I bought these specifically for jogging, so the range would only ever have to be about 2 feet, but I've also used them at my desk and I really appreciate the freedom to get up and walk around up to 20 feet away with several walls between my phone and me. When the headphones do get out of range, they just disconnect, and then reconnect when they're in range again. The volume is also very good, and although they do not cover the ears completely, the volume can be turned up to the point where it covers most outside noise. If I were choosing headphones just for work or travel, I might choose something with greater noise isolation, but since I chose these for general use and especially exercise (where size and weight are the main consideration) these work nicely. The headphones are quite comfortable, more so than other behind-the-head earphones I've tried. Wearing them for a couple hours at a time did not cause any numbness or pain. They are also pretty secure, and jogging with them hasn't been a problem. I appreciate the fact that these charge with a micro-USB cable, which means that I can charge with my PC and a standard cable when I'm on the road. Sadly, the included charge is a hard-wired micro-usb type, unlike the ones that take a powerplug and provide standard USB-out, so if you don't want to bring the power charger with you you'll have to buy a micro-USB cable.My biggest problem with the headphones so far is the buttons. There are a total of 7 buttons; one for power (with indicator LEDs) and volume up and down all located on the rim of the headphones, and then a D-pad layout for call, play/pause, >> and << on the outside of the right earphone. The buttons located on the rim are loose and feel cheap. Worst of all, they rattle when jogging. That clickety-clack is quite loud when it is right next to my ear, and it is distracting. The other buttons all work fine, though as other reviewers have noted the >> and << buttons don't work with the iPhone/iPod Touch because of Apple's software. I've also found that I have to be a little careful in handling the headphones because it is easy to accidentally press the "call" button, which automatically triggers a call to the last person you called, and that can be somewhat embarrassing.My final annoyance is with the auto-power-off feature, which does not seem to actually work. The manual states that if the headphones are unused for 5 minutes, they will power down, but they obviously just go in to "sleep" mode and will automatically wake if there's an incoming call. This can be frustrating since the headphones might be 20 feet away in another room but when someone calls, the headphones will take over the call and I've found myself on many occasions talking into my phone while the person on the other end is talking through the headphones. This is, I'm sure, an issue that my phone is just as likely to be the cause of, but it's worth noting because it does happen a lot. Just make sure to turn the headphones off when not in use and it won't be a problem.Reading that last bit of my review one might get the idea that I'm not happy with these headphones, but that's not true; I think they're good for the price, and I would certainly recommend them to anyone who is looking for an inexpensive pair of wireless headphones for office or exercise. But those looking for the best at any price are likely to find more expensive headphones better.
summary: Very Decent Headphones for the Price

reviewText: I was looking for a set of wireless headphones to wear at work.  I prefer the behind the head method.Likes:1). Comfortable wear, even for hours at a time2). Style and design.  Button location is good once you get used to it.3). Audio prompts as the unit is turned on and offDislikes:1). Short battery life.  Sometimes it's difficult to get through an 8 hour day listening to the radio.2). Difficulty in installation.  Had to scour the internet for additional drivers for Windows 7.
I've been using these headsets daily for over 2 years now.  They don't fall off and are comfortable to use for over 4 hours.  I've replaced the foam cushions once (google it for instructions).

I got this headset because I was tired of using a clunky wired headset that sat on top of my head and I wanted to experiment with wireless headphones.PURPOSE: I want to listen to streaming music on my computer while not disturbing others if I am in my small apartment, a coffee shop, an airport, or anywhere else.PROS:-- An acceptable sound range (nothing amazing like high-end headsets)-- Wireless-- Light to wear-- Don't blare music where others who are nearby can hear it-- Has a microphoneCONS:-- Pairing was not super easy on a computer. Kept dropping and starting up again.-- Distance range is laughable. The signal started to fade when I walked into my apartment's kitchen and completely stopped when I went into the bathroom.  Again, I am in a very small apartment. Most times, I only need it sitting at the computer but it'd be nice to have tunes playing if I walk away for a minute.-- The music skips a little with short distances (5-10 feet away).  I have a high speed internet connection so that's not the issue.  This means reception can be spotty on the balcony which is literally right next to my computer area.-- The buttons don't work with Windows Media Player or an internet browser playing Pandora (or any other music site).  These downsides aren't obvious after reading the product description because it focuses on cell phone or iPod/iPhone.  Maybe there is a way to rig it up but it would be great if these features were seamless for users (the buttons serve no purpose to me while on my computer).I am not blown away by the headset but being wireless and having a cheap price (1/2 a Logitech headset I was considering and much less than the Beats) allows me to look past the complaints.

I bought these for a plane ride about 18 months ago and used them without issue with a couple of iphones (4), an older ipad, an fairly new ipod, an imac, etc. Having no issues with them (turned them on, used all the buttons, worked OK) on the Apple stuff, I didn't think much about them for a while... Even put them aside for about a year... (Hey, I moved, changed jobs, etc.) Eventually, I came back across them and wanted to use them with a Gateway T-1628, Vista Sp2 laptop. I'd used them before on an XP machine, and they were, "OK," so I thought, "next." But, Oh, baby - what a mess! Had to add a bluetooth adapter to the laptop... Fine. Until I tried several... No way to link up with these headphones to use them as I'd been using them with the Apple stuff! Turns out Microsoft took more and more features out of their bluetooth "stack" until the S305s were limited to Skype-like stuff. Weird! Figured out I could buy some software from [...] (from $20-30), or, I could just give up on this particular idea. Yay for Appple and its support of commonsense. The headphones themselves were OK with my imac and phone. Very pleasant, actually, to just fire them up and go about my business. Sound quality, at this price, was excellent. Range was the advertised 30 feet or so - even through the walls of the house. Early buyers apparently wanted to use these to exercise. No. These things would soak up water like a sponge and they have several obvious holes in them. But, for around the house stuff - light work - these have been fine. If they worked with the PC stuff without additional grief, I'd give these a "5" at this price. But, they don't... Or, won't without too much (my opinion) effort. Kudos for the batteries, by the way. After leaving them sitting around for so long, I just charged them up again and they've been fine... I've yet to run the battery down since I've started using them again. They just keep working.
summary: Yay..! For moble phones and macs... Boo for PCs!

reviewText: I've been eyeing this headset for a while. Someone splurged and got them for me for Christmas. Overall, I am very pleased with the gift.Connection: Easy to connect to iPhone - my primary device. And the range is suitable. I've run all over my first floor without an issue - clear all around. I don't see myself needing much more than that.Comfort: Putting your head on a pillow or leaning back on the couch? You may want to choose another headset as you may bump the neck wrap on these and push the headset around. Wearing a hat that goes past your ears (beanie)? This can be difficult (You can put the beanie over the headset in some cases). Glasses can be a pain too, depending on what style you have. However, if you are sitting up, walking around, no hat, wearing a baseball cap, etc., then these work great and are very comfortable. Where they wrap over the ears takes some time to get used to, but that's about it. I run with these, and they stay where they are supposed to and feel great, start to finish. Lightweight and cozy. And no wires!Sound: Pleasantly surprised. Excellent quality for a bluetooth headset. Music and calls come in crisp, clear, and perfect for my needs. The mic works great as well. I have had no complaints from those I've been speaking with regarding call quality, so I'm happy.Quality: The plastic wrap has a little give to it, but I don't want to put it to the test. This is the only part of the headset I have long term concerns about.Wishful thinking: I wish these came with an adapter that was compatible with the latest iPod Nano. I'll be hunting for an adapter soon. I also wish there were controls on both ears. Maybe play on one ear and pause on the other. With gloves on, it's difficult to track down the proper button on the single ear panel. Lastly, I wish they came with a case or folded neatly to put away. I don't want to stuff them in my bag, so around the neck is about the only storage I have - unless I purchase a third party case.
This headset is an excellent "ALLY" to my LG...Mp3s sound good....during a call,the mic pics up and puts out good and clear.....Comfortable "behind the ear" fit.....

As other reviewers have written, these headphones will not hold up to sweat/liquid exposure. But then again, they aren't intended to. The purpose of the headphones is to have wireless access to your music/phone while doing leisurely activities, which they achieve almost flawlessly. They aren't meant to last through rigorous exercise routines. So if you are looking for a product fulfilling that purpose, then move on, they're not for you. The sound quality is surprisingly really good; the music comes through clear and crisp. On that topic, however, they could use improvement on interference and range, as you will notice gaps in playback if you stray too far away from your device (a microwave *as expected* causes the signal to stop working entirely). The construction does feel a bit fragile, but If handled with the care a high tech pair of headphones deserves then you'll be fine. They are extremely lightweight and feel natural when worn. The controls are conveniently placed and work great. I don't recommend buying these if you're going to primarily use them for phone calls because the caller on the other end will notice a slight distancing of your voice (I imagine due to the placement of the microphone). reviewText: UPDATE July 2010, re Moto Droid:This product is fine for some items, but keep it away from your Droid. I relied on it, for months, with my Moto Droid. Then weirdness started-- the screen would spontaneously jump up and down; actually make selections as if I had clicked an icon, when I hadn't touched the screen; etc. When a series of soft reboots and factory resets didn't cure the problem, I contacted Verizon. At the time, I had no clue why my baby was sick. In any event, Droid #2 arrived shortly thereafter.Because I would sometimes go a week or two without using this product, I didn't initially make the connection. Then one day, I attached it to Droid #2 and immediately saw that screen weirdness again. *That's* when I realized what probably caused my woes with the initially purchased Droid. Fortunately, my quick disconnect prevented further/prolonged screen hassles.Please accept my apologies for the earlier review. In my own defense, I note that everything was fine for months. Looks to me like -- at least with the first batch of Droids, some sort of build up occurs before the Droid has its version of a resulting nervous breakdown. With later released Droids, you get immediate clues to what amounts to "wrong charger, Sherlock!".Meanwhile, I grabbed two SPN5334A wall chargers (long cord, thankfully), a car charger, plus a spare battery -- all OEM. (Note: a trip back to the Motorola site confirms the 5334A *is* compatible with the Droid X. {huge grin})================One word: amazing! I have juiced my Moto Droid about 3 times, and only now have I  replugged this device into an electrical socket. Even then, there was still some juice left prior to the recharge.Initially, I had planned on getting a spare battery and battery-specific charger, but decided to chance this item for the overall convenience factor. Just seemed it would be much easier to toss this into my bag, than the whole spare-battery deal. After *studying* the assorted reviews here, I can only say I'm soooo glad I bit the bullet. The bonus factor is that I can charge dang near anything, given the assorted tips in the box, including hubby's decidedly non-hiTech phone. Tried it on my iPhone 3GS, which is headed to CraigsList (yes, the Droid is THAT good!); also worked as advertised.I assume you're looking here for the best bang for the buck. Don't be penny wise and pound foolish. This thing is great!Final point: This was not available to purchase directly from Amazon, but a 3rd party merchant yielded the same effect (Prime membership, free 2-day delivery). Up-front cost appeared higher, but it was actually comparable given shipping/handling cost considerations.=====[I am a member of Amazon Vine. However, I learned of this device only by running assorted searches via Google and here at Amazon. I paid out of my own pocket, and for the record, would do it again-- in a heartbeat! In short, Vine had nadda to do with this purchase.]

reviewText: I got my packet of these just yesterday, and boy, am I glad I got a pack of three, 'cuz I needed every single pack to successfully apply one set! The plastic LCD screen covers were cut to fit my LG EnV Touch just fine, but getting everything clean and pristine enough for a truly successful install was a task. If you're careful about washing your hands well, and completely cleaning and degreasing your phone's screens, AND you take PLENTY of time to align these screen protectors just right, I'm sure that you'll find they're worth every penny. But I had to make multiple attempts before I got the covers to stick properly to my phone without any bubbles trapped below.If you use a spray eyeglass lens cleaner with the small cleaning cloth that comes in each package, and really get your screen glass clean, then take as MUCH time as needed in as dust-free an environment as you can get to, you'll probably have success putting these over your phone's screens. Just be sure to try your best not to bend the covers overmuch, use the cheap paper "squeegee" to help smooth them out (you might also want to line the covers up on an angle before gently laying them down, going from one end slowly down to the other to get them to stick), and keep the extra screen protector packs handy, 'cuz you'll probably need those, too, before you're done. The packaging on these also describes them as "washable and reusable". Uhh, not so much there, with that. I actually DID try washing one of these with soap and water in an attempt to reuse it. If you're okay with big water spots on your screens, sure, they're washable and reusable. But if you actually want your phone's glass screens to look clean, don't believe that. I don't know why the manufacturer thought it was wise to suggest that, because it just isn't true.Since I'm still not completely satisfied with the way that the interior screen protector looked after three + application attempts (especially since the corners don't stick if you try to lift them to reposition the covers - they just never bend back and stick in place after you do), I'm seriously considering ordering another pack of these, just to have on hand, in case I decide to try ONE...MORE...TIME to get the interior screen properly covered and protected.These are worth the purchase price, if you've got the patience to really work at getting them onto your phone just right.

I've been looking for a long time to buy Bluetooth stereo headphones for the workouts in the gym - I got tired of having to deal cords that would get tangled up during the workouts or would become a mess in the gym bag. When this model came out I jumped at the opportunity to buy them since they were the first stereo Bluetooth headset with a form factor that is appropriate for wearing in public. (Most of the other ones are too big and just scream "Look at me, I am a dork!") And since I bought them a little over a year ago, I have been extremely satisfied with them - for the most part. Here are a few pros and cons that I have come up with.Pros:1. Comfortable enough for a daily workout. Even with my moderately large head, I did not have much of a comfort issue with wearing them every day for a couple of hours. I would not recommend wearing them for more than three hours in a row though. But that would be the case with most headphones anyways.2. Easy setup. I had no problem connecting them to either my cell phone/mp3 player or my laptop.3. Decent range. As long as there is an uninterrupted line of sight between the linking device and the headset, you can use them on the other side of a large room or a smaller gym. Comes in handy when working out and don't want anything attached to any part of your body.4. Decent music playback sound.5. Decent battery life. For a relatively small device like this one, it was pleasing to find out that it did not have to be recharged more than a couple of times a week with standard use.6. As a phone earpiece it is useful to have around the head headset because it improves stability a lot. All of my other earpieces fall out of my ears way too easily.7. Being transferred from the mp3 player to the phone when receiving an incoming call is really useful and cool. This works with iPhone as well.Cons:1. It would be really useful if these headphones were collapsible. In that case they could be taken with you in your pocket almost anywhere you go. Plus, it would avoid dangers of having them twisted while stored in your bag.2. Touch-sensitive controls are too sensitive and very, very small. It took me a while to get used to them.3. The stereo feature works only for music. When using them for calling, only the left earpiece delivers sound, which is sort of weird. This takes some time to get used to.4. For some reason, when I linked them to my laptop, they got de-linked with my cell-phone. I had to go through the whole process again to have them back in the desired configuration.5. When using it with iPhone, the track-skipping buttons don't work.6. When using it with iPhone, the headphones don't work with all applications. This turned out to be annoying and inconvenient when I tried using them with Skype.Unfortunately, a few weeks ago one of the touch-sensitive controls broke, and now I can't decrease the volume. This is really annoying because other than that they still work great. I tried sending them back to Motorola, but apparently they don't fix products that are bought through Amazon, EVEN WHEN THEY ARE BRAND NEW! This is extremely annoying to say the least. I decided to buy a new pair, and found another one on Amazon for $40. (If at the moment all the available ones are more expensive than that, you may want to wait a bit.) Since this price is about 2.5 times cheaper than what you could get in any AT&T; store, it seems to me a worth-while investment. I am now on my third pair, but I figured that paying about $40 a year for something that I get to use every day is worth it.

reviewText: I could't believe the low cost of these earbuds considering their build quality. Due to the big sound effects and lots of bass there are reverbs and the sound gets muddy and lose some clarity. I don't have a problem though because these still sound great for what I paid.Be careful about your hearing and watch the volume level when using these because the sound pressure is slightly strong, especially the bass hits the eardrum harder than other earbuds I've used. Although its nice that they tone down the high end frequencies so they don't suffer from sharpness found in many cheap earbuds.Overall, these earbuds has a warm sound with good bass kick and does not suffer from sibilance, but could improve on midrange clarity.

I bought this charger and a compatible back over for my Palm Pixi plus. The original back cover was almost broken due to daily charging process via the cable.  Touchstone charger is really convenient, especially when you have to charge the phone everyday at least once.

I bought this wireless charging dock mostly out of curiousity.  My biggest question was, "Does it actually work?".The answer is a resounding YES.This is a very well-designed product that makes me wonder why I bothered fiddling with a micro-USB plug every day to charge my phone for as long as I did.  It isn't that plugging in the Pixi is at all challenging - it certainly is not.  It's that the Palm dock is so incredibly good.Simply plug the dock into the Palm power adapter and set your Pixi on top of the angled dock.  The magnets within the Touchstone cover and the dock align the phone properly for you.  The dock's charging surface angle is another well-engineered feature.  It sets the phone up slightly so you can see the screen, without it sticking up out of a dock like an iPod.This dock will NOT work with non-Palm power cords or chargers.  I suspect the reason is that the specific amperage coming from the transformer is required to let the magneto-electric field in the dock work properly.  I'd imagine that if you could find a charger with the same amperage output (not just the same voltage), it would also work.  If I find out either way, I'll follow up.This product is a must-buy (I'm getting another one) for Palm owners!
Awesome devise. Work perfectly. Best dock station I've ever seen. Just place it on it and your phone already charging, phone calls automatically goes on speaker.

I love how it charges just as fast as when the phone is plugged in. I'm very tempted to buy one for my car since it works so well. I highly recommend it!

reviewText: I like this dock with the Pre2. It turns on the clock, and the speakerphone if a call comes in. It was fussy with the Pixi Plus. Had to be perfectly centered. Not worth the effort with that phone.
