reviewText: Makes charging easy. (Mostly.)I use this to turn phone into a bedside clock and alarm.IT Needs the charger unit and cord, not always includedbut you should have one already. Nice to have an entireextra cord/charger for travel or other locations.There seems to be some sort of repeatable problem ofnot going over an 83% charge when charging this way.Often it is 100%, but as many times as not is 83%.I do not know if this is an exact placement thing as Ijust charge with the cord once in a while if I notice this happen.Edit 3/2013. I went back to charging with the cord plugged in direct.The unit was unstable at charging to 83% too often.I will use this again but glad I got it a LOT cheaper than list price.

These are ideal for charging HP Veer, Palm Pixi (with magnetic back), Palm Pre 2 etc. Very easy, just keep on the slider, and take out after charging, when phone call comes etc. Also they act as a display of clock when charging. Especially useful in nights to see the time in a dimly backlit screen. Incredible invention from Palm/HP, but alas the market did not welcome the HP phones after they acquired Palm. I wish if Palm remained independent if they would have innovated more.

I purchased this only because I think the design of where the plug input on the phone is terrible. You have to slide the phone open showing the QWERTY to be able to pry the tiny plastic flap to recharge and or use the data port for this phone. With the charging dock you just lay the phone on it and you'll feel the magnetic pull and that's it, your phone starts charging. I have the Verizon version so the Touchstone phone back already is setup to use the dock but from some of the reviews the sprint version you have to purchase the back cover for this to work.I'm glad I purchased it and it works great!UPDATE:There seems to be defective Touchstones out there and mine was one of them. After contacting Palm 3 times and of course being told 3 different things. With some research I found that there is an issue with the Touchstones. Something to do with the magnet inside. Basically they won't fully charge the phone (gets to 97%) and then the phone keeps beeping every 5 seconds telling you that the phone is charging. Palm was nice enough to send me a brand new replacement and its now working correctly.

reviewText: I got this for my SGS3. I picked up the Samsung back cover on e bay....this works fine with it, but the phone(with out a case on) barely stays in place. You have to get it just right for it to start charging and it is very touchy...u move it the slightest, it stops working. The sloped design of this thing is makes it more difficult than a flat surface.O, did I mention it won't work with even a slim rubber case on the phone. I have this case:GreatShield Guardian S Series Slim-Fit S-Line Design TPU Case for Samsung Galaxy S3 - BlackMight as well just plug the phone in if I have to go through the hassle of removing my case.I assumed that this would come with the cable and wall plug you need to actually use it....but no...this is the DOCK ONLY! (the seller has since added this info into the title of the listing)You must have a micro usb cable with a very thin head, because the "tunnel" in the back of this dock that the cord goes in is very narrow. Lucky, one of my older Samsung phones cable was small enough....and I have my own usb charger....but no indicator lights on the dock...I found a much better solution:Qi wireless Charger receiver pad for Samsung Galaxy S3 S9300Nokia DT-900 Wireless Charging Plate - Retail Packaging - RedI can confirm that these 2 products work perfectly with my slim case on the phone. The Nokia pad is a tad smaller than the S3, but it sit on there much better than the palm touchstone.

reviewText: This device was wonderful while it worked!.  It quit after about 9 months.  It might be the special back required for the phone, to be able to use this charger, but after multiple switching around of cords, I believe it is the charger that failed.  This is, after all, a type of transformer to change AC current to DC, and I think something in the device failed.

What can I say, it works as advertised with no issues.  FYI I found out that the touchstone only works with palms ac wall adapter because before I purchase the touchstone I've been using a two way usb outlet.
This is another one of those items that's pretty simple, it does 1 thing and does it well.  I used to "hack" wireless charging into my S3 phone and it did it's part perfectly.

I bought it from BobTronics. At first I thought it doesn't have wall charger etc and found a better price at verizonwireless. But when it arrived, it included everything along with USB. Very happy with the price. The product works great, though will update its long term use later. I don't think you can transfer data with it, or even charge from computer. I still have to try myself, but that is what I heard. That is a bit disappointment.
I had no chance to use it because it is the charging dock only! It comes with no USB cable whereas I found most USB cable will be too big to insert in the dock.
Plugged it in and did not work. Did not bother trying to figure out which from the shipment was broken (i.e., stone or back). I'm sure it would have been great had it worked.

The Touchstone back and charger work perfectly, as expected. The original back is kind of a pain to remove. Luckily nothing was broken during the process. This kit is much easier than having to pop out the USB cover to charge it.Just make sure you purchase it for cheaper than the ridiculous seventy dollars it is retailing for.

reviewText: Just like the Pre itself, the Touchstone is an adventure to unbox.  Everything is neatly packed in a way that looks more like a museum display than a regular consumer product.The back was fairly easy to change out on the Pre itself.  Following the instructions to work around the original cover with a fingernail to "pop" it off worked with a little effort.  The new induction back went on very easily.The "Touchstone" itself is surprisingly heavy and sticks better than expected.  On the first try, I did not get it exactly where I wanted it on the nightstand - I nearly lifted the loaded and heavy nightstand off the floor to get the Touchstone pulled free.The magnets in the base and phone back work to align the two so that charging can commence!  The only thing to be aware of is that when the phone is on the Touchstone, the face lights up with the time (currently, there is no option to have the phone remain dark while on the Touchstone).  If you need a totally dark room for sleeping, this could be a problem.I'm so happy with the Touchstone that I want to get a second for traveling and plan to get an actual piece of stone (countertop) to "permanently" mount it too since removing it once it's stuck is not so easy.
summary: The Easiest Way to Charge Your Pre

reviewText: This is probably the best add-on for my Pre that I could have gotten. First off, the flat black backing makes it less slippery so if it doesn't slide around. Second, the magnetic base is such a easy way to charge my Pre. I rush in the mornings sometimes and I hated having to stop, unplug the cord, pick it up off the ground and close the cover and then leave. Same thing with the evenings when I get home, I'm tired and I just want to set my Pre down, not mess with a cord and cover in order to charge. So, this is definitely a great investment for it. Lastly is an added bonus: I use my Pre as my alarm, but I couldn't always as it would slide across the table before I could turn the alarm off, but now it sits at an angle and I can see the time at night without being blinded and it doesn't slide everywhere when my alarm on it goes off.Simply, I love my Touchstone.

I bought this kit for my wife. She found the touchstone quite cool.  The touchstone kit allows you to charge the Palm Pre without the annoying process of removing the micro-usb cover to insert the micro-usb charging cable into the phone.The kit comes with the phone back panel and one dock (hockey puck).  The dock has a reusable sticky surface on the bottom to hold it firmly onto your desk.You connect the dock to AC power via a micro-USB cable.  The kit does not include the micro-usb cable or the AC adapter - these come with your phone.  The instructions state that you should not connect the touchstone dock to a computer via USB; I think the average computer USB port may not deliver sufficient electrical current.The next question is, do you want to buy additional docks to charge your phone at the office or in the car?  You can order an additional dock separately.  If so, you may also need to buy an additional the micro-usb cable and AC power adapter (or car charger).
summary: Touchstone rocks - but be sure you have all the right parts

reviewText: Charges quickly and adds functionality to the Palm Pre.  When the phone rings I just pick it up to answer it.  Otherwise, I can just answer the phone while it is still sitting on the touchstone and the phone automatically switches the speakerphone on.  The base "sticks" to my desk/table and is easy to move from one place to another.  For the price it should have come with the OEM charger and cable.  Amazon had the best price at the time I purchased mine.  Using the touchstone is more convenient than having to remove the charger port cover on the Palm Pre every time I need to charge.  It also makes all my friends with iphones jealous (that plus my phone bill and reliable coverage).

reviewText: It's definitely more convenient than having to pull that little flap back every night. Just position it correctly on the touchstone & you're good to go.

I've had it running for 2 days now and everything seems to be working great. I really wanted to give this product at least 4 stars, but a couple of issues held me back:1) The Amazon ad lists this as a New product. The battery I received is most definitely a refurbished original Palm battery. It physically looks more worn than the battery I was replacing. But for $5, I'm OK with a refurb. And a refurb that charges up to 1088 mAh is good enough for me. They should just advertise as Refurbished.2) The battery arrived completely discharged. Not one ounce of juice in it. That means that my phone had to be off for at least 15 minutes while it charged up to 5% before the operating system would actually boot.3) The first time I installed the battery, the screen showed the big empty battery icon that it gives until the battery reaches 5% so the OS can boot. But instead of getting to 5% and booting, about 25 minutes went by and the screen icon changed to a big battery with a question mark in it...then the screen just went off. I was worried that I received a bad battery and thought I would have to return it. But I took the battery out, put it back in, and the second time it operated properly.But as I said, I really do recommend this product. I will probably buy another one for my wife's Pixi. reviewText: Like many smartphones, the Palm Pixi, Pre, Pre Plus, and Pre2 are battery hogs, but the Palm phones' tiny batteries make it even more evident.  You can increase your battery life by connecting to WiFi and disabling 3G whenever possible, by keeping Touchstones around the house/in your car/at work, and by configuring your apps to sync sparingly when on 3G, but you will inevitably drain your battery dry at some point.Ideally, you should top off your lithium ion batteries every chance you get, because fully discharging them on a frequent basis actually decreases their useful lifespan.  However, for less than $5, this battery is a good backup for those times when you need to go longer than 8 hours between charges.

reviewText: I bought this case for my husband. reviewerName: Joel Avrunin "Electrical Engineer who loves S...
reviewText: I received my Skinomi on Friday.  I nervously opened the box, and was amazed to find a little spray bottle of solution, with the skin itself and installation card hidden in the cardboard. Knowing it is a super-high-tech sticker, I was a little nervous about installing it.I would recommend making sure you clean the surface really really well, and make sure to do the installation where you have good lighting.  I sprayed my fingers, and then went to remove the protector.  One thing the instructions did not make clear was how to even peel the protector off the backing.  I could not get it up, and I was afraid to crease it.  I finally removed the entire thing from the back (not just the die-cut middle, but the square edges), and once it was removed, I could easily remove the die-cut middle with wet fingers.To be honest, I thought during installation I was messing the whole thing up.  I used the microphone hole as an alignment fiducial, thinking that of all things, the microphone better be clear.  It wouldn't matter if the ear speaker was a little covered.  Amazingly, I got the entire sticker aligned, and then I used the card to smooth it out.  About 5 minutes later, I noticed it had started to set, so I was done.  At that point, I found a bubble!  The bubble was trapped on all sides by set plastic---no way out!I put my phone down and went to bed.  I have no clue how this thing works, but there was no bubble in the morning, and all streaks were gone.  Where did the bubble go?  I do not know.  I do know that my pre screen is now protected, and honestly, this thing looks better that the screen by itself.  My only complaint is that it is a little less slick, but that's a small price to pay.  The protector also seems to show finger prints less, so less need to wipe the screen.5 stars---highest recommendation.***UPDATE 5 MONTHS LATER***The screen protector is still going strong.  I have had thin plastic sheets on my PDA screens back as far as my original PalmPilot.  None have stood up to abuse like the Skinomi.  It is part of the phone--I never even notice it.  It is more durable than the screen and protects it quite nicely.  I just wanted to update and say this is well worth the money.
summary: Absolutely awesome - not too hard to install, looks better than without

I have had the NT70T for a few months now and it is easier the best battery charger I have had for one simple reason- I don't have to remember anything other the itself.By having the cables built in, it always ready to go and/or be charged. I don't have to carry a separate cable (with a differ plug). Plus you still have 2 usb ports to use for other devices if you need (help a friend out maybe?)I'm able to get 2 to 3 charges of my phone (Galaxy Nexus) out of it. It's also able to charge my Blackberry, mifi, Contour camera (with mini adaptor) and everything else I have tried with it.I also love the fact the botton is recessed  since it keeps it from being turned on by accident. And the auto off once you disconnect it is great. Just grab your phone and go.Simply put, you are going to be hard pressed to find another charger that is as convenient as this (unless you have an iSomething maybe- still compatible with a cable).

This thing is so useful i actually got 2. All smartphones (specially android devices) drain battery like there's no tommorow. This thing will let you last one full day(My 1 full day is About 20 hours of continuous non stop heavy usage not the lame ass 8 hours some blogs refer to)Highly recommended for heavy smartphone users.
summary: Definitely a must buy for smartphone users

reviewText: The product looks very nice.  Recharges my phone very fast.  Great if you have multiple devices to charge when traveling with other people.  Life saver when you spend long periods of time away from a wall charger and is essential to stay connected for work or in touch with family.

Upon receiving the NT70T I found it easy to unpack and understand the functionality. I liked several things about this:It can be charged with desktop/laptop computerUniversal adapters for charging and putting out chargesSmall and lightCharges fast for a battery packLasts long enough for multiple charges of multiple devices before needing to recharge itselfLED's are not overly bright for nighttime useI plugged it and waited until it was fully charged. The first item I used it to charge was my Iphone4S which was at 13% battery life. I found the NT70T charge time to be adequate. It took less that 4 hours to fully charge my Iphone 4S to 98%. It would not charge over that percentage. The battery pack only lost 1 green dot. I used it again to fully charge my phone from 16% the next day. I then hooked it up to my Ipad 2 which charged overnight and left my pad from 8% to 82% in 7.5 hours. The NT70T has 1 dot remaining.  I can see myself packing this into my work bag and always having it in case anything needs a boost or is on its last leg. It will also be useful for when I go boating because I lose AC power out on the water and this would be a great support device .

I got this particular device because it is slim and basically the size of another phone and has a ton of power for it's size.  We have a power monkey and it is nice, but my wife uses that one, and I don't like how thick it is in my pocket.  This gives my phone a couple charges and a couple charges to my bluetooth headset.  Good product.

I can never have enough extra juice for all of my electronic gadgets. Between multiple tablets, phones, and handheld consoles in my bag daily it's a complete mess when things start running low on power. New Trent comes to my rescue once more. It definitely works as described it does charge variety of smart phones as well as the most current gen iPad. I love how if nothing is plugged in it has a self turn off timer and it doesn't waste the power. So if the button gets pushed accidentally in the bag then it'll just turn itself off (as long as nothings plugged in of course). This time around the LED indicator for how much power is left isn't separated like other devices so it can be a little trickier to read but you can get the hang of it after some time. I like the back of the device this time since it's actually a matte feeling and not as prone to finger prints and such as well as provide some grip the front still has a glossy feel to it but still with the back and front combined it has a nice grippy feeling not slippery.I like the color contrast of the chrome around the edges but at the same time I'd be just as happy if it were matte black. Definitely still has the wow factor when you bring it out and plug in your devices.Pros: One matte side one glossy side providing less surface for finger print and also a grip feeling so not slippery. Does exactly as it says it does it'll provide juice for your iPad and for your phone. LOVE the auto timed shut off when nothings plugged in.Cons: Not really a true con and so not worth knocking down a star for but my preference in LED light tends to be more separated rather than together. Just takes a little getting used to in reading how much power remains in the device.

I have a Galaxy S2 and use it very heavily.  The battery life is terrible on my phone and I was looking for something to charge it when I was out.  I came across the New Trent Easypak and my problems were solved.  Not only does it charge my phone, but it does it faster than the car charger.  My favorite feature are the on board cables so I don't have to lug any around!  I can get a minimum of 4 full charges before the New Trent battery pack needs to be charged again.  It can charge my Android, Kindle and my daughters iphone.  If you are thinking of buying a charger, this is the way to go.

I got this a few months ago and it has been great so far for all my long and short trip.Even works great on the plane.Pros:It can charge my iPad 2 and iPhone 4S without any problems.It holds a charge for long periods of time.LightCons:it's glossy black which leaves finger prints.

I used this all day everyday for at least a year , it never let me down and I've used it to stream videos . I always used it on long flights and I never had to worry abt finding an outlet at an airport . So convenient I never leave home without it
summary: I couldn't live with out this

reviewText: The NT70T is a good product with a really solid form factor. I like that it is sized height and length like my smart phone and that it’s about 2 times thicker than it with a case.  This one is going to go in my wife's purse so she can charge if she needs to.I don’t like the shiny surface; it’s just a means for fingerprints to be all over it for no reason. If it was matte like the rest of it, I would like that a lot more. I know it looks pretty out of the box, but even minimal handling caused fingerprints to show on the surface.The two USB ports are clearly marked as to which is for a smart phone and which is for a tablet or something that needs more output. It’s nice to have both along with the integrated micro USB cable, which works great for me since my phones have that as a connection.It would be nice if there was an included adapter (if possible) for IOS devices to maximize it’s market, but that is just nitpicky. Most IOS users are pretty used to having to carry a cord with them.The power input seems like it might be a bit weaker than the output, which could be a problem down the line. It worked fine for me but I could see it eventually being an issue. And if it breaks there is no other way to charge the device. I’m torn because I love it being an integrated charge cord, but there is no replacement if it does break. Maybe have it be an additional plug in option at the top? Not sure if that’s possible.The instruction booklet was small but really well done. Having seen the other NewTrent books this one is done a lot better. It’s clear and concise without unnecessary words. You know exactly how to use the product.I was able to use it to charge up multiple devices. Obviously it would full charge my IPad 2 if it was dead, but it took it from 40% to 100% and still had enough left to charge my Samsung Galaxy Nexus phone from 80 to 100%. I used it to charge my cell phone over the weekend 3 times in a day as I was heavily using it in a pretty dead zone for coverage so it was searching for signal a lot too.I wish you could turn the item off, or that it was clear or not that you could. If you can it’s not clear that it’s powered off. The button seems to be there just to check the charge. That’s fine, but it means that it is constantly on and draining at least a small amount of power. With my iCarrier I can leave it for long periods of time without charging and it holds a charge really well since I can turn the power off. I haven’t had this long enough to check how long it holds a charge when not used. If it does power on/off it would be really nice if there was a different light that came on showing that it’s on.This does have an advantage over the iCarrier, the lights don’t stay on when used because it’s always on you don’t need to know if it’s on or off. The iCarrier has a really bright blue LED. It’s pretty, but annoying. This uses green (I’m colorblind but I think green) LEDs and they don’t stay on long. It’s clear by pressing the button whether you have a 25,50,75% charge or if it’s fully charged.I've plugged in a Nintendo DSi, Kindle, Kindle Fire HD, Kindle Fire, Ipod Mini, Ipod Touch, Iphone 5, Samsung Galaxy Nexus and an iPad 2 into it and all of them took a charge. It’s very versatile and easy to use. I really love the form factor, I greatly prefer it to the iCarrier and would definitely carry it on a more normal basis. I’m a big guy, so this fits in my pocket with my phone if I’m going to be away from power all day and using my phone a lot it will come in handy. Being able to fully charge my phone in 30 minutes is pretty awesome. I’d give it a 4 out of 5 rating with the power input cable and the glossy-ness being the biggest issues. I do find it odd that it carries a 10 month warranty. A 12 month would make a lot more sense.
summary: Good, easy to carry battery back up

reviewText: I was able to charge my Galaxy S3 from close to 0% about 3 times before exhausting the battery. Next I am going to try it out on the Note 2 and see how it handles that! The battery is about the size of a deck of cards. It has a built in USB cable and a micro USB cable. There are also 2 USB ports that you can use to plug in other usb chargeable things like a tablet or rechargeable camera. This thing is great if you know your going to be at an airport or on a long car ride and you don't have a car charger or feel like looking for a plug. It is slim and light and easily fits in your pockets. There are led lights on it to let you know that it is working and how much life is left in the battery pack. It also comes with an extension cable if you need a little extra length to reach something. I carry this battery pack with me all the time in case I need it for anything. I also use it in my car because the car charger doesn't work when the car is off so I have this with me for times when I need it and don't want to keep my car running.  I recommend this to everyone because who hasn't been out and needed to charge their phone and had no way of charging it!
summary: Something everyone should have while traveling!

reviewText: I have been shopping around for a while for an external battery that is inexpensive but still well-made. The ones you buy at a wireless carrier's store are usually far overpriced. This one is reasonably priced and I can't think of one reason that the carrier store ones are better.The battery pack has two built-in cables that clip securely into the sides of the pack, each about four inches long. One is a male full-sized USB cable for charging the battery pack, and the other is a micro USB connector for charging a device. This is a great feature, as you can keep it in your bag/purse without having to remember to also bring a cable (unless you have an iOS device). There are also two additional female USB jacks on the battery pack for either your iDevice cable(s) or more micro/mini USB cables.So far I have tried charging a Samsung Galaxy S3 and an LG G2 with this battery pack, and both charged at least as fast as their respective included wall chargers. My G2 charges from it's wall charger from completely dead to 100% in just over an hour, and this pack charges it at almost exactly the same rate. I have yet to run the thing completely dead. After three complete recharges of a Galaxy S3, the pack still had two of four LEDs on the battery indicator. I am very impressed.I have also used the battery pack to power a mini WiFi router, which worked just fine. I wasn't able to test how long it lasted, but I used it for at least an hour and the battery indicator didn't drop below the full 4 LEDs.My wife keeps this in her purse now and is happy that it is plenty small enough to fit in any of her purses and clutches. I highly recommend this product for anyone looking for a small, well-made and inexpensive external battery for phones and/or tablets.
summary: Excellent value and very well engineered

reviewText: This thing works great for keeping my iPhone charged while on my bicycle.  Using GPS which usually drains the phone battery quickly, not a problem with this battery pack.  It keeps the phone battery at 100% without a glitch.  However, it does not work on charging batteries for my bluetooth headsets.  When hooked up, I press the on button and it will start charging but then quickly stop charging like the headset battery is fully charged.  The fix is to plug in the iPhone in one usb port and the headset battery in the other usb simultaneously.  Only then will the headset battery charge properly.  If it charged batteries for my headsets without this little trick, I'd give it 5 stars.Overall I would reccommend this battery pack.

I've been searching for a battery pack to buy after an incidence where bad things happened when everyone's phones died and there were no nearby outlets. In any case, getting a battery pack deemed a necessity. I ended up choosing the easypak due to it's price and functionality for the set price. The packaging was pretty cool, with a magnetic clip, and the product was easy to take out and use. Upon opening the device comes only about 1/2 charged, which is very obviously shown to the user via stickers on the plastic casing.The battery pack itself is fairly light and very easy to take around with its compact size. It's able to fit in most if not all of the pockets of my bags. The built in cable makes charging it easy since I just connect it to the usb charger that came with my iphone, however its not very long, but is able to charge by laptop or by the proximity of an electric extension cord.I especially like the fact that it turns off when you disconnect your device or when your device is fully charged. This is very handy so that I don't have to keep and eye all the time on it and have to make sure to turn it off. Being able to charge my iphone 6-7 times in one battery pack charge is indeed very nice when unable to do so using a wall charger. One charge takes about an hour, from a completely dead battery. Also this is able to charge my ipad mini about up to 70% from none in about and hour and a half. Making it fully charged within about 2 hours.The only thing I'd have different is the gloss front, as I would've preferred it to be matte. But overall I am very pleased with the NT70T Battery Pack.
summary: Life saver, one of my favorites

reviewText: I purchased this on sale to have an external charger that could charge my iPad. It works really well. I can fully recharge the iPad with this. It was useful during the prolonged power outage after Hurricane Sandy. Very happy with this purchase.

I recently purchased the NT70T.This is the first portable charger I have purchased, so I wasn't sure what to expect.I find this model almost perfect for my needs.The size and weight are perfect.It takes awhile to fully recharge my Galaxy Note (SGH-I717), But no more that plugging it into the wall.I believe I am going to find this device very useful.I would rate this a 4

There are a number of things to like about this product. First, it looks really nice. Curb appeal may not be anything special to everybody, but it is nice to have a product that is visually attractive. Not many products can achieve thatSecond, it is charged through a built-in USB connector, which is convenient for me because I can just plug it into the front USB port of my computer. I dislike having to plug things into power outlets constantly, especially if it is something that I use frequently.Third, it has a built-in micro USB output cable. I do not have to worry about bringing the extra cable in my bag. This means a lot for someone who always has to carry a lot of things around.I tested the capacity of this product just to see if it does hold the 7000 mAh that it advertised. I tried it with my Samsung Galaxy S3, iPod Touch, and an iPhone 4s.It managed to fully charge my Samsung Galaxy S3 about three times from 15%, with the charger being fully depleted the fourth time. This seems about right because the Galaxy S3 is said to have a 2100 mAh battery. I noticed that it takes slightly longer to charge my phone with the NT70T on the built-in micro USB connector as opposed to the original USB cable that came with the phone.It was able to charge my iPod Touch 4th Gen twice while only dropping a bar. It was able to charge my Galaxy S3 and an iPhone 4s simultaneously.I never really knew how long it took to charge the NT70T but when I leave it plugged into my computer at night before I go to sleep, I would wake up the following morning with three bars. That's more than enough to get me through the day.It would also be fair to share that this charger was dropped to the floor once from hip height. It still works.In summary, I have another solid New Trent product at my disposal.

I've owned the New Trent IMP70D for over 6 months and it has given me plenty of battery life on my weekend getaways. It can charge two devices at the same time and it gives about 3-4 full charges to my iPhone 4S before I need to charge it again. I usually charge the portable charger over night so I don't have to worry about it during the day. A very easy to use, portable charger you can take anywhere. Despite the con, I still give it a 5 star rating.Pros: Charges two devices, light, portableCons: Cannot be charged while charging other devices

I love this charger and I would recommend this to anyone that is away from their office or car for extended periods of time and have the need to charger their phone. Convenient power is the first thing that comes to mind when I use the NT70T, this battery pack is so convenient, as I travel between projects all the time, and as my Tablets and smart phones die quickly with heavy use, this charger has helped me with battery life, it is no longer an issue.  It is great that it can charge two phones, or a phone and a Tablet, and an Apple device.It is extremely small for what it can do. I typically stack it under my smartphone when on the plane, it's easy to talk on the phone and charge at the same time.  I also have on several occasions helped coworkers charge their devices when they wouldn't have been able to otherwise. I also have used it to charge my external Bluetooth speakers and Bluetooth Keyboard.  I really like that you can charge your phone or tablet at the same time as recharging the NT70T, this has been convenient so I only have to bring one plug in USB charging device in my travel bag.I also have the IMP52D, it is helpful but didn't have enough juice for the larger tablets where the NT70T comes into play.If there were anything to improve on this charger I would say to have it charge faster, but as I charge overnight for the most part it really has not been a huge issue, and maybe a travel bag like the IMP52D
summary: The NT70T, The Right Charger for the Job

reviewText: This battery charger is a excellent solution as back up power, especially for traveling. It charges quickly and is relatively light weight.

reviewText: I believe almost everyone here has said exactly what I want to say so I will be straight to the point. This is it for all 5V devices that need on-the-go charging. I was extremely please that I was able to recharge the Motorola Photon with ~ 1800mAh battery rock solid 3 times easily. I am in queue for the Kindle Fire and will be in Africa for a month. This will definitely keep me connected. You will be very pleased and I don't see a lot of devices this size with this much power density on the market.

I love the larger capacity, and you can't go wrong with the solid black color.  Very stylish. Reasonably quick charge of the product considering the large capacity. I love the fact that the cords are already built into the product!  I don't have to fumble for finding the cords, or worry they fell out of my pocket.  My only regret is that I wish product was slightly smaller in physical size, but considering the large capacity I not sure that could be done.

eviewThe NT70T is a great size and form-factor. You don't always want tohave to fumble in your bag to find the cables to charge your device, butluckily this battery pack has them built-in. Depending on yourcollection of devices, you may not even need to carry a separate cablewith you most of the time. I was easily able to charge a Nexus 7 andiPhone 4 at the same time. I had hoped I could possibly charge 3devices (output1, output2, and built-in cable), but output 2 would stopcharging when I connected the built-in cable. reviewText: Pros:- during testing, the IMP70D charged my iPhone 4 at the same rate that the wall charger charged my wife's iPhone 4 -- very impressive- charges the iPad at a better than expected rate- the size is fantastic, very convenient to carry around - for anyone with a ScottEVest jacket/coat/vest, this battery fits perfectly in either of the phone pockets!- lightweight- dual USB configuration is also very good as I love the flexibility to charge multiple items at once-- inexpensive compared to other alternatives- does not give off heat either when it is charging or discharging- peace of mind as I travel a lot for work and personal and never have to worry about my devices running out of powerCons:- the mini-USB charging port does not feel sturdy when inserting the power cable, I am concerned that it could push into the case and render the product unusable- the black top surface tends to collect fingerprints and smudges easily - would rather see it with a brushed steel look- LED flashing lights are annoying in dark rooms- takes longer time to recharge than expected (minor concern)- difficult to tell exactly how charged it is as the LED lights are hard to read at a glance- coiled power cable tends to pull the battery on most surfacesRecommendations:- replace the power cable with a non-coiled version- replace the black acrylic top with something more like a brushed steel look or something that doesn't show smudges and fingerprints as much- firm up the mounting of the mini-USB port- replace the 4 light LED configuration with flashing with a 5-10 light configuration that would more accurately show the charge level- eliminate the flashing lightsI have traveled twice internationally with this battery along and another time on a 26 hour drive with my family in the car - trust me, you don't want the batteries in the kids' iPod Touches to run out of juice then!  The IMP70D performed beautifully and allowed us to also charge my wife's iPad at the same time.  The value derived from this trip alone was enough to pay for this battery pack.  Well done, New Trent, and I would highly recommend this product.

I love this thing. It's small, light, and fits great in my laptop bag.I had been looking for a backup supply for my cell phones for a while now and recently purchased this one. It works great. I've been able to charge my phone numerous times on one charge of this battery pack. I don't have an iPad, but actually recently used this to power a friend's. I recommend it.I wasn't really crazy about the USB cable that came with it. But hey, I didn't buy this thing for the cable. (It's actually one cable with two adapters that plug into the end. One for USB mini, and one for USB micro.)I would definitely recommend buying it, and I'm considering getting another one.

I purchased the IMP70D so that my wife and I will both have phone chargers for our LG smartphones and IPODS.  I travel frequently and am often in airports where access to wall outlets is lacking.  The IMP70D is a nice upgrade from the 5000 mAh model I purchased previously, due to the increased power.  (Since I travel the most, I am claiming the IMP70D).  With the 5000, the first charger cable I got had a problem with a loose connection at the USB end.  That was solved with a new cable.  The IMP70D seems to have tighter connections; the first thing I did when testing it was to move the charger, the phone, and the cable around quite a bit--no lost connections!  The IMP70D features great user friendly packaging--no sealed blister pack to cut through to access the charger when new.  It has a rubberized finish on the bottom which will probably end up being more durable than the hard plastic of the 5000.  Very satisfied new user!

I bought this for my kid to take on a school trip to charge his phone, and for me to take on business trips.  I've charged my Nexus S 4G three times from completely dead using the IMP70D, and still had power to spare.  It completely charges the phone in less than one hour, and charges itself in about 3 hours.I decided on this particular model because it does not require a proprietary charger cord.  I use one of the USB to Micro USB cords I have lying around to charge it and also have the short one that was included just in case.I've used it to charge an iPhone, iPod touch, Nexus S 4G, and an HTC Evo 4G.  It works perfectly, and I can't recommend it enough.

I got this to charge my iPhone when I'm stuck in class without a power outlet. I fully charged it and I've been able to juice up my iPhone 4S at least 5 times from an almost dead battery, and the backup pack is still reporting a full charge. I carry it around with me in my backpack in case I get stuck out without power now. It's about the thickness of the iPhone, and just a little bit wider.I'd recommend picking up a short USB cable - I found a 3" iPod dock to USB cable that I keep with the backup charger.
summary: Saved my iPhone 4S from dying on long work/school days

reviewText: To begin, I am writing this review of a demo unit provided to me by New Trent. Beyond that, they have no say in this review, and I have the duty to potential buyers AND the Amazon review system of reviewing this unit honestly.This is the 3rd New Trent unit that I've been able to use (the other two were actual "blind" purchases of mine for the holidays trips), and it holds up to a standard of quality and usefulness that I'm learning to expect. This one is special though, in a number of ways.1) You can charge the battery, AND a device, at the same time. You may be thinking "so what?" so I'll tell you what. This can have a very nice life extending effect on your devices that you'd otherwise plug directly into the wall. If you have a house with old wiring (dirty power), or live somewhere with frequent power outs, plugging your device into the battery, and then the battery into the wall, should have a "cleaning" effect on the power supplied to your device. The value of this is unimaginable if you have ever had a device "burn out" on you after a year. It works similar to UPS systems for computers and servers. My 2 other units do not behave in this way, which adds a tremendous value to this one.2) The cables remain attached to this battery, so you never have to search for a microUSB charging cable for your device, or a USB charging cable for your battery. You still do need a wall plug with normal USB output (or plug it into your computer for a slower charge) in order to charge the battery. See #1 though, plug a wall plug in, plug the battery in, then plug your device in. Your devices will thank you.3) Included with the battery is a USB extension cable. You probably have never seen one, so had no clue how useful they are. This is a $5-10 added bonus value which you can use to charge your battery, but you can also use it to extend the length of any USB device. These are extremely handy to have.4 stars instead of 5 due to the fact that if you break the input cable, this thing becomes a brick. Unless you're good with soldering. There is no alternate USB input to charge the battery. I can vouch that the input & output cables that are attached to the battery have held up to my rigorous use this far, however I can totally see an unfortunate "stretch", bend, or fall causing one or both to break in some way.Great products, and the price is spot on.
summary: How do they do it? Another amazing backup/charger

reviewText: This charger is wonderful for anybody who frequently goes places where they can't charge their mobile devices. Having kids, power outages are no fun when there's nothing to do, but giving the kids a way to charge their devices has a way of saving one's sanity! This has a port for charging iPhones, iPods, and other mobile devices that can be charged via USB cable, and there is a second port that will charge an iPad. It is more of a battery booster for the iPad because the iPad is a power hog, but will completely charge an iPhone and iPod. It's portable and fits in any laptop or iPad bag, and will allow you to charge your device, even if you have to leave your car to go into the store. The non-skid bottom insures that you're less likely to have it slide off of a desk.

I absolutely love this battery. I've recently been having problems with my smartphone battery dying by mid-day (long story) while I'm out and about with work. I'm not near a electrical outlet most of the time so I decided to give this battery a shot. I was able to use my phone continuously all day long with it plugged into the battery pack and didn't even drain half of the juice from it. And all of that for less than $50 was a nice bonus.Now the unit isn't perfect. My only gripe with it is that the LED lights displaying it's charge level only illuminate when the battery itself is being charged (while plugged into the wall, for example) not while it's charging a device. It would be nice to know how much longer the battery can charge your device. But I was still willing to rate it 5 stars because of how portable it is (fits in a dress shirt pocket). I've very happy with my purchase. I was considering purchasing a similar Energizer unit for about the same price but it was only 5000mAh.Pros:- tremendous amount of charging power- very portable (small for the amount of power it provides)- works with any smartphone that can charge from USB- can charge two devices at once- has a 2.1amp port for charging tablets and phones very fastCons:- battery meter doesn't display how much juice the batter has left while charging your deviceEdited 5/24/2010----------------I'm disappointed to report that the battery has given up the ghost after only a year of light use (used it maybe 20 times for trips). It will still take a charge (battery shows that it's full) but it will no longer charge any other devices. I thought maybe it was a faulty cable but buying another one didn't correct it. And there is absolutely no tech support available anywhere for New Trent products from what I can tell. I was expecting more. reviewText: This is my second New Trent portable charger and I like it a lot it so far.  It really packs a lot of power into a small and cost-effective device.To get an idea of it's size- Compared to an iPhone it is just a little bit thicker, almost exactly the same length, and about an inch wider.As far as its power:-Fully charged my iPhone 4S from 5% to 100% a little more than 3 and a half times.-Charged my iPad 2 from 5% to 73%.-Charges two devices at the same time with no problem.-I didn't do a full test on each but I made sure it was able to charge a handful of my other devices such as a Sansa Clip mp3 player, Garmin Forerunner 110 GPS watch, TomTom XL 340S GPS, and a Polaroid USB AA/AAA battery charger.One of the biggest improvements made to this device is the use of a micro-USB port for charging it.  My older device uses a special power supply which I would frequently misplace.  This device comes with a micro-USB cable but even if I misplace it I have a few of these cables laying around (like many people these days) and they only cost a couple bucks on Amazon if I were to lose all of them.As far as the look and feel, the device looks very nice with a smooth, shiny top, rubberized bottom, and a metal ring around the whole thing (like an iPhone 4/4S).  The shiny, black finish on the top looks nice at first but a negative is that *every* fingerprint on it is visible.  For future devices I suggest using rubber finish that was used on the bottom on the top as well.  The ports on the unit are clearly labeled with "2.1A For iPad" and "1A For iPhone 4S" which is nice but for future products I suggest removing "For iPad" and "For iPhone" and leaving only "2.1A" and "1A" to avoid confusion with folks charging other products.  It also has a power meter bar which they (thankfully) made a bit smaller than my previous device but I do not like that they go off while in use (they only go on while charging the unit and when you first turn it on).Functionally, this is a great device which I will get a lot of use out of and all of my complaints are cosmetic so I can deal with them.  Overall I would rate this device a 4.5 out of 5 stars but Amazon doesn't allow halves so I'm bumping it up to a 5.

I got a NewTrent Easypak NT70T to review from the company and it did a great job of charging my Samsung Galaxy S2 while on a business trip.  I also have a PowerGen PGMPP6000 mAh External Battery Pack which is comparable.The NewTrent Easypak NT70T is rated at 7000 mAh, has a micro USB cable in the unit, a USB cable built in the unit for charging, and a 2amp and 1amp output to charge various devices such as smart phones and iPads.The unit itself only came with a USB extension cord to charge your device, so you would have to use your own USB charging cables to charge various devices ... unless you have a device that uses a micro USB cable of course.The unit itself is a little larger than the PowerGen PGMPP6000.  Even though it was a little larger, I did find that the micro USB cable built inside the unit was sturdier and it didn't feel like it was going to break.  It also felt more comfortable having the two units together while charging.ChargingThis unit was able to charge my Samsung Galaxy S2 2+ times using the 1 amp output.  I only charged it when it was below 20%.  It's not an exact gauge, but it has enough juice to keep your phone charged when needed.I also tried charging an iPad 3 using the 2 amp output.  I didn't get a chance to measure how much of a charge it could produce, since I'm usually at home while using the iPad.  If I happen to go out, I make sure that I charge my iPad fully which is usually enough time for me to do what I need to do on it.One thing that I noticed is that you don't have to power on the NewTrent unit to start the charging process; it will just start charging the device when plugged in.  Also when the NewTrent device is completely dead, it took about 8 hours to recharge using my Samsung Galaxy S2 charger.Overall thoughtsI thought that this NewTrent unit provides great value for the price and comparable to other external battery packs out there right now.So what makes this unit stand out from the others?  One thing that makes this unit stand out is that it has 2 different outputs for various devices that you might need to charge different devices.  The only downside is that you have to provide your own USB charging cables.  It's not that bad since you will have the cables anyway.  The micro USB cable also seems a bit sturdier and doesn't seem that it would break easily as the PowerGen unit.If I had a choice on the PowerGen or the NewTrent, I would get the NewTrent.9/9/13 Update: I used this to charge an iPad3 and the NewTrent Unit was able to charge it from 0% to 30% on a full charge.  This is more than enough for my needs when I'm out and about and need an emergency battery back up.
summary: Great external battery backup to charge various devices!

reviewText: I really like this external charger because it has two ports, one of which is capable of charging an ipad. I brought this along the last time I flew and it was great to be able to charge both my ipad and my phone at the same time. I didn't let either device drain down completely before charging but I'd estimate the IMP70D holds about two full charges for an ipad and maybe two or three for a phone.That said, I'm giving this four stars instead of five because it annoyingly has no light which tells you that it's on (there is a light which comes on briefly when you power on the device) or a battery meter to tell you how much charge is left.  Also, it's size is a negative for me though it may not matter to others as much.  It's thinner yet wider than my last New Trent battery, which makes it harder to hold in my hand.  If you're someone who typically charges their phone out on a table, this may not matter to you as much.

This unit has been very good. Its one flaw: it delivers approximately 80% of rated capacity. I still do not understand the wide-spread use of overly optimistic ratings in the field of external mobile battery devices when other industries seem to rate their batteries to correct capacity. I have several radio controlled helicopters and airplanes, and I buy and build my own battery packs. All of the good quality batteries I have used have delivered their rated capacity or better. The NT70T also has a great form factor, and is reasonably light for the stated capacity. What sets this device apart is the ability to charge three devices at once. The integrated USB and Micro USB cords are one of the best features on any mobile battery, and I do not know why it has not been implemented on many more of these devices. It is very handy to not have to carry or search for a USB charging cable. The four LED lights that display capacity are not very accurate. Most of the capacity is delivered by the “halfway” indication of two lights. I find that with two lights out of four left, the battery has much less than half the capacity. This is one thing I would ask manufacturers to do, and that is to design better charge remaining indicators. As it is, the New Trent NT70T is one of the best mobile battery packs I have tested.
summary: Excellent Portable Battery with one flaw

reviewText: This is my third external charger and it is definitely the best. The first was something I bought at the airport, from Sharper Image. Decent charger, but only a 1A output, so it was pretty limited in its charging abilities. I paid $75 for it. I sold it and bought a Zagg Sparq 2, due to the fact I could charge a tablet. It was 6000mAh, but bulky and relatively heavy. I got it on sale for $45. It worked fine for me, but the wife took it over so she could keep her iPhone charged. I looked around and finally settled on the New Trent N70T.  It was one of my best electronics purchases.It is the perfect balance of form and function, for me anyways. It fully charged my iPhone 4S from 40% twice,  fully charged my iPad Mini from 38%, charged a portable speaker, and still shows it has power left. For me, that is plenty of power- what I figure a long plane trip would take.The N70T charges with a built in USB cord that folds into the side of the plastic shell. New Trent includes a USB extension cord, so you can use any USB wall plug you own and not be stuck using a computer. The instructions say to fully charge it before the first use, so I plugged it before going to bed. It has 4 LED lights that flash while charging and glow steadily when full. The LED lights glow, not shine like a headlight; finally someone realizes that we aren't lighting the way for an alien invasion while charging.To use the battery, plug in your USB charging cable to one or both of the outputs and press the button to turn it on. It comes with a built in micro USB cable, so you can charge many GPS units and cameras without any additional cords. The 2.1 A port seems to work as indicated. It rapidly charged my my iPhone 4S from 40% in 1 hr and 20 min. To check the amount of power remaining, press the button and see how many bars light up.Very happy with this product and would recommend it to everyone.
summary: Perfect balance of charging capacity and price

reviewText: There are a good number of times I need more juice, regardless of where I am.  The #1 case is my verizon 4G mifi hotspot.  The battery life on that is a joke and they should be ashamed. I can power that hot spot for a long time (have not hit the limit yet).  It can quickly charge my phone (thunderbolt) which also has poor battery life.  It can charge my tablet too, though it has wonderful battery life.  :)Pros:Very nice looking, solid construction.  Big battery life.  Two USB ports (with different amperage levels if that matters to you).Cons:No charging cable included, which is odd.  it charges by micro USB.  And yeah, everyone has 5 of those power adapters around - at least people who would need a portable USB battery.  But still.Once 'on' and charging, the indicator light turns off.  It is still working as you can see from your device.  But nothing on the battery shows it is on and working.  I suspect this do this to limit the wasted energy that the light takes, but I could see this being an issue - thinking it is charging something and it is not.  Always check your device.NeutralThe cable that comes with it - which is the cable that goes from USB to micro or mini usb (this is what you use to connect the battery to the device you want to run is really coiled and kind of short.  This may or many not be a pro or a con.  You of course can use your own USB to mini/micro that is longer and not coiled.Oddity:The two USB ports, which have different amperage levels/output (2.1a and 1a) are labeled as such:  Ipad (2.1) and iphone 5 (1a).  So this must be from the future as the iphone 5 is still a ways off.  :)

Three very good reasons to buy this NEW TRENT EASYPAK NT70T 7000mAh power bank are:  (1) the high storage capacity (7000 mAh); (2) the built-in connector cables (Micro output and USB input) that nest snugly along the sides and are always available when you need them; and (3) the two USB output ports (one for an iPhone, one for a tablet) that allow you to deliver the right power to two kinds of mobile devices.Because of the high storage capacity, this power bank takes several hours to charge, even when plugged into an AC adapter for a wall outlet.  For the same reason, the power bank is fairly heavy (6.7 oz.).  However, it's still small enough to fit easily into a purse or pocket (2-7/8" x 4-5/8"; about the size of a Motorola Droid Razr or Samsung Galaxy SIII smartphone).  And the high storage capacity means it can provide the auxiliary power you need for a larger mobile device (e.g., an iPad, a Nexus 7 tablet, or a Kindle Paperwhite or Fire), as well as for a cellphone.To charge the power bank itself, you connect the USB cable to an AC adapter (e.g., theAmazon Kindle 9W PowerFast Adapter for Accelerated Charging), and hit the power button to start the charging.  There is a USB extension cable included in the box, in case the built-in USB cable isn't long enough to reach your power source for charging the power bank.  To charge a mobile device, you connect the device to the power bank's built-in micro output cable, and hit the power button.  (The power bank will not charge the mobile device until the power bank is turned on.)  Four LED lights indicate the level of power stored, when charging the power bank or charging a mobile device.In choosing a power bank, you generally look to the mAh (milliampere hours) number, which is the measure of how much energy the power bank's battery can store.  A power bank rated at higher mAh can power a cellphone or a device that consumes more power (e.g., a smartphone or iPad) for a longer period of time before needing recharging.  For example, a 1500 mAh power bank can power a device that needs 100 milliamps of power for 15 hours, or a device needing 150 milliamps for 10 hours.  (Note that a power bank rated at 1.5 Ah is equivalent to 1500 mAh.) Choose a power bank with an mAh rating suitable to your particular needs for powering your portable devices, keeping in mind that power banks with higher storage capacity (higher mAh rating) are usually larger and heavier than power banks with lower storage capacity.New Trent power banks have a good reputation, and I like this one in particular because of the high storage capacity and built-in cables.Disclaimer note:  This review is based on a product supplied to me free of charge for review purposes.  I have no financial interest or business relationship with the manufacturer or seller, and this review represents my independent opinion of the product.
summary: Three Reasons to Like: High Storage Capacity, Built-in Connector Cables, Two USB Output Ports

reviewText: I purchased this because I am simply tired of having literally dozens of old cell phone spare batteries for phones I no longer use lying around.  Plus, my new phone (Droid Razr) has a fixed battery like the iPhones do, so extra batteries weren't an option.  I occasionally travel long distance by air, and needed enough juice to keep my movies and music going for 20 or more hours of heavy usage.  Finally, I HATE being half way through a movie when a battery dies and you have to swap the spare--an external battery takes care of that.I purchased this particular model becuase I had a chance to look at the IMP50D.  The IMP50D I received was defective, so I decided to go with the IMP70D trading the extra size for for the 40% increase in juice.  As far as build quality goes, the unit is very solid, and very professional looking.  The USB output port is a little on the loose side, but connects and charges just fine.  As for charging, the micro USB plug for power in is nice, as it is the same plug my phone uses.Keep in mind I originally bought this for air travel.  Since getting my new phone, and playing with it way too much, I've found this charger has been a life saver when I get a late afternoon or evening call.  If the battery is burnt down, I can quickly grab the IMP70D, plug it in, and take the call.  HOWEVER...The IMP70D should have enough juice to fully charge my Razr at least 3 times, if not more.  I have been able to reproduce this problem:  Either the battery pack  does not have the advertised capacity, or it is unable to hold a charge.  I should be able to fully charge my 1780mAh cell phone battery fully at least 3 if not more times.  I am averaging less than two.  To make matters worse, after one charge, the LED indicator will show the pack has 3 out of 4 LEDs, indicating a decent charge.  I check this by briefly turning the pack on, then making sure it is shut off.  The very next use, I ended up with one blinking LED--indicating the pack was exhausted.  I had the exact same issue with the IMP-50D, in that it died after one full recharge, well short of the stated capacity.For the size, the awkwardness of the product, I was expecting something that did what it is supposed to.  I am only giving this two stars because I got it on sale, and it does work somewhat.  But this is one heck of a brick to carry around and only get 1.5-2 charges out of.
summary: Does not seem to keep charge

Just a suggestion:' OUT 2.1ATablets, etc' OUT 1ACell phones* Also, the cord....oh my the cord that comes with the ACD66 is not really good. I would rather have the cord that came with the IMP500.
