The New Trent Arcadia Pack has been great for me.  For the price, I wasn't really sure what to expect.  Honestly, I was expecting to be disappointed.  However, as soon as I received the item and started using it, I decided that my expectations were all wrong.  For this type of product, all you want from it is to work and have the capacity to charge as is stated.  From my experience, it lives up to what is described from New Trent.  I have used the pack to charge my Samsung Galaxy S2 as well as my iPad 2.  With both devices, I have had no issues.  Here are a couple pros and cons:Pros:* Price.  I can't find anything comparable in price for the same capacity.* Form factor.  The pack is nice and compact.  You can carry it in your back pocket even.* Capacity.  7000mAh is great.  I can go a long time between needing to charge it back up after using it to charge my phone and iPad.Cons:* Cable.  The supplied cable with the two little adapters seems odd to me.  I feel like they should just give you a standard micro USB cable instead of needing an adapter to change it to micro USB.* No power adapter.  I was fine not having a power adapter to charge it due to the price, but it would have been nice to include.

I plan to do a follow up to this review with much more detail, but this is a great universal backup for any phone or tablet, without question.One minor drawback, this unit doesn't actually come with a 120V AC to 5V DC (USB) charger, but those are easy enough to appropriate.  Personally, I would recommend a charger with 2 amps output since the battery will draw one amp to charge, and that's a fairly common adapter to find.  For example:Samsung OEM 2.0 Amp Travel Charger with Detachable Micro USB Cable for Samsung Galaxy Note, Galaxy Note 2 II, Galaxy S3 S III, Galaxy S3 Mini & Other SmartphonesAnything less than 1.2 amps output is going to be tasked so close to its maximum rating that you run a higher risk of damaging the charger.The biggest drawback is the charging time, which is going to take 7-8 hours when you drain the battery to 25% or less. That's simply because the capacity on this pack is so high that it takes longer to recharge.  This is only a "drawback" and not a "flaw" that the manufacturer should pay for in rating points: I love this battery.I can't do any more justice to the specs than others have already done, but I can try to illustrate the performance.  I had this in my backpack for about a week after charging, before its first use.  I know for a fact that all batteries (especially rechargeable) have a trickle discharge when not in use, so realistically it was not at 100% when used.  My Note II (stock battery) was still able to completely charge the first time from ~40% phone battery, and a second time several days later from ~30% phone battery.  And the New Trent battery pack still had juice left to spare (albeit low) after both uses and no charging for two weeks!Right now, it's going for $30 and I may purchase a couple more as gifts.  These are fantastic.  You never know when you may need one and they take up as much space as a cell phone.  The performance is there, and for this price you can't go wrong.  Definitely recommend this to others with confidence.

I wanted to try this product, so that I would have something to be able charge two different devices without relying on an electrical outlet.  The IMP70D did charge my HP Touchpad in a reasonable amount of time, if charged separately from my iPhone 4.  My IPhone 4 charged in about 2 hours, at separate charging sessions.  The best thing about this product is that I can charge my touchpad and iPhone without relying on an electrical outlet, if an electrical outlet is not available for charging my products, or when traveling.It takes a while for the IMP70D to charge my HP Touchpad.  I understand this takes longer, due to the fact that my touchpad has a much higher mah than my iPhone 4.Overall, I really like this product, and will be using it a lot in the future.

PRO: 7000mAh charger can easily charge any smartphone as well as act as an emergency charge for tablets (iPad). Embedded charging cable very convenient for recharging the pack! Embedded micro USB so you can just carry the adapter for your phone. Nice glossy, professional and clean look.CON: A little bit on the bulky size considering the mAh size.I bought this for my brother for a birthday gift and he loves it! Just stores it in his bag and uses it whenever he needs. It's incredibly handy. He recharges via his macbook so he doesn't carry any extra cables since it has the USB embedded!
summary: Great battery pack on the go!

reviewText: I've had this product for some time, and I've been nothing but impressed by it. After charging it for the first time since I got it, I haven't had to recharge it yet. Had myself a predicament at a popular coffee place when all of the outlets were in use by other customers. No worries there! My phone and iPod were taken care of thanks to this battery. It's a back up device power house, and well deserving of that title. It's also lightweight, portable, and reliable for my charging needs.
summary: Just the thing I need to charge all my devices

reviewText: I used to use this all of the time but since I wouldn't shut up about how much I liked it, my family has taken it for themselves. It stays in the car for long and short trips.Cables are built in so there is no need to run a cable to the cigarette lighter. No need to unplug the GPS either.Power enough for two charges +.Small and powerful. New Trent has done it again! Never have I been disappointed with their products.Buy one for a gift and buy one for yourself.

It works great!I normally have two or more devices on me at all times. I've been looking for a charger that charges more than one device at a time and I finally found it! Most chargers out there can only charge one device at a time or it is only is usually only for the Apple device. The is above the rest. The iCurve has two ports and also allows me to charge my Nexus 7 and the iPhone 4s at the same time. I can get about 75% on my Nexus 7 and 100% iphone simultaneously.The most awesome thing about this device is that it fits in your pocket. It's about the size of a wallet and weighs about as much as one as well.Pros:- Small (fits in my pocket)- Lightweight- 2 PORTS!- Battery life indicatorCons:- The only thing that I would change on this device is to incorporate the charging cable to the device.I would highly recommend the iCurve to anyone that have multiple devices.

I bought the IMP70D battery pack right before a long trip after quite a bit of research and after a brief experience with a friend's IMP99D, which saved the day.  I chose the IMP70D because of its flatter and cleaner form factor despite the slightly lower battery capacity.  It does exactly as promised, reliably charging all manner of devices from iPhones to iPads (simultaneously) and of course non-Apple products as well.  Included in the package is a relatively short pigtail cord with standard USB on one end and mini/micro USB adapters on the other.  Be aware that a wall transformer is not included in the package -- your existing Apple mini-cube transformer or other USB power source will do the trick.  One feature this newer model has that the older ones apparently do not have is a smart sensing (power saving) capability which turns off the battery pack once your device is fully charged.  Interestingly, the IMP70D does not get hot when charging (or discharging), likely a sign of good power and thermal regulation, which should lead to a longer service life.  Some of the previous generation battery packs had cooling vents but this one appears to not need them.  Overall a solid product that will keep you mobile.
summary: Solid performer in a great form factor

reviewText: This is wonderful! Got 2 of them and they both work awesome. In the woods all day, fishing, out in the field working. This is a must have for every one. It will charge several different devices. Wish I would have known about them years ago!

Recently purchased three products from New Tent.  Bluetooth keyboard for IPad mini, USB dual car charger and this external battery.  I have used all three and am impressed with them all.  New Trent is a solid company providing excellent products just as described (if not better) and with quick delivery.  I am a fan of New Trent and their products.

I've had smaller USB battery packs, like the Motorola P893.  They're fine in a pinch for adding ~30% to your battery charge before going empty.This 7000mAh pack, however, is in another class.  It can take my phone from Low Battery Alert to 100% charge several times, even after sitting in the bag for weeks.  Just the ticket for travel, where finding an outlet in a foreign place can be a hassle.The on-board LEDs are a bit.. muddled.  They all merge together to where it's hard to tell precisely how much charge is left.  The good news is that it doesn't matter much -- the thing generally has plenty of power to go.It puts out 1A on one outlet, and 2A on the other.  iPad3 and Nexus7 benefit from the added current available on the 2A port.  The 1A one is great for most modern phones that exceed the typical 500mA of a standard USB charger.  The difference is dramatic -- topping off a phone in 1 hour instead of 2.The included cable is odd.  It's a tightly coiled cable with a USB connector on one end, and then a coaxial connector on the other.  Included is an adapter for mini-USB and micro-USB.  I would have preferred to have two separate cables, one mini & one micro.  The coaxial connector tends to pull out easier than the USB and the fittings are easy to lose.  This is a double problem because of the short cord and tight coil.  Really, your phone has to be right next to the battery pack.  You can use other USB cables, but not all of them have the right signaling to indicate to the phone that 1A or 2A is available.  Test stuff before travel, of course.Anyway, the biggest feature is right there in the title.. 7000mAh.  Sweet.  Having this kind of power on-tap is useful in new ways.  I can rent a WiFi hotspot on travel, couple it to this battery, and leave it on all day long.  No more worrying about how long the little internal hotspot battery will last.It's the kind of thing that doesn't get frequent use, but when you need it, it's awesome.Five stars, minus one for the included USB charge cables and nondescript LEDs.  Call it 4.5 stars.

If you're anything like me, you use your iPhone (or some other mobile device) ALL the time, and you get frustrated by the battery life. Not only do I use my iPhone to make calls, send/receive emails/tweets/texts, browse the internet, and navigate using a map app, I am a mobile photographer and use my iPhone constantly to take, edit, and share photos. After finding myself on more than one occasion in the embarrassing position of having a dead iPhone battery while my friends continue to capture and share great photos, I decided it was time to buy a portable charger. I did extensive research and settled on the New Trent Easypak NT70T, which I ordered from Amazon for a great price. This was my first New Trent product, and I could not be happier with it. Straightforward to use right out of the box, small and light, sleek in appearance, and highly effective (I've used it now on numerous occasions to charge my iPhone and iPad, which the NT70T charges quickly without any trouble), the NT70T has exceeded my expectations. Never again will I be caught without a charged iPhone at exactly the moment I need my iPhone most. I highly recommend the New Trent NT70T to anyone considering a portable charger for their iPhone or other mobile devices.
summary: A life-saver for those who use their mobile device often (and who doesn't?)

reviewText: This battery pack is everything you need in a single device.  New Trent has hit the mark with this compact little battery pack. The battery pack is small enough to carry around in a purse or laptop case and charges every Apple and Bluetooth device I own and a lot of devices I don't.  It has 3 charging ports, two with USB connectors that you can plug any sync cable into and one short Micro USB cable that is attached to the battery pack and conveniently folds away into the side of the pack.The charging cable is attached and it too tucks away into the opposite side of the pack from the Micro USB cable. They also include an extension cable to make charging a snap. The only thing you need is an AC adapter to plug the battery pack into for charging and you have an all-in-one ready to go, power unit.The unit is sleek looking and the ports are nicely labeled on the back of the battery pack so you know which one to use for each device. I made use of all three.  It charged my Iphone and my Ipad on one charge of the battery pack. The micro USB cable also fits my LG bluetooth headset so I need only carry this one device and I am good to go.The NT70T has lights on the bottom of the pack to indicate its level of charge, so you are never surprised and always know how much power you have left in it.I am very happy with this battery pack and highly recommend it.Shipping was extremely fast and the product was well packaged.
summary: Perfect little battery pack, I LOVE it

reviewText: I bought my IMP70D a couple of weeks ago, not knowing what to expect. At home we have three cell phones, an iPad, iPhone and two iPods. It has worked beautifully on all of them. On my IPad 3rd series, it has actually charged my IPad faster than plugging it into the wall. When my wife's iPod was out of juice and she wanted to use it for a walk, I simply gave her the IMP70D, plugged it into her iPod and sent her on her way. She loved it as well.This is one of the single best tech investments I have ever made.The only downside that I have found is that it seems to get dirty very easily on its shiny gloss black finish. Nothing a little rubdown won't fix though.If you need a portable battery charger for your electronic devices, look no further.

*** Disclosure: I received this product for beta testing. The review is based on my own tests. ***I like this product a lot. I have purchased New Trent products before and they are yet to disappoint me. I normally use the external battery packs to charge my Nexus devices. As per my testing so far, I can charge Nexus 7 completely within 8 hours and still have about 50% juice left in the pack. Nexus 4 can be completely charged within 3 hours and still have about 80% of the charge left in the pack. I am still testing this pack and will see how the charging interval changes over time. I charged Nexus 4 and Nexus 7 together and both got charged by more than 50% before the pack went out of charge. I would have liked the ability to charge both the devices up to 100% using the pack. Another thing I missed in this unit is the ability to know when the unit lost all the juice without hitting the power button. Apparently, the charging light doesn't show up while I charge my devices using this product. This is a little inconvenient as we often don't realize that the pack has lost all the charge and is not charging our devices anymore.Another thing I really like about this product is how fast I can recharge it. It is a lifesaver if I am too far away from the charger or need to use my devices while charging.
summary: New Trent Easypak NT70T 7000mAh External Battery Pack and Charger

reviewText: Bought this for my wife, nice that it has incorporated charging cables.  Although, if the charging cable for the unit breaks, there is no other way to charge it (that cable is pretty short too, it hangs from the wall if there is no table close).Works perfectly and charges our Android phones and tablets (Tablet charging drains it fast though).
summary: Works great, charges 2100 mah Android at least twice.

reviewText: Here is another great product I discovered to use with my Note 2.  This particular unit has a very portable footprint and it's relative slim with dimension of 119mm x 74mm x 18mm (4.7" x 2.9" x 0.7"). It's also pretty lightweight for 7000 mAh capacity, at 6.8 oz (193 g). It's definitely very comfortable and pocket/purse friendly. As a matter of fact, this unit is actually intended to be used on the go where you don't even have to worry about power cables since it has built in full usb cable for Input charging (a fast 5V, 1A port) and also micro-usb cable for one of the Output charging ports (5V, 1A). In addition to 1A output port with micro-usb cable, it also provides 2 additional usb ports with 2.1A and 1A outputs. These got you covered for any smart phone or tablet, and can also charge two devices at the same time.For convenience if input charging cable is not long enough for you, New Trent also included USB extension chord which I found to be a great bonus. No other chords or adapters were included with this product. The device itself is very slick with a footprint reminding me a small external hard drive. The bottom of this power bank is finished matte while the top has a shiny piano finish. On the top you also have a discretely placed power button and 4 led power meter indicators with cool green lights. Those 4 lights partition power reading into 25% increments.Beside its portability and convenience of built in cables, the main attraction of this device is a whooping 7000 mAh capacity. This is some serious number!!! And NT70T has this 7000 mAh speced at 3.7V - the voltage of the actual lithium battery. To be honest, I was a little skeptical at first because external battery market is flooded with a lot of high capacity external batteries that have exaggerated labels. So right away I put this battery to the test. I had my Note 2 discharged down to 25% while NT70T was charged all the way to full (4 leds lit up). I used 2.1A output port for a faster charging and used my own usb-to-micro-usb cable. My Note 2 battery got charged up to 100% in under 3 hours. That was very impressive. After charging it up, I checked with NT70T and it still had 3 leds on!!!! Of course, 3 leds doesn't mean it's at full 75% charge, but rather between 50% and 75% charge. But still, very impressive considering we are talking about our GN2 with 3100 mAh stock battery. As a bonus, you can actually charge your phone while charging NT70T, pretty cool although not recommended by manufacturer since it can accelerate aging of the battery.In my opinion this is one of the top small footprint portable external battery chargers that offers simultaneous charging of two devices at the same time with one port being 2.1A and others at 1A, and having a whooping true 7000 mAh capacity!!! A must have if you need a portable backup battery and don't wont to part with your current smart phone case (to accommodate bulky extended battery). I definitely recommend NT70T EasyPack!
summary: Review of New Trent NT70T EasyPack 7000 mAh external battery

reviewText: Was using theEnergizer Energi To Go iPod Charger With 2 AA Lithium Batteriesfor my ultra-portable power source for my Apple products.  Liked this well enough, but with the batteries costing $2 each it would only take 13 charges for this to pay for itself.  Plus the iPhone or iPad could not be in a case for the Energi To Go to function properly.  Finally, I liked that the New Trent would charge both an iPhone and an iPad at the same time.The New Trent is both as tall and thick as an iPhone, and about 150% the width.  It's a handsome unit, but the footprint/form-factor is not why I bought it.I ran both an iPad and iPod Touch down to virtually no battery life.  Plugged them both into the New Trent and started running a movie on both w/o sound.  Below is how much run time which was delivered by the New Trent (i.e., completely depleting the New Trent and both Apple devices):iPad - 5 hoursiPod Touch - 6.5 hoursNot necessarily up to the numbers they are advertising, but this is overkill for my typical situation and just what the doctor ordered for an long plane trip or layover.A couple of considerations (but not big enough to be negatives) are:- takes 9 hours to recharge the New Trent (maybe this is b/c I charged it via my laptop's USB port, though other reviewers have posted this is a good indicator of its durability)- you'll need to keep the USB charging cord for the New Trent as well as the USB charge/sync cord for the iPhone (not included) in the same bag with your New Trent (again, bag not included)- it cannot deliver juice while it is being recharged itself- cannot charge two iPads at onceIf a year from now the New Trent can give me half the performance it is giving me currently (no pun intended), I'll still be a happy camper (pun intended).

As someone who is on the road a lot, this item is a must for all Iphone and Ipad users, or any other gadgets compatible with this product. Charging time is fast (about half an hour to 40 min) and best of all, you can charge 2 devices at the same time.Pros: Sleek design, dual charging option, fast, small, easy to useCons: Only blue LED lights that indicate the condition of the battery. Would be nice to have a red one light up when almost out of juice.

......had me wondering if I should return this item ...This pack(mine being the 6600MAH,,7000MAH just came out a few days ago) took over 12 hours to get a full 4 LED Charge..The charge finally arrived and this battery pack delivers big..Gives my LG Ally a consistant charge/runtime for many hours while on the go..The seller Idealpoint/Amazon is an Ace in customer service...They are there to assist(in a timely manner) no matter how many email questions a customer may have..Will definately order from them again..

I like the protection this case offers, as well as the grip it gives me phone to keep it from sliding out of my pocket in the car ;). I do think it could be a little more rigid but the softness does help with the shock protection. I also think it would be better with the screen protector built in, so it can have a solid strengthening piece at the base of the screen that goes all the way across. This would get rid of any of that flappiness on the sides. Incidentally, using this case with the included screen protector (and perhaps a black rubber band at the base of the screen) definitely makes me feel better about my phone's security =D. I've quite drop-prone, so this is definitely an improvement. I bet it'll be even better when I put a rubber band on it.
I've always been an OtterBox brand person. And this case does not disappoint, I've dropped my phone Nokia a few times with the case and did its job on protecting my phone.

It doesn't get much better than this. It fits literally like a glove on my E71. All the buttons work and I access to all my ports/slots. The included screen protector is thick and will protect the screen well.Very good value for the money.
summary: The best case for your E71 or E71x

reviewText: The case fit the phone without any difficulty and has remained in place through daily use. It allows access to all of the phone's functionality without restriction. It seems to provide excellent protection from minor falls -- i.e. being knocked from a table onto the floor, etc. My only complaint is that the particular polymer used for the case is somewhat attractive to dust. This means that after dropping the case in dirt, one must wipe it off with a clean damp paper towel. I will certainly buy other OtterBox cases for whatever phone I get next.

The OtterBox case for the Nokia E71 is perfect for the phone. This phone is sleek and beautiful, so it's hard to put a case on over all that design. BUT the phone is so slippery, a case is a necessity. The OtterBox case is a great fit, feels good, isn't sticky and looks good. It totally protects the phone, even if dropped on Uffizi's marble floor.

I liked the design, but should be a mix of hard and soft to be perfect. My biggest problem is that this rubber material picks up all the lint from my cotton shirts and gets fuzzy white and have to constantly clean it.

The Otterbox Impact Case for Nokia E71X is just what I needed to protect my new Nokia E71x phone.  This particular case is solid black and comes with a screen protector also.It's easy to slip on and feels sturdy.  The black color will hide the dirt that is likely to gather on it.  My phone is silver with white keys and it looks fine with the black case also.Glad I bought it!

OtterBox case for my Nokia E71 (also purchased on Amazon) arrived earlier than anticipated. The skin is completely functional and has survived a number of removals over a month (for charging in a Nokia base purchased on Amazon) without losing either firmness or shape. When using a the portable Nokia plug-in charger, the OtterBox allows enough space to plug and charge without removal, which many will find sufficient. Would have given the OtterBox 5 stars, except the included screen protector was rendered useless by a sticker that refused to completely come off. Fortunately I had other generic screen protectors, one of which I cut to size and applied. The OtterBox has proved to be an attractive and functional addition to the E71.
summary: Solid outer protection for Nokia E71

reviewText: the good:it connected to my phone so easily and quickly!the USB cord is good (especially since I somehow lost the AC cord 3 days after I got it)the plug is the same as my Motorola phone so I can use my same car charger (also good since I lost my AC adapter)the directions are very easy-I have a Plantronic, which is good, but the directions are so silly to remember I have to carry the manual around)it is lightweight and comfortablethe lights are a good ideathe bad:it is a bit too lightweight and feels flimsythe use time is way shorter than my Plantronicthe ugly:the plug is very hard to put the cords in and out and I'm afraid it will snap off

reviewText: Jabra continues to make high quality headsets.  I bought this to replace a Motorola headset that I had to return.  That was a very good decision.  I haven't had any problems with this unit.

This is the 4th BT headset that i've owned. It is the best one so far but still not perfect.Things I like about it:* good sound quality. I've used it when driving and could hear very well. There were no complaints on the other side too so I assume they could hear me well.* comfortable. I use it with the ear piece and it fits well. You can keep it on while driving and it doesn't bother (almost...). I don't know if it's my ears that are different from all the rest of the world but the 'in ear' innovative ways to mount headsets just never work for me... I must have an ear piece that goes around the ear.* affordable. I got this for the incredibly low price of around $15. I am not comfortable with spending $100 or even $50 for a BT headset no matter how nice its features are. The only thing I would pay more for is for excellent sound quality that can handle background noises and winds. I still haven't heard of a headset that does this perfectly so until there is one, I'll just look for ones that don't cost too much.* easy pairing* can be charged via USB so no need for a power socket (but can still be charged using a socket)* dedicated power button* battery and connection indicatorsthings that I think need to improve* power button is very awkward placed.* power/battery/connection indicators only light when the power button is pressed* this is the most annoying thing: you need to press the power button for a few seconds to turn on/off. A sliding power switch with an on/off position would be best: it will be easy to use and will immediately indicate if the device is on or off. I think Jabra are using this for newer modelsIt's worth noting that integration with iPhone is different from my old headset. for example, i don't know how to direct music to the headset (but maybe you're not supposed to do this. I mean why would you listen to music on a one ear headset...). However, with this headset the phone still rings and most sounds are not directed to the headset until you actually start or answer a call, which i find very useful. with my old BT, all sounds were re-directed to the BT so you couldn't hear 'click' sounds when dialing or even message tones etc.
summary: Affordable, comfortable with good sound quality, but has some design flaws

reviewText: Large ear piece did not fit in my ear. Very uncomfortable. Had a difficult time pairing this item with my phone. Recommend that you keep looking.

The price is good, it is easy to set-up and very user friendly. It is not very comfortable to wear, so I do not recommend it to those people who wear their headsets all the time.One major flaw that I found (maybe it's true for all bluetooth headsets, have not tried others) is that when using it on my computer to make phone calls on Skype, it interferes with my other bluetooth devices such as my Logitech V470 mouse. Hopefully there would be a firmware update to fix this issue.

This unit works seamlessly with my blackberry phone and i got it for a great price. These units cost much more in stores. I have seen them upwards of $60 in some arenas. It works well and connects easily.

Being most grateful for this device, and diluding myself that it's another step in the direction of safety, I've enjoyed this product however, the battery stopped working and it was never left on other than what was in the manual. Telephoning Jabra, I learned they do not have repleacment batteries, we have to buy another unit if it's more than a year old, and I have no idea - it was a gift.However, thanks to Amazon, I'm ordering this one because of the price. It's a stable product, IMHO, for all that I know, and I hope it's somewhat of a protection from direct listening, although I don't use my cell phone for talking very often. Tired of the dang things. I'm moving backward to fountain pens, stationery, and great stamps with music in the background.
This thing allows me to get phone and internet service where others get none. It has to be aimed, but that is pretty quick if you have an idea of where the tower is.
summary: Great product from Wilson, as usual.

reviewText: I live in the country and have a MiFi device for internet that needed a boost.  You need some extra parts for this antenna (listed here) for setup but it works great for me.  I have two computers set up in a 'home group' on Windows 7 and need a wireless connection for them to talk to one another.  The wireless connection doesn't have to be fast for that but it does have to be consistent. The internet is another matter. Without decent speed I can't watch the occasional YouTube video or get a screen refresh before falling asleep, to say nothing of hefty downloads.  The Verizon MiFi 4510L gadget was working fine at first on 3G from my local tower, but then they upgraded to 4G and since we are in a '4G extended coverage area', I sometimes would get 4G (WooHoo!), but sometimes back to 3G or sometimes nothing at all.  Sometimes the MiFi card was switching back and forth so much the thing would just give up and/or my computers couldn't reconnect consistently anymore.  On busy internet days over the holidays, it was so frustrating I was ready to scream.  I was reconnecting, rebooting and resetting more than I was getting any work done.  I prayed there was something that could help me.I had no idea what that might be so called Wilson directly and ended up getting my the stuff from them, but it's a much better deal here.  Still I'm not complaining because I'm not techie at all and wouldn't have known what to buy without their help.I know where my tower is so having a directional antenna works fine for me (they sent an omni-directional type too to try, but this is the one that works best for me, so I'm sending the other back).  The antenna must be mounted outside on a pole.  My pole is stuck in the ground rather than on the roof. I bought a 10' galvanized pipe at Home Depot which is now sunk into the ground about 18" and is about 18" from the side of the house where the mounted antenna can be pointed at the tower.  The directions say not to aim the antenna 'through' the house to prevent 'feedback' so you have to find a location with a fairly straight shot in the direction of the tower (trees don't seem to matter, we have plenty).  Distant buildings apparently aren't a problem either.You also need to buy a low loss coax cable to go from the antenna to a small MiFi connector cable.  I got a 20' coax which they call 'RG-58 Cable FME male to MCX connector'. This cable attaches to the antenna and then to the small connector cable that plugs into the MiFi card.  I already had a MiFi connector from Verizon from when I'd tried their small inside antenna (which didn't work at all).  The MiFi cable is called a 'Novatel 4510L TS-9 Antenna Adapter'. I didn't see one here, but Verizon has them. My outside pole is near the room where the desktop computer is and where I have the MiFi when it is plugged in (it has to be within 30' of the computer) so I drilled a hole for the cable to come inside the house at that location.The hardest part of setup for us was sinking the pipe into the ground, which we did from a ladder with a small hand sledge hammer.  It didn't matter that the top of the pipe was squashed a bit from being beaten on as the included U clamps to attach the antenna are generous.  We tried a couple of slightly different directions and tightened up the antenna when it was pointing in the best one.My improvement in speed is wonderful.  So far, I've had consistent 4G connectivity and the speed is as fast as the broadband my son gets in town.  I'm a happy camper.  Even if it isn't always this good, it's definitely better than before.

I work in a dead zone.  I have little to no signal even though I can see the cell tower in the distance.  With this mounted on a mast on the roof I get a solid 2 bars of 4g through a wilson sleek booster that did not work with the original antenna that came with the booster.  This even works with a 75ohm cable that I am using dispit being a 50ohm antenna.  Would buy again and will use this until it falls apart.  I doubt it will fall apart though...  it is a very solid construction.

Clear 4G Internet service is great, but I had to move to a different part of the city.  The building is mostly metal I'm in but I'm in between 3 towers.  Closest window gets me -85db.  Hooking this up on roof and slowly aiming around to known antennas I achieved -50db!  Back to 6+Mbs(Had to purchase a cable N to SMA... did it at Fry's since I wanted to match up physically instead of hoping to get the right connections)
summary: Works great with my 4G Clear Express Hub!

reviewText: I like this antenna, not just wild band range also very even the gain for all bands, good for price as well.
summary: nice quality as usual as Wilson made

reviewText: I used this over a gap of 20 miles to the tower with some hills in between. The reception with the antenna was just not there. With the antenna I had a stable 2G signal. The tower was just 2 G.

This antenna will not work with the Virgin Mobile WiFi, even though it says it will work with all cellular networks. The Virgin mobile device has the antenna outputs on the Sierra Wireless, but an external antenna it is not supported. The only thing you can use is a cradle that they sell, as far as I have been able to find out.I paid an exorbitant amount for shipping from this seller and ended up returning it and had to pay for more shipping. I lost $$ on the deal and it didn't work. I am sticking with Amazon Prime on everything from now on.
summary: Will NOT work with Virgin Mobile WiFi

reviewText: This antena is nice. Please note that you can get this same antenna as 50 ohm or 75 ohm.  some cell amplifiers are 75ohm (the cheaper ones).  However, you wont loose too much if you use the more available 50ohm wilson-400 coax and the 50 ohm antenna and attach it to a 75ohm amplifier.  You will loose way more signal by not purchasing high quality co-ax (LMR-400 or its knockoff wilson-400).

It's hard to review just an antenna, which is only part of most cell signal amplification systems (commonly known as repeaters). This antenna came as part of a larger package that included a Wilson amp, cable, etc. Before installing the Wilson system, we had constant dropped calls, when we could make or receive a call at all. The majority of the time I'd call my wife and her phone would never even ring do to poor reception inside out home. We only live four miles form the Sprint PCS tower, but our home was built in the 1930's and has very thick, solid walls, and the tower is blocked by large trees that surround our home.I still need to tweak the system I put in, but now we have a solid three to six bars signal throughout our home and we haven't lost a call since installing the system. I have the antenna mounted to the outside of my house withWinegard DS-2000 Universal Antenna Mount with U-boltsand it was a quick and easy installation. I used six 3/16" x 2 inch long lag screws and drilled right through the siding and into a vertical 2"x4" on the inside of my attic. Then drilled a hole through the frame of the plastic vent located on the outside wall near the peak of the roof, ran the coax cable through it and liberally caulked the hole around the cable with white silicone sealant.

I guess I'm going to need one that has the neoprene inserts.  This one just has a speaker insert that doesn't help it stay in the ear.The over ear loop is hard plastic and tends to hurt after a while.For the price, it works, but my old headset sounded a lot better.

Snapped off pretty easily soon after I bought it, so I had to tape the flimsy plastic earpiece together so I could get some use out of it, but it looks silly.If you have another $20 to spend, maybe even just another $10, you could get same quality but better earpiece, even better looking.  This could be a five star device if they had just asked a half-smart monkey to design the plastic ear hook better.---Recently bought a Plantronics bluetooth for about $40 that is heads and shoulders above this one in build quality.  Obvious when I opened the box that they did find a half-smart monkey, or at least a decent engineer, to design the earpiece which is thicker and connected to the actual device better.  I rely on my earpiece too much to have one that breaks unnecessarily.

Pros:Very clear voice qualityVery good noise cancellationCompetitive priceComfortable with the earhook onIt feels like it will be a very durable headsetLasts all day, even when I talk for hoursBeeps when you leave the range of the headset, auto reconnects and beeps again when you return to the range of the headset (most headsets just disconnect don't warn you that you have disconnected.  Then they don't try to reconnect on their own.  You have to do it manually.)I LOVE the on/off button.  This is the only headset I have ever had (and I've had a lot) that had a dedicated button for this.  It keeps you from oops calling people by bumping the headset in your pocket or wearing down the battery by accidentally turning it on.Cons:If you push the headset all the way in your ear, the sound gets muffled.Headset looks like it should be comfy without the earhook, but it doesn't stay in my ear.The earhook is very awkward at first and takes some getting used to, but once you get used to it it's very comfortable.For a very low price point, here is a headset with as good of call quality and noise cancellation as the BlueAnt Z9i (and less than half the price).  Bravo, Samsung!

reviewText: I have owned several headsets over the years.On a scale of 1-10 (1- junk to 10-love it):Motorola 500 = 1 (returned in less than a week)Jabra 5020 = 10 (still going strong, except noise cancelling is getting worse)Cardo 700 = 10 (worked 100% the longest, now the microphone works intermittent)SoundId 100 = 10 (still working, lasted almost as long as the cardo before the noise cancelling went out)Plantronics 232 = 1 (like the motorola 500, why bother producing junk and souring your reputation)And that leads me to this one - Samsung 470. I give it a 9 (would have given it a 10 but because of the button and fit..see below)I gave it 5 stars above because I feel my gripes are personal and not because of the product.After 2 weeks of use, I am amazed at the quality of this little bluetooth. Sound quality is great. Both sides of the call are hard pressed to know you are on a headset. Mic and speaker are crystal clear. Volume is loud and clear. My only gripes are the ear hook and button. The ear hook can become uncomfortable after an hour or so of wear. I consider myself to have larger ears and know fit will be different for everyone as no two ears are the same. As for the button...the main multipurpose button is a tad hard to push. Its hard to tell if it was tapped or not, so then you try it again and find out you are in your phones voice assistance mode. But its early, and could just be a learning curve to get use to. All in all a great product. I ended up buying another for a friend. Almost forgot, the best feature is the sliding on/off switch. Tired of others having teeny buttons that need to be held for 5-10 seconds. With that time lag, one cannot turn on the headset and the phone is ringing because it wont connect in time. With the Samsung, when your phone rings, flip the switch to on and you are connected by the 3rd or 4th ring. Very fast!***UPDATE 1/5/2011***Still using this headset as my everyday bluetooth. Still works like day one and still very happy with it. Sound is loud and clear. Pairs quickly with my HTC Incredible.

reviewText: After suffering real pain every single day using the headset that came standard with my new Blackberry Torch, I knew I had to make a change or give up listening to my audio-books and music. They have a microphone and a remote control with the volume, skip and pause on the cord - no need to remove the phone from your holster or pocket! All these buttons worked properly as soon as the headset was plugged into my phone. If you have voice dialing set up on your Torch it can work with this headset and that is very nice. Sound quality is good with simple voice narration from an audio book. The sound is very good with actual music - in fact this headset is louder than the original, which means I no longer have to keep the volume at it's highest level. Additionally, if you click the options in the BB menu on your phone, you can adjust the sound to reflect the type of music you're listening to and this headset does reflect the change. The carrying case is hard and fits well in a purse or the center console of the car. But most importantly the ear buds are size adjustable with the three different size tips included. The multiple options are easy to change out and since one of my ears is slightly smaller than the other I can put a small tip on the left and a medium tip on the right side - NO MORE PAIN!!I like these so much I am considering buying another set for travel.*************Jan 2012 UPDATE ***********************After almost a full year of regular use, these headphones are working just fine with no issues at all. Additionally they work nicely with my Kindle (audio books) around the house. I have had no problems with them at all.

reviewText: I have a number of bluetooth earpieces, and found that I despise the kind that hang, clip, or poke into your ear.  They are uncomfortable, and for some reason, whenever I see one of the typical ones clinging to someone's ear, it looks like some high tech cockroach perched there.  Obviously, I wanted something else.I read a gazillion reviews--I needed reliability from my headset.  I want good sound--I don't want it to sound like I'm on the end of a string with a tin can.  This headset manages that...but...**It picks up interference from common household appliances, causing sound to break up for the other side.  This was despite remaining within 8 feet of the phone.**There is nothing to indicate how much charge is on the headset, leaving the user guessing whether or not it's going to last through the next call.  It's battery life is as unpredictable and short as the Android phone it's paired with, but unlike the phone, the mystery is always how far it's gone down.**It randomly goes to sleep and then resumes the connection, without warning.  That left me uncertain whether to pick up the phone or the headset, and you could bet it would be the wrong one.**The buttons on the headset are right over the earpiece, so if you go to readjust the position of the headset, you are apt to disconnect the call or change the volume before you get the earpiece readjusted to perch over your ear properly.**The headband is very thin and flimsy to the touch, and I'm afraid that with rough usage, it's apt to break, rendering the headset useless.  That means that bringing it along on a trip and NOT wearing it is very risky.This wasn't an expensive headset, and it is partly true that you get what you pay for.  Overall, I feel it was a reasonable purchase, since I couldn't afford a $100+ bluetooth over-the-head-headset right now.  I like the absence of the dangling wire, but I miss having buttons I can see and use appropriately too.  It does perform as well or better than any other blue tooth headset I have used in this price range.  It's performance is good enough for the price that my daughter is planning on purchasing one for herself as well.

So I'm kinda stuck because I really like the sound quality and it works great on my iPad still, but I cannot use it with any other devices.ProsComfortableVery good sound qualityLong battery lifeRange is good (25 ft. easy for me)ConsSupport is non-existent.

No go. Took about 30 seconds to wiggle it out. I'm pretty sure I would have missed my call from my boss by then.I decided to use the case with iPhone 4s bare and it worked wonders. reviewText: The cover and battery came new as listed, however once I inserted the replacement battery and tried to put on the cover that came with it, I immediately started having problems. First of all, the battery cover wont properly latch into the phone and from time to time it will actually come off. Second thing I noticed was, the battery life of my Palm Pre Plus Was only ever so slightly extended and I mean it when I say, it was hardly noticeable.For the extra bulk it makes, that in its self is not worth the extra 30 minutes of talk time it gives. But the major problem I have over all other problems I listed is that, the replacement battery charges poorly to say the least. Not only does it take forever to charge when not in use, but when I use the Mobile Hotspot feature on my Palm Pre Plus, it drains the battery extremely fast. So upon realizing this, I started plugging my phone into my home charger, however I found that even when it is plugged in, the battery still drains!I have sense boxed the big bulky worthless battery, bought some car chargers and switched back to the original battery and cover. Spend the extra money on a better quality battery, I wish I had!!!

UPDATE: I found a method at precentral to determine the actual battery capacity as identified by the manufacturer. It turns out this battery only has a capacity of 2300mAh and I am feeling very ripped off. I also have another battery from this brand and it is also showing itself to be mislabeled. I will be complaining to Siedio and posting back here if/when they make it right.It still gives me much better life than my standard battery, but if they continue to mislabel them I am forced to recommend the other brands available on Amazon and not anything from Siedio. This explains why I was barely getting twice the life when I should be getting at least 2.3x Grrrr.I love my Pre+. No one does contacts and calendar better than Palm. No one ever has, no one is now, and perhaps no one ever will. But, the Pre uses the same battery as the Centro and battery life is terrible. I spent my first day doing nothing but internet and appstore stuff, and I got about 5 hours of life from the stock battery. Palm should be ashamed of that - I get a lot more than 5 hours from my notebook PC!So, this is about 2.3 times the capacity of the standard battery, so it should get you through until evening before you need a recharge. If you don't use it for more than a phone, you should be able to talk for a week on one charge.This is a great choice if you just want capacity. It comes with a nicely finished back cover that is actually easier to take off or put on than the stock cover.Two problems that you should consider:1) It doesn't work with the Touchstone charger. I didn't think that would be a problem because I didn't even buy one. Then I tried the Touchstone. They are the coolest thing ever. Sure the wireless charging and intelligent behavior changes when it is on the Touchstone are nice. But, I'm impressed because I can stick in on my dashboard or console and I have the equivalent of a car kit. So much better than having it slide around, or having to look down to dial. I've ordered the smaller Seidio 1350MAh battery that fits in the standard cover so I can have 17% more battery and use the Touchstone when I'm on those long drives. I would give this battery 5 stars if they had an option for a Touchstone back plate. I'd be willing to pay $25-$30 for it, too. Hopefully there is no technical reason why they can't make that for this battery. If you don't care about Touchstone support, this wont bother you.2) It makes your phone much thicker. Not a problem for me, and it actually makes it easier to type on the keyboard. But, it goes from being "Droid thin" to 3/4" thick. That's thicker than the 1st-generation iPod and about 50% thicker than a Blackberry Curve. If you are looking for razor thin, you need a battery that works with the stock cover. If you only care about long life, this this is great.There are other batteries that are even bigger, but they are more than twice the price. This hits the right mix of capacity and size for those that can live with a thicker phone. If those two items don't bother you, this is a great battery for you, and at a great price.Oh, several have mentioned problems with being loose fitting. That has apparently solved, because this fits as well as the stock battery. You should ignore those complaints.
summary: mislabeled, turns out to only be a 2300mAh battery. lowered my rating

reviewText: when I got the palm pre i knew that the beautiful screen, multi-tasking, bluetooth streaming, constant facebook, myspace, and text checks would eat the little included battery alive: four hours tops with all above mentioned.with the seidio extended battery: all day, with 30% to spare at night.and it gives the phone a sturdy feel. the rubberized coating is perfect.if you have a pre and intend to use it like a laptop like i do, get this battery. best [...]i've spent in a while.

I ordered one of these for my Pre to try it out.  Price on here is great.It is very easy to insert into the phone, and the back cover goes on more easily than the OEM one.  God bless China.  The feeling is more grippy and rubberized than the factory back cover, and it is impossible to accidentally touch the camera lens with it on (where it was unavoidable before).  The camera flash does cause a gray fuzzy image due to light reflecting off the bottom of the deep camera hole in this replacement cover.  There are rumors that Sedio is redesigning the back and will replace these for free in the future.As for the overall feel of the phone with this battery, it feels more substantial and less awkward to open, close, and type on with the slight added thickness.  The cover seems more durable than the original.Battery life is dramatically improved.  After two weeks of break-in, I am able to get about 72 hours with wifi on and location services on.  This battery is an absolute must if you want to avoid having to worry about topping off the charge half way through your day.  After using mine and liking it so much, I just ordered a second for the wife's Pre.

I have purchased two Seidio extended batteries now, one for my Blackberry Tour and one for my Palm Pre Plus. Both last amazingly and get better with training time! I read a recommendation to charge 100% and keep charging for at least a couple more hours to begin the battery training, so this is how I started both batteries. I let them run down to the 20+ percent and recharged like the first charge for a few times. The Blackberry Tour battery has performed right from the start, and only improved from there. The Pre Plus battery held charge all day and I recharged in the evening overnight. Because of my Blackberry use (I just used as I normally would) I thought I needed to push the Pre Plus battery more by uber-using it all day; Pandora, texting, calls, browsing and playing games to run it down. The next day it performed better and each day has improved. Now I am using it as I personally would normally use my device. I really appreciate Seidio extended batteries! The back cover for the Blackberry added a little more bulk, but the Pre Plus back cover has definitely added more. Since I am new to Palm Pre Plus and I started with the extended battery within a few days of using it I can only say I don't mind the bulk. My daughter tried it and said it makes it easier for texting (she is the one who gave me a Pre Plus) and it made the phone a lot chubbier, but the cover looks nice on the phone. I think the Pre Plus cover looks nicer than the Tour cover, but only because of the latch on the Tour cover. Maybe Seidio should have made the latch black also on the Tour cover, instead of the "silver-ish" paint they use now. I would recommend Seidio extended batteries to anyone who can use them for their smartphones. I also use Skinomi Tech Skins on my devices. Both products are worth the money paid!

I've had this battery for 5-6 weeks. First, let me say, yes, this battery makes my palm pre much chunkier... but I would rather a chunky phone with a charged battery than a make a fashion statement with a phone that's constantly connected to a charger. After my first charge with the new battery, my phone stayed at 100% for hours! It gradually dropped and I charged it on the third day! Unthinkable with my original battery, as I was charging it twice a day. Now here's where it gets strange. I plugged the battery in to charge it the first time and it immediately dropped from 12% to 0%. I thought that was strange, even disconnected it to see if it would go back up to 12% but it stayed at 0%. I didn't have an incident like that again ........ UNTIL NOW. My phone was completely charged 2 nights ago so it was at 100% yesterday morning ... last night it was somewhere around 78%, when I went to bed and this morning it was turned off with a 0% charge. Not happy about that. Especially since I just threw away the original packing. Up until last night, I was getting 2 to 3 days out of a charge and was extremely happy.One of the main reasons I bought this battery is we're going on a trip next week and I wanted a reliable battery because I wouldn't be near a charger most of the time. Now I'm worried that my battery will drain in a flash. I may have to pack my spare.SO... had I rated this battery yesterday, I would have given it 5 stars, but to lose 78% of it's charge overnight definitely made me re-think that rating. 3 stars for my fickle chunky battery.
summary: Seidio Innocell Battery for Palm Pre ...coulda been a 5-star

reviewText: The product is what it says it is.  It adds significantly to the battery life--Seidio claims 90% more.  I haven't even attempted any scientific test, but it has changed me from having my Pre typically at 10-20% of battery life remaining at the end of the workday to having about 50%.  Substantial improvement!For me, almost as important as the battery life is the coating on the outside of the replacement battery cover provided.  One of the things I disliked greatly about the Pre is that the sleek and shiny surface of the case makes me live in constant fear I'll drop the thing.  The added bulk of this battery means that it needs more room than in the factory case, so when Seidio provided a new roomier battery cover, it coated it with a soft, slightly grippy substance that makes me feel a LOT more comfortable with my Pre!  I like this a lot.  If you have handled a Treo 755p (and presumably other late-model Treos) the coating is similar to the grippy stuff on those phones.  This is a worthwhile upgrade in itself!  It has a more matte appearance compared to the shiny surface of the original case, and if you are highly sensitive to appearances, you may dislike the mismatch between the top case around the screen and the bottom case with the coating.  Doesn't bother me at all, though.The downsides are minor for me, but I am one of those who is hung up on function over form.  Shifting to this battery and battery cover means your Pre will bulk up quite a bit!  It is much thicker, and I've seen others compare the new form factor to a hockey puck.  I'd prefer the Pre be smaller and thinner, but it doesn't bother me that much.  With the bigger battery installed, my Pre is about the same size as my old Treo 755p--A tiny bit thicker and definitely not as "tall" in the longest dimension.  As of now, I know of no battery case that is designed to fit this combination.  Presumably Seidio will provide one soon, and you can probably locate one that works by trying out cases designed for larger phones, but I am carrying my Pre in my pants pocket "bareback" for now.For me, this was an excellent upgrade.
summary: Add life and a bit of bulk to your Pre

reviewText: For summary, skip to the bottom.So, I've owned my Palm Pre for just under a year now.  I love the phone.  I didn't think anything would be able to pull me away from the world of Blackberry after many years of faithful service; but with RIM's desire to cater to the iPhone crowd and their devices becoming more "consumer" rather than "business", I felt the need to jump ship.  Additionally, my monthly bill was extremely high, which in this economy was unacceptable.I've never been a Palm fan.  I felt the operating systems were archaic and their devices not attractive at all.  While some business types swore by them in the 90's, especially the legendaryPalmOne PalmPilot Professional Organizerand the once-ubiquitousPalm Treo 650 - Smartphone - GSM - bar - Palm OS, I just found them less than appealing compared to other devices at that time.  When Palm announced the Palm Pre and the Palm Pixl, I didn't bat an eye at either.  Both looked like extremely ugly, "consumer" phones, and I felt that they had done what RIM was also doing: bowing down to the iPhone crowd.  When RIM released theBlackberry Storm Verizon 9530 OEM  RIM Cell Phone, I knew it was time to jump ship, and I went searching, eventually settling on the Palm Pre Plus, from Verizon (DROID just looked ugly and unusable for what I wanted in a phone). I will tell you the one thing that sold me on the Pre Plus: the free Mobile Hotspot.  It allowed me to drop myNovatel Wireless MiFi 2200 3G Mobile WiFi Hotspot Modem (Verizon Wireless)line entirely and just have one device for wireless internet and phone.  Over time I grew to love the phone; the multitasking was superior to anything I'd ever used, the interface was pleasant, and the phone easy to hold.  Touchstone was also quite innovative for its time.  But something was wrong.In the middle of all of this, the battery life was an absolute joke.  I don't just mean it wasn't good.  I mean it was absolutely HORRID.  To the point it wouldn't last half a day if I had two hour-long calls.  To the point that if I left Mobile Hotspot active, the phone would be dead in an hour.  This was unacceptable.I ended up buying a Touchstone for work and one for home, which helped, but I couldn't help but be frustrated at the notion that I had to keep my phone docked in order to keep it charged.  I don't make or receive very many calls, but I'm a strong data user and I can't live without my email on the move.  I resolved to look for an extended battery, and saw that across the Interweb, this was the one to get.  Only problem: Seidio refused to create a Touchstone-compatible back case.  Absolutely unbelievable.  That little oversight alone prevented me from buying the battery until very recently, when I just got so frustrated I decided to bite the bullet.  I'm glad I did...but not all is well, even with the extended battery.  Let me be clear.- With the regular battery, a two hour phone call and your phone will be less than halfway charged.  Push email and your phone will be dead in 3 hours.  Enable Mobile Hotspot, and it's dead in an hour, MAYBE two.  Screen brightness at full?  4 hours tops.  It just does not handle its battery well at all.  With the extended battery, the only things that will kill the battery before its time are Mobile Hotspot and certain apps that don't let the processor go to a lower MHz, such as certain clock apps that are designed to leave the phone screen active.  With the extended battery I was able to get battery life equal to the MiFi out of Mobile Hotspot; however, one night I went to bed with the battery remaining at 73%, enabled a clock app I bought from the Catalog that leaves the screen on, and my phone was dead by the morning.  Very odd, for just a persistently active screen, but I'm guessing the screen being active means the processor was running at a higher clock than in its standby state.- If you don't ever use Mobile Hotspot or those types of apps, it's quite possible to have the phone last more than 24 hours without needing to be charged.  That's unheard of in a smartphone these days.- The battery is about 1.5x the thickness of the standard battery, so the regular case is no longer going to fit.  This means two things for you: One, you will no longer have the cool "Palm" logo on the back of your phone.  Two, the phone won't work with Touchstone (See comments to this review though).- The case that Seidio does give you is not the same texture as the Palm case, so don't expect it to feel as top notch.  Quite the contrary, it feels quite cheap.So...do I recommend it?  It's hard to say.  If you don't know what Touchstone is (or don't care), yes it is worth it.  If you don't use Mobile Hotspot (or don't know what that is either), then yes I do recommend it.  If you're like me and you maximize the use of your phone, then you might be at odds with your decision.  I can say this much: it's better having it than not.  It makes the phone feel more like the competition, and those that have used the Palm Pre or the Palm Pixl for any extended period of time know that webOS is by far and away superior to anything out there, held back only by the battery and the quality of the hardware.  This battery at least resolves one of the two issues.
summary: Does what it promises.  Be aware of a few things.

reviewText: This case has many 5-star reviews.  I suspect the reviews were written soon after the user got the case, put it on the Pre, and was impressed with the fit, finish, the attractive minimalist design, matte finish, and that it's the only case that still allows you to charge via touchstone.  I give it one star b/c what good is a case that you won't be able to use in a month?One of the main reasons I bought this case is b/c of the high praise from pre cen tral (seemed like everyone's standard case there) and the fact it's touchstone capable. If you have a Sprint Pre, you know that the touchstone back is not included unlike the Verizon Pre Plus (edit 5/17/2010: Pre Plus will be avail for AT&T; and it will include touchstone back and the charger! Sprint continues to fail by by selling the original Pre, not Pre Plus, and without any accessories, yet it's still $150 in many cities!). I thought Seidio's back can replace Palm's touchstone back and it was only after I received the package that I discovered that I needed to buy a separate touchstone case (another $20). Side note: these accessories can cost some good change - $26 for Seidio case, $35 for touchstone charger, and another $20 for touchstone back. This is after having just spent $ 1 30 on a new Pre at Radio Shack with a 2 year contract. If you're new to Pre, make sure you use your Pre for at least a month and happy with it before you start plunking down money for expensive accessories.Back to the topic: The case is way overpriced for what it is. It's just 2 pieces of plastic (plus a foam insert for the back cover when you're not using a touchstone cover). Depending on where you buy, you'll spend anywhere from $22-30+. The plastic is quite thin, however this is a good thing b/c it also feels quite strong, so it will not add significant bulk to the phone. That's one of the main differences compared to the $5 plastic cases on ebay. Plus it's feather light. Fit is perfect. The thinness is the reason why touchstone works. If you're familiar with touchstone, with the regular touchstone cover, the magnetic field makes the phone snap into place quite firmly onto the charger. This is putting a thin piece of plastic in between the touchstone cover and the touchstone base.  So the phone doesn't "snap" as firmly onto the charger and you have to more or less find the sweetspot (you'll know it when you feel it), but once on the charger, the phone stays on. Unfortunately, as others have mentioned, the magnetic bond is too weak to make it stay in place in a moving car.For those wondering, the case does not protrude into the gesture area or impede gesture or the slider mechanism whatsoever.  How is this achieved? By making the tabs that clip the case onto the phone as small and unobtrusive as possible. And THAT is the major flaw. There are 4 tabs at each corner of the top cover and bottom cover.I lovED the case. Then on day 3, the bottom-right tab snapped off. No, I did not abuse the phone nor the case (it's a new phone, remember?). This is just during regular use. You have to understand, these tabs are VERY VERY small and thin. To give you an idea, each tab has a width of a dental floss and only about 3mm long. It's really just a matter of time before they give out and break off. So the back cover with 3 tabs now became a bit loose but still usable. B/c the Pre has legendary fit and finish (ha!), the loose back cover only added to the slightly loose slider mechanism and the overall, the phone felt cheap and old.  Fast forward a month and today, the bottom-left tab broke off and now the back cover is pretty much useless. I've had the case little over a month.Obviously, I'm not the only one with this issue. You can find countless other reviews about the tabs breaking. Don't think we are the few unlucky ones. Given time, this case will break. It will happen to you. You will not be the exception.So until Seidio addresses the major design flaw, you may be better off investing in a different case. If touchstone is important to you as it is to me, then you may want to consider getting one of those Zaggs clear films on the front - the film advertised as being used "to protect helicopter blades" that wrap around the corners and edges of the phone, not just the flat top surface. The back cover won't need protection b/c the touchstone cover has a rubbery, scratchproof finish and is replaceable.I've read one reviewer saying Seidio replaced the case for free so I will be contacting Seidio soon to see if I can get a free replacement as well. But even if they did that, do I want to keep repeating a pattern of having to ship the broken case and get the new one?Update 5/17/2010: I actually contacted the seller (authorized dealer) about the case and they replaced it promptly for free. I just had to ship it to them, which cost me just two stamps and an envelope. This time, I got to enjoy it for about a month, then unfortunately, one of the tabs broke. I'm done with this case. I'll look into getting a clear film for the top while using the touchstone back.With everything said, I cannot recommend this case. Save your money and look for alternatives.Update 7/20/2010: AGF now makes a case that's touchstone compatible. Google "agf grt pre case".  That said, I have been enjoying not having a case on my pre which also means I don't have to put up with the bulk and the headache of it breaking. In the beginning I thought I needed a case instinctively to protect my new investment. But with anything, with enough use, the amount of care and attachment dwindles over time. I just have a screen protector film in the front and a touchstone back. I bought the screen protector film off of e bay (5 for $3 shipped) and while it's not Zaggs and does not cover the entire front surface (does not go to the curved corner areas), it's good enough for me. Zaggs is overpriced anyway.
summary: Best case out there if only not for the HUGE flaw - Seidio, I hope you're reading this

I also like the case to have a small "lip" that protrudes past the glass for drop protection and so that I can place it face-down when putting it on a table to protect the glass screen.  I've tried:A leather vertical flip case from Belkin (great protection, but interfered with the sides of the touch screen and made answering the phone a little awkward);Casecrown Polycarbonate Slim-Fit Case (not enough drop protection);Switcheasy Rebel-Serpent (great drop protection, nice front lip to protect the front,  and it looks very cool, but it felt too bulky in my hand);In-Case Slider (I felt it had inadequate protection for the front, the top kept slipping up AND it left a hairline scratch on the black back of my phone):A rubberized case from Squaretrade, which was given as a freebie with my iPhone warranty purchase (real good protection but the lint factor was nasty);The Speck Candyshell:  perfect. It has a lip that protects the front. It looks very sleek and feels good in my hand. The funny thing is that it may be the same bulk as the Rebel, but looks sleeker simply because you can see the chrome bezel of the phone. Also, it feels better in my hand. More tactile, though you would think it would be more slippery since it has a high gloss finish. After a lot of research looking for best 3GS case, I ordered the Candyshell black.  As many others have already said, I didn't want a soft case because of lint and stretching.  I didn't want a hard case because of lack of protection and potential damage to the phone and because I wanted to be able to leave my BestSkinsEver (like Zagg InvisibleShield) full-body skin on inside the case to keep it like new for when I sell/pass it to someone else.The Candyshell is made very well and seems like it would provide great protection.  The fit with the installed full-body skin was no problem at all due to the flexibility of the Candyshell.  Since the Candyshell doesn't overlap the chrome on the front, there was also no issue of the screen protector being dislodged or damaged by the case.Unfortunately, after only a week of careful use (desk to pocket to car to pocket to desk) with no drops, the back of the Candyshell is scratched very badly and looks pretty bad.  I still rated the case 5 stars since this is entirely a cosmetic issue as it doesn't affect the ability of the case to protect the phone.  It is very annoying on something that is so new (for me, anyway), so I'm going to try the white instead as I've read that the scratches are much less visible.  It seems that maybe Speck should have used a different finish or coating on the rear of the case.Still seems like the Candyshell would provide the best protection and easiest installation of the more substantial cases available.  The ability to use it with a full-body skin is a huge point for me.  I just didn't like how bad the back looked after so little time.  Hopefully, the white will look better.
