reviewText: I looked around a lot before deciding to purchase this product.I really like that it has a special Samsung USB cable included that allows Samsung smartphones to see the device as an AC charger, thereby pulling the extra electricity to charge the device faster like a wall outlet.It is also nice that it includes both a 1amp and a 2amp usb port and can use standard usb cables.

Summary:  Great little battery that charges my IPad faster than the wall charger.Alright, I have three batteries now.  Bought two of the larger IMP models, and wanted one for my wife so got this one too.  If you see below, my review of the IMP120 follows, and this is essentially the same type of device but slightly lower battery reserve (9900 versus say 10-12000 some others have).PROS:  Small.  Has two USB outputs for either 2A (Ipad)or 1A output (phones/etc).  Relatively inexpensive.  Kind of cool looking.I hooked this up to my IPad and found that it charged several times faster than say plugging into the wall with the standard IPad charger.  For example, had the IPad at about 60% and within about less than hour I was up to full power.  Plug in your IPad into the wall and it takes considerably longer to do this...don't really know why, probably has something to do with efficiency of DC vs AC or whatever...I am sure some science nut can clarify why this is so...doesn't really matter...just know I like it!CONS:  You have to hold the power button down a full four seconds or so to turn it on...Though this may be a PRO for some people worried about it accidentally turning on in your backpack or purse.What I would like to see in a portable charger:  Would like to be able to strap my phone into this thing or something..  If you are like me, you may keep one of these in a work bag/satchel/briefcase as I do.  I tend to attach my phone to it while I am out and about.  They tend to bounce around in my bag separately.  NO BIGGIE.  But it would be nice to have the option to somehow integrate some form of strap or device to keep them together without overheating or whatever.Bottom line summary:  Got this so my wife could pop it into her purse as a backup as for some reason she goes through her battery quite fast and she doesn't mind the extra weight and bulk in her bag.  Guess that means she likes it?  ...or is she just putting up with my electronic accessory fetish?__________________________________________________This is now my The New Trent IMP120 provides easy, reliable portable power. Owning several devices, our family devices vary from droid phones, iphones, ipods, to the kindle and IPads, it has proven to be an essential part of my travel gear. I take it with me on personal and business travel, and don't have to worry about access to an AC source no matter where I am. Even brought one to Disneyland knowing that one of the family phones would drain throughout the long day, and it really was reassuring to have it so we could stay in contact at the park.What I like about the device is its portability as well as ability to charge and recharge my devices. I have owned the older and now have the two port USB model. With the newer model now having 12000 mAhrs of battery life, it can easily recharge my iPad (as long you don't drain the iPad battery) or several phones to full power before needing recharging itself.Compared to similar devices , it is competitively priced and simple to use, compatible with most phone and devices.The downside to the device is its slight bulk and weight, however, this is to be expected for the amount of juice that it allows you to carry. Also, they provide a neat and fancy carrying case, but it is only just big enough to fit the device and not the charging cord or any other USB cords that you would intuitively want to bring. It may have been a good idea to include a sleeve into the carrying case to accommodate most smart phones. In addition, if you have a Samsung galaxy, you will need to use an included USB converter which seems easily lost.The device is rated for about 500 charges, about what you would expect from a backup battery source. However, having owned one for about a year with probably intermediate amount of use, it still holds it charge very well and has not had any issues whatsoever.I am a pretty picky consumer and now have two of these devices, and that is as good as a recommendation I can give!

I have the HTC EVO 4G LTE, which does not have a removable battery.  So I purchased this to be my backup.  I love it!  It does fit in my purse, though with everything else, it's full now...  lol  It lasts for several recharges for my phone (plus I'm always loaning it to daughters... lol).  It has two USB ports, so 2 girls can charge at the same time.  I love the soft-touch material (NO FINGERPRINTS) that it's covered with.  My husband has the more powerful iCruiser but he was jealous of my iGeek!  ;-)  Many, many times I would have been without my phone if I had not had this great tool!

I recently switched from the iPad 1 to the New iPad when I needed to video conference with classes while I was away from home. All of the amazing improvements in the New iPad make it a battery hungry device. I enjoy camping, hiking and other outdoor activities. I use both my iPad 3 and iPhone 4 to stay connected while I am camping. I use both navigation and GPS apps which take a tremendous amount of battery. I chose the iGeek (IMP99D) to make sure that I always have a charge.I found that the iGeek is great for my battery needs. The actual design is great. It is small and sleek, so it fits in the same pocket as my iPhone in most of my bags. The blue lights that line one side indicate how much battery you have which is good to know before you go on a hike looking for specific GPS coordinates. (I wish I could use this battery with my hand held GPS, but the GPS requires AA batteries- it may be time to upgrade that!) The rubbery texture of the devise makes it easy to grasp. Besides outdoor uses, the battery is perfect for when you want to work in the coffee house and cannot sit near an outlet. All you have to do is plug in your device's USB cord and it begins to charge. (The battery comes with a variety of adapters for various devices.) The iGeek is strong enough that my New iPad actually charges while I am using it! Older idevice chargers cannot even do that.The only thing I would wish could be improved with the iGeek is that it won't completely charge my iPad3. I know little about electronics, but I assume more power would require a bigger battery. I like the small design and would hate for it to be larger. The specs say it will charge 60% on an iPad3. I am always using the device when I plug in the battery, so I have never turned off the iPad to see how much of a charge it actually gets. That being said, the battery sufficiently charges my iPad till long after I finish using it.I would highly recommend the iGeek (IMP99D) for anyone's external battery needs

I. LOVE. THIS. CHARGER! It's powered by a cable that I thought I might lose but so far it all fits quite neatly in the little felt bag. I do not use my chargers frequently, but when I need them, I want them to be useful. I hated the my ZAGG Sparq would be down to half charge after a week or so of no use at all. This has NOT happened with my IMP99D! Maybe it's because you turn it on and off so it holds a charge in the off better. I don't know. I just know it's always been ready when I needed it with no battery drain when not in use. It has charged my iPad 2 and iPhone 4S at the same time with no issues. It comes with all sorts of USB adapters to charge other devices. The plastic feels very substantial - not cheap at all - and I really like the look. It has come in handy on long flights with no charging for my iPad as well as at conferences when I've been too far from an outlet to charge up. I was hesitant to buy it because I already owned the Sparq but I haven't regretted the purchase at all. I wish I'd gotten this one in the first place!

There are now many options available to recharge your cell phone.  I struggles between something small and portable for a quick boost and something larger that can be used several times.  The IMP880 is the latter.  It fits nicely in a laptop bag but you would not carry it down the street in a pocket without a good belt.  The IMP880 was the right choice. Sitting in the airport for 5 hours with a thousand other waiting for the one wall outlet is no fun.  I can easily charge my phone after a long day on the road and not worry about using power to tether or surf. Go ahead, help out others and don't worry about running out of power. I estimate 4 to 5 full charges for the phone. Possibly more since I am often using the phone while connected to the charger.Another factor to consider when purchasing an external battery is the charger required for the device. After checking with customer service (before purchasing) I earned the IMP880 requires a separate charger because it would take too long to charge over USB. If you want to limit the number of chargers, New Trent has a similar lower-powder model that will charge from USB.  For most trips, you can leave the charger at home and rely on large battery capacity to get you through.I highly recommend the IMP880 to all that want the flexibility of a high powered external battery for your phone or any other portable device.

After going to Disney and using all the Disney apps, I found my phone was dying before we even reached lunch.  Never again.I did some research and found that this had very high praise.... It came with its own cords, even including an adapter for the Galaxy if you have one. I love the fact that before I go on an outing, the LED indicator lights show the charge level, so I know if I have to charge it before. The battery has an amazing life, and can still charge a tablets battery faster the tablet drains it.

reviewText: Pro's: Great price for the amount of charging capacity it has onboard. I like the smooth exterior surface (I dare say it's kinda sexy, what kind of coating is that anyway? I charged my iPhone 4 from near dead 4 times before I plugged it in! I like how the lights oscillate when it is charging, good indication that it is still charging (cleaver!). It chargers fast! I like how it turns off automatically after the iPhone is done charging. I found that after I charged the iPhone4 with the pack that it was a strong, lasting charge, just as if it were charged from the wall! All of the connectors and cable accessories means I can charge all of my families devices like the iPhone, Nintendo DS, etc. when we are traveling.Con's: Sorry, I can't think of any cons at this point, it is everything I would want in an external battery pack! I guess my only wish would be: If it could be a little smaller it would fit in my pocket better but for the power it offers it it understandable that it is this size! New technology will make it smaller still I am sure!

reviewText: This is now my 2nd battery from these guys.  I also have the New Trent iCruiser IMP1000 11000mAh External Battery Pack which is also incredible.When I first bought the IGeek model, it only worked a week before it wouldn't charge. These guys are efficient, friendly and fix any problems you have immediately.I will be buying another battery from them soon for a friend of mine and I recommend them highly.Oh, and by the way, I have had several other types of "external battery chargers" that were much more expensive but didn't have nearly the charging capability.  These are definitely the best I have found on the market.

I ordered this external battery pack/charger to charge multiple items, and it works with every one of them.  I have a Verizon MiFi 2200 wireless antenna, which does NOT have the greatest battery life.  This was the #1 item I wanted the Trent IMP880 for, and it works like a charm!  The IMP 880 comes with many different adaptor "plugs" to fit various items.  The IMP880 charges my iPad (and it also included a dedicated iPad charging cable), my Nokia cellphone, my iPod Nano 4th, and the Verizon MiFi.  I used the IMP880 recently on a trip to recharge my iPad when it was at only 10% power, and then had plenty of power to recharge my iPod, my cell phone and my Verizon MiFi which were all at about 1/4 battery life (estimating on the MiFi, 'cause you can't tell!).  Since the iPad is a big energy drain, this was pretty impressive to me.  The iPad battery itself is pretty darn phenomenal, but when it is very low or drained it can take several hours to fully recharge on household current.  Anyway, the IMP880 includes many adaptor plugs that are likely to fit just about anything you own. reviewText: Let's face it, the battery life on the iPhone is awful.  While I don't see myself as any sort of power user, I'm lucky if I end the day with 5% left on the phone.  I chose New Trent (formerly iMaxPower) because I rarely see products from any company on Amazon that are consistently rated 4 1/4 ro 5 stars across the board.  Every review praised the quality of the product, and even better - the technical support.I needed a case with battery for my new iPhone, as well as a standalone booster charger because our family is going on a 6-hour plane trip and I need the iPhone to last the entire trip.  My kids are also bringing their DSi, so we needed the booster to charge that as well.So this review covers all of the New Trent products I purchased: the IMP130, IMP550, and IMP880.IMP130The IMP130 is an iPhone case that contains an integrated 1700mAh battery.  That battery is higher capacity (according to wiki) than the one in the iPhone 3GS (which is supposedly around 1219mAh).  Capacity isn't everything; battery quality varies greatly.  After using the IMP130 for a week or so, I estimate the it to effectively double my time between charges.The IMP130 case completely covers the iPhone (other comparable cases leave the top exposed).  To put the iPhone in the case, you detach the top of the IMP130 case and slide the iPhone into the bottom part, where it docks to the standard Apple connector built into the case.  You then have the option to re-attach the top piece, providing protection to the top of your iPhone, or leaving it off.  The only reason to choose to leave the top part off is that when the IMP130 is fully assembled, access to the iPhone buttons is difficult at best.  You need to use your fingernail to mute the phone and access the volume controls.  I hope New Trent addresses this in a future version.  The standby button and headphone jack are much more easily accessible.  NOTE: If you do decide to leave the top off the case, there is not much friction holding the iPhone in the bottom part of the case.  It feels secure, but I would not trust it - I don't think the designers expected you to use it that way, but the case design is very clean even without the top piece (as if it was designed with that in mind).  I find no degradation in 3G signal due to the case, nor are the speakers degraded.Now the best part - for those of you who (like me) have a full-body Invisible Shield on your iPhone, the phone WILL stil completely fit in the the IMP130!  I have not heard of that with any other case.The IMP130 is about 3/4 the weight of the iPhone, so it almost doubles the overall weight. It also adds a bit of bulk around all sides - but provides a good feel in your hands.  The texture of the case provides a good amount of grip, but I still prefer the grip the Invisible Shield provides.  To me, the IMP130 case could use a little more anti-slip texture.The IMP130 is charged through a standard Micro USB cable (included).  Say good-bye to the proprietary iPhone cable.  This is a very good thing.  The case has an on/off switch in the bottom.  When the switch is Off, you are running on your iPhone battery.  When the switch is On, you are still using the iPhone battery, but it is being charged at the same time by the IMP130 battery.  When the IMP130 finally gives out, the "charging" indicator on your iPhone turns off and you are solely using the iPhone battery.  Whether the switch is on or off, you can still sync through the Micro USB cable.  Any off-the-shelf Micro USB cable will work with this product.  Here's the typical scenario: you come home with your iPhone at 90% charge and your IMP130 at 0%.  You connect the cable to your PC to do your sync.  The IMP130 begins to charge and the iPhone starts to charge once the IMP130 has enough juice.  After a couple of hours, both are at 100%.  The IMP130 has 3 LED indicators that show the current charge (100%/66%/33%/0%).Finally - and this is a GREAT one - the IMP130 has a built-in super-bright white LED that can be used as a flashlight (say good-bye to those stupid "flashlight apps").  It also solves the problem of those impossible low-light pictures.  The LED has a switch to turn it on or off.In all, the IMP130 is really a great product.  The only negative is the hard-to-access volume and mute controls.  And remember, if you have an Invisible Shield full body wrap, it WILL fit in the case nicely.IMP550While the IMP130 is great, there's no way it will take the iPhone on a 6-hour flight of pure video and 3D games.  So that's why I also got the IMP550.  This is a brand new product from New Trent.  It's the big brother of the IMP130 (much bigger in fact).  It has a very large 5500mAh capacity.  That pretty much quadruples the iPhone battery.Unlike the IMP130, this case does not fully enclose the iPhone; it leaves the top exposed - granting easy access to all of the iPhone buttons.  The case is lined with a velvety material which not only feels neat, it helps keep the iPhone in place.  An iPhone with a full-body wrap Invisible Shield DOES fit in the case.Also unlike the IMP130, the sync interface is not Micro USB, but rather standard Apple.  That means there is no cable included with the IMP550; you can use your original cable that came with your iPhone.Because this is a serious battery, the case adds serious weight to your iPhone, as well as bulk - mostly overall thickness.  However, unless you have very small hands, I think you will find that the case feels much more comfortable in your hands than the iPhone itself.  I find it to be quite ergonomic.  I also find the grip of the IMP550 to be slightly superior to that of the IMP130.The IMP550 does not have an on/off switch; it provides a charge to the iPhone when it needs to.  Like the IMP130, you will charge both the case and the iPhone while you are connected to your PC, wall charger, or car charger.Personally, I don't think the IMP550 is suited to be a full-time case solution for your iPhone.  It is simply too bulky and heavy for that (as is any other 5000+ mAh battery case).  It's great for long trips, golf courses, or any other time you will not have access to a charger for many many hours.Sadly, the IMP550 has no flashlight LED (maybe on their next revision?).  Three LEDs indicate charge, and a fourth tells you if the IMP550 is charging your iPhone.In summary - another 5-star product.IMP880When I am on that long trip, my iPhone is covered by the IMP550.  But what about my kid's DSi and my wife's smartphone (not everyone has an iPhone)...  New Trent has that covered, too.  The IMP880 is a standalone battery that charges a multitude of devices.  It has a staggering 8800mAh of capacity - almost two IMP550 worth, or roughly 6-7 times the capacity of an iPhone.  That's some serious capacity.  The unit is quite small - about the size of a man's wallet.  It weighs about the same as a man's wallet (before a Vegas trip).Four LEDs indicate battery charge and a Test button lets you know the current capacity.  NewTrent made a Youtube video demonstrating this unit.  In that video, they say you need to turn the unit on by holding down the Test button for 5 seconds before you charge something.  I find that the unit always charges a device if needed; maybe I have a newer revision.The battery may be small, but the wall adapter used to charge the IMP880 is not.  The Youtube video shows a nice, small wall-wart.  My unit came with a very bulky in-line AC adapter.  It is larger than the IMP550 itself.  Not a big deal, but much larger than I expected.  Remember, the AC adapter is something you pack in your suitcase; you carry the small IMP880 on the plane fully charged.The IMP880 can charge a variety of items, and has several ports:DC-IN jack connects to the AC adapter.  This is how you charge the IMP880 from the wall.DC-OUT jack is only used for charging specific notebook PCs.  My unit included a cable for this, but I am not certain NewTrent will support notebook charging going forward.  I do not see notebook devices listed as charge targets any longer on their website.Type-A USB connector is used to charge your iPhone, Blackberry or DSi.At this point, I need to speak about the USB cable that is included with the IMP880.  The IMP880 replaces a smaller charger called the IMP500.  This was the workhorse of the imaxPower line of products.  In fact, the IMP550 is basically the IMP500 designed into an iPhone case.  The reason I bring up the IMP500 is that - like the IMP880 - it charges devices through a USB cable.  This cable has a standard USB-A connector on one end, and a generic adapter on the other.  You can configure the cable for different devices by connecting a different plug on the adapter end.  That way, you can use the USB cable to charge an iPhone, or Blackberry, or DSi, etc.  The USB cable that was included with the IMP500 had a FEMALE adapter on the end.  All of the flavors of connectors had a male adapter.  The USB cable that is included with the IMP880 has a MALE adapter on the end.  All of the flavors of connectors have a female adapter.So what does this mean?  For me, it meant a slight problem when I tried to use the IMP880 to charge my kid's DSi.  You see, neither the IMP880 nor IMP500 come with a DSi adapter.  Not a problem - the website clearly points that out.  So when I purchased the IMP880, I also bought the only DSi adapter they sold (it was about $5).  Unfortunately, that adapter is male, and only fits the IMP500 cable.  It will not fit the USB cable that came with the IMP880.My solution was to then buy an IMP500 USB cable.  NewTrent sells them, and so does EBay.  But that means I now have one cable that only fits the DSi adapter, and another cable that fits all my other devices.  Plus, I had to spend money on the extra cable.  NewTrent says they are working on the problem, and will standardize on the cable.Again, this was only a problem for me because I wanted to charge a DSi.  All my other charging needs are met with the cable that comes with the IMP880.By the time you read this, the issue may have been resolved, but contact the company if you intend to use the IMP880 to charge a DSi (or consider getting the IMP500 instead).When the IMP880 is charging a device, the IMP880 remains cool.  I believe the main reason for this is that NewTrent has a current limiter in the IMP880 that keeps charging current lower than what you get from a wall or PC.  Devices will charge slightly slower, but the IMP880 will not get hot.On those very long trips, the IMP880 can charge either the IMP550 or IMP130 directly.  NOTE: I am told by the company that this is not a wise thing to do on a daily basis, but a few times on a long trip is fine.Because of the adapter compatibility issue, I'd have to give the IMP880 4 stars.  I'd ding it more for the trouble I went through, except it just works so darned good.  I had the time to get the adapter issue straightened out; had I discovered this the day before my trip, I'd not be so happy.A word about NewTrent customer service: EXCELLENT.  I had a couple of questions that I sent via E-mail.  I asked if someone could call me back, and I got a phone call within 10 minutes - from the owner of the comapny.  Show me one other company where this happens.Conclusion:Three great products from a great company.  The customer support quality is amazing.  What is also amazing is how poorly written the instruction booklets are.  If you want to see the devices in action, there are videos on the website that explain it all, but hopefully this review did that as well.
summary: Great product, but read this review before using with DSi

reviewText: I was thrilled upon opening this item.  I LOVE the feel of it, I LOVE that it comes with a case to protect it and I LOVE that it works exactly as stated!  I was actually able to charge 2 iPad's (iPad 2 and iPad 4), our phones (iPhone 4S, 5 and my son's 3) 3 times and a Kindle (current gen) with this, before I had to recharge it...they were not all the way dead, and I didn't charge them to 100%, but it worked like a charm!  It is amazing to have in the car, when I go someplace (the dr's office and karate are good examples!) and my phone is dead, which happens a lot since my kids watch Netflix on it all the time!  This item I have told TONS of people about, and cannot contain my joy in having it!  The only issue I saw, which isn't really an issue, is the fact that it doesn't come with a charger for an iPhone, pad and such...BUT, they actually took the time to write in the paperwork that it was because of licensing issues!  WOW, just wow, I'm so excited to read that, and not have to wonder what was going on.  That alone would have sold me on the product; they treated me like a person, not just skipped over that detail.  I'm very impressed!  It took me several days to run it dead, which I wanted to do so I could charge it from completely dead back up.  It took about 5 hours to charge it all the way back up, which is not a problem, but I wanted to know the time frame.  I was very impressed that when I charged my iPad (2) on your product, and my husband's (4) on the wall brick (the one the iPad came with!) and they charged at the same rate.  I expected a slower charge from an external battery product, but was very impressed that it charged at the same rate. I love how clear the lights are to see what the remainder of the charge is. The only other downfall I saw was that you have to read directions to use it at first...I assumed you just pushed the button to start it, but you have to hold it for 5 seconds.  This is actually great so you don't accidentally turn it on, but I just tried to use it before reading, and couldn't get a charge...of course it was because I didn't ACTUALLY turn it on.  Once I turned it on (holding for 5 seconds) it worked like a charm :)

reviewText: I just purchased this model mainly for my new iPad. I'm going to be flying across the country for Christmas and I wanted a battery pack that was portable and that would last. This battery does not disappoint.Considering how solid it feels, it is surprisingly lightweight. It is about 2" wide, with a non-slip coating. 4 bright blue LEDs indicate charging and when the unit is fully charged. I generally plug my batteries in at night to fully charge for the next day. This battery has no problem keeping my iPad charged fully all day long.You can be fooled into thinking this unit doesn't work, however. When I first plugged in my iPad and turned on the charger, it didn't register with the iPad--- no charge. I checked the connection, and even plugged in my iPhone. Still no sign of charging either device. Initially I thought the unit wasn't designed to work with my new iPad or iPhone 5, even though it said it would. Then, while my iPad was still plugged in, I held the power button down for a few seconds, and bam, it began to charge. Same scenario with my iPhone. So, once I figured that out, everything was fine and it charged my iPad with no problem. So, remember to hold the button down for approx. 3 seconds to (1) turn the unit on to charge AFTER the device is plugged in and (2) to turn the unit off.I used it for a period of time today and it still has 3/4 of charge left after being used for over an hour on my iPad while I was watching Netflix. I would rate this unit (5)

5 Stars for another great lifesaving New Trent product. This little powerhouse is one of the best devices I own. It recharges my Ipad and Iphone at the same time effortlessly and it gets me through power outages. It also serves as a backup when I use my devices too long. It recharges quickly and I make sure it's always ready to go. I like that I can keep it in my pocket and simply run a usb cable to my device when I'm out and about. I buy them and give them to my family members as presents and they love them too!

This battery is a lifesaver when you're on the go and thus not able to consistently charge your devices at a power outlet for long stretches. It has a very solid feel to it, and the outside rubbery-smooth coating is a nice touch (compared to plain plastic).I used this IMP880 battery recently with a small 4-port usb hub simultaneously connected to both a Motorola Razr, and my Galaxy S Android phone; they both charged a number of times and still had 2 out of 4 battery indicator lights remaining.The only major downside for this battery pack, imo, is that you can't charge it at the same time you're charging connected devices, but that's not a huge issue most of the time.
summary: Great to have the juice when away from civilization

reviewText: I would rate it a 5 but they just came out with a IMP1000 with a little more power - I will purchase that one when this one dies. This thing has REALLY helped out with my phone that dies every 4 or less!

Overall this is a great product for those who want to charge multiple devices and also need a lot of charge.i have an Ipad, Iphone and Galaxy S4 and this device works well on all of them.Not only is it a great product but it is durable then other chargers in the market and its compact design is better than the once I have seen.I recommend this Charger to anyone who loos for performance and convenience.

The device is packed with power.Pros: has both 2amp and 1amp USB ports so I can charge my phone and tablet at the same time, multiple times. The case is rubberized which is a great feature as it keeps it from slipping out of your hand and keeps it from getting all scratched up.Cons: I wish the device was able to be powered w/ a regular USB type cable instead of the supplied power supply and cable, however I think the supplied power cord supplies more power than a regular USB power adapter.Overall this is a very small device for the amount of power packed inside and it seems to charge my devices faster than if I plugged them into the chargers that came with them.
summary: Packs a ton of battery juice into a little form factor

reviewText: I originally bought this product about six months ago - before I had an iPad 2. It worked fine in charging my iPhone.  I then got an iPad 2 and found that it was unable to charge it, and displayed a "Not Charging" message.  I thought it might be my cables, but then wrote to New Trent and got an immediate response from Sammy explaining that the older versions did NOT charge the iPad UNLESS there was a special adapter and cable.  Sammy promptly sent it to me and it works great.  I also found out the the newer models of this battery do not require a special cable or adapter - it works fine with the cables supplied by Apple.  So hats off to New Trent and for getting a loyal customer.  In addition, just so I would never run out of juice, I got the New Trent iDual Port which works directly with the iPad 2 and charges it and my iPhone at the same time.Jim

I bought this product because I need something to charge my iPhone and View Sonic tablet on my trip to Europe.This is my second external battery pack I owned. The other is a 1,000mAh Duracell. Obviously, it will not work for a 12 hr flight and 2 devices. I needed something with more juice.I choose this model over other New Trent products because of the price and price/mAh. They have one that outputs 11,000mAh, but was outside my price point.The other model I considered was the  IMP70D 7,000mAh. I choose to go with the IMP880 because it had more juice. The main thing the IMP70D has over the IMP880 is dual usb output.Now with the review of the IMP880.Pros: 1) sleek looking.2) built well.3) auto shut-off - you can leave your device connected to it and it automatically shuts off when your device is fully charged.4) smart turn-on - meaning you must have a device connected to it in order to turn it on. You cannot accidentally turn it on.Cons: 1) I am only getting 6700mAh of charge. Not 8900mAh.  I figured this output based on charging my iPhone 4 using the % remaining battery indicator. The iPhone 4 has a 1420 mAh battery, according to cnet. [...] I was able to recharge my iPhone 4.7x and 5x. That would equate to 6,600mAh and 7,100mAh. I ran this test twice, and got about the same results.A few things that could make device better:1) increase surface area, and make device thinner. The device is not huge, but it is too bulky to carry in a pants pocket. It's about 2x as thick as my wallet, about the same surface area.2) a digital output of % remaining or mAh remaining vs the blue line that symbolizes 100%/75%/50%/25%3) charger for device could be smaller. The charger is about 1/2 the size of the battery. It would be nice if you could charge it with a USB like an iPhone or EVO.Overall, nice device...3 stars because of the 6,600mAh and 7,100mAh output when it says 8900mAh.<<<<<<EDIT>>>>>>I was originally a bit upset with the product because I thought I was being "shorted"  1900mAh or so; however, after reading the Technical Details for the IMP99D, I feel like I prematurely judged the product.  The IMP99D is 9900mAh vs the 8900mAh one I bought.  The technical details say: "Ultra reliable Lithium-Ion battery with 9900mAh, 500% iPhone 4 Battery life" - well, on my 8900mAh one I got 4.7-5x charges on my iPhone4. I also talked New Trent's customers service and they said storage does not equate to output. My point is: well, my charger works just fine.5 stars... upgrading to 5 stars from 3 stars because device works as advertised.
summary: nice,  after better understanding the product <review edited>

reviewText: This external battery does exactly what it's supposed to.  It's small, but packs a mighty charge.  It comes with a sweet little carrying pouch for cables, and even includes USB and android cables.  It doesn't include an Apple charging cable, but that's not a big deal.The battery itself holds a lot of juice.  I can charge both my iPad and iPhone 4 a couple of times with leftovers.  That makes this battery ideal for travel.Count me very pleased.

I was initially surprised at how small this item is...it isn't much bigger than two iPhones put together. I've used it with iPads, iPhones, the HTC Inspire, Samsung Galaxy SII and SIII. Note the 5V/2A port does not work with the ASUS Transformer tablets. The shelf-life of the battery is a a great feature, so you don't have to worry about regularly charing it if you don't use it. The device delivers exactly as promised...very straightforward.

I've used a number of NewTrent products before, and haven't been disappointed once. This product extends that trend! The iGeek IMP99D powers everything I have fully and quickly. My wife and I were heading on a road trip from the Baltimore MD area to Cape Breton Nova Scotia and back, and I wanted to have some spare battery power for our devices, so I bought this. Our devices: both have Samsung Galaxy S3 phones, and she has an original Amazon Kindle Fire tablet.Although this battery pack DOES use a separate external AC charger to fill the battery, this was not an issue for me.Once fully charged, this battery pack provided at least two full charges for the Galaxy S3 AND a full charge for the Kindle Fire. I topped the battery up overnight on the wall mains, and the next morning off we went for another day's adventure, and no worries about running out of juice on the trail somewhere. Beautiful!Comes with a nice carrying case, too. This device made traveling with our various electronica much easier and hassle-free. Recommended highly!

This IMP99D is the best little charger that I have seen.  Right out of the box I was impressed with the look and feel.  It has a soft smooth almost velvet-like feel making it very comfortable to hang onto, it wont slip out of your hand when plugging devices into it.  It was fully charged in about 4 hours and it holds an amazing amount of charge.  It charged the dead battery on my HTC Evo LTE and my Kindle Fire BOTH at the same time in under 2-1/2 hours and it had only used about half of its charge.The IMP99D comes with several different adapters making it work for just about any device you have that needs charging.  It is simple to operate with just 1 on/off button (that you press and hold for 5 seconds to turn it on or off) and 3 charging ports; one port for charging the IMP99D and 2 output USB ports for charging your devices.  There are 4 neon blue LED lights that indicate how much charge there is remaining.  I really like the fact that the 2 USP ports and the charging port are all on the same side so that I can leave it in the protective cover while charging the IMP99D or charging my devices.After plugging a device into the IMP99D you have to press and hold the on/off switch for 5 seconds to initiate the charge.It is a little cumbersome having to carry the wall output plug with you instead of a standard USB plug but I can understand it with the juice that this little charger takes to charge up and the impressive charge capacity that it holds.The only negative experience that I have had with this super little charger is the first time I put it into the protective pouch and pulled the strings to close it, one of the little balls on the end of the string pulled off and I had to rethread the string and tie a bigger knot on the end.

I bought the New Trent IMP880 a year ago (now called the iGeek IMP99D), and it has been handy on trips. The battery itself is solidly built, and has an auto shut off so you don't drain it unless a device is actively being charged.The weak link is the cables supplied with the batteries. The usb and micro usb cable tips are not very sturdy, and mine fell apart at the mold seams with less than ten uses. Not a big deal because most people have a few spare micro usb cables, which work fine.Unfortunately, the dock cable designed to charge iPads, iPhones, and iPods quit working. I tried every Apple cable I could find, and even ordered a higher end cable than Apple ships themselves. Not one worked with the New Trent battery. After some Googling, it seems that ONLY the cable supplied with the battery will charge an Apple device.I emailed the manufacturer, but haven't heard anything back, so for the forseeable future, I have a rather expensive paperweight.I think the newer models allow the use of ANY Apple dock cable, so I would look at one of those if you are using an Apple device with this product.Update: New Trent was quick to respond to my inquiry, and sent out replacement cables.
summary: Battery works fine, but iPad / iPhone cable is proprietary

reviewText: I've read a lot of reviews regarding the product before buying. I'm pleasantly surprised that this product has a great battery life and charge pretty fast. When I first received the product, I'm upset that no iPad cable was included since a lot of the reviews mention that the product requires a proprietary iPad cable. I contacted the manufacturer and they told me that the new shipments has been improved. The IMP880 now doesn't require a proprietary cable for the iPad which is a great improvement. I don't have to worry about losing the proprietary cable anymore.This product is capable of charging multiple devices, including iPhone 4 and iPad at the same time. I was recently on a 14 hours flight and was able to use my devices to play game, watch movie and work on my iPad and there was still some battery left.
summary: Great multiple charger with long battery life

reviewText: Received product quickly and just as expected.  I have had it for about a month... charged it once initially... have used it to charge my Moto Droid a few times when I needed it.  And I still have more than 1/2 the charge left on the Trent.  This product is AWESOME!  Very convenient.  It's not too bulky to carry around with the phone.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Recently I purchased the NT99D portable battery charger. I liked the fact that I received it already fully charged and ready to use. It's compact enough to fit into my purseIt does need some sort of cord storage or prongs on the device that clasp the phone cord to wrap around the device  If that is not possible, then maybe it could come with a small bag that one could put their cord/battery charger into.All-in-all, the product does exactly what it is supposed to do and I have not had any problems with it's charging function. The product's weight and feel seem to be of excellent quality.....definitely not some flimsy device.
This charger is amazing, but if you want a charger that holds even more, go for the iCarrier. It'll charge you phone at least once more and not any bigger.

I recently ordered this product here off Amazon and I must say I am quite impressed. I'm on the go a lot, and I am constantly on my iPhone. The iGeek is the best way I have found to keep my phone charged and ready to use. As long as I have my iGeek with me, I never have to worry about my phone running out of power.Aside from this battery pack having a huge capacity (which I love!), I also love how it has two usb ports. Now, when I'm on the go with my friends and family I can easily keep all of our devices charged and ready to use. It's also great how small the iGeek is, it's smaller than my phone, so I always have room for it.It is also really handy how the iGeek comes with a nice carrying pouch and adapters to use with other devices.This is the first New Trent product I've ever bought, but it definitely won't be my last, I look forward to getting more great accessories from them!
Keeps my iPad powered on my long trips to Asia.  It does not really have the umph to charge my ipad3 but it keeps it powerd.  All in all I love it

When I received this device, I allowed it to charge overnight before trying to charge my iPhone 4 or my iPad 2. I plugged one then the other into the "correct" USB slot and neither the phone or the iPad would charge. I was so disappointed.  I reread the instructions and found the problem.  First plug in the devide to the correct USB slot while the battery is off.  Next, press the On/Off button for about 4-5 seconds until the LED begins to BLINK.  Now it is working great for both my iPhone and my iPad.

Size / Appearance: 5/5The iGeek IMP99D offers a slim low-profile appearance with dual USB ports and a convenient LED charge indicator. The product is very lightweight and will fit easily into a pocket on the go. I take it with me to work or just on the run with friends and it's almost like it's not even there.Charging: 5/5The iGeek packs a 9990mAh battery that will power devices through the day and more. This is great for those long busy days at work that your phone just won't make it. Another great part about this portable charger is the variety of devices it will charge other than Apple products, which I use it mostly for. This is great for anyone using Droid, Blackberry and many other devices.Overall: 5/5I recommend this product to anyone in the market for an external battery that will get their iPads and iPhones plenty of juice through the day. This is also a great addition for non-Apple users looking to stay powered much longer.
summary: One of the top iPad chargers

reviewText: Small and powerful.  This is a great charger as it packs a lot of recharge power for all my devices and easily fits in any small bag.  Powering off is a bit tricky but it keeps from accidentally turning off the battery while charging your device.  Great little charger for quite a deal.

I got this for my hubby because he was always needing to charge his phone on trips but didn't always have access to a plug.  He uses it all the time when waiting for a plane or when he forgets his adapter

The iGeek IMP99D is one powerful charger that's roughly the size of a full wallet.  The design is sleek and everything is clearly marked.  The charger is quiet and has ample exhaust to keep it from getting hot.  A computer friend once told me to buy the largest capacity of anything that I could afford and with chargers it's no different.  The 9900mAh capacity seems to be the middle of the road right now and is great for recharging the iPhone 4S several times over and/or my new New iPad once.  The manual claims to take up to 7  hours to charge but I've been hitting full charge around 5 hours.  The charger's blue light system is clear and bright, but I would rather see a digital display telling me what percentage of battery I have left.  The box comes with a few adapters but because they are not licensed for Apple products, you will need to use your own cables if you own any Apple products.  There are two outputs for charging.  One is meant for phones while the other is meant for larger tablet products.  It would be nice if both outputs could be used for tablets but for what I have, it's not necessary.  Make sure to read the instructions when charging as it took me a few moments to realize that I had to hold the on/off button for 4 seconds to actually turn on the device to charge.  (This is nice so that you don't accidentally turn it on or off.)  There is also a drawstring carrying pouch that holds the charger and the accessories.  I didn't know it came with it and didn't realize it was folded up neatly in the packaging.  It was a nice little surprise.  My only complaint is the only way you can charge the product is through a wall with an AC Charger.  It would be nice if you could draw power from a laptop to charge the IMP99D if you have limited sockets which I'm finding at many hotels recently. Other than it not having a USB charging capability, I would recommend the IMP99D without hesitation.
summary: Little size with lots of power!

reviewText: I run through my phones battery at least twice a day.remaining in touch with people is crucial to my job and I NEED a reliable back up power source. Enter New Trent... This device has saved me, time and time again. Thie unit easily fits in my jeans or suit pants equally well, and provides enough power to get me through the day. I recommend this unit highly. You won't be disappointed: I promise.

I recently purchased the iGeek, IMP99D from New Trent. Previously I carried a Mophie that took forever to charge, was slow to charge my iPad and finally "bought the farm." When I contacted Mophie to ask about the product the rep told me that iPad battery was big, it would take a long time to charge and that I should use the product to only "top off" my iPad instead of completely charging the unit.When I received the iGeek, my first charge went flawlessly. I am currently in the first duty cycle and I am finding the iGeek to be much faster charging both my iPad and my 4S. The other brand only provided partial charge on the phone and even less on the iPad. The iGeek has a large enough capacity to charge both my devices without the time lag and partial charges.I am so amazed by this product that I convinced my daughter and son-in-law to purchase one also. Their iGeek arrived today and I expect to hear from them how much they enjoy having the extra battery life.Thanks New Trent for such an amazing product.
summary: Great to have additional battery for my iProducts

reviewText: So I bought this guy to be my travel charger for my android phone and my iPad for when I am doing some serious flying, further than any of my older batteries will last, this guy jumps out of my bag, plugs into and I  an watch whatever while he charges away, worked really well on a trip with a 8 hour flight I think, not sure how long but more than 1 phone battery & half iPad battery given the fact both units have so e age, nice rig, would certainly recommend.

Bought it for my son's recent extended trip abroad and he couldn't be more pleased with this device. I my self have New Trent CarbonPak (see my review for it) but took iGeek on 4 day motorcycle trip across NY/NJ and needed back up power for my iPhone 5, my BlackBerry Playbook and my bluetooth headphones. The device is very solid, surface made of scratch free material, simple to use and small size make it a perfect back up battery to take on any trip.The only issue I had, is my BlackBerry playbook would not charge. But before the trip, I contacted customer service and they sent me different cable which is not included with original package. Charging cable came within few days and I was able to charge my BlackBerry tablet.I highly recommend this product. It is well priced, very convenient, and it works as advertised.

Awesome charger.  USe this all the time.  Have it for over a year.  Only negative is that that the model I have has a proprietary charger.  I believe all the newer ones use a micro usb.  I have several newtent products and they are great.  Got friends and family to get these too, especially after the area had a power outage for a few days.

My office does not allow charging devices on the PC USB port or in the power grid, so I am forced to carry a stand alone battery charger to work. This unit actually replaced two smaller Energizer chargers, which were inefficient and it still keeps going. It charges my Droid Razr super fast and still has plenty of juice to charge my Kindle Fire. It adds a little weight to my bag, but that is to be expected with this much charge. Put it on the charger at night and you will have more than enough power all day. I only wish I could charge this unit with my USB port at home instead of the DC block. A very minor issue. I highly recommend!
summary: Superb product! Will give you lots of power when you need it

reviewText: Just last Wednesday, my IMP99D sat by my side in class with an iPhone and a Blackberry plugged into it for a quick charge. The guys in my study group were amazed that such a small device had enough juice to power their devices and give them enough energy to get through the rest of the day. Then I told them it still had power left to charge my phone a few more times before it required a recharge. This is an excelent accessory to have for anyone who keeps several tech devices and can't always get to a wall charger. I highly recommend this!

By far one of my best purchases in a long time.  I take it on travel in place of other chargers so I can charge from it at night and then leave it to charge up again by day.  This thing charges anything I can hook to it.  It seems to last forever on a charge.

Use this to charge my iPhone 5 and 3rd gen iPad, works incredibly well, just as advertised and looks really cool as well. Can charge virtually any piece of electronics with usb connection, saw all the great reviews here on amazon and wanted to try it, glad i did! Excellent all around
summary: Beyond happy with this product, lots and lots of backup power!

reviewText: The item I am reviewing is the IMP880, this is the older version of IMP99D. I may be a little late with this review with the newer version out in the market, but I just couldn't take a pass on it without letting the world know how satisfied I am with my purchase.  Basically, both products' build and functionality are about the same with the only difference that the IMP99D has that added juice into it. My IMP880 has the capacity of 8900mAh vs to the current version of IMP99D's 9900mAh, that's all. I imagine that the newer version can provide your devices with longer hours of charging and extra lasting power.The IMP880 (also known as iTruck, previously known as iMaxpower) at the time was the best in the market that I could afford for the power it could provide. Now, the company New Trent offers the iCruiser IMP1000 and the Air Grip IMP1100 with 11000 mAh on each. I own an iPad, kindle touch, and a blackberry. My IMP880 has enough juice to power up these devices (and then some!), without recharging this external battery. In fact I only recharge it every couple of weeks, and I do not even totally drained it yet by that time! It is portable and very convenient when I am on the go and when I travel for long periods. This has saved my life, power-wise, countless of times. For some reason, my Blackberry, particularly, has become so power hungry nowadays that I have to keep feeding it up with juice in every few hours. And of course, each and every time, my knight and shining armor, er, IMP880 comes to the rescue!These external batteries, my IMP880 including, that New Trent offers are a must in today's growing USB powered devices when you are on the go, especially when stranded in, say, the airport and could not find any available power station. Well, you can create your own scenario. Anyway, I would definitely recommend getting an external charger from New Trent. I am going to buy some more and give them as gifts this coming Holidays.

I had purchased this product for my trip to New York Comic Con. I had fully charged it once and knew that I would be needing to use it for my 3DS, iPhone, and many of my partners' phones as well. There were no outlets near our location and this device was a lifesaver! Lasted nearly all weekend too.

Any time my mobile/mobiles need charging and I can't find a plug or I forget the charger that came with my mobile this battery saves meAnd all the people I work with keep borrowing it from me (I'm the hero now)

This is by far one of my favorite battery backups. The small size and incredible battery life makes this the perfect travel buddy.Pros:Quick rechargeAmazing battery backup, full charges an IPad 3rd generationSmall, compact sizeTwo USB charging portsComes with a great drawstring bagCons:Has to have a special adapter to chargeTouchy top button seems to require several seconds to turn on (Which is to avoid accidentally leaving the unit on. Not saying this is a bad thing, just a personal quirk with me)Included USB cable isn't as nice as some lower priced external battery packsUpdate 1/10/13: This battery pack is still going strong. I haven't had any issues or concerns to report. One thing I have noticed is that when I have two devices plugged in, the charger will NOT automatically turn off when the battery reaches 100% like it does when only one device is plugged. Not anything bad, but just something to be aware of.Recommendations:The included USB cable could be more like the retractable cable that is included with other productsNot sure if this could be changed, but the only way to charge this product is through an external adapter

The IMP99D works very well, charging both my tablet and cell phone. I have gotten multiple charges from the Trent charger. I particularly like the little bag that can carry both the IMP99D and two small charging cords.New Trent iGeek - 11200mAh External Battery Charger for Smartphones and Tablets (IMP99D/NT99D)

My wife gave me a IMP99D iGeek battery pack for a Christmas gift in 2011. I took it to dialysis with me three times a week and never had a problem with it until a nurse knocked it off a table and broke it beyond repair. I decided to wait on replacing it. But after a week without it, I found how much I relied on it. I ordered a replacement seven days after my unit was destroyed by accident. During those seven days, I missed calls due to my phone running out of charge when an outlet was not available, had my iPad die with 8 minutes left in a cliffhanger movie, and lost power to my Kindle HD when I was seconds away from beating my daughters score on Angry Birds.Most of these instances are not life or death. But in our world today we rely on power to make many of our tools to work. This battery pack extends the life of our devices. You are waiting on an important call and your cell phone runs out of battery. Now you to tell you child that you have to go home from the playground. Well, with the IMP99D iGeek battery pack you don't have to be the bad guy and you can stay out until it gets dark....I know this isn't an nuts and bolts review you can get them elsewhere. I just want you to know that I like the product and think that you will too.
summary: I thought that I could do without it...

reviewText: Does what it's advertised to do, and does it well.  Just be careful, when packing it, that the on/off switch isn't stuffed up against anything solid.  It can hold it "on".  Don't ask how I found out...

The IGeek has very durable construction with a rubberized (almost military grade) exterior, and performed above my expectations in charging multiple items (smartphones and tablets).  Holds a charge seemingly indefinitely, and did better than the advertised 40+ hours of charging.  I look forward to using it on backpacking trips, where the loss of a phone charge is inevitable and annoying if a call is necessary.  The rating would have been 5 stars had the user manual been better than bare minimum (if that), but the operation was intuitive, and easily figured out with use.

This thing is great. I love the feel and the design of it. Charges my devices just fine. I like the battery meter on top and the easy on and off button. Nothing bad I can say about this. I like to use this when I go snowboarding or out on really long road trips. For snowboarding I use this to charge my Contour Roam camera while I'm taking a break and it charges it fast. I also use this for my Note 2 when there's not wall outlet in sight. I'd definitely recommend this to others.

I have had this batter pack for a long time now, and it has just been the biggest life saver ever. I would recommend it to anyone that needs a little more juice throughout their day. This battery can charge any phone that supports being charged through USB and it can even charge devices with a bigger battery like the iPad. The only complaint I have with this battery is that you need a special cord to charge the iPad (The cord is included!!!).

So far I am happy with its performance. I travel quite a bit for work and possess many devices for which the battery is coming in handy. I chose the IMP99D because of its high capacity and because it has two ports with enough resistance to actually charge 2 devices, including an Ipad.My only complaint so far is that a hard-wired, round port A/C adapter is required for recharging the iGeek. I would love to see a micro USB power connection, for use with an AC/USB wall adapter. I have a Nexus S and a Blackberry Bold 9700, a Nook, and a Bluetooth headset - all of which use micro USB connections for charging ports. Most (non-Apple) devices use a micro USB connection these days. As I already carry several micro USB cables and an A/C wall adapter to go with it, I would not need to carry an additional AC adapter.With that said, for short trips, I find that I can leave the AC adapter behind as I rarely drain the IGeek.  For longer trips, I pack the adapter in my checked bag so that I have it in my hotel throughout the trip.In addition to the above products, I use an Ipod Touch 3, an Ipad 2.  Any of these two devices will charge simultaneously.I was able to charge my Nexus S 4G four times over without draining the Igeek!I can even charge devices inside of my backpack while on the move (works great in the airport).  The battery doesn't overheat.  My Nexus gets warmer than the IGeek!I would definitely recommend this product.Next, I am interested to try the IMP1000 (11000 mAh).  I find that even though I have the ability to charge two devices at the same time, I rarely have a need to.  I would definitely trade the extra USB port for an additional 200 mAh.  Putting it in my Amazon wish list....
summary: Awesome, high capacity, dual charging, battery pack

reviewText: I purchased the NEW TRENT IMP880 about a week ago upon the recommendation of a friend of mine. I first have to describe myself as a complete electronic junkie and during vacations and business trips I am normally carrying a slew of portable adapters, which has become a little cumbersome. One of the biggest issues during travel is wondering whether I have brought all of my portable chargers along???Immediately after seeing what the IMP880 was capable of, I was destined to get my hands on one and ordered one immediately. My product arrived in just one day's time and I immediately charged it up. I found that it actually came from the factory already pre-charged so it was already good to go. I am sure that those I-Phone users out there can relate to the fact that the battery life is terrible on Apple's over-rated device. Throughout the day, I must be careful not to browse too much or make too many calls if I do not have an outlet or one of my chargers readily accessible for fear that I will not be able to make or take an important call when that time arrives due to an extremely low battery  I have put off getting a portable charging device because those that I had come across were just a little too bulky.So far I have fully charged my I-Phone three times and my IMP880 is still showing three bars/diodes, which indicates that it still has a little over half of it's charging power left. In addition to my I-Phone, I have discovered that this device can charge my Blackberry, I-POD and two of my family members other phones.It's size is not too overwhelming and it can easily fit in my front pants pocket for easy transportation. I will definitely be bringing this device along during my future excursions. The IMP880 holds and provides a good charge and I hope that it will continue to meet my high expectations. I believe that it is needless to say that so far I am thoroughly impressed by this device.

Pros: Small and lightweight, rubber coating finish, easy to use, nicecarrying pouch, includes adaptorsCons: USB ports are very tightRecommendations:Overall this product is working great for me. It charges my smartphonequickly and efficiently and I can take it anywhere. The LED's make it veryeasy to know the status of the battery. The only downside is the USB portsseem to fit very tight. In fact, it fits so tight that the cable pulledout of the plug on my iPod Touch USB cable. I believe this issue willremedy itself with regular use. Very good product overall.

The IMP99D is a fantastic backup battery. I previously owned a similar Energizer product. It had about half the capacity, yet for some reason weighed only very slightly less than the IMP99D. I have gotten more than 4 or 5 charges of my phone without draining to an indicated half capacity on the battery. (I've never drained it fully.) I love that the device has two USB ports on it, which is the reason I chose the IMP99D over the higher-capacity IMP1000.The power brick to charge the IMP99D is fairly small and juices up the IMP99D pretty quickly. The only thing I would change about it would be to use a USB-based charger to charge the IMP99D, rather than the proprietary barrel-plug charger. That way, I'd have to carry one fewer proprietary chargers and could instead use, say, my iPad charger.

Since I had seen another New Trent product, I had an idea of what I wanted. I searched for items that met my criteria (have a couple of iPhones and and iPad). I was looking for a product that would not require charging every couple of days or so. The New Trent iGeek exceeded my expectations! The iGeek is still running on it's initial charge ( 3 three weeks ago. I use it a lot to keep my stuff charged.) I am extremely satisfied and I will purchase more items. I would rate it 5 + stars!

Carrying this around with me gives me a reassurance that if I do drain my phone battery I won't be stuck. I feel more confident being oncall 24/7 and I don't want to be stuck at home near at outlet.I used this battery with my Kindle Fire. It started charging the kindle and I was able to continue reading my book and drinking my coffee.I've also used it to charge my Droid Razr phone while attending an all day conference. I could continue to keep up with calls and email while away all day.Likes:Light weight and compact.I like the matte black and blue color scheme. It looks high-tech yet professional.Small, fits well in my messenger bagExcellent variety if adapters in case I switch devices or want to help a friend.Easy to operate.Suggestions:The included bag does not stay shut, drawstring stayed open. I switched to my own zippered bag. Not a big deal.

If you go on long trips, or are away from an electric plug - this is a MUST for your portable device.  I keep it in my purse.  It's so popular that many of my friends have asked to use mine when their cell phone batteries are low and they don't have access to a plug!  It works great.  I had purchased another one earlier for myself, but my husband kept using mine so I gave him the original one and I kept this one (as it has 2 USB ports so I can charge my Iphone and Ipad at the same time).  On my recent trip, I charged my phone 100%, then when it went down, I plugged this Battery Pack up and it extended my IPhone battery until the rest of my trip...and more... I never leave home without this pack in my purse.  Can't say enough about this item as it has been a life savor for me since I use my IPhone and IPad all the time!

I ordered the IMP99D Mobile Power Pack that has the dual USB output and I have found it very useful. I have always had limitations charging my phone when it came to traveling by plane, transiting thru the airports, hanging out at the beach or on road trips with my motorcycle. The IMP99D power pack resolves this problem for me.I thought it would work on my ASUS TF300  pad but it turns out that my ASUS needs up to 15V to charge. For those thinking to buy this power pack for an ASUS Transformer pad, DO NOT because your pad need up to 15V. When I hooked it up to the ASUS Pad it only lit the screen butdidn't charge.The power pack does work on smart phones and I have tested it out on my friend's iPad and Galaxy Tab with no problems.I also use it to charge my Panasonic 3D Glasses and blue tooth ear piece.The package comes well equipped with an A/C charger for the power pack, a micro and mini USB extension plus USB cable, Samsung galaxy tab cable, and carrying case.PROs:* Fairly light weight (8.75 ounces) compared to other power packs so I am able to throw it into my backpack or my wife's purse without complaint of excess weight* Holds a Super 9900mAh battery capacity and it provides me with 5 to 6 complete battery recharge cycles for my HTC Thunderbolt that carries a 1400mAh size battery in it. So if I was camping or traveling that would cover me for a good part of the week.* Two - 5V USB outputs, One providing 1A for cell phones and the other provides 2A for units needing more juice such as iPads and Galaxy Tabs. I have used both ports simultaneously to charge both our phones and had no obvious delays in complete charge time.* Well built without any flimsy parts and has a nice silky touch to the cover.* I like that it has a smart chip to detect when your phone or unit isfully charged so that it powers off itself instead of continuing totrickle charge* The power button needs to be pressed in for 4 seconds in order toturn on and this is a plus so that you don't accidentally turn it onwhen it's in your back pack* In case you turn it on and forget to plug in your phone, it will automatically turn off after 15 seconds of no use.* Remaining battery charge led display is broken down into 4lights presenting (100%,75%,50%,25%) which is better than previousmodels that broke it down in thirds)CONs:* I don't really see anything negative or missing from this product.OVERALL Conclusion:Well built unit and holds a great charge and the dual USB is a convenient plus. The 9900mAh capacity of the power pack allows it to hold a longer charge and provide greater time of available energy supply.I hope this review helps everyone considering the purchase of this wonderful product.
summary: Very useful power pack.Can't leave home without it!!!

reviewText: If you are like me, you have an ever growing collection of USB devices.  I have a tablet, Bluetooth speaker, smartphone, kindle and MP3 player.  And they all have one common thread...they charge via USB.If you are like me and travel a lot, or if you find your phone is not lasting the duration of the day, then this device is NECESSARY.This is what this device does:  it charges your phone 5 times on one charge; it charges your tablet 2 times on one charge.Because of the 2amp connection, it will charge your phone in about 2 hours.  It will charge your tablet in about 5 hours.  You can watch movies on your tablet/phone while connected to the charger.It is really small and elegant.  It is about the size of a deck of cards.  It is relatively light.  I keep it in the velvet pouch it comes with in my backpack or car.  It is always within arms reach when I need it.  I like this item so much that I am making this product my bday/Xmas gift of choice.  I have already bought a couple for family members, and they are greatful for it.If you have even one mobile device, you must own this.  It is one of the best purchases I have made in the last year.

New Trent iGeek IMP99D (9900 mAh) External Battery Pack and Charger is an impressive beast - it is packed with juice you can easily charge your iPhone at least three to four times. I have used it on many long flights and had it in my pocket roaming LA streets. I was so impressed with it one year later I bought another one for my kid.Pros1. Long lasting. It is rated 9900 mAh. iPhone 4s battery is 1440 mAh, iPhone 5 is 1440 mAh, 5c is 1507 mAh, and 5s is 1570 mAh. You should have no problems fully charge any of these phones three, four times. I have often used this battery to top off my iPhone 4s for several days without charging the battery pack.2. It holds charge well. The one I bought for my kid was not used often. After a recent trip, it was kept in a drawer with roughly full charge (only lightly used on the trip), it retained three quarters of power judging by lights after about a month.3. It is reliable. I bought my first one in Nov, 2011. I have used it fairly often. It is still functioning very well after almost two years.4. It does not run hot. Whether it is charging other devices or being charged itself, it is only warm but not hot.5. It powers iPad 2 with no problems on its 2A port.6. It charges really fast. It charges my iPhone much faster than using my computer's USB port.7. It comes with adapters/cables for micro and mini USBs and a cable for use with Samsung Galaxy pad.8. It comes with its own charging power adapter and its input voltage range is 100V to 220V. You can take it to travel the world.Cons1. It is on heavy side. But, hey what do you expect for a 9900 mAh beast. It is a reasonable tradeoff. I had no problems keeping it in my pants pocket.2. The lights indicating remaining power are too bright. Your sleep may be disturbed at night if you use it in your bedroom.3. Occasionally, I may have to try several times to activate the charging process by holding down the power button for a relatively long moment.I wish the lights indicating remaining power only light up when it is first turned on to inform the remaining power and then automatically turn off after say 10 seconds. It will really help at night. Or at least the light should not be as bright. The second improvement could be the weight. But I guess the weight is proportion to the charging capacity. The third could be colors. At the time when Apple is playing with color to constitute as innovation (think about the shortage of gold 5s) and the market is eating it up, New Trent can also add a few different colors to attract a few more non-geek customers.But overall I love this battery pack very much for its large capacity and compact size. I give it a five star rating.
summary: Long lasting reliable battery - very satisfied

reviewText: I've owned this external battery for 2 weeks and so far it has exceeded my expectations.  I originally purchased this as an emergency back-up for my iPhone and iPad and it has functioned exceptionally well in that capacity.  The benefit that I didn't even think about was the fact that this external battery has 2 USB ports, which seems to be compatible with several other electronic devices that I own.  One example of that is a portable hot spot that I own.  The charger for the hot spot plugs into a port on a charger with a USB cord and unfortunately the hot spot's battery only lasts about 3 hours.  With the New Trent external battery I can power up my hot spot all day.  I've found early on that if I use the New Trent external battery for a few hours in one day I need to charge it at night.  If I only use it to take my iPhone from an almost dead battery to fully charged (just over one hour to charge) then I can use it for two days without recharging.  I personally don't mind plugging my phones and batteries in every night and if you do that with the New Trent external battery I guarantee you won't ever have to worry about a dead battery on your iPhone or iPad.  The other great thing about this product is you can charge your iPhone and iPad at the same time!  That obviously takes longer to recharge the devices but you won't have to worry about running out of battery on either device.  I would highly recommend this product!Pros-Never need to worry about battery dying if you aren't near an outlet-The need to always be on the lookout for outlets to recharge devices-Can charge pretty much any device that connects to USB port-Small enough to carry in briefcase/backpack, about the size of a deck of cards (but heavier)-Display lights are very obvious to see how much power remainsCons-Need to charge every night if heavy use in one day (not an issue for me)

I previously purchased a New Trent external battery for use with my smartphone and was very impressed with the product. When it came time to make a trans-Atlantic flight, I was quite excited to use the IMP99D to ensure that I had plenty of juice in my iPad for the entire flight. The IMP99D performed as advertised and charged my iPad 2 from empty to 100%. Even better, since the battery has two charging ports, I was able to charge two devices on the overnight trains in Europe. My girlfriend and I used the IMP99D to charge both of our phones at once, or our iPad and one phone. In both cases, the battery charged our devices in a reasonable amount of time.Pros:-Compact size makes the IMP99D extremely useful to business travelers and others that find themselves frequently on the road.-Dual Port allows user to charge two phones at the same time, or one iPad and one phone, etc. Extremely useful when travelling with more than one person!Cons:-It's difficult to come up with any complaints for an external battery that works as advertised: I expect the product to charge my devices, and the IMP99D does a great job at that.-It would be great if I could charge the IMP99D via USB, but I can see how a DC port is necessary in order to charge the battery in a timely fashion.

I like the reliability of this external battery and use it to recharge an iPhone and Moto X. My criticism is the size and shape. I wish it were thinner and longer — more similar to the shape of a smart phone. Otherwise, it' works really well and has saved us untold numbers of times from a dead-battery disaster!

reviewText: I got the 9900mAh version of this battery in 2011. I've been using it regularly for almost two years, and I couldn't do without it.
