This is a great product. This battery holds an impressive capacity. I did some tests to see how far I can get with it, and here are the results: For example, I fully recharged a completely empty Kindle Fire HD7, which took 3 hours on the 2A USB port and 4 hours and 45 minutes on the 1A USB plug, and I still had 25% left in the battery afterwards. The 25% should be pretty accurate because the blue indicator lights went from 50% to 25% just before it finished charging. I also tried charging my iPhone 4 for one hour on a fully charged battery pack. The iPhone 4 (2.5 years old) went from 22-81% in 1h, and the battery pack lost a bit more than 25% of its charge. Extrapolating from that, you should get at least 3 full iPhone4 charges out of it.Apart from the impressive capacity, the battery has a great look & feel. It has a rubberized surface which makes it feel comfortable and sits in the hand easily without slipping. I find its mostly rounded form factor very good to stick it into my laptop bag or jacket without any need for a major case. The little cloth-ish bag that comes for it does the job. I also like the button (big), and the indicator lights (spacing is wide enough to make it easy to see where you stand charge-wise).I think the weight is good for such a high-capacity battery - it does not seem to add too much weight to my bag considering that it gives me peace of mind with all my devices (I am a mobile worker!).There are 2 USB ports on the battery. The battery comes with a bunch of plugs and adapters, which I did not use because I already have all cables I need (you probably do too). There are plenty of other reviews detailing which plugs come with the battery in case you are interested.I cannot comment on the company's service because everything works as expected so I haven't had the need to contact customer service. The best customer service is the one you never need to call.(One note: the form factor is almost the same as the same company's more pricey "New Trent iCarrier 12000mAh" battery. So if you want even more capacity with hardly any extra size and weight and a similar form factor, you should also consider upgrading. I own both the 9900mAh and the 12000mAh and both are great!).

When i received the IMP99D, i knew it would be a quality products just from the packaging. I have had this charger for about 2 months, it has saved me on numerous occasions!PROS--Surprisingly small and mobile: It size is comfortable and can fit in any bag, even my skinny jeans!-One and Two amp charger- this was incredibly useful when i needed a fast charge, or when i needed to charge two devices simultaneously.-Great packaging and handy accessories: With several USB for basically every products, there wont be a need to go out and buy a new USB cable.CONS--LED battery indicator- The lights are become solid blue when you are either charging the device, or charging your device. Ive noticed the light is so strong it brightens my dark room.-Not that durable: On the split shown on the picture, if you drop your charger, it can split open. it has happened to me.Conclusion: the IMP99D is a simple, yet reliable product ideal for all that are always looking for a charge. I would Highly recommend this products, and brand.Note: I have used this product on an iPhone, iPad, GPS, and those ancient phone.
summary: A must buy for all with poor battery levels.

reviewText: Slim, easily portable with tremendous power. Able to recharge my phones at least three times off of one charge. Well made quality product. Highly recommended.

his review is for the New Trent iGeek IMP99D/NT99D 9900mAh External Battery Pack and Charger:I am giving this battery pack 4.8 stars (rounded up to five stars).5/5 for Style & Design - The rubberized case and blue lights make it look very high-tech5/5 for Accompaniments - Included are a nice carrying bag, micro- and mini-usb adapters, retractable usb cable, and another cable (for the Samsung Galaxy Tab).5/5 for Compactness & Weight- Slightly bigger than a deck of cards and it weighs 230 grams or about 8 ounces (about the same as 1 Cup of water).5/5 for User Friendliness - The operation is very simple and the user manual is thorough. The two different ports (2A & 1A) are very handy for iPads and iPhones!4/5 for Battery Life - I have an iPhone 4s with a New Trent Power Rock battery case (IMP210B). The combined battery capacity is 3532mAh and I was able to get about two full charges from the external battery pack (after charging the external battery pack overnight). I was expecting a little bit more than that (9900mAh divided by 3532mAh = 2.8 charges), so I emailed New Trent to ask them about the issue. The reply I received said, "The math is correct but the math does not include heat loss.Though the transfer of power there is always power lost somewhere in the system. While power is being transferred between the batteries, there is heat also in the process which means energy is given off as heat." For the record, I noticed only a slight amount of warmth from my iPhone/iRock during charging, but it definitely wasn't hot. A good rule of thumb for external battery packs (in my opinion) is that you can expect about 75% of the charging capacity to be available for charging devices. My experience seems consistent with their advertising claim of the 9900mAh iGeek providing 100% battery life for an iPad 2, which supposedly has a battery capacity of approximately 7000mAh.All in all, this battery pack is a solid piece of equipment for charging a smartphone or tablet while traveling or on-the-go!
summary: All in all, this battery pack is a solid piece of equipment!

reviewText: My CrackBerry trackball suffers from greasy fingers, exposure to elements, and all kinds of crap. I'm surprised it lasted as long as it did. Actually, what did it in was my feeble attempt to clean it. I took it a part, cleaned the little magnetic bits, put it back together and managed to cram it back in place. The ball worked better but was oriented 90 degress off! Argh...Then I looked on Amazon for a replacement was was dismayed to find they were only $2-$3 a piece. After reading the reviews, I noticed that some balls are inferiors. So I ordered this five pack. If one gets clogged, I've got more!Replacing was easier with the little blue tool. It popped out the retaining ring. I replaced the trackball and tried to replace the retaining ring. The "legs" on these retaining rings are a thinner metal. It's hard to line the legs up properly. Fortunately, my original retaining ring still worked fine. I used it.My CrackBerry is now fixed and the trackback glows green! I love cheap replacement parts!
summary: Maybe not exact replacement - but fixed my CrackBerry!

reviewText: I got one of these batteries from OEM Planet via the amazon.com marketplace. It acts and looks exactly like the one that came packaged with my phone, and it works great. The price was terrific, too. Later, I bought four more from another seller on amazon.com marketplace. I will omit their name to avoid possible problems with them. They claimed to be selling actual "made-by-Motorola" batteries. But, with no notice to me, they shipped an off-brand that I had never heard of. I was able to get a refund without hassle through Amazon.com, because this was a "Fulfilled by Amazon" purchase. To be clear: Amazon was not the seller; they only handled the fulfillment of the order for the actual vendor. I subsequently purchased a battery from BTO, Inc. on amazon.com marketplace. But first, I emailed them and specifically asked if they would assure me that the battery was a true Motorola battery. They promptly responded that it was, and when the battery arrived, it was indeed a real Motorola. At a great price. So, there are substantial bargains out there on this battery, and they are worth seeking out. But, BUYER BEWARE - be sure of what you will receive, and be sure of the return policy of the specific vendor that you choose.

reviewText: Update:  If you were thinking about the Seidio Innocell 2600 mAh Extended Battery for Motorola Droid, my advice would be "don't do it."  The OEM battery is a much better power supply.  It actually lasts longer than a few months, which is more than I can say for the Innocell battery I purchased.Review:I enjoy my Droid phone and with my usage, I go through batteries quickly. You can conserve power by turning off options you are not using (Bluetooth, 3G, Screen Brightness, GPS, Wi-Fi, Checking Email) but sometimes I forget or don't want to cut my features. I got a spare Original Equipment Manufacturer battery and an extended life battery at the same time.  This is an OEM battery worked properly from the start, unlike the extended life battery which needed to be "trained" in the phone.  I could not tell the difference in run time between this battery and the one that came with my phone from Verizon.The GoodThe battery fits in my Motorola car dock, which I use all the time.  It also fits in my desktop charging dock which I like to use. The Extended life battery does not fit the Motarola car dock or the desktop charging dock  The OEM battery does not add bulk to the phone.The BadThe OEM battery does not last as long with the features most people use turned on.  It is a pain to have to manage phone usage to keep the battery alive.  I am a heavy user of "Advanced Task Killer" which I usually access by holding down the Home key.ConclusionI am happy with the purchase.  I chose my battery according to what my use will be. When I have been out all day with my first battery and I'm going out at night it's nice to be able to snap in a charged battery. (without taking the time to charge my battery)  If I'm going to be in my car I use the OEM battery.  If I am out and about I use the extended battery.  It is nice to have options.  I still bring my OEM spare battery when I don't want to take the chance of having a dead phone.Unlike our I-Phone friends we have the ability to pop in a new battery. ;-)
summary: It's Nice To Have a Spare

reviewText: Here is how it worked for me (or actually for my wife who went to a conference in France and then to Amsterdam). I had an old off-the-contract iPhone 3GS that I had AT&T; unlock for me. Installed the SIM card (regular for 3GS - not the micro version), activated the OneSim account on-line and got a USA phone number assigned to it (turned out to be a Texas area code) and the SimCard already had an international (Estonian) phone number printed on it - so all seemed good, until over the course of the next 10 days, while she was away, I discovered the following:Receiving calls1. The US phone number is NOT FREE. It's free to a caller from the US (if they have free US long distance like most people do) but the OneSim account is being charged $0.20 per minute while it is accepting a call placed to that US phone number.2. The international number that the card comes with is the Estonia country code. One of the most expensive out there, except maybe countries in Africa. So the OneSim card will not be charged for a call to that Estonian phone number, but the caller from the US will pay at their regular international call rate. I tried using my Google Voice (turned out to be $0.33 per minute - for comparison a Google Voice call to Israel or Russia is about $0.02 per minute). Also using MagicJack, calling from home, was about the same price per minute as Google Voice - and calls to Israel and Russia are also next to free from MagicJack.So it seems like the solution would be to call the US phone number assigned to it and pay $0.20 per minute off the OneSim card account, right? Not so, really... I paid $40 for it and it came with only $10 credit which pretty much all got used up while I was testing the SIM card (calling/answering and texting to/from) after the installation while still in the US. Oh, yes, sure you can recharge the SIM card account but it starts with the $25 minimum!Placing calls:Calling from France and Netherlands to the US was about $0.30 - 0.50 per minute! If the account balance drops below the per minute price, you can't place calls or receive calls to the US phone number assigned to the card (as would be expected) BUT also you CANNOT receive calls to the Estonian phone number either (which is supposed to be free and not require any money from the SIM card account). So no communication, then. The person calling you better check your account balance to see if you have money there to receive a call that is supposed to be "free" for you. And you can add $25 minimum. That seemed like a scam to get you to pay at least $25 more to continue to use the "free" features that come with it! My wife ended up having to send me emails using wifi to recharge her account until I figured out to check the balance regularly. I ended up recharging the card account for $50 in the end just so that she would not be without a phone while I am asleep here (time difference).Texting:YOU CANNOT TEXT TO THE US NUMBER ASSIGNED!!! I called the customer service, they picked up pretty quickly, but the girl at first pretended like she was not sure what problem I was asking about (like no one ever asked about that before) and then sounded pretty annoyed that I was even asking why my texts to the OneSimCard's US phone number get returned with an error message. She explained that it says so in at least three(!) places on the website - "so of course you can't text to the US phone number - it's a landline!" I asked if I will have to pay my regular international text message fee (AT&T;) to text the Estonian phone number - she said something like "Duh..., obviously". AT&T; I think takes like 50c to a dollar for one of those international texts. However if you have two iPhones and the international one is connected to WiFi at the hotel or at the conference or wherever, then the "Blue" iMessage will work and will be free to both sides. But you never know. If it turns green after a few minutes, you will have to pay for a text message. So I waited for my wife to text me that she is at the hotel before texting her back.She was able to text from WiFi only. I opted out of the OneSim data package when I activated the account. It seemed too expensive to begin with.Technical weird stuff:When you call a US phone number from that OneSim card phone you are not actually calling that number. You are letting their computer know what number you want to call. You dial the number and press "Call"/"Send" and the phone immediately hangs up with "Call Failed" screen. A second or two later, it's ringing as if that person were calling you back. You pick up and hear the dial tones - that's when the phone of the person you were calling begins to ring. Not a major inconvenience, just seems like not the most elegant way to do it and feels like ancient technology like that should cost next to nothing, but it does not!!! (see the pricing above).Conclusion:It was better than nothing (worked for voice calls most of the time - unless the balance was low), but turned out to be much more expensive than I expected. I ended up paying a lot of $$$ on top of the original purchase price and will not be using this card again. I will try to do more research and find a better alternative.I could not believe how many 5-star reviews are out there for this product so I clicked on some "See all my reviews" buttons next to the glowing 5-star reviews. Seemed like the ones I saw came from people who wrote only one review total. Just for this "awesome" SIM card and their unparallelled customer service and never any other product reviews. And most of the ones I saw were not "Amazon Verified purchase". Maybe whomever wrote them will read this and catch on to that and add a couple more reviews for other products to make it look more legit. In any case, this is hardly a 5-star product. Not zero stars (it kind of works for voice calls and you don't pay more than you would have paid if you just brought your regular iPhone abroad), but it's 2-stars at best.UPDATE: The next day after posting this review, I got an email from OneSimCard demanding to edit the last part of it and remove the sentence that was there saying that I thought that maybe their marketing guys wrote those 5-star reviews under various aliases. I was happy to remove the sentence to make them happy - everything is clear regardless. I also used that opportunity to change the rating to from 2 stars to 1 star.
summary: It's a lot more expensive than I expected - feels like a bit of scam

reviewText: I purchased a nano SIM directly from the company for an iPhone 5 as they are not offered on Amazon as of this writing. However, the cards appear to work the same so the rest of my review should be relevant.As others have noted you will need a few add-ons to make the card truly useful the most important being a US (or your your country of choice) based number for voice and SMS. You will also need to add funds to your account which must be done in $25 min increments from the companies web site. There are several discount packages available for voice, SMS and data which can reduce the cost of these services. It's nice they can be purchased separately depending on your needs but costs start to add up quickly. Sorting through the options can be confusing as the website, while complete, can be difficult to navigate. They company rolled out a new data package in the middle of my trip which came as an unwelcome surprise as the previous package was not grandfathered. Documentation that arrived with the card was pretty good although somewhat generic.Set-up was a little tricky; make sure to test in advance. If you are comfortable fiddling with settings I recommend against auto programming on Apple products as it permanently installed an APN profile which can not be easily removed (understatement) even after returning to your original SIM. This may be anomaly of the Verizon variant of the iPhone 5. I had the most success immediately resetting my network settings when switching SIM cards. Note this will also erase all of your stored WiFi passwords. On two occasions I had to fully restore my phone from backup as data failed to work after installing my original SIM. Possibly a Verizon only problem as some network settings are hidden with the Verizon SIM installed; there may have been some leftovers from the OneSimCard configuration.Customer service is a bright spot. I had the opportunity to interface via chat, traditional support ticket and voice from the US and France. In each case the response was excellent with knowledgeable, helpful personnel. I sensed the company did not have extensive experience with the latest apple products distributed through Verizon but they worked hard to address issues quickly. Calls to customer support are free.PROS: Excellent voice quality calling to the US from France, Italy and the UK all on the same SIM. Nice! The company also offers a VOiP option when connected via WiFi which drops the rate to 1-2 cents per min. Perfect for extended conversations from the hotel and other areas with a good WiFi signal. I found the VoIP app needed to be in the foreground to work reliably. Data worked in all countries once properly configured which can be a pain. Make sure unnecessary background services, especially iCloud, are disabled while roaming as rates are still expensive even with discounts. Detail usage reports can be viewed on the web in near real time.CONS: SMS was flaky and did not integrate well into iMessage; I could only effectively communicate with colleagues using apple devices. While incoming SMS messages are free they are exceptionally awkward to send so most folks didn't bother. Some test messages never arrived further discouraging use. iMessage refused to send outgoing SMS messages to folks I had previously communicated with as it appeared to strip the country code prefix from phone numbers even when manually entered and/or updated in contacts. Frequent SMS users should look elsewhere especially if using apple products.SUMMARY: A good card for voice centric users who will be traveling to multiple countries.
summary: Excellent for voice; data/sms can be troublesome

reviewText: First of all, I should disclose that I am not a traveler, and do not plan to use this Sim card soon. I purchased it to put in an iPhone in order to enhance its value when I sell it on eBay. I had a lot of questions as to how this card works, and I sent an e-mail to the seller with some questions. The head of the company called me personally to talk to me about the card the same day. My question had to do with whether the card would work in a CDMA phone such as Sprint or whether it required a GSM phone such as AT&T.; It was explained to me that iPhones have the special ability to work on either network after they have been unlocked and the Sim card is installed. That is part of why this Sim card is so powerful. He told me that the Motorola Razr was the only other phone that could do this.  If you plan to take your phone traveling, you will have to call up your carrier first and have the phone unlocked.  The card will work with many other types of cell phones as well.  There is a table on the OneSimCard website that identifies the makes and models that it works with.I put this Sim card in my phone and activated it, and then started fooling around with the phone. I found that the phone number is based in Estonia, and I had to dial the prefix 001+ area code-phone number in order to reach friends in the US. You can get an extra US phone number associated with the phone so that your friends don't have to call abroad in order to reach you, but that does not make the phone useful in the US. When you call out, it uses the Estonian connection.While in the US, the phone attaches itself to whatever network has the strongest signal, and where I am it varies between AT&T; and T-Mobile. This was a bit confusing at first until I called customer assistance and had it explained to me.If you look up OneSimCard on the Internet, you will find their phone number on every webpage. You can reach a customer representative without going through an extensive automated menu, and they speak American English. They are kind and patient and explain everything as thoroughly as they can.If you read the ads presented by the company on the first webpage of this product you'll find out a lot of features of this type of Sim card. If you look OneSimCard up on the Internet, you can find coverage area, rates, FAQs, and many other pieces of information that will help you decide whether to purchase this. You may purchase this card directly from the company, but it won't save you any money so you might as well get it through Amazon and get the free shipping. When you get it, it comes with explicit instructions for setting it up on your phone.If you do not have an iPhone, you'll have to go to the OneSimCard website and look up the table that will identify whether your phone is compatible with it or not. This would be a VERY wise first step before purchasing the Sim card.This is a complex and extensive service with many, many features that will come in handy as you travel. This does not mean that it is not easy to use. Once it is in place and you have figured out the basics, you will have no trouble with it. I highly recommend it!

I've tried a few different Silicone skin cases, and while they did make this slippery phone more grippy and protect it from bumps and scratches, they were all quite loose fitting and "cheap" looking.This Otterbox case fits remarkably well and looks great. The 2 parts are molded to fit together nearly seamlessly and really do not look like a separate case once installed. The plastic shell has a texture for grip, but it's still more slippery than just a Silicone skin. However, it is more grippy than the stock phone (which is quite slippery on its own), so it should help prevent drops, and offer protection it you do drop it.I see a lot of reviews complaining about the price. It is quite an expensive case, but the quality is great, so if you don't mind spending a little extra for high quality then this case should be on your short list. The MOTOROLA T505 BLUE-TOOTH CAR KIT is simple to set up and use right out of the box! It gives you the option of either using the built in speaker or the FM radio and speakers in your car to talk on the phone or listen to your MP3s. No other equipment or tools are needed!It paired with my LG EnV2 right away and I've never used a blue tooth product before, so this was a pleasant experience. The T505 has visor clip that attaches to your sun visor and so it's always within speaking and listening range.From the calls that I've made with the T505, I can hear the people on the other end clearly and they report hearing me clearly too. I did try using the system to broadcast through the FM radio in my car, but that didn't work out too well because I had to really crank up the volume on my radio to actually hear the caller. But that's OK because I'm not going to use that feature and I'm not using  my phone as an MP3 player.I got this because of the new law in California about "no driving with a cell phone in your hand" so that's the only reason I'm using it.A few minor complaints that I have about the T505 is the power button. The button has to be held down for a couple of seconds to power on/off the unit which is a pain especially when you want to get in your car and go. And it's also a pain to have to constantly turn it on and off when you get enter and leave your car, so that becomes a hassle too.Another peeve is recharging the unit. Although you can use the T505 when it's recharging from the car's cigarette lighter/charger, you can't hang it on your visor or the cord will hang in your face. To fix that issue, I just put the unit on an old magnetic-holder that I had attached to my car's interior for an older phone.All in all the MOTOROLA T505 BT CAR KIT works pretty well as an alternative to having a blue-tooth ear piece.

reviewText: I wasn't even going to give the T505 a try, but, after reading pages and pages and pages of good reviews here on Amazon (650+ people have reviewed it, and it still has 4 whole stars), I thought I should give it a chance. If it didn't work out, I could just return it and only lose a few dollars on shipping. I'M SO GLAD I BOUGHT IT! And it's definitely not going back!I previously tried the Jabra Freeway and the Motorola Roadster bluetooth speakerphones. Neither of those devices met my standards for having clear, handsfree conversation and streaming music and audiobooks through FM with very little static the way the T505 does. The T505 is fantastic and works so much better than those two speakerphones put together! Handsfree conversation is much clearer and crisper, voices aren't muffled. Callers have told me road noise isn't too intrusive or unpleasant either. I drive a 2008 VW Rabbit, and road noise isn't very loud in my opinion. FM streaming is clear, and hardly any static is present when the T505 directs me to a station. The T505 seems to take over whichever frequency it chooses to stream through, even the ones on which I can normally hear faint voices and/or music playing! You can also choose to have the T505 remember presets for you if you prefer a particular frequency, and the guide tells you how to set that up. It's pretty easy, but, even if I use a different frequency each time, I don't have a problem hearing my streaming media without interference here in Knoxville, TN.The volume range on this speakerphone (the unit itself, not through my car's speakers) is very good, and I usually don't have to adjust it when I get a phone call. Another thing I like about this device is the fact that the function tones are short, pleasant and not annoying to hear, and the automated British-accented female voice is pleasant as well. I mention these things because on the other devices I tried - the Jabra Freeway's automated voice was too loud and not adjustable, and I could never find a comfortable setting for the regular volume during a call. I also didn't particularly like having the words "call ended" blurted in my face every time I hung up my phone. The Motorola Roadster had a generic startup sound that I didn't care for, and the shutoff tone was a little piercing and annoying. It did have a decent volume range, though, which could be adjusted quite high and low during a call, but callers' voices always sounded muffled anyway.One of the coolest things about the T505 is that somehow there is a little more bass pumped through my car speakers when I play music using the FM function. It's like I got better speakers without having to buy them! I don't know if that is due in part to the applications on my phone having better sound quality than regular radio, but, needless to say, music sounds great and better than expected. Also, the play/pause button works perfectly with the Pandora and Audible apps on my HTC Droid Incredible smartphone, and the volume up/down buttons become next/previous track buttons.My only very, very, very small gripe about this speakerphone is the lack of an auto on feature. It does have an auto off feature, which powers the T505 down after 30 minutes of no bluetooth connection. So when I walk far enough out of BT connectivity range - about 30 to 50 feet, I don't have to worry that the speakerphone will stay on for hours on end and lose its juice. Auto off is good enough for now, but if Motorola could start making new T505s with an auto on feature, too, it would then be pretty near perfect.Can't comment on battery life yet as it hasn't run down all the way. I've only had it for a week. I will update that info on here once I reach the first charging session. I don't mind that it only came with a car charger, because wall chargers are cheap on Amazon if I need one for in the house.The T505 is a wonderful speakerphone, and I highly recommend it to all looking for a handsfree solution for clear conversation and a more enjoyable driving experience. I am almost tempted to buy another one as a backup for the future in case the one I have now ever breaks. I hope Motorola doesn't stop making it, because, whenever I need to replace this unit, I'm coming back for another.
summary: I hope they don't quit making it!

reviewText: In most respects this item is exceptionally good.  The positive aspects are covered by other reviews on Amazon and also in reviews at cnet.com, pcworld.com, etc.  I want to emphasize that there is one substantial flaw with this unit (in my experience) that is so fundamental it amounts to a show-stopper: the microphone is not good.  It adds static to voice, and the sound is fuzzy.  It also does not eliminate as much of the background noise as newer technologies.This problem seems oddly unexpected at first, because the built-in speaker is so good that I find myself NOT wanting to use the option to play the sound through my car radio speakers.  So to the owner of this unit, the sound is GREAT.  However to the party on the other end of the call, it does not sound so good.I'm going to retain it and use it to play voice-mails and also to play spoken recordings (presentations, talks, audio books, etc) and it is wonderful at this.  I might even use it to play music on occasion.  But I won't be using it to make outgoing phone calls, which is unfortunate.The problem with the microphone MAY be rectified in more recent models.  This model is several years old now, as I understand.  I recently purchased a bluetooth earphone with microphone by Etymonic and people on the other end of my calls tell me it that sounds exceptionally clear.So it goes.
summary: Does almost everything GREAT!  Microphone is noisy though (a "showstopper").

reviewText: After buying a cell phone with Bluetooth I was pretty excited to find a device that I could use to listen to music/books through the car audio system.  Turns out this device does not work very well for me.- Turning it on and off requires holding a hidden button on the back of the unit for several seconds.  This is not so bad the first time you do it, but becomes increasingly annoying over time.  I don't understand why the unit was designed to require such a long hold on the on/off button, and why the button does not have any tactile feel.  It has a slight depression where you're supposed to push, but I often miss it, requiring even more time to turn it on/off.- I find the FM modulator unusable.  I live in a congested area - there are only a couple FM frequencies that are open during my entire commute.  The unit automatically searches for open freqs - you can't set them.  All you can do is push the search button so the unit looks for another open freq.  I never could get it to find the truly open freqs, so would have to change freq several times during my half hour commute.  After a few days I gave up.- Due to the problems with the FM modulator I ended up using the built in speaker exclusively.  That actually works pretty well for audio books.  It is only slightly louder than my cell phone, but is easier to hear since it is on the visor near my ear.  Unfortunately, with some books recorded at lower levels, I sometimes have trouble hearing over the road noise, so this mode is only slightly better than just listening to the phone directly.- The phone function works OK.  Some people have complained about the sound quality they are hearing, but most think it is OK.- Since it is battery powered, every few days I need to recharge it which is a hassle compared to my previous fm modulator which just stayed plugged into the cigarette lighter.Today I accidentally dropped it with the charger plugged in and the charging connector broke, so my 9 months with this unit are happily over.

The Motorokr does everything you need a car Bluetooth adapter to do, but a fraction of the cost of most other units.  The FM transmitter is strong enough for clear reception by my rear antenna, which was not true for my previous FM transmitter.  With my Motorola Droid, free Pandora radio, and the Motorokr, its like having free satellite radio in the car.  Some of the Motorkr features are especially useful, like searching for the bext FM frequency and announcing it, as well as simple phone controls on the front of the unit.  For me I just need to plug it in to the car adapter for about 1 hour and it will run on batteries all week.  The only issue I have is that it occasionally shuts off FM transmission and/or Bluetooth by design - I would like the option for Bluetooth and FM to remain ON when I am not streaming music or using the phone, so I can receive a call and listen on FM at any time (note I can still listen via the adequate Motorokr built-in speaker).
summary: BEST Solution for Phone/MP3 Bluetooth in Your Car

reviewText: A big reason I bought it was for the motospeak app.  Unfortunately, it has only limited functionality with motospeak.  I can listen to my text messages, and say yes when the nice lady in the unit asks if I want to call them, but I cannot dictate a reply to the text.If I had to do it all over again, I'd buy the motorola roadster which has full functionality with the app and doesn't look like something from an old science fiction show.Oh well.

I have had this for over a year now and have used it quite a lot.  I bought this product because my vehicle does not have an input jack for the stereo or built in blue tooth.  If you plan on just using the built in speaker for hands free talking it works well.  The quality and clarity of the call are good on both ends.  However, if you plan to play music through the speaker it does not sound very good.  Also, if you plan on playing your music/phone call through your cars speakers with the FM transmitter, even on the best of frequencies there is some static.  And as you drive you will have to keep adjusting the station to stay on an open frequency.  Overall, its good but not great.
Others may edge this as it is an old model in terms of features but none even today can match or better it for performance & clear quality sound and reception.

I love this device and was sad when Motorola discontinued it.  The model that replaced it seems ugly, while this one was sleek and easy to use.My husband and I have used one for years to broadcast lastfm or pandora or even our own mp3's from the cell phone to the car radio.  It's good for its intended purpose of phone calls too of course, but we've also used it indoors with a stereo as a conference call device for large groups.It comes with a car charger, but we usually just bring it inside when its light turns orange and charge it from a laptop using a standard usb mini cable.  The battery seems to last around 10 hours, which is awesome given what AZ heat can do to a battery operated device.Over time our unit lost the British lady who gives verbal instructions, despite her mysterious absence the device continues to function perfectly.  We had it long enough before she disappeared that we already knew how the device functioned anyhow.  The only difficulty now can be guessing which station she's broadcasting to (since she doesn't announce it anymore, though the station doesn't change unless you tell it to, which we only do if another stations signal bleeds into the frequency she's currently using).I was excited to be able to purchase another online to give to my mother, who has to drive great distances across radio-free plains to get to "the big city".  I actually came back and bought two extras, one for my sister in law who also has dead zones in her commute to the city, and one to replace my husbands and mine should it actually eventually die.

I really like this device.  I've used it for several years now and it has not disappointed me.  The battery life is terrific!  A charge lasts a month or longer.  The sound quality is fine and I especially like the feature that allows me to channel the audio to my car stereo speakers.  The controls are easy to use while driving and if I forget to turn it off, the unit shuts off automatically when out of range of my phone for 30 minutes.  It is small in size and clips easily to the sunvisor in my car.  The only negative that I can point to is that it comes only with a car charger.  However, the charging port is a mini-USB (?) and the wall charger for my Blackberry works very well with it.  This is an excellent bluetooth device --what you would expect from Motorola.

After reading the rave reviews of this product, I have finally decided to purchase this product over a bluetooth headset. Big mistake.I live in Los Angeles and drive a Mercedes I bought ten years ago without the technological amenities common in today's cars. But it does have a premium sound system.The problem with this device is the incessant hiss. I hear hiss with all the different FM frequencies (some more than others). I hear hiss while having a phone conversation. I hear hiss while listening to music. I do not hear a hiss when I am listening to FM radio stations so the problem isn't my stereo.You can play music from your smartphone (I have an iPhone 4) via bluetooth to a specific FM radio frequency determined by this device. Contrary to what other reviewers have said, the sound quality is definitely not CD quality. It is FM quality with a noticeable hiss. I have a CD player in my car and the sound quality is not even worth comparing.If you are looking for a bluetooth device to have a phone conversation, I recommend a bluetooth headset instead.Pros:1)Easy to use and configure.2)Decent battery life.3)Usable bluetooth phone system for conversations.Cons:1)Hiss, hiss everywhere and with every FM frequency.2)Mundane FM quality music via bluetooth with a lot of hiss.3)Need to turn on bluetooth in smartphones which drains battery life (but this would be true of every bluetooth device).

The Motorola T505 works great with my Treo 800w.  The fact that it supports both phone calls and A2DP audio makes it a fantastic solution.  I have been frustrated with the Treo 800w because of its low quality external speaker.  When in a car you simply can't hear it.  The Treo is great because of Sprint Navigation, Sprint TV, and the thousands of streaming options from the Kinoma Player software.  But none of the these can be used in the car because you can't hear anything from the speaker.  I have used a Jabra bluetooth headset that supports both voice and A2DP but even with that, I had to hold the earpiece tight to my ear when at freeway speeds.The noise cancellation is really good.  I placed some test voicemails to myself with the car windows down, the defroster at the highest setting, and the radio on.  The quality of the call was very good.  I could hear some slight popping once in awhile in the background but it was very minor and my voice remained strong and clear.The T505's volume can be too loud, which is great.  I can take and place calls, listen to Sprint Navigation instructions or listen to streaming music, all at comfortable volumes, all handsfree.I am also pleasantly suprised by the FM transmitter.  I have used a variety of FM transmitters in the past, including those in Garmin GPS units.  I gave up on them because of the lack of signal quality.  I am sure that this transmitter isn't more powerful than FCC guidelines but it seems like it.  When activated the selected station is simply silent on my radio - no noise at all.  And the auto frequency selector with voice instructions is a great feature of the T505.For the ultimate test I have Orb installed on my home laptop.  It is connected via 802.11g to my router.  Using Kinoma Player on my Treo, I connected using Sprint 3G data to Orb on my laptop and streamed a song.  My Treo connected to the T505 via bluetooth which then connected to my FM radio.  The song played without drop-outs, without stuttering in a reasonable less-than-hifi quality.  But remarkably decent for 4 different wireless links.The T505 is a great product.
summary: A really nice solution for the Treo 800w

reviewText: This speakerphone works great. It does not take much to figure  out how it works. The sound is clear and the light in front of it (green or blue) will inform you whether u r paired with your phone or not. U can call pressing the phone button for 2 seconds, and then say "call home" for example. The battery can last up to 5 - 6 hours. Very good product.

Very disappointed.  My friend Daniel swears by the T505 and I bought it based on his recommendation.  Many nice features like the FM radio transmitter, which can come in handy.. but what's the point if people can't hear you on the other end of the conversation?  Had to send the first one back after 5 months because people on the other end of the conversation couldn't understand me even though I could hear them fine.  The replacement from Motorola seemed okay at first, but after 1 week, it too is failing me: my friend said it sounded like I was talking to her underwater, but when I switched to my iPhone headset my voice was crystal clear by comparison.  Perhaps the earlier ones were assembled with better components?  My friend still loves his and he sounds fine on it.  I have not had such great luck.  Never wanted to love a product more, but this one has been a real disappointment, and now I'm out ~$8 in shipping fees and all the time wasted sending the old one back to Motorola to be stuck with another dud.  Ugh.
summary: Audio quality degrades over time!  Disappointing

reviewText: I love this product and purchased a second one for my wife.  I hated using an earpiece for hands-free driving and this made life much easier.PROS:* Long battery life* Easy connecting to your car's radio* Easy pairing* Bluetooth streaming of music from my phone to my radio* Other parties claim good quality on their endCONS:* Not always the best choice on finding an available radio station, but rarely more than 2 attempts required* Grabs my bluetooth connection when I'm in the house and I leave the unit on and the car is in the garage* The controls are not ideally placed and take a bit of getting used toOverall I love it and I'd be lost without it.
The unit works well but instruction say to not leave in car in heat, You might forget to put back in car when you need to.

I wanted to have something portable that I could use in my car and cars I am traveling in as a passenger to listen to music on my phone. Based on prior reviews I selected this older model rather than the newer one. I do not regret doing so. I have found that it doesn't always select empty clear radio stations however when it selects stations higher up the dial (102.5, 104.5... etc) the static interruptions seem to occur less often than when it opts for the lower stations on the dial. I have mine tuned to 102.5 and it seems to stay tuned to that unless I bump the wrong button when turning it on. In my area there are broadcast stations on 102.1 and 102.7 but they do not interfere with this device. I charged it over night when I first got it and have used it on many half hour trips to and from work. I haven't recharged it since I got it about 2 weeks ago so for my needs the battery life is good. When I want to charge it I bring it indoors and use my former phone's charger as it uses mini USB and my new phone uses micro USB. I had no issues pairing it with my HTC EVO 4G. I have made a call (as a passenger) and received a call. My caller was able to hear me without a problem and indicated it was better than the phone's own speaker phone feature which was good. I like that it is louder than my phone by itself so I can clearly hear my GPS instructions when looking for a new place without having to look at the screen to figure out where to turn. The speaker on the device also seems quite loud though I don't use that feature much at all. I'd happily buy this again and recommend it to friends and family members. I hope Motorola doesn't stop making this device just because they do have a newer model.

I am not the type to wear a bluetooth on my ear. And lets face it, there is a type. I call them cyborgs and I can't tell if they are crazy people walking around or have one of those things on their ear until I get close enough to see that they are not having a conversation with no one. Those things freak me out and people look ridiculous using them. This device, however, is incredible. I envy the newer model luxury cars that include bluetooth through the stereo of the car with hidden microphones. I rented a car with that kind of system and LOVED it. But I figured it would be a while before I drove another brand new Lexus. Until Now.The Motorola T505 Bluetooth Portable In-Car Speakerphone is amazing. It paired with my Thunderbolt no problem. It can act as a stand alone unit making and receiving calls or you can have it broadcast through your car stereo, on FM. I read that part of the description and doubted how well that would sound. I figured the little speaker on the device would suffice and I wouldn't ever use the "via the FM car stereo" option. WRONG. It sounds amazing in my Jeep. Crystal clear reception, nice and loud as I want it with zero feedback (another worry I had about the FM setup).I read many reviews of many devices and was tempted to buy one for $10 or $20 less. I am glad I got this bluetooth and I can safely say, "Cyborgs- you're missing out."

I don't usually read instructions but I had to for this one. And still it kept not working right.Using Blu tooth with my car was a routine reselect and a disappointment.Really can't recommend to anyone.I actually threw it away.  :-(
Wife uses this with her LG enV 3.  Works and keeps her from getting a ticket since texting and cell phone use has been banned in town except for hands free devices.

I've tried them all and the T505 is hands down the best when performance counts.  The FM performance on this unit is vastly superior to either the Motorola Roadster or the Jabra Cruiser.  If you don't require FM connectivity the Roadster is a good second choice however at a higher price. Pairing is a breeze.  Plus the standby and talk time seem to last forever.I won't repeat the other features etc. Just sharing the most important points of my experience here.  I highly recommend the T505 after trying the allegedly "better" and more expensive models.
summary: The Best Bluetooth Speakerphone On The Market

reviewText: I recently bought a 2008 Cadillac CTS.  It is the best car I have driven to date, but the biggest problem it has is that all vehicles manufactured prior to April 2008 have no bluetooth.  This is the first car I have owned without bluetooth installed since the technology first became available.  Since I run a business and constantly use the phone in my car, I scrambled to find the perfect device.Right now the two most popular BT devices are the Blueant Supertooth Light and the Motorola T505.  It was a tough choice which way to go but I chose the Motorola because it had FM transmitting capability.The one thing that is misleading about the pictures depicted of this device on Amazon is its size.  I was amazed to see just how small the T505 is.  It comes with a very strong clip that secures itself on the visor, and it easily slides on and off whenever you need to remove the T505 for charging purposes.The included car charger is worthless for most because who wants that cord dangling from the visor?  What is visibly absent here is a wall charger.  I can't really get upset about this as it does have a USB socket that allows you to plug your device in your computer's USB port for charging.Pairing was easy.  Hold the Power button down for a few seconds (you may have to press PLAY as well) and the T505 goes into pairing mode.  My iPhone immediately recognized the device and once you type in 0000 you are instantly paired.  No need to pair the phone each time you enter the vehicle.For best results make sure the bluetooth volume is all the way up on your phone.  This will provide the loudest results from the built-in T505 speakerphone.My first call came today while I was driving.  A british voice announced the incoming phone number. I simply pressed the front PLAY button and the call was connected.  Speakerphone was crisp and loud.  It was pretty incredible as far as the overall voice quality.  People sitting in the back seat would have no problem hearing or joining in the conversation.  The caller said I sounded great on his end and would never have guessed that I was talking on a speakerphone.Press the FM locator button on the back of the unit and a British voice will announce a vacant FM channel that is available for you to tune and have your call directed to.  Directing the call to FM produced a rather good quality call though slightly fuzzy.I would not hesitate to recommend this device to anyone looking for the most ideal bluetooth solution for their vehicle.  For portable hands-free bluetooth, this is about as good as it gets.
summary: This is the bluetooth device you were looking for!

reviewText: Does what it's supposed to and more. Pairs with your mobile phone in a flash.  You will need to spend 5 mins with instructions to learn how certain features work, but worth it.  One button tap gets your phone's "voice" menu. When call is initiated, or is incoming, the radio is silenced and conversation is directed through your speaker system (has it's own 2 Watt speaker when radio isn't available).  Very civil.  Voice commands are in a young woman's British accent...very calming.  No wiring/just works.  Needs 5 hours to fully charge, or it's plugged in while recharging.  Might invest in converter from Radio Shack that makes a DC male plug convertable to an ordinary AC wall outlet at home. If you're always on the phone it'll be handy. My top rating is FOUR stars.  I've yet to meet a FIVE star anything...smile.  You'll be happy with this and Motorola's Customer Service.  Phone number right on install form!  How about that?
summary: MOTO T505 Bluetooth In Car Handsfree.

reviewText: we now have 2 of these with the 2nd device purchased to easily connect to our home stereo.  these are also great for longer car rides as we can connect our bluetooth enabled devices (LG Dare and Blackberry Tour) to it and listen the the hundreds of songs stored on the micro sd cards and not worry about cd's or finding the few radio stations that play what we like.  it may not be the best thing out there but for the price we were pleasantly surprised (hence the purchase of a 2nd one).  even if intent is for car use only, i would recommend getting the ac adapter for overnight charging in the house rather than dealing with the car charger that comes with it standard.

This product is very well made and works perfectly for what ever it advertises except one issue.I will definitely recommend this to any one.Pros:* Easy sync every time i turn on the unit.* The voice is very clear on both ends as no one complaint so far and no one repeated the what i am saying.Also  end of  week i asked them do they see any difference. they didn't know that i am on hands free in a car.* Battery is doing good so far.* small unit easy to mount and remove for charging.* Before buying i had doubt about duplex technology.Even though this unit lacks duplex technology,you wont see any difference in real world.* Music streaming is flawless.The inbuilt FM transmitter is very strong.I have my antenna in front side,so i never had any hiss or static.The music or calls are of CD quality.* The transfer between unit and radio is very easy.Just hold the FM button until the white led turns off to bring the voice back to unit.* Unit remembers the last FM frequency.So you don't need to keep selecting the FM frequency.also you can set 5 frequencies as preferred ones.Cons:* The unit needs to be charged in between.i would love if starts and turns off when i start and off my engine.* When connected to iphone4,the forward and backward controls doesn't work on the unit.* the unit keeps connection with phone up to 20 feet.This is kind of annoying as ,many may have attached garage at home.* the led indicators could be better.Update:This unit performed much better then bluetooth soundfly.

This product works by enabling me to listen to my iPod or talk on my iPhone (or any Bluetooth-enabled smartphone) in my car, via hands-free Bluetooth technology. My iPhone features hands-free voice controls that work in unison with this device. I can call contacts, perform internet searches and request to listen to a certain song from my phone - all hands free with this device. The device clips conveniently to your sun visor in your car and it holds a charge for days before needing to be re-charged.I have an older car, so I don't have a direct, audio port on my car stereo system that I can plug into, so this device works by scrambling a selected radio station frequency.  Tune in to the station it tells me to tune into and I'm all set.It's also great for hands-free conversations on your phone via your car stereo speakers. Everyone in the car can join in on the conversation! The device is the perfect alternative for people who have older cars that are not equipped with Bluetooth built into the car.

I received my Motorola T505 several weeks ago and am delighted with it. No more problems with an earplug that ultimately leads to having one hand to hold a Bluetooth device in the ear - totally defeating the purpose of "hands-free" driving. I have tried four different Bluetooth devices over the past three years with the first three purchases (totaling $300) being a waste.The T505 is easy to set up and operate. You can leave the charge cord in (depending on where you put it) and run the device on car power all the time. I run off a charge as the cord is too short...but the battery life is sufficient for my use.One simple touch turns it on and connects to your cellphone immediately. My cell gives me a positive yes/no choice when connecting so I know it is working. Another simple touch will tell you which station to set your car radio to. This may need to be changed when driving long distances as you are susceptible to radio interference.I have no problem hearing the person on the other end and they have no trouble hearing me. Most cannot believe I am on a device at all. Sound quality is excellent (I use a Blackberry).So far, this is the best hands-free device yet.
i worked overnights and operated a fork lift i used this to stream music heard the music clear with all the sounds around me

I wanted a device to play music from my Droid in my truck. Initially I was going to settle for a wireless with a small speaker etc. But when I saw this could be run through the FM radios/speakers ,thought I would give it a try. Out of the box it was synched and ready to use within two minutes. Just turn it on,activate you phones Bluetooth and away you go. My phone is a Motorola Droid and I did not even have to deal with pass codes. It just synched and was ready to go. Next I hit the FM button and it told me to go to a specific setting on my radios dial. Went there, turned on the Droids music and  I was hearing it through the radios speakers,clear as a bell. Later my son called my Droid, answered with the Bluetooth operating but did not tell him. His voice was coming through the radio speakers and I was simply talking in the truck with the phone sitting in the center counsel.I asked him later if he know I was using Bluetooth and he was really surprised.He said the voice was normal, no feedback or echo. Same with his voice in the truck. A very nice feature ,when you arrive at your destination, just pick up your phone and leave. After a set time the Speaker turns itself off. I would highly recommend this to anyone interested in a simple to use, quality wireless speaker for a cell phone/MP3.
summary: Very good,easy to set up and use

reviewText: This is probably the only bluetooth handsfree device with FM transmitter that actually works!  Which, given the performance of other devices in this category, is reason to impress me plenty. :-)Before this, I tried theVenturi Mini, which on paper does have a nicer feature set:  It plugs into (and can be locked in place in) your cigarette adapter, and so powers on and pairs with your phone automatically when you start the car; it has 3.5mm line in and line out jacks; it allows you to manually tune to the FM frequency you wish to use; it can download your contacts list from your phone and allow you to scroll through and call people that way.  However, the sound quality is horrible both ways: The FM transmitter is too weak to overcome white noise through the car stereo, and the built-in microphone (at least in my car) is too far away to pick up my voice over the background noise.  There is no noise cancellation, and the  line-in jack does not work for external microphones (needs output from a powered device, such as an MP3 player, and will only play that sound through the car stereo, not back to the phone via Bluetooth HSP).After this, the Motorola T505 was a very pleasant suprise.  Most significantly, the sound quality is decent, both ways.  There is little distortion or "white noise" heard through the car stereo, and it picks your voice up well even when driving on noisy concrete.  To be sure, both of these merits are partly due to its location at the visor in front of and above your head, rather than in the cigarette lighter outlet, but this device also has quite effective noise reduction.  To boot, it has a built-in loudspeaker which used by default once you power it on, and the FM transmission to your car stereo is therefore optional.Now, just to be clear:  The sound quality is still not the same as if you were using something like aCassette adapteror any line-in port in your car audio system: It is limited to the frequency response for FM broadcasts as dictated by FCC (~ 35-15000 Hz).  If you are looking to primarily play music from your cell phone through your car stereo, and have "choosy" ears, you might want to use that instead.  Personally, I mainly use it to stream live radio from abroad (via the Nokia "Internet Radio" application and a cellular data plan) through my car stereo; for that, I get the same sound reproduction as if I am listening to local FM broadcasts.Likewise, for phone call use, you will sound clearer to the other party by using a decentheadset.Of course, I miss the ability of the Venturi Mini to power on and connect to my cell phone automatically when starting the car, so that it is ready to stream and take calls without any manual intervention, and so that I don't have to power it off after use.  Plus the ability to manually tune to an available FM frequency.  And of course, I realize that I will have to charge this baby now and then (not so far though, after about 6 months of use).That said, for what it is, I couldn't be happier with its performance. :-)

I really like this little device.  I have purchased 2 of them.  The sound quality is great and I love the fact that I can put the sound through my stereo.  I also loved the fact that I could pipe music through my stereo from my phone.  Don't want to talk on the phone while driving without some sort of hands free device. Now I don't have to.  The only thing I wish is the battery would last a hair longer.  I got a car charger from an old phone that fits and keep that handy.  Now it looks like I have a radar detector plugged in but I don't care.

I've been looking for a way to get my HTC Touch more "integrated" with my factory sat nav system in my Yukon. I already had the BlueAnt Supertooth II bluetooth speaker phone, but really wanted something that would work with the stereo.So I pre-ordered the ROKR T505 and have been using it for about a week now. First, in the box, you don't get a whole lot. Just the unit, visor clip, a DC charger, and very detailed and easy to understand instructions. However, since it uses mini-USB, any one of my many AC, DC, or USB chargers will work just fine. This device is also quite compact when compared to the blueant device and looks good sitting on the visor (also unlike the blue ant).After it was charged, I easily paired it up to my Touch, and media player (which was already open) immediately start playing music. I made a few test calls in the house, and it works great. The internal speaker is nice and loud (on par with the BlueAnt), controls are well placed for car use, lights and tones are easily understood, and the music will automatically pause/resume when you receive or place a call.After reviewing the rest of the instructions to understand what the buttons did (recommended), I took it out to the Yukon, and pressed the "FM" button. The unit talks to you telling you which station to set it to. Once you tune the requested station, you now have full stereo sound through your car stereo for both Voice and Music. If it has a bad signal, simply press the FM button again, and it will find the next free channel.I made a few test calls while parked and while driving around and it works just as it did in the house, except in stereo sound. While people could hear me OK, they could easily tell I was on a speaker phone. This is partly due to the vehicle being louder than usual on the highway (aftermarket exhaust). Voice recognition (voice tags) on the Touch also worked through the T505, just as it does with a bluetooth headset.Through the stereo, I could hear the caller just fine. But in my area, which is in a big city, I did keep getting intermittent static, regardless of which station I was on. While not a major issue, it is rather annoying. Changing the station does help, but as you drive, it tends to pickup other stations in the form of breif static and may interfere with your phone call, requiring you to find another free station.As noted earlier, incomming calls will mute your music, and it tells you the phone number that is calling. It won't say the name of the person on caller ID however. Even though I didn't really buy this to play music via FM, it works about as well as your average FM transmitter. So when a call comes in, I just press a button for the pre-programmed FM station that I previously saved in memory, then go back to CD when it's done. Although if you prefer to use FM for Music and Voice with your phone, this will makes things a lot easier for you. Just keep in mind that this is still FM, so don't expect anything near CD sound quality.Overall, everything does work as advertised. The battery has lasted on a single charge all week, but haven't had a chance to see how long it will go. Unfortunately, the FM issues are annoying, but expected. Your results will of course vary depending on the sensitivity of your receiver and number of stations in your area. So to wrap things up, here is a list of pros and cons.Pros:* Excellent compact design with well placed controls* Bluetooth supports A2DP (Stereo Bluetooth protocol)* Very easy to use* Voice dictation of certain commands* Speakerphone nice and loud* Mic picks up voice over moderate background noiseCons:* Expensive* FM transmitter could be better* No AUX outputBasically, once you understand what it will do and determine that it meets your requirements, this is definately something to consider. However, I personally plan on waiting for something that uses your AUX audio port instead of FM. Not to mention something that is a bit cheaper ($139 US at time of review). I returned it.
summary: Works well considering it uses FM

reviewText: I've been a fan of Motorola products but this unit is driving me crazy.  The battery life is terrific.  That being said, it doesn't interface nicely with my Droid X.  It does play music from my phone through my car speakers and if I had any interest in that I guess I would be happy with it's performance. reviewText: bought this ear piece about a year back. hasn't failed me yet! fits well and connects right away. couldn't have bought a better bluetooth ear piece, i would buy this again if something happened to mine. still going strong.

dealer shiped item quickly & on time delivery. this product is easy to connect to your phone & easy to use.very clear &soft ring tone.compact & the fit is comfortable.easy to switch from left to right ear.

Good product headset has an eight hour talk time unlike other headsets. You can fold it and put in your pocket safely, its clear, redial is great. I have used this model for at least five years and have given it as a present. I will buy more, as long as they are on the market.
Great clarity and sound.. volume is above my previous unit which was a jawbone.. recommend for all.. battery life only issue with Motorolla

I have owned several bluetooth headsets but the Motorola H720 outdoes them all at a relatively low price.I have tried them on phones ranging from a Blackberry, a Galaxy S2, an I phone 5, and a Droid Razr MaXX HD. I have had a:Jawbone ERA:Spent 80 dollars on this little guy.Pros-*Others can hear you well**Volume is good**Average battery*Cons-*Crackles when you put your phone in your pocket often.**Sags on your ear over time (this could be because of my job), constantly repositioning**Controls are irritating. Touching the outside of the earpiece doesn't always activate it for answering or hanging up. You press and wait, nothing happens, you press again and then it dials someone or hangs up. No distinct volume controls. Only button is on the back**Not worth the price you pay*DO NOT BUYSamsung something or other:Bought this Samsung for $20 on Amazon. Been a good backup for the price.Pros-*It was cheap**Fit great on my ear. Didn't hurt my ear at all and was snug**I could hear everyone great on it**Controls were simple*Cons-*Poor mic. People can't hear me on it very well sometimes*Motorola HX-550Pros-*Great sound. could hear everyone**Great mic. Everyone could hear me**Nice controls. Had a button on top to hang up and answer and a flip piece in front to shut off the device**Great range, I could walk 60 feet away from my phone and it would still be connected**Price- was less than 40 dollars*Cons-*Fit. Ear was irritated after a couple hours and I had to reposition to hear people when in loud surroundings**Rubber ear grommet. Tore after a few weeks and had to buy replacements.Motorola H720I bought this earpiece after my Jawbone. I had the Motorola HX-550 for a few months but unfortunately its not water proof. I sent it back and tried the Jawbone ERA much to my disappointment. I put up with the Jawbone for awhile before I found this Motorola H720 online for 35 bucks. Never had an 'out of ear' headset so was a bit skeptical, but for 35 dollars I thought I'd give it a shot. Wow, was I surprised. Such a great headset for so little money. Great decision.Pros-*Great volume. Fantastic. VERY loud. Has volume buttons on the top and bottom of earpiece for control. Surprised the sound was so good for an earpiece that didn't actually fit in your ear**Good fit. Doesn't move around on your ear at all if positioned properly initially**Everyone can hear me. I have never had anyone say they couldn't hear me**Controls are excellent. Volume up and down on top and bottom of earpiece. Answer and end call button on outside of earpiece. Tap once to initiate voice activated dialing (on my phone)**Front flip piece to shut off headset when taken off of ear. No need to go into bluetooth settings to deactivate**Fits easily into pocket when taken off. Don't have to worry about rubber ear grommet or ear hook getting lost.*Battery life is above average*Cons-*When I initially got this earpiece, the way the hook folded to fit the headset snug against the ear, it pinched my ear a bit to where it hurt. I have gotten over that for the most part (took a couple weeks). I have very sensitive ears though. My father wears the same one and it doesn't bother him at all. I wear it now with no problems.I would definitely recommend the Motorola H720. I have had at least a dozen headsets, and the only ones that comes close is the Motorola HX-550, but after using this, I would never go back.

reviewText: Yup. I agree with the most popular positive review. This is my Third H720 (I've washed one, and lost one). In-between, I thought I'd try some *better* units. And by that I mean more expensive of course. I sure spent more money. And what did I get? Something I can't carry in my pocket without something falling off of it. Something that doesn't just answer when I flip it open, but has to tell me how much battery power is left... The simplicity and reliable functionality of this device is what sets it apart. And NOTHING goes in your ear.Big benefits:But button is easy to push for answer/hangEar hook is comfortable and can be flipped around to either earNothing goes in your ear, so it fits all earsFlipping out the boom turns it on and answers without any real delay or "talking."No menus to figure out or mess up.Good enough rangeGood soundGood battery life with clear indicatorNo giant blue flashing light when wearing.The thing is a reasonable price and does exactly what I want without doing the things that I don't want it to do. The more you pay, the more bells and whistles you get... that I don't want or need. I just want to talk without holding the phone. And this is the best at doing that.

Pros: Very loud and clear, great sound quality. Nice off/on feature by flipping the tip shut & open. Very stylish design.Cons: It took a bit to get used to the "floppiness."This is my 1st Bluetooth that just sits on the outside of the ear. There is no portion that goes into the ear canal. Very strange for me, and most Bluetooth headsets sit in the ear in some way.It took a couple of days to get used to the "floppiness," it really isn't very loose, it just seems to be since again there is no part in the ear. It seemed like it was going to fall off whenever I moved my head, but didn't. So after a couple of days I was fine with the design. It no longer is an issue.The sound quality of this Bluetooth is just phenomenal. In fact, the other caller is so loud I have to turn it down a notch. So far the other caller hears me loud & clear. There is no static at all, unlike the Plantronic Bluetooth's I previously owned.To turn the unit off when not in use is so simple & revolutionary, you just flip the tip in and the unit is off. flip it open & it turns back on. In fact, it disconnects and reconnects flawlessly with my phone each time I flip it on and off. A great feature.No problems connecting, no dropped calls, the button on the unit is perfect, a light tap and the call is picked up.I'm starting to like the fact that there is nothing in my ear, forget I'm wearing it. Very good Bluetooth.
