I purchased the headset to replace an older H710 version.  For the most part, most of the features carried over from the older headset, but a few features changed for the worse.  The headset is paired with an HTC TouchPro 2.Pros:1. Pairing is easy and quick and I have had no issues with losing the pairing or having to reconfigure the bluetooth settings.  Very easy setup.2. Voice quality remains strong as in the previous model.3. I like the fact this is an over-the-ear headset.  I don't like sticking something in my ear.4. Voice commands work well and are very smooth.  Of course, there are times when my phone doesn't understand, but that could be background noise or just poor voice recognition on the phone's part.  For the most part, it seems to do better than the previous model.5.  Range is much better than the previous model and I get a audible signal when I get in or out of range, which is a nice feature.Cons:1. Button on the side of the headset has been moved too far back and is "softer."  It is probably just a matter of getting used to pushing further back than on the previous model, but I find that if you don't press it directly on the center of the button, it won't activate the commands, so I end up pressing it several times to get a response.2. Even though it is almost identical to the older H710 version, the ear clip doesn't fit on my ear as well.  The older version would wrap right around my ear and feel snug.  This one takes a bit more work to get it to feel like it is on firmly, otherwise, when I move my head quickly, I can feel it moving off my ear.  I may switch out the older ear clip.For the most part, the headset works well.  It provides all the basic features, which many headsets (and couldn't we say smartphones these days?) fail to do.  Voice quality is good, range is strong and provides solid voice commands.  I have tried 3 or 4 other headsets in the past few years and keep coming back to this line of Motorola headsets.
summary: Some Good Features, Falls Short on Others

reviewText: Low  volume wants to fall off. Typical problem with BT makes them unusable. I am a ups driver so the BT needs to stay on, and overcome the the noise of traffic and my truck and wind. Tried 3 plantronics, 2 noisehush and this motorola. They were all garbage except the noishush clip on. I finally found a winner as the battery lasts longer bout 9 hours and it kept the cord away from my phone stayed in my ear and overcame the noise.
summary: most bluetooth headsets are crap this one is no different

reviewText: I replaced the previous one I had as I lost it.  My last one fell in the water & still worked.  I totally recommend to anyone.
Love everything about it.  Easy to use and works great.  People can hear me.  Sturdy but light on your ear.

I was really hopeful that this earset would finally be the end to me buying a new headset for what has felt like every other month for years now.I have tried to expensive ones from Jawbone, and even and older Motorola headset that predates this model that worked well for a few months until many software upgrade made the connectivity on them an issue.Pros:- Decent range so your cell phone doesn't need to be in your pocket (necessarily) when using the headset- Lightweight- Provides a middle-of-the-road hands-free experience that many people are looking for.Cons:- Awkward placement on the ears- Default setting is for the left ear and has to be changed for the right year (just a personal peeve)- No replacement parts were included- It can be hard to flip open the mic to answer a call if the headset is settled into your ear- Sound quality can be bad because the mic is weak and far from your face
This paired so nicely with my iPhone giving me the freedom i need to talk and multi-task.  I recommend it!
summary: For the price a great buy

reviewText: This is one of the few models that fits ON your ear, not in it.  It is light and very comfortable.  Sound quality on my end is superb, although callers say I sound a bit muffled.  I absolutely LOVE the flip out to switch on.  It is so fast and convenient.  It connects quickly to my Android Evo phone.  And with the Froyo 2.2 update, I can now use voice dialing by touching the button on the headset!  It works GREAT.  The unit has a standard micro USB and I can use the same charger as my phone with it (although it came with a charger, too).  Battery seems to last forever.  I do find it a bit hard to use the volume controls, but I rarely mess with it anyway.  I am very pleased with this purchase and would do it again- Amazon had a GREAT price ($37) making this headset a superb value.

I have owned about 5 of these. They last me about 2 to 3 years each before the book switch fails and the unit no longer knows it's on. I buy them for my wife, my daughter and myself. Don't have any noticeable issues. Once in a while if air is blowing on it or my air purifier is running in my home office I have people tell me they are getting feedback, but it occurs less than it has on some much more expensive blueteeth I've bought in the past. And at this price, $35, you don't have to punish your daughter too much when she loses it.
summary: I love these cheap little Motoraols Blueteeth

reviewText: This bluetooth works well, but I'm sure the more expensive ones have less issues. It's fine when you want hands-free, but there are issues with it. In the car with the windows down, it's hard for the other person to hear you. With the windows up, it works pretty well, though. If you walk away more than about 5 feet from your phone, it starts breaking up. Also, the length of charge seems to be getting less and less.  It says 8 hours of use, but it's more like 2 to 2.5 hours. I would look elsewhere and spend a little more.

I already had the H700 and really liked it, so I decided to try the new H720. I like it better than the H700. It pairs easily and has a good sound quality. Connects faster than the H700, and is one of the best bluetooths I ever tried.

I never thought that I would buy a bluetooth. I always thought that people who walked around with a bluetooth in their ear looked crazy. No offense. I decided I'd be Bluetooth free until one day I almost rear-ended someone trying to switch my phone to speaker while having a conversation. That was the wake-up call I needed.It was super easy to connect the Motorola H720 Bluetooth to my Droid 2. The sound is crisp. I have no problems hearing the person I talking to and they have no problems hearing me. There's a volume control on the side of the bluetooth that's a little difficult to adjust. On accident, I discovered I could control the ear volume using my phone which is what I now do.The button in the middle is to answer and hang-up. With just one touch I can answer a call. No fiddling around trying to find the button. It's the perfect size and doesn't require a heavy hand to activate it.The battery life is phenomenal. I've only charged it once since I bought it. Granted, I don't talk on the phone a lot and I only charged it because I was getting paranoid that the battery was going to die on me even though there was no indication that it was.The earpiece is comfortable. It's very light and sometimes I forget that I'm wearing it. My only complaint is that it's kind of big for my ear (I guess I have small ears) so instead of sitting snug against my head, it kinda dangles a little.Thanks to this great earpiece, I've been converted.
The price was good and the ear piece performs well with all my cell phones I have used it with.
summary: Great performance and price so far.

reviewText: I picked this up in anticipation of the new "hands free only" law that I knew was set to take effect in IL in 2014. As a tradesman, I am constantly on the phone in my car - whether making calls or checking directions or (GASP!) even texting. Though I try hard to avoid the latter, the first two simply cannot be avoided. I've already received on traffic violation for talking on the phone while driving through a construction zone, so I knew I had to get a device like this. After shopping around for features and prices, I settled on this model and have been very happy with it. It is easy to set up, is (mostly) unobtrusive while wearing it, is lightweight, has a great battery life, and seems to broadcast and pick up clearly, as my customers and wife and coworkers have not complained about not being able to hear me through this device. My only gripe is that I wish there were some way to make it fit onto my left ear rather than my right, only. Other than that, I am very pleased with this product.
summary: Easy to set up and use, and at a decent price. Time to comply with new laws!

reviewText: First I bought one as a gift for my Father in Law who requested a BT that did not go in the ear. I did some research and bought this one. He loved it so I bought one myself and it is super comfortable with zero ear fatigue for lack of a better description. Now my wife has one and also loves it.The best part is the people you are talking to never complain they can no hear you as they did with my old BT.I rate this a 6 out of a possible 5!!One tip - BUY THE RETAIL ONE as there are counterfeit bulk ones on the market. Also if yours sounds bad you got a fake. The retail is version is also only a few dollars more.

About a month ago, my old Jawbone 2 Bluetooth headset finally died. Over the last month or so I have tried four different headsets until I finally found one that met all of my needs. I am including my brief opinions about each of them for comparison, and to hopefully help some of you narrow your selection down, if you are considering any of these.MOTOROLA H720PROS: Easy to use, flip to talk makes answering calls easy. Comfortable.CONS: Floppy feel. Noise canceling does not work very well.MOTOROLA HX550PROS: Flip to talk makes answering calls relatively easy. Its Comfortable. Noise canceling works very well while on calls.CONS: Noise canceling does not work for voice commands. The compact nature of this headset makes it more difficult to flip open than the H720.PLANTRONICS M165PROS: It looks good. Deep sleep mode means you don't need to turn it on and off every time you want to use it.CONS: Noise canceling not nearly as good as either the HX550 or any of the Jawbone headsets.JAWBONE 2:PROS: Noise canceling works very well, both for calls and voice commands.CONS: Hidden buttons are hard to use. Plastic cover over buttons eventually fatigues and cracks. Turning on headset requires holding hidden button down for three seconds, followed by another three seconds to connect to the phone, causing missed calls.JAWBONE ICON HD:PROS: Noise canceling works well, both for calls and voice commands. Single multi-function button is MUCH easier to find and use than on the Jawbone 2. Power switch is easier to use than the hidden button on the J2. Time to connect to an incoming call from power-off is about 1 second, so no more missed calls. 10 days of standby time, so probably won't turn it off anyway. "mytalk.jawbone.com" provides an easy to use interface to the headset. Downloadable voice personalities are fun. Ability to reconfigure multi-function button for volume control or enabling/disabling Noise Assassin is nice.CONS: Slightly less comfortable to wear than HX550 or M165 in-the-ear, but not bad for short duration. Would probably use over-the-ear hook for extended use.

I tried this Bluetooth headset out because at the time, I did not have a car that had Bluetooth integrated in. It is literally more trouble than it's worth. It's a constant cycle of turning it on, answering a call, looking like an idiot in Walmart, hanging up, charging...I mean this is a daily thing. If you don't have the time do complete this cycle ALL the time, then don't bother. There are better headsets out there and for goodness sake, just answer the phone like a normal person. Absolutely ridiculous.
summary: Motorola best in audio? Not 100% true

reviewText: Gets the job done-i insist on having a bluetooth, not sure how people hold the phone when on long conversations.

I like the design and it seems to stay on my head just fine.  The charge lasts quite a while and it is small and light.  It picks up my voice pretty well, but could do a better job of cutting out the background noise.  It has great range and I can walk far away from my phone.  The volume goes up just far enough that I can hear people while I'm driving, and I'm not hard of hearing, so for those that are, this tooth may not be loud enough.  For the price it was a good buy, but it could tick a few more boxes for sure.

the quality needs some improvement! While the headset itself is a great design, the flip mechanism wears out pretty fast. This is my 3rd unit of the H720 I bought, because it wears out too fast and makes connecting sometimes quite a task! I like the fact that I don't have to squeeze a stupid ear-bud into my ears which hurts after a while. The flat-against-your-ear design makes it comfortable to wear. That is my main reason to buy the H720 again, over and over!
It's a non-invasive fit with clear, crystal sound. The battery lasts and the ease of use could not be simpler.
Fits my ear perfect and the sound quality is great. Also no complaints from the people I talk to, they can hear me pretty well.

This is perhaps the fourth H720 I have owned over the years. I either lost the previous headsets or forgot to take them out of my pocket before washing  my clothes. This headset does not hurt my ear and the sound quality is crisp and clean. No one knows I am using a headset when they speak with me.  It pairs up wonderfully with all of my cell phones.I have owned other headsets but did not find them as comfortable.

i had a Project with the iphone 3g due and this thing saved my life. i have every iphone made but this battery out last the all!! from the 2g to the 5

reviewText: I really like how low profile the holder is. On my car (Jaguar X Type), it works great in both portrait and landscape mode. The hold is very steady and I use it with the matching iPhone case.I've tried 3 holders in my car so far and so far I prefer this the best mostly because it is so small and practically blends in with the car. The magnets work much better than I expected.

I'm a believer. I just recently bought an iPhone 5S and an Elago Outfit case ($10 on amazon) for it to replace my iPhone 4 (and it's elago case) and the best part about this kit is that it includes 5 of the metal buttons. the package doesn't go into that much description of them but they all have a very special purpose:The ones with the logo pattern (square and circle) are best for most smartphones because they tend to stay put with a little bit of resistance when trying to re-angle or rotate the phone on the tetrax mount.The ones that are small and smooth are best for smaller things that you don't weight as much as a phone and that you don't mind mind spinning freely - of course they don't 'spin' they just are more free to, so like a remote control for example is perfect.The one with the flat washer type area - is best for items thaht you want to stay perfectly perpendicular to the surface and not angle, this is good if you position your tetrax in such a way that you want it to be permanently in that angle.I want to buy another one but I honestly don't need it, everything is in the box, it's lasted and hasn't lost it's magnetism.The product still impresses me, it's like magic, you just hold your phone up to the dash near the tetrax and it just finds itself; it's an involuntary motion i just do now, i get in the car, wave my phone over the dash and let it go and start the car. I love it! I'll never buy another kind of mounting hardware ever again.I use my iPhone for GPS (waze app) every single day both ways on my commute and for just about everywhere I go. I mounted the button about an inch and a half above from the center and it's perfect, if I take a really hard hairpin turn it'll creep to a slight angle but has NEVER fallen off or swung sideways or anything. It's very strong and I'm glad I bought it.
summary: BEST way to mount a phone to your dash, least obtrusive, very reliable and is nearly invisible.

reviewText: I had to glue the device to the vent clip as the clamp has rubber pads that cause it to slip off when pulling the phone out.  I wanted something that did not look gadget like to a new Lexus and this is very subtle and the nub on the back of the phone is  not very intrusive and keeps the phone relatively flat.  I like it.

The design is really simple. Turning the round top tightens the clamp onto the vent louvers. It's easy and will most likely work with almost any vent type. But, if you've got one of those vents with the stupid guiding knob in the middle, and the knob sticks out more than 3/4 inch, then this one may not work for you. The problem: the knob on your vent will get in the way and your phone/gps won't be able to reach the magnet. They do provide a slightly larger metal button for your phone but even so it may be a stretch.Other than that, hats off to the person who came up with this design.
summary: Clever little thing, this ... but make sure you measure your vent "knob"

reviewText: The magnets on this holder are extremely powerful. The downside is the little metal plates with the sticky backs have a very weak adhesive. I'm going to find my superglue and use it to attach to the case I think this will make it strong enough to hold the metal plate to the case so it doesn't get ripped off.

reviewText: Four out of five cables work perfectly.  The last one will work if the iPod/iPhone is perfectly still (no jiggling the cable).  Considering the retail price of a name-brand cable, this would be a great bargain even if only one cable worked!  Great value!!

Ok so what do you expect when you are buying 5 of these for less than what Apple charges for 1? It would be nice if they all worked and much like many other reviewers, only 3 out of 5 worked for me. I did however manage to find that one charged my iphone but would not sync and this was placed next to my bed for night charging. The 5th one.. well, what can I say but it went in the trash as it wasn't even worth the time it took to send it back. Quite honestly I don't know how they can possibly be making any sort of profit, even with sending 3 out of 5 when you use Amazon Prime (no shipping) and less than $5 for all of them!
summary: You get what you pay for!

reviewText: This product looks like and works as advertised. These adapters either work or they don't work. This one works just fine!

None of the 5 worked for my iPod Touch (tested on a system with known working USB port and iTouch; in other words,I just replaced a different working cable with each of these one at a time, and waited several seconds: no charging, no device recognition by iTunes, nothing at all to indicate the cable was passing through any signal at all).

I've been wary about buying third party iPhone cables, since most of the other ones appear to not work (either not at all, or don't charge, etc). So when I saw this, 5 cables for $10 I was definitely a bit skeptical. But after reading reviews from everyone else I decided to give them a shot.And I'm glad I did! All five of them work properly as chargers and connectors to my head unit in my car, and let me listen to my music. Considering I've broken two official Apple cables (at $30 a piece) in the car already through various things (like getting caught in the seats), I'm happy to have all of these cables, and at a huge savings over the official product! I'm tempted to buy more before they disappear!Edit: I should mention that I used these with an iPhone 4.

These are fine for what they are, a cheep replacement for OEM cords. I bought 10 since my wife and I are constantly loosing cords. These are not as well built as the OEM ones are but they are a fraction of the cost. One thing to note if you keep your phone in a case, the plastic part around the end that goes to the iphone is much bigger than on an OEM one. it will not fit in the cut out for any of the cases i have tried. the plug will still work but it wont slide all the way in unless you take the phone out of the case.

I require a lot of these USB cables, so am always looking for the best price.  These were low, but worse quality than others I have gotten in this range.  I accept that a percentage might fail, but this batch (of 10) had about a 50% failure rate for various reasons.  Some would not charge, some would not fit, and one got stuck.  Not a bargain.

These cables are well-built and do what is advertised. All functions are available when charging using these cables. The only drawback to these cables is that the connector is a LOT larger than the standard Apple charging cable. This can create problems with a number of aftermarket cases. I've found several Touch and iPhone cases that simply will not work with this cable.
summary: Work as advertised, but large connector.

I've never understood why people complain about the bubbles.  Yes, if all conditions are right, you shouldn't get any bubbles, but if you have a serious amount bigger than a fleck of dust, that's user error.  Don't blame the screen protectors because you don't understand how dust + a sticker = bubble.  That and it's so easy to push the bubbles out with your finger that you had to have messed something up if you can't get rid of them.First things first, these screens are sloppily cut.  The top is actually rounded, like a small hill instead of flat.  It sits pretty much flush at the very top but the top edges (where the LED indicator is) of the top "droop" down about 2 mm.  Secondly, the bottom, with the top part at the very top of the Droid, is about 1 mm too long.  Instead of being an idiot like most people who get bubbles, I slightly lifted the bottom part and cut off said 1mm with a pair of scissors.  While doing that, I managed to get 2 flecks of dust under the protector.  So now I have 2 very small bubbles that are barely even noticeable unless the screen is completely clean.These are 100000 times better than the stupid Verizon screen protectors.  Verizon's screen protectors have these completely useless "handles" at the top of the protector.  Why?  So it doesn't cover the LED indicator lights.  Why they felt it necessary to not protect them with a CLEAR protector, I have no clue.  Either way, these stupid handles NEVER lay down completely flat and are always susceptible to getting lifted up accidentally.Because these protectors are completely rectangle (minus the cut out for the ear speaker) there are no issues with accidentally lifting the protector.Also, for $5 versus Verizon's $15, what do you have to complain about?
summary: Much better than Verizon OEM Screen Protectors

reviewText: I've had the HTC Hero for almost a year and can honestly say that this is the worst cell phone I have ever had the displeasure of owning. There are so many bugs and glitches in this thing that it's better suited as a paperweight. Yes, I have done all the updates and am using the app killer and it's still junk. My 2 major gripes are battery life and lag. PLEASE, before buying this phone, do an internet search and check out the numerous sites that are dedicated to this piece of junk phone.**UPDATE**I am still under my 2 year contract with this phone (2 months to go) and it's still a collosal piece of junk. Absolutely the worst phone I have ever had. I can't saying anything good about this phone. I think HTC should refund everyone who bought this phone, seriously. HTC knowingly put out a phone that they knew was a complete piece of junk! Anyway, do not buy this phone!

This is a very attractive phone and the HTC Sense enhancements to the native Android OS makes HTC phones much more polished than non-HTC phones. HTC enhancements include multi-touch, integration between Facebook and contacts (the Facebook profile photos of your contacts can automatically be associated with the contacts in your phone, for instance), and more. Android by itself is great, especially if you use Google Contacts and Google Calendar since the ability to sync between the phone and these apps is part of the Android OS. The phone looks cool, has a decently-sized screen, isn't bulky, has a nice built-in camera, and is generally a nice product from a hardware standpoint.The problem is that Sprint's version of Android leaves a lot to be desired. Specifically (based on my own experiences and/or experiences of others):* The phone ships with Android 1.5, even though 1.6 was released in September 2009, 2.0 in October, and 2.1 in January. The Sprint/HTC version of Android 2.1 doesn't actually provide full Android 2.1 support, however. Live Wallpapers, for instance, is mysteriously missing from the upgrade. And, to add insult to injury, the upgrade to 2.1 requires a Windows computer. The irony here is that Android is built on Linux, yet Linux users can't use Linux to upgrade their Linux phones. The last time I checked, even Mac users appeared to be left without a way to upgrade.* Android 1.5 for the Hero is buggy. Receiving picture messages (MMS) while the phone is connected to WiFi, for instance, is just one huge bug. There are also GPS-related bugs requiring either temporary disabling of GPS and/or reboots of the phone (which take several minutes to complete) and problems where the phone will go to voicemail after only ringing a couple of times, if at all.* Sprint/HTC's Android 2.1 upgrade has released even more bugs that include reports of random crashes, delayed dialing (in some cases it takes several minutes to be able to dial out), inability to answer some incoming calls or shut off the alarm, and problems with Bluetooth among other things. A quick web search should turn up a lot of complaints.* The Android ships with preinstalled NFL, NASCAR, Sprint TV and other apps that use resources but cannot be uninstalled. Personally, I like the Sprint TV app but have no need for the NASCAR or NFL apps but I can't uninstall them. The only way to get rid of them is to "root" the phone, which voids the warranty on the phone.* Sprint has confirmed that it will not be providing the Android 2.2 upgrade for HTC Hero phones, despite the fact that 2.2 actually provides incredible speed enhancements for Android phones and Hero users who have rooted their phones and installed 2.2 from other sources report huge performance increases with the Hero.If you want a phone that fully supports Android 2.1 and above, and if you want a phone that will support Android upgrades in the foreseeable future, do not purchase the Hero--and certainly not on a 2-year contract in which your contract will outlive Sprint's commitment to keeping the phone upgraded (that appears to have already ended). There are a lot of angry Hero owners who are furious at how Sprint has handled upgrades for this phone. You're probably better off either paying a bit extra for the HTC Evo, or looking at other Android phones from other service providers.If, on the other hand, you don't mind voiding the warranty and hacking the phone a bit to use non-Sprint Android software, you may find that you're able to tap into the phone's real potential and surpass the limitations and frustrations experienced by those who have played by the warranty rules.
summary: Plagued by bugs and will not receive Android 2.2 upgrade

reviewText: Pros:Nice screenAndroid OSMarket (Store)Sprint Support folks attitudeCons:Battery issuesNetwork issuesHTC SenseText appSprint Support folks ability to solve issuesVoice MailThis is a beautiful phone. It feels great in your hand. It has a premium finish. I like the way the phone gives tactile feedback when you're using the on screen keyboard.For only being up for so short a time, the Market (app store) is very full of (sometimes) useful and inexpensive apps. The Android OS itself seems like it is well planned out.I also have to say that during the forty or so hours I've been on the phone with them, the folks at Sprint (their advanced technical folks) and the folks at HTC have been quite nice. Very friendly.I'm currently on my second handset in as many months. The first one refused to let me see texts, or voice mails. It had about a 3 hour battery life (due to what I was told was an issue with the text application). The processor was never allowed by that app to ever sleep. It was running 100% of the time.Those nice folks at Sprint sent me a new phone and battery.The new one has had some of the same issues, and others that have been baffling. The browser would refuse to ever open. Apparently you have to clear the History just about daily to keep this from happening. The browser seemed to think I was in Germany, flipping over to that language despite my never requesting it.The thing still won't let me see all my voice mails, sometimes dropping them in days later. Changing over to the Handcent text app (per those same nice folks at Sprint) seemed to clear up the sleep issue with the processor, but now Sprint is telling me Handcent may be to blame for my phone locking up and not letting me answer phone calls.I cannot get my Hotmail account to load to the phone. You have to use an Advanced Task Killer to preserve the battery. The phone is already to quiet, and heaven help you if you get a case for it, as it will muffle the phone's speaker phone by huge amounts.Apparently, if you use too much of the internal memory (the only place apps can reside) it will cause the phone to loose its mind as well.I've just tried turning off the HTC Sense. That reduces the number of screens and types of widgets you can use, but since they've got me paranoid about using the internal memory, it isn't a huge hit.REALLY SAD I GOT THIS PHONE. That said, my fiancee's phone has worked with little or no problem. That's why it is getting two stars. I'd not give it any.Lagging processor, unreliable build quality, OS that kills the phone's usefulness. Stay away. Stay far, far away.

I both love and hate this phone.  I love the Android operating system.  It's very elegant and easy to use.  The Market is filled with Apps, and I was able to find an app for everything that I needed to do.  I've used several different Android phones and generally found that the Android OS is reliable and stable.  The phone and the user interface is also visually appealing.  Simply put, the phone and the OS are beautiful.HTC is known for adding its own modifications to the internal OS on all of its phones, and this one is no exception.  HTC has modified Android on this phone to make it better looking and in some cases easier to use.  However, those modifications may also have introduced problems, as I'll explain, below.There also seem to be some serious build quality issues at HTC.  The first phone that I got experienced an intermittent problem that caused the voice recognition feature to never work the first time.  If more than 30 seconds passed and I tried to use it, it would be wrong the first time, no matter what I said.  This was a minor issue, but there's really no reason why it should have occurred on one phone and not on another.  I got a replacment phone, and the voice recognition now works, but it takes forever (up to 20 seconds after I stop talking) to work at times.  There are a ton of posts on the internet about voice dialing problems on this phone, and so I'm not the only one complaining.Voice dialing is a major issue with this phone because the phone lacks any tactile keys.  When you're driving and you want to make a call, you can dial on a phone with a regular keypad by touch.  Since this phone has no keys, you either have to look at the keypad, or you have to use voice dialing.  Voice dialing on other phones (including the Samsung Moment and even my very old Motorola RAZR) can work very, very well.  Unfortunately, on this phone, it just doesn't.HTC also makes the Google Nexus One, and it too has had a mixed reception on quality issues.Even worse, my first Hero also had repeated crashes of software that should have worked fine, including the application that you use to program the phone with your phone # and MSID.  These are basic phone functions, and they really shouldn't crash.My second phone continues to have application crashes for apps that I know should work fine, and do work fine on other phones.  For example, today, the telephone dialer application crashed.  The telephone dialer application is the application that gives you a dialpad so you can use the phone.  It's a basic application, and shouldn't EVER crash.  Yet, on the HTC Hero it crashed for me today.I suspect that HTC's modifications to Android are responsible, as the problems have occurred on two different HTC Hero phones, and I've found that other Android phones are very reliable.While HTC's modifications make the Android OS visually appealing, they also replace text based labels which are easy to understand with often confusing icons.  HTC's modifications also make the phone take about 30 seconds longer to boot-up.  There is simply no reason why HTC needed to do this to its customers.  Honestly, I'd rather they at least give me the option to disable their enhancements...(Update:  Apparently, you can disable at least SOME of them: Go to the Home Screen, Press MENU button, Press Settings, Press Applications, Press Manage Applications, wait for the OS to compute application usage, Scroll down the list until you see HTC Sense and select it to go to the Application Info page, Press the Clear Defaults button, Press the HOME button. You will be prompted to select which app to compete the action with. Select Home and chose to make this the default action.  If you want SenseUI back, follow the same steps, but instead of selecting "HTC Sense" from the applications list, select the application called "Home" (not the HOME button), and then clear the defaults.)The processor may also be a bit slow.  I've noticed on several occasions that the phone seemed to miss the fact that I pushed on certain buttons.  For example, in order to answer calls on an HTC modified phone, you have to swipe your finger down the screen.  On several occasions, I've actually missed calls because the phone didn't register my swipe until the call went to voicemail.Why not just use the hard buttons?  Good question!  The layout of the call and answer buttons makes them very hard to use for someone with medium to large size hands, so its difficult to push one of them without also pushing one of the other nearby buttons.  The speakerphone volume is also a bit low, making it almost useless when you're in a car.Also, if you have a bluetooth headset and you're used to using the button on it to activate voice dialing, you're going to be disappointed.  For some reason, HTC didn't properly implement that feature.  So, if you push the button on your bluetooth headset or speakerphone, nothing happens.  Again, this is a basic feature built into most phones nowadays, and it surprises me that HTC didn't implement it on their flagship Android phone.I've also used a Motorola Cliq (which also runs Android) and the Samsung Moment and found them to be quite reliable.  The Moment definitely has a better screen, is a little larger than the Hero, and has a slide-out keyboard.  Given my experience thus far, I think that I like the Moment better.  Although it's a bit larger and I don't really care about a slide out keyboard, I can't stand the apps crashing on the HTC Hero..

I've had the Hero for about a year now and I couldn't be happier.  Aside from a few minor glitches that were easily resolved bt Sprint customer service, this is a great machine.  I highly recommend it.

I have had my Droid since Day 1 on launch day and have been looking for the perfect case the entire time.  I had the black silicone snap-on case from Verizon and liked it initially but fell out of love for several reasons.  I finally stumbled on the Seidio Innocase Surface and it is PERFECT. The cutouts for volume, camera, power, microUSB port, headphone jack, mic, camera lens, and speaker are spot on perfect.  My old Verizon snap-on cover covered all the buttons so it wasn't easy to always get a good feel for where the buttons were.  My old case also covered all but a 3rd of the speaker on the back, which I never could figure out why.  The Innocase reveals the entire rear speaker.  The plastic snap-on case by Seidio is coated with a soft material so that it almost feels like a rubber case.  I had Seidio cases for my old Blackberry Curve as well.I also like the top part because it's rigid enough that when I swipe the screen from side to side, the sides of the case do not flex.  My old VZW case flexed so much that it eventually felt like it was going to fall off.  The cutout for the mic is also done very nicely and I hope it improves the audio quality as I had problems sounding muffled with the VZW case.  The entire case is also very easy to install and also to remove.  I nearly bought theOEM Body Glovecase but read a LOT of complaints about how difficult it was to remove and how it added significant bulk.The Seidio Innocase Surface case for the Motorola Droid is absolute perfection.  You can really tell that a lot of thought went into the design.  It is also very slim and adds only the tiniest amount of extra bulk.  If you wish you could keep your Droid naked, but don't want to risk it, this is your best solution.  It's not a mil spec Otterbox case, but who among us really need that level of protection?  Go buy this today, in two colors, if you can find it in stock.

reviewText: When I recently purchased my Droid, I quickly found out how case-unfriendly it was.  I started my case hunt with the Body Glove hard rubberized case.  It caused a little too much resistance when sliding open the keyboard and it was very hard to remove the case if I needed to access the micro-SD card, pop out the battery to reset my phone, or place the Droid in a dock or cradle.  My next attempt was the snap-on silicone case offered at the Verizon store.  That case completely blocked my keyboard from sliding open.  I searched the web for suggestions and all signs pointed to the Seidio Innocase Surface.  I saw that the case had great reviews on Amazon and decided to give it a shot.  Boy, I'm glad I did.  The cover snaps on and off very easily.  There is no resistance at all when sliding open the phone.  Both pieces feel very secure and the case adds virtually no bulk to the phone (the Body Glove adds significantly more bulk, but does feel as if it would offer better protection in the event of drops).  The texture has a very smooth rubbery feel and is a bit slippery.  It's stylish but definitely not for the butter-fingered.  The Innocase also easily shows smudges if your fingers are moist or oily, but they rub right off.  I read the reports of top pieces popping off for some users.  I have not experienced this problem and it doesn't appear imminent.  My case seems very well made.  Seidio offers accessories, such as car windshield mounts and desktop cradles, that work with the Droid in the Innocase. This is definitely the best case out of the few I've tried.
summary: Best case available for the Droid

reviewText: The case is a perfect fit on the phone. I seem to do things that would mess up most phones but this case is a big help to protect the phone. This is a good case for the Motorola Droid, but it is not perfect.  On the plus side, this is the slimmest hard case on the market for the Droid.  It offers good protection from normal wear and tear, but I have not tried dropping the phone onto concrete to see if the case offers serious protection.  All the controls are accessible through the case and I do not have any problem with the keyboard like some people are reporting (maybe depends on the size of your fingers or how you hold the phone).On the minus side, the case does make the phone noticeably thicker and bulkier.  I used my phone naked for a month before buying the case and the phone does feel much bigger with the case on.  On the other hand, the case is comfortable in my hands and easier to hold securely than with no case.  Typing on the keyboard is probably easier than with no case because of the additional grip.Also, you cannot use the Motorola desk cradle or car cradle with this case on.  Seidio makes their own cradles that work with this case, but theirs are more expensive than Motorola's (much more expensive for the car cradle).  You can remove the case to put the phone in one of the Motorola cradles, but the case is not designed for frequent removal and I'm guessing that it will break if you do this very often.  Note that you do need to remove the case (at least the back piece) if you need to change the battery or SD card.I wouldn't pay the original $25 for this case, but now that the price has dropped to $15, it may be worth trying if you're thinking about a hard case.Otterbox also makes a quality hard case for the Motorola Droid.  It is reportedly sturdier, but also even bigger and bulkier.  If you use your phone a lot in dirty or dusty conditions, the Otter case has gaskets covering all the phones buttons (though it is not waterproof).

reviewText: Ok...so I bought a Droid a few weeks ago.  I also purchased a Verizon snap on case with a holster.  The verizon casing and holster are well made but more bulky.  It was also difficult for me to place my Droid into the Verizon holster because it has to slide in exactly straight or else you won't get it in there.  I usually had to use two hands to place the phone back into the holster.  It kind of defeats the purpose of a holster if you need to use two hands.  The Verizon model was easy to take out of the holster,  just hard to put back in.  When I received the Seidio and took it out of the packaging it seemed cheaply made to me compared to the Verizon model.  I chose to put the Seidio on anyway and try it out. The Seidio case had received many excellent reviews so I definitely wanted to give it a try.  Here is what I found.The Seidio case & holster is much sleeker and attractive than the Verizon model.  The verizon model is thicker and heavier than the Seidio.  The Seidio holster is a one handed operation which I LOVE!  I can put the phone in and take the phone out of the holster without a problem.  The casing itself feels great in my hands compared to the rough and edgy Verizon model. This case also has a larger opening for the speaker on the back of the phone.  Why Verizon's model is cut smaller, I cannot comprehend so Seidio wins on that  fact too.  The design of this case is terrific.  It is more costly than most of the cases on Amazon but I don't think you will find a nicer looking and more well designed model than the Seidio.  Now if Amazon only carried Seidio's Innocase Car Kit.....  I would be set to go!

Apparently, either Seidio dropped the ball, or Motorola changed the dimensions of the phone after Seidio created it, but whatever the root cause, the front half of the case won't stay attached. Browsing some of the forums, I see similar complaints. In theory, very nice, but the one I got just doesn't fit, and is being returned.

I really love this case. I bought it from Verizon with my discount for around the same price here. I like how you snap the case together and you can use it as a standalone without the holster and also just slide it into the holster if you want to use it. I just had one issue with this thing. When using the small face cover it has the raised edges at the bottom the length of the back and search touch keys. I usually push those with my thumb holding it with one hand while in calls to look for something or just out of habit. It is awkward with the raised edges to do this. I see Verizon has one cover that has a flat edge I just wish it came with the same quality as the Seido Case.

I tried an unnamed competitor's brand and had to return it - it was that bad. The Seidio Innocase on the other hand is perfect! Fits great and does not add much bulk. I got 2, a black one for me and a purple one for my wife.The small clasps on the top part of the unit snapped off the other day. I've had the case for about a year now and it is plastic so I guess you could expect this. I liked it so much though, I just ordered another one. The good news is that my wife's is still going strong.
summary: Hands Down BEST Case for the Droid

reviewText: Worked well for me. Provided enough protection for me at the time.Like the soft touch material gives a nice sure grip.

Case was a real bear to get the front cover on.  However it didn't stay on.I have read that some of the earlier cases had a "Fitting" problem that was resolved in later manufactured cases.  I sent an email to Seidio and they sent me a link to a webform to fill out and upload a scan of the sales receipt.  They have put a replacement case in the mail and hopefully this one will stay on the phone.The case itself is very nice.  Fits very snugly and appears to almost be a part of the phone until you look closely. Compared to other droid cases it has a much snugger fit.  I did alot of research before ordering this case.  It was by far the highest rated, with the only complaints being with the front covers of some not staying on (like in my case).  It would have been nice if they could have tracked down the bad cases and had them returned to Seidio so customers would not have to go through this hassal.Assuming the case stays on as it is designed to when I get my replacement I would upgrade this review to 4 1/2 stars..  The cut outs are all well placed for the buttons and openings on the phone for earphones and charger connection.One bonus it seems, is that a naked droid appears to have problems coming off of silent mode when the volume rocker is accidently depressed while moving around in your pocket.  I have read complaints about this in the Droid forums.However, I have not had this issue, as I have kept the back case on my phone and it appears to offer protoection from the volume rocker accientaly being depressed while in your pocket.  The case creates a recessed area where each button is.I would recommend this case to anyone with a Droid with the caustion that they hang on to their receipt in the event they get one of the earlier manufactured cases with the front covers that won't stay on.You can avoid this problem by buying directly from the Seidio website, but it will cost you a little more in price.
summary: Waiting on a replacement case from Seidio

reviewText: At first I was very pleased with this product.  It fit my Motorola DROID snugly and works wonderfully with the other SEIDIO products like their docking station and car dock.Less than three months later, however, two of the tabs that hold the cover in place have completely worn down and disappeared.  The top cover will no longer stay in place by itself.  The good news is that SEIDIO offers a 180 day warranty.  The bad news is that upon requesting a replacement, I had to wait 3 business days for a response to my request.  I then have to mail the defective part back to them and then "allow 1-2 weeks for processing" after which they will mail the replacement.  That means at least two weeks without a cover for my phone.  And this for an item I ordered directly from SEIDIO.  What I'm most concerned about is that, if this is the design of this item, I imagine it will suffer the same problem repeatedly, needing to be replaced every three months.  While I use my phone frequently, I am gentle with it and the cover has not been removed since I originally put it on, so there has not been excessive wear and tear.A previous item of theirs (the docking station) I ordered from a separate vendor originally arrived defective.  I requested an RMA from them and was over a week into the process before they told me they could not replace it because I bought it from an outside vendor.  I had to go through that vendor because it was defective within 10 days of the purchase.  That vendor was not Amazon, but I mention it here so that people can be aware of the customer service they can expect should something go wrong with any of SEIDIO's products.
summary: Durability in Question and Seidio Customer Service is Mediocre

reviewText: This is a fairly nice case.  Unfortunately it only lasted about 3 months until the little tabs the hold the front cover on broke off.  I'm not sure how I'm supposed to give it more than one star since it didn't last long enough to be any better than the $5 cases you can get here.  Sadly I think that the biggest weakness of all of the cases for the phones that slide open to reveal the keyboard is that they are two piece and I can't see a way to make them more durable.  Seems like it would be better to just avoid phones with slide out keyboards.I don't see a point in asking for my money back since it's just a phone case and the hassle of sending it back isn't worth it.  I just won't buy another case from Seidio since they only sell high-priced cases.

I have been reading on the reviews that some people were unfortunate enough to receive front face plates that did not fit the droid properly.  Unless you were shipped a defective product, there is no reason to give this case anything less than a 5.  It literally is the perfect case for the Droid.It's thin, but just thick enough that on a bad fall it really will protect the corners.  It will definitely protect the droid from scratches, and the battery cover from popping off / getting moisture in it.Because of the nature of the Droid (being a slide phone and all) it will not offer the same protection as a case designed for a solid body phone...  But so what, the keyboard on the droid is worth it.This paired with the "High Quality Screen Protector Film Guard for Verizon Motorola Droid A855" is perfect to protect your new phone.I say this after having tried out Verizon's see through plastic "snap-on hardcover" case for the droid which by comparison is much bulkier and cheaper looking.

Bought the extended battery, and the innocase front and back for the extended battery to use on my moto droid.The battery, in less than 90 days has come apart.The case back is ok.The case front pops off whenever it feels like it and is useless at this point. All within a matter of a few months.Seidio will replace their garbage with new garbage, after going through a dog and pony show and giving you 7 days to respond to their RMA which they send via email. 7 days from when they sent the email, which means if you don't get it due to spam filtering or other issues,  you're screwed.A defect like a battery coming apart and a case wearing out because the tabs are not good enough should be covered by a refund more than just 14 days. They know it's crap.There are other covers that are on the market that are made better, fit cleaner and stay on. Seidio is overpriced foreign crap pushing their sweatshop products into the American market just like every other 3rd world country is doing right now. Just because they have a website doesn't mean their a good company.Like crap, buy Seidio.

I'm a case freak, I get a case for everything I possibly can.  Some case are great, some so-so and some are worthless.  This case is amazing.  First and formost it is a PERFECT fit for the Moto Droid.  Even the slide down keyboard works with no hangups (a lot of Droid cases hang up at first until they get "broken"in).  The case has ample room around buttons and plugs and has NO slop around the edges.  I love the feel of this case- it is exactly like the feel of the back of the droid.  Grippy with out feeling tacky.  My Droid still slips in and out of the holster with ease, but I never feel like I'm going to drop it when pulling it out.  There are 4 Droid owners in my family and we all have different cases- but mine is by far the nicest, and the other 3 owners are looking for an excuse to break their current case so they can get this one (funny thing is that mine was NOT the most expensive case!)  I have dropped my Droid twice (from hip high onto tile floor) with no ill effects.  If your looking for the BEST Moto Droid case out there- Look No Further

reviewText: I bought this case and was very happy with the way it fit and the protection that it offered.  You know sooner or later you are going to drop your cell phone.  It is heartbreaking to see physical damage that could have easily been prevented.The case fits well, looks nice, and does not add bulk to the phone.The Problems:I use my Motorola Car Dock all the time. I have found the horizontal on screen keyboard more user friendly anyway.My Conclusion:Buy the cover and only use the front if you find yourself in the same situation as I do.  It is much better to protect the front screen then not have any protection.

I have had my Droid since Day 1 on launch day and have been looking for the perfect case the entire time.  I had the black silicone snap-on case from Verizon and liked it initially but fell out of love for several reasons.  I finally stumbled on the Seidio Innocase Surface and it is PERFECT.  Forget everything else, this is THE case to own for the Motorola Droid.PROS:- Perfect fit (no gaps)- Easy to install AND to remove- Provides extra grip around the Droid- Perfect cutouts- Durable plastic material w/soft coating- Does not pick up lint- Easy to place Droid in and out of holster- Belt clip allows 7 angles of adjustmentCONS:- Price- AvailabilityThe best part of the Seidio Innocase is the perfect fit and solid build.  The cutouts for volume, camera, power, microUSB port, headphone jack, mic, camera lens, and speaker are spot on perfect.  My old Verizon snap-on cover covered all the buttons so it wasn't easy to always get a good feel for where the buttons were.  My old case also covered all but a 3rd of the speaker on the back, which I never could figure out why.  The Innocase reveals the entire rear speaker.  The plastic snap-on case by Seidio is coated with a soft material so that it almost feels like a rubber case.  I had Seidio cases for my old Blackberry Curve as well.I also like the top part because it's rigid enough that when I swipe the screen from side to side, the sides of the case do not flex.  My old VZW case flexed so much that it felt like it would eventually come off.  The cutout for the mic is also done very nicely and I hope it improves the audio quality as I had problems sounding muffled with the VZW case.  The entire case is also very easy to install and also to remove.  I nearly bought theOEM Body Glovecase but read a LOT of complaints about how difficult it was to remove and how it added significant bulk.The holster is great to have because you can choose to use the Seidio case without it and just throw the phone in your pocket or use the holster on your belt with the case still on.  It's nice for when you need to dress a little nicer and don't want to have a bulge in your pocket.  The spring clip makes it super easy to place the Droid in and out of the holster and the screen faces in to protect it.  The inner portion of the holster has a soft felt material to protect it from scratches.  I myself have an InvisibleSHIELD screen protector on so I'm fine either way.  The Seidio case fits around the InvisibleSHIELD without any issues.The Seidio Innocase Surface case for the Motorola Droid is absolute perfection.  You can really tell that a lot of thought went into the design.  It is also very slim and adds only the tiniest amount of extra bulk.  If you wish you could keep your Droid naked, but don't want to risk it, this is your best solution.  It's not a mil spec Otterbox case, but who among us really need that level of protection?  Go buy this today, in two colors, if you can find it in stock and can afford it.
summary: STOP!  This Is The Case You Want For Your Droid!

reviewText: This case and holster rock!  The fit for our Droids are perfect.  The texture is soft to the touch and gives a good amount of "traction" so as not to make the phone slippery.  No rattle, no slop, and no tendency to pop off on it's own like some do.  There is no restriction to opening and closing the keyboard like some other cases have stated in their reviews.  The only down side is if you already have or are going to purchase the Droid docking station for home or car, you will have to remove this cover first in order to use them.  You will be much better off purchasing those items directly from Seidio as we did.  Seidio supplies an adapter with their docking stations so you can use them with or without the case attached.  Their accessories are just as well made as their covers and holsters.  The holster suited me perfectly too.  I used something similar on my Moto Razor for several years, so this feels natural and is much easier to grab and replace compared to a pouch.  We also put Screenguardz on both of our Droids, so now they are protected 360 degrees.  I highly recommend these items over the ones sold in the Verizon store.

reviewText: I purchased this case for my motorola droid and have to say this is by far the best case I have ever had. It does an excellent job protecting from everyday elements plus. I even had my case tested by holstering it in the combo holster and wearing it externally while riding an ATV. It endured mud splatter, branches and shock from the uneven terrain. Stupid, yeas but after having it a month I have witnessed the durability, and reliability this quality product has to offer. I would never have done this ever before. The only issues I have is when typing and hitting the top keys it is cramped but I have big hands and finger. Also after 2 weeks I noticed the flat coating giving the rubber-like feel has started rubbing off the edges showing a glossy black, not a big deal to me still as long as it still offers the protection. It does not have any extra friction while sliding to expose the keyboard; I was apprehensive of this when buying so if your thinking the same don't worry.Update 12/2010This case seemed nice but I have gone through a second warranty case. It seems the little tabs to hold the case on the phone are too brittle. As this being my replacement case and not used rough as all; it still managed to fail. It a great idea for a slim case but they need to reinforce the tabs!

reviewText: This is an awesome case and holster for the Droid.  We have one for both my husband and my phone and no problems with either one.  Great product.

I purchased this combination in April 2010 when I ordered my Droid. Now that I have had it for some time, I would like to make a couple of remarks.First, the holster: It is great, holding the phone securely and with easy accessibility. I am more than pleased with the holster, and would recommend it highly.Second, the cover: Not so great. The finish has worn off around the edges with use, giving it an appearance that is not so appealing. Worse, the tabs that hold the cover in place have not held up.  First, one of the tabs that holds the front (screen) cover in place broke. That wasn't too bad as the remaining three still held the cover in place securely enough.  Recently, two of the tabs on the back (battery side) cover broke off. These happened to be on the same side of the cover so it will not stay on unless I hold it in place while using it. The only way to hold it on now would be for me to use some form of double-sided tape, but that would make it non-removable which makes it a non-viable option.I contacted Seidio, and found that their warranty on this item only lasts for six months. Unfortunately, that time has passed. I then asked about getting an out-of-warranty replacement. The answer was that I would have to purchase another one. If I did so from their web site or by phone, it would be at list price ($29.95) minus 20%, but shipping would be free. I looked on Amazon, and found that it is listed for less and qualified for SuperSaver shipping which brought it in at about a 32% discount. That extra 12% makes the purchase from Amazon a little less painful, but it would seem that Seidio should offer a greater (like about 50-60%) discount for those replacing a product previously purchased.I had also purchased the desktop charging cradle from Seidio and need a cover that will work with this cradle. I know the Seidio cover will work. I am not so sure about other brands of covers as they may be too thick or have protrusions that would interfere with the phone sitting in the cradle properly. I should be able to answer that shortly as I have placed an order for a new cover from Seidio, one from BodyGlove, and one unbranded cover. Both the second and third choices were significantly less expensive than the Seidio cover. I am confident that both will work with the holster. The cradle is the issue. I will know when they arrive and I test them.The bottom line:  The holster is great, and I would definitely recommend it as it is both functional and durable. The cover is one I would recommend with caveats: Be very careful with it so the tabs do not break off and be prepared for the finish to wear. If you drop it, the tabs are likely to break, but it will help to protect your phone. Since Motorola and Seidio are the only ones that make a charging cradle and only Seidio's will work with a cover (theirs confirmed, others unknown), Seidio's products seem to be the better choice. Just expect that you will probably be replacing the cover and that replacements are only a little less expensive than the new products. Since these are specialized and limited production items, perhaps I should not have been surprised. However, my experience is your gain since you now have more information than I had when I purchased them.Edit November 20, 2011:Well, the second cover from Seidio recently lost one of the back tabs. The Body Glove model is too thick, and the unbranded one had protrusions which kept it from working with the Seidio stand. However, a little work with a couple of tools to file the protrusion down and then a little paint to cover the white plastic (Seidio's is clear), and I have a working cover that will slide into the cradle, albeit a bit tightly. The tabs are a bit thicker and should hold up better. They don't seem to interfere with the top sliding open, so it is good there too.The problem with the Innocase is that the tabs are just too thin. The sliding top rubs on them and eventually wears them down so they are just too thin to hold on. I can see the wear on the one that did not snap off yet. It too would shortly have worn down enough to snap off too. It is a problem that is inevitable. If it is made thin enough to not interfere, it wears down quickly. If the cases were significantly less expensive, then it would not be so much of a deal. However, Seidio still sells these for the same price. Paying about $30 every 6-8 months for a new case is unacceptable. I like the case, but it just is not worth their price, especially when one can find an acceptable substitute for so much less.
summary: Holster: Wonderful; Innocase Cover: Not so good

reviewText: Update: October 4, 2010 from a letter I just sent to Otterbox..Dear Otterbox:I am writing to let you know of another defect in your Defender case for the Bold 9700 by BlackBerry.Please do not send a replacement. It will be discarded and not installed.When I purchased your case, I had previously been using Zagg's Invisible Shield for my devices. I purchased the Defender both from the advertised design and as a result of word of mouth endorsements for Otterbox and your overall reputation.As much as I liked the hard core techy look of the Defender, there is also some hassle factor - dismantling to do a battery pull, blowing talc "air" on the screen at cleanings to avoid the watermark on the screen, etc.I could put up with all of this, but not with the numerous defects.First, there was the holster, then a cracked window, then the tabs on the case breaking from the pressure of the holder clips. The last straw was a repeat of the last, making the holster completely unusable.I have thrown out the latest broken case and the holster you just sent - along with all of the parts and silicone sleeves I was keeping as spares.Did it escape your attention when you designed this that cases are not supposed to be intricate systems demanding constant care, repair and other attention - that they should just protect the phone and not be given a second's thought otherwise?Also, looking over your site and other reviews about the 9700 Defender, it is obvious Otterbox cut corners in its design. For the little money you might have saved, you must have lost it in the warranty claims. In my case alone (pun intended), you have sent numerous parts free of charge including shipping - including at least 2 but maybe even as many as 3 complete replacements. There is no way you could have made any profit from your sale of this to me at this point.Unfortunately, I cannot recommend you on to others given my experience. I will in all fairness agree that Otterbox stands behind its products - but that is only half of the equation. The other half is making a product worthwhile to stand behind - and this case Otterbox failed. Since it is the only product of yours I have tried, I would be loath to try another product of yours without giving another manufacturer a chance.In this situation, I am ordering a Zagg screen shield and have dusted off my BlackBerry cheapy free holster.Sincerely,Adam LamarBurbank, CAOriginal Review:I just received my own case today, having bought the Blackberry Bold about 2 weeks ago. It is my first experience with an Otterbox product.First, The case is like nothing else I've seen. And there appears to be a significant improvement over the Defender for the Blackberry Bold 9000 Series - there is now a clear film shield that fits in place very well and very easily over the keyboard, leaving an opening for the electronic touchpad. Otterbox got rid of the film for the screen and replaced with a clear, hard polycarbonate screen that is affixed to the polycarbonate portion of the case. So NO worries about screen clarity, bubbles, etc. Once everything's together you can't even tell anything's there.The case assembled fairly quickly.Use: I like it - the buttons were all premolded out on the inner film, so it's about the same as not having the shield. The trackpad takes a bit of getting used to in the "up" direction. Otterbox accounted for this by cutting into the polycarbonate part a bit, but you can still feel something. It's not bad, but just something you have to get used to.The side buttons I find actually much easier to find and use with the extensions Otterbox made on the silicone skin - so here you have an improvement over the original blackberry.The top buttons for Lock and Standby/Mute also have silicone extensions and easy access.The only drawback I could find in the case itself is no immediate access to the battery/SIM compartment, but to create such access I think would have severely compromised the protective quality of the case. There's a program called "QuickPull" I tried that simulates a full battery pull - but it does not work on the 9700 version yet. That was my own experience, and all other reviews I read indicated the same. So hopefully, until QuickPull resolves this, you will have to get by with the soft-reset by pressing alt-shift-delete.The sound, screen resolution, etc are perfect.Holster - there is some controversy on this if you search online for reviews. Otterbox made a change from their original sleeve design to a dual-clip that the phone ratchets in and out of - so you can't really slide the phone in, you have to go in diagonally and snap in place. Also - VERY important - the screen must be facing in toward your body - not outward - they did this on purpose for another layer of protection.. Fit seems snug enough to me but I was able to deliberately pop out the phone by "accident". I can see where users of previous models would be less than pleased by the change. I prefer to wear the phone in a horizontal rather than vertical position. I'm sure this will help prevent accidental bumps that could dislodge the phone. It is so new, I'll have to wear a few days and will follow up on this page. I am not thrilled with the holster design, but it might be ok. I am going to keep my eyes open and if Otterbox ever does update the holster with their original design, I'll probably pick it up. Either way, in my own opinion this isn't bad enough to pass on the case or even the holster.Cheers,Adam LamarUpdates:1) Have worn around for about a week now. The phone has NEVER popped out of the case by accident. I personally like wearing it horizontally because of the bulk of the phone with the case, comfort, and better control taking the phone in and out. Maybe this makes a difference?2) I found a watermark does appear on the hard screen. I also ran across a video on how to get rid of it - and it works![...]

With three layers of protections, it protects the Blackberry Bold 9700... too well like a Russian gunship or a King Tiger tank.  It adds bulk to an otherwise slim Bold 9700 so you can't use the OEM swivel belt-clip pouch.  The only part not protected is the trackpad.The silicone layer provides shock absorber protection & grip but it's a magnet for dust.  All the buttons are covered while the micro USB & earphone port has a rubber flap to protect from the elements.  You can't dock the Bold 9700 to charge it since the contacts are covered up.The plastic layer is hard to open to get to the battery and the micro SDHC card.  One needs to take their time and be careful so as not to break the delicate plastic tabs. The keyboard bezel makes it hard to press the surrounding edge keys.  On the good side, it has a hard clear plastics pieces that protects the screen and the camera/flash.  The "diaper" membrane protects the keyboard.The swivel belt clip is one of the most important feature I'm looking for in case and it has the mini magnet to make the unit go on stand-by.  The problem is that this layer of protection is flawed since my armored Bold 9700  popped off & fell to the ground twice already from the belt-clip only in a week's use.  Thank god I didn't lose it.  The other 2 layers protected the unit from harm though.  It held through sprinting up a few flights of stairs though.  Latching the Bold 9700 needs getting use to since your shirt or earphone cables tend to get snag in the process.Audio comes out undistorted and doesn't affect call quality. reviewText: I got this phone as a replacement phone for my father. He had been using a Motorola V195, but it suddenly stopped working after many years of faithful service. I was looking for a simple, easy to use phone similar to the V195, because he's not tech savvy, and for him, the simpler, the better. The Nokia 2720 S40 Flip fit the bill. An added bonus is that the call quality is much clearer on the 2720. It's a straightforward flip phone, with some nice features. In fact, after setting up his phone, I liked it so much, I bought one for myself, to replace a Samsung flip phone. But the 2720 I bought for myself came from WalMart, for $31/shipped site-to-store. The phones are similar, but not identical. I'll do my best to explain the differences below:To begin with, the Amazon 2720, even though it says "US Version with Full Warranty", does NOT come with a full US warranty from Nokia. The good folks at UnlockedCellPhoneKings, who filled the Amazon order, explained to me that ALL UNLOCKED CELL PHONES void the manufacturer's warranty! They also stated that Amazon writes the headings for the ad and they have no control over what Amazon writes. In terms of the warranty that does come with the Amazon 2720 -- THEY (UnlockedCellPhoneKings) provide their OWN warranty (in this case, a 1 year warranty). And while that's better than nothing, it is not the true full US warranty that comes with the WalMart pre-paid Nokia 2720. Furthermore, the WalMart prepaid 2720 comes in a sealed package, with the actual manual that's specific to the 2720. The 2720 that I got from UCPK's came was in a generic box with a generic manual. I called UCPK's to ask why, and they explained that they buy in bulk, then put together packages after they get an order. They claimed that the phones are brand new, but there's really no way of knowing that. I would suggest that if you buy one of these phones from Amazon, rather than from WalMart, you buy it from UnlockedCellPhoneKings -- they were a pleasure to deal with, and they have a toll free number.As far as the phone itself, I prefer the one from Amazon. It has certain options (i.e. it allows you to re-configure BOTH soft key pads, rather than just the left soft key pad), and the home page (the page you see when you first open the phone) has the time in a much bigger font than the WalMart 2720. But that's basically aesthetics, and each person's preferences are going to be different. In terms of actually using the phone, they're both easy to set up and easy to use. (I had read that some people felt the volume was too low when using the speakerphone. I think the reason is that the speakerphone does not use the same volume setting as the normal mode. You have to press the up volume button while you're on the speakerphone in order to increase the volume to a more audible level.) The only real drawback I found is that these phones are fingerprint magnets. I would suggest getting some inexpensive face plate covers (front and back), since they faceplates not only provide protection to the phone, but also they cut down considerably on the fingerprints.In terms of a simple, easy to use flip phone, the 2720 does a good job, and these types of basic phones are becoming harder and harder to find.  And while I like some of the features of the Amazon 2720 better than the WalMart 2720, for the price, I'd go with the WalMart 2720 for $31/shipped to the store. The one inconvenience, as another reviewer pointed out, is the fact that there's no USB outlet or removable memory card on the 2720, so even though it takes photos, there's no simple, direct way to GET the photos from the phone to your computer. There are two possible options. 1 is to get a USB Bluetooth dongle to plug into your computer. You then pair the phone with the computer (but not as a modem) and you can transfer files from the phone to the computer, or vise versa, IF you have the right software. (Nokia has 2 free software suites -- Nokia PC Suite (which is older), and Nokia OVI Suite. Even though PC Suite is older, a lot of users seem to prefer it to the newer OVI Suite. Both are available for free download on the Nokia site.)Another option is to get a USB SIM card reader. They work like memory card readers, and range in price from around $8 to $30. I read some reviews and the cheaper ones don't seem to work all that well. The one that seemed to get the highest reviews was the: Dekart SIM Card Reader + SIM Manager 2 software. Here's the Amazon link: http://www.amazon.com/Dekart-Card-Reader-Manager-software/dp/B0045BIUGG/ref=sr_1_5?ie=UTF8&qid;=1296592924&sr;=8-5. It can also be purchased directly from the Dekart site: [...](Personally, I find the shipping costs to be ridiculous from both places, but I was unable to find this item from any other source other than Amazon or Dekart directly.)(NOTE: I have T-Mobile, and the SIM cards from the old phones worked perfectly in both the Amazon 2720 and the WalMart 2720. I simply inserted the old SIM cards, synced them with the built-in phone address book memory, and was on my way. The folks at UCPK's explained that the 2720's that they sell are designed to work fully with T-Mobile. They will still work with AT&T;, but not all of the options will be fully operational. The ones from Walmart appear to be locked into T-Mobile, but I'm not 100% sure about that.)

But I digress.DESIGN/QUALITYLet's first talk about the design. Primarily this iPhone case is to stop your phone getting scratches. It will most likely not do too much to protect it in case of a big fall, but you phone will take every day use and pocket/purse abuse a whole lot better. That said, as another reviewer mentioned it does get dirty quite easily. It cleans well with a damp cloth/clorox wipe.CAVEATSAs I mentioned before, this cover is not meant to take a whole lot of abuse. One of the major problems (and the reason I give it 4 stars) is that it does almost nothing to protect the screen. Sure, it's not meant to, but even a silicone case will come up further around the front to give it a little bit of protection, but this case almost sits flush with the screen. Another couple of millimeters would have really helped. That's really the only problem I see with it.WHY 4 STARS??- Good for the price (+)- Definitely looks awesome (+)- Feels good in the hand - subjective (+)- Doesn't protect screen at all (-)- Won't absorb shock from a fall (-)OVERALLI am pretty pleased with this, and until this (a) breaks, or (b) becomes uncleanable, I will be sticking with this cover. Due to the price, I totally recommend this product...if it gets more expensive I would keep looking!

I am a female truck driver in a predominately male profession and the only thing that I didn't like about this set it that the ear piece and around the neck pieces were very large and did not fit well. I prefer to have the over the ear piece as they are more comfortable and don't get caught in my hair. the over the head piece is comfortable enough. The noise reduction for blue Parrot is out of the park clear no I talk to even realizes I am driving usually the engine noise is coming through vary loudly.
