These screen guards arrived undamaged in a flat, business sized envelope.  When I opened the package for them, the three guards were sandwiched between the two layers of the cardboard labeling. The microfiber cleaning cloth was there also. However, contrary to the instructions on the package label, my package did not contain the squeegee for removing the bubbles. That was not a problem, as I used as a substitute one of the key-ring tabs for a store affinity program, which worked just as well.1st attempt:1st issue:  It should be labeled clearly which side of the protector is the adhesive side which should be applied to the screen. Both sides had a protective cover, which was good. One tab was labeled 1 and the other as 2. Both said to remove before applying. I first had to figure out which was the non-sticky side since nothing on the label indicated which was which.2nd issue:  Unless one has very small fingers, it is difficult to use the tiny cloth to wipe the screen without touching it.3rd issue:  As others have said, the alignment of the guard with the screen is tricky. Getting it in place while peeling the protective layer is finicky work. My first attempt wound up having dust under it, making a couple of bubbles that could not be removed. Also, by removing the outer layer of protective plastic, it made it difficult to avoid scratching the plastic of the guard.  After several attempts to reposition the first guard, and unable to avoid touching the underside while attempting to remove the dust spots, I removed it so I could try again with a new one.2nd attempt:Using the lessons I learned with the first one, I did not remove the plastic protecting the outside surface. I re-cleaned the screen and carefully positioned the second one, peeling the protective layer for the adhesive side as I went. This time, I had the alignment correct and there were no dust particles visible.After using the card to remove the remaining air bubbles, I removed the protective plastic from the outside.  I needed to work a couple of tiny bubbles from the corner which had been covered by the tab and not visible. After that, I had a clear, unscratched guard on my new Droid. I hope it will stay there and perform well.  That is, of course, something that will only be evident with time. I still have one unused guard in reserve for when the installed one finally needs replacing.
summary: Nice product, but easy to mess up installing it.

reviewText: I have had a Skinomi screen protector for the last 6 months and its scratched, dented, and faded. I was blown away that something this inexpensive would be this good compared to $10+ other brands. That POS (Skinomi) is supposed to be invincible and it easily scratched with the plastic applicator. When I installed this one it comes with a tiny piece of cardboard and it was not adequate to apply the protector. I used the hard plastic one and it did not scratch the screen at all. I would recommend using a credit card or one of those keychain cards, it will not scratch it. This screen is even more clear that any other out there. I bought this and ruined the first 2 by getting dust under them. If you get even the smallest spec of dust you will have a air bubble. So the 1st one removed any dust that was on my screen and the second I got finger prints on the sticky side. So make sure you buy a few packs of these especially for the price. Make sure you apply this by holding the sides and do not touch the sticky side. Slide the credit card as you apply the film, do not put the film on 100% then try to smooth out the film it will have air bubbles in it.P.S. I just bought 2 more packs of these today for backup.

I have tried several of these blue tooth hands free car kits/speaker kits (under $50) by several different manufacturers and all of them have been disappointing.  THIS ONE IS NO EXCEPTION.  After reading so many rave reviews, I took the chance and bought two of them at a great price.  I agree with several other posts: unit is very light and small, but feels cheap like you could easily break it.  It gets cool points for solar, which appears to keep it charged all by itself with minimal usage.  The mounts are a problem.  The slide in case with the suction cups easily loses the spongy grommets used to cushion the case between the window glass.  The clip on case used for a visor has a small clip and would not clip onto the visor of my 09 Tacoma.  After prying it open and praying it wouldn't snap off the plastic, it awkwardly sits on the visor, BUT the position of the clip does not allow you to flip the visor down and let the sun charge the unit unless you take it out and flip it over and re-insert it into the holder so the panels are out.  You then have to remember to re-insert face up before use, because the buttons and speaker would be up against the visor.  THE BIGGEST PROBLEM is the most important.  The speaker, LIKE ALL THE OTHERS sucks!  The volume is way too low.  I have tried it on the windshield and on the visor and my callers are a whisper at 65 MPH on the freeway, windows up, AC fan off, and no radio on.  City streets are no better.  This is with both units in both a pick-up truck and a small SUV.  When speaking to people, the complaint is that you sound far away and "tinny", the volume is TOO LOW on both ends with the volume on the unit at full.  This was tested with a blackberry and a motorola cell phone on BOTH speakers I bought.  Placing the unit on the visor and flipping the visor down so that it's almost at mouth level makes it a little better, but then your vision is blocked by the visor.  Completely disappointed.  I am giving up on these type of systems, they just don't have the volume and speaker capability we need.  I am assuming the only true option is a built-in vehicle system.  Maybe my next car.... VIDEO REVIEW:  [...]
summary: Don't waste your time or money!!!!

reviewText: I ordered this because I have discomfort with the usual plug-in bluetooth headset, and this one was well reviewed.  It's important to put it on the closest part of the visor to your face, because the pickup fades if you put it far away, but my listeners have said it was good sound quality, and I can hear them well.  Sometimes I have to turn the volume down because it is so loud it gets distorted, but when I turn it down, it's fine.  The controls are very easy: just press and hold the big button at the base until it beeps to turn it on (blue light flashes when on) and the same to turn it off (red light flashes).  The volume controls say "+" and "-", and there's a mute button on the side.  You put it on the visor holder to speak, and you can either put in in the window holder to charge, or swing the visor down and face the unit's solar panels toward the sun to charge (if your state doesn't allow the windshield mount, or if you have problems with thieves breaking into cars with windshield mounts).I bought a second unit for my mom because she gets confused by complicated equipment... not the I blame her, having accidentally turned off bluetooth headsets by pushing on the wrong part when they were in my ear.  She is also hard of hearing, but she has no problem hearing me when I call her on this, and I can hear her very well too (better than when she's on a regular phone, in fact).I charged it once on a cord, but since then I just put it in the sun with the solar panels up sometimes, when I think of it.  So far, no problem with the charge (it's been two months since I got the first one).  I'm so pleased, I'm considering getting it for friends whose built-in bluetooth in their vehicles is so bad, I can't hear them.
summary: Very easy to use, good speaker and microphone

reviewText: Product is easy to use and works as advertised.  It it very sensitive and will pick up wind noise.  For the price, it is a bargain.
Installs effortlessly and works fine.  I've been using two Of these for a couple of months, and solar charging is all it needs.  I've never had to plug it in for a charge.
I've only plugged this thing into the wall once. Other than that, it's been 100% solar. Works well as a speakerphone. Wish it went a little bit louder (for our car w/ a lot of road noise).

I am totally happy with this product...and I have things to compare it to, like the $75 addon bluetooth device for my truck stereo, which sucked...this thing, I opened it up, charged it for a few hours via usb and haven't worried about it once since. I touch the button when I get in my car and it works right every time. No complaints about my voice being muddy or sounding like I'm in a tin can...and the build quality of the device is nice as well.Very satisfied.

I've only used this a few times. The solar is great, I just keep it on my visor at all times. The holder for attaching to the window is a bit cheap. The visor holder is better. Sound quality is good, easy to set up with my blue tooth phone.

This bluetooth has exceeded my expectations:1) Sound quality (both transmission and reception) is near-perfect. People are surprised when I tell them I'm calling on bluetooth, because they can hear me so well!2) It never requires charging, because it's solar-powered. I keep the unit either clipped to the visor or mounted on the suction cups on the windshield and it charges itself while driving. I charged the unit just once on an electrical outlet - the first initial charge - but even that may have been unnecessary, as the instructions say that the first charge can also be on solar.Some small cons:1) The device shuts down after a few hours of no use, and needs to be powered back on.2) Sometimes the phone doesn't connect to the bluetooth, which can be fixed by simply turning off and on the phone.3) The bluetooth is so powerful that it connects to my phone even when I call from my living room and the car is parked in the garage! When this happens, turn off the bluetooth connectivity on the phone.---(I use a Droid 2 Global smartphone.)
I like the solar charging panel, I don't have to remember to charge it. on the other hand , the battery over heated and it stopped working.

PROs+ Loud speakerphone: I have no problem hearing the callers, even on the highway.  It is a lot better than the iPhone's built-in speakerphone.  Also, people I talk with say I sound crystal clear on this device.+ Solar charging: My car is parked out in the sun while I'm at work, so why not put all that sunshine to good use?  This device keeps itself charged without having to keep yet another cord in the glovebox.+ Auto-Off: If your phone moves outside of the bluetooth range (20-40 ft), it will turn itself off after 10 minutes or so.CONs- Power button: You have to hold the button for 4 seconds to turn this device on.  I wish you could just tap it quick when you hop in the car to power it up.- The range is too good: With my car parked in my attached garage, the bluetooth never disconnects when my phone is in the house. Therefore, the speakerphone never turns off.  I have to remember to manually power it down with the 4 second button press (or disable the bluetooth on my phone) when I get home.Some reviewers commented that their device doesn't charge when it is in the sun.  Basically, this device knows when it needs charged.  The battery has to be low enough before the red charging light will come on when charging via solar power.  It's kind of like your cellphone; your phone won't charge when you plug it in if it's at 100% already.UPDATE: 1 year later and this bluetooth speakerphone is still going strong.  I've never had to plug it in other than the initial charge when I first got it.  The solar charging works great.
summary: Great sound quality, practically charges itself

reviewText: I bought this car kit because I wear glasses and have a tough time getting the over-the-ear Bluetooth units to stay either inside or against my ear.  I tried 3 different headsets until I finally gave up and ordered one of these.At first glance, it appears light and flimsy, but I can't complain at all about the speaker and microphone quality.  After two weeks of daily use, nobody has complained about the way I sound to them.  The only drawback I have found is that if the radio is on, even at a low level, the microphone gets confused and will not operate properly, but that's a minor issue given all the advantages.Pairing with my Blackberry Bold was quick and easy, it was recognized and ready to use within 30 seconds.I charged this unit via USB when I first received it and have not had to charge it since, so the solar charger seems to be working well.If you have trouble with earbuds (or hate the feeling), this is a great alternative.

we have tried this device in two different cars, using two different phones. every time, the other end of the line complains of horrible noise. they can hear themselves talking more than they can hear us. i even sent my wife out in her car while connected to the device, and i called her. the noise was so bad i could barely concentrate enough to finish a thought.it's too bad, really. in the car, this thing sounds very good. it's plenty loud and clear. i especially like the solar charging feature. we have had zero issues with connecting to our phones, and it pairs up nicely every time. if only the noise cancellation actually worked in both directions, this would be a 5-star product for sure. as it is, i will probably have to return this because no one wants to talk to me when i'm using it.then again, is that really such a bad thing? ...
summary: noise / echo cancellation is nonexistant with this device

reviewText: This thing works great.  I nabbed one for only $15 on eBay. I have mine stuck to the sunroof of my CX-7 and it fits perfectly (even when I roll the sunroof back!).  I can hear every call just fine, they can all hear me.  Nice that it's always charging, no cables needed.  Very happy, sure you will be too.
Bought one and loved it and gave it to a friend in need and bought myself another one.,  Works great and good clarity and no need for charging cables - woot!

This appears to be a good concept, but It did not last long. I bought this in 1/2011 and today (7/11/11) I noticed the battery had expanded from the heat. I do live in Florida and it is extremely hot right now....but I would think that a device that is supposed to be charged by the sun would have a design to reduce the battery expanding. I have thrown this out as of today.In addition, I was informed by many people, during the time it worked, that they could not hear me. Many times I had to switch to  my mobile's speaker phone rather then use this unit. I would turn my AC down and mute my stereo while I was using this, people still complained they could not hear me.I would look to spend more money a bluetooth handsfree speaker phone.I would NOT recommend this to a friend.

My friends are ultra impressed with theirs but I'm less than thrilled. Yes, it's helped me through some tight spots, but I've had to be prepared to use it, making sure its fully charged before use. This thing drains its battery doing absolutely nothing. The times I've REALLY needed it, I've found it dead. I'm also annoyed that I can't charge my iPhone and iPad at the same time. Doesn't matter which I put I'm the "optimized" slot, only one charges when they're both plugged in. I paid $70 which was with a big discount from ZAGG directly. I wouldn't pay that again. The price drop to less than $50 would only make me consider it but I'd rather check the competition with that money than spend again on the Sparq.

If you are looking for a battery backup solution to keep your mobile devices charged while you are on the go, keep looking.  While I've had a Zagg Sparq for years, there are a couple areas where I feel that this product really falls down.The first issue is the swinging plug prongs.  In theory this is great because you can fold them in when it's not charging and keep from breaking them off.  The reality however is that this is a huge point of failure and is in fact how I broke my first Sparq.  I had unplugged it at home before throwing it in a bag and heading out of town.  When I got to my destination I discovered that one of the prongs was missing making it impossible to recharge.  I found the prong still stuck in to the power strip I had pulled it out of before leaving home.  Thankfully, I was just out of warranty on the device and Zagg sent me a new one at no charge.  The new one is still working, a year and a half later.The second issue that I think is important to point out is that this device does NOT seem to hold a charge well, and never has.  If you charge it to full and store it (indoors and at room temperature) it will bleed off power at a fairly dramatic rate (in my opinion).  Granted, you only have 4 lights to give you charge levels, but after 5-7 days I would loose 25% when it was newer, now it's down to 2-4 days that it will shed 25% just sitting on a shelf.It is nice that it can charge two devices at once, but anymore, 6,000 mAh isn't that much juice to begin with and coupled with the fact that it won't even hold the charge that long, you can definitely find better products presently that will work better to solve your portable charging issues.  Prime example, I have an uNu Enerpak Flexi that has been sitting on my shelf for almost 3 weeks and it still reports a full charge.Hope this helps!
summary: You can do better, for less

reviewText: I won this product from a web site contest, and have been using it regularly for several months. It provides a smooth, reliable charge for my HTC Amaze 4G phone, generally providing about 2.5 full charges from 20% or so.I also found during travels that this battery doubles as a charger. Just plug in, then plug in the  USB/microUSB cord and connect your phone/device. The Amaze uses an OEM 5W-1000mA chargers and takes up to 900mA during a full charge from 10%. This ZaggSPARQ works great in this regard; I've seen it provide up to 600mA of charge, more than sufficient for the phone.  I found it invaluable during air travel, working in remote offices, etc. The Zagg battery generally charges up from 80% depletion (one light lit) in a few short hours. It does seem to charge up even with a phone connecting that's sucking 300mA-600mA from it; as the phone takes less current, the ZAGGsparq charges up faster. So for travel, this doubles as a power source, and an overnight charger for a mobile device.The case is so-so quality. Not very rugged, so I carry it with a microUSB cable in aCase Logic PHDC-1 Portable Hard Drive Case. It fits very nicely, leaving room for a cable or two, and the hard shell of the Case Logic protects the battery from damage.
summary: Works great as a backup power source, and as a charger during travel

reviewText: I now have several techy items that need recharging frequently when I travel, so I have a number of these small backup battery devices. You charge them before you leave home, then if you run out of juice you can quicky keep the device going until you can get to a charging outlet. The problem is, none of these devices worked for my Kindle Fire - the battery is much larger than my backup devices could handle. And with all of the use the Kindle gets, I find I frequently have to recharge. Well, the Kindle Fire battery is rated at 1800mAh, so the 6,000 mAh Sparq is perfect. I had a hard time justifying the $99 list price (1/2 the price of the Kindle!!) but I finally found it on sale on Amazon for $44, and thats a steal. It is solid, well made, and not too heavy. I am very pleased, and highly recommend it.1 week later....2/9/12HOLD THE PHONE! After using this device several times, I have realized it does not work very well. It charges the Kindle Fire only if the Sparq is fully topped up (all four lights show, just unplugged from wall), but it drains quickly and does not completely charge a depleted Kindle battery. Worse, if its sitting on the shelf, and charge level shows 3 lights (75%), IT DOES NOT CHARGE the Kindle AT ALL.There is a possibility that mine is defective, so I have asked Zagg for an exchange ONLY IF THEY HAVE TESTED THIS WITH KINDLE FIRE. I suspect they have not tested it. Otherwise, I have asked for a refund. Hopefully someone will read this review before purchasing.2/13/12 - I have arranged for n return authorization and full refund. To be clear, this unit DOES work, it just does not work for the Kindle Fire (and maybe other large tablets too).
summary: Just what I was looking for - Charges my Kindle fire!

reviewText: If you're new to buying power banks, get this one, it was my first power bank. It's very easy to use and very reliable. You'll probably be like me though, this thing is like 400mah, and it's not enough, you'll soon be moving on to the other ones here on amazon, i currently got a 16,000mah one that can charge laptops and stuff, moving on to a 36,000mah one.

This was my second external battery, replacing a a Sharper Image product I bought at the airport.This battery is very straightforward in its use. Fold out the prongs to charge it, plug into the front to charge something. This charger allows you to charge a device while it is plugged in, so it can be used as a wall charger in a pinch. I have used both ports at the same time to charge two iPhones. It seems that you only get a 2.1A charge when one thing is plugged into the battery.The capacity of this is excellent for most users, unless you have a bunch of kids who drain their electronics at the same time. I used this on a plane trip to charge both an iPhone 4S and a Samsung Galaxy Tab 2.0, and it worked perfectly. The only reason I'm not using it now is because my wife has taken it over. She uses it during the day to charge her iPhone.My complaint with this product is the fact that to self discharges. If you leave it for several days, you will have a dead battery. Supposedly the new Zagg batteries fixed this problem. This is a big deal it you if you are using it on a hunting or camping trip.If you are able to pick one up for under $50, I would say it would be a good value. Just remember to plug it in the night before taking it on a trip.

Got mine in July 2012, RIP on my vacation Oct. 4th.  I just used it to charge my Droid 4 phone when traveling and could get a couple charges out of it.  Appears to be a short where the plug flips up and down on the ZAGGSPARQ2.0.  Will not charge or charge my devices.  Called Zagg and they are sending replacement, but require a charge card to send me a new one.  I then have 60 days to send the other one back.  I would have preferred to have just sent the item back and they send me a new one.  I do not like the idea of having to give a charge card to get a FREE warranty replacement. I like the form factor and design, but should have listened to the other reviewers and gone for another brand battery pack/charger. I asked if they will send me the new model Zaggsparq6000 that replaces the Zaggsparq2.0, but they said I would get the old model instea.  Hopefully, this one will not be a lemon.  If so, I am going to insist they give me the new model since it is clear by all the bad reviews this ZAggsparq2.0design has issues.

The specs on this are great.  However the battery drains on its own.  I've charged it completely only to find that it's drained (although not used) on its own before I even got to my destination.Look elsewhere.
summary: Looks great on paper, doesn't work in reality

reviewText: This is a fabulous battery.  It is very fast and Amazon is selling this battery for a great price.  Since this battery charges so fast, you are not kicking yourself for forgetting to plug in your phone.  Also, this battery is extremely easy to use.  To charge the battery, it has a built in plug that you just plug into the wall.  Great product, I recommend this product strongly.

I was anxious to use the ZaggSparq 2 since I travel and drag along a couple of IOS devices.  After 1 week anytime I plug in the device to try and charge my iPhone I get the error message, "This device doesn't support charging"I have to believe that version 2 is still not ready.  Maybe a version 3 will actually work.

This bluetooth headset is the best model I've used..I like:- The "stone" serves as a portable charger and carrying case.- Headset is very light and comfortable.- Appealing, aesthetic design.- Good sound performance on both sides.- Noise reduction seems to work well.Dislike?- The touchy button is accidentally pressed when putting on or adjusting headset.Overall, I think the Stone idea of a portable charger is a great innovation.  It solves two major problems I have with my other bluetooth hands-free:  battery life and loosing the tiny thing.  The Stone is a convenient place to store the headset when not in use, and extends the effective battery life quite a bit.  A long commute or short business trip no longer requires bringing the plug-in transformer.The control scheme matches the minimal design.. the face of the earpiece is sensitive to touch.  Swiping controls volume.  Pressing activates a mechanical switch.  I've found that it is hard *not* to click the switch, however, when putting the thing in your ear or adjusting the fit.  This means you will undoubtedly hang up on people occasionally when using this headset, and is the only reason I deducted one star.I was very happy with the sound performance, even though the thing sits nowhere near your mouth.  I was able to carry on conversations on busy streets where my other entry-level Jabra headset would fail to be useful.Summary:  4.5 of 5 stars.  You won't be sorry w/ this headset, but I expect perfection at this price level.

I have had a few different Jabra bluetooth models and this one just didn't make the cut.  Unless your ear is exactly the size of the earpiece, it won't sound correct, and if you are trying to adjust the headset, since the button is right at the bottom, you will either re-dial or disconnect a call.  for the few minutes that I was able to get the earpiece perfectly aligned, it did sound great until the headset shifted and then I couldn't hear anything.

Pros:1. I liked it for its looks at first sight. One of the sleekest looking Bluetooth ear devices that I've ever seen.2. Almost unnoticeable when nestled in tight, snuggling up to your ear3. Nice convenient pod for charging and carrying around, looking like a cute little black eggCons:1. Once you can get it to fit comfortably in your ear, it sounds wonderful. Unfortunately, it doesn't fit my ear and due to the placement of the invisible control buttons, every time I try to adjust it, I either disconnect the call or re-dial the last call.2. It makes me do a LOT of redialling as it keeps slipping out of place.3. Maybe I was doing something wrong but I couldn't get it to pair with my Blackberry or my iPod.4. Does not keep the charge for the 8 hours as promised. It discharges very quickly (in a couple of hours, or so it felt) especially when compared to the length of time it takes to re-charge.5. I couldn't use it on my left ear, which for me, wasn't quite right6. The art of raising or lowering the volume by sliding a finger along the headset has thus far eluded me.This device is one you'd buy for looks, but not for life.Amanda RichardsOctober 25, 2010
summary: Jabra-cadabra? Sure didn't work magic for me

reviewText: Recently, I had an opportunity to test this Jabra Stone as well asJabra EXTREME Bluetooth Headset.Jabra STONE is a beautifully designed headset with very good call quality, but certain shortcomings prevent me from recommending it.  In my opinion, Jabra EXTREME is a much better headset at less than half price.Below are the details behind my evaluation of the Jabra STONE:Pros:* Good call quality, altough callers sound slightly muffled, but it was not a big deal* My BB 8900 voice recognition works flawlessly with this headset* Light weight* Looks niceCons* The main issue for me is the proprietary charger connector on the headset itself.  The charging pod has a micro-USB connector, but the headset cannot be charged without the pod.  I usually charge headset at home on my nightstand AND, occasionally, in the car.  Forgetting to bring the charging pod every day to the car could potentially leave me without a handsfree option in the car if the headset's battery dies.  That is not acceptable to me.  For example, Jabra EXTREME and Plantronics 975 both have micro-USB on the headset, which allows me to use the same car charger to charge my BB 8900, and either of the headsets.* The second issue is the volume control.  The volume is controlled by brushing your finger up or down on the wide section of the loop.  I noticed that if I had to adjust the fit of the headset while on call I would acidentally change the volume.  This happened more than once, so I found it to be a problem.* Slightly uncomfortable fit. The headset is very light; I had it on my ear for 7+ hours without any problem.  However, the little speaker that goes into my ear canal was uncomfortable when I pressed the multifunction button (call answer/end, voice dialing, on/off) at the bottom of the loop's wider part where Jabra logo is; it pushed the speaker deeper into my ear which was unpleasant.* Very short charging cord.  The AC charging cord that came with the headset is about 1 foot long.  I charge my portables on top of my nightstand and the power strip is located under the night stand and all cords are routed behind the nightstand.  I would not be able to use the original Jabra charger with this setup.  Thankfully, Jabra uses the same micro-USB connector as my BB 8900, so I was able use the charger I already have.I do not care about how "fashionable" a bluetooth headset is, because I use them as a handsfree option in the car and not as a fashion statement.  I do care a lot about: 1. call quality, 2. ease of using controls, 3. fit comfort, and 4. ability to charge headset using standard chargers.  Jabra STONE scored very well in the first category, OK in second and third, and poor in the 4th.
summary: It's OK, but I'll use something else...

reviewText: In one sentence, if you are a heavy phone user, you won't be satisfied with its battery performance, otherwise it is generally an excellent Bluetooth headset. You should also know that this headset can only be worn on the right ear.Pros:1. This headset looks trendy and cool by itself, when worn on the ear, and when it's in its Stone charger.2. The fit to the ear is very comfortable.3. The sound quality is excellent.4. Voice-activated dialing really works, even in noisy environment.5. Pairing with your phone is automatic and quick.Cons:1. Being so compact and streamlined, your fingers need to aim pretty accurately when answering a call and adjusting sound volume.2. Battery doesn't last 8 hours straight; you need to recharge it using the Stone charger after about two hours of continuous use.So it really comes down to how many hours you use your phone in a day. I do not use my cell phone for more than two hours per day, therefore I give it five stars for all the pluses that this headset has.
summary: How many stars depends on how you use your phone!

reviewText: I primarily use the Jabra Stone Bluetooth Headset while traveling. My car has a hands free Bluetooth system in it but I do a lot of traveling with work where I'm in rental cars in various parts of the country.Positives:* A great looking, LITTLE headset with unique styling which is verydiscreet, unlike most Bluetooth headsets* The Stone serves as the headsets traveling case and charging station* The headset is very simple to detach from the stone and activatesexisting paired connections quickly* Very comfortable in the ear for long periods of time, with adjustable inear attachments for a customizable fit* The touch volume works well* This works well with PC (Skype) and Cell phone connections simultaneously* Quick charging times* Lightweight but solid construction* Great call quality on both endsNegatives:* When detaching the earpiece from the Stone it is easy to activate thecall button. It takes some getting used to to prevent this.* No USB charging cable included in a premium headset is very disappointing* DC charger cable is way too short at no more than 8 inches long!* Headset (not Stone charger) battery life is on the short sideOverall it's a Bluetooth headset that I actually like using - i.e. it doesn't make me look like an idiot with a large attachment on the side of my head like the majority of Bluetooth headsets on the market do. I can attach it to the Stone during flights and recharge for use when I touch down in another part of the country. It's been very useful and worth the price.
summary: Bluetooth without Looking Like a Dork

reviewText: I originally ordered this item from Amazon, and it arrived in a very timely manner. The problem was that it didn't work. Right out of the box, wouldn't pair with my phone, then became completely unresponsive. I contacted the manufacturer and after faxing them my receipts they promptly sent me a replacement via UPS Ground. I hate regular ground. If it takes more than 3 days to reach me, I'm unhappy. The upside, is that the replacement they sent wasn't a Jabra Stone, they sent me the newer generation of Jabra Stone2. This compensated my hurt feelings for having received a defective unit and the cheap/slow delivery method of my replacement. Right now I'm listening to Mozart on my Jabra Stone2, streaming from my Blackberry, with which the unit in question paired flawlessly. At this point in time I can't complain and am quiet satisfied. Especially since I ended up with a more expensive unit than what I paid for.

I have not used the item for too long. The speaker volume is too low, so it does not work for me. Because I did not use the item long enough, I cannot confirm the battery life. Otherwise, it's a great headset. I really like it. I wish the speaker volume were higher.

To begin, I have never had a bluetooth before. But we live in an area that has huge fines for handheld devices while driving, so I decided to give this a try. I am the type of person who tries to figure it out first before reading the directions, which sometimes backfires but this time did not. It's pretty intuitive for most people. After a few hours of charging, I decided to give it a try.The first thing to take note of about Bluetooth (that probably most users already know but for this novice I didn't) is that you can't get too far away from your actual phone, otherwise it's cuts out. So that took some getting used to. It was super fast connecting it to my Palm Pre, didn't have to use any passwords that they said I might need to. And I used this in lots of different ways: keeping in on my ear for a few hours (didn't bother me), keeping it plugged in and running to get it on when the phone rang (no problem there) and keeping my phone off of bluetooth mode to see how long it would take for it to detect the Jabra. All did not disappoint.I have some general observations:Pros: lightweight, easy to conceal, and love the portable charger that sits on your hip or thrown in your purse.Cons: doesn't fit perfectly on my ear and has no adjustments to make it tighter. It was easy to fall when I brushed my hair back over my ears, just not snug enough. This is really the only huge flaw I see in this product, thus my 4 stars. But not a reason not to buy it. Also the charger cord is less than a foot long which seems lame.I think the "stone" concept is the wave of the future in cell phones, my Palm has a stone charger and it's great to eliminate the endless cords that take over my counters. I like that this stone can also clip to your belt.All in all, a great product.
summary: Sleek Design, Easy on the Eyes

reviewText: I'd been using my prior headset for a couple of years now when I was asked to try out and review the Jabra Stone.  I'm personally a pretty moderate cell phone user.  I don't wear my headset all day just in case I get a call.  I also don't generally talk for hours at a time.  All I really want from a headset is good sound, decent looks without being overly showy, and the ability to run reliably for the amount of time I normally talk.They clearly put a tremendous amount of thought into making this headset look good.  Even the packaging is very attractive (and thankfully made to be extremely easy to open).  I was a little concerned about whether it would fit comfortably onto my ear, but once I'd played with it a little the first time to get a feel for the positioning, that wasn't a problem.  The addition of the base that you can carry around is wonderful since it extends the time between needing charges, makes it easier to find the headset in my purse, and also provides some structure so that I worry less about whether the headset might get broken rattling around in there.On the downside, I'll agree with everyone who's said that the position of the end call button is very unfortunate.  It's far too easy to accidentally tap it while absently adjusting the headset, though after doing that a couple of times I learned my lesson.  I should also add that I think that I'm in the sweet spot for Jabra's target market on this device.  Someone who wants to wear their headset for 8 hours or more a day obviously isn't going to do well with this, but I chose to assume that they're just not the market Jabra is trying to target here, rather than count that against it.

Thanks to all the other reviews...it really helped me specially in the part of trying to open the packaging...it was a lot of fun to get the puzzle solved!!! and what about the headset itself..well because it is so different than the standard headphone (no visible button) you need to practice...also fun! it is so worth it.  The stone is very light and if you wear glasses: no problem at all..amazing! It also reconnects to your phone really fast when you take it out of the base...and because all the light indicators are on the inside...nobody knows if you are using your phone or not..cool...Best ever...

I saw this headset on Jabra's website and was immediately attracted due to the physical design and the fact that you can charge it on the go.  So here goes:PROS:1. I think it fits comfortably on the ear and looks great when worn.2. It turns off when placed in the charger and turns on when removed.  Very thoughtful feature.3. More inconspicuous than other headsets.4. The lights are on the inside, and they turn on only when needed.  Again, very thoughtful.CONS:1. Too expensive.  This is perhaps the most expensive headset I've seen.  It's worth more in the $70 to $80 range, and that'spushing it.2. You can't just tap the headset to answer/end a call.  Jabra's manual states that these functions are done with a tap, butit also does describe it as a brief "press", which is what's needed.  This press tends to force the earpiece more into theear, which can be uncomfortable. So keep in mind, it's NOT a TAP.3. I had a lot of problems with increasing the volume. Lowering it was much more responsive and I used the same force and slidmy finger along the same area, and MY MAIN COMPLAINT:4. The speaker is aimed toward the side of the ear canal (in other words to the front of the device), and not to the insideof the canal.  This baffled me because a lot of the sound is actually muffled by part of the outer ear itself.  I wouldthink that Jabra would want to direct the sound INTO the canal.  This is like placing boombox speakers two inches from awall with the sound directed toward the wall.  Speakers should be place TOWARD their intended targets. Anyway, I pushedthe speaker little more to the inside of the canal and, lo and behold, the audio was excellent.  Unfortunately, the headsetpulls itself back out (normal fit), so the sound will be muffled.I actually WANTED to like this headset.  I would have kept it except it really makes me wonder why Jabra aimed the speakerlike that.  I could have certainly lived with the other CONS I listed.

This works well, just that I have small ears and I had to buy a different ear bud to make it fit correctly.  It works extremely better then my Motorola H721 or Plantronics in the car at high speed with windows down.  It doesn't have the talk time as my H721 or my Plantronics V521. I use it in the car only and use my other ones for home and office as I talk 10-12 hours a day.

I anxiously awaited my new Jabra Stone bluetooth headset because I am not a fan of driving and holding a phone in one hand.  Once I finally got the thing out of the container; which is a work of art, mind you, then I realized something terrible.  You can only wear it in your right ear!  I am a right handed person, and hold a phone to my left ear with my left hand, so that I may use my right hand for tasks such as writing, etc.  I have never worn a bluetooth in my right ear.  So when I tried to do it, it was just not going to work for me.I called my husband using it, and we spoke cell phone to cell phone, and he said he heard a lot of noise, which is one of the main selling points of this headset.  True, I was washing dishes and using my the fan over my cooktop, but it was not like I was using a vacuum cleaner or something really noisy.  He hates when I talk to him on my bluetooth and can't hang up on me fast enough.  Same problem with this Stone, unfortunately.I really think Jabra should offer this in Left Ear and Right Ear models because it really does matter.  Anyone with an eye for design would immediately love it like me, but I can't get past the ear thing to even use it. I would rather just wait to make my call until I get somewhere than to try to put it on my ear.
summary: You can only wear it in your right ear

reviewText: I wanted to list 'pros and cons' but some of these things aren't clearly one or the other, as 'it depends':Which ear: The most important thing to notice about the Stone is that you can't use it on either ear: It's a right ear device only (so far I was able to figure out). Since I hear better in my left ear, that's what I prefer to use. So only look at this if you don't want a left ear device.Fit: I was able to get a very comfortable fit, but I think that this was pure luck on my part, as I didn't get the feeling that this would be the case for everyone, as it doesn't seem very adjustable to me.Call Quality: This seems very good to me. I have used an Aliph Jawbone (though mine is about 18 months old) and this one is better both in terms of general sound and in terms of blocking out how much surrounding noise it transmitted to the other person.Battery: The battery life is fine for me, but I'm not someone who has long conversations. I like a BT headset because I get frequent calls during the day, but they aren't typically very long. My other BT headsets have done better.Buttons: I have large hands and large fingers and I find the buttons very small and annoying to operate, as I find it too easy to hit the wrong 'area' (they're not really buttons). Again, this may not be a problem for many people.Aesthetics: I find this thing attractive and the charging case it 'cool'. Does that matter? I dunno.Annoyance: The usb cable is too short, especially for a device of this cost.Would I buy it? (Mine came from the Vine program.) Probably not - it's just too expensive for what it does well.
summary: One of those love-it, hate-it kinds of things

reviewText: Well, I spent some time with this headset and I can definitely say that it is NOT for power users who run down batteries and spend hours each day using the Bluetooth headsets.  The problem is that this headset would have to spend about half the day sitting in its charger.  (I added an update with a quick battery life test.)I, on the other hand, consider myself a normal or even light cell phone user.  My usage includes one Bluetooth headset in the office that I use for meetings that total around 3-4 hours per week.  There is another headset in my truck that I only use for answering incoming calls as well as calling people using the voice-dial feature of my BlackBerry phone.  The headset in my truck is turned off 99% of the time so the batteries tend to last for weeks on end.  Rarely do I go over 900 minutes on my cell phone in any given month.Given that usage model, this headset actually works OK.  Here are the things I like about it:1) The outgoing call quality is excellent!  I've never had a headset that worked as well as this one for voice dialing while driving.  With my previous headsets, I could only effectively use the voice-dial feature when I was either stopped or idling at a constant speed.  With this headset, I can voice-dial in traffic and don't even have to turn the radio off!2) This headset only takes around 3 seconds to connect to my BlackBerry phone once it is removed from the charger.  Both my Plantronics headsets take closer to 7 seconds - and that is after holding the power button for a couple of seconds to turn them on.  This makes a big difference when answering incoming calls in the car where I typically don't wear the headset until my phone rings.3) The 'Stone' charger is a great idea for someone like me who leaves the headset in the car with no charger for weeks at a time.  I like that the headset turns itself off automatically when inserted into the charger and then turns on when removed - this gives me plenty of time to put it on my ear and answer incoming calls while driving.4) It's easy to tell if the 'Stone' charger itself needs to be charged soon.  With my Plantronics headset, it typically just dies unexpectedly during calls; so it's nice to have an indicator for when the Jabra needs to be brought into the house and recharged.5) My first thought after opening this headset was that it didn't look very comfortable; but that has not been true at all.  I wore it for 8 hours straight just to verify that it is far more comfortable than it looks.  (Fortunately for me, I like wearing the headsets on my right ear because I would be out of luck otherwise with this one.)6) I love that it connects with 2 different phones, which lets my wife and I both use the same headset when driving the truck.Even though there is plenty to like about this headset; there are some really irritating things that make me think Jabra was trying to put form before function:1) The answer button couldn't be in a worse position.  It's almost impossible to insert or remove the headset from the charger without pressing it.  It's also difficult to put the headset on my ear without pressing the answer button.2) The volume control is kind of cool, but it's also easy to hit the answer button when messing with the volume.  Unfortunately, this has caused me to hang up on callers when I just wanted to increase the volume.3) The incoming call volume doesn't go as loud as I would like in some cases - a problem I haven't had before with other BlueTooth headsets.4) Normally I don't care about product packaging - but Jabra went through some serious effort to make it hard to open so I figured I should mention it.  The packaging is complemented nicely by not containing much usable documentation:).At this point, I think the pros outweigh the cons and I'm planning on continuing to use this headset.  If, in a couple more weeks, I can't figure out how to use the headset without hitting the answer button all the time, I'll probably switch back to the Plantronics.The sad thing is Jabra would have had a serious 5-star hit for people like me if they had just made the answer button into an actual button that wasn't so easy to press by accident - but I guess that wouldn't have looked as sleek and cool...UPDATE: After a few more days of use, I've decided up upgrade this review from 3 to 4 stars.  Once I got used to putting this headset on without hitting the power button, it became a lot less irritating - and the positive features I mentioned in the original review are really nice.  (I love the quick connection time to my phone as well as the voice quality for voice dialing!)  Overall, I'd give this headset a full 5 stars if you aren't going to use it for calls lasting longer than 2 hours; otherwise, you'll have to deal with the short battery life.UPDATE #2 (4/27/2010): As I mentioned in the original review, I don't spend much time on the phone.  Today, however, I was on a call for almost 6 hours as I worked on debugging a customer issue.  I went ahead and recorded my battery life statistics from the call using my Jabra Stone headset with the newest firmware installed.Here are the results:* The call began at 9:30 using my Blackberry Bold and the Jabra Stone headset (both fully charged).* The Jabra Stone died at 10:40 and I switched over to the Plantronics Voyager 520.* My Blackberry died at 12:20 and I had to plug it in to continue.* The call ended at 3:10 and the Plantronics headset was still going strong (after 4.5 hours).This is a huge difference in continuous battery life!  The Jabra Stone is a great headset, but the battery life doesn't even compare to my Plantronics Voyager for long calls.  Personally, I hardly ever run into battery issues since most of my calls/meetings are under an hour and I really don't have that many anyway.  I suspect that if you're going to be making lots of shorter calls (and the Jabra Stone stays docked in the charger between calls), then the Jabra may actually do better in overall battery life than the Plantronics.
summary: Voice dialing while driving with the radio on!

reviewText: no no no no no no no no no. cheaply made. looks cool but functionality is useless.  couldn't use it for anything.  battery was super poor.  would never buy again.  ever. actually i returned it because  it was so bad

Pros:1) Opened packaging, and unit already fully charged2) Turned on bluetooth on my blackberry curve 8300 and it found the headset immediately3) When making calls I can hear the other caller clearly and they say they can hear me clearly too4) Small and unobtrusive unit5) Portable charging unit that fits in the palm of your hand6) Charger is a nice hard plastic and headset sits firmly in it. I don't feel worried about just tossing this unit into my backpack or my pocket and it getting ruined7) People ask me, "What is that?" It looks cool and gets noticed8) When I get an incoming call the alert is a several beep tone. It wasn't overly loud, painful or an irritating alert.Cons:1) Turned it off a few times when actually trying to adjust the volume2) Turned it on & off when just trying put hook it on my ear. Once in my ear, no indicator if it was on or off3) When I received a call on my blackberry and answered, I couldn't figure out how to switch (if possible) from holding blackberry to using this unit. Turning the unit on didn't take over the phone call. Apparently each new calling "session" I need to tell the blackberry to allow the headset to be used BEFORE attempting to take or make any calls.4) OVER $100!!! Gimme a break. For the $20-$30 range I could live with out the portable charger just fine.5) Interestingly enough, when I search Amazon for other Jabra headsets, the $20 range ones have better reviews than the $60+ range ones.
