Makes one wonder.OVERALL:This is a very good unit.It looks nice.The charger acts to protect the unit when put in your pocket by giving you more options than just leaving it on your ear.But a hefty pricetag and fumbling with controls that were only made for tiny fingers kept me from loving this at a five star rating
summary: looks cool and safe to carry with you

reviewText: The first thing you'll notice when you get this headset is the very high quality packaging it comes in.  I kid you not, it looks like the company is presenting high class jewelry to you, not some lightweight plastic earpiece.  That was quite impressive.After fumbling around trying to open this unique package, I'll get straight to the important details:CALL QUALITY:Incoming Sound: 4/5 (at first everything sound great, even with lots of traffic around, but if you're going to be talking for a while, your ear will become sensitized and you'll max out the volume pretty quick; for short calls it's a 5/5).Outgoing Sound:  4/5, it's not crystal clear, but frankly I haven't found a headset that is.  No major complaints from the people I have talked to.CONTROLS:Ok, this one is a real bugger.  When you get the headset you'll see this thing is tiny.  I mean, my pinky will have trouble not hitting two "zones" (not really buttons) at the same time.  This leads to a really annoying problem when (see above) having to adjust the volume after prolonged use:  you end up hanging up on whomever you're talking to (quite often).COMFORT:Lightweight: Check.Fits well: Check (for my ear at least).Long run comfortability: Check, no painful issues after prolonged use.CHARGER/BATTERY:I'm around the office a lot, my laptop is my life, hence the USB charging capability is a HUGE bonus.  This unit can last a few days with REAL heavy use and more than a week for regular users without recharging.  Bonus points for that.***This charger is overall quite amazing.  Plug in the headset into the base.  Plug the base into the wall.  You end up charging both.  So, once the headset runs dry, put it into the cradle/base WITHOUT having to plug in the base again into the wall, and VOILA!  You get extra talk time.OVERALL:Functionality would point you in the direction of:  you can get a similarly functional headset for about $50-75.  But if you incorporate design/style and that's important to you, I wouldn't pay more than $100 for this unit.UPDATE:I wanted to note and add to my earlier review, that eventually you will get used to fumbling around with the "touch zones"/buttons, and the whole call drop issue won't be that big of a deal overall.  I'd rate this a 5/5 overall now.

Wow. My original review is below. Then I gave this thing to my wife. In less than a week, it was malfunctioning, and now it doesn't work at all. I am very disapointed now. I've never had a review become so inaccurate, so fast. Truly disappointed. Don't buy!!!First, let me tell you a little about my cell phone use. Predominantly, my calls are less than thirty minutes, and I tend to use my phone for less than two hours a day. As such, the battery life on this is not an issue for me. I can put it in the charger overnight and then use it again the next day. Perfect!Second, it is worthwhile to note that I have used this for a couple of weeks, and I haven't had any major problems with it yet.That said, there are many reasons that I like this headset. First, the noise-cancelling seems much better than on the Plantronics headset that my significant other and I also share. When someone is speaking to me through that headset, I sometimes have a hard time hearing what is being said, but with this, we haven't had any problems yet. Second, the earpiece is actually small enough! I have had a hard time finding one that doesn't hurt my ear after a while, but I can wear this all day with no problems. Beautiful! Third, the volume feature makes the nerd in me squeal with joy every time I use it (which is pretty often, trying to turn the volume up on incoming calls). You basically slide your finger up or down the body and a sweet little series of clicks tells you whether you were successful. Fourth, unlike many others, I like the Call Answer/Power button. Careful insertion at the beginning of the day prevents any problems (it only turns off if you hold it for 3-4 seconds anyway), and answering is a snap (particularly compared to some other models that I have used).The downsides for this lovely little piece of technology? It only resides in your right ear, and the incoming volume doesn't go quite high enough. The charge in the charger doesn't last a week, but...would you really expect it to?All told, I was very pleased. Considering buying another one, so that we both have one!Grade: AHarkius

I wanted to like this thing (the Jabra Stone). Turns out this is a lemon, although a pretty lemon. The idea of a bluetooth headset that was unobtrusive was highly appealing to me since I didn't want to go for the 'connected to my phone all the time' look. I was also interested in something to permit me to talk hands-free while driving. The Jabra Stone sucks awfully while driving. It's just plain mediocre (which it should not be for the price) while relatively stationary. The microphone does not pick up your voice very well and the speaker built into it is insufficient. There is a clip for attaching the base to things, but it didn't help because I couldn't find a comfortable place to put it.The fact that you can charge the headset in the little base is an interesting feature, but it stops at the novel concept stage. It gives you the impression that the headset can go for long periods of time without a charger, when in fact the battery life is worse than most headsets on its own. Long conversation? You're screwed. Listening to music on this is pathetic. Would not buy again. Would not buy Jabra again.

The sound quality is amazing, but for me it's a tight fit, which is why i caution you that if you are a bigger built person or have big ears the Headset most like will be tight or wont fit at all. Besides that it really good at blocking the wind and cutting background noise out.
summary: Good, but not for all ears

reviewText: VERY FRUSTRATING!!! I removed the Stone from its elaborate packaging, plugged it into the base and charged for two hours until the red light indicator turned off (as instructed).  Afterward, I paired it with my new Droid, made a few test calls and could not stay connected beyond "hello" and a few words.  The earpiece kept inexplicably dropping its connection to the phone.  I kept reconnecting it and tried more calls but any attempts to maintain a pairing beyond a minute was an exercise in futility.  I then attempted to test it on a different phone, an LG ENV2, only to discover that the earpiece would only stay powered on for a few seconds before it stopped functioning altogether.  I  plugged the earpiece back into the base and tried charging it again.  After several additional hours, I tried pairing with the ENV2 again.  The earpiece still would not stay powered on for longer than a few seconds. I finally gave up.As far as design, the Stone is sleek and attractive, however, the styling is a double-edge sword.  During the brief moments it did work, I encountered difficulty getting the earpiece to position properly in my ear.  Any attempt to adjust it (as well as attempting to adjust the volume), resulted in inadvertently hitting the answer/end button, which, along with the volume slider, is located internally, just beneath the outer surface of the earpiece.  The touch sensitive controls are a cool idea in theory, but if you have to touch the earpiece for any reason, you  risk inadvertently ending your call.  The power cord for the AC adapter is also very short, (roughly 12-inches long).The included documentation (a fold-out quick-start poster) offered no help for my issues.  I checked Jabra's website and their compatibility chart indicated the Stone should be compatible with both phones I tried.  Their knowledge base articles  offered no help for my particular issue.Although I may have gotten a lemon, an Internet search revealed several people experiencing the same erratic behavior with the Stone losing its Bluetooth connection moments into a call.  I only believe I got a lemon  because the earpiece has stopped working altogether.  However, the similar issues relating to loss of pairing  does makes me wonder if some of these have a design flaw causing a short or failure to properly charge.  My new out-of-box experience with the Stone left a lot to be desired, or even accomplished.
summary: Frustrating. Couldn't get it to work

reviewText: I received my Jabra STONE as part of the Amazon Vine program, and I was excited about it, because I'm the kind of person who is self-conscious about wearing a Bluetooth headset (they seem to have become some kind of de facto status symbol). The STONE is unobtrusive, without a mic "boom" pointing toward the mouth. I like the way it looks--or rather, doesn't look.For me, though, the problem was obvious immediately: The STONE can only be used on the right ear. I have significant hearing-loss in that ear, to the point that there's no way I can use my right ear for phone conversations. In terms of writing a review, then, I had to go to plan B. I gave the STONE to my wife, who has never used a Bluetooth headset before.In short, she likes the STONE, too. It's unobtrusive, comfortable, pairs easily, sounds good, and has sufficient volume. In my calls to her while she was using the headset, I was pleasantly surprised by the clarity, especially since there is no obvious microphone pointing toward the wearer's mouth. If you're looking for a headset that really doesn't look like a headset--the STONE is an excellent choice.
summary: Nice, unobtrusive headset for the right ear ONLY

reviewText: I've owned many bluetooth headsets and this product fits my ear the best. I wear glasses all the time and have a larger than normal ears and this product is much more comfortable that many other headsets including the new Jawbone which would not fit at all.Also, the stone's design is great as I've always had ear hooks fall/break in the past, but now that this is protected by the stone. Despite some online reviews by websites, think the battery life is fine provided that you don't want to keep the headset on your ear constantly, despite its minimalist looks.The packaging was a bit over the top just like the new Jawbone but was easy to setup and use and came precharged.Am still testing out the call quality now but so far, a great product to fit my needs.
summary: coming from a former new Jawbone user

reviewText: This is my Second Bluetooth Headset. This is definitely a nice little gadget. The charging case is a great! I only have to charge it about once a week. Sound quality is OK, and I don't really notice any difference in noise cancellation from my other bluetooth device. Main drawback is that the fit is a little funky. I have small ears and it tends to shift around in my ear. This directs the sound in the wrong direction and I can't hear the person on the other end. I'm constantly fiddling with it in my ear to get the most comfortable fit and best sound direction. Not a bad device for a decent price, but should be avoided by people with small ears.Second review:I was messing around with it and rotated the ear gel 90 degrees. this directs the sound directly into the ear canal instead of bouncing it around. The fit seems more comfortable and the issue with it shifting around and losing the sound seems to be fixed. Definitely a great buy!

It's always a little disappointing when a product is SO stylish and well-packaged but has certain annoyances that make it less than a 5-star product.First, the good:- Style!  It looks great while you are wearing it, and the storage/charging pod is a nice size and fairly convenient (see below on the negatives though).- Pairing was fast.  It paired quickly and easily with my homeVtech DS6321-3 DECT 6.0 Digital Expandable Cordless Phone Systemand my cheapo Virgin Mobile Arc cell-phone.Sound quality:- On par with other high-end bluetooth headsets.  Incoming sound is clear (as long as you have the volume turned up to a reasonable amount - see below for a caveat), and outgoing sound is great as well.The bad:- Controlling the volume and other functions is a nightmare while its in your ear.  With no tactile feel to the volume control (you just slide your finger up and down the side), it's difficult to tell if you are even hitting the right place on the piece to adjust the volume while you are on a call until the next time the person on the other end speaks.  Also, the on/off/answer function is activated by pressing in on the bottom, which is also somewhat difficult to do while it is in your ear.  You'll also find yourself often hitting the non-tactile controls accidentally while adjusting the piece in your ear.  The PlantronicsDiscovery 975andDiscovery 925are much easier to control.- Putting this thing in your ear takes some practice.  It's definitely not as easy as popping the above-mentioned Plantronics models in your ear.- The storage/charging pod is cool-looking, but definitely not as convenient as the one that comes with the Plantronics Disovery models.  The pod isn't actually like a storage case... it offers little protection to the unit as a whole while in a pocket or purse.  At this price point, I'd feel much more comfortable with a nice case that doubles as a charging unit like the Discoveries have.  It's also bigger than the Discovery ones are.So, to sum up: 5 stars for style, 4 stars for sound quality, 3 stars for function = 4 star average.
summary: 5 stars for style, 4 stars for sound quality, 3 stars for function

reviewText: Everything went smoothly after I called Tech support because I could not remove the charging unit from the plastic base. There are plastic pinchers on the bottom that you pinch release it. It was unique packaging.The fit is much more comfortable than earlier bluetooth versions, using a hard plastic around the ears rather than a more flexible rubber that tends to fall off.The sound is clear although the touch on the headset for volume controls was difficult to get used to. You slid a finger up the headset. While the volume is not loud, the noise cancelling works well enough to be able to hear a voice at a lower volume most of the time. This is the biggest weakness though. If you like to hear at a louder volume than most speak on a telephone than this product is not going to work for you. Part of the problem is that the ear piece does not fit well on smaller ears. If you try to reposition, then you may accidentally click off your call as I did.I really like how it answers and ends a call. It is a slight click at the end of the handset. It is not a button but built in to the plastic so you feel it but do not see it. Very workable and looks great as long as you do not reposition the headset on your ear and accidentally touch "end the call".The charging unit stores the headset and protects it is a purse or briefcase as well as charges it while it is not on your ear. The cord for the charging unit is only about a foot long so it needs to sit on a counter with an outlet or it will sit on the floor. I thought that a little unusual but it makes sense.Only time will tell whether the product is worth the steep price.

I love the look of the new Jabra Stone.  The fit of the device definitely takes getting used to, but the REAL issue I faced with the device was keeping it connected to my Blackberry Storm 2.  I actually own two Blackberrys and had both connected to the Stone.  The fact that you can connect two devices at once was a definite plus.  The sound quality was superb, considering the microphone is nowhere near your mouth.  I wondered why Jabra would give you a charger to keep the device fresh, but quickly learned that this little gadget will only last about 2 hours on a full charge!During calls, the device would just cease to connect to my phone without warning.  I first thought it was the battery, but soon learned that was not the case.  I would have to insert the device into the charger to get it active again.  I would also have to physically connect the device back to the Blackberry instead of the device automatically connecting.  The Stone didn't seem to like my Storm 2 or BB Flip Phone.  I finally tried the connection on my wife's LG phone with similar results.  I'm not sure what to make of this device.  Maybe I got a lemon, I'm not sure.  I've have very good success with Jabra bluetooth products in the past.  This one just didn't make the grade.
summary: Would Not Stay Connected To My Blackberry

reviewText: Jaba products in general are good products until they go small, the talk time on the stone decreases, only made for one ear side only, it will cut off on you instead of beeping or notifying you first. It is not made for long talking just short time talking. Maybe it's because I have a blackberry too. Considering all of the blue tooths that I have had between 1 and 5 this one is a generous 3.

When I ordered the headset I was kind of skeptical. But I really love it. The vendor I ordered it from got it out in record time. And I have not had any problems with it. I do wish it was a bit smaller so it could fit my ear better. It sounds pretty good too. I didnt think it sounded hollow or anything.

I think this is a good electronic gadget.  Actually, it made me upgrade my phone to one that uses Bluetooth.  I was still using a cell phone that only lets you receive and make calls, and play a few games so I guess it was time to move forward technically speaking.The sound is clear, I had my daughter answer the phone at home while I was driving and it worked marvelously.  She could easily understand me and vice-versa.  After I got home I put my cell phone on the kitchen table after calling my land-line and I walked outside of the house with the Jabra Stone only.  I was surprised that I was still able to talk to my daughter from almost 100 feet away from my cell phone.  As I walked down the driveway and into the street it finally lost connection.  But, I know that at least within a few feet I don't need to always have my cell phone right with me.The Jabra Stone worked just like the directions said it would but I still kept messing it up during the learning curve.  I wish it was a little more secure around my ear and for those who like to tuck their long hair behind their ears (me) it's difficult to do that with the earpiece on.  And I have to remember to untuck my hair before putting it on or it will not go on.  But once you get the hair problem solved it's well hidden - I don't think anyone can see it while I wear it.  Also, it only works for the right ear, at least as far as I can tell so I don't know if it can be modified some way to hook on the left ear.  I tried to fit onto my left ear but couldn't figure out a way to do so.  So, if you are deaf in your right ear I would check to make sure it could be changed somehow to fit the left ear.It's small, convenient and functional.  So much easier than trying to drive and hold a phone at the same time, but I rarely drive and yak on the phone anyway since it's so dangerous.  I don't want to be distracted from driving.  But when out shopping or doing something else on foot and I'm expecting an important call it's great to have my hands free to continue shopping as I yak.The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 - kind of loose on my ear, and the charger doesn't hold a charge for very long. It's frequently plugged into the wall re-charging.  But it's great that you can hook the charger to your shirt pocket (men will like that) so you can continue to receive calls all day long.

I recently purchased a Plantronics Discovery 975 Bluetooth Headset, and I'm unhappy with its performance.  When the opportunity arose to try out the new Jabra Stone Bluetooth headset, I eagerly took it.  Despite the Stone's problems, I'm glad I did.The Jabra Stone has a unique design, resting comfortably over the ear without a boom arm.  A compact carry along stone acts as a backup charger and storage case.  Included in the package are multiple ear tips for a customized fit and a belt clip.  Features include A2DP type music transmission, connecting to 2 devices simultaneously, up to 8 hours talk to 12 days standby time, and crystal clear sound with noise blackout technology.I use my Bluetooth heavier at the office than during personal hours.  Even then, I am not constantly on the phone.  Nothing about my day would suggest I am a heavy phone user.  Even so, I can typically only make it through half the day before needing a recharge.  I get through 4-5 hours while talking an hour at most without recharging.  I don't see how 8 hours talk time is possible, however it would require using the charging case multiple times to accomplish.  The Plantronics 975 also has a portable charging case, but I don't need it to last through two consecutive days use.Controlling the volume and answering a call doesn't work smoothly.  Adjusting the volume requires lightly rubbing the finger up or down the side.  This works fairly well, but the sound is jumpy as the volume doesn't adjust smoothly.  Answering the phone requires pressing the bottom of the headset, or more accurately pushing it into the ear.  This isn't normally a problem, but occasionally can cause a little discomfort.Unlike the Plantronics 975, I can listen to music using the Jabra Stone headset and connect to two Bluetooth devices.  I don't use these features often, but it's nice to have when I want to.  Pairing to the PS3 was a simple task; however the headset will not connect with my blackberry curve while connected to the PS3.Comparing the sound between the Plantronics and the Stone, it's difficult to gauge which is superior.  The Stone tends to fit my ear better, making listening easier.  The person on the other end of the call claims to hear me a little better too.  It is possible the Stone has superior sound quality, but not significantly better than the Plantronics 975.The short talk time is a serious flaw which would prevent me from purchasing the Jabra Stone.  However, the Plantronics 975 has some big flaws too.  In spite of the short talk time, I prefer the Stone over the Plantronics 975.  If you are looking for a fashionable quality Bluetooth headset and have the opportunity to recharge throughout the day, the Jabra Stone is a good option, but there are better options available for those needing long talk times.PROS:Elegant appearanceTransmits musicGood sound qualityMultiple ear tips for a customized fitCONS:Short usage timeVolume doesn't adjust smoothly
summary: It Looks Cool: A Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme Noise Blocking Review

reviewText: I am a Bluetooth junkie.  Trust me on this.  I have purchased and reviewed 18 bluetooth headsets in the past 12 months... Not because I have money to burn, but because I'm in sales, on my phone all day and have been looking for the "perfect" bluetooth solution.  My Jabra Stone as I use it has anywhere from 8 to 16 hours talktime continuous!  Yes, I said continuous, here's the story...After buying and using headsets from Plantronics, Altec Lansing, Motorola, Samsung, Blue Ant, Jabra (BT3030 & BT8040), Jawbone (the supposed Cadillac of Bluetooth), JayBird (expensive), and a slew of other lesser know (like GoldLantern in case you think I'm exaggerating) I was stuck on the Jabra Stone because of it's low-key, minimalist design, without ever buying it.  I hesitated ever buying one because of the abysmal 2 hour talk time from the actual headset itself.  I knew it was rated for 8 hrs with the stone charging unit but that required you to remove the headset and charge for an hour or so making the headset useless for someone like me who is on the phone all the time.After being dissatisfied with other good, but not great headsets, an idea occurred to me... What if I bought 2 Jabra Stones at the same time?  This way I could use one while the other charged.  Good idea right?  Since you have to carry around the Stone charger clipped to your belt anyway, why not have it charging the second headset?Well, it works!  And it works so well I don't know why others aren't doing it.  I carry one Stone charger clipped to my belt, always charging one of two headsets, while I wear and talk on the other.  THE BATTERY NEVER DIES ON ME!!!  EVER!!!  During a day's use once I get the low battery beep from my headset, I turn it off, take the freshly charged earpiece from the Stone on my belt and put the low battery earpiece in the Stone to charge while I use the other.  On occasion I've traveled, and I take both Stone chargers with me, still rotating the earpieces.  VIOLA!!!  16 hrs talk time!!!  I've gone for 2 days without charging my earpieces with a wall charger!I know this is a lengthy review but this is how to make the Jabra Stone the ultimate bluetooth.  Notes:  I paid $45 for each Jabra Stone from an internet company.  Both were brand new.  So for a grand total of $90 I've got two Jabra Stones and NEVER HAVE A DEAD BLUETOOTH HEADSET!!!  EVER!!!  Jabra should have upped the retail price to $130 or so and included two earpieces with each Stone charger.  The reviews would have been off the charts vs. the 3 stars you see here on Amazon.PROS:- 8-16 hrs continuous talktime (really--but you have to buy 2 headsets).- Super low-key design (no geek factor with boom going across your face).- A2DP enabled, so you can listen to podcasts, internet radio, etc., albeit in mono.- Super elegant design with no flashing blue light, no buttons.- Touch volume control is awesome! (Don't listen to the other reviewers! It is elegant!)- Excellent noise-cancellation w/2 mics!- Produces great sound on the caller end of the call.CONS:- Have to have 2 earpieces to get it to perform like other headsets (talktime).- In-ear speaker sound quality is only fair at best.  (The most disappointing aspect for me.)- Single fit.  Right side only.  (No adjustments to how it fits.  It either fits or it doesn't.)SUMMARY:Buy 2 Jabra Stones and you'll have the absolute best, form and function bluetooth headset on the market!  The Jabra Stone isn't perfect, but no bluetooth is.  The low-key design and overall performance (especially with 2 earpieces) far and away make up for any of the "cons" listed above.  If you can justify buying two and using one Stone charger... the results are awesome!
summary: HOW TO: Jabra Stone Headset 16 Hrs. Talk-Time!!!

reviewText: The Jabra Stone is the forth Bluetooth earpiece I have owned.  I owned both the originalAliph Jawbone Noise Shield Bluetooth Headsetand its successor theAliph Jawbone II Bluetooth Headset with NoiseAssassin.  I also have owned thePlantronics Discovery 925 Bluetooth Earpiece, so I've been through my fair share of Bluetooth earpieces.  This one is a disappointment.  In some ways it performs very well.  Once I finally got it working, the call quality is very good.  I'm not sure how the microphone really works but it seems to pick up my voice well when in use.  However, there are many small quirks in the way this product performs.PROS++ Very simple setup++ Call quality is good++ Microphone is super sensitive++ The integrated charging stone works well to extend battery life throughout the day++ Bluetooth pairs quickly and reliably with several phones I triedCONS-- The functions of the unit are difficult to use:---- It is difficult to know where to put your finger to raise or lower the volume---- The way you press the unit to answer calls is also how you turn it off or on---- The "press twice to redial" feature works sporadically-- It is difficult to get a good fit:---- The unit includes 2 flanged ear gels and one ring, for 3 options, neither of which is comfortable---- The curved design is easy to over-rotate, leaving the earpiece unsecure---- There is no way to make a tight seal due to the 90 degree angle of the earpiece to the frame-- The unit is uncomfortable; discomfort seems to increase the longer I wear it-- Design works for right-ear use only; alternatives can be used in right or left ears-- Curved over-ear design may be difficult to use with thicker rimmed glasses-- There is a low static that can be heard when the unit is in your ear and its not in use-- The performance, relative to other options, does not justify the expense-- Though looks are subjective, to me this new design looks like a cross between a hearing aid and a Star Trek transponderWith the Jawbone units, there was a recurring problem with the over-ear portion frequently breaking.  Perhaps that was the motivation behind this integrated curved design.  Call quality has never been a huge problem with the other high end units I have used.  But while this unit's design might make it more durable than previous units, it makes it a lot less comfortable.  It's a trade-off I hope they can fix with the next model.CONCLUSIONThis unit was easy to pair and performed well enough that it's clear there are quality components inside.  However, the strange angle of the earpiece to the body make it nearly impossible to get a comfortable fit.  The longer you wear it, the less it may bother you.  But it never really feels comfortable.  I never could adjust to having it in my ear for long periods of time.There are a lot of earpieces at a quarter of the cost.  While most don't sound as good, most are more comfortable if not at least as uncomfortable.  I recommend you look elsewhere.
summary: The Jabra Stone - Good Call Quality, Poor Functions, Bad Fit

reviewText: This product for the price provides all the usefullness of a bluetooth device and a headphone to listen to music from the phone.
The Jabra stone2 is very nice,but the charge seems not last long when in use!Also the stone sometimes fall off your ear.The does not block all air noise when in use outside.

reviewText: If you like to leave your Bluetooth headset in your ear all day - or even when you're in the car - then the Jabra Stone is a good option. It's not "wow!" comfortable, however. There is a plastic ear bud that rests (note "rests," it is not jammed inside) your ear canal. And you can feel it. After testing this headset for a few weeks I concluded I prefer the Plantronics Discovery 975, which has a gel-earpiece that you can pop into your ear in a second or two and then remove when the call concludes.Pros of the Jabra Stone:* The case is also a charger - and it has a small, elegant form factor. Easily fits in your pocket (the Plantronics Discovery 975 also has a charger-case bit that case is huge in comparison and won't fit in your pocket - well, it will but will be bulging out).* Excellent noise-cancelling ability. I used this on the train, outside in wind and in the car. Folks I was talking to reported hearing no or little background noise and I could also hear them fine.* Nice volume control. There are no buttons. You just swoop (slide) your finger up to increase volume, and down to decrease. If you have a hard time hearing people, the Jabra Stone is a good option as it can really be cranked up to a loud volume.Cons* It's easy to accidentally call the last person you dialed if you touch the earpiece.* The case has no meter to indicate charge levels of the headset or the case (the Plantronics Discovery 975 does, but again that case is 2 times larger (at least).* If you wear glasses/sunglasses, you may have some trouble with it resting on the arm of your glasses. I did and it was annoying but not a deal-breaker.Summary: The Jabra Stone is a fantastic headset: elegant, easy to put over/into your ear (you can do it with one hand - I've used headsets that required two). The volume levels are very good and the neat control with the swoop up/down is outstanding. It cancels noise as advertised but you will "feel" the headset in your ear.
summary: Elegant, easy to use, nice volume levels and fits nicely in pocket with case

reviewerName: Nathan M. Rose "Movie Guy from FlickDirect"
reviewText: Most of the time I support anything Jabra releases and I was overly excited when I received this product. However the new Jabra Sone bluetooth headset does not meet the standards of Jabra. The earpiece is extremely hard to turn on, or put in it's charge cradle, it also does not stay on the ear too well. However, staying all this when you do finally get it working (even for a short period of time) the reception is great.

This is a beautiful piece of technology. I had little trouble pairing it with my phone and the sound quality was fine.  Don't plan on tossing the directions though because you will need them just to get the device out of the charging unit-that is once you figure out how to get it out of the packaging/display.  The entire unit is designed to be something that works well and looks fabulous ONCE YOU KNOW HOW TO OPERATE IT.  There are no visible buttons or obvious indicators for use either on the headset or the charger which makes for a really cool look but causes mucho frustration for someone new to the device.I was concerned that the microphone was way up by the ear and nowhere near my mouth but my husband said my voice came through fine on the other end.Best feature is that the charger~~ "the stone"~~ stores power wehn plugged in and then can recharge the unit one additional time without being plugged in.  Great portability feature!  Bottom line, once you learn how to operate this thing, you will be the envy of anyone who sees it
I did not like this device.

If I were rating it on just looks alone, it would be a 5 because it's a very clever design.  Overall performance rates a 4.  When I first got it; I'd go to put it on and I'd always accidentally be hitting the power button or making a call because of the location of the button and how you have to place it on your ear. With experience, I seldom do that anymore.  The volume control took getting use to also, but once I did I liked it.  The voice quality is definitely better than average. The mobile charger is awesome. The unit fits comfortably and securely on my ear.

While my husband can wear the Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with ease, it constantly falls off/out of my ear.  When looking at my husband while he is wearing it I can't see any of the speaker's metal mesh.  However, whenever I put it on, the metal mesh is very easy to see and the loop doesn't keep the device held securely to my ear.  Sound quality is good and it's a nice bonus to be able to listen to music from my iPhone (thanks to the A2DP technology) between calls.  This ability is what keeps me from downgrading this product by another star.  I simply recommend it for men or those with larger ear canals.Pros:It's attractive.The charging "stone" is small and fits easily in a pocket.A2DP technology allows for music streaming from your device.Decent sound qualityCan connect to 2 devices at the same time.Cons:While attractive, the headset is nonadjustable and uncomfortable.  (It does not fit in my ear & I'm an average sized woman.)The charger comes with a very short cord (about a foot long) that will require an extension cord for a lot of common places such as your desk top or night stand.  It does not come with any kind of adapter for the car.The buttons are annoying as I was constantly hitting the volume buttons or the make/drop calls button when simply attempting to adjust the ear piece.  This was a big problem for me because the fit was very poor and the device fell out unless constantly re-seated (which meant more accidental button pushing).The headset I received is built for the right ear only.

reviewText: I bought this bluetooth because I have small ears and always have trouble finding a bluetooth that fits.  Also, I got it because Jabra is a very good brand. I liked the fact that it goes around your ear. The problem I have with the bluetooth is that it un-syncs after a couple of calls. Even after been fully charged, the battery life is minimal at best.  I am very disappointed in this product!

This was the first bluetooth that I have tried out. And I was definitely impressed. The size and shape, was easy to attach to my ear. And soon, I forgot that I even had it on. The call quality is very clear, much easier for me to hear than from the speaker in my iPhone. The stylish look is very eye-catching. And I love how the earpiece fits into the charging dock to look like a stone.Now for the cons: The charging cord is VERY short. When pushing the on/off connection on the earpiece, it's a bit uncomfortable as it pushes into the ear canal. And the set size means that even tho it may fit easily, it doesn't stay on the ear well. Touching it too much will easily dislodge it from my ear.But, all-in-all, I love this bluetooth and will definitely recommend it!
This is very comfortable and you tend to forget you are wearing it.  I can listen to any audio I want in private. Both my husband and I love this bluetooth.

Once you manage to get this out of the box you'll find it comfortable to wear.  The packaging leaves a bit to be desired though, I had quite the struggle to get the box open.  Battery life is definitely not as great as it claims but overall not a bad headset.

This was an impulse buy, sort of. When I was buying my htc EVO phone at a Sprint store, the salesman recommended this headset to me, I agreed, and he paired it up to my phone. I returned the Stone for a refund less than 48 hours later. I couldn't get it to stay in my ear. (Note that as a result of its design there's no way to adjust the way it loops over your ear.)And every time I touched it, I inadvertently hit some concealed switch that messed up its function.Yes, it's pretty. But it's a great case of form over function, with controls that are cleverly concealed. From everyone. Including the user.I never got a chance to experience its battery life, because it kept flopping around on my ear and I couldn't bear to have it there for more than a few minutes. In the limited time it stayed put where it was supposed to be, it did seem to work OK. But the flopping around was physically irritating, like a pesky insect buzzing around your head. I nearly threw it out of the car window in disgust about the 10th time it flopped out of position. Then I remembered how much I'd paid for it, and placed it carefully in the console.If your ears are configured just right so that it will fit you, or if you are so smitten with the design that you can tolerate the hassle of poor fit, this expensive headset is for you. Me? It only took a few hours for me to develop a hate for it.

Oh Jabra. You promise so much with your fancy packaging and bold claims of "up to 8 hours talk time". But, unfortunately, you failed to deliver, right from the start.So let's begin... at the beginning!The Struggle with the Box:The box begs for your attention. A very funky looking cylinder that, unfortunately, doesn't provide an obvious way into the packaging. An obscure piece of tape removed, and you can twist the cylinder and it comes apart into two, or rather, - three pieces: The two large ends of the cylinder and a center part. An almost invisible set of instructions wraps around the plastic circumference of the center part, telling you how to take the headset and charger out of the packaging. I can't tell you how annoying I found this. With more and more manufacturers trying to push toward frustration-free packaging, Jabra takes this in a completely different direction with its plastics and squeezing of clips to get the darn headset out!Once you've battled the headset is out, you are met also by a little charging "stone" and an AC charger. The AC charger has a STANDARD micro-USB plug on the end. However, the length of the actual cable from the charger to the micro-USB plug end is only 12 inches. Yes, you read that right: 12 inches. That means if you plug this power adapter into the wall, be prepared to get on your hands and knees to plug the headset in. I can't think of any good reason why this cable is so short, except for the fact that it fits into the packaging... And no, Jabra didn't bother including the more useful detachable-cable-style AC adapter so you could plug the headset into your computer.Even MORE frustratingly, the manual included with the Stone headset is almost pointless. It's a basic set-up guide, and It tells you the full manual is available at their website. Once at at this website, you're greeted by the most obnoxious Flash-based nastiness I've ever seen. I just wanted to read useful information about the headset, not be inundated about why it would be SO COOL to own one of these. I already own it! Give me the manual already!! Oh wait, there isn't one on the site! Yes, you read that right: only go to Jabra's site to be annoyed.So, because of the annoying-as-heck box, we lose a useful manual, and many, many inches off the AC adapter cable. Not. Cool.Pairing it:Pairing it with my iPhone 3GS was very simple. Take the device out of the charger, and it immediately goes into pair mode. Load the Bluetooth menu from the phone, punch in 0000 for the passcode, and you're away.Using it:The headset fit fairly comfortably into my ear, and the touch sensor on the side of the headset to adjust the volume is very futuristic. However, for some reason I couldn't adjust the volume to absolute maximum on my 3GS. It always would show one bar below full on my iPhone, and I'd have to hit the volume-up key to put it to actual maximum. Also, perhaps because of my ear shape (which my wife tells me is normal), I still craved more volume. If I pushed the headset more into my ear, it was plenty loud, but otherwise it just doesn't have that punch I need, and that was in a quiet room. Outside on a busy street I'm sure this wouldn't be very usable, at least not for me.Adjustments to the headset on my head would result in the volume being adjust up or down because of its touch-based interface. Even MORE annoying is that to end a call or to initiate the voice dial, you have to push the headset so it clicks, and let me tell you that is NOT comfortable to be pushing the darn thing into your ear when you try to do this. You have to push pretty hard to get it to click.Talk time:Oh Jabra. "Up to 8 hours talk-time" you state. What that really means is TWO hours talk time before you have to charge it for 2 more hours. The stone charger in theory will hold enough to charge the headset three times before needing a wall. But yep, you read that right, too: If you use your headset for more than a couple of hours in one day, you'd better be remembering to charge it straight away. And because the actual headset has no connector, if you lose the "stone" or leave it in the car, you've no way to charge your headset.Call quality:Aside from the volume deficit, the call quality is very good. No real noticeable hiss, and on some test calls my recipients said they could hear me quite well.HOWEVER, when I switched to my Motorola H710 (still my BT headset of choice), the volume level became much more usable to me - loud and clear - , and people on the other end said they, too, could hear me clearer. I switched back and forth from the Jabra Stone to my Motorola H710, and each time the recipient said they preferred the Motorola. And so did I. And the Motorola gets around 6-7 hours talk time without having to plug it in...Overall, more style than substance. More than any BT headset I've ever used. In this economy, today, substance is so important, and Jabra just fails to deliver.3/5
summary: Don't believe the hype. Just a "fair" headset. At best.

reviewText: There are MANY technical features to like about this product:  2 device connectivity, stereo audio, noise cancellation, etc.But before any of that matters, comes comfort and fit.This device ONLY fit in the right ear.  I did a search on the Amazon product description, and this is not mentioned ANYWHERE!  I prefer to wear my earphone in my left ear, so this was already close to a non-starter for me.I decided to still give it a shot though.  In my right ear, I found the headset to be completely un-adjustable.  The angle, the depth it goes into my ear, etc ... all do not lead to a good fit, and the headset feels lose and moving around.I've owned a BlueAnt headset for quite some time ... and it doesn't take much adjustment to allow for a good fit.  But it does take some, and this device has zero.
summary: Zero fit adjustment.  Right ear only.

reviewText: I would say the Jabra Stone is the most stylish bluetooth headset I have ever owned.  I am a huge fan of a bluetooth headset and use it for my cell phone, for VoIP applications like Skype and for streaming audio from my notebook computer every day.  I have owned more than 5 bluetooth headsets so far and the Jabra Stone has the best look.  The transparent, cylinder style packaging case is a real eye candy and everything comes with it looks just great.  And it fits on my ear very well.  The Stone is not a adjustable headset other than replaceable ear pieces, if it does not fit, you are out of luck.  And you can only use it on a right ear.  I had no problem to pair with my Macbook Pro, my desktop with a usb bluetooth dongle and my cell phones.  The sound quality is fair and it does not give any pain to my ear after hours of usage.The great thing about the Stones is that the charging cradle works as a portable charger.  The AC adapter comes with it charges both the headset and the cradle.  So if you are out and happen to bring the charger with you, you can charge it one more time from the cradle without any power source.  This is such a brilliant idea and I absolutely loved it.  And my friends who saw the Stone were fascinated by the its gorgeous design and a neat idea of the portable charger.  The AC adapter cord is too short, though.  I mostly liked it.But, there is a major problem in the Stone to be my primary bluetooth headset.  As I stated above, I use a bluetooth headset more than several hours each day.  With a single charge, the Stone can only last for an hour and half.  And to recharge, the Stone must be placed in the cradle.  There is no port or connector on a headset to recharge.  I have a Plantronics bluetooth headset that I can use while I am charging the headset.  However, the Stone won't let me do that.  Althought I am carrying the charging cradle every day, I have to stop using the headset after approximately 90 minutes of usage and it is bad.  The product description says it has up to 8 hours of talk time and I do not believe that.So, sadly, I decided to use it as a cell phone only headset.  And there was one more problem that I had had.  The touch style volume control.  It is so cool and my kids were wowed by this.  However, I had cases that I disconnected my phone call while I was trying to adjust the volume since the on/off button can be easily pressed by swiping the surface for a volume control.  Not once, more than several times.  Now I got used to it (I mean I can touch softly not to press it) but it was a quite a headache in the first place.The Jabra Stone is so light and stylish.  It is the coolest and the most expensive headset I have ever had.  However, if Jabra does not improve the battery life of this headset to last as long as they claimed on the specification, I would stick with my old Samsung or Plantronics bluetooth headset for my daily, somewhat heavy usage.  I really wanted to use the Stone every day.
summary: It just does not last long enough for me

Hello All,This review is for the WEP870I know that I am late to this party and that this unit is all but discontinued except in Europe. Samsung has updated this to a unit with similar design, and therefore I feel my thoughts might still be relevant.I have owned two of these units, both however suffer from the same flaw , which I will cover in a moment.Pros: I liked this unit because the design is unobtrusive, no one even knows you have it until you put the unit in your ears. It is very comfortable to have around your neck and the unit produces some pretty good stereo sound. From mid-bass up everything was clear and the soundstage felt well defined. Deep bass was absent most of the time even with making sure the ear pieces were well seated. Otherwise the sound was very good , I cannot overstate that. The fit is good and it is easy to pair with all the devices that I tried it with. The display on the main unit is clear and easy to read and the battery life is outstanding, going 2 days moderate use before recharge. And the recharge time was quick, fully charged in less than an hour.Cons: Worst, First. There is a flaw in the design so that the weight of the main unit pulls on the wires of the headphones, then it stretches and seperates from the plug end and then breaks. This has happened on both units. In addition to that call quality suffered for those on the other end which complained about all sorts of interference, the calls were super clear on my end however.Also the ear piece on the main unit that you might stick in your ear,but now is hanging around your neck as a pendant, got caught often on stuff and on my first unit pulled apart, bummer.Conclution:There will never be a perfect product, and if there were it would become obsolete in short order anyway.The WEP870 (and the new units based on this design)has benefits as well as flaws. If you can find a unit for cheap, i think it would be worth it, as I said in the begining, I have purchased and daily used 2 of them.But at this point I am looking for new technology that has improved call quality, fewer foibles, with out sacraficing the fine sound quality I enjoyed these units, which continues to be a standout IMHO.Enjoy. JB
summary: Very good bt headphones with flaws

My original review of this product was pretty scathing after trying out not just one, but two of these headsets, only to find that each was defective. Both had been bought through Verizon Wireless' website (at higher prices than are offered here on Amazon, in both cases). Perhaps Verizon Wireless got a bad batch, and that's why both of those headsets had such abysmal stereo and general Bluetooth sound...... I started to type the entire ordeal out here, but, really, that's not what readers looking for reviews of the product are really interested in, so... The abbreviated version is, I had an abysmal time initially trying to get Customer Support for my defective second headset, but Lindsey Williams in Samsung's Customer Care Center for Executive Customer Relations made it right by sending out a brand-spanking new headset.And the sound is BEAUTIFUL!The design of this headset is very smart. The Bluetooth headset itself works as a traditional one does, with great sound. I DO have to toggle the sound - from the headset, to my phone, and back - to ensure a strong connection with the headset for optimal sound during calls, but once that's done, the sound is great, and I think that probably has more to do with my phone than Samsung's WEP870. The sound on this headset is perfectly clear on my side, and my callers don't have any complaints about the sound quality either. But it's really the nifty little stereo headset portion that sold me on this Samsung Bluetooth headset.The traditional earpiece-style Bluetooth headset neatly and VERY snugly nests into the cradle on the stereo headset portion (there are release buttons on the side to detach the headset from the locking mechanism). The sound is then streamed wirelessly through the Bluetooth headset and to the Left/Right earpieces. The sound quality is GREAT. It's crisp, deep, and rich. The bass comes through clearly, and with no compromise on sound (I love a good regular dose of the Dancehall Reggae that I grew up with, and that's my go-to music to test any bass. These pass the test with flying colors)! Even though I worry about the charge lasting long enough to get me through a cross-country flight on these headphones (probably not the smartest thing to have Bluetooth enabled in the air, anyway), I really enjoy the fact that, even though there IS a cord to these headphones, it's only to keep the stereo headset around your neck, lanyard-style. There are no wires connecting my headset to my phone in my pocket and getting in the way of everything else.Now that I've gotten my hands on a well-functioning Samsung WEP870, I couldn't be happier! Bumps on the road notwithstanding, these headphones get two thumbs up from me! GREAT stuff!
summary: Great sound, both mono via Bluetooth AND stereo! Just what I've been looking for!

I have been using one of these for several months and just ordered another at the current amazing price to have as a spare.  The call quality of this earpiece is amazing.  My wife was always complaining about the stock wired headset that came with my iPhone 3GS, but she says this one sounds great.  It has a couple of minor quirks that annoyed me at first until I got used to them.  In fairness, I think it is more the iPhone's interaction than an issue with the WEP870 itself, plus an element of operator error.1.  I use voice dial a lot.  When you press the earpiece to initiate voice dial there is an initial confirming beep.  Thinking this was the voice dial tone I would start speaking, and the phone would obviously not understand.  I finally realized that after the intial beep there is a slight lag before you hear the double beep to start speaking.  Issue resolved.2.  As an outgrowth of 1. I would sometimes inadvertently start music playing.  Pressing the earpiece would have no effect so I would have to take the phone out to stop the music.  After a while it occurred to me to try voice commands to control music, and it worked like a charm.I have only used the stereo attachment a couple of times, but it seems to work great.  I am very happy with the sound quality.I would like to respond to a couple of criticisms in other reviews.1.  Foam cover comes off and gets lost - This happens with ALL earbuds with the foam covers.  For years I have used a couple of dots of rubber cement to secure them.  This will keep them in place for a long time, but after a few months they still come loose.  I consider the foam covers expendable anyway and keep several replacements handy.  These used to be impossible to find, but seem more available lately though still not a stock item in stores.2.  Comfort - Initially, I sometimes found this earpiece uncomfortable.  Then I noticed that the "bud" part that actually goes in the ear is off center a bit from the "post".  This means that at some angles the bud may be applying pressure that can be uncomfortable.  By trying different angles I found more comfortable positions.  Now it is comfortable enough that I often forget it is there.  At home I sometimes put my phone down when I am changing clothes and don't realize I don't have it until I get to the other end of the house and the bluetooth beeps because it has lost connection.  Which reminds me, the range is very good.  I have not actually measured, but I would say it gets the full 33 feet.

reviewText: I have been searching for a good, portable, reliable and compact charger for my iPhone 4. The phones recognized the charger with out a single glitch; the other two iPhones were a second iPhone 4 and a 3Gs. My test charge was from 37% battery to 89% after the charge on my iPhone. This was from a fully charged charger(4 lights), and after this charge of 52% to my iPhone it left the charger with two (2) lights. This means that it still had 50% of more battery left.I will continue testing this charger, but so far the first result speaks for itself. I have purchased other chargers for my iPhone, surprisingly at double or triple the cost of this one, only to find myself very disappointed and left with a product that is unreliable and with no way of returning it to recuperate the money I wasted on them. Also, one last note, I bought it from the Amazon seller BestDealUSA at a whopping total cost of $7.47 ($6.97 charger + $0.50 shipping). I have bought a second charger from this seller and I recommend this product to anyone, like myself, who has the need of additional portable power for the iPhone when you are out and about.Update as of 8/01/11: I have purchased three more for gifts from this vendor. I have used my charger at least once a week and I can charge it and leave it alone for over one month with out having to charge it again. I am a highly satisfied user and would recommend it to anyone looking for a cheap, small and reliable charger for an iPhone.

I bought this to provide an emergency battery boost for my iPhone, in situations where I needed to keep the phone running but couldn't conveniently plug it in (like when the low-battery warning pops up when you're on a call away from home).  To be useful for this purpose, the auxiliary battery needs to hold its charge, steadfastly waiting for its opportunity to serve.  Unfortunately, this battery pack seems to lose its charge fairly quickly.  Every time I pulled it out of my briefcase to use it, it was close to dead.  Sort of like having a fire extinguisher that loses its charge after a few weeks -- not terribly useful for the emergency situations it was designed for.  After carrying this backup battery around in my briefcase for six months, and finding it dead every time I needed it, I finally retired it.  As an emergency battery backup, zero stars.The backup battery is more useful as a daily extender, if you charge it every night and use it daily to get extra battery life.  For this purpose, I'd give it three stars.Averaging across these two different uses, two stars.  Useful, but just barely.

reviewText: It's really hard to complain for this price because it's really an incredible value. I recently ordered (and returned) an iPhone 4 case with a 1700mAh battery built into it. The case was 9 times the cost of this battery and only charged my phone 10% more. That said, it does have it's drawbacks. Due to the curvature of the newer devices (iPod touch 4g and iPad 2) the battery will not fit into the 30 pin slot far enough to make a connection. The battery will light up and "think" it's plugged in, but it's not. It would not charge my son's iPod touch 4G no matter what I did. Much the same issue with the iPad 2. Just simply could not make full contact for a charge to happen.That said, it works perfectly with my iPhone 4 and original iPad due to the flat base. I let my phone die completely and plugged in the battery and it was charged to 60% in about 2 hours. I'm a little annoyed about this because it says it will charge my phone to full in 2 hours, but I think they're playing with words here because it may very well fully charge an iPhone 3G to full simply because of lower capacity. However, as I mentioned above, I paid MUCH more for a battery case that didn't charge my phone much more than this one did, which brings me to another minor complaint. The shape of the battery is rather awkward. It's almost half the size of the phone and it's not exactly comfortable to hold while the battery is plugged in. You get what you pay for though. If you want a quick boost to your battery while your phone is sitting in your bag, this will do the trick nicely. If you want to continue using your phone while it's charging, you're going to have to pay more for a battery case.The LED indicators are a nice bonus as well. I like to see how much charge time is left by noting how many of the LEDs are lit. After charging the battery, the FULL light was on, but I noticed the next day when I actually plugged it into my phone it was down to 3 bars (from 4). I definitely don't like what this indicates. If the battery drains 25% in under 24 hours with no use, I'm not sure how much I'm actually going to benefit from it. Only time will tell on that one.The size is small enough that I can drop it in my purse and forget about it until I need it. I also own the 11000mAh New Trent iCruiser which definitely has more bulk, so I have this little guy as an emergency backup. Overall, if all you need is a quick boost to your battery when you're away from a power source, this really can't be beat for the price. Just know what to expect and what not to expect and you'll be pleased with the value received.

My sister in law received one of these as a gift and she was elated.  She works long hours and is the go to answer person in her large real estate title company.  Shortly after she got it she called me and asked me to look at it and tell her what was wrong.  She had used the power pack several times and she could only charge her iPhone 4 about 50%.  She had borrowed one of my wife's larger power packs that could charge her phone 3  times.  She wanted to know why hers didn't work as well.This unit, while cute, is absolutely underpowered.  It claims to have 1900 mAh capacity but in reality that is not the real charging capacity of the device when you consider how it works.  The battery pack has internal electronics that consumes power, the connector creates a contact that inserts some resistance and the iPhone has internal electronics in the charging circuit that consumes power and also drops the voltage from 5 VDC to 3.7 VDC to charge the internal battery of the iPhone. (more power lost)  The final efficiency of the charging is somewhere around 75% of the rated capacity.  This means that 75% EQUALS ONLY 1,425 mAh capacity to charge an iPhone 4 that has a 1,420 mAh Lithium Polymer battery cell.  That means that the likely hood of getting a full charge for your iPhone is about zero.Her experience was only a little over 50% and she returned it to the store it was purchased from.  I think you can see from the number of poor reviews and the new selling price that this product has some serious performance issues.  My recommendation is to buy a better power pack!

I'll add my review to the list of people here who are happy with their Icon headset.  Here are some things that I like about it:- The sound quality of received calls is excellent.  To me, people sound better through this headset than through the speaker on my Droid X.- The voice quality is pretty good.  My parents say that they can't tell a difference between the headset and using the phone mic, but my brother can tell.  He doesn't say that it sounds bad, but just not as good.- The noise cancellation is great!  I was outside working in the yard and talking to my mom on this headset.  It got windy, but she couldn't hear it.  What sold me is that someone rode by on a loud motorcycle, I apologized for the noise, but my mom never heard the motorcycle.  That really impressed me.- Hands free.  Sure, not unique to the product at all - but this feature is why I bought it.  Being able to talk while walking around my house or yard with my phone just sitting in one spot is fantastic.- The headset stays in place really quite well once I get situated correctly.  I almost removed one star because sometimes I can't get it set right, but it might just be that I need more practice.  I don't use the earloop, and I love how I can wear this with my glasses.The earpiece does start to get uncomfortable to me after about an hour.  That's one thing that I'd change, for sure, but given all the positive things about this headset - it's definitely worth five stars to me.

Comfortable in ear and stays in place if you use the right size earpiece.  Disappointed in the small plastic ear loop deal that goes around your ear; Bluetooth only comes with one and it comes out easily (and, thus, is easy to lose... which we did).
The product is as per what is promised, except for the fit part which kind of sucks. Have trouble to get it on and keep it that way. The Jaw falls of at times and is kind of iterating.

Let me start off by saying I hate bluetooth headsets. I have owned two previously, and I always found they had poor sound, were uncomfortable, full of buttons I could never remember how to use, and never would stay in my ear. For the longest time I was much happier with a cheap wired version. However a recent upgrade to an iPhone left me pretty much out of luck with regard to wired headsets.I finally broke down and decided to try this headset, and I was pleasantly surprised. For some reason, my ears just don't seem to do well with earbud type devices, but this one is actually comfortable. It took a little effort to find the right combination of eargels (the unit ships with a few) and the earhook, but I can leave this thing in my ear for an hour or so and not feel like I am being tortured. The earhook works fine around my glasses.The sound quality is more than loud enough for my ears, although the loudest environment where I typically use a phone is the car. People on the other end of the phone calls have said the sound quality is good enough to have a conversation with, and that is really all I care about.There are two buttons. An off/on switch that has a color indicator so you know the headset is on. The second button, easily found on the back of the device, handles all the other answer/call stuff. A pleasant little voice gives you the occasional status on the amount of charge left. I much prefer this to the complicated "press the button five times in just the right sequence" to turn the unit off that other headsets seem to use. I can actually use this headset without constantly referring to the directions.Synched right up to my iPhone4.Wished I had bought a carrying case, until I discovered that an old prescription bottle makes an excellent protective case. You can even fish the charging cable through a small hole in it...works better than any case I have seen for these.The only con-the thing feels a bit flimsy, especially the earhook/earbud part. Time will tell how it holds up.

Ok to start off I couldn't wait to buy this guy online so I rushed out to Beast Buy and picked it up.  I have owned a first gen jawbone and the jawbone II as well... The jawbone II suffered ear barrel breakage... Did I mention I'm death on a headset?  Well the first 4 days with icon were bluetooth bliss... No more wind noise, no more anything... Way better noise assassin than that of the jawbone 2 or the prime.  I only compare this jawbone to other jawbones... simply because there is no other headset to compare a jawbone to... they are that good.  So alas I was shoveling snow and noticed my headset was not in my ear.  OMG it was brand new.  Well it lost connection to my phone and I started like a mad man raking through 16 inches of snow I had piled up into 3-5 foot tall hills... No luck :(  So I tried again for 3 days and it kept snowing so it was hopeless... My jawbone was in a snowy grave... I then bought another one just because they are that good.  Well today the temp was 62 degrees and all the snow melted.  Low and behold I found my fallen jawbone at the edge of my yard.  This is hopeless right?  WRONG!!!  It charged right up and paired perfectly with my wife's phone.  Now she too has a jawbone icon.. If that isn't the testament to the best bluetooth in the world you tell me what is?  I could talk about how it fits and how awesome the call quality is and the battery life, etc... but hey if you are looking here you know what you are looking at.  These bluetooth headsets are very comfortable and come with many ways to customize it.  The on of switch and sensibly placed button are improvements over recent models.  I still think a jabra mini gel ear bud is better than the included gels; but to each his own.  All I'm saying is; unless you physically break the thing; the electronics will NEVER FAIL!!!  Kudos Aliph on another stellar product.
summary: The toughest quietest bluetooth on earth... PERIOD!!!

reviewText: I own an original Jawbone that is getting a little shopworn. Since Aliph just introduced a new model, I decided to buy this one for its price point vs. performance. It fits better than th original. With several types of ear buds included, it was easy to find one that fits my ear and allows me to forgo the loop that most Bluetooth earpieces have. Sound is great and of the noise cancellation is fantastic for the people I call. I work in a truck all day and none of my friends can hear the road and engine noise that permeates the cab. It also links to 2 different phones at once. Great since I have a work phone w/push to talk, and my personal phone, a Droid.  You can hear music from your phone right in the ear piece. I paid $54 and the price has dropped since then. Good value.

Have had for a couple of months.  I bought into the possibility of having apps and updates.  Not many apps.  Only voice upgrades and some config settings you shouldn't have to go to a website to change.Fit is fair, not TOO uncomfortable (I use the in-ear option so I can wear sunglasses too).  Stays in pretty well unless your chewing.  If you like gum, don't get this ear piece, or use the over-ear option.  Would have preferred a true in-ear fit, as it really just wedges itself in the outer ear and does not go IN your ear, as I thought it might do.  The 'wedgie' you get can be a bit irratating at first.  You don't want to try and wear it in-ear style for more than a couple of hours as the 'wedgie' starts to hurt after that long.Incoming sound quality is fair, not fantastic.  A lot depends on the fit in your ear.  If not exactly tight, will be weak.As other reviewers have mentioned, no volume adjustment.  Is done with phone.  I use a Nokia XpressMusic 5800 and sound in some apps is low and suddenly gets really loud when taking calls (especially OVI maps GPS navigation where you can barely hear the turn by turn directions until you get a call and suddenly it's so loud you can't hear the person on the other end when the app gives directions).I do like the light weightness of it, buttons and the on/off switch which connects to the phone very fast, almost instantaneously.Is kind of pricey and the car charger available is really only for older Jawbones.  Will work with the Icon, but comes with an incompatible USB connector and you will have to use the USB that comes with the Icon.  The USB that comes with the Icon is really short, which in most cases is advantageous, but would have liked an additional one to keep in the car and not have to carry around.Staying power is fine.  Was concerned a bit about long trips in the car not having enough battery time and having to recharge a lot.  Not the case unless you are a non-stop talker on the phone.Overall, would have looked closer into the Plantronics Discovery 975 Bluetooth Headset having had this for a while now.
summary: Not sure what the fuss is about...it's an okay product

reviewText: I've been eyeing a jawbone since they first came out but refused to spend more than $50 on a bluetooth, which I normally lose or break.  When I saw a refurbished icon up for grabs for $35 (shipped!!!) it was a no brainer.  Given the options currently out at my time of purchase it was either $100 for the Era or this.. the Era adds another processor and an acceloramater... neither of which I need. I still get the great features like using the android app and the great customizing options from the jawbone.com site and a sleek top notch headset.I love this thing, it's very small (that's a plus and a minus), light, plenty of attachment options (ear hook or no, and about 5 or 6 different bud sizes).  The one button function is a blessing and a curse.  No complicated dials or buttons to fool with just one large easily press-able button.  Now, one feature I was looking for was a2dp which allows me to stream music over bluetooth to my headset, which the jawbone does have.  HOWEVER, because the jawbone only has one button it does not support AVRCP which allows you to play, pause, ff or rw from the headset.. I have to do all of that from the device.  No big deal really for me, but a heads up for anyone where this might be a deal breaker.The sound is a bit tinny to my ear, though I'm guessing that's because of the shape of my ear, the speaker wont point directly into my ear or something.  I have found an earplug combo that fixes this mostly though but given that I do listen to music/podcasts with this thing, I have to admit this will not be a replacement for my dedicated headphones.  I've had other mono bluetooth headsets do a much better job (plantronics and jabra have good ones.. but I lost one and broke the other).  I called my wife after I got it and tested the noise assasin.  She definitely heard noise reduction (I had the windows down and the radio up) but was still able to hear the radio clearly with NA on so don't expect to wear this at a concert and expect your caller to hear a pin drop, but it's definitely better than other noise cancelling headsets.Overall I'm happy with my purchase.  It's a refurb so I expected to put up with a glitch or two (something cosmetic or some minor audio issue) but so far nothing has presented itself.  Would I have paid 100 for this?  Probably not.. the lack of AVRCP reduces the value for me, but i would have paid $50 or $60... instead I paid $35.  Winning.  I'll be buying one for my wife soon!
summary: Great headset at a great price

reviewText: There are two things that make a good BT headset; technology and anatomy.  Technology is relatively easy to assess, unfortunately we all have slightly different anatomy so everyone is going to have a slightly different result.  Aside from comfort, different earpieces will line up differently with different ears and this will effect sound quality.  I've had headsets that sounded crappy unless I held them in an unnatural position they would not rest in on their own.  My review is based upon my experience, take it for what's good and bad but you need to evaluate on your own to be sure.On to the Icon....Technology:- It charges quickly and will last an entire busy day, I haven't verified the actual amount of talk time, but in mixed use it's fine for me and I average around 2500 minutes a month on my cell.- It's small and light, not nearly as obvious looking as the original Jawbone, the only flashing light faces inward and is only visible when you're not wearing it (a Pro to me, I don't need to look more obvious).- It will pair with up to 8 devices and automatically connect to the first two it finds on power up.  I carry a personal and a work phone, I have not been able to get it to accept calls on both at the same time, but the work around is actually not bad for me.  I have it paired to both and I just turn BT on/off on the phones when I need to switch.  It connects quickly and reliably.- A2DP - I installed it but I turned it off, I'm not looking to use it for music, but it's nice to know I could.- Noise Assassin - I guess this is the big selling point and honestly, it works for me.  I was completely unimpressed with the original Jawbone, but the Icon actually works.  I've left myself voicemail driving 70mph with all the windows down and then with the radio playing too loud to hold a normal conversation (with the windows down) and I could still understand what I was saying in the message.  Subjectively, everyone ekse says it sounds great on the other end.- Changeable voice prompts - nice touch, but for me it's not a make or break option.Anatomy (Subjective):- Fits securely - for me. This is the first headset that I haven't needed to use a loop on.  It won't fall out of my ear from chewing gum or yawning like some others have mentioned, chances are your mileage may vary.- The fit lines up with my ear well so that sound quality on my end is very good. Oddly enough though; while on calls the audio is perfect volume for me and audible in most noisey conditions, but the audio prompts and notification sounds are lower volume and hard to hear sometimes.  In certain noisy situations I'll hear or feel the phone itself before i hear the headset. Maybe I missed a volume control in the Aliph MyTalk but I like the unit enough that I'll deal with it.- Doesn't hurt to wear it, but it makes my ear sensitive/sore.  I don't notice it while wearing it, but after a while if I touch it, I'll notice it's sore, and after I remove it touching my ear is uncomfortable, but oddly it doesn't get uncomfortable that I have to remove it.  I'm really hoping this gets better with time as I really like this unit and I'm not ready to call it quits.Conclusion:For me it's the best sounding, comfortable (when my ear is not sore) headset I've used to date.  I recommend trying it for yourself.
summary: Ultimately you have to try it for yourself, but it's the right one for me.
