reviewText: I love to listen to AM KFI640 while driving. John & Ken, Bill Handel... ..."Turn off your radio!!!" That is the first thing comes out from the other side of the line each time I picked up call from my wife with my Sound ID 200 blue tooth. Now, I'm glad that I made up my mind to get this Jawbone ICON Hero series. I can have my radio on (not even tune it down) while pickup call from my wife and won't get yielded at =). My Toyota Matrix also generates a lot of road and wind noise. My friends always complain about it when I have my old blue tooth on. They said that those noises are loud and unbearable. And noises only came up during those times that I was not talking. They're surprise that those noises are all gone now - no more with this Jawbone.Reviews from Amazon help me a lot on my decision making. I read those bad reviews as well as the good ones and came to one conclusion: As long as this device works, its sound quality and noise canceling is excellent. With this in mind, I'd rather pay a higher price to avoid the BULK packaging items. I even checked out from Costco Warehouse since they have the best return policy as well as the convenience.Highly recommanded. Remember to check out video on YouTube about test run on this product as well.Keep up with your good job, Jawbone!Updated on 10/15/2012A couple of excellent designs need to be brought up:1. A separate power on/off button - I has been very upset with my two previous bluetouthes that have the single button to power on/off as well as ending call. There were so many times that I was trying to power off my device and end up activating the redial instead.2. Remaining battery life on voice as well as displaying on smart phone status bar.3. Voice quality and noise cancelling is by far the best.I'm lovin' it!!!

This is the third jawbone, I have owned. The first one I loved it, but my dog chewed it. The second, I gave to my brother, and this is better than those. I recommend jawbone to anyone looking for a bluetooth. I can actually mow my grass and talk on the phone and they don't even realize I am mowing.

I've tried several other BT's and this by far has the best reception for my Droid. People say I don't sound 'tinney' and it's clear. There are no complicated button push patterns to learn or voice commands to figure out. For me it's simplicty and clarity. In very windy conditions there are still issues, but if you turn your head away from the direct source, once again the call was clear. The one down side was the talk time battery life. But Jawbone has a customer for life with me!
summary: Easy to use and best reception!

reviewText: This was my second Jawbone, and about the 5th headset I've owned.  The sound quality is terrible.  Really Jawbone?  The noise cancelling is far below that of the previous headset?  Really Jawbone?  The fit and comfort is excellent, but it's so light, it has a hard time touching the cheek, which is required for good sound.  The switch is cheap and difficult to work.  No on-device volume control.  Being returned.
summary: Poor Sound Quality, Poor Noise Cancelling, Nice Fit

reviewText: In my experience with an iPhone 3G S, I've had very good luck with this earpiece.  Easy to use, good battery life, etc.
summary: Great ear piece in my experience

reviewText: I've been struggling with battery life on my Evo for awhile because I use it a lot for wifi tethering.  This battery is a must-have.  I don't know yet exactly how long it will last, but I can say that I've been using it all day and at the time when I'd  normally have 40% battery life left with the normal battery, I still have 90% with this battery.

I loved my Droid Eris before, but love it even more now that I don't have to worry about battery life.  I can play as much as I want and still make it through a full 24 hour day and more.  I'm using it to play audio books, games, shopping, navigation, and even as a phone.  I find the thicker phone more comfortable to hold.  Please be sure to follow the battery instructions - charge it a few hours longer after you get the full charge signal.  I've had the new battery for about a week now and I've noticed improved life with each charge.
summary: This battery makes the Eris even better

reviewText: improved the battery life of the phone but made it very bulky. Wish they could get better battery life without such a big battery.

Purchased the Seido Extended Life Battery 3500 mAh for my Droid Eris I received it yesterday, charged it over night and put in my phone. Oh man what an improvement. Before this battery the regular battery would last about half a day at most, with the Seido battery was on all day with the internet and texting all day it still is at a little less than half on the batt indicator. I would recommend this battery for anyone with a Droid Eris and needs a long lasting battery get this one.

Recently purchased an HTC Droid Eris from Verizon after hours and hours of reviewing blogs and input about which new cell phone to get.  I was looking at a Blackberry unit, having used one at work.  After going over several phones and features with the Verizon sales representative (Tara), I decided on the Eris.  I was amazed at all the features this phone has and really like the touch-screen functions.  Even the 'virtual' keyboard works for me.  The one big negative was the standard battery.  It would not last a whole day without having to be charged.  I understand that Seidio makes better batteries for the Eris and I plan on purchasing one as soon as possible.  Would have given the unit a 5-star rating, except for the battery situation.

Wow! I must say in a word Zagg SmartBuds are awesome! I have the Bose version. Both in the ear and over the head. Not real wild about either, but they work. Then I found something that I though nobody would beat. The Plantronics Back Beat 906. A blue tooth variation that controls your music, has excellent volume range, allows you to take calls and even pause everything and open the mic so you can hear your suroundings. I thought they were tops. Then I ordered the Zagg Sparq2.0 back up battery system. They offered a pair of SmartBuds free with the order. Ok, I always keep my Bose wired headset close or in my computer bag incase I just get tired of wearing the back beats and need something different. So the package arrived and out came the smart buds. I plugged them in and....WOW! These things crank louder than ANY headset I have tried since I started using ipods and iphones, many, many years ago. I also have ALWAYS had my EQ setting on bass boost. Not needed with the Zagg SmartBuds. I loved my blue tooth ear phones because I could never get an "in ear" version to stay in my ears. Not a problem with the Zagg cord management system. These are by far the most comfortable ear phones I've ever used, Back Beats included. The only thing I would change if I could change anything would be the slider volume control. It's just a little touchy with such a broad range in a small slide area. It's easy to blast yourself when trying a small adjustment. Call quality is awesome. I'm loud and clear and so are my callers to me. I am very impressed and will order another pair to keep in my other bag.. Now I just hope I like the Zagg Sparq2.0, the whole reason I was even introduced to the SmartBuds, just as much...

My Zagg Smartbuds fell apart repeatedly. Zagg's customer service offered me a discount on another pair but that's it. I've had to fix mine repeatedly. The last time they fell apart, the button was lost. I like that they loop around the neck but the way that the mic/volume controls are set up is terrible because it falls apart. The plastic around the jack has also cracked. Never buying from Zagg again, I don't recommend that you do either.
summary: Falls apart, Zagg support is terrible

reviewText: For plug in headphones, these are GREAT. My problem is that I am not in love with things inside my ears. Otherwise they are GREAT

ALL of the provided sleeve sizes are big enough to plug an elephants butt! The volume is scaled way down and the buds are way to large for everyone in my house. They won't stay in place. Would never buy again!

I was looking for a set of buds for working out in the yard and for work. I needed something that controls work with my Galaxy S3, had good sound, and good cable management. These fit the bill perfectly. I was a little worried about the build quality after reading some of the other reviews but I was pleasantly surprised. The cables them selves appear to  be reinforced, at least they are better than a standard ear bud.If I run into any issues, I will update the review.
summary: Good  sound, better build than the reviews lead on

reviewText: I haven't noticed any difference between the length of time this battery lasts vs. the amount of time of the battery that came with my phone (neither of which are stellar). Plus, you can't beat the price.
I used this as a spare battery.  Anyone with a Droid Eris knows the battery is weak.  This one did not out perform the factory battery, but it did last almost as long.  I would buy it again.

This is the second battery I have ordered. It works fine for me -- I keep my phone on 24/7 and it holds a charge much better than the one I replaced. It is a good battery -- and seems to do as well as the $40-plus battery Verizon wanted me to buy.

It's an OEM HTC battery for a fraction of the price that most  would charge you for.  What's more to ask?  Anyone that owns one of these phones knows that it will plow through a battery no matter how careful you are with power management.  At this price, you can definitely afford to have a spare or two, and be comforted by the fact that it's an OEM battery, not some cheap knock-off that may or may not work.

Bought it as a spare battery together with the battery compartment cover. In combination with simultaneous smartphone & battery charger (there are a lot of them on eBay from Chinese sellers)this charged spare battery allows for the quick replacement of depleted battery in the phone (no need to look for power outlet in airport or hung around outlet while battery is charged).I'm still using my antique Droid Eris because it's small and does the job. But battery doesn't last for full day if the WiFi is heavy used. The extended battery increases the thickness of phone almost twice. But spare battery doesn't need much space and may be placed in bag. During last 6 months have used it only twice during the business trip but it was a real savior.
summary: It's original HTC battery so it works perfectly with my Droid Eris

reviewText: I've used all kinds of headsets in the last few years including the original jawbone.  My recent headset, the Nokia BH 703 seemed to be pretty good, but this jawbone Icon blows it and anything else I've used away. The sound clarity in my ear as well as on the other end (I've asked the party I'm speaking to) is excellent: clear and loud.  The noise assasin works as advertised.  Window down, music blaring-the other party barely notices. It works when in a crowd, a store, etc.  Connects instantly to my Nokia N97 and paired effortlessly on the first go.  Battery life is also good at about 4 hrs of talk time.  Pressing the talk/end button and hearing approximate time left is also a plus.  I highly recommend it.

My buddy swore by the Icon claiming it was the best noise canceling tooth he's ever owned. I took his advice and bought one. I absolutely hate this thing. Connection is hit or miss with my Samsung Galaxy smartphone. Sometimes I turn it on and it connects right away and sometimes I have to re-connect it by going into the phones bluetooth settings and pair it up. there are 2 tiny pinhole microphones on the side of the Icon but they will not pick up your voice if the little rubber nub on the bottom of the device doesn't touch your face (MAJOR FLAW). 50% of my calls with this are fine but if the little rubber nub pulls away from my skin by just a tiny bit then the person on the other end won't hear me or they'll tell me that I sound very far away.  This happens about half the time using the piece making it completely useless for me. I can't risk loosing clients because they can't hear me.The device has some positive aspects and I don't want to overlook them. It is very lightweight, the standby and talk times are good but I've had other bluetooth headsets that have lasted 1-2 hours longer. It charges very quickly. There are multiple ear pieces that come with it so that you can customize the fit (though non of them keep the rubber nub to my face very well). The sound quality on my end is very good and I can hear the other people talking to me crystal clear.If you are overweight and have fat cheeks you might have better luck keeping this device pressed to your skin and it might work well for you. My face is pretty sculpted so it is basically useless for me and only stays pressed on my face 20-30% of the time.  I tried for 3 months to get it to work right and finally called up Jawbone to see if i could trade it. They had some of the worst customer service I've ever experienced. They told me that if I didn't buy it directly from them they wouldn't do anything for me. They also said I would only be able to trade it within 60 days of purchase even if I had bought it directly from them.  Plantronics would go above and beyond to help their customers but Jawbone falls far short in customer service.  I recently bought another bluetooth device from Jabra. I will never buy another jawbone again.
summary: Buyer Beware - This item does not work for everyone

reviewerName: Dr. Sam Beckett "Hoping for that last leap home"
reviewText: I briefly owned an original Jawbone in 2006. Loved the noise cancellation, hated everything else about it: awkward physical design, hopelessly uncomfortable fit, uselessly goofy controls, silly charger design.It's now 2010, and the above haven't changed. The Icon's sound quality and noise cancellation are still top-notch. But the design still doesn't fit right - I can't get the important little nub to stay on my cheek. It still doesn't fit - I don't have large ears, yet even the largest earbud fails to hold the thing in my ear. (And my ear will feel like it's on fire up to that point.) The controls are improved - I sure do like the iPhone integration, and the single button's functionality is much simpler, though that button is in a hard-to-press location. The charger sees a welcome update to the micro-USB standard; so to be true to its past, Jawbone supplies a charging block guaranteed to cover more than one outlet, and a THREE INCH LONG charging cable. That's right, 3", so either leave your headset on the floor, or go get a 6' USB-micro USB cable at Radio Shack for another $20.I get the feeling Jawbone was, is, and will be run by mad scientists with no experience or interest in ergonomics. My Jawbone is going back (again - sigh), and I will look into Jabra (which always gets everything right) or Plantronics (which deserves a 2nd chance).PS: The caller ID function is useless. The voice only reads digits, not names (for someone in your address book). Who remembers #'s any more?

This is my third bluetooth earpiece, after thePlantronics Voyager 510and thePlantronics Voyager 855.  For its primary function (phone calls) I would give it the edge over either of those earpieces because of the excellent reception and noise cancellation, but if you are strongly interested in using A2DP to listen to music or podcasts, then the Voyager 855 is very competitive.- Appearance: The Jawbone Icon is tiny and light, and shows clear design influence.  Even the frickin box is beautiful, and the whole thing is something you might expect to see at Target - clearly mass produced, but still distinctive and attractive instead of merely functional.  This model is "The Rogue" - two shiny black squares, with subtle red undertones.  There are five other models, each with its own color and pattern.  After a few weeks in my pocket, there are a couple scratches on the finish, so you may want to carry yours in an altoids tin or something.- Sound: Here is where the Icon wins.  The reception is great, even when my phone is in my pocket, at least on the same side.  With the phone in my opposite side pocket, it's occasionally choppy.  The Icon also has the latest Jawbone "NoiseAssassin" technology - basically, a piece of the phone touches your cheek to help the phone figure out what noises are coming from you and what is external.  It's not perfect, but it is *much* better than anything I've used before.  I can walk through a windy parking lot or talk while my car radio is on, and the noise cancellation eliminates most of the external noise.  Icon also has automatic volume leveling, which seems ok, although some calls are still a little loud.- Connectivity/Software:  The Icon charges and connects to a PC through a microusb port, which is nice, and has the capacity to download software from Jawbone's app store.  It has voice responses "I'm on and ready to go" or "Call from 555-..." instead of beeps, and you can actually select the voice you prefer from the app store.  There are some apps for iphone integration -- for example, one app works with an iphone app to display a headset battery meter on your iphone, and apps for software upgrades like A2DP.- Controls: There is a single control button on the back of the earpiece and an on-off switch on the inside.  This simplicity is consistent with Icon's slick design philosophy, but I would have liked some extra buttons for functions like volume.- Fit: The fit is not perfect.  If you look at the picture, you will see a soft circle at the back of the earpiece.  That circle presses up against the back of your ear, and the front presses against the front.  Because the earpiece does not actually sit in the ear canal (like the 855), it doesn't block out as much exterior sound, and unless one of the three included circles is a good fit for your ear size, the fit may not be perfect.  Alternately, there are earloops included too.  I like the ear circle when it fits, but I've had the medium fall out a few times, and the large seems a little too big.- Other: The battery claims to have about a four hour charge, and the voice will tell you how much you have left when you push the button.  I've left mine on overnight without much loss in charge, and it seems like I get at least a few hours from it, maybe four.  Multipoint bluetooth connectivity is good - I connected this to aBlackberry CurveandNokia Nuronwith no trouble, although I haven't been able to get A2DP and multipoint to work simultaneously.- A2DP: As I said, you can install A2DP from the Icon app store.  This allows you to use the Icon to listen to podcasts or music on your phone, and to use voice to control some phone apps.  (Of course, music through a bluetooth connection in one ear only is not a Bose-quality experience, but sometimes it's still nice to listen to tunes without people knowing it.)  The sound is good, but I still think theVoyager 855is better for A2DP - the 855 has extra controls that let you adjust volume more precisely and to skip tracks, and the 855 has a second earpiece that you can connect if you want to go full stereo.  (Update 4/8/11 - my understanding is that Jawbone now ships these with A2DP standard, but you can still install it from their app store if you don't have it).- Comparison: Currently, this unit is twice the price of the Voyager 510 and is at about the same price level as the 855.  On the other hand, it's much lighter than the 510, and is better looking and has much better noise cancellation than both.  Overall, I'm happy I have it, but IMHO, the choice is close enough to depend on your specific needs and budget.Update October 28, 2010: five months later, I love this earpiece more than ever.  The fit still isn't perfect, but I love how light it is.  (Between 9-10 grams according to my kitchen scale).  I also love its design sense, and while the A2DP also less than perfect, I have happily listened to about a hundred podcasts since getting this thing.  On balance, it's far and away my favorite bluetooth earpiece to date.
summary: Good for calls (not the best A2DP Solution)

reviewText: I love the Icon but it has its set backs because it is so small it is very hard to find a position that it rests on your skin for the voice assian to work properly  if it were a little longer in length it would be great. The other problem is that when you receive a call Icon only tells you the phone number not who is calling unless you know all your contact phone numbers what good does  this do Jawbone coulddevelop some downloadable software to correct  this Voice ID that would be very easyfor  them to do if they would  do this they would have the best on the market

Probably the best looking blue-tooth I have ever owned, & I have had many.  Unfortunately, it hurts my ear like all jawbone BT's. I use the loop, because if I don't, it doesn't stay in my ear & I would have dropped it many times over.  Almost returned it because the sound quality seems to be a bit tinny, which is unusual for Jawbone, just have not gotten around to it.  Would not mind if the seller offered me an opportunity to return it.

Great product at a great price, what could be better................love the way the jawbone works. Can't be without one. I dropped my last one in a swimming pool and it stopped functioning so I was on Amazon ordering one as fast as I could.

This is my 4th bluetooth headset and probably my second best.As far as size goes, this headset is awesome.  It's compact and when I wear my hair down, you can't see it.  It's lightweight and pretty cute.I like that I can listen to music through the headset.  I don't use that feature a lot, but when I occasionally do, it's great.I do sometimes have problems with people being able to hear me with this headset.  I bought the jabra eargels for this headset and it made a huge difference because the little rubbery part that needs to touch your face now does.  If I turn the headset on during a call, I find that the quality is far worse than if I make or receive the call with the headset already on.  This doesn't make sense, but in the year that I've owned this, I've found it to be true.I don't know if I could find a headset that would work better for me.  I'll probably use this one until it dies or until great strides have been made in bluetooth headset technology.

I have always owned a Jawbone bluetooth. The icon was a great step forward and backwards. The bluetooth worked great with certain cell phones and the change in the answer/end call button is a vast improvement because the old Jawbone button hindered my ear. The icons button is at the end of the bluetooth near the ear hook. Con: The bluetooth ear piece gets loose after wearing it for a while and falls out. Too big.

I needed a new bluetooth earpiece because my old Plantronics Voyager finally died. I decided to try a smaller in ear earpiece rather than another large around the ear type.  My wife loves the Jawbone Icon she has so I thought I would give it a try.  I found one on Amazon that was affordable and ordered it.  It came very quickly and I was happy with the size and look of it.I quickly lost my enthusiasm when I couldn't get it to fit my ear using any of the included eargels that came with it.  I liked the sound it provided but it was annoying to have to hold it in my ear while I was using it.  This is especially annoying when driving because it kind of negates the whole point of having a hands free head set which is the law here in California for drivers.I did some research and discovered that I was not alone in this problem but others had found a reasonable work around.  Jabra makes a set of eargels that fit the Icon very well and keep the earpiece in my ear without having to screw it into my ear canal AND use the earhook.  Once I fould this solution I was very happy with my earpiece and would recommend it to anyone looking for a small in the ear bluetooth earpiece.The sound is great, the special features are great (I find that the volume is fine for me and don't need a volume adjust button) and I like that it actually tells me how much talk time I have (You have approximately 3 hours of talk time left) in a voice I can choose from the 6 on the Jawbone MyTalk website.I especially love the fact that I can now listen to music and podcasts through it and don't have to fumble with wires while driving.  My car stereo doesn't have an Aux plug and the FM transmitter I bought as a work around  stinks.If I hadn't had to find a work around for the eargels I would have easily given this earpiece a 5 star rating.

I have been meaning to purchase a product like this for some time as I am constantly running out of battery on my nights when I go out after work. Most times my iphone 4s will be completely dead by 9 or 10pm. I already have the IMP90D which works great but I always forget to take it with me.  So now to my review;The IMP201B comes in a nice clear plastic package with a micro usb cord, case, and screen protector. The instructions are only in English and very easy to understand. The product itself feels great in your hands and the rubberized feel will give you a solid grip over the slick surface of the iphone. It is a two piece case with the top portion of the product coming off so you can slide in the iphone to connect to the 30 pin connector. You then slide the top back on and it fits the phone snugly giving it a clean look. Being that product has a 30 pin connector, it makes the size of the phone a bit bigger giving it the look of an iphone 5. I have had has a few people ask me if I purchased the new iphone. The camera and flash are not so you do not have to worry about picture quality but the case provides a great deal of cushion to the back of your phone for shock. All buttons are easily accessible and you do not have to worry about the headphone jack. There are also two slits on the case that allow your sound to come out properly as well.In regards to power, it took me around six hours to charge the product off a completely depleted batter on the case. After fully charges I tested the device on a 50 percent battery and I had a fully charged product within 1.5 hrs. You can then leave the product on or turn off the batter by holding the small button on the back of the phone. Your phone will then stop charging. It seems to be true that your battery life doubles with this product as I use it for video, music, on the train every day and for phone during work and I still come home with a full battery.The only drawback to this product is that the case fits flush with the iphone making the screen on the same level as the side of the case. Most other cases wrap around the phone even just a little to provide some support for the screen. In this case it is a must to use the screen protector for some protection of the front screen. Also another good/bad thing is that the iphone connector now becomes a micro connector. This is great since most people tend to have micro connector for their other devices and they can easily be obtained for a cheap price. The problem is that you now have to take off the case when you want to plug your phone into alarm clocks or other iphone ready devices.Overall this is just the product I needed to keep my phone going all night and protected at the same time. I definitely recommend.

I'm constantly on the run and having a dozen devices in my bag I'm always on a forever search to make sure I have enough back up power sources to keep my devices charged at all times. This is a great case! It's not slippery, it's resistant to smudges and finger prints... then again if you have sticky/oily fingers it may not hold true for you ;) it's easy to slide the phone in and out. Case isn't too bulky doesn't have issues blocking all the buttons and port I need to access. Easy read meter to see how much juice is left. I had no idea it came with a screen protector so that was a nice surprise!Pros: everything listed above it's not slippery, phone fits great it doesn't get stuck in or you won't have issues trying to put it in. Case isn't bulky and no issues blocking all areas that I need to access. Easy to read meter. Nice small surprise bonus of a screen protector! =)
summary: Love love love. Did I mention love?!

reviewText: This is an excellent product. I also own a Juice Pack Air and the NT is a much nicer product. Well done!I've owned a Mophie Juice Pack Air for about a year. I received this product as a gift. I sold the Mophie on eBay. This is the better product.Pros:1. Mimics the design of the iPhone 4/S (Better match with the iPhone design than the Mophie Juice Pack Air)2. Comes with a screen protector3. Very clean design, only 4 small blue lights for battery level, a small silver on/off button and a very small connector for synching and charging4. Soft-touch finish makes it look and feel good in your hand5. No hard-switches (the Mophie Juice Pack Air has a slide on/off switch)6. Has enough power to completely charge the internal battery with some left over (~25%) to run the phone for several hours as though it is plugged in or to provide a second partial charge after the battery gets low the second time (just remember to turn off the NT after the iPhone is fully charged the first time or it will keep charging the iPhone until it is fully depleted)7. On/off function provides decent flexibility in how the battery is consumed or chargedCons:1. Instructions are a little brief and unclear2. Unique connector for synching and charging3. Top piece can slide up a little too easilyI'm very happy with this product. It provides the extra battery life I need and the flexibility to charge the iPhone when and how I want. It looks great and the soft touch paint makes it look better and easier to hold. This is the one to get. Very pleased.

This is a solid choice for an iphone 4(s) case with battery pack.  I have used and owned a few different ones.Pros:- case itself is well made and has a very low profile compared to other battery pack cases- I really like that the lights (that indicate the battery level) turn off while it is charging (hate how others stay on)- you can still sync your iphone to your computer, through micro usb.- comes with a screen protectorCons:- hard to tell when the power is off when it is not connected to your phone- cannot use any apple accessories when in the case (since it hides your apple connector and has a micro USB port instead).- micro USB cord that comes with it is very very short (not that big of a deal though)I use my phone all the time and can NEVER get a full day out of any phones stock battery power.  I have many different devices for adding charge to my phone, external battery packs of all sizes.  But sometimes you just don't have the option of holding another device to charge your phone and that's when I bring this case around with me.  But you definitely need to know how to use the case properly.  I let my mother use the case and she didnt realize you could turn the case on and off.  So from the time she unplugged from the charging cable, the battery pack was on and juicing up her iphone.  So basically her phone remained a 100% battery life for several hours until the pack died.  Apple Iphones have a mechanism that stops charging the phone in cycles once it gets to 100%.  Basically losing a lot of power from the case.  I wont turn on the power to the case until my battery is at least below 50%.

This is my second new trent case and overall I'm happy with it. While the battery life isn't as good as my previous case (which had a larger battery) it has a little bit slimmer design and is lighter than my first case. The top cover is a big improvement than the previous case. It's a lot more secure than the old case and seems it will last a lot longer when opening to get the phone out (the tabs on my previous case eventually broke off because i took my phone out almost daily). My only problem with the new style top cover is the opening around the headphone jack is smaller so some headphones/aux cables may not fit properly.
summary: Extra battery life goes a long way!

reviewText: I like this case because it has saved my phone right when it is about to die, I just switch to the power case and charge up. No problems so far.

The case is easy to use, comes with its own charger cord, and pretty much charges my battery to 100% if my phone was on or around 20%. The only trouble that I have with it is that it's rather difficult to separate the two parts of the case. It takes a good ten seconds to take off, but it doesn't bother me much considering that just means that it protecting my phone efficiently.

I had a friend with a Morphie Air case and he seemed very satisfied that it got him trough the day without having to recharge his phone.  I like the idea and although the case made his phone much thicker, it wasn't too bad.  The only problem was the high cost.  I looked at several alternatives. One of my requirements was that the case cover the entire back and sides of the phone (except for cutouts for buttons and camera and such). That narrows the field quite a bit.  This case seemed just right but I wasn't sure about it since it had few reviews and was so inexpensive (comparatively).  I decided to give it a try and I am actually very satisfied.  I only have one problem with the case: it takes forever to recharge it so that both my phone and the case are topped off.  I heard one reviewer of the Trent IMP190, a similar case, say it took 4 hours.  I left mine charging over night and it didn't finish. I am contacting the company to see if this unit is defective (that is unreasonably long). Once the unit is fully charged, I can make it through though my normal day without a problem. It seems to roughly double the battery life of my phone.For the money, it seems a good deal.I will update my review after I hear back from the manufacturer.Imaxpower was very good about responding to my problem. I ended up getting a newer one from them and it has worked very well. Early units appear to have a bug in the firmware that results in faulty display of charge level.  The new one doesn't have that problem and works very well.  There are two other issues that are also worth mentioning. The case seems to sometimes have a mind of its own about when to charge the phone and when to let it synchronize. Sometimes it seems to decide to charge its battery first until it has a sufficient charge and then start charging my iPhone. Until it is charging the phone, there doesn't seem to be a connection to my computer so it won't sync. Odd. In general, I still like the case and still think it is a good value for the money.  Oh, one more thing: the case seems to have a slight effect on getting a cell signal for the worse. It doesn't seem to be significant unless I am in areas where the number of bars is close to 1.

Let's face it, the battery life on the iPhone is awful.  While I don't see myself as any sort of power user, I'm lucky if I end the day with 5% left on the phone.  I chose New Trent (formerly iMaxPower) because I rarely see products from any company on Amazon that are consistently rated 4 1/4 ro 5 stars across the board.  Every review praised the quality of the product, and even better - the technical support.I needed a case with battery for my new iPhone, as well as a standalone booster charger because our family is going on a 14-hour plane trip and I need the iPhone to last the entire trip.  My kids are also bringing their DSi, so we needed the booster to charge that as well.So this review covers all of the New Trent products I purchased: the IMP130, IMP550, and IMP880.IMP130The IMP130 is an iPhone case that contains an integrated 1700mAh battery.  That battery is higher capacity (according to wiki) than the one in the iPhone 3GS (which is supposedly around 1219mAh).  Capacity isn't everything; battery quality varies greatly.  After using the IMP130 for a week or so, I estimate the it to effectively double my time between charges.The IMP130 case completely covers the iPhone (other comparable cases leave the top exposed).  To put the iPhone in the case, you detach the top of the IMP130 case and slide the iPhone into the bottom part, where it docks to the standard Apple connector built into the case.  You then have the option to re-attach the top piece, providing protection to the top of your iPhone, or leaving it off.  The only reason to choose to leave the top part off is that when the IMP130 is fully assembled, access to the iPhone buttons is difficult at best.  You need to use your fingernail to mute the phone and access the volume controls.  I hope New Trent addresses this in a future version.  The standby button and headphone jack are much more easily accessible.  NOTE: If you do decide to leave the top off the case, there is not much friction holding the iPhone in the bottom part of the case.  It feels secure, but I would not trust it - I don't think the designers expected you to use it that way, but the case design is very clean even without the top piece (as if it was designed with that in mind).  I find no degradation in 3G signal due to the case, nor are the speakers degraded.Now the best part - for those of you who (like me) have a full-body Invisible Shield on your iPhone, the phone WILL stil completely fit in the the IMP130!  I have not heard of that with any other case.The IMP130 is about 3/4 the weight of the iPhone, so it almost doubles the overall weight. It also adds a bit of bulk around all sides - but provides a good feel in your hands.  The texture of the case provides a good amount of grip, but I still prefer the grip the Invisible Shield provides.  To me, the IMP130 case could use a little more anti-slip texture.The IMP130 is charged through a standard Micro USB cable (included).  Say good-bye to the proprietary iPhone cable.  This is a very good thing.  The case has an on/off switch in the bottom.  When the switch is Off, you are running on your iPhone battery.  When the switch is On, you are still using the iPhone battery, but it is being charged at the same time by the IMP130 battery.  When the IMP130 finally gives out, the "charging" indicator on your iPhone turns off and you are solely using the iPhone battery.  Whether the switch is on or off, you can still sync through the Micro USB cable.  Any off-the-shelf Micro USB cable will work with this product.  Here's the typical scenario: you come home with your iPhone at 90% charge and your IMP130 at 0%.  You connect the cable to your PC to do your sync.  The IMP130 begins to charge and the iPhone starts to charge once the IMP130 has enough juice.  After a couple of hours, both are at 100%.  The IMP130 has 3 LED indicators that show the current charge (100%/66%/33%/0%).Finally - and this is a GREAT one - the IMP130 has a built-in super-bright white LED that can be used as a flashlight (say good-bye to those stupid "flashlight apps").  It also solves the problem of those impossible low-light pictures.  The LED has a switch to turn it on or off.In all, the IMP130 is really a great product.  The only negative is the hard-to-access volume and mute controls.  And remember, if you have an Invisible Shield full body wrap, it WILL fit in the case nicely.IMP550While the IMP130 is great, there's no way it will take the iPhone on a 14-hour flight of pure video and 3D games.  So that's why I also got the IMP550.  This is a brand new product from New Trent.  It's the big brother of the IMP130 (much bigger in fact).  It has a very large 5500mAh capacity.  That pretty much quadruples the iPhone battery.Unlike the IMP130, this case does not fully enclose the iPhone; it leaves the top exposed - granting easy access to all of the iPhone buttons.  The case is lined with a velvety material which not only feels neat, it helps keep the iPhone in place.  An iPhone with a full-body wrap Invisible Shield DOES fit in the case.Also unlike the IMP130, the sync interface is not Micro USB, but rather standard Apple.  That means there is no cable included with the IMP550; you can use your original cable that came with your iPhone.Because this is a serious battery, the case adds serious weight to your iPhone, as well as bulk - mostly overall thickness.  However, unless you have very small hands, I think you will find that the case feels much more comfortable in your hands than the iPhone itself.  I find it to be quite ergonomic.  I also find the grip of the IMP550 to be slightly superior to that of the IMP130.The IMP550 does not have an on/off switch; it provides a charge to the iPhone when it needs to.  Like the IMP130, you will charge both the case and the iPhone while you are connected to your PC, wall charger, or car charger.Personally, I don't think the IMP550 is suited to be a full-time case solution for your iPhone.  It is simply too bulky and heavy for that (as is any other 5000+ mAh battery case).  It's great for long trips, golf courses, or any other time you will not have access to a charger for many many hours.Sadly, the IMP550 has no flashlight LED (maybe on their next revision?).  Three LEDs indicate charge, and a fourth tells you if the IMP550 is charging your iPhone.In summary - another 5-star product.IMP880When I am on that long trip, my iPhone is covered by the IMP550.  But what about my kid's DSi and my wife's smartphone (not everyone has an iPhone)...  New Trent has that covered, too.  The IMP880 is a standalone battery that charges a multitude of devices.  It has a staggering 8800mAh of capacity - almost two IMP550 worth, or roughly 6-7 times the capacity of an iPhone.  That's some serious capacity.  The unit is quite small - about the size of a man's wallet.  It weighs about the same as a man's wallet (before a Vegas trip).Four LEDs indicate battery charge and a Test button lets you know the current capacity.  NewTrent made a Youtube video demonstrating this unit.  In that video, they say you need to turn the unit on by holding down the Test button for 5 seconds before you charge something.  I find that the unit always charges a device if needed; maybe I have a newer revision.The battery may be small, but the wall adapter used to charge the IMP880 is not.  The Youtube video shows a nice, small wall-wart.  My unit came with a very bulky in-line AC adapter.  It is larger than the IMP550 itself.  Not a big deal, but much larger than I expected.  Remember, the AC adapter is something you pack in your suitcase; you carry the small IMP880 on the plane fully charged.The IMP880 can charge a variety of items, and has several ports:DC-IN jack connects to the AC adapter.  This is how you charge the IMP880 from the wall.DC-OUT jack is only used for charging specific notebook PCs.  My unit included a cable for this, but I am not certain NewTrent will support notebook charging going forward.  I do not see notebook devices listed as charge targets any longer on their website.Type-A USB connector is used to charge your iPhone, Blackberry or DSi.At this point, I need to speak about the USB cable that is included with the IMP880.  The IMP880 replaces a smaller charger called the IMP500.  This was the workhorse of the imaxPower line of products.  In fact, the IMP550 is basically the IMP500 designed into an iPhone case.  The reason I bring up the IMP500 is that - like the IMP880 - it charges devices through a USB cable.  This cable has a standard USB-A connector on one end, and a generic adapter on the other.  You can configure the cable for different devices by connecting a different plug on the adapter end.  That way, you can use the USB cable to charge an iPhone, or Blackberry, or DSi, etc.  The USB cable that was included with the IMP500 had a FEMALE adapter on the end.  All of the flavors of connectors had a male adapter.  The USB cable that is included with the IMP880 has a MALE adapter on the end.  All of the flavors of connectors have a female adapter.So what does this mean?  For me, it meant a slight problem when I tried to use the IMP880 to charge my kid's DSi.  You see, neither the IMP880 nor IMP500 come with a DSi adapter.  Not a problem - the website clearly points that out.  So when I purchased the IMP880, I also bought the only DSi adapter they sold (it was about $5).  Unfortunately, that adapter is male, and only fits the IMP500 cable.  It will not fit the USB cable that came with the IMP880.My solution was to then buy an IMP500 USB cable.  NewTrent sells them, and so does EBay.  But that means I now have one cable that only fits the DSi adapter, and another cable that fits all my other devices.  Plus, I had to spend money on the extra cable.  NewTrent says they are working on the problem, and will standardize on the cable.Again, this was only a problem for me because I wanted to charge a DSi.  All my other charging needs are met with the cable that comes with the IMP880.By the time you read this, the issue may have been resolved, but contact the company if you intend to use the IMP880 to charge a DSi (or consider getting the IMP500 instead).When the IMP880 is charging a device, the IMP880 remains cool.  I believe the main reason for this is that NewTrent has a current limiter in the IMP880 that keeps charging current lower than what you get from a wall or PC.  Devices will charge slightly slower, but the IMP880 will not get hot.On those very long trips, the IMP880 can charge either the IMP550 or IMP130 directly.  NOTE: I am told by the company that this is not a wise thing to do on a daily basis, but a few times on a long trip is fine.Because of the DSi adapter issue, I'd normally have to give the IMP880 4 stars.  The only thing is - it just works so darned good.  I had the time to get the adapter issue straightened out; had I discovered this the day before my trip, I'd not be so happy.A word about NewTrent customer service: EXCELLENT.  I had a couple of questions that I sent via E-mail.  I asked if someone could call me back, and I got a phone call within 10 minutes - from the owner of the comapny.  Show me one other company where this happens.Conclusion:Three great products from a great company.  The customer support quality is amazing.  What is also amazing is how poorly written the instruction booklets are.  If you want to see the devices in action, there are videos on the website that explain it all, but hopefully this review did that as well.

Pros:- Combines protective case and additional battery capacity- Doubles the usage time of the iPhone 4SCons:- Has Micro USB connection rather than Apple 30-pinThe New Trent Power Rock IMP220B is an excellent solution for people who need more on-the-go power for their iPhone 4/4S - it effectively doubled the usage time of my iPhone 4S.  It also provides good protection of the phone, although I did not do any serious tests of this - I'm not going to throw my phone around for the sake of an Amazon review!It essentially is charging your iPhone all the time, and the phone will display 100% charge until the IMP220B battery is depleted.  The IMP220B has a 4-light LED to indicate how much charge is left in its battery, so you can easily see how much reserve power you have.  You can also use it as an emergency charge battery, where you just turn it on when you want to charge your iPhone.The one drawback of the IMP220B is that it uses a Micro USB connector for charging.  You can still sync your iPhone to iTunes via this connection, but otherwise you will not be able to use any accessories with an Apple 30-pin connector unless you remove the case.  However, this really did not affect me, so I am not going to deduct any rating points for it.One thing to bear in mind with ANY battery case is that it will make your phone bigger (the IMP220B is about 1/4 inch longer and deeper than an Apple bumper case).  I prefer to keep my phone in a belt holster, which does not work with a battery case, so unless I know that I am going to need additional power for an extended time (say, hiking with GPS), I will not use a battery case.  However, a battery case works great for my wife, who keeps her phone in her purse so the additional size is not a problem.
summary: Great battery case for your iPhone 4/4S

reviewText: My wife and I each have a New Trent Power case for the past two and a half months. These cases have performed well so far and typically add a full day of use before needing to recharge the phone. For someone like myself, who uses the GPS on the phone regularly this adds peace of mind and avoids the need for recharging halfway through the day. Itunes connectivity is still available to the PC with a micro-USB cord.The case is heavy and bulky because of the extra battery size, but I have not been bothered by this. Some people that I have shown the case to did  comment that they did not like the extra heft. The exterior of the case has held up welland does not show scratches or scuff marks. Fit and finish surrounding the phone has been tight and flush which is achieved by assembling it in two parts to achieve a close fit.The camera seems to work okay. Images are clear and don't seem to be constricted in any way. The flash works well too, although some may feel that it is blocked by the relatively deep well that surrounds the lens and flash port. Other buttons and jacks are not impeded in any way and are as easily accessible as any other case.The battery takes a LONG time to charge at least 6 hours I would say. I think that this is due to the size of the battery and not because of a subpar charger. Battery level in indicated by 4 blue LED's on the back of the case. A push of the button will light up the level of charge. Holding the button down for 3 to 4 seconds will disconnect the case from the phone and vice versa. I personally leave them connected full-time with no apparent ill effects.So far so good. The case provides a bit of peace of mind and has done so with style. The price is half that of the more popular cases which makes me feel like I beat the system somehow.  Delivery was prompt and hassle-free. A good buy all around.Update 10/12/12The case worked flawlessly up to this point. It charged and discharged in a very consistent manner for the past six months. However, the top portion of the case has cracked and broken off. This part of the case is made of flimsy plastic and, not surprisingly, most susceptible to damage. Using the case without its top portion is awkward and negates its usefulness. In sum, the battery works great while exterior durability has room for improvement.

reviewText: The New Trent IMP220B for the iPhone 4/4S is an awesome unit. It has more power (2200 mAh) than comparable units from competing companies, while maintaining the same features. The unit comes in all black with a matte finish, it comes in 2 pieces, has a 4 blue LED's for battery status, power on/off button, access to all ports and buttons including the Verizon iPhone 4, AT&T; iPhone 4, and all 4S models. In order to get the white iPhone to fit properly, you have to peel off the FCC sticker on the inside of the case. If you dont, the phone is a little too big to fit in the case. Apple doesn't advertise that the white models are thicker than the black ones, but they are.Pros: Black Matte Finish (less fingerprints, soft feel), All iPhone 4 Models supported, All buttons and switches are exposed, iPhone feels more secure in your hands with this case, comes with a SCREEN PROTECTOR and microfiber cloth, made for iPhone logo, 500 charge cycles (same as any li-ion battery), on/off switch and 4 blue LED indicators, can be synced with iTunes with out removing from case.Cons: Takes a long time to charge, top piece is flimsy and seems like it could break easily, only supplied cord will sync the phone with out removing it from the case, the bottom of the case is hollow to allow the speaker and mic to work--but since the bottom is hollow--sound is allowed to bounce around inside before it exits the bottom and sound from the speakers are muffled and when talking on the phone i was told there was a mild echo--this is understandable because the sound is not directed out of the case--just into a chamber where it can bounce--hence echos and muffled speakers (not a big problem for me, because i use the supplied headphones to talk on the phone), its a little hard to use volume and mute buttons/switches because of the depth of the case--but this will only be a problem for some people, sometimes the phone says "Charging is not supported with this accessory"(just restart the unit and it will charge fine)Recommendations: More colors, direct path to speaker and microphone,Conclusion: Overall this product is great. Its not perfect, but nothing can be made for everyone. If you have smaller fingers, the buttons wont be an issue, bigger hands will tend to have a harder time with volume and mute switches, but on the flip side the bigger your hands the more secure the unit feels in your hand. There is no other case out there right now that will give you 2200 mAh for this price. The build quality is excellent.
