This is my second purchase of this iphone case - not because the first one failed - but... my wife wanted one!  She was sick of running low on battery, always charging, and being held hostage by her charger,electrical outlets,etc.  I offered her this idea, and she loves it.  It gets her a full day easily, and probably two.  My iphone batter would run out by lunch (with all my useage), and now i can easily get into lunchtime the second day without charging!  Now that's what i call a backup battery.So far, my New Trent has lasted about 4 months - however, i can see the life span starting to deplenish.  What used to be 20 hours, is now 18 hours, etc...  I know this is normal for batteries, but I can see this lasting a year or more.  Which works for me @ $40!  I love it because it also doubles as a protective case!  My wife doesn't because it's not decorative enough and wished it came in different colors,etc....There seems to be much cheaper ones out there now, and a few more expensive - i went with this one because it's right there in the middle, and a name like NEW TRENT... Works like a champ...UPDATE 1/21/2013 - I purchased a similar model for my wife's iphone4, and 2 months into it's life, the charging port has stopped working, with intermittent failure.  I am in the process of contacting New Trent, to see how well they handle returns/RMA.... Stay tuned!

This device quickly recharges your iPhone battery.  It proved to be very useful for a job where I needed to use my phone on 3G for 6 or 7 hours.  As soon as my phone got to about a 30% charge, I turned on the backup battery, and restored the battery to 100% without breaking stride.  Great product.

I have tried numerous battery cases for the iPhone.  This is by far the best.  I purchased a Mophie Juice Pack a couple months ago and ended up taking it back.  I thought it was just a bad instance, but each replacement only charged for about 20 minutes.I check and send email, go on the internet, and use apps all day.  This battery pack keeps the phone at 100% until about 7 or 8 o'clock at night.  This case is perfect for someone who's always out and about.You can't beat it especially when you compare the price.  I will definitely be buy more products from these guys.

What can I say, this case did the job pretty well! Its 2200mAh battery was able to charge my iPhone 4S fully and then some before requiring a charge. It also allowed me to use the mountain of micro USB cables that I have laying around rather than Apple's proprietary cable. It also recharged the device very quickly.The only negative I can see with this case is that it doesn't have much protection for the screen during a drop. The lip that rises over the screen is minimal at best. I often put my clear TPU case back on after charging just because it gave me a better feeling that it would be protected during a drop.Overall, this is a good case. It adds bulk, but it should, it has 2200mAh battery in it! It's much cheaper compared to the other guys, I recommend buying it if you need the extra juice on the go!
summary: My iPhone needed some extra juice

reviewText: This New Trent Power Rock case IMP210B with Extended Rechargeable Battery really ROCKS ! I really like the sleek design; I was impressed with size and weight.  Added a little to the length, but still shorter than some cases with no battery.  The "non-slip" material feels great in your hand, and does not allow the phone to slide easily from where it is placed. I really like the battery life indicator, and the on & off switch in the same button.  The blue lights are not too bright at night like the white lights can be.Being that I'm a bit hard of hearing... I also liked the speaker "re-direction" to the front.  It is nice to have it directed towards my face and not down to the ground.  At Least twice the use time between charging.  And depending on the work day that was extended to almost three days.I would like to have a belt clip or holster.  Because of the sleek size I think that one could be designed and not be too big. Other than that love this case ! ! !
more than doubled my battery life and protects my phone also. easy to use i have no complaints would buy again

I have a mophie and an unu, and this one powers up my phone the fastest, hands down.  I have used these (I say these as I took advantage of the buy one get one free deal) since January 2013.  Now from 2%, it will only take my phone to 77%....but very quickly.  I can see the battery is not what it was new.  It states that the battery is good for 500 charges.  If you do the math, I have owned these over 200 days and I have alternated chargers everyday.  So I have only used one charger 100 times, but it's life seems at least half gone.  I don't think these chargers will last me another 6 months.  While they charge my phone up super fast, it has to burn the candle at both ends to do it.

The IMP130 is better than I expected.  I am the proud owner of TWO IMP500's and although that is an amazing product as well, this iPhone case and battery charger is AMAZING.  What impressed me the most is the thickness of the actual case.  It only adds about 5mm thickness to your iPhone and no real length.  Believe me when I say that I almost don't even notice the difference.  I am shocked.  In addition, I now don't have to worry about running out of power so quickly with just my iPhone battery.  I have now just doubled the life of my phone.  This is an amazing product.  It is highly recommended and I am telling everyone I know that has iPhones about it.  BUY ONE!!!

I originally bought this case to use when traveling but after placing it on the phone to test the fit I found that I loved this case.  It not only provided edge and corner protection but it was sleek and sexy enough for daily use.  It is a really sharp looking case and the additional battery life is phenomenal.  Instead of charging my phone every 6 hours I was charging my phone every other day.

I have been using the New Trent Power Rock case for about three months now.  It has been a great addition to my iPhone.  I can easily recharge my phone twice before needing to find an external power source.  I have used other battery cases on my phone that have not included the power button and the battery never quite seems to last that long.  The addition of the power button on the New Trent Power Rock case helps to conserve the battery in the case and helps you gauge how many charges you actually get from this thing.  The only complaint that I have with this product is the recesses for the power button on top as well as the volume  buttons and the mute switch on the side.  The openings are small and the buttons and switches are very recessed due to the dimensions of the case.  As a result it is difficult to reach the power button with one hand or the mute switch without digging your pinky finger into it.Over all the case has been fantastic while camping or traveling.  During short trips I don't even have to take my power brick or sync cable with me.I would definitely recommend this case to anyone looking for a battery case for their iPhone 4.
summary: Great for long days and travel

reviewText: This product is a great battery case that provides constant charge to my iPhone4. With that being the main function of this product, this is a great product since my phone is always fully charged. Some people are complaining about battery on the new trent is slow to charge, but I don't find it that way. I don't use the charger provided by apple, but use another product that allows higher amperage draw on the USB charger.Few things that I find can be improved is the ability to protect the phone. The corners could use some rubberized/silicon gel type material and raised a little bit more on the front part (similar to sugru type bumper shown [...]) to protect the phone in case i drop it.Another possibility is to add additional color for the product. I like black (I choose black over white iPhone even when white is available), but not everyone does.
summary: Great Product with room for improvement

reviewText: Works great. The only thing I don't like is that is may not charge the phone completely when the phone is almost dead. Also, the charge that you get from the case will only charge the phone once and then you need to charge the case again. It does add weight to the phone but its not unbearable.

This battery case is a good battery life extender.  It fits the Iphone 4s perfectly.  The case slides apart so you can slip your phone in.  It's a hard case with all the holes needed to access the functions on the phone.Pros:-Fits the phone perfectly-Adds significant battery life to the phone-Looks clean and professionalCons:-Makes the phone noticeably heavier to carry/use-The thickness of the case around the buttons can make it difficult to use them-with the case on, you can't access the phones stock charging jack, and the case uses a proprietary plug for charging.  That means either I take the case off each time I want to charge my phone, or only have one cord to charge with.I would definitely recommend this to someone who is having trouble keeping their phone charged.
I not only was a big fan of these for myself, but gave them out as gifts to several people complaining about limited battery life with their iPhones.

The Power Rock case for iPhone 4/4s is an excellent product for an amazing price. I bought my friend a PhoneSuit Elite about 3 months ago and it has already broken on him, and it was 2x the price when I bought it. At the current price, the Power Rock case is an amazing find, I spent 3 hours researching iPhone battery cases for an upcoming conference I am attending with my company. I am happy I picked the Power Rock case as my conference lifesaver. I have been using it every day since I bought it and I could not be more happy with the performance. On light days, I go to sleep with 100% charge still in the phone, and that is amazing peace of mind if you sometime forget to plug your phone in after a long day of critical thinking. I give it 4 stars because the front of the case is perfectly aligned with the face of the phone. If I drop it for any reason on it's face, it's almost assured of sustaining some damage. My old non battery case came with a bit of a lip that surrounded and raised above the front of the case, providing a few millimeters of impact resistance. I think treating the phone with a bit more respect is an excellent compromise to double the battery life though. Cant wait for the next version of this case for the iPhone 5!
summary: An excellent product with few downsides.

reviewText: The New Trent Power Rock case IMP210B with Extended Rechargeable Battery Juice Case is two great ideas in one.  It's a sturdy case that also doubles the life of your battery.  The hard rubber case is very comfortable in the hand, is not bulky and fits comfortably in the front pocket of my jeans.  I had no problems installing the phone into the case.  The top portion of the case feels a little flimsy but when snapped together, it seems fine.  The cutouts for the various buttons are of ample size but they are a little deep which makes it difficult to mute the phone, change the volume or put the phone into sleep or power down.  Slightly annoying but not enough to make me not recommend the product.  The included screen guard is great to have but trying to get all the air bubbles from underneath is virtually impossible.  Having an on and off button is very helpful and the blue LED display is easy to understand.  The only three complaints I have is that I wish there was a belt clip as I like to wear my phone on the outside, the case gets hot when you are charging the iPhone and I wish it had the standard Apple Dock Port connector on the bottom.  I have way too many cables in my house and to use the one standard cable instead of having to keep a Mini-USB cable as well would be nice.  I just wish they had different colors so that I can easily identify my phone with my wife's phone if I buy her one.UPDATE:I spent the entire day at Disneyland posting pictures and wait times to mousewait.com and ran low on my battery (20%) around 1:00pm.  One push of the button on the back of the IMP210B and within an hour, my phone was almost fully charged with juice still left in the IMP210B.  I made it the entire day without ever having to turn my phone off.  I am more than pleased with this product.
summary: Great Two in One Combo..A Case AND a Battery!

reviewText: The IMP220B fills the failing gap that Apple left when they enclosed their battery, preventing us from adding an extended battery to the phone. The 7 hours of talk time it provides is huge for those of us who use our phones for both personal and business needs, and the usage of the new standardized USB interface is excellent as most devices are now using the same cable, so most people will have them around the house (not to mention it comes with one).
summary: Perfect for those who live on their iPhones!

reviewText: This is a good way to keep your iPhone charged. The cost is not much  more than some of the cases alone. Only down side is the length of time to recharge the device , expect 3+ hours

I purchased the IMP210B about a week ago and I'm impressed with this little device. I love the fact that it's very sleek and really doesn't add that much more depth to the iPhone. It adds a little weight but nothing worth crying home to mom about.The case in itself is really nice. I love that you can also turn the battery charger on and off by holding down the charge button.  This way, I'm getting twice the amount of battery time for my phone.  I use my phone for everything, so this is really a good thing.  I can also charge the case while my phone is still in it and it charges rather quickly.The packaging and advertisement for the case say that it will completely charge an iPhone battery from 0 to 100% one time. I found this to not to be true, although it does pretty well. My phone had about 7% of battery juice and when I plugged it into the IMP210B, it charged it to 88% before the charger went dead. Again, not horrible but it would've been nice to charge it to a full 100%.Overall, it's a great device and I would recommend it. I give it a 4.5 stars out of five.

My boyfriend uses his iPhone 4 for work all day long.  He was constantly having to re-charge his phone as the battery would never last all day.  Since using this case/back-up battery he charges both over night and no longer has to re-charge during the day.  The case offers good protection and really isn't too much bigger than the phone.  Just a little thicker.  We like that you can charge the case and phone at the same time.  We did find that if you allow the phone's battery to get really low and then turn the case on to re-charge the phone the case get really hot.  We have found it's better to leave the case turned on so it is constantly charging the phone every time it gets just a little bit low.

The case works as a extended battery very well. I charged both of my daughters phones from 0% charge to 80% charge without having to recharge the actual case. The leds on the back let me know how much charge was left on the case, which made it very user friendly. Not having to use the propietory apple charger makes it very easy to charge without swapping out cables. The case was a bit bulky but worked very well.

First off, I just want to say I was extremely impressed by the overall look of the product. I have seen other cases with the same recharging funcionality, and they just looked bulky and not as appealing.  The hard edges on this really gave this product a nice sleeker look and I also noticed that the case was smaller than those other competitors.  The charging time of the case it self is moderately good.  While I wish it would charge faster, I think it may just be that I am used to the speeds of the iPhone charging, and has nothing to do with the case being slow, which I am sure it is not.  The case itself charges the iPhone just as fast as a traditional wall charger which I was very happy to see.  I liked the simplicity of being able to hit the button once to see the juice left in the case, and having to hold down the button to begin the charge.  I do wish that the case would not automatically start charging the phone upon putting on and to only be able to charge the phone when the button is pressed.I did however, notice that the case was not a 100% exact fit on my iPhone 4S.  There was a slight gap in the top right corner in which I am still able to see some of the silver on the phone.  This is not an issue on the overall reliability of keeping the case on or if I feel it is any less great than what it is, but I feel that others may hold that as a factor in the product.  I also noticed that on the back of the phone, the two pieces do not sit as flush as I would imagine it would with the smaller sliding piece being slightly raised higher.  Overall, I think the fit of the case is very good and holds the phone in with out having to worry about the case coming off with out force.So in short, I think the case functions VERY well, and get the job done perfectly.  There are a few minor tweaks that can be done, but it not entirely a deal breaker in this product.
summary: GREAT CASE AT AN EVEN GREATER PRICE

reviewText: This is a nice, basic battery case.  The others with similar features are $20 more.  It is pleasant to hold and gives you all-day capabilities even with heavy use.  I use the battery hard when metal detecting with GPS and various apps that use location services.The first case died after 7-8 charges.  When fully charged, and connected to the iphone, it would cycle on and off... making the "power connected" squeak sound on the iPhone 4 repeatedly.  Pressing the button near the LEDs would not do anything.  I've chalked it up to a fluke and giving them another chance (exchange.)The battery case does not leave any protection for the front screen and it's pretty tricky to get the phone out of the case (not that you need to that often... I just leave it on and charge / sync ia the micro USB.)If this second one fails I'll be in to drop my star rating to 1 star.
summary: Like it so much I'm giving them a second chance

reviewText: Definitely an excellent product.  I only have one of these right now and my wife and son fight over it! The extra charge it provides is ridiculous.  Lasts forever.  The matt finish is great because it doesn't collect finger prints.  It will take a while to charges the case with your phone in it, simply because it is such a large battery... but its worth the wait because you won't have to recharge again for a while.  Build quality is great... feels good in the hand.  About the size of an Otterbox... maybe a bit smaller.  Very nice.  Looks like I'll have to order another!

I have had the case for 7 months.  I like it very much but it is not perfect.  The good things are;1) The case seems very well made.2) I like the textured feel of the case - less likely to drop it, and not prone to fingerprints and smudges.  And it is slightly less likely to fall out of your shirt pocket when you bend over - although I have dropped it a couple of times.3) It protects the phone from drops and most types of damage very well.  The phone almost bounces - and I have never had any physical damage to my phone since I put it in this case.  But it does not protect the phone from water damage if you drop it into water.  Sigh.  I know that for sure.  But that is another story for another time.4) The built-in case battery seems to double the life of the battery - more than enough for a day's usage 99% of the time for me.  I never attempted even a quasi-scientific measurement, but from my usage pattern, that appears to be the case.5) It has an on-off switch - not absolutely essential, but it is nice to have some control.6) The LED indicator system displaying battery life works well.7) The connector is a standard 5-pin mini USB connector.8) You can sync the phone, charge the phone, and as far as I can tell do the same tasks you would do if the phone was not in the case.9) If you want to take the case off, it is fairly easy to do, and yet the case stays securely attached to the phone unless you want to take it off.10) The case covers the back of the phone from top to bottom and overlaps all four sides - unlike many cases that only cover the bottom half of the phone and overlap only three sides.  That makes it a much better choice as a protective case, in my view.11) It is slim - you can argue that there are slightly smaller and slightly slimmer cases out there, and there are, but this has a nice feel to it, and from a practical standpoint, is an excellent size.The bad things are;1) It is very difficult to flip the mute switch on the side of the phone.  I have big fingers, and once in a while I can flip the switch to 'mute' with my fingers, but most of the time I have to use the tip of a pen or a key to reach through the narrow access slot on the side.  I can never flip it to 'on' without a tool.  I really find this annoying.2) The case takes a very long time to recharge.  I mean a VERY long time.  I would guess about 5 - 7 hours if it is nearly completely run down.  But I have developed the habit of recharging overnight (I use the phone alarm for wake-up, and plug the phone in on my nightstand), and that works fine, unless I forget to plug it in - then the next day I have to be careful not to exhaust the battery.3) The battery life seems to be deteriorating - I have had the device 7 months, and it still works fine, but it seems to not be holding quite as much charge as it did when new.4) The case is a sliding two piece case, and the upper piece appears pretty fragile when the case is taken off the phone.  It is very sturdy when on the phone.  So when I do not have a pen or a key to reach through the narrow slot to mute the phone, I have to slide the upper piece up and off the phone so that I can access the mute switch.  I am always concerned that I will damage the upper piece - but so far I have not damaged it.5) I am in an area with very poor AT&T; reception (so what's new - hurry T-mobile and get the I-phone).  But the case seems to have zero adverse affect.  Reception quality appears equal with or without the case.ADDENDUM - Yesterday I lost my phone - left it in a rental car at the Orlando airport, and when I went back 20 minutes later, the phone had gotten up off the seat and walked away, and of course, no one knew where it was hiding - probably it climbed into someone's pocket - so this morning I got a new I-phone - another 3G - and after researching the cases available for several hours, I came to the conclusion that this Trent case was still the best choice for my needs - so I bought another one for me new phone.  I guess that is as good a testamonial as anyone could give.

As anyone that owns an iphone knows the battery life is woefully inadequate if you use for anything other than a phone for a few minutes a day.We looked at every battery case out there and the IMP130 seemed to be the best choice going on reviews we had seen and specs on the website etc.I am confident that we made the right choice, there is no degradation of signal like in some other cases, it is less bulky than the other cases, the battery last longer than the other cases, the battery is made by the same company that makes the OEM batteries for Apple.The case is a perfect fit except for the mute switch is a bit harder to get to unless you have finger nails.EDIT: (Just got another one today 7/30/10 and the newer model has a larger hole for the mute button so that one tiny complaint is now fixed) So the case is now basically perfect.We get approx twice the battery life of the iphone itself so easily enough to last all day long using it about as much as you would like.For long trips or camping trips we also purchased an IMP880 and we can hook up both iphones to it and recharge both phones & cases 2-3 times each.Another very good thing about either the IMP130 and IMP880 is the fact that New Trent is an outstanding company to deal with, very responsive and will literally bend over backwards to make you happy.I have absolutely zero complaints about the 3 products we received from them (2 IMP130's and 1 IMP880) they work exactly as advertised are better to actually FAR better than the competition and as if that wasn't enough the cast HALF AS MUCH!I would, and have recommended everyone I know to get one of these and most everyone has, all are very pleased.I love my iphone but I could not even imagine owning one now without this case.
summary: Best iphone battery case out there

reviewText: Good: Certainly does provide a decent about of additional power, I was pleased with that. You never know how accurate the extended life claims are. Also no one I talked to could tell I had the case on my phone. I was concerned that the phone microphone being covered would muffle the sound. The slits in the case seem to work just fine however. I was concerned with how "frail" the case was going to be but it seems pretty stout. I wasn't going to drop it or anything to see how stout it is but I feel confident it would hold up to the same amount of abuse as many other cases. Maybe do even better then a lot.Not Good?? The case is fairly heavy but that is to be expected when adding a battery. I have an Otter case and it does not have a battery but is just as heavy. The weight on that case comes from it being very rugged. So for me the weight wasn't an issue at all. It was actually lighter then what I expected.

This is a perfect battery pack for the iPhone 4 (and I hope for my soon-to-arrive 4s). It is compact, good looking and provides easy access to all of the ports and buttons on the iPhone. It has the ability to charge itself and the iPhone from a single USB connection, which cuts down on the number of adapters the traveler needs to carry. It even allows the iPhone to be synced while inserted, although with iOS 5, most syncing will happen wirelessly.The Trent folks make economical, high quality iAccessories, and this one is most highly recommended.
summary: Perfect Battery Pack for the iPhone 4

reviewText: I found this product to be very thin considering it is an extended battery case. It gave my iphone double the battery life and for the size that made me really like this product. It does take a full night to charge when first receiving it but after that it works like a charm! The cable it comes with is about the same length as an iphone cable so it does not really hinder you to switch over. Over all i like this product for the size and extended power it provides. It is perfect for those overseas traveling or long road trips.

I was hesitant on removing my iPhone from it's total encasement in my Otter defender case, but this may be the only case which will change my mind. I enjoy having the ability to recharge my dying phone battery with the push of a button, and it occurs quickly. That is one less cord I have to carry around! The case is sleek, nicely fits in the hand and is not bulky or heavy. There is also the added bonus of being able to wirelessly synch to iTunes while the backup battery is charging your phone. Although I am still hesitant about not having my screen fully protected, I will just have to be careful. I would recommend this highly to those power hogs.

I really wanted to love this case.  Given the price, I was so excited, I bought three of them about two months ago.  The ones I bought were for a iPhone 4S.  The case was great at first except for one major design flaw.  Every time you unplug the case, it automatically goes into charge mode, trying to charge your iPhone.  It's full!  It doesn't need to charge it!  This requires you to depress the charge button on the back EVERY time you unplug it from power.Another thing that popped up less than 60 days after ownership is the two small clips that hold the top piece onto the bottom half of the case.  These wear out easily and the top half comes off with no effort at all.  (See photo I submitted under this item's photos) This really sucks when you have your phone in your pocket and pull it out to answer.  The top  half either slides off into your pocket or falls to the floor when removing from your pocket.  This might not be a big deal for ladies and their purses, but for guys, it is not good.  I did not expect this only two months into ownership.Given these to flaws, I'm only giving it two stars.
summary: Case goes into charge mode every time you unplug it, requiring you to turn it off.  :o(

reviewText: "Very fast shipment and great iPhone battery case. This case charged my iPhone 4S from dead in a little over 2 hours. Its not to bulky and feels good in hands. Best case by far and you can't find a better deal. This is my 3rd different case from New Trent and will but again. Highley recommended."
summary: Great Battery Case for the iPhone 4S

reviewText: I am a huge fan of all Apple products and they have just about everything figured out.....except battery life on the iPhones!  I travel quite a bit and just wanted to figure out how to count on one full day of battery life with my phone.  After reading several reviews I chose the New Trent model and absolutely love it!The first day I owned it I was on the phone for a solid 8 hours.  I couldn't think of a better test for my new battery extender than that and although I was down around 10% charge by the time I went to bed I was very pleased.The case is very small in comparison to some other battery life extenders and although it adds weight to my phone I don't think it is excessive.  I charge my phone overnight every night and if I can survive an entire day on that charge, problem solved!!I highly recommend this product!
summary: No more searching for power outlet!!

reviewText: You wont have an issue if you purchase the Morphie. All these mom and pop brand names that just come out and make something out of junk material is an insult.

This is my second case for my iPhone 4. Before getting the New Trent IMP210B I was using a rubber case from Speck that, while it protected my phone from the odd fall, did nothing else beside acquire scratches. It was also a pain to get my phone in and out of the Speck case. So far, this battery case is much better than my old one.At first look the New Trent case looks great. It has a textured finish that makes it easy to hold but not grab onto my pants when I try to pull it out of my pocket like some Otter Box phone cases. The finish on it matches my phone and aside from the extra width from the battery, it does not look like the phone has a case at all. It has a 2-part design that makes it very easy to attach and detach from the phone.I am a heavy iPhone user. Whether I am using maps, browsing the web or listening to podcasts in my car, my phone is in constant use throughout the day. Instead of looking for an outlet to plug into, this case has allowed me to go without charging for an entire day. The other day I let my phone drop down to 20% batter life, turned on the case battery and saw it go up to 75% in ~30 minutes. I was able to go for the rest of the day without charging my phone, although I still charge it at night.Some reviewers have mentioned that it is difficult to access the volume buttons on the side of the case. I have had no such issues, although it does take a few times to get used to the case. My only issue is that the battery engages immediately after charging it while attached to the phone. I normally turn off the battery after charging, but I feel that the battery should NOT start charging the phone by default. But this is a very small gripe, as it takes me 2 seconds to turn off the case.In my opinion, this is a "Must Buy" for anyone who worries about their battery running low.

PROS:Slim and slender design makes for convenient handling, storage, or use.Lightweight material.4 Blue LED lights on back plate of case makes it east to identify charge level (1 blinking LED = <20%, 1 solid LED = 20%-40%, 2 solid LEDs = 40%-60%, 3 solid LEDs = 60%-80%, 4 solid LEDs = 80%-100%).Ergonomically comfortable to grasp, fits well while in hand.Full charging time for iPhone 4 internal battery while docked in battery case is comparable to conventional charging method.CONS:Battery case sits flush with front face of iPhone, providing little if any protection from damage.USB connection port when plugged in protrudes more than 1" from bottom of battery case, making it susceptible to being damaged.Battery case obscures iPhone's 30 pin Apple USB port, making it unusable with Apple accessories.Confusing when determining if battery case status is on/off via LED lights on back plate when iPhone not docked.RECOMMENDATIONS:Incorporate slim, raised "lip" around front face of battery case to protect iPhone from damage.Design USB connection port to be shorter when plugged in.Move USB connection port to long side of battery case and incorporate "optional" port for iPhone's 30 pin Apple USB access.Design "slide-type" switch specifically to turn on/off battery case.RATING FROM LOWEST 1 STAR TO HIGHEST 5 STARS: 4 stars

I've had the case for about a week now. It charges up well and extends the life of the battery significantly.I got this so I could use GPS based trail applications while I'm out walking. Using the iPhone battery alone the GPS application will drain the battery in about 2 hours. I'll be testing it on a trail this afternoon. The phone stayed fully charged while using the GPS on a hike of about 5 hours.I have noticed that I keep getting the "charging is not supported with this accessory" message but, the unit is charging my phone. The message seems to appear when the battery pack is left on continuously. Maybe there is a variation in the voltage? Has anyone else encountered this?I bought this in May 2012, its now February 2013. I haven't seen the "charging not supported" in quite a while.Other than the top piece being a little loose, I wish it fit a little tighter. I would rate this case at 4.5 stars. I purchased this case because it had the best and highest rated reviews on Amazon.com. reviewText: I didn't want to review this until I'd used it for a while.The Symbian OS is being phased out and the GUI isn't very intuitive.  Some menu selections need one touch, others need two. Can change ringtones and background without using the internet or phone company (unlike my old Samsung).  Battery is easily accessible and cheap to replace.  Keypad took a little getting used to (touchscreen) and switching to other characters.  Wi-fi is great.  I can log on at the mall, bar, stores or at home.  You will need the headphones plugged in to recieve radio stations.  Headphones suck, but not as bad as Apple's.  USB cap doesn't fit very well.  At least the lint blows out.  Screen layout has limited changes.Camera is o.k. (it's a cell) and so is the video.  Didn't realize it had a small camera sensor on the other side, so you can see yourself on the display.I'd liked to have gotten a Droid or i-Phone, but this was within my price range.  No contract either.  Put my old SIM in and connected to AT&T;'s network.  No drops / good reception.  UNLOCKED!!!Aside from the GUI (1 vs. 2 taps) I really like this phone.  Apple may have a better GUI, but for the price ($50 more out of pocket, but no data contract or 2 yr. commitment) it was really worth it.

I was using a Nokia E71 and decided to upgrade to a touch screen with full multi-media capabilites. I couldn't be happier with my purchase.UNBOXING: My phone came with Nokia's Car Kit which was a nice surprise. The phone bracket can be placed on the dash for using the GPS when flying down the highway. A car charger AND home charger are included along with some fancy headphones. The only accessory I needed to add was a case. Otter Box makes a great case for the X6.SET-UP: Wonderfully easy to set-up. I inserted my SIM card and plugged in the charger then off to the races. Initial set-up is quick, easy, and intuitive. Within minutes my contacts, email, 3G, and internet were running fluidly.TOUCH SCREEN: It takes a bit to get used to the screen, especially coming from a tactile keyboard on my old E71. Some actions require a double-tap while others are single taps. There is a slight color change on the buttons letting you know that a second tap is needed. If your impatient and keep hitting the buttons the X6 will lock-up. Patience, young grasshopper, patience.CALLS: No dropped calls so far with good sound clarity. The screen automatically disables itself so your cheek won't activate anything. Voice dialing is a breeze to set-up.INTERNET: Initally the X6 was somewhat slow using the built in web browser, but then I downloaded the Opera browser. Whoa Nelly! The Opera browser flies along with proper 3G speeds. Web pages can be zoomed in/out if that site is not mobile ready.MUSIC/VIDEO: The X6 has 16gb memory on board. More than enough for my music and videos. The sound is somewhat "tinny" when played through the speakers but the included headset makes up for it. Videos play without any chop and the screen resolution is wonderful.A-GPS: You will need a data plan to use the GPS. The GPS only took one minute for initial set-up and locking. The OVI Maps are okay, but installing Google Maps allows you to sync with Google and keep all your starred favorites. The Ovi Maps didn't show my street, but Google did.BLUETOOTH: My Plantronics Voyager Pro paired to the X6 within seconds. No connection issues.WIFI: Again, the Wifi worked immediately. I tested the Wifi at Borders, Starbucks, McDonalds, and the local park. No issues with scanning.CAMERA: 5mp is decent for a cellphone and the X6 doesn't slouch one bit. The Carl Zeiss lens helps, but you'll still need decent lighting. The video is adequate but nowhere near HD quality.IMPRESSION: Excellent value for the money, especially since the X6 is unlocked. No issues surfing the web, listening to music, taking pictures or watching videos. The X6 does everything it's supposed to plus more.

Many of us travel today with a bunch of electronic devices that require access to a USB port for charging. This handy little device provides four USB ports, each providing 500mA at 5 volts. It is compact, has AC prongs that fold into the unit and four USB ports with diodes to indicate power on/off status on the port. The unit is reasonably well made. The AC prongs were easy to pull out for use, fold up with no problem and have no significant play or looseness. The unit is small, about 2 x 4.5 x 1 inches and weigh little.I don't know how long they'll last in operation, but at the price, they're economical enough to replace as needed.Just remember: this is not suitable for fast-charging your devices.Jerry

These batteries described as OEM are not all the same. It is a bit of a gamble buying these batteries but fortunately it doesn't involve much money. The first time I purchased inexpensive Droid batteries from Amazon I received two batteries (from UnitedIntegral according to Amazon's order history page). Each worked for about three hours after my older, original battery lasted at least twice that. They clearly were not real OEM batteries (or were defective), but at the price I didn't mind too much. For the price it was still of value to have spares on me in case my main battery died while traveling, even if I did have to change the battery twice on some days.Obviously having extra batteries with a full charge is much better, and I tried again more recently from another seller (listed as OEM Planet in the order history page). This time both batteries are lasting longer than the original battery in the phone (presumably being true OEM batteries with my original battery now having a reduced life due to age). The original battery typically had to be recharged in late afternoon. The last two batteries I received typically last into the evening, allowing me to wait until I'm home to recharge.I'm not certain if the listings as to where each battery came from is accurate as when I click on the first order listed as from UnitedIntegral I get to a page for OEM Planet. When I clicked on the more recent order which lists as OEM Planet on the history page, I wind up at a page saying yet a third company, Accessory One.When I tried to write a review of the second set I wound up on the same page as the review I wrote of the first set despite receiving them from different sellers and a considerable difference between the two. It appears Amazon is lumping all the Droid battery reviews together regardless of seller, but from my experience these are not the same product from each seller. This probably also explains the differences in reviews here.

While I already have a main cell phone, a Galaxy Note 2, I do not like to carry it with me all the times when I hop in the car for short trips (bulk) or take it with me on my multi-mile running exercises (potential rain/damage).  However, it's always nice to have peace of mind in carrying a phone when driving around, due to potential crimes, accidents, tow service, or simply to make a call to a friend or family in a sponteanous event of need.  This is where Tmobile's prepaid shines because I can do all the above with their Gold Rewards plan.  Simply purchase a $100 card and your prepaid account turns to GOLD status which means your minutes don't expire for a year AND if you top off the account with as low as $10, all your minutes roll over and last another YEAR.  So if you read this right, that means you can theoretically get annual prepaid service for $10 idefinitely.  Of course, this only works if you don't use a lot of minutes - which works fine for someone who sparsely uses their phone to begin with.As for the T139 itself, it's a typical small flip phone.  Text entry was easier than I remembered with these numeric keypads so not too bad for short messages.  Camera is VGA but quality is surprisingly pretty decent and useable for situations where you need it.  Battery life is, of course, phenomenal when compared to any smart phone.  Also, with bluetooth, if you keep this in your car and hook it up to a cig charger, you can have a real "car phone" where the bluetooth will just sync all the time to your radio and never worry of a dead battery.Overall, if you're looking into purchasing a secondary phone with prepaid, this is a great model to get.
summary: Makes for a great car or secondary phone

reviewText: Samsung T 139 phone:  What I like about this phone is that I don't have to worry about a case hanging on my belt which made me feel like a geek. INTROMy wife really wanted to like this case. She had long looked for a Robin's Egg blue case, and while was a little different from the Amazon color (I use industry-standard calibration, so it's not just my monitor) she was very excited to receive this!BUILD/QUALITYWe were impressed at first with the quality and build. It looked like it would protect the phone very well if it was ever dropped, as it was thick and hard without being brittle. It snapped on and was quite solidly applied - it didn't look like it was going to come off easily unlike some other shells we had tried.WHY 3 STARS?Well sadly this case is now in the trash. The front part is rubberized (as supposed to the rear hard shell), and after only a few weeks the rubber started peeling off in the same manner as a pencil eraser would. This wasn't a huge deal at first, but as you can imagine once rubber starts to wear off and lose its smooth edge, it gets a lot harder to clean. The second tragedy was the the front rubber part eventually snapped in two, as other reviewers had mentioned happening. While this didn't great affect protection, I was very disappointed with Speck who normally make great covers, and we ended up going with a case-mate hybrid that has lasted ever since. With all of this, keep in mind that my wife doesn't put her phone in her pocket nor abuse it in any way - it is either in the cellphone pocket in her purse, on a bedside table, or in her hand.OVERALLSadly we cannot recommend this case, and would highly suggest the Case-Mate Hybrid instead. While I own several Speck products (my macbook Pro shell going on four years now), this once turned out to be a disappointment. If you don't mind aesthetics going down the drain from broken parts, I guess this would be a decent thing to keep on your phone?

The product delivered is a Motorola P323 Battery Charger and comes with a Motorola one-year warranty. The Amazon product description says that this charger will ONLY charge Motorola brand batteries. That is NOT true.  This charger will charge BC, BK, BP, BP6X, BS, BN, BT, or BQ type OEM or other branded batteries for Motorola cell phones. One reviewer complained that the charger would not charge his generic battery. Something must have been wrong with his battery. Because I can say with absolute certainty that this charger will work with non Motorola branded batteries. I just completed fully charging a generic BT battery. The charger is two sided to charge different types of batteries. Be aware that this charger does not come with its own power supply. You will have to use your Motorola cell phone charger with a mini or micro USB connection, car charger, or a USB cable for connection to your computer. The output of this charger is only 450 mA, so it may take as long as 3 or more hours to fully charge a completely discharged battery. This, of course, depends a lot on the amount of discharge and the mAh rating of your battery. The Motorola cell phone charger has a greater mA charge rating and will therefore charge your batteries in the cell phone quicker. Other than this minor issue, the charger works flawlessly to fully charge spare batteries. It has a charge indicator LED that's orange for pre-charge, red when charging and green when fully charged. If it flashes red / green constantly, you have a defective battery. I would highly recommend this product to anyone needing a charger for their spare batteries.UPDATE: If you want this identical charger with the AC wall charger included, check the Amazon website for "Motorola SPN5564A P323 Platform Battery Only Charger with micro USB Travel Charger".

This dock isn't perfect:- It lacks an 'eject' button to easily remove the phone; it's a two-handed affair since the charger grabs the phone pretty tightly.- This could be due to the additional weight, but this dock isn't quite as rock-solid while driving as the official motorola one.- Bulkier than it needs to be, charger cable sticks out the side instead of being in the back, out-of-sight.With all that said, it's a nice solid dock that charges your phone without requiring the extra step of chasing down your charger cable; great for people who are frequently removing & replacing the phone in the dock. reviewText: It could be a little cheaper, but overall, this mount is great. It fits perfectly with the Seidio hard case (remember to remove the insert) or can be used with a naked droid with the insert. The cable was long enough to go under the steering wheel, up the far left side of the dash, and around to the doc. I hardly see any cable at all.Some minor annoyances: 1) the bracket comes right up to the bottom buttons (the back key and menu key) on the droid and sometimes it's hard to press them. 2) This is two pieces- the suction cup w/ tilting mount and the phone holder mount. They fit together with sliding tabs. I've had the holder come apart when I was trying to remove my phone, once. Maybe I should superglue it together.But overall, this thing has been awesome. I use it all the time for social GPS (Waze - get it!) to get notified of speed traps and traffic. And/Or you can use it as a music player.

I bought this unit mostly because it fit into the space I had in my car for a Droid mount.  It does the job of holding the phone steady while driving, but has several things about the design that just seem odd.1. There is a power out port on the side.  This is a mini-USB..  Problem is, nobody makes a mini-USB to mini-USB cord that would allow the unit to be used to charge other USB devices.. So... that port is essentially useless.2. The mini-USB plug that is supposed to go into the phone is loosely mounted, so when you slide the Droid in, you have to line the plug up with the port on the phone.. Why???3. There is a sleeve that is removable that surrounds the phone.  I'm assuming this is to allow the dock to be used with a Droid in a protective case (although the case would have to be thin to fit).  Problem is, there is no way to secure this sleeve in place short of gluing it down.  If you don't do so, it constantly pulls out when you remove the phone.. Kind of a pain.. So much so that eventually did glue mine in place.4. There is a huge amount of space behind the phone (basically the bottom 2/3 of the phone has 3/4" of space behind the phone of open space.. This makes the dock much deeper than it really needs to be.  Maybe this space has a use for some users, but I can't imagine for what..My suggestion:  Buy the Motorola Droid car dock instead.  Its cheaper and does the job better.

I purchased this item over the one Motorola sells for the Droid because the Motorola dock will not accept a phone with a protective cover on it.  I for one am not willing to pry my phone out of its protection every time so I can place it in a dock.  Seidio fixed that little oversite by including an adapter so you can use it with or without their cover in place.  This item is sturdy, and easily adjustable for vertical and horizontal movement because of an adjustable friction ball where the docking tray meets the mounting arm.  The suction cup is very secure to a clean window and feels like it would take a tremendous force to get it to come off unintentionally.  All the buttons on the phone are still accessible while docked, although you cannot slide the keyboard out (which you shouldn't be doing in a car anyway!) until you remove it from the dock.  The only down side we found to having this mounted in the window of the car (which has nothing to do with the actual Seidio dock itself) is that the heat of the sun caused my wifes phone to begin acting strangely and eventually had to be shut down until it cooled before it would take a charge again.  Be careful how long you leave your Droid exposed to direct sun in an unnattended car, in OR out of a docking station.
summary: Some companies still make good stuff!

I almost bought this car mount because I have a case installed that I don't want to remove every time I use a car mount like you need to do with the stock Motorola model. Guess what? I made my own with a generic XM Roady holder that I no longer use since I cancelled my XM. I just super-glued a 15-cent round magnet onto the mount in the proper place to operate the car dock feature automatically and voila! -- a good, solid, dock system for little cost. I was so excited about this item but I quickly realized that Seidio must have rushed through quality and control on this item since others are having the same problem. Seidio needs to redesign and fix this problem! I would not buy this car kit if I were you!Initial Review in March of 2010:Yes, this car kit is very good. My AC plug is located in the center console of my Camry so there is enough cord length to reach the cradle which I placed on the windshield to left side of the steering wheel. reviewText: I've resisted getting a smart phone until now.This one is smart enough and big enough to make me want it. It is truly an amazing device. Takes your connection to the online world to a new level...Two caveats:It's a complex device, it takes a lot of work to get it set up right for you. The benefits are huge, when you do get it tuned to your needs, but that can take days...  If you're not 'techie' at all, you may be happier with a simpler, no set up, but still very capable phone, like a 'Droid' phone or an iPhone for example. They're not quite as fully functioned, but they are much easier to get started on. If you can live with a week or so of fiddling to get it working right, the HTC HD2 blows them away, though,And it, and its operating system, are both very new. There's one or two little bugs still in there, and T-Mobile staff don't yet have much knowledge or all the equioment they need. I expect both of those to be fixed soon, though, and there are simply work-arounds for the thing(s) that don't work right yet.Those are my only two concerns. I love this phone.Oh, and don't buy a car charger, buy a cigarette lighter to USB plug from Walmart (in the Automotive section, for about $6), and  use the USB cable that comes with the wall charger...
summary: Finally a smart phone where I can read the screen!

I wish I could say I got to try it out, but it was obvious when I got the package that the item had been heavily used and even broken by the previous user. reviewText: I have a Motorola H17 that I recently ordered and these worked on it like a charm. Even though the earpiece of the Mororola H17 is not bad the piece that hooks around the ear would hurt after a while.  These solved the problem.

The short form:  BUY THESE!  THEY WORK!  THEY MAKE THE ICON THE VERY BEST HEADSET ON THE MARKET TODAY!!The long form:Imagine my distress when I found the PERFECT headset for call clarity and features such as voice calling and music streaming, and it was the MOST uncomfortable headset I'd ever worn in my life!  That is how I felt about the Jawbone ICON.  (See separate review.)I read all of these positive reviews with skepticism, but ordered the ear gels out of desperation!  They are everything everyone is saying!!  They are super comfortable, they channel the volume into your ear (I've got it turned WAY down) and you will NOT lose your headset even without that AWFUL hook Jawbone provides.  I will say that I may be lucky that the small fits my ear perfectly - if one doesn't fit your ear snugly and comfortably I guess you could lose it, but mine fits like a finely honed jigsaw puzzle piece - it goes in and out easily, but fits perfectly and is "joined" so I won't lose it!  I don't know how to describe it :(  There is not any pressure on my ear - it just - FITS and when I shake my head it stays in snugly.  I'm not ENTIRELY certain it is allowing the ICON to rest on my cheek enough to touch the voice sensor like Jawbone advises, but I attribute that to my really skinny face rather than any fault of the gels - I think someone who didn't look drawn all the time will not have any trouble with that issue.  **** IMPORTANT **** The reviewers who say the gels do not fit the ICON have not placed the smallest doughnut shaped earpiece supplied by Jawbone on their ICON before installing the Jabra eargel!  Do that, and it fit's PERFECTLY!Now for the cons.  I know we get to rate the sellers separately, but we can't leave specific comments for each other in that section.  So I just need to say that Happy Cellular did not meet my expectations.  (THEY CAME THROUGH - READ UPDATE BELOW!)  If all you care about is getting a product and getting it fast they did fine.  BUT I cared about a few other things.  I could have gotten this same product on e-bay in "bulk" packaging for $4 less, but I wanted the real deal - both to know they are genuine, and to know they are CLEAN.  I got neither reassurance because these arrived in generic bulk packaging - just three little plastic ziplock bags inside a mailer.  AND to make my impression of the company worse, they shipped it media mail.  My understanding - and please correct me if I'm wrong - is that these ear gels would not qualify for media mail. It seems to charge to 95%.  Sometimes more, but the only time it says 100% is if I'm using the phone while it is charging.This charger does work decent.  It charges the phone quickly but the charge itself doesn't seem to last as long as I think it should.  I made the settings on my phone use as less energy as possible, including turning down the backlight to reduce the battery load.  If I start out on 100% charge, by the time I get to work listening to music on low, the charge is down to 88%, give or take.  With traditional charging, there's barely a dent and is usually around 95%-98% by the time I get to work.  I'd say the battery runs down about 10% faster than traditional charging.  At first I figured it was the battery, since my phone went up and I reverted to using my 5+ year old 3GS handset.  When my new 3GS arrived though, the result using this charger was the same.On the pro side, you don't have to deal with shorted out cords, it stops charging to prevent over-charges and you can just set your phone on it instead of the constant, plugging in and out of the traditional cord, which may reduce the chance of shorting out the charging port. Samsung Solstice is a touch screen phone that tries to make leaps towards features of a smart phone. In summary, the Solstice is a slim, dependable, and easy to use phone.My thoughts:- I like the touchscreen. It's generally very reactive, just off by a millimeter or so sometimes. Very responsive and becomes second nature after a while.- The main screen lets you put your favorite apps on a bar that acts like the taskbar of a PC. You can also drag the app icon onto the background for ease of access. The charge meter, network indicator, and time are all generally lit well and easy to read.- On idle mode, it's difficult to pocket dial and mistouch something, as long as you lock the phone each time. It's very simple to use and becomes an easy habit after a while. Almost every phone has that option. If you don't lock it, then it's your fault, not the phone.- Design is very nice, actually. The back button is the center on the bottom, with the dial and end call buttons on the left and right ,respectively. The lock and unlock button is subtly placed on the top right, which is very convenient. On the left side of the phone, there's the volume control, which also is slim enough that you wouldn't accidentally bump it. The battery charger and usb slot has a cover that is attached to the phone, preventing any dust or debris from damaging the phone.- Camera is fairly good. 2 megapixels is enough and the pictures are generally clear.- Call quality is fair. It's certainly not optimal, as you may get some bad signal sometimes. However, more often than not you'll have a good experience. A caution though, is that the phone can become obscenely hot after talking, even for as little as 10 minutes. I'd recommend a bluetooth or headset.- I like the ease of connectivity between this phone and PC. You'll need a USB chord, and I recommend getting theOriongadgets Sync & Charge USB Cable for Samsung Solstice A887 (Black), or any compatible chord. It's a simple drag and drop into this phone's folder. I've easily uploaded songs and pictures.- The texting interface is solid and generally responsive. You may have some typos, but with some careful practice, it's fairly easy. Everything has a learning curve, so give it some time! However, you may only text up to 7 different contacts on a text message.* * * *Some counter arguments against existing reviews:- A reviewer said that the battery life was horrible. Not for me, and others. Me and other Samsung Solstice users have no issue with the battery charging. On estimate, I'd say a fully charged phone can last up to 3-4 hours of talk time. The battery charging is good, but the battery life is definitely sub-par. I'm able to charge every couple days, so it's not that bad.- Bluetooth connectivity is a breeze. After some simple instructions, you'll be connected in no time. MySamsung WEP460 Bluetooth Headset [Retail Packaging] works perfectly with this phone.Overall, a solid phone that is capable as an all-purpose daily phone and tries to have features of a smart phone. Also, as a word of caution, it seems that the not so favorable reviewers of this phone just simply had a bad luck experience with this phone. I'm sorry to hear that, but there are plenty of happy Samsung Solstice owners like me, my brother, and several friends, but they just haven't expressed their satisfaction here on Amazon. The people whom had bad experiences just seem to scream louder. Anyways, don't let that prevent you from buying this phone. Highly recommended phone.
summary: Solid and dependable phone - with many fine details
