summary: Giving low stars because the cords received were not HTC cords - I believe they are Blackberry or generic

reviewText: I really am please with thus product it is Durable! This cord is actually better than the one supplied with my phone! Before I ordered it I had gone through 5 cords. I recommend this product it is great!

This cable completely drained my battery.  My Evo would not respond at all - to anything.  When I plugged in to the stock charging cable provided with my Evo when I purchased it, the charging light wouldn't even come on.  I had to go out and buy a new battery.  (So much for saving money.)

As many others have said these cables do not work for charging your phone. Cheap Chinese knockoffs. Data transfer works but no charging (although the phone reports that it is charging, the meter doesn't go up) Tested on HTC EVO 4G and HTC Design 4G.

I wanted a radio frequency blocking wallet and there are few on the market. This one is slim, stylish, and organizes plenty of cards.  Plus, it has a zippered coin pocket, which many others didn't.  The material is somewhat slippery, which makes it easy to slide in and out of my purse.  Wish it came in more colors.
It's a nice ladies wallet, secures all debit cards and credit cards from RFID. I will definitely use this everyday.
Roomy, lots of slots for things, pretty inside and out... came on time, packaging was sufficient... was a Christmas gift for my Aunt.

The wallet looks so much better in person than it looks on Amazon.I love the weight of the wallet, it's very lightweight.  I'm not really a fan of orange but I adore the interior fabric.  My old wallet was a Coach wallet that I spent WAY too much money on.  My new wallet is so much nicer.I'm very happy with my purchase!

I was honestly bit surprised by this wallet, I thought it would be entirely functional, but this wallet is really nice.  It is roomy, without being too bulky.  I can fit all of my credit cards, customer reward cards into this wallet easily.  It has a very spacious coin portion, and honestly I couldn't ask for more.  I love that this wallet also has RFID protection.  I feel safe and comfortable with this wallet for so many reasons.  If you are looking for an RFID blocking wallet, this is definitely one you should consider.

The only good thing about this is that it's waterproof.  It's bigger than expected and even turned up all the way, it would no way be loud enough for a boat an being more than 3 ft away.  I was very disappointed.

This case does just as advertised.  It givrs a great sound to your portable device, while keeping it safe from water.  Since it floats, we case use it in the pool without concern.  As the case is solid, you can not access your devices controls once it is sinde.  However, if you have it set on your play list or favorite channel, you will be good to go.

Sometimes I'm not sure why I get things but I bought this because I wanted to listen to my ipod in the shower.  This is not a good choice for that. The first issue is that you can't interact with the ipod at all except for the volume. The volume knob is not easy to turn, especially with wet fingers.  However, I can see this being good for a playlist you just want to hear out on a ski mountain or camping somewhere.  I'm actually not sure where I would want to just set up this and listen. The sound quality is no better than than the ipod itself. All this does is amplify it.  It is a nice strong case though that will protect anything you put in there.

I bought this as a waterproof alternative to the Goalzero Rockout. It has a few benefits and drawbacks compared to that speaker. First, it's certainly not as loud. I find myself turning it all the way up for virtually every purpose. If you open it, it doesn't have to be turned up quite as high to be loud enough to hear. Second, it's more noisy than Goalzero's offering. At high volumes, there is an audible hiss.These drawbacks are, to my mind, overcome by this speaker's positive points. First, it is obviously quite robust. The case, latches, speaker grille, and even internal components are of reassuringly sturdy quality. It's waterproof--but then you probably knew that. Finally, it takes AA batteries, which I find vastly preferable to a non-replaceable lithium.
summary: Okay, but falls down on a few points.

reviewText: I purchased this product to use on a fishing kayak. I have been using it anywhere I want to listen to the music on my phone without ear buds. The sound is quite impressive especially considering the price. I am in sales and have shown this item to a lot of people and so far all of them have agreed that the quality of the sound out of the speaker is quite impressive. I had two people at the Sprint store agree. They were trying to sell this expensive Bluetooth boom box (not waterproof) and were amazed at the price of Eco Extreme. They were not even aware that this product was on the market. One of the guys at the Sprint store could not wait to order one for himself.

this is the best investment ever! I go paddle boarding at the lake a lot so waterproof speaker for my phone makes it more fun for me. It's a very good quality, and is pretty loud!I would definitely recommend it to my friends!

I got mine last year when it was around 40 bucks.  I've used it at the beach and sailing in 2-person dinghies and a j/22.  It's loud enough to give nice background music on the J/22 if I keep it on the floor of the cockpit.  Not booming, rocking-out loud, but loud enough.  If you clip it to the boom the music gets lost in the wind or when the speaker swings facing away.  I haven't fully submerged it yet, but I'm pretty confident it would be fine.  All in all a good purchase that I use a lot with either a cheap sansa mp3 player or a phone with Pandora.

Wow what a great, sturdy little speaker for the price. If you're looking for BOSE sound quality this probably isn't for you.  I bought this for a recent week at the beach, and our whole family enjoyed it.  It did a good job keeping my iphone 4 free from the sand.  Was very easy to connect and turn on.  The three or four AAs kept the unit powered up for the entire week listening to tunes on the beach and back at our beach house.Its not SUPER loud, especially on the beach. Probably was listenable to the three or four of us sitting closest to it - which worked well for us.  If you want to blast a larger area, might want to look at the larger unit.  The speaker gets distorted at its max volume.I noticed some people complaining that they dropped this thing in the water, and it wasn't fully waterproof.  I'll just give that an eye roll.  Its a $40 speaker that will definitely survive splashes and wet hands, probably even a quick dunk.  You might not want to take it scuba diving.Very happy with this purchase.

Bought it for beach/pool side music. Speaker is loud enough to be played next to the hot tub and I have tested the cases claim of being waterproof. Once case is closed speaker sound does gain a deeper/fuller sound. One thing to note is the case may have a problem with the size of your phone. I have a Droid Razr Maxx and my phone wont fit in the mesh inside the case. I have to just place my phone in the case and plug in the audio cord. The Razr Maxx is almost too tall to fit at 5.15" or 131mm so google your phone measurements to be sure you phone will fit. 5 stars highly recommended for inexpensive, near water, music.

It was bigger then I thought it was gonna be. I took it on a kayak trip and it got splashed a lot. It held up just fine. I gave it three stars because the sound sucks. It gets decently loud but the sound itself isn't great.

I recently purchased the Eco Extreme waterproof case to protect our MP3 player while out on the river tubing, on the boat, or by the pool.The unit seems to be well made. I wish the packaging would have been a little better because by leaving the speaker grille exposed there was a small spot that the paint was rubbed off. Not enough of a problem to return it but it still should have been protected better.Also, the clips seem a little flimsy. I had one already "pop off" but it was an easy fix to snap it back on. Hopefully, this won't happen when the case is wet and when it could potentially allow water in.The speaker case has surprisingly good sound. Once you get the volume set correctly on your mp3 player (about 3/4 on an iPod Touch in my case) the speaker sounds pretty good. I wish it was a little bit louder but for its size and being only one speaker it has decent volume.I'm a little worried about the clips holding up but for the most part its a pretty nice mp3 player speaker. I would recommend it if you are looking for a combination speaker and waterproof case for your MP3 player.

A LOT bigger than expected.  The pictures really does not do it justice, nor does the description and dimensions.  Other than that, I was excited to give it a try because I'm looking for a good speaker to take canoeing.  I put my phone around 75% and plugged it in.  The sound was terribly low even at full volume on the Eco and not very clear or crisp at all.  I can't see hearing this in the great outdoors.  A couple seconds later, it starting emitting a high squealing noise.  I stopped the music and the noise continued.  I don't know what the problem was.  I unplugged everything, turned the device off, and started over, but the same results, so I RMA-ed it.  I was really hoping this would be better.
summary: Not as good as it's rating

reviewText: I wasn't sure how good a sound quality this product was going to be for the price, but I was pleasantly surprised.  No it wouldn't be like a stereo system, but it is great for floating in the boat or down a river or 4 wheeling.  The inside is big enought to hold a lot more than just the iphone, it holds my keys and credit cards and money.  I would definitely recommend this product to anyone who is looking for just some personal music to listen too in outdoor settings,

Here's a case that allows music lovers to take music with them - ANYWHERE! I'm talking about the Eco-EXTREME, Rugged All Terrain Speaker Case.Take it hiking, fishing, or rock climbing! The waterproof case connects to your mp3 player with a universal 1/8" headset jack and works with most mp3 players. (See website for a list.)The high impact, shock resistant case is made of durable rubber, and includes a built-in 3" full range forward firing speaker. The sound quality is awesome - whether you're listening to rock or classical or country western. For the technical purchaser, the speaker output is 3W RMS; frequency response is 200Hz - 10 KHz. I even like the volume control on the front - it feels rugged and is very responsive.It requires 3 AA batteries that will provide about 30 hrs of play. It's very easy to set up - just plug, snap shut, and play.The internal compartment can hold your mp3 player, keys, credit cards, driver's license and cash. How handy is that on a hike!A very sturdy, detachable carabineer is included, which allows you to clip the case on a bike or backpack.The manufacturer offers the case in jet black, cobalt blue and orange peel. Retails for $49.99. I guess I'd have to say, I like everything about this case. In other words, it's EXTREMELY COOL!

This one is a gift.  Loved it so much, had to get one for a friend too!  Sound will not blow you away, but, for 30 some dollars, this is a bargain!  Only problem is, want to buy another one for more friends!
Works and sounds great. I use it mainly when I go out kayaking. No leaks so far. Pretty loud for the size.

No leaks. Used for iPhone 4s but very tight fit for Galaxy Note 3. Volume good but too low in Loud environments. No headphone jack. Still have it but use ECOXGEAR bluetooth now. Output doubled. Lithium battery You may wanna just go straight to this One. Just a question of money.

Look good at the enclosure, at first appearance this product is "rock solid" it is exactly what i wanted. (I only bought this for a shower radio for my ipod 4 and it WAS awesome for that)having said that after less then (but almost) 3 months of 4 times a week, 15 minute use the latch just crumbled to pieces? and it is so odd because this thing is so well constructed EVERYWHERE ELSE? but the latch is so inadequate! the plastic that holds the latch together is about 1/8 of a inch thick! and its a pressure lever that hooks on to the upper case and pulls it snug shut and latches while holding enough pressure to make a watertight seal. (same style latch that plastic toolboxes use) when mine broke the ipod fell out of the case and free fell until the end of the sound cable. Kinda like a dog that sprinted to the end of his leash. hopfully it did not damage the socket on the ipod. (seems to still work fine) It is amazing that this oversight was made. I wish i had the time to take a photo? ive been meaning to write this review for so long and finally got around to it and never did take the photo. i still have the speaker enclose it doesnt latch shut anymore but i can close it like a book with the ipod on the back of the toilet and still get some use of it.* If you are considering buying this despite my review make a comment here (ill get is withing 6 hours the message pops up on my phone) and ill upload a pic if your interested otherwise i dont want to bother getting the cam and laying everything out.
summary: i loved it for almost 3 moths? till it broke.. read my review...

reviewText: I used this with my iPod classic and the sound is pretty good.  It's waterproof, so I didn't worry about taking it in the boat without protection and supposedly it floats but I didn't want to test that if I didn't have to.  There's extra room inside for additional items like money and credit cards.  I've used the small $10 speakers from electronic stores as well as the ihome portable speaker.  This is the only one thats waterproof and shockproof, and the sound is comparable to ihome.  The downsides are these: 1.  I thought the sound would be louder. While it has good bass, you get that crackling noise if you turn the volume all the way up (or you have to turn down the device volume to 80%). Also, you need to aim the speaker, it will not flood an area. 2. ITS BIGGER THAN IT LOOKS!!  Don't let that clip in the picture fool you, it would definitely be akward to clip this to a backpack while hiking, etc. 3. Last, though I knew this in advance...it's not made for ipod specifically so there are no exterior play/seek controls.  Would be much better if they added that in addition to the regular plug.I would still recommend for the beach, camping, and boating as one of the best options.
I use this on the beach and in the shower to listen to music or my pod casts.  The sound is great and it's water proof so what else do you need?  I love it and highly recommend it!
summary: One of my FAVORITE things to listen to music.

reviewText: My daughter was listening to her ipod in the shower by sitting it on the counter (attached to her clock radio) and cranking it up. The whole house could sing along with her, and her brother was losing sleep. I wanted a way for her to bring the ipod into the shower with her, so the volume could be turned down. Of course, it would need to be waterproof. Enter the Eco Extreme. After hunting around quite a bit, I bought this one, because it's universal (I could use it with my Droid2, and with my Sansa Clip, and she could use it with her ipod), it's "water resistant" (true waterproof ones were too expensive, too bulky, or both), and it can be put on the shelf in the shower, or hung on the showerhead pipe. The sound, while not sound stage quality, is better than many cheapo boom boxes, and the volume is adequate for anyone listening within a 6 - 8 foot radius.You do have to set a playlist, because you can't fiddle with your mp3 player while in the moist conditions, and the batteries tend to die quickly (especially as my daughter disconnects her ipod, but forgets to turn off the Eco). Overall, though, I'd easily place this in the "buy again" category.

I use an extended lithium battery for this and so far after hours of music, it has not quit on me yet.The audio quality could be a bit of a problem or weak, especially if you don't want the sound to crack.Your best bet is keeping your audio source's (ipod, etc.) volume level at around 80%-90%. Then you can go at the highest volume on the speaker unit without the sound cracking as much. Also, the blue color depicted on this photo is a lot lighter than the actual unit.
summary: It does what it says it does

reviewText: We had originally bought her a big-ass wireless Blue-Tooth speaker, but she wanted something to take to the beach with no worries. She can take this sucker into the WATER if she wants, and the volume and sound quality are really impressive. Well worth the price.

I got this case a while back and it works great, I used it work, hiking, camping, and biking, the speaker volume is great enhancing the volume from the speakers of the phone it's self.It protects the phone from the elements(moisture) and drops.

Finding quality portable gear that can deliver the tunes without breaking the bank is no easy task. Lets face it, there are a lot of posers out there. When my antique JBL system bit the dust, I went through a couple of dog products that found their way back to the seller. Six months ago, I picked up the black bodied Grace Eco Extreme. Finally a winner.Out of the box, this product looks impressive. Weighing in at almost 14 ounces and measuring 6 1/13" x 3 1/13" x 1", its no light weight. The body is protected by an outer rubber casing. The 3" speaker is covered with a metal mesh screen. This model also is mounted with a working pressure release valve and volume control dial. The two throw latches do a great job in providing air and water tight integrity. There's also a detachable carabiner. The platform feet are so so and offer no real balance or protection against a wind gust. I noticed no big difference in overall sound quality when the unit is laying flat.Inside, just pop in three AA batteries and you're in business. The 1.8" jack and cable is hardwired and easily marries up well with my Sony Mp3 players and smart phone. I like the double weaved pocket netting. The interior is roomy and easily secures my player, phone and cash. Surprisingly I still have room for my jeep keys. Sound wise, this model will never be accused of shaking the paint off the walls, but it does take care of business. Whether its open or closed, standing up or laying down, performance is very good indoors. Outdoors, it is what it is. I got zero distortion. Overall battery life has been consistent with just over 24 hours before its time to slap in new rechargeables.Warranty wise, the folks at Grace Digital tack on a one year limited package. As far as durability goes, this product has lived up to its billing. On more then one occasion its found itself overboard. When I fished it out of the water the tunes were still pumping out and there was absolutely no interior water damage. It is buoyant. For price and overall durability, the Eco Extreme is a keeper.
Sounds good , super easy to setup and use , just plug the wire into your headphone jack and bam....

I got the yellow one because it had the cheapest price.  I take it with me to the beach-- keeps the sand off my MP3 player.Keep in mind it's not super loud on a windy beach day.  You're not going to throw a dance party on the beach with this thing.  But it's good for personal listening.
I wanted a product that I could use around our pool and this has worked very well. It is easy to use and I don't have to worry about my iPod getting wet. The sound is fine.

We haven't tested this outside yet.  I purchased it for use on the boat, but it's cold here and we haven't been on the boat lately.  We did test it with an old-school iPod.  It seemed to work excellently.

just ok, yes it keeps ur unit form water and it is made well, but for sound , no way, i have to put it right by our heads and the volume all the way up at the beach to hear it and it distorts alot, alot. the color is good but the sound is not there,

I primarily use this in the shower and it works perfectly.  Excellent sound from the single speaker.  My iPhone 5 is in an Otterbox Defender and with the length and jack placement it takes a little work to make it fit.
summary: Works great with iPhone 3GS; iPhone 5 might be a tight fit

reviewText: This is a downright brilliant invention just on the face of it. The ability to pack up your MP3 player or smartphone in a water-tight container is good enough. But add to that an amplified speaker and external volume control and you have a VERY handy little gadget. Clipped to a support on my kayak, it yields the sound I need when I need it and the batteries are lasting pretty well so far. Have also carried it out on the golf cart with me occasionally and it does the job there too. Overall, a little pricey at almost $40 (and the blue one is now less than $30!) but I am not unhappy in the least. I expect to get a number of years of use out of it and would probably replace it with the same item if damaged.
summary: Excellent box and plenty loud for most things

reviewText: This works great around my home or when I have my ipod inside. Although, when I went to the beach on vacation, it was difficult and nearly impossible to pick up a radio station with my portable radio inside. Otherwise, good sound quality and only uses a few batteries.
summary: Great sound quality, but difficult to get weak radio signals

reviewText: We needed something to use in the shower, but would protect the various iPods & iPhones from water damage. This case fulfilled all our needs. It's great in the bathroom since you can hang it on the shower head or towel bar. The volume is high enough to be heard above the water regardless of what you're listening to, music or audiobooks. It's great for generally any outdoor activity when you want to share audio sounds with people around you. We may end up ordering another one since the kids have pretty much taken over this one. Another plus, the batteries last a long time and aren't drained easily. We're still using the original ones  from when we first got it.
REALLY LOOKS NICE AND SOUNDS VERY LOUD. PROTECT MY DEVICES AGAINST WATER. I USE IT WHEN I TAKE A SHOWER. NO WATER AT ALL INSIDE.
This thing is awesome its water proof and very good sound and pretty loud too,battery is lasting for long time I am glad I got this...

Good solid product, the speaker is great, it's bigger than expected in a good way.  Buy it and enjoy.I use this mostly in the shower, so I can rock out while I scrub.  The cheapy key ring style carabiner is a nice touch too.

Been using it 2 years now and it still works great. We had a couple minor mishaps where someone didn't turn it all the way off when they were done, so the batteries got ran down really fast and it makes a strange whining noise that we couldn't figure out as the batteries died. Besides that, it works as expected and is very convenient.
summary: Works great, make sure to turn it all the way off when not using.

reviewText: This speaker case works as advertised and does a great job. Perfect for kayaking and canoeing. I have used many times and it works well.

I just got this product and wanted to warn anyone with a larger phone that it may not fit this case. I have a Droid X, which is larger than an iPhone and has a thicker camera section. The case is really big, but even so it will barely hold my phone. Anything taller or thicker wouldn't fit. The reason is the space for the phone is compromised by the corner mount for the carabiner. It intrudes into the top right side of the area you can place your device into. If your phone is too tall, it will be smashed between the speaker and the button that secures the carabiner. Be sure there's room for your device before you clamp down the lid. It would be easy to break touch screen glass if your phone was pinched. I have to be careful to push my phone down as far as it will go to avoid pinching the display.Sound quality is about what you'd expect from a small, single speaker that's compromised by waterproofing. It's not very good, it's not very loud, but at least it's not terribly distorted. As with any "waterproof" case, take some care to keep the gasket clean and free from obstructions. The build quality compared to other waterproof cases I own doesn't instill confidence. I personally wouldn't use the case as primary water protection for a player or phone for whitewater boating or other active water sports.
summary: Beware of fitting a large phone!

reviewText: This phone works great! I actually use it everyday in my truck. I find it's easier to hold than my iPhone. It has a hangup button that works great! It's basically a regular headphone but in a much cooler style. Good quality and hard construction. I'm probably going to purchase the model with the base.

I thought this would be a nice novelty item, but it turned out to be extremely practical. It has amazing sound quality and it has the feel of a substantial piece of telephone equipment. Naturally, people are very curious when they see me using this in the street or my local park. Great conversation starter and really nice add-on cell accessory!
I like the concept, but my unit had a distracting buzzing sound that was bothersome enough that I returned the product.
summary: buzzing sound, had to return product

reviewText: I didn't know such a thing like this had existed until I encountered it on the Amazon Lightning Deal recently.This handset is great because the sound from the earpiece is loud and clear.You do need to make sure that it is FULLY plugged into your iPhone or iPod Touch though, as most users have some kind of protective case around the phone which may prevent full seating of the plug.I travel a lot and I use my second generation iPod Touch in tandem with the Skype App to make calls in places that have Wi-Fi available, such as at airports and Starbucks. I have always been using a headphone/earphone with mic, but the sound isn't great, wearing it isn't comfortable, and it needs to be replaced every few months because of poor durability.Now I bring this MM Retro POP handset with me on trips and it feels great. It does take up more room in my bag, but I like the quality of audio so much that I can overlook that.
summary: A Fantastic Piece Of Hardware That Makes Calling On Skype Look Normal (At Least To Older Folks)

reviewText: Bought gift for mom as a silly, yet sensible gift. If you have a parent who still prefers a telelphone handset instead of holding a cellphone, this is perfect for them. My 55+ mom smirked at first, but after her first use, she hasn't stopped using it. Says calls sound clearer and not holding up cellphone to head gives peace of mind.

I forgot how nice it was to talk with a regular phone in your hand... I've had a cell phone for many years now so am used to using it, and also use a headset all the time,  but using this brings back a pleasure I took for granted back when.... holding the phone between your ear and shoulder while you do something else and then switching to the other side or back to hand held when you want, just great.In addition, this Moshi Moshi unit has a "grip" coating to it so will not snap out from your ear to shoulder hold like the old heavy, slippery jobs used to now and then.Also just plain fun to use it outside the house with your cell phone hidden away.  Be prepared to talk to strangers in person, as they will come over to see what you are talking into and get all the info on where to buy one.Sound is pretty good, both incoming and outgoing.I really wanted to use this for Skype on the computer, but seeing that their USB adapter is two thirds the price of the Moshi Moshi handset itself, I'm not so sure I want to do that until I find a third party adapter that cost less.Or if not USB, a 3.5mm female to "T" for standard PC 3.5mm microphone and headphone plugin.I'm also a bit surprised by the price of their adapters to fit cell phones that don't use a 3.5mm plug... each one is not bad at about three dollars, but for some reason you have to buy a "set" with five adapters in it, half the price of the handset and four of them you will not even need.Be careful if you are looking for an adapter as most you find are only for stereo and are not microphone compatable.This is a fun and practical item and if you have a phone with 3.5mm socket and don't need an adapter, it doesn't cost any more than most good headsets out there.Note that my review is for the actual ~ Native Union ~ handset that was advertised and not the generic handset now being offered in Jan 2013
summary: Review for original Native Union handset NOT generic knock off that has taken over page

reviewText: I often use Skype (and similar) on my laptop and mobile while in the office. Call me old school - but I wanted a nice familiar handset. Despite the relative low cost, the build quality was decent and the matte finish ensures no finger prints. I use it all the time and no one has made a comment about bad quality and I can now fully hear the other people as well.
summary: Works fine, though I was dubious

reviewText: This is a great conversation piece.  I can't stop people from asking about this phone.  I'm a very fashionable guy, and people are suprised when they see such a retro item hanging on my shoulder as i'm walking down the street.  Love it. Get's lots of attention.  I'm almost jealous of my phone!!

The main attraction is voice clarity and comfort during long calls. Looking nutty is a bonus.PROs:* Super comfortable for long calls* Improved voice clarity - incoming and outgoing- Earpiece blocks out external sounds- No radiation issues from phone (for those who are concerned)- Retro goofyOKs:- Problem free- Case-friendly 3.5mm jack - works even with thick phone cases.- The coil cord is nice. Somewhat stiff.- The flat soft-touch finish is kind of nice, but might look bad as it wears.CONs:- Warranty: No stated terms or duration- - - Pricing - - -Low tide seems to be around 26.- - - Alternatives - - -For even better comfort and clarity, consider...-JLab J3M Micro Atomic In-Ear Earphones with Microphone-Creative EF0540 HN-900 Noise Cancelling Headphones
summary: Comfort, Clarity, and a bit of Crazy

reviewText: I purchased this handset for the iPhone. I will not have my iPhone until April. I have tried this on a iPhone and it works great. Also I use this now on my Droid and it works fine. Just a little note this is not a Native union phone. I have purchased an Original Authentic Native Union phone. You have to register the Native Union phone. If you want a Authentic Native Union phone it must say the following when your order it from Amazon...."by Native Union LTD." and Ships from and sold by Amazon.com. I have brought 8 different handsets and they all have come from different sellers. Make sure when you purchase any phone that it comes from the company logo that it says it is. This phone says Native Union it is by GLD and Sold by Lily's Home and Fulfilled by Amazon. This phone works great ...however it is not a Native Union phone. Like I said I have purchased many of these phones so I am learning a lot. I did not no the difference until one of my purchases was a Authentic Native Union handset which was the most expensive it was twenty dollars. But all of my other handsets price range were  from 9.99 to 10.99. I love all of them.
Fantastic. I use it all the time with my Samsung Galaxy Tab 3.

Batman: [on Batmobile Batphone] Commissioner?Commissioner Gordon: [on Batphone in his office] Yes, Batman?Batman: Could you arrange for the immediate delivery of four one hundred pound sacks of sodium dichlorite to the Batcopter? I'll explain later.Commissioner Gordon: Consider it done.If this were Back to the Future, batman could use this really cool red Moshi Moshi handset connected to his iPhone to speak with Commissioner Gordon.Sadly, the Moshi Moshi doesn't light up red like the real batphone, but it does remind me of that phone.What a funny funny phone accessory. You'd never imagine this, but it works. There's some thing very strange and exciting about holding an old school handset while talking on a cell phone. The plastic is nice and satiny soft, it feels good in your hand. There's a little tiny button on the inside of the handle to answer or end calls. And it has a stealth function, that button will start up your iTunes or music on your phone, so you can listen to tunes while holding the phone.The sound quality is passable (music actually sounds pretty bad). The interesting thing about this handset, you can press it up to your ear and it does block out extraneous sound. I'm not sure where to put my phone while I hold this handset, so it's a bit like a Whopper - it takes two hands to handle the Moshi Moshi.As a funny piece, I like this thing. The paradox of ultra retro handset and ultra modern iPhone is pretty cool. My phone is red, and does look a lot like a red hot line. reviewText: My initial reaction when I saw the Moshi Moshi handset was that is was a cool novelty that I wanted to get a few laughs from friends.  But as I used it on my iPhone 4, I noticed an immediate improvement in reception and call/voice quality. People I spoke with also commented that my voice was much clearer compared with my Bluetooth headset or even when I'm not using any headset at all.I get a lot of calls on my cell when at my desk. I never used my Bluetooth headset when not "out and about," and now leave my iPhone docked to the charger/radio/stereo unit with the Moshi Moshi handset plugged in. It's wonderful to have a comfortable "old-fashioned" headset again. I guess technology has done many things but it my opinion it hasn't yet replaced it.The handset is of seemingly simple yet durable plastic construction. There is a single button under the receiver (in the center) that lets you answer calls and also hang-up.Incidentally, the phrase "moshi moshi" is Japanese and is how most Japanese answer the telephone. I lived in Tokyo for 7 years and thought that was a very cute and clever name for the product. Two thumbs way up from me!

First of all the packaging for the Moshi Moshi MMO1 Handset is just as cool and neat as it comes! The handset feels quite comfortable in your hand and the color is also a nice shade of red in this case I suspect that most people will want a wider choice of colors for theirs. The handset is quite east to use and after I got an adaptor for it soI could use it with my cellphone; I found myself not only wanting to use it often, but wanting to show it off to others. The thing is in many ways a conversaion starter. I would suggest that Native Union consider putting eithera set of adaptors in with the handset so a person does not have to go shopping for one. Yes one is included forI Pads and I Phones, but perhaps a set for the rest of cellphone users would be nice. Would I take this everywhere I go? Maybe not. It is a little bit big to carry around with one, but it is fun and functional

This is a lovely handset, with a comfortable grip and feel to it.  MUCH more comfortable than trying to just hold your cell phone to your ear with your shoulder (i.e. if you're doing dishes), AND much clearer than a Bluetooth...the sound is perfect.I emailed the company about an adapter for my Samsung Gravity 3, and they sent a mini USB adapter to me (GREAT company -- excellent customer service -- a rarity these days).  Unfortunately, the mini USB adapter "approaches" the socket from the side, which makes it impossible to plug in, due to the non-removable battery cover that swivels to one side.  If the mini USB adapter had just been made like any other charging tip that I've ever seen, it would have fit...bummer.  So I wouldn't recommend this to use with a cell phone that has a mini USB port and not a 3.5mm headphone jack.But it worked exceptionally well with my computer (through either the headphone jack OR through the USB adapter they also sent me), AND it sounded great on another cell phone that I borrowed that did have a 3.5mm headphone jack.  Great with the iPhone.Finally, this is such a great novelty to turn some heads with! You'll definitely want to bring it to work and freak people out.  :-)  Just wish their mini USB adapter was made like normal charging cords.
summary: Doesn't work with Samsung Gravity 3, but great product/company!

I was curious to see exactly how well this would work out with my BlackBerry. After receiving it, I hooked it up and I am happy to report it works just as described - no hassles and crisp, clear conversation quality. It feels nice, looks great, and I could see it being a wonderful gift for somebody who might otherwise be tough to buy for. It's also a great idea for somebody who's still young at heart but might not be the best with relatively new technology like cell phones.Although I do like it, I can't see myself using it regularly as I prefer my Bluetooth. Also, be aware that for many cell phones, you'll need to purchase an adapter for this product to work. Most of the time these adapters can be found for cheap, but it's something to keep in mind if your phone doesn't have the 3.5 mm jack that's needed for this to work directly out of the box.Overall, this is a fun novelty product that many will find useful. I chose this handset to use with my wireless phone in the kitchen because the product description says that it blocks most of the radiation coming from the phone.  Unfortunately, it has not worked out for me.Here's my experiences with the MoshiMoshi handset:PROS:1.  The handset has a nice, heavy weight to it.  The finish is comfortable to hold.CONS:1.  The 3.5 connector does not fit my cell or wireless phones.  The adapter included in the box was for an Ipad (which I do not own) or a MAC (don't own this either).  So it took a trip to my local RadioShack, and $7+ to get an adapter that would fit. Seems to me that a thoughtful gesture would be to include All the adapters that might be needed in the box.  Strike One.2.  When I did attach the headset to the phones (I tried it on three different phones), I found that the microphone portion of the headset did not work.  And, no, the phones were not on "mute."  And, yes, I did push the "on" button.  Strike Two.3.  The instruction booklet states that the product is covered under a limited warranty, and that if the "trouble-shooting" section of their website does not answer my problem, to follow the instructions on the support page.  However, the support page is not to be found.  "Does not exist"  Strike Three.The idea of a handset that prevents the radiation that occurs with the use of cell and wireless phones is great.  And, if your handset works, this might be a great product. Otherwise . . .

I actually got 2 styles of this phone - one with the base and one without so that I could compare the two, and also so that I could keep one in my handbag while leaving the "desk" model at home!  The desk model is just as portable as the one without the weighted base as the phone simply unplugs from the rear.  For those considering the weighted base option, I think it is most useful to help keep you from dropping your phone while talking but most especially, it's best suited for those who Skype or do other webcam/voice related activities.  Plus, well... it just looks cool!  Kind of like a hot line or "Bat" phone for those of us who actually grew up with corded phones!  You'll need to determine if the extra cost is worth it to you.The first time I took the phone out into the "wild" was when I was responding to an emergency call from one of my parents who was in hospital.  It was late at night and I was wrapped up in a jacket (I always freeze in hospitals) with my phone in my pocket.  I was propped up against the wall talking into this phone (and periodically pacing up and down the hallway).  Eventually, one of the nurses asked me "what is that??!" and then proceeded to try it out with her own cell phone.  She then, of course, had to show it to the rest of the nurses at the nurses station.  The next day, the doctor did a double-take when he saw the phone sitting on the window ledge and asked me if it was my direct line to the President.  Needless to say, when you use this device, you are going to attract attention!Audio is pretty good.  I use it with my iPhone and actually love to use it for extended conversations to avoid the heat generated from keeping the cell device held to my ear.  Just like the olden days, this phone cradles pretty comfortably between your chin and shoulder.  I don't suggest you use it in the car - unless you are the passenger (prepare for stares)!  There is a button in the handset that allows you to pick-up and drop calls.  It also activates the iPod on my phone, delivering a one-eared muzac experience (not during calls).I gotta say, I love this device!
summary: Feeling big love for this brilliant handset that wins huge points in the retro style department!

reviewText: This thing is just great!  I don't like those dorky-looking blutooth ear pieces, so this handset solves to problem of trying to hold a razor-thin cell-phone between my shoulder and the year.  I can now talk conveniently with excellent sound quality for longer periods of time without worrying about my brain being zapped by those scary signals that my phone is sending to a cell tower half a mile away.  The handset has a very nice rubberized feel and is very well built.  Everyone who seen me use it go: "Wow!  what is this? Where did you get it? I want one of those!".  So - highly recommend.

reviewText: I received this at no cost through the Amazon Vine program. It is simple to use: Just connect the headset jack on your cell phone to the handset using the included cable and you can now speak as if on a landline phone.NOTE: A Samsung phone requires a special adaptor for the included cable to work, and the required adaptor differs depending on the Samsung model. However, just email the company and they will send you at adaptor an no cost (they did it for me).This product is nicely made, and my voice is much clearer than when I just speak into my BlackBerry Tour. For a long cell phone conversation, my wife says it is more comfortable to use this than hold her cell phone to her ear.I am tempted to bring this to the beach, keep my BlackBerry in a bag, and see the reaction on people's faces. That might be a good idea anyhow because then my BlackBerry would not be exposed to the sand granules that always seem to find their way onto it when I am at the beach. Same concept applies if I am boating on a lake--no worry about the spray from a wave zapping my BlackBerry. While this handset can't slip into your pocket, it's not too big or heavy to make transporting it impractical.For people who spend a long time on their cell phone at home or in the office, this is great if you don't like wearing a headset, and will also improve your voice quality.Bottom line: This is well designed and works as promised.Update August 4, 2010: Customer service from this company is excellent. Initially they sent me at no cost an adaptor that did not work with my wife's particular Samsung model cell phone (through no fault of their own--unknown to both me and them, the Samsung Gleam requires different adaptors depending on when it was made). After I emailed them about this, they sent me again at no cost (via air mail from Hong Kong) a second adaptor, which worked fine. They also sent me emails in advance showing me a picture of the second adaptor (to make sure it was what I needed) and the date it was being sent out. I was impressed with the prompt and courteous customer service.

reviewText: Pros: I can hear out of this as well as a land line.  It's kinda rubbery and feels really nice to hold and talk into.  It's a great concept.Con: people can't hear you very well. After reading my amazon.com Vine Program friend, "Wulfstan" review on this product posted on November 24, 2010, I knew I just had to have it, albeit any color except yellow.Having lived six years In Japan and one in Okinawa decades ago, it tickled me that the product's name is Moshi Moshi.  Moshi Moshi (hello) is the greeting Japanese people there used when answering the telephone.I always have trouble hearing people on the cell phone, the speaker phone drives me crazy and I find blue tooth devices equally hard to follow conversations.Eureka!  When I plugged my red Moshi into the headset jack on my Blackberry and called my wife I could clearly hear her and she reported that she could hear me better too.I can now cradle the phone between my shoulder and chin and work hands free, just like the good old days.From the thoughtful packaging to the hard rubber grip and the on/off button on the handset this product is useful.  It is fun and comfortable to use and practical especially for long calls.I have not used it in public yet, but I can imagine that it will be like my Kindle 2.  People will be curious at this unique product, ask a lot of questions about it and end up buying one for their selves.I love it and bet you will too. Enjoy!

reviewText: Talk about a nifty product - the Native Union MM01 Retro Handset is the coolest thing since the blue-tooth headset.  I can't recall the last time I held a phone to my face that was tethered to something.The handset is extremely soft to the touch, I can't quite explain what it is made of but it feels like a silicone material. It is easy to hold and pretty comfortable in the hand. The weighted base keeps the phone from tipping over or sliding around on my desk. Now I can type on my keyboard and hold the phone up with my shoulder to have full use of both hands, unlike trying to hold a cell phone the same way that is nearly impossible without dropping it.I have the iPod Touch and an iPad, but I am using it only with my Droid Smartphone since I don't have a clue what to download for my Apple products (but I bet "there is an app for that"). I cart it around with me all day in the office since you can also just take along the handset without needing the base. Besides looking totally cool, like I am answering the "batman phone", it makes it so much easier for those long cell phone conversations with business calls that make your cheek all warm and makes your hand feel sweaty (you know what I mean). To hang up/end the call, all you have to do is hit the button located on the headset handle. However, I do get strange looks when I was sitting in a park on my lunch break talking from a telephone handset that was coming out of my tote bag. At home, I am using the Native Union Moshi Headset that comes without the base. That one sits on my computer desk at home so I can use both hands while talking on the phone. One bit of advice - don't use it while driving, I don't think law enforcement would consider this an actual "headset". LOLMany of my friends have commented that my voice is clear with no static or that "you are sound like you are talking in a tunnel" effect.In regards to the reduced cell phone radiation, I have a tough time buying into that one. If cell phones were a real big health risks to the people using them, wouldn't you think they would have been banned by now? If that was the case, I would not use a cell phone and so far no health risks have occurred to me from using it.It looks like a novelty item but it actually is very useful and a terrific product!

The idea behind this product is excellent; the product itself, however, is far from perfect. I have no complaints about functionality -- everything seemed to work well with my phone. The problem is that this headset itself is awkward -- big and clunky with a weird base. The whole thing is a bit too bulky; I don't see why this would be a better option than a hands-free handset or something like that.If you're absolutely looking for a handset like this, this product works fine. Just a bit too clunky for my tastes.

The short form: I love this thing. Way more than I thought I would.The long form: First of all, I should mention that I've seen a few reviews talking about incompatibility with specific phones, and can't speak to that. I will say that there are no adapters included, so if you don't have a standard 3.5mm mini jack on your handset you'll need an adapter, though they often come with your phone.But I use this with my BlackBerry Bold (9700), which does have a standard mini jack, and couldn't be happier. It's extremely basic: there's a weighted base, a handset with an attached cord, a second cord to connect to your phone, and a rubber pad for your desk that you can put your cell phone on.The handset can actually be plugged directly into a cell phone via its coiled cable if you feel like walking around carrying an old fashioned phone that appears to be plugged into your pocket, or if you want to look like Commissioner McMillan from the old TV series when you're driving around (if you're old enough, you'll get the reference). More likely, though, you'll just plug it into the base, then plug the base into your cell phone via a straight cord.The handset itself has a soft finish and is quite comfortable. More importantly, it can be tucked between your head and shoulder (which is incredibly irritating to try and do with a cell phone), allowing you to talk hands free without using a speakerphone.The only feature on the handset is a single button. Pushing it answers or ends a call. On my BlackBerry, though, pushing and holding it starts the voice recognition software, allowing me to make calls without reaching for the cell phone itself. Perfect.The base is heavy enough that I don't worry about the corded cable pulling it off the desk, and the included rubber pad for my cell phone is a nice bonus.Overall, something so very simple and yet does exactly what it's supposed to, and does it in retro style and comfort. I couldn't ask for anything more.

This is a stylish handset and easy to use.  Sound quality is good.  It has a single button in the center of the handset for mute, hang up and voice dial.  The build quality is sturdy and the base is heavy so it doesn't slide around the desk.  This is not a flimsy piece of plastic.  You can also use it without the base.  Simply connect the handset to your cell phone.  There is no loss of sound quality or features by doing this.This handset works with any phone/computer using a standard 1/8 inch phone jack.  Other names for this connector are headphone jack or its technical name, TRRS connector.  If you want more info, search Wikipedia for "TRRS connector".  According to the instructions, if your device doesn't have this connector, you can get an adapter (I didn't need one for my BlackBerry Curve).This handset works well for:* Keeping your head away from the radio waves of the cellular phone (although phones today are much lower power than earlier versions).* Being able to hold the handset with you head and shoulder (the old-fashioned hands-free method).* This handset causes less hand fatigue when making long calls compared to the small and awkward cell phone.* Using the computer to make phone calls (using VOIP/Skype).* People with arthritis or hand mobility issues will find this easier to grasp & hold than a cellular phone.
summary: Nice Design - Comfortable & Easy To Use

The idea behind this product is excellent; the product itself, however, is far from perfect. I have no complaints about functionality -- everything seemed to work well with my phone. I don't see why this would be a better option than a hands-free handset or something like that.If you're absolutely looking for a handset like this, this product works fine. There's nothing revolutionary about the MM02. It is a wired headset in the form of a telephone handset. It has one button to answer and end calls. Like the single button on Bluetooth and wired headsets it can redial the last number, activate voice dialing if your phone supports these features. On the one hand it takes the place of a $15 wired headset which often comes with your mobile phone. On the other hand it is a very comfortable phone to hold against your head, the audio is as good or better than your phone's, it looks great, is passively powered, and looks great ( I said that twice). Setting aside another reviewers xenophobic bashing of the french, the adapter works with all iPhone, and 3.5mm iphone like 3 band headset plugs. If you have a phone with a proprietary adapter,Native union sells a bunch of adapters or you can get one from any local best buy, radio shack etc. as most phones have converters from proprietary to the 3.5mm standard. You can use the phone with or without the base. The base if fairly heavy and stays put on your desk. The light weight of the handset makes it very portable to take anywhere.

I can't get it loud enough to hear when used with the iPhone. It does work ok plugged into my computer. I have room on my desk at work for the base and the pad for the iPhone is a nice bonus. Since I knew I like the feel of a standard handset better, I ordered the Native Union MM01H Moshi Moshi Retro POP Handset for iPad 2, iPad, iPhone 4G, 3G/3GS, iPod Touch, HTC Android EVO, Blackberry, Samsung Galaxy S, and Droid - Soft Touch Orange. reviewText: To be honest, I ordered this on a whim, and I wasn't quite sure why.  I had to figure out why I ordered it and if I made a mistake, so I set out to give it a try.  Opening the Amazon box yields a swanky and well designed package that's sure to impress any gift recipient.  More significantly, its easy open/close velcro top and window proudly say, go ahead open me up, check me out, and I dare you to return me (as opposed to piranha-like clamshells which just scare you into keeping crap).  Anyway, it never was returned.  Here's what you get:You get all that is promised, a corded handset (no Bluetooth here and it's a handset not a headset) for a cell phone, a weighted base (which I believe you can get by without if you'd like), and a somewhat useless silicone pad for your cell phone.  That's it.  The genius is in the execution, and  quality exudes from the design and the workmanship.  I actually rather like the humble handset, and I imagine it'll be something that others who have forsaken landlines will grow to love too.  If you're concerned about radiation, the lack of Bluetooth will certainly be a plus, and the longish cord can allow desktop users to keep the cell phone away from other desktop items such as their PC (which can hinder reception).  Lastly, the audio quality rocks.  Without Bluetooth issues to worry about, it does have a head start, but the microphone and speaker are also top notch.  I already got unsolicited compliments on my first call (maybe my old headset was that bad!).
summary: Better than expected, but it is what it is

reviewText: Synopsis:  The Moshi certainly puts distance between one's head and cell phone radiation.  However, it does so at the expense of convenience; reducing the cell phone to the status of an old school corded telephone.Cell phones emit low levels radiation during calls.  We humans, especially children, absorb at least some of that radiation as we talk on our phones.  Many smart persons believe this radiation absorption is potentially very harmful to the health of cell phone users.  Other smart persons, along with the cell phone industry, do not associate ill health effects with the type of radio frequency radiation cell phones emit.  For those who wish to play it safe by avoiding the radiation, altogether, the Moshi Moshi offers a simple alternative to head sets, ear pieces, and hands free devices.  By plugging one's phone into the handset base and using the rather old fashioned hand set, one can keep the radiation emitting cell phone well away from one's ear.  The Moshi does this well.The Moshi, though, does take some getting used to.  To get the most out of it, one must unholster or unpurse one's phone and set it close to the handset base in order to plug it into the base.  The Moshi ships with a soft, rubbery, grippy phone rest which adequately holds protects the phone and table surface upon which it sets.  This means one has to "run" to answer the phone instead of just reaching for it.  On top of that, unless you manage you hold the handset and your cell phone, you will be unable to wander while speaking as if you had returned to the pre-cordless phone days.  The convenience factor of the cell phone, therefore, diminishes.And then there is the styling.  Out of the box, this unit fails to impress.  Co-workers who saw me using it agreed is rather unattractive looking.There must be a better way to protect cell phone users from radiation.  A journey back to the days of corded, old school handsets is not a trip I enjoy making.

reviewText: Works very well. Audio quality could be better considering it is from Sony/Ericsson.i liked my old Bluetooth headset, it was from SONY (Sony DRBT100CX Ear Bud Style Stereo Bluetooth Headset) audio quality was very good and clear  .

I have tested many different bluetooth products and ended up being disappointed in the end. I purchased this product taking a risk after reading some of the reviews about this product going into a Reset mode where you must wait for the battery to drain. Well that did not stop me b/c while some had problems you can clearly see there are also many who did not have this problem. What works well is the bluetooth connection without any interruption or loss of signal, battery life is amazing but it is b/c of the size of the receiver. The sound quality through the headphones are amazing and now i don't have to blast the music like i did on other headsets to hear music while walking/working out. The downside and I'm learning to get used to this is the length of the cable on the right earbud. The picture is deceiving b/c it does not show or state the right earbud wire is longer then the left. I would have preferred the same length for each but I understand they did this so you wrap it behind your shirt under your collar for business reasons. The sound quality is so good as is the fit I'm learning to deal with this but once they break ill replace it with another set of Sony earbuds with short length wires. I'm still getting used to the volume touch feature but not a huge fan. Also the Call answer and power button are a little small but still not a big issue. Overall even with all the little quarks I'm pleased with this product. One more issue which is not really related to this headset and probably a device problem is I have this tied to my blackberry and while listening to Music if i get an email or calendar alert which goes off it is very hard to hear and faint. There are no setting to change the volume of the alert other then in the profile which i have it set to Max(10) but i can still barely hear it at times over the music. On the upside if you receive a phone call the music is completely stopped and a pleasant chime notifies you of a phone call so I know at least I will not miss phone calls. To address the alert issue i used a different alert tone which is longer and louder which has helped.So would i buy this product again YES, out of all the options out there I like this so far. Time will tell on battery life the more i use it but so far it is amazing compared to all the others I have used.

reviewText: I wanted to like this but I don't and here's why.PROS:- sound is great on theseCONS:- clip is pointless; it's too small to really grip anything thicker than a t-shirt and, if it's bumped or brushed against (on public transit, for example), it immediately pops off and dangles by the headphone cord- bad button layout- if you open the clip to attach it to something, there's a 90% chance you also just pushed the call button on the front without realizing it- assuming it's clipped to your clothes or bag, it's likely that movement or pressure will push buttons and change/pause tracks (when you unclip it to get a better look at what's going on, you're probably going to push the call button accidentally)- the volume strip is stupid and badly placed - to get it to work, you have to hold the unit firmly while avoiding the buttons that are exactly opposite and sort of 'drag' your fingerIf you're super careful when you use it and handle it delicately, this might work for you. If you just want it to work and prefer not to focus on touching it "just right" every time you interact with it, you should find something else.

I initially did not catch that this has multipoint, I purchased this mainly because I want to sometimes continue listening to the FM radio when I leave the car and dont prefer to run down the iPhone battery streaming radio and sometimes in certain locations I dont have good reception for calls let alone streaming internet radio.So the multipoint came to be a surprise, unfortunately it does not multitask multiple device as true advance multipoint does. Bizarre stuff. Still trying to make this work. Otherwise dump the FM radio (which I specifically purchased this for) and just keep the headset version only. Those are very neat.Note about the volume touch control, yeah I can see that as annoying already familiar with Sony's use of touch controls, not too keen on that. Another user commented that screen when clipped on you left side/collar will appear upside down, this is due to the short cord for the left ear phone, then when you flip the screen around the head phone jack/jack is point to the right of you so the cord is pulling across making is awkward.UPDATEThe bizarre connection issue with the iPhone4 continues, example call is being received, iPhone vibrates only, Sony screen flashes incoming call... but no caller ID as it normally should show, no sound anywhere, volume is turned up, phone is NOT set to vibrate. Incoming call is terminated on callers end, resulting in miss call on iPhone4 screen, the Sony continues to act as if the call is still ringing flashing inbound call on the screen. Caller attempts to call again,iPhone begins to ring normally, Sony makes a strange deee daa dooo sound like a disconnect and nothing more. iPhone4 Bluetooth shows it disconnected. Sony is fully charged and 2 feet away. This is a reoccurring issue. I can repeat this repeatedly, solution is to reset from scratch and it works fine for awhile. Turning off the Sony and then turning back on auto reconnects but then has the same issue. At first I thought it may have something to do with the password lock on the phone causing a reconnect issue. But now Im thinking it may be a iOS issue, and I may need a iPhone update as I have heard BT issues with iPhone needing updates. So I will try one last time and see...I really like the FM radio receiver but I feel that I have to return this item if issue continues. With the possible compatibility issues between Sony and Apple, I think this devices is more for Android phone users which appears to have an overwhelming positive experience.Note the Sony Bluetooth headphones only version appear to work well.Last comment, sound quality, its decent, honestly I feel nothing can compare with a wired headphone.

I threw away the crappy earphones that came with MW600.2) Battery has been showing still full after about 4hours of use.
