reviewText: The Good: Excellent design, lots of power, superb features from Google, amazing cameraThe Bad: App store is still young, processes running in the background kills battery life, keyboard is a bit cumbersomeGoogle as been known for revolutionizing the internet and now they are with their Android phones. The Motorola DROID (A855) is the newest and most advanced phone on the market right now, and this bad boy does an awful lot. A lot of people are going to compare this phone to the iPhone, but the DROID trumps the iPhone in features, and freedom. I will discuss, first, the tech specs and compare them to the iPhone head-to-head so you can see how powerful the DROID truly is.Techno BabbleThe DROID has a 550 MHz processor, and to be specific the Arm Cortex A8 processor that is also present in the iPhone 3GS by Samsung. The 3GS is clocked only 50 MHz higher and can be overclocked to 800 MHz. To compare that the original Xbox has a 733 MHz processor. So can the DROID be overclocked to this as well? Most likely. With a monster processor the DROID can multitask and has one of the first actual mobile OS (besides Windows Mobile 7). This also means maintaining processes running in the background to gain battery life, uninstalling apps (not just deleting them), and a lot more, but we'll get to that later. The iPhone however can not multitask due to the OS running on it, and the processor is only used in games.When it comes to graphics the DROID still hasn't been pushed to its limits. There are very few 3D games on the Android market, but as of right now the iPhone stomps the DROID in the graphics department. The DROID has a 200 MHZz PowerVR SGX 530 GPU. The iPhone has the same, but due to the slightly better CPU is can currently outperform the DROID. The iPhone has been on the market for quite some time, so there are bigger better games available. The DROID should start getting the same quality soon. They both have 256MB of RAM, so under the hood they are pretty much the same.The DROID has a slightly bigger screen sizing in at 3.7' and the iPhone at 3.5'. Does 2 millimeters matter? Yes it does. There is a good 2 millimeters on the top of the iPhone that could be screen, but for some unknown reason it's not. The DROID has a higher resolution of 854480 and 265 ppi (pixels per inch). The 3GS has a 320480 resolution with only 163 ppi so the DROID has double the resolution of the iPhone. That is great for people wanting to watch high-res movies on their device.Both devices have the same input such as the 3 axis accelerometer (tilt sensor), digital compass, Multi-touch display, proximity and ambient light sensors etc. The DROID is a bit heavier than the 3GS, but only by 1.2 oz. The DROID wipes the floor with the 3GS' camera. The DROID camera is 5MP compared to the 3GS 3MP. The DROID has dual LED flash, and geotagging and it can even run higher than 30 FPS. The 3GS has all this except the dual LED flash and this is a huge plus.When it comes to storage the DROID wins with its external memory option. You can insert up to a 32GB micro-SD card, but you're stuck with the 3GS' internal memory and have to pay a huge price for more. The DROID even comes with a 16GB micro- card when you buy the phone. So when it comes to comparing junk under the hood they both have the same hardware, but the DROID has the extra tidbits that push it over the edge.GUI: Graphical User InterfaceThe DROID has an excellent GUI and the whole marketplace is run by the community. There are programs such as PandaHome, OpenHome, GDEHome etc that allow you to change "themes" for a small price or for free. These also change icons, clock widgets etc. The DROID has a great interface that is more like a computer that gives you a desktop, then a slide up menu where all your apps are stored. You can drag and drop as you see fit. The iPhone, however, is plagued with the mundane Apple OS that only show apps in a grid format with a black background. Sure you can change your "wallpaper" but this is only when the phone comes out of sleep mode so it's rarely seen. This makes every iPhone look the same so the DROID wins in customization by a long shot. There are four touch buttons located at the bottom of the screen which are your back button, menu, home, and search. You will use these buttons a lot so Motorola and Google were smart to put these here.Apps: Who's Better?It all comes down to the apps. Who has more right? Well the iTunes marketplace has hundreds of thousands of apps that the DROID doesn't have so the iPhone wins there. However, the Android market is ever-growing, and thanks to the user run community a lot of great apps are showing up that the iPhone can't run. These include a lot of customization apps and loads more. Apps are easier to run on the DROID since there is no iTunes type program. The app store is run off the phone, downloaded from the phone as well. If you don't want an app anymore you go to your settings and uninstall it. Google also allows you to refund anything you buy within 24 hours and Apple does not support this. While iTunes may have more stuff, Android has better customer service and a better community and setup. There are really no "hardcore" games for the DROID like there is for the iPhone, but it's getting there. You do not want to get a DROID for a gaming system just yet for sure; stick with your iPod/phone.Features: Welcome to Google TownThe DROID has a lot of little things going on in it. You can do everything a touch screen phone can do, but it also has a slide out QWERTY keyboard. The buttons were a little flat and the top row is hard to get at if you have big fingers, but it works well. If you tilt the phone sideways you can type with a landscape keyboard or use Google text-to-speech. I found this feature extremely useful when typing long messages or writing reviews for apps. Since this is a Google phone you get all their awesome apps such as Google Earth (yes it's in 3D and you can see every detail), and Google maps. Switch to your "car app" and press navigation. Speak your selection (i.e. Phoenix, Arizona) and Google will give you directions for a car, bus, or walking (God forbid you walk that far!). Press get navigate and the phone will speak you the directions. It doesn't update in real-time, but it does update as you drive down each block.Google Sky is a fun app that lets you point your phone in the sky and it will show you, in real-time, where each constellation and planet is. You get plenty of excellent Google apps such as Gmail, YouTube (yeah Google owns YouTube), and Google Goggles which allows you to take pictures of products or objects and the phone will scan it and search it for you. There's even a Google search bar on the desktop with a text-to-speech button next to it. Brilliant. There are plenty of other apps such as the Amazon store, eBay, Bank of America, MLIA, FML, and even ShopSaavy. This app allows you to scan a barcode and it will tell you where you can find it cheaper online or locally. Of course you have all your social networking apps like Twitter, Facebook, and MySpace which run great.When it comes to things like ringtones, pictures, and videos, so the DROID delivers. You can store any MP3, or picture and set them as wallpapers, notifications, or just ringtones. Mount your SD card via USB and just create the folders. No having to sync with a program on the PC. Total freedom is what Google gives you and this is what I love.Problems: It's Not PerfectThere are some issues with the DROID, but not many and they are minor. The biggest one is the running processes in the background that can kill your battery even in sleep mode. You have to get the Advanced App Killer app and every so often check everything you don't want running and kill the apps. Another problem I ran into was that since most of the apps are user made they can be glitchy and screw up your phone so watch out and read reviews before downloading anything. You could say that the major issue is the app store. There is a lot of apps, but some of it is junk. There aren't any excellent games available, and the app store doesn't have any sort feature except Top Paid, Top Free, and Just In.For a $550 phone (if you pay for it without  a plan) the DROID delivers and trumps the iPhone in every direction except the apps. The DROID is a very advanced phone, and is for people who love using their phones constantly and make it a part of their every day life. With a sleek design, excellent features, sturdy hardware, and monster processing power the DROID should be the #1 phone in 2010.Update: 10/15/2011Now after I have had this phone for 18 months I don't like it as much. The phone started having issues with serious lag, slowdown, and just hardly responds anymore. The touch screen lost sensitivity after about a year, plus the hardware is ancient compared to what is out now. Due to that all the apps are now optimized for higher end phones so the Droid is left in the dust.Overall the phone just doesn't really work anymore internally. It won't come out of sleep mode some times, won't answer calls, turns off randomly, and the internet is just impossible to surf due to the now weak processor. Hardware wise it has stood the test of time with many drops, slides, fumbles, and kicks. Not a single crack or anything, but thankfully this phone is now discontinued. If you have the original Droid you are probably finding the same problems even after a factory reset. The phone was great 22 months ago, but now I just absolutely hate this thing. If I were to amend my score I would give it a 4/10 now, but of course that's unfair and should be remembered for how great it was at the time of release. Did I also mention that the appraisal price for the phone is about $20 now-a-days?
summary: Was amazing when I got it then slowly stopped working

reviewText: Not everyone wants to deal with the occasional hassle of blue-tooth headsets, like charging, pairing, and occasional interference and dropped calls.  If you prefer a wired solution for speaking hands-free over a cell phone, this headset is an excellent solution. I tested this on an Iphone, and it worked great, although the plug size did not fit my Motorola Brute cell phone. I don't know if it will work on other phones with the same size headphone plug as an Iphone.The ear buds sling over the ear, and the buds are designed to be noise isolating and should be fitted deep into the ear canal.  This set comes with various sizes of rubber ear buds so you can get a set that fits your ears the best, the same as you would get with quality music earbuds.  When the earbuds are seated properly in your ears, these deliver good quality that works well for listening to music.  The highs are good, and they deliver a fair amount of bass as well.As for making and receiving telephone calls, the microphone delivers crisp, clean voice quality, which isn't always the case with wired headsets because the microphones are usually located well below your mouth and often have difficulty picking up the speaker's voice.  This set picks up the speaker's voice just fine.  Calls placed with this headset didn't sound any different to the other party than when the phone was used normally without the headset.This headset is reasonably priced in comparison to blue-tooth solutions, so if you want a wired solution for hands-free cell phone usage (and you really should unless you like traffic accidents) this is a good solution at a decent price.
summary: Good sound quality for both voice and music

reviewText: I had a specific usage for these in mind when I selected them,  I wanted something that would stay in my ear when I go for brisk exercise walks,  and while these can be a bit fiddly to put on,  once on they stay there,  and sweaty ears or windy walks make no difference. So they win full points for that.  The sound is fine to my not very sophisticated ear. But they are not exceptionally comfortable and I wouldn't wear them just around the house,  and if you hook the wire unexpectedly (as seems to happen to me more than it should) they give you a strong tug on the ear as they fall out.  My husband who has much better appreciation of sound than I do,  found them average in sound quality.  I tried my son's ear phones in comparison,  and actually found my son's far more comfortable, but not as secure when exercising.  So I guess it depends on what you want them for.  If you want security/sturdiness,  they're it.  If comfort is really important to you,  they're not it,  and if sound quality is paramount,  they aren't it either. So I'm happy to use them for exercise but don't love them for anything else.
summary: Depends on what you want them for...

When I was a child, numerous infections in my left ear made me hearing impaired.  I am now a classic film buff; I especially love the Italian gialli that were mass produced in Italy during the mid-sixties to mid-seventies.  These films are memorable for their black-gloved serial killers who stalked gorgeous women during the accompaniment of electronic, synthesized music.  Unfortunately, many of the gialli in my collection don't have English subtitles for those of us who are hearing impaired.I have owned a Dynex 9-inch portable DVD player for nearly three years.  It is not uncommon to see me at a local restaurant watching a film with my portable DVD player.  The headsets I've used were always low cost.  I never thought the more expensive brands would produce a noticeable difference.  I was wrong.  The Philips SHH8006/28 headset was a godsend for someone who is hearing impaired.  Now I can clearly hear every word that a main actor is speaking.  I can even hear the voices of extras in the background.  The sound from the Philips headset is much clearer.  I just love having it.During the past two weeks, I have watched six Italian gialli (fans of the genre will recognize them):  Lucio Fulci's "Don't Torture a Ducking," Antonio Bido's "Watch Me When I Kill," Umberto Lenzi`s "Seven Blood Stained Orchids," Lamberto Bava's "A Blade in the Dark," Sergio Martino's "Torso" and Luigi Bazzoni's "The Fifth Cord."  Using the Philips headset made them more enjoyable to watch and hear.  I used my Dynex portable DVD player and Philips headset while I ate at home, work and at various crowded restaurants such as Panera Bread and Jason's Deli.  I also watched them late at night in bed.Many hearing impaired people complain when one of their favorite classic films doesn't have English subtitles.  They, like myself, are forced to turn up the volume of their television, which causes friends and relatives to complain.  With my portable DVD player, I can turn up the volume as loud as I want and, thanks to the Philips headset, only I can hear.  And the hearing, thanks to Philips, is so much clearer.  I also used the headset while watching my Italian gialli films on my Hewlett Packard desktop computer.  The audio was great; I could hear and discern every word; unfortunately, my computer isn't portable like my DVD player.  I was hoping to be able to use the headset with my landline telephone but the plug wasn't compatible.The Philips SHH8006/28 Headset has a standard 3.5 mm "I"-type plug which allows it to be used with most portable digital audio devices.  The flexi-rubber ear hooks fit comfortably over my ears and prevent the ear buds from falling out of my ears as they did with other brands.  The ear caps come in three standard sizes.  The medium set is more comfortable for me.  The cord measures approximately three feet from the 3.55 mm plug to the junction where the cord splits to go to the ears.  At the junction, it is another foot to the ear hooks.  The long cord allowed me ample room for getting up from my desk, table or bed and continuing to hold my portable DVD player.The Philips SHH8006/28 Headset is highly recommended for the hearing impaired.  Buy a portable DVD player and this headset and you will be able to privately enjoy your favorite classics - the ones that don't have English subtitles.  Until we can get all film distributors to become more sensitive to the needs of the hearing impaired, there are always portable DVD players and high quality headsets like this one from Philips.  Thanks to Philips, my life has become more enjoyable.Joseph B.Hoyos
summary: The Philips SHH8006/28 Headset Is Highly Recommended For The Hearing Impaired

If you're looking to replace buds for your smartphone, go ahead and spend the extra money on these.

This will be my second pair of these, they are EXCELLENT. My favorite set, they stay in my ears, they are very well made, the remote is the BEST out there - i actually prefer it to apple's inline remote buttons; it's easy to operate without looking (just by feel) and the construction is perfect in every way for my purposes. the most important part for me? they don't fall out of my ears while running. And if you snag on the cord they don't *hurt* you like so many other earhook style sets, the soft finishes and clean look make it my favorite. I had been waiting several months for Amazon to restock these, as my last pair went up against a kitty cat unfortunately, Now that they're back I'm buying two pairs.

reviewText: I got these based on the reviews. They came with three different sizes. I must have very weird ears because I cooldnt keep any of then in very good. Technically this is a headset, but you would not know it.  By far the best quality and comfort fit for the money.  Crisp clear sound and security over the ear.  At first glance you are thinking that the plastic rings are going to make your ears sore, but not at all.  A sturdy rubberized loop and a snug ear cap adjustment if necessary, and you don't even know they are there.  I tried laying on my side with head on pillow and had no discomfort.  Light weight but quality craftsmanship.  The bonus of the thinnest volume control and microphone is great.  You instantly get used to how to adjust and click without looking.  For full function, this is ideal for the iPhone, iPod nano, classic and touch.  However, I used it on my older shuffle clip just fine, but the remote will not work with it.  Only negative aspect to this is that there is no storage case. With larger earpieces and extra ear caps, they should have at least provided some type of pillbox type of storage.  I have bought and tried so many earphones through the years, but this is the first ideal match for my needs, and I like the cross platform functionality.

Bought this to a) use wiht iPhone and b) Listen to music (on iPhone or computer)Serves both purposes, the sound and microphone are both good quality, no one who hears me speak has complained yet. Music is clear, and volume is so good, I set my computer vol control almost at lowest setting.I specifically wanted the hooks since regular iphone headsets keep falling off. This works nicely for me, stays on my ears nicely.I have all styles, in the ear, over the ear,  and like this style best

I also found it to be impossible to have a conversation on the phone using these because they sit so far into your ear and muffle your own voice.
summary: Not god for running. Easily come out of your ears.

reviewText: For the past few years I had been using a Bluetooth headset but have yet to find one that is both comfortable and that stays in my ear.  The other problem with the Bluetooth was remembering to keep it charged all the time and having to re-pair it with my phone when it would "forget" and would occasionally cut out.  This Phillips SHH8006/28 headset solves those problems and has some nice features of its own.I first tested this headset with an iPhone that I borrowed from a friend.  The inline remote controls worked flawlessly to initiate calls and answer calls and the mic picked up my voice well according to people on the other end.  A couple people said I sounded a little "hollow" but that could have been the connection.  Most said I sounded perfectly clear. For such a small mic I think it worked very well.  I liked the fact that I didn't have to reach for the iPhone every time I wanted to do something.  It works kind of like a Bluetooth, but with wires.  When listening to music I could use the inline remote to skip tracks and adjust the volume.  There are 3 different sizes of covers for the earbuds so you can choose the one that fits your ear best.Next I tried it with my iTouch.  The sound was better than with the earbuds supplied by Apple, and as good as any I've tried in this price range.  The notes were crisp and clear and the bass was decent. If you're looking for something with good noise canceling ability, these won't block out all outside noise.  But since I wanted them for walking and for use with the phone, I don't really want all background noise blocked out so they're perfect for me.  I've always shied away from over the ear holders for earbuds but the flexible rubber ear hooks on this Phillips SHH8006/28 headset are amazingly comfortable.  I usually forget that I'm wearing them even after having them on for a few hours, they're that soft.  They stay in my ears whether working out, cleaning the house or just riding in the car.I was hoping when I ordered these that they would work with my Blackberry Curve 8330 Smartphone since they have the same size plug.  They do!  I can use the in line remote to initiate calls (voice dialing) and to answer and hang up the phone and to raise or lower the volume.  The mic works fine, just like with the iPhone.  I had a friend call me on my home phone using my Blackberry and the inline mic and the sound was very good.  I don't store music on my Blackberry but I did try recording my voice and listening back and the sound was crisp and clear.I use this headset all the time on my Blackberry and really like the comfort and the ease of use.  It fits my needs perfectly both for the phone and the iTouch.  The only reason I'm giving the product 4 stars instead of 5 is the noise canceling feature that isn't really that great and it could be an important feature for someone else.
summary: Tested on iPhone, iTouch and Balckberry Curve

reviewText: I am not generally a big fan of in ear monitors (IEMs).  I dislike the sound being present inside my head, find putting the plugs in my ear to be uncomfortable, and find the cable noise to be amplified.There are times, however, when IEMs offer advantages.  They give sound isolation even better than closed headphones and fit easily in the pocket like ear buds.  I also like to have a mic because I use Skype on my ipod touch.These IEMs are surprisingly decent.  The sound is very similar to my Koss Sporta Pros, which are my reference set for cheap headphones.  The cables are much less noisy than the cables on my Sennheiser headset.  The sound is not particularly muddied or distorted or dulled.  There is not as much detail as with higher end headphones, but the sound is fine.The cable fits over the ear with a rubber loop.  Some IEMs have wire that bends over the ear, others just fit in.  These are fairly comfortable (I still hate wearing the buds in my ear).Overall, not bad for an IEM head set.  I like these better than the Sennheisers.  The Sennheisers have slightly more sound detail, but the cable is noisy.

Nice headset. Stays secure with ear clips and offers multiple ear buds for you to getjust the right fit. Sound is very good. Can't fully judge because I stream music from"Zumocast" and Internet based "Tune In Radio" apps rather than carry music directly onmy phone. I suspect they sound great with direct MP3 music on device. Recommend.

This is an excellent set of earbuds and definitely outdoes the typical iPhone set. The buds are designed to fit deeper into the ear and can feel like earplugs - both in terms of how far into your ears they go as well as in how well they block out outside sound. This allows for crisper sound quality and deeper immersion into what you're listening to - whether it's music or a phone conversation - the headset also includes a microphone for conversing. Though the buds go deep into your ears, the set is still extremely comfortable. The shape of the ear pieces does draw a bit more attention to your ears (from yourself, that is) than the smaller iPhone buds, but this also makes the ear pieces feel more secure - if the bud itself comes out they're still wrapped around your ears so they won't fall off. Definitely recommended for any iPhone users looking for an upgrade in their earbud experience.
summary: Comfortable, high sound quality, and blocks out outside noise

reviewText: The cable was really thin and felt really cheap. When connected to my car charger it wouldnt keep the phone charged, it lost about 5% on my 45 minute drive to work. It worked decent paired with my wall charger though. Its also pretty long which was nice.

I purchased this cable when I received my Droid Incredible 4G LTE smartphone.  The Droid Razr MAXX I had before had the charging port on the top of the phone (annoying!) the HTC has it on the side.  This cable is really convenient for side charging ports.  Unfortunately, it cannot carry the high current required to operate and charge most higher end smartphones.  Using my Droid Incredible 4G LTE the maximum current I've seen the phone receive is 350mA.  I have tried it with both an 850mA Motorola OEM USB wall charger and a 2A Nook Color USB wall charger.  In both cases the phone didn't receive more than 350mA.  I did both tests with the phone in airplane mode to ensure the radios didn't interfere with the charge rate.For the price, and for overnight charges only (I keep this cable plugged in next to the bed and only use it at night), it's an ok cable at best.  A much better extended cable option is here:Mediabridge - USB 2.0 A-Male to Micro-B Cable (6 Feet)The mediabridge cable can provide as much current as you can throw at it, though they don't make a right angle cable sadly :(.  I use the Mediabridge when I travel (see my full review on it's product page) and this right angle cable at home only.  I wish the right angle cable could carry the full current as it is much more comfortable to hold, but just can't keep up with the power needs of higher end devices.  The mediabridge cable is also a thicker diameter cable and has much higher quality connectors on both the standard USB and micro USB side.
summary: Nice angle, but can't carry high charging current

reviewText: I've been wanting a Right Angle micro USB cable ever since I got my Sprint Samsung Moment cell phone.  And anyone who has this phone knows how horrible it is on battery life.  I had to buy an external battery pack just so I can make it through a day with my "cordless" cell phone.  Aside from the obvious hassle of constantly being tethered to my external battery pack, I was getting a little annoyed with the micro USB cable that came with my phone -- the plug on a standard micro USB cable sticks out WAY too far from the phone and makes it inconvenient to keep the phone in your pocket.  Hence the need for a right angle cord.  But beware, not all right angle cords are created the same!!  Once plugged in, most of them will send the cord UP the body of your phone.  But this one sends the cord DOWN the body of my phone, making it more convenient to use AND get in and out of my pocket while connected.  PERFECT!  And the cable is nice and long too!!  Added bonus since most cut corners by keeping the cords short.  Great cable for a great price and really good quality.  If you need one of these cords, this is the one to get!
summary: Good Angle for Sprint Samsung Moment - Nice and Long!

I don't like the tiny micro USB connectors that everything comes with nowadays. They look way too fragile, it's too easy to jam one in at a bad angle and bend or break the little tab inside your phone. Mishandling a device when connected, or worse, dropping it can snap it off completely. Such things have happened to my family members twice now. A good precaution is one of these angled connectors. It really reduces the connection profile, which limits the amount of bad leverage exerted on your device's connector if it's mishandled. I got this in the mail today and love it. It's the right length and conforms nicely to devices. Right away I ordered more. Anyone want to buy some slightly used straight micro USB cables? I've got several I won't need anymore. :-)

But if you plug the normal charger in, you end up with a "T" looking arrangement that is a bit unwieldy.Enter this cable.  This plugs into the side of the connector and then angles the cable to follow the AV cable, even to be zip tied together if desired.  I spent a lot of time closely inspecting connectors to find the right one to fit the HTC AV cable and THIS is the one that works best.Note: On the Incredible, when plugged into the phone by itself, the cord goes up toward the volume buttons.  You may want that, but if you want it to point down while the phone is vertical, you would want a left angle plug.  I believe this is opposite of the Droid X.UPDATE 5/3/11: Just got an HTC Thunderbolt and it works great with this phone too.  However, it bends the opposite way as it does on the incredible, so while the Incredible had the cord bend and go up toward the volume buttons, on the Thunderbolt it bends and goes toward the phone bottom (points down, as I think it does on the X).  Just an FYI, in case someone is searching.UPDATE 1/11/13: Also points down on HTC Rezound, like the Thunderbolt

The clips are not so secure with my slightly heavy smart phone so have to be shoved in all the way which makes the bottom catch worthless.  If that bottom catch and the clips can work together, it is probably pretty good, which can happen if the vent is angled upward.  Not possible in my car so the mount will hold ok, but can easily slip out if I'm turning, or just on an extended drive.I already have a round pad from my GPS mount on the dash and this suction cup is very good on top of it.  I may put the included pad on there as well so I can use both.  The reason I hadn't used the suction mount before it is rode too high above the dash blocking some of the view.  But I just figured out that flipping the arm all the way backward, the holder can sit low and below the level of the dash.5 stars for the suction mount, but a reduction for the vent mount. My old mount had spring loaded clips that held the vent slat between them so it is possible to make a vent mount that will hold in my car.4-19-12 Update: I bumped it a star to four because the suction mount is pretty good.  So much so that I've bought a second one as the suction cup on my Garmin mount will not longer even hold its own weight.  So I have two of these, one for the GPS and one for the phone.  The ball on the end of the Garmin arm is the same ball as on this one, so the holder just goes right on.

reviewText: I picked this up based up recommendations from other reviewers who said it would work with the Droid X - it absolutely does.  With a thin gel skin on the phone, the holder cushions easily fit the phone and ratchet up nice and tight.  The arms on the side provide -just- enough clearance to fit a car charger.I haven't tried to attach (or needed to) the window mount just yet, but the vent mount has worked decently well.  It's a bit hard to make it work on a 2010 Mazda3, but clips will work for the vent mount on the center vents, spacer flipped up, with the vents wide open (unfortunately).  Having the vents open means the phone warms up a bit in the winter, but I aim most of the warm air either at my feet or the windshield, so it's not a huge issue.The bigger issue with the vent mount is that the clips can soften up if they're warm, so if the vent mount gets jostled, either when you're mounting the phone to the holder or rotating it, the clips can lose their grip on the vent vanes.  Not quite sure how to fix that, but it's a huge distraction when the phone pops off after a speed bump/pothole and tumbles to the floor with the charger still attached.  However, once you start to expect it, it becomes second nature to push the whole assembly into the vent after moving anything.  I've contemplated switching to the window mount, but honestly, the vent mount suffices to stay out of my field of view and within reach if I need to adjust GPS without pulling the phone off the window.The cushions on the feet and arms are starting to show signs of continued compression, but I'm not particularly concerned yet.  They're still soft enough to provide a good grip without being too tight.  The push button release for the ratcheting arms is quick and easy to use, and so far hasn't released unprompted.
summary: Works well with a Droid X in a gel skin, affixed to a Mazda3 vent mount

reviewText: I purchased an Arkon car mount for my PDA about 7 years ago and I just recently had to get it replaced so I decided to go with Arkon again.  I have always used it with the vent in my car and it holds my phone perfectly well.  I can see how some people complain that the mount is not THAT secure when used with the air vents but for my car, it is not so bad.  Sure it wobbles a bit when I push it with some force but it never wobbles when I make turns on my car or when I go up/down hills.  I love the fact that the mount can swivel so I can either use my phone in landscape or portrait mode.  I am not really sure how long the tightening mechanism for the swivel joint will last but it works really well now.  The design of this mount also protrudes far enough from the vent that it does not block the air flow as much as other mounts that I have seen which is also a bonus.

Have not used the vent mount and probably will not. Not needed. The windshield mount works very well and is easily mounted above the dash at eye level so that it is easily accessible for the HTC Incredible phone charger. When traveling and using the GPS navigation mapping on the phone the mount makes it very easy to listen/check the route without having to divert attention from the roadway. The mount mounts and adjusts very easy.

Great product for most smart phones, easily adjustable, holds position well, used the vent mount, but have the option for windshield or dash. Easy to change phones.  High quality product, worth paying a little more to get it right. Works for both T-mobile G1 and HD2
summary: Arkon Universal Windshield and Dashboard and Vent Mount Review

reviewText: I really like the mount for the dashboard.  It sticks very well and I can place my phone right where I want it.  Don't expect much out of the windshield one though...it falls all the time.  The vent one I havent tried yet but in the past I've had vent mounts and they work fine (might be a little wobbly when hitting bumps)

I've bought cell phone mounts before and they all turned out to be junk. This one is nice! It feels solid. My phone fits in the holder perfect and doesn't feel like it will fall out. I would definitely recommend!

Both the suction cup and the vent holder work well for the Galaxy Nexus phone.  It is a lighter phone, so perhaps that makes a significant difference in the ability to keep it in position.  The suction cups works best on glass, and although it may hold on the dash of some vehicles, on many it won't.  I can't complain for the price and I've been using it all summer with no problem.  It certainly beats out paying nearly $60 for an OEM mount that may not work as well.
summary: Seems to Work Well With the Galaxy Nexus

reviewText: Just what I needed for my car. So far working great but I have to see if it will stay sturdy in the long run.
These are the cheapest priced yet most well made products I've ever come across. I've recommended these Arkon mounts to many of my family and friends and we all have them and they are perfect!

I'm glad I bought this because I originally wanted to use it for my vent. I attached it and it fit well but then I decided I wanted my phone closer to where the road is when I'm driving. So I just swapped out the connecter, so easy! Fits my iPhone 5 and my girlfriend's Samsung Galaxy S2 no problem.

It's well made but my Galaxy Nexus wobbles a lot over the slightest little bump when I have it dash mounted. The arm that connects to the phone just isn't thick enough to handle the weight without a little give.

This works very well to hold my phone.  I have used all of the adapters and they work as described.  I would very pleased with the quality of this product and the amount of options you have to attach it to your vehicle.  I would purchase this again if I ever need to!The part that holds your phone can swivel around so you can position it as you like.  The pieces that secure your phone have foam attached to them so your phone is not damaged or scratched.

I got this for my Galaxy S3. The phone's just too big to put in the center compartment, and I didn't want to risk having the phone slide around and get scratched/damaged.Anyways, this mount holds my phone securely. Both the dashboard/windshield mount and the air vent mount was easy enough to install and put away after use. Securing and removing the phone from the mounts was fast and easy. While the phone is mounted, you can swivel the mount into any position you desire so that the phone is visible from any location you decide to mount it, which I find EXTREMELY useful when I use my phone as a GPS. The mounts allow your phone to be plugged in while in use, depending on where your car charger outlet is located. This helps a lot when using the phone as a GPS, again.All in all, it's a great mount.My only gripe with it is the ball-and-socket joint used to swivel the mount so that the phone faces you isn't as tight as I would like it to be. A few minor bumps in the road will cause the mount to face downward, and I find myself readjusting the mount every so often.
summary: Does what it's supposed to do, and it does it well!

reviewText: I like this product alot. The only thing is it shakes a little to much and is at its last click for tightness on my droid incredible, but it still a great design!
To keep it simple, it works, all the dongles work wonderfully and look great.  Fits easily in your glove box.  I highly recommend this product.

Initial Thoughts:-It's plastic and probably of cheap quality-Does have quite a bit of accessoriesPros:-You can literally mount this thing anywhere-The 3m backed smooth disc is holding on to a non plastic dash-Holds any sized phone properly without scratchingCons:None that I can find weirdly enoughOverall:This is holding my Droid X fully extended while being mounted to the dash with the disc.  This is on a 300c that sits in the sun a lot and the phone never moves since I use it for data logging and real time engine diagnostics.  It's amazing that the kit didn't cost a lot more.  I couldn't be happier!
This was a great value for the amount of items in the kit. The suction option works well, the phone is secure in the cradle. I have not tried the air vent mount option in the kit.

I purchased this mount for my Samsung Galaxy S2 and HTC Amaze cell phones. Phones fit great and still have accessible ports (usb charger and microphone holes) while on the mount. This mount is very sturdy (on the windshield, I don't/haven't use the vent mount). Naturally, the mount will move/vibrate slightly, but it's definitely not a big deal especially compared to others. Also compared to others, the mount is a great price. I will be purchasing the same mounts for some of my family members as well.

love it ... i have it on my dash ... facing down so my phone is getting aircondition. because as you know it gets hot when it charges in the car... great holder. all you need to get the job done... thanks

I have a ton of Arkon mounting gear in my company and personal vehicle.  It's nice that they have so many options.  I like this mount because it supports my Galaxy SIII perfectly.  Plus, it attaches to all the existing mounts I have (since I'm not using the one that came with it). I recommend this item.

So far, this has worked great. It holds my iPhone 5 snug, and one push of a button releases the phone (opens the jaws). It only fell off my windshield once and I think it was because the temperature fell down 10 degrees. There's a gap so that the phone can be charging on a cable while in use.

I tried all the cheap holders on Amazon and this one is the one I stick with. I just bought a second one for my new car. It's a good solid built unit and has a few mounting options. I think it's a solid choice for under 20 bucks.

I've been using this for couple years now. It holds my Galaxy s2 skyrocket real well. If there's a lot of condensation in my windshield then it looses the grip. Small enough to carry with me wherever i go. Very sturdy... dropped it numerous times from windshield to the floor and still in one piece. Very satisfied with this and well worth the money.

It works perfectly with the Samsung Epic 4G. The holder can adjust the size so it will work for most smartphones. There are a plenty of room on both the top and the bottom for cables. The vent mount works with my 06 Accord.

I got this for my Samsung Moment, which is a rather heavy and bulky-looking Android phone (about 6 ounces), so that I can use it as a GPS.The windshield mount is very sturdy and attaches tightly to my windshield.  It hardly bends at all, despite the weight of the phone.  The description doesn't really mention it, but in addition to the vent and windshield mounts, a sticky plastic disc is also included so that you can mount it to your dashboard.  It's easy to adjust and tighten and the mount grips my phone securely, with a quick-release button.If I had to criticize this product somewhere... the vent mount doesn't really fit my car (Mazda 3) at a good angle, but I am happy to use the windshield mount so it doesn't matter.  The windshield mount vibrates ever-so-slightly (maybe a fraction of a mm) when driving fast, although this is probably dependent on the car and mounting position, since it is otherwise extremely stiff.UPDATE: This thing worked pretty well for about a year and a half and then the arm of the window mount just snapped in two.  Not so durable after all.  Hrmph.
summary: Good car mount for heavy phones

reviewText: I did not keep this product. It would probably work well for other people, but not for my personal preference. I was looking for something I could just set my phone on/in and not have to make sure it was clamped in. I gave it a shot, but this was not the universal windshield with dashboard and vent mount I was looking for.

I can't speak to the effectiveness of the vent mount, but that's not why most people would buy this especially with a the reviews stating the vent mount is not great.  As far as windsheild mount this item is without parallel that I'm aware of.  The suction cup design is the best I've used.  There is a wide variety of adjustments and configurations for how you can use this mount.  It does a great job securely holding my HTC Evo and my Samsung Epic both in vertical and horizontal positions.I'm always concerned when buying any item that mounts to the windshield.  I drive a Corvette Z06 and I have limited windshield room due to the steep rake and low roof but this thing works great.  I also need something won't come loose while cornering and send my $500 phone flying out a window or under my pedals and this is the right product!

I purchased this item based on many reviews.  I owned this item for about a year and i will not buy anything from this company again. The holder itself is ok. Its the vent clip and dash mount adhesive.  The clip was ok for about 3 month then broke off. One hot summer afternoon, i got into the car and found dash mount on the floor,  The adhesive simply came off due to heat.  VERY DISATISFIED.  I need to buy another one but not from AKRON....

It comes in pieces and you construct what you need.  It is not a perfect fit for any phone, but it was inexpensive, and had the vent mount, which has been hard to find - I find the suction cup mounts to be problematic myself.  They never seem to stay on and fall off at bad moments.
summary: Cheapo set, but does what it suppose to do

reviewText: I've boughten two of these now, they work great in my Tacoma. My only complaint is that the clips that hold the unit to your AC vents are weak. On two occations my phone went flying off, but craddled insite the unit it was ok. I emailed the company and requested new clips which they sent for free. As long as your not driving crazy or hitting big dips you should be all good!

This holder works in 2005 Toyota Corolla S vehicles. I've got two complaints though. The vent clip doesn't really hold the whole apparatus very well. While you are driving it will shift around because the hooks don't secure it firmly. Also, the release mechanism feels cheap, like it may work for a while but break later. It works ok though.

I put this on my wishlist and received it for christmas. I used the vent clip. It doesnt really stay back, but it doesnt fall out. I lent it to my husband when he went out of town on business and missed it so much that I ordered myself a new one before he got home. He said it was a good thing because he had no plans of returning my original. He prefers the window suction cup. It is very strong. I have had to use mine also because the clips on vent attachment on the second one I ordered were bent. It is great though. It fits everything from my iTouch to my Galaxy SIII. would recomend to anyone.

Bought this for my HTC Glacier (mytouch4g) as I use it's GPS instead of my garmin now (google maps is just so much faster and more accurate) so I got this to use for that and I'm very happy with it.It's well built, feels really solid and not cheap at all.  The suction cup for the windshield is nice and heavy duty and doesn't let go in the hot sun the way my garmin will.  The vent clip fits on both my old S70 volvo and my wife's Audi but isn't quite as tight gripped onto the fins of the vent as I would like.  My car has a tighter than stock aftermarket suspension and the phone holder jiggles up and down a little bit making it hard to see.  The windshield mount doesn't do this however and in my wife's car, the vent clip doesn't shake so I just attribute the vibration of the vent clip in my car to the tighter suspension.That's my only real gripe about it and not a deal breaker by any means.Another thing I like about this is that the ball socket joint allows you to use the phone in either portrait or landscape mode which is nice.Oh and it holds the garmin snugly too :D

The holder works fines with the suction mount but my complaint is about the Vent Mount.  The Alligator Clips on the Vent Mount are too weak to hold it's grip in the vents.  It keeps slipping out from the vent and falling down.  That's why I bought the i.Trek Vent Mount for my Garmin Nuvi.  The i.Trek Vent Mount uses a different grip system that hold in the vent much better.  If you only need the dashboard mount then this product is fine.  But I would not recommend this product if you need to use the Vent Mount, you're better off buying the i.Trek Vent Mount.
summary: Alligator Clip on Vent Mount Weak Grip

reviewText: Phone: Moto Droid X  Veh: Ford FusionI'm only commenting on the vent-mount portion of this model since I prefer not to use the window mounts (can't use a sunshade with a window mount).First off, before I even installed this, it felt like a very solid mount. It didn't look or feel like it was flimsy plastic or about to break. The install was easy enough. Took less than a minute to get it clipped in and in place where I wanted it.Once the arms were squeezed into place around my Droid, they held on great. I'm pretty sure the entire unit would become dislodged from the vents before the phone would slip out of the arms. The added weight of the phone did make the whole unit tilt forward more than I expected though. I could see at this point that the clips that slide into the vents are only held in place by the interlocking teeth at the very ends of the clips. Not quite what I was expecting, but perhaps this is by design.So far it's been a great mount while driving. Keeps my phone in view, able to use it in portrait or landscape, and it doesn't block any ports. I do have 2 gripes though: It can be knocked off the vent with a pretty slight bump. While removing the sunshade from on my dash, the shade brushed over the unit and one of the clips came out, leaving the phone dangling by the other. And the other is to change it from portrait to landscape takes 2 hands and isn't very easy if you had the unit tightened up to begin with.Over all it's a decent phone mount and will suffice for what I need it for. I may try the rubber tubing trick one of the other reviewers mentioned though to make the clips more stable.
I bought this for my wife for hands free calling - she loves it. With the vent clips it's off of the windshield and onto a vent. very useful for using the phone as a gps as well :)

The product holds my larger cell phone with no problems making it easy to use the hands free options and use the phone as a GPS.  I use the product in my AC vent and it fits well though it can easily be moved around with the errant move between shifter and steering wheel, depends on your car.

I use this with my HTC EVO 4G phone and it works pretty well.  No real complaints other than when it is connected to the air vents (2010 Kia Forte), it makes an annoying rattling sound.  Also, my air vents are verticle, not horizontal, so it makes keeping the cradle seated in one place, tough.  It wants to slide down and shift side to side.  The windshield mount, however works very well and holds firmly.  If I had to do over, I'd still get this, but I wouldn't bother with the vent mount.With the phone mounted, I can still get to the volume buttons, the charging port, headphone jack and the power button, all without problem.  Also, the cradle adjusts perfectly to hold the EVO.  Overall, the build is very good, but I would have liked the actual cradle to be heavier and less prone to rattling.
summary: Works adequately and a good price

reviewText: I think that this is a great product! It is a great way to hold the phone while driving and keeping everything in my eyesight!

I liked how you can use this for multiple electronics.  I use it for both my smartphone and my GPS.  It has three different attachments to use it as you can see fit for your vehicle (suction, vent clip and stick on base). It holds my electronics in place without scratching and allows to tighten swivel part to keep electronic from moving around. Serves its purpose very well.  I would recommended it to others.

I was looking for a vent mount and this combo is a great price and quality.  I have the iphone 4s with a otterbox defender case and it has plenty of room when you open the clamp. Closing the clamping mechanism securely holds the phone w/the oterbox in place. the tension screw to position the phone is easy to use and locks your phone in any direction.

The holder is so convenient I wish it came with two, one for the car with the vent holder and one for at home with the stand-alone mount!  Very visible when mounted on the car's vent near the steering wheel; a little shaky but has not fallen off.  The stand-alone mount (for windshield, dash, etc.) can also be used in the cup-holder or at home next to the bed, etc.  Worth every cent!
Quite a let down.  The vent holder is horrible.  The windshield holder is ok but this thing is extremely bulky.  I cannot believe there are not better phone holders for the car.

I have a Motorola Droid 2 with the Superior holster and case combination. This case wraps the Droid 2 in a rubberized plastic case that clips into a retention holster, so as a result the Arkon clamp won't be able to touch the volume or photo buttons.I used the suction cup mount and it works beautifully, although it gets hard to remove from the windshield.The vent clips work great, I just push them into the grille or yank them out without worrying about it falling out. It is less conspicuous than a suction cup mount but does the same job. The clamping base has a cut-out that allows you to easily attach a car charger or micro-USB cable without interference.Overall, this package gives you 2 great options at a decent price.Pros: Versatile mounting choices: traditional tried and true suction cup, or vent clips.Cons: None really, other than making the vent clips a bit longer and/or beefier.Overall: 5/5 stars, works as advertised, works great with my Droid2 or the Droid.
summary: Best car mount package I have seen

reviewText: My main reason for buying this was for the vent-mount feature. I have tried multiple clamp positions and different vents, but this thing swivels and easily falls of of the vent. The suction cup mount works fine, of course, but I wanted the vent mount so that it would be closer to me when using the phone as a speakerphone.In order for me to get it close enough to my head while using windshield mount, I have to mount it high on the windshield, which is illegal in CA.
summary: Vent mount is useless for 2003 Camry

reviewText: I wanted an airvent mount for my iPhone since I'm driving for Lyft and need my phone handy at all times.  The windshied on the Ford Escape is pretty far forward and the dash isn't much more accessible.  I mounted this to the right of the steering wheel and now I have great access to my phone.
summary: Fits the 2013 Ford Escape just fine,

reviewText: I've been using this for about 8 months now and it works fine.  still suctions on, works with the 4 different phones that have been used in the car, used it for work alot as well.  would definitely recommend it.

I received the item on time and I liked the design and it's ease of use. I have not tried the air vent mount and I don't know if it works well or not........ totally I like it specially when you are on the road and use your mobile map all the time..... :)

I have used and reviewed many stands and holders for my Galaxy S4 because I was looking for something that would hold my phone for using it as a GPS. I have tried a bean bag holder and a magnetic holder, all of which did very well and I was pleased with the outcome. However, the problem with those holders were that it sits on top of the dash and wasn't very subtle. I originally didn't want something that covered a vent, but it ended up working very well. The height and distance from where I am sitting is perfect and the clips held the holder in place very well. The vent slats in my car are quite thick, so I don't have the same issue as other people with the holder sliding.

I bought this since every time I would turn my smartphone would go flying into my door. This is a great product and will fit any size of phone, even my 4.3" Android with Otterbox case. The vent mount is alright but the suction holds the phone much more securely. I've already recommended this mount to several friends.

I have this in a 2003 Yukon XL attached to the A/C vent. It works great, however, I now can't turn that A/C vent toward me and my cell phone blocks most of the air from blowing on me. I'm the kind of person that uses the A/C all the time, so it's bothersome to me.I also have a 2000 Toyota Sienna, and it won't work on the A/C vents.  But it does work fine on the windshield.  The one problem with the windshield is that in California I believe it's technically illegal to put anything on the windshield. However, the windshield in the Toyota is so big and long that it doesn't interfere with your view of the road.But I do love the fact that I can now easily see my cell phone while I'm driving.

This holder is a decent price and quality. I am very pleased that it expands large enough to hold the Note 3 if you take out the pegs on the bottom. I also like that the arms are spring loaded so to open them you only have to press the button once unlike other holders. Over all I am pleased with this.
This basic apparatus works just as it is purpose for. I live in the desert and the window suction works perfectly. This was a great buy.

I used the alligator clips over an A/C vent for a week or two, until I was sure it was going to work out.  That was over a year ago.  Since then I permanently attached the small black disk.  Now I can unmount the whole thing very easily, but that disk is a permanent fixture in my car.  It's unnoticeable when not mounted.It holds my HTC Evo, which is a larger & heavier than average phone.Using the alligator clips, it's not super.  Make sure you attach the disk in the perfect location.

I haven't had much success with car mounts for either the HTC Hero or Droid Incredible, but the Arkon has been the best I've tried so far and is inexpensive compared to others. I've used it in both a Honda CR-V and Toyota Yaris.Pros:- The windshield clamp is secure and doesn't fall off, and the cradle also holds the phone safely.- Inserting and removing the phone is very easy, which is important since you'll be doing that quite often!- The mount is very flexible, and can be set in a wide range of positions (it can also hold the phone either vertically or horizontally).- It's very simple to install, though be aware that there's only one windshield adhesive so you can't use the windshield mount in more than one car.- The vent mount works flawlessly in the CR-V, and seems most suited to vents with thin plastic bars that are fixed.Cons:- Conversely, the vent mount doesn't work in every vehicle. It won't fit on any vent in the Yaris at all.- The windshield clamp can be tricky to attach (you have to make sure you create enough of a vacuum).Overall, so far so good - I can finally use my phone as a navigation unit while it's charging in the car. Note that there are no power cables or FM transmitters included.
summary: Not perfect, but as good as it gets for the price

reviewText: Works with both my iphone and GS3. I got this to use the air vent mount which once you figure out how to make it work is ok, but is by no means a "firm" hold. If using the vent mount, I recommend programming your nav, plugging in the charger, and turning on the bluetooth before securing your phone into this mount. I have not tried the suction cup (since in my car the winshield is too far for a comfortable mount - why I wanted the vent mount) but appears to be a standard gps-type mount with lever to secure the suction tight.

If you have an oversized smart phone, like my Galaxy Nexus with additional an extra large battery, this car mount will hold your phone just fine. The only thing I would fix on this device is make the suction cup a little bit stronger. I have had to reset it a couple of times when the suction cup moved just a little bit. However, other than that, a pretty good car mount.

Vent mount is unstable!  A hard road bump or accidental contact with hand will dislodge the mounting potentially damaging device or distracting driver. The ball mount allows great alignment of device but bulk causes the device to vibrate a bit while driving. The windshield mount is more stable, but positions device too far away in my car. The adjustable mounting works with many devices, but interferes with either headphone jack or iPhone dock connector, depending device orientation. The grip mechanism works well, but tension spring sounds cheep and sometimes vibrates. Bought this to replace Griffen 3GS vent mount which worked very well. Overall this product is disappointing.
summary: Terrible vent mount; good windshield mount

reviewText: I couldn't be happier with this product.  After viewing several other similar products, I finally decided to purchase this one.  I've so far used it as a suction mount from the windshield, and the vent mount.  Either way I mount it, it works great - though I prefer the vent mount because it places the device closer to me, for easy access to my ipod.The vent mount is very sturdy - even while driving the device is held firmly and I have no complaints about the mount not holding its position.  The bottom pads are adjustable which works perfectly for the ipod's above average sized power connector.  I've uploaded two images - one of the vent mount, and the other showing how I was able to adjust the bottom pads to hug the iPod connector.I purchased this one for my girlfriend, and I am now purchasing a second one for myself, to use with my new HTC EVO 4G phone.

I was skeptical when I ordered this windshield mount, even though it has gotten positive reviews. I mean, $10? I've paid more than that at a mall for a mount that rattled when I drove and fell apart when I touched it the wrong way. Well, this is the real deal. It is solidly built, easy to adjust, versatile. It is the kind of quality I'd expect from a mount costing three times the price.

This seems to be a good quality car mount.  I tried buying other ones at higher prices and returned them all for various reasons.No the vent attachments aren't great, but after researching other ones, I've come to the conclusion all the vent mounts available are lacking.  Every car has a slightly different vent, all car vents move around quite easily, so it would be truly difficult for a manufacturer to make one that holds well and stays put.  The fact that this one comes with a little "arm" for stability shows they at least made an effort.The mechanism to hold your phone has cushion to keep from scratching it, and I love that it holds tightly and you just have to push the knob in to release your phone.Happy with my purchase and will recommend it to my friends.Update 1/2013:  This mount lasted in my car a week before I threw it away.  I've changed my review to 2 stars.  Even the windshield mount didn't stay stable for long.  Any bump I hit caused it to move enough that I feared for the safety of my phone.  It's better than others I've tried, but I no longer feel I can recommend it to others.

I move around alot from different cars, this thing still sticks with no licking of the suction cup.  My only problem is that it has a short arm so for the cars I drive, it must be next to the rearview mirror.  Other than that, it's awesome.

PROS- Suction cup is strong as hell (on glass, didn't test the plastic base)- Work as advertise and good priceVent clip is a good solution, but there are a few shortcomings- it uses phone's weight as an anchor, but will rattle if it's not holding any phone during driving- phone naturally gets hot when using 3G/4G & Nav. Blowing hot air behind it is probably not a good idea.TIPS:- tilt the unit slightly upward, my phone pop out a few times due to potholes.- use sun shield when parked, all plastics don't last long under the sun.
summary: A Great Product, not sure about the vent clips

reviewText: Pros: High quality material. Good adjustability.Cons: A little tricky to tighten the ball joint. Can be difficult to attach to a vent. Moves around a bit.I have only used this item's vent mount. It fits my 2009 Toyota Highlander. The cons listed above are minor. This product is much better than a similar item I recently tried that cost just a few dollars less.Bottom line: High recommended.
I brought three of these for each of my cars.  We totally love its versibility to mount is various areas.
sticks to my windshield, handles all the bumps of off-roading in a jeep. I have not used the vent clip as it is too heavy for my vents. Love the windshield mount though!
This item is a bit flimsy used for the air vent car mount holder.  I haven't tried the dashboard  mount yet.
summary: Windshield Dashboard Air Vent Car Mount Holder for Samsung Galaxy S4

reviewText: Everything works well. the suction cup is pretty strong. i have a galaxy note 2 which isnt the lightest of phones and it holds in place with little shaking. after using it for awhile it has fallen on me once or twice after i moved it. using alcohol swabs when applying seems to fix that. but worth it for the price

This is quite possibly the best windshield mount I've ever purchased. It's rock solid, so there is little to no vibration, it's able to hold my huge EVO with the Ballistic case on it, and has yet to fall off the windshield, been on for over a month now. Very Happy Customer!!
Holds strong, has only fallen off once, status tight in orientation, flexible positioning.Only gripe is that the foam flakes off a little bit.  No biggie.

This mount I used for about two years.  The suction cup only lasted about a year and gave out. I used the vent mount after that which worked pretty well in my Honda Fit but it started to get annoying when one side would come loose on sharp turns.  It would also rattle unless you kept it clamped.  If you left it clamped for say overnight though, it would loose a little bit of springiness so I had to always unclamp it when I left the car and clamp it when I got in the car, EVERY TIME.  It was really easy to mount the phone with one hand while driving, which was a big plus.I have since moved onto another mount that is not quite as easy to mount with one hand but superior in every other way.  It looks much better and is not bulky.  It has one very springy arm that tightly comes down on side to lock it securely in place.  It uses a gel suction cup that I have never removed in over two years.  This new one doesn't rattle and I highly recommend just checking out the most popular dash mounts on Amazon
summary: had for while but moved on

reviewText: The whole reason I purchased this model of car mount was because I wanted the ability to  mount it via the vent clips so I wouldn't have to permanently stick anything onto my dash which would 1. obstruct my vision of the road and 2. be a pain to remove - especially if I didn't end up liking the where I positioned it on my dash. It worked for about a week or so but on an extended road trip, the vibration from the car ultimately made the vent clips "weaken" for lack of a better word and the clips to open which of course caused the whole thing to fall out of the vent. I thought I would just rubber binders to keep the clips closed but it was a pain in the rear to finagle them back onto the vent and it  ended up taking up so much space on the clip that it would no longer fully go onto the vent.Frustrated, I ended up just attaching it to the section cup attachment and my phone (Samsung Note 3) is too heavy for it apparently or the suction cup is just poorly made, but keeps coming unstuck after a day or 2. :(I would not recommend this product to anyone who has a heavy/bulky phone.

reviewText: I go this to hold my Droid Maxx in a protective case while in the car. reviewText: Bought this a little over a month ago.  I drive a 2004 Honda Accord LX - large dash, and mounting to the dash or windshield isn't as easy (too far from windshield, and the dash would require a long-necked holder as well to make it usable while driving).  I have mounted it to the air vent as a result; it works well enough for my purposes, but can be frustrating at times.This was fairly obvious out-of-the-box on how to assemble it and mount it to the air vents, which is a plus; simple design is always a good thing.  It took me 5 minutes to put it together and mount it.Pros: Simple design, easy to assemble, easy to mount.  Holds the mobile phone in just the right spot for driving.  Good price for the product, and not too many other similar choices on the market that I saw.Cons: How it holds onto the air vents isn't very strong - if you try to adjust the angle of the phone, or attach a power or earphone cable, while the phone is held in place, it will easily fall off the vent (dangerous to the phone itself, if it fell in just the wrong way).  The spring that releases the clamped in phone must be used to remove the phone when done, or else it falls off; the spring mechanism feels cheap to the touch, so I'm guessing that eventually, it will give way and break.Overall, it seems like it works well enough once you've gotten used to how easily it falls off.  If you're prepared for that part, it's a decent product.  I'd give it at least one more star on the rating if it had better air vent clips that held on with more pressure.
summary: Works at least well enough for my purposes, but a not robust

reviewText: Good quality - suction cup stays on very nicely. Only con I can think of is it shakes more than I would expect when my iphone is being used as a GPS or screen.

reviewText: I am using this for my HTC incredible. It holds it perfectly and no interference with the charging cord. This mount is constructed well and does not rattle as you drive.

reviewText: This device does improve signal strength. However, if I had been buying it (rather than evaluating it as a review model), I would probably be debating whether to return it. It just doesn't work as well as the manufacturer claims. The Sony Ericsson (3G) phone that we have goes from a typical 3 bars in this area, up to 4 rather than 5.  The iPhone and Droid I tried it with did get a signal boost, but they were already starting at 5 bars so it wasn't a dramatic one.It's not a bad product, by any means. It clearly does work, and for someone living or working in a spot that has a very weak signal it would certainly be worth considering. It's quite easy to set it up, and having a phone holder built into it is nice. It's just that the company is so emphatic about the idea that this will consistently boost the signal to 5 bars that, particularly when one of the phones was already starting at 3, it was a disappointment to have it fall short.
summary: Good, but not as good as promised

reviewText: The hype claims that this unit "guarantees 5BARz for mobile phones, voice and data on all carriers". However, after opening the box I found a 4" x 5" note that says "It will extend the weakest of signals from all cellular carriers (except Nextel)...........". The hype further says that the signal extension includes netbooks and notebooks with cellular connectivity. I carry along a netbook on my travels so this was the main factor in my selection of this product. In the only user instruction included with the product, the "Quick Guide" there is a miniscule amount of information but no mention of netbooks or notebooks. However, a web site URL is provided "for additional information or troubleshooting tips".I went to the web site in the hopes of obtaining netbook information. You would have to visit this web site to believe it. The first thing that strikes you is that the initial page is mostly made up of popups of useless fluff.  Kinda like those annoying popups you get when surfing. I did finally find a support box and clicked on it which produced a menu. I chose the register option. There were the usual name, email addy etc boxes and one box labeled messages or questions. I had neither one so I clicked send.  Surprisingly, my registration would not accept until I posted a message/question. So, my question was "Why do I have to ask a question to register?"Next, I tried to find information on netbooks. I could find none. I gave up. A third grader could build a better web site. I gave this product 3 stars overall. It does have the ability to extend signals for a cell phone on select networks.  I deducted one star for the rinky dink web site and its lack of pertinent and necessary netbook information and also because there was no netbook information provided with the product. I deducted one star for the shameful and misleading hype. For me personally there is no way that this item is worth its high cost for solely increasing signal strength on certain networks for a cell phone. For example, my daughter lives 650 miles away. From my home to hers there is one area where the signal is weak. It takes a few minutes to get past this area and all is well again. Not a big deal to have a few minutes of down time over a 12 hour period. So, if your travels are such that you absolutely must have a strong signal for every inch of the way and at no time can you pause long enough to get through a low spot then you may want to consider purchasing this highly priced product. Without netbook information this item is of little value to me.

This unit does seem to increase my iPhone's reception noticeably when it's within range. However, I'm just not sure that there is really a good place for it, except maybe in an office environment.  Around the house or in the car, the components are bulky and there are wires running everywhere. It doesn't look good in the house unless you can find a nice way to hide it.  But then you'd have to move it as soon as your earpiece goes out of range.
