reviewText: If you're getting at least a bit of a signal already but not nearly enough, and either live in a rural area or in the city in a basement, this could be exactly what you need...if you also have a bluetooth set-up! Keeping the phone two feet or less from the unit might be a hassle, and the bt will solve that.5Barz is exactly what you need for those situations, and for driving in the middle of nowhere. This puppy is your solution for those problems, and if you use your phone a lot, it will be worth the 2.4 bills. If you don't have a bt, or aren't getting any signal at all, this unit is probably not what you need. It is indeed a bit spendy, but its value lies entirely in your own specific situation.As long as you're getting a bar or near to it, this will boost your signal plenty, and you will love 5Barz.
summary: Does what it should, for specific situations

reviewerName: Mary Jo Sminkey "15 years of Amazon Reviews!"
reviewText: I don't use my phone in the car so haven't really tested this device in that situation, but I do have an even more common issue which is very poor reception at the office. Many office buildings do a great job of blocking cell signals and if you are anywhere other than near a window you often won't be able to use your cell phone. I usually have to make a trip outside to make a call so this device sounded like the perfect answer to the problem. And indeed, it really does work! Now, I don't get the promised 5 bars, but I do get at least 2-3 and it sometimes creeps up to 4. Which is fine by me, it's enough to make and receive calls.The downsides for me are that the signal degrades much more than the promised 2 feet radius. I find I have to have the phone in the cradle to keep the signal. It's not a big deal since the cable is long enough to use the phone with the cradle attached (and of course you can always use a headset) but it's a disappointment nonetheless. We tried an iPhone with it and found the same thing, and also noticed the iPhone seemed to have more problems getting a strong signal.My other gripe is the flimsy stand on the cradle, it doesn't lock open (or closed) and isn't sturdy enough to really support the phone well. It just really feels like it's going to just snap off with use, and considering that I have to use the phone attached to the cradle it'd be nice if it worked better.The device support iGo which means you can buy a tip for about $10 to use for charging the phone while using it. I always am forgetting to charge my phone so this is something I plan to get, it's a nice bonus feature to have.The device doesn't work on all networks so be sure to do your research first. I also can't see how it would possibly work with a laptop, at least in my situation, considering that I can't get a signal even a few inches from the cradle. So I'd hesitate to buy it for indoor use if that is a desired option.Overall, fairly pleased with what this device gives me. I do sometimes travel to locations that have very poor signals (national parks being the most common) so I do plan to try it when I travel to see how much it helps in those situations. It's not cheap but if having phone access at all times is important to you, it might be worth the cost.
summary: Great for boosting a poor signal, with some caveats

reviewText: This gadget is designed to boost cell signals in poor coverage areas, essentially an external antenna.  It does this task well if your network uses one of the ranges it is compatible with. It is primarily designed for car use but can also work indoors as long as you don't mind leaving your phone nearby. It also allows for charging provided you connect to the USB port or purchase an adaptor.  It won't make a good signal any better, its really just for those who need cell phone access in low coverage areas. For that purpose it works exactly as it should.

This must be simplest little gadget out there.  It keeps your cell phone from suffering those frustrating and annoying dropped calls when you drive through an area with weak signal reception.  It maintains your cell phone signal at "5 bars", hence the name.  You simply place the device on your dashboard, plug it into the FREE CELL PHONE HOLDER, and connect the holder via a gooseneck plug into the cigarette power source outlet in your car (but any 12 Volt outlet will do, including those on boats, big rigs, and farm equipment), then place your cell phone between the two clamps in the holder, switch the device button to "on", and hey presto, you're in business.I didn't have a cell phone holder before, BUT NOW I DO!  Important here in California where hand holding of cell phones while driving can potentially yield a traffic ticket.You can also use the device at home, if you have the problem with dropped signals there too; the cell phone holder has a movable stand that you extend to allow it to rest on a table.  The same simple assembly at home too.According to the accompanying brochure, the device is NOT designed to provide this coverage outside of a 2 foot radius of the phone holder.  Within the two foot area, you can get clear phone calls on up to 20 phones, iPhones, and Smartphones.Highly recommended.
summary: Great little device---AND YOU GET A FREE CELL PHONE HOLDER!

reviewText: My townhouse has a finished basement which I use as a den.  Unfortunately I get NO cell phone reception down there which is not very convenient.I set this up and tested it out using my land line to dial my cell phone:* Turn the unit off.* Call my cell phone.  I do not receive a call.* Turn the unit on.* Repeat the call.  Call is received on my cell phone.* Move 6 feet away from the unit.* Repeat the call.  I do not receive a call.I also called myself, answered and walked around the room, talking into the land line and listening on the cell phone to see how the connection was.  It was good for 3 or 4 feet and was cutting out at around 8 or 9 feet.I believe it's really intended to be used in conjunction with a bluetooth headset for your phone.  I can leave the phone on the holder and use the bluetooth headset to answer calls and chat and walk around, since my bluetooth headset has a much greater range.I haven't tried this in my car yet since I get good reception there anyway but I'll probably take this with me the next time I go on vacation -- I like to drive and there are definitely dead spots here and there which this should resolve.There are other cell phone repeaters to choose from, though, and you'll have to decide what features you want.  For this one, the bad news is that it only extends the radius by "2 feet", as advertised, or slightly more in practice.  The good news is it works straight out of the box.  I've seen other cell phone repeaters for the home that cost about the same as this and provide a much wider coverage but they seem to involve installing antennas, and, of course, do not go in your car.This one has power adapters for house and car and there is literally nothing to do except plug it in.
summary: Cell Phone Coverage From Thin Air

reviewText: This is possibly one of the easiest to use cell phone contraption I used. It's usage is mainly to get a strong signal at areas where you have sketchy signals. It maintains 5 bars as the name suggests.You simply plug the device into your power source in the car and fuggedaboutit. A snap to use in the car when on the go as well as at home.Recommended.

I won't go into detail, as many reviewers have already mentioned the pluses and FEW, if any minuses.  All I can say is that this product really does deliver a CONSISTANT 4 bars, no matter where you might be, even in the drop off zones.Yes, it is a bit pricey, but if you are a businessperson and want to project a professional image without "dropping" important client calls, then this is the product for you and in the long run, will pay for itself several times over.

Installed about two weeks ago, took off and threw away today. I followed the instructions, and took my time. Initially didn't look to bad. Kind of orange peel look and micro bubbles. All supposed to go away in a few days. I let the phone sit for 2 days after application before I used it. After 2 weeks the micro bubbles were still there and the screen side started coming loose in the corners. Also didn't like the rubbery feel of the screen. It also made the phone look really cheap. Ordered a scosche band edge and put it on afterwards. Keeps the screen from contacting surfaces where you lay your phone. I'll just need to be careful of the screen because these products a terrible.

I have used Zagg invisishield on the past two iphones I had, so I purchased one for my iphone 4. Much to my dismay, the invisishield was nothing but garbage. It never completely dried, and the slightest touch would move the shield. Forget about putting it in your pocket, the whole thing would move and peel from the phone. Zagg's lifetime warranty is also a farce. First they try to say I installed it wrong,( me and about a 1,000 other people I guess) and then finally agreed to send me another one. Why would I want another one I don't know, because they don't work as advertised. I wanted my money back! Needless to say I chalked it up to experience and will never buy another Zagg product.Hence my review on the skinomi skin. I wish I knew about this company earlier. The product is 100 times better than Zagg. It actually fits percisely over the phone, and it includes front, back, sides and top and bottom protection, that actually stays on the phone. I don't even use a case just slide it into my pocket. Try that with Zagg and the film stays in your pocket. Even skinomi side protection stays on the phone which is very impressive. The film is clearer than Zagg and you don't see any orange peel effect. Everything is crystal clear.On top of it all, the Skinomi is half the price of the Zagg at $14.99 and still has a lifetime warranty. I'll bet when word gets around of this great product, Zagg will have to resort to selling their crappy headphones to stay alive.

reviewerName: G. Proulx "Up to my Neck in Tech"
reviewText: I got this because it got good reviews online and because I have tried Zagg in the past and wasn't a fan. I originally just got a front skin. Application was pretty easy. However I noticed that there was a .75 inch vertical scratch in the plastic. It was some time of manufacturing defect. It looked like how scratches look on the iphone screen. It would reflect light and give a rainbow effect. It wasn't too noticeable unless you were on a white background. So I called Skinomi and right away got someone to pick up. I told him my problem and that I wanted a full body kit next. He allowed me to upgrade for a couple bucks which was great.So the new one came and I put it on. Installation wasn't too bad. The coverage of the side pieces is good too. However, I noticed the same problem again. On the front I had different vertical scratches, this time a couple of them. Not a dealbreaker because they aren't too noticeable. It just seems like their manufacturing process hasn't been perfected yet.However, the back was more of a dealbreaker. The reason I upgraded to a full body kit was because my gel case was distorting my flash. However, I was still noticing hazy flash pictures. I was really skeptical that the skinomi skin was causing it. My friend didn't believe it. My back skin was lined up perfectly. However, it seemed hazy. So I tore it off and took comparison shots before and after. Sure enough, this skin reflects the LED flash and distorts low-light photos. This could be remedied if you did a bit of your own cutting I imagine. I still can't believe that such a thin skin, with what seemed like an adequate hole caused this haziness, but I have the pictures to convince me.Anyway, called Skinomi back. Had to call several times before getting someone. They were nice, offered me another kit, but I declined. They gave me a refund.So, this product could work with some cutting and if you turn a blind eye. Only 3 stars, however, due to the streaks and the camera cutout being too small apparently.Hope this review was helpful in your decision. If there are questions or if there is anything I can clarify, please leave me a comment.

This is what I get for being impatient. I should have been worried when I saw how flexible the skin was prior to application. The damn thing doesn't stop moving! Then it picks up pocket lint which makes it lose it's mediocre stickiness and renders it completely useless.Second worst property... it's thick vinyl. Much like a shower curtain. reviewText: Want to know why to buy this product?Here's the why: It's super slim and leaves your whole phone protected from the normal wear and tear of scrapes and scuffs. It keeps the device looking new, while making the device feel just like it should in your hand. It's excellent for someone that take good care of their phone, but needs scuff protection from items in your pocket or purse.Why shouldn't you buy this: If you intend on regularly dropping your phone in lava, coffee, poop, or other unusual semi solids and liquids, don't get this... or if you just intend on dropping your phone, period. This isn't for you. This isn't a "case", so don't expect it to be one. It's a screen/body protector. If you cannot clean your device or take approximately 30 minutes of your time to apply the skins properly, don't get this. Or if you can't leave your device untouched over an approximate 12 hour period after applying the skin - still not for you.So that said, I like it a lot. No, it's not a case - but I like the excellent coverage, clear image (no distortion when applied properly), and good looks. It does take some patience applying it and waiting for it to dry properly - but if you take your time, it's not hard at all... just takes a little patience.Eat your heart out ZAGG! :)
summary: Drops, and scrapes, and scratches - Skinomi!

reviewText: Skinomi has great products and excellent customer service. Don't waste your money on overpriced InvisibleShields. They live up to their warranty promise no questions asked.

Wow. Went on perfectly the first time.  Next came the Skinomi and since I just put the Zagg on the front, I put the back film, well, on the back.It, too, went on perfectly.I compared the optics. This is a great product. At first the screen was a bit foggy but after 24hrs it's nearly invisible. I can't stress it enough, TAKE YOUR TIME! Apply this in a room that is as clean and dust free as possible. It's very easy to apply but you need to have patience. Love the product!

The box and accompanying spray bottle look nice, but really how important is that?This is a standard screen protector that is the standard level of difficult to apply. i have had better covers. the Zagg ones are top of the line and even though this works just fine i dont think i wil order it again since zagg is much better quality for me at least. This product is ok and is cheaper than zagg but up to you how much you want to spend.

reviewText: This is a difficult review to write, for several reasons.This screen protector does in fact work, but it requires such detailed precision that it becomes aggravating.Once you have made the mistake of touching the sticky side of the screen protector, that's it. You're done. Meaning: there will always be a fingerprint on the sticky side. This screen protector film literally reminds me if the tape used on the show "CSI" to lift prints. That's basically exactly what happens though if you make the mistake of touching the sticky part. Fortunately, I touched the sticky part in a corner that isn't likely to be noticed. I made this mistake when applying this to my daughter's Fubu Nabi Jr II tablet. The protective case comes with literally a screen protector solution designed to clean the glass prior to installing it, and a really decent yellow rubbery-like square designed to help remove bubbles as you apply the cover. They also provide you with the address to a YouTube Video that gives you step by step instructions. I found all to be very useful.Yes, this product is expensive. However, when you consider all the things offered in order to VERY carefully apply the protective film, and understand what the protective film contains, you might find it worth being as patient as possible to ensure proper installation. The one I installed on my daughters tablet isn't perfect, but I will say that it holds up to everything she does to it. She's a three! Need I say more?I likey kent purchase anothr one of these, I've found that specific brands are just as effective, less expensive and easier to apply. Although I will always be grateful for the company's willingness to assist in any way possible to your success in installing this cover, I'll stick to the simpler version. I don't possess the patience that's required. The "Oops I just spent how much on this cover and I've already ruined it by getting it stuck to itself AND have a fingerprint on it" was enough for me just to be grateful for the cleaning solution and move on.I hope that's helpful!
summary: Decent Product, but requires too much patience!

reviewText: The best screen protector I've ever used and very easy to install/apply onto your phone. I love it. The price is right.

reviewText: The outside is a textured plastic shell which feels somewhat "soft" but not rubbery. If you keep your phone in your pocket, this is great because there is no sticky rubber to catch on anything. This was a huge problem for me with the "bodyglove" case I had before. The look is cool too. It looks and feels very high quality (almost like leather), much better than any of the other cases for the Droid I have seen so far.The inside is all soft rubber; the thing I like about this is that there is nothing that can scratch your phone on the inside. All connections between the case and your phone are soft. Both pieces fit snugly and securely to the phone.There are rubber stoppers that cover all ports on the case. If you don't like these, you can easily and cleaning sever them with a knife. I really like the rubber covers on the power, volume and camera controls, as it actually makes them easier to use than with just the phone by itself anyway.It comes with a screen protection, but really these are superfluous anyway. The Droid already has a real glass screen. Real glass is not like the plastic on most cell phones; it is very difficult to scratch. You could take steel wool to a glass screen and not leave a single scratch.This is definitely the best case I have used so far on any phone. And they make them for a variety of models, not just the Droid. So if you have a non-droid cell phone you might want to visit their site and see if they have a version for your phone.
summary: The best phone case I have ever owned

reviewText: I've always heard how otter box cases were the best out there, this is the second case I've bought for the phone and I can't say I see what is so special about the brand.My first case was some generic brand, had to be replaced because the tabs that attach the front cover snapped off after a drop. This otterbox has a very secure front piece, almost too secure when I had trouble getting it off when I put it on before I intended to. I also do like how it extends the buttons out since it can be a bit difficult to press them when a case is on otherwise, though I do think they extend a bit too far out.The problem is the back piece, it is rather loose fitting and while it hasn't come off during a drop yet it has when I am taking the phone out of a cradle in my car. From that is has developed small cracks along the side where it bent while coming out, the rubber underneath should hold it together but still. What holds it on the back of the phone is basically friction and the charging port/3.5mm jack covers, hence why it keeps falling off when removing it from my cradle when I have both plugged in. This case is also also rather thick which makes it a tight fit in said cradle not helping the issue. The included screen protector was a nice bonus but it's nothing special, and I was quite annoyed that there was a sticker on it that left a residue that had to be scratched off, the sticker was supposed to be used to easily remove the screen protector from the backing but there are better ways to achieve that without putting anything on the plastic.Aesthetics wise this is a fairly ugly case, the big "Otter Box" logo on the back is unsightly, and like I said it is bulky.
I broke the front plate so bad I just removed it, but it protected my phone so it did it's job! Well worth the money to only break a cover and not replace a phone.

great product, protects perfect, fits perfect, no defects i can see i have had it on and used it for about 2 months now and not a single problem.. i see some have a problem with the top piece but mine fits and stays on and protects just fine! great product all the way around!

I bought this product in October 2010, so I've had it for roughly two months now.  Let me tell you that this is a terrible product and the entire thing is broken now.The top protector that snaps onto the touch screen broke within a week.  I dropped my phone on a tile from 3 feet up (I was pulling it out of my pocket on the way out of the bathroom) and the two sides shattered cleanly, so I had two "U"-shaped pieces of plastic.  There was no way I could possibly reattach this thing to my phone without supergluing it on.I continued to use the Otterbox because the back seemed to provide adequate protection against falls.  Then, right after thanksgiving, I was sitting down on a couch and the phone fell from my hands onto a concrete floor.  The distance was no more than 2 feet, but the back shattered as well, leaving the bottom end of the phone without a hard plastic covering.  It snapped on both sides of the speaker on the back, where the plastic was thinnest, I suppose.I will amend this review of Otterbox ever sends me a new case unit, and hopefully that won't break.  Maybe I just got a bad version, but it seems to me that something that sells for $40 in stores should be a little more resistant to falls - the whole purpose of the case!
summary: Broke after Normal Use.  Will not buy again or recommend to others

reviewText: The otterbox commuter series for droid is the worst otterbox product I have ever bought. Not only the worst otterbox but even the worst case I have ever bought. I paid over 40 dollars for this case and it literally only lasted 3 days, it did not hold up at all. The front part of the case broke the second day without even being droppped, and the bottom part of the case lasted only 2 days more, I did drop the bottom part, but for the fall the case shouldnt've reacted the way it did. In my opinion do not waste your money on this product buy a SEIDIO case like I did its cheaper and I have not had a single problem out of it for about a month now.

I have Otterbox for other items and loved them. I have this currently on my Droid. Recently I dropped my Droid and it survived the fall with only minor scratches to the screen protector. Fitment is great and port covers work well to keep dust and moisture out.

Let me introduce myself to explain the conditions my phone endures during the events of a day. I am an archaeologist and spend my days working in the dirt and covered in sweat as its typically between 98-107 degrees Fahrenheit where I work. Dirt gets into absolutely every piece of gear we use. On top of that due to humidity here never falling below 90% during the day, when I say my job is hell on phones, I mean it. This Otterbox is my second smartphone Otterbox, and I am just as pleased with the Commuter series case for the Motorola Droid as I was with the same series case for my Blackberry Storm2. This case does an excellent job of keeping dirt and dust out of the ports and side buttons of the phone. But it isn't perfect and hence receives a 4 star rating. The phone itself prevents a 5 star rating for any  case available. Dirt tends to get into the ear speaker and on the keys of the keyboard as well as accumulate at the edges of where the top screen guard case overlaps with the touchscreen. Don't get me wrong, this is an absolutely wonderful case that stands up well to the rigors of daily use. For field conditions I would also using an Aquapac to keep dirt and water off the phone, which does a great job at the expense of hindering use of the touchscreen.
summary: Best case available for Moto Droid

reviewText: This case has proven itself to do everything I could ask of a cell phone case.  First and foremost, it protects everything it needs to.  The rubber "plugs" do a great job of covering both the charging port as well as the 3.5mm jack.  This becomes VERY apparent if you carry your phone in your pants pockets (like 99% of all guys do) and keeps all the lint and crud out of it.The material it's made of is perfect for it's application.  It's hard enough to withstand being thrown around but soft enough to keep from damaging any parts that it attaches to.  Better yet, the glossy-veneer material it's made of makes sliding it in and out of your pocket a breeze, MUCH easier than a few of the rubber-based covers I've tried.The front snap-on perimeter cover works great, although there really isn't much expected of it with it being so small.  The 2-part case works great with the sliding action and doesn't limit any movement in any way.  One of the biggest bonuses that the case has to offer is how the power/screen-off button at the top is now raised slightly so that it can be pressed without much effort, deeming it even BETTER then the phone without a case.  Both the camera and volume buttons both have a similar raised feeling.As if the case wasn't a good enough deal, it also comes with a very nice static-cling crystal-clear cover for the screen, which is very nice as an added bonus that I didn't even know about when I bought it.The only downsides I see with the case wouldn't really be about the design or functionality of the case, but more of what using it entails.  You obviously can't remove the memory card and/or battery near as easy without removing the case first.  Second, the OEM Droid GPS mount obviously isn't going to fit with the case on, and it does seem to be the best mount I've found for it.  Finding another mount that perfectly holds the Droid with the case on is a bit of a challenge with the side buttons sticking out slightly due to the aforementioned raised buttons.Aside from those points, it's been a flawless product for me.  I've accidently dropped the phone at least twice from 3+ feet, and both times the case has protected the phone greatly.  One of those times, it even took the permanently-scratched grunt of the fall, thus keeping the phone in flawless shape.  I'd VERY highly recommend this case to anyone looking for a great all-around case.

Either this doesn't fit the phone or I'm not smart enough to figure out how to snap a piece of plastic on the thing.  And since I have a Ph.D., I'm leaning toward it doesn't fit correctly.  Money wasted.

I wanted something that was made well and didn't care how much thicker it made my phone. This fits the bill. I love the fact that it has dust covers that cover all the buttons so no dirt/dust gets in. I was sitting with it in my hand the other day and the outer ring for the front of the phone just snapped. I attempted to super glue it but it was just under too much stress to hold. I have also removed the main back part of the case and noticed the tabs are extremely fragile and have broken slightly. They did not break completely off and the case still holds fine on the back. I am EXTREMELY careful with my phone and anything I buy (especially more expensive items). I was not rough with this and was very upset at the fact that it just started snapping randomly with no real stress other than it just being on. The only saving grace is Otterbox has excellent customer support. When I contacted them they told me they were having a lot of customers reporting issues with the cases on this specific phone. When they investigated they noticed that the sizes of the phones were changing with each one coming off the line. Each company has a range of specs to keep within a certain tolerance. Motorola has gotten worse since the design of this case as far as staying within this tolerance. If Otterbox created the design of the case based on Droids manufactured from the same plant/size, it is really not their fault if the tolerance widens on future phones. Therefore, Otterbox has not issued a recall and will not. Why should they pay for a manufacturing mistake of the phone manufacturer. They are now sending me a replacement case (so in a sense they are still paying for it). I do not hold them to blame as many customers have had no issues whatsoever. I do however think if your considering purchasing, you should be aware of the issue. As far as everything else, I love the case in every way.EDIT 05/01/2011 I have edited my stars down from 4 to 2 because this case did not last. It broke apart from the constant temperature change from cold to warm inside (work). What good is a case that only lasts a short period of time? Go with a seidio innocase surface instead for this phone.
After reading the instructions i opted not to apply this to my Droid. Looks to risky to mess and tricky to mess with but it did arrive on time.

This is probably just me, but I couldn't get this on my phone's screen without bubbles.  I've never been a huge fan of these things, but I figured I'd give this one a shot...to no avail, I'm afraid.  So, if you're good with this sort of thing, go for it.  But if not, just be careful with your phone!
summary: Couldn't get it onto my phone

reviewText: I only trust my cell phone screens with skinomi. Only 10 dollars plus free shipping, where can you go wrong? In addition, if you ever have any problems with the screen protectors (you wont), they can be sent back for a free replacement. The only bad thing about this product would be the installation. I dont know about anyone else, but im not too fond of putting water near or on my cell phone. Done it twice now and havent had any water damage or any problems though. They are amazing the screens last pretty much forever : )

This screen protector is hands down the best I've ever used. Reading some of the negative reviews and seeing some of the videos made me a bit skeptical, but trying it out for myself, skinomi now has a customer for life.Installation was super fast and easy. I don't know what the deal is with some of these guys, but it took me no more than three minutes and I'm writing this review right now on my droid x less than an hour later. No bubbles. No smudges. No complaints. Just read the instructions first and there will be no problems.

I have used the Skinomi TechSkin protector on multiple devices and have been happy with every one of them. The installation takes a little bit of time and patience, but the end result is well worth it. The streaks and bubbles do take a few days to completely go away, but after about 12 hours you can turn the screen on and barely notice them.

Slow to apply if you are new at it. Make sure to follow the instructions and use plenty of the spray that comes with it. It will look like junk at first but after drying for a few hours it will clear up. It scratches easily but its better than permanent scratches on your screen. Looks better than the Fellows RightWriter protectors I used on my old phone.
This was a little bit complicated to put on, but I followed the instructions and did it perfectly, the thing never peeled of in two years!

I purchased this product after reviewing several screen protectors.  This protector was less expensive than some of the others but had great reviews.  When I installed this I was amazed at the difference between this one and the generic ones that come with the phone.  My screen was amazingly clear.  After three months the protector is still crystal clear, free of scratches, and completely adhered to the phone.  I am extremely pleased with this product and highly recommend it to anyone. I even purchased the Skinomi version for the Kindle Fire.  More difficult to put on, but equally happy with it.

the protector is very clear, especially after a few days for the bubbles to evaporate after application.  the instructions were easy enough to follow though a little daunting as liquids and electronics don't mix.  since applied the film hasn't moved or peeled up; it stays put.  i also like that the film is smooth (except where indentations have appeared, next paragraph), my finger glides across as i use swype or flip though screens.my issue is that the protector itself doesn't resist scratches or indentations.  i have several very visible and tactile marks as a result from coins carried in the same pocket as my phone.  i was expecting a harder film to not only protect the glass underneath but resist scratches itself.i would reapply this film if i were to switch from the silicone case I currently have to a pouch.  i want to find something that is completely devoid of a clip and covers all of the phone so i can continue to carry in my pocket.  such a case, i believe, would negate the effects of coins, keys or other items that would affect the look and feel of the film.

I found this protector quite easy to install compared with other adhesive screen protectors.  I wore latex gloves (washed with soap and water) to prevent finger prints.  It took me a couple of attempts to line it up with the edges just right.  It really does look a little crappy at first, but within a few days, it sets and the screen protector clears right up.  It is a tough material that seems to resist scratching and you can clean it with any soft cloth.  I haven't had any issues with it and it looks like it will last as long as my DX.  I highly recommend this item.
summary: Easy installation, patience required for settling in...

reviewText: I applied the screen protector with the applicator spray which did worry me because liquid on your screen=NOOOO!. I didn't seem to have a problem with that as it calls for your phone to be off 12-24 hours but I turned mine on in about a hour. It went on easy and fit very well. I did not like the feel to the film tho as it felt tacky and sticky. Now the next day it was very hot at work and having the phone in my pocket seemed to cause the edges to become moist and allow dust to slip underneath. Im guessing that it wasn't completely dry:(. The screen did look flawless with no bubbles or anything but the edges become all dusted up and looked horrible.I broke down and removed it. The lifetime guarantee covers scratched torn and damaged screens but as far as my problem.."The replacement guarantee does not cover silicone cases, installation errors including air bubbles, dust or dirt caught underneath the TechSkin, and improper alignment of the film on your device. Please follow the installation instructions carefully when applying"

Captivate Skinomi Screen Protector / B003F32X9KI had to smile a little at the hype on the description page - this is a nice little screen protector, but it's really just that: it protects your screen reasonably well.The liquid application technique that this uses is rather nice; save the leftover liquid for later touch-ups or if you ever just want a new screen cover entirely. Most of the bubbles do come out, but like all screen protectors there will be a leftover bubble or two that just won't come out. Period. It's irksome, but I suppose a bubble is better than a permanent scratch. The protector is easy enough to apply (good) and easy enough to remove (better), so I have no complaints on that end.There's absolutely no way that this protector is finger-print resistance or reduced glare, but I've given up looking for those things in a screen cover - again, it's the price you pay for safety. The protector does feel a little "sticky" to the touch - Swype is still certainly useable, but occassionally you'll notice the sticky feeling, like your finger isn't swiping at it's full potential. This never becomes overly distracting, though.The protector is definitely shaped for the Captivate, with the proper curving to avoid covering the light sensor and the front speaker. I'm happy enough with this cover, and it does what it's supposed to.~ Ana Mardoll

They skin comes in a large box kinda making you wonder whats actually in the box but when you open it, there is only the skin, and little plastic card and a little spray bottle about the size of a cigar.  the instructions were fairly direct but still complicated.  you have to dust off the phone, take the battery out, spray your screen with the spray solution, spray your fingers so that no fingerprints get on the skin, and spray the skin and handle the skin while your fingers are still wet. use the card to push out the air bubbles and wait 12 - 24 hrs before using your phone again.  so yeah long process.  But the skin has been good overall, when i scratch it with my fingernails, the skin just absorbs it and looks like I didn't do anything.  Sorry this was a long review

These are very thick screen protectors, thicker than i thought they would be...i would guess these are the most durable available...which is good....however they have a kind of rubber feel to them that detracts from the ease of sliding your finger on the screen, they also seem to have an "orange peel" effect going on when you look at from certain angles...straight they look clear though.I am going to keep this one until my new ones (different brand) arrive. I am looking for a clearer less rubbery one.As for ease of installation, i kinda of disagree with everyone else i guess, as i found it kinda hard and i messed it up and got a little dust under the screen...creating a dust free environment is probably the most important step in installing imo...which they do not provide any tips...i found some online; spray a water bottle on mist in the air of the room you plan on doing the install, let the mist settle the dust for a few minutes then proceed. Make sure your hands and the screen are also very clean.if you are looking for a very durable screen protector this probably the one for you.

Everytime I look for screen protectors when I get a new portable device, it's always hit or miss as I could never determine which is a good product or not (especially buying online).  But this has to be the easiest to install screen protector I've used.  The install is similar to adding car window tint.You spray the included solution onto the sticky side of the protector and your fingers and carefully install to line up perfectly.  The solution gives you the ability to slide the protector in perfect position.  Then you "squegee" the rest of the solution off (best if you have a lint free cloth ready to soak up excess solution as it comes out of the protector).Having the solution sprayed on your fingers during the install helped reduce/remove the fingerprints that were left on the protector during handling (though try your best not to touch the stick side).  Once it's on to my liking, I left the protector on for 24 hours before use.  Reason for this was when the protector is first installed, it looks as if there were liquid that couldn't be removed.  Having it settle seems to make it go away, so my install came out perfectly after one day.Durability is really good as I've tried scratching it with my fingernail with no marks left on it.  Too scared to try my keys, so I don't think I'll be doing that, lol.  I can still use the phone without problems in terms of swipes and scrolls.  The protector does not hinder the performance of finger swipes.
summary: Easiest install of all screen protectors!!

reviewText: Best screen protector out there. I first bought it for a tablet I bought for my siblings and up to this date the screen is like new. No scratches on the screen and it lasts for ever. I now buy the Skinomi screen protector every time I get a new phone or tablet.Even when it looks like you've put a bad scratch on the phone the material protects it really well. What seems like a scratch disappears in a matter of a few minutes. Highly recommend it.

I just got this in the mail. My home is in one of the RF (at cell phone frequencies) black holes common in the mountains. Even the Razr (that has the best receiver of any cell phone ever made) and would pull in only one bar very intermittently. After fabricating a 12volt adapter and clamping the antenna on a 6" scrap of sheet metal to a window sill, I slid the phone into place and instantly saw 3 bars. And, it stayed at three bars. A good solid signal. I don't have a bluetooth device, so just used the phone on speaker and made a few test calls. Perfect. Next, I'll move the antenna a little higher and cut some metal to have a proper ground plane. Then, I'll look for a bluetooth headset. I highly recommend this little miracle from Wilson Electronics.UPDATE: Just got a smart phone that shows signal strength. -104 without the Wilson, -70 with! Awesome.
summary: Huge signal strength increase! Wow! This thing works great!

reviewText: I have several Wilson electronics items and could not be happier with their performance and the company. When they say they warranty the equipment, they mean it! I had a water problem that ruined a handset. Within a few days I had a new handset!I am so satisfied with how well their electronics allow me to use my ATT cell phone almost anywhere with high speed data. Anyone in a rural area needs Wilson Electronics for their internet on their phone. I am a loyal Wilson Electronics user for life!
summary: Best customer service and best electronics in the business

reviewText: I just moved into a new office cube at the first floor of an old building. The entire area where I am at is considered a giant dead zone due to the high wireless head set activity. I used to get no signal from AT&T, period. Once I bought this item, I was anxious to try it out since I received the product over a long weekend. Oh my!! this thing gets FIVE BARS!! no kidding. I am rediscovering the iPhone I love in a dead zone. The only negative I can think of is the fact that the phone has to be on the cradle at all times to get signal. This is fine by me as I do not move around with the phone when I am at work. Thank you Wilson !!!!
summary: Rediscover your iPhone in a dead zone!!!

reviewText: It's nice to have something so small and integrated actually work so well. With my offhanded testing I'd say that I averaged 2 extra bars, sometimes more.

This booster brings in a signal in areas that were dead before. It's easy to use, easy to set up, and works. Don't just look at the bars go into your phone and actually see your signal to find the real difference, in weak areas my signal goes from -95db to -45db.

This is my second sleek booster (same bands). My wife and I use them on the Sprint network but I've had other friends try them with iPhones on AT&T and Verizon with the same results. In our case, it doubles our signal which, when on the network edge, can be a lifesaver for both calls and data. It's also a nice holder!

In some locations, this resulted in a slight increase in signal.  The boost isn't huge, but if you're in a place that's just on the edge between usable and not, this might give you what you need.  Installation and use is quite easy.
summary: Small signal improvement, but not huge

reviewText: I bought this as a gift for my brother who lives in a rural area outside of Hilo, HI. Whenever I visited my phone got zero bars. His cell did not get reception either. It is a true dead zone. Even walking around outside did not get any bars. Cell phone usage was impossible on his land. He received this very quickly from Amazon, less than one week to Hawaii! When he called the call was as clear as a land line. No static or delay. He said his phone had full bars. Was expecting some improvement but to have full bars was amazing. I highly recommend this for anyone in rural areas that thought cell phone usage was not possible. It works!

For now I gave it 4 stars, I will change it to a 5 once I get the correct antenna for it. I tried this out using the including mini magnet mount antenna. I got the amazon bundle, which included the wrong antenna, it had a female end that was the same as the sleek device. No questions asked on the return total refund and refund on the shipping too. Thats why I shop a lot on Amazon. I have very few incorrect orders. A+ on the service.  Now the device.  I downloaded a few apps that showed signal strength so I could measure the boost of the signal.  I live on the fringe of 2 antennas, N. Illinois, US cellular.  US Cellular is by far the best for coverage in the northern 3rd of Illinois and all of Iowa. I don't know how it is elsewhere.  The results were o.k. a 1 bar gain, again keep in mind it is the very small mini antenna that was included I expect more when the correct(larger) antenna arrives. The numbers I got were 15 to 25% increase.  It seemed to be more variable meaning it would go up and down a lot and not stay on a consistent level as it does when not using the booster.  I would say if you are in a weak signal area...meaning you do get some signal then you will benefit from this. If you are in a complete dead zone without an antenna within 10 miles then you are not going to get any with this. It boosts whats already there. just wanted to mention that because I read some bad reviews  that pertained to that.  I expect a 50% boost with the other antenna, if I get that I will change to a 5 star.  One other issue is that it uses the bigger micro usb for a plug in, I havent had that type for years. Last few years all of mine use the mini USB. I dont know the ratio of the 2 types of chargers but Id prefer the other type. It just adds another charger to the collection. Well built, I believe I read  made in USA. Always a plus.  The wrong antenna had no number on it to know it was the wrong one until I opened it. Seemed odd there wasnt a model number on it, no wonder the wrong ones are being sent out, There were other reviews of people getting the wrong one. I was extra careful ordering and still got it wrong.

I purchased this item a couple months ago and have to say that I am very pleased with the performance of this product. It does not manically raise my signal to full strength when I have no signal but it does however give me enough signal to use my phone-3G and data in places I could not even send a text prior to using it. If you have no signal it is amazing to see your signal return as you slide your phone into the cradle. I would recommend this product to anyone who has trouble with signal or is tired of dropped calls.

Tested this product as soon as it arrived - not in the car but in home office in basement.  I usually get between 0 and 1 bar, consistantly get 3 to 4 bars with unit on.  Without unit, calls would fade in and out as well as dropping - first call with unit on had no problems.  Just looked, 4 bars as I write this.Only complaint is not fault of product, just technology.  There is mounting hardware and the running of wiring, both of which are cumbersome.  I am sure with time technology will overcome these issues (think Telsa, wireless transmission) but, for now, it is as practical as can be expected while holding costs down.My setup:  Boost Mobile at $40/month (in 4 more months it will be down to $35) for UNLIMITED talk, text and data (yes, data included - they advertise "talk, text and internet" - I called and "internet" means data); paid $49 for new Kyocera Hydro w/ newest Ice Cream Droid and 3G just before Christmas thru Amazon; and $65 for Wilson signal boost unit reviewed here.  4G is very spotty in this area, happy with 3G for now.The Wilson SIngle Unit Signal Boost has my recommondation as a good product.

I was very skeptical about this cell phone Booster. We live practically in the woods and for 10 miles we have never got any reception, so I came across this Booster and decided to give it a try..So glad I did,,,Now instead of zero bar's, I get 2-4 bar's, I could'nt believe my eye's. I really never though anything would work. I do have to keep my phone in the cradle to get reception but it don't matter because I either use blue-tooth or my speaker...I would def highly recommend this booster to any one with a no signal zone....:)
I returned this item because the reception did not improve. I bought it to use at work and it just didn't work for this area at all.

My new office at work has terrible reception.  Constantly dropped calls or the voice drop-outs made communicating impossible.  Ordered this hoping it would solve the problem.  It did.  Double the signal strength in my office.  Now my calls are crystal clear.  I also purchased their 'office adapter kit' which came with a suction cup antenna mount and 110v charger.  Inadvertently ordered the wrong one.  The antenna mount works great, but came with the wrong charger.  No big deal, I have an extra USB charger or use my laptop.  Both work.  If you do order the office kit make sure you order the one with the correct charger.  The cradle itself is easy to use, seems very robust.  I'm very please with this purchase.  Worth every penny.  Way to go Wilson.  Amazon had the best price and free shipping.  Can't beat that.

like me...that uses a Motorola Droid (X2, now)...this is a MUST HAVE for travelling in poor cell coverage areas.I have used this booster in areas that have dropped calls regularly...even in areas when I am right near a VZW tower.I tested this one night...one particular 90 mile stretch of road loses calls in about 6 zones...and can lose those calls for 10 minutes at a stretch.  I made a call...and chose to talk for the entire drive...without a loss of call.  The signal would waver, yes...but across large hills...deep valleys...and areas that normally 'drop'...this booster WORKED.I AM impressed!  Worth every penny!

Anytime I see a product that claims to boost signal of any type of device, I get skeptical.  I have tried various products in the past that never worked...Until now.The Wilson Electronics Cell Phone Signal Cradle is a well designed signal booster that utilizes an external antennae and an external power source to boost cellular signal.  My test phone:  The iPhone 4.What comes in the boxPhone cradle with adaptersDC AdapterExternal magnetic antennaConstructionThe cradle is made of hard plastic and has a padded surface for the phone to rest.  A green indicator light on the lefthand side of the cradle lets you know the cradle is on.  The plastic grips on the side are flexible enough to fit the phone into the cradle easily.  There is an adhesive backing that attaches the cradle to any flat surface of your choosing.  I would have preferred additional backings or mounts for users who move from one location/vehicle to another.  The cradle rotates on a ball and socket joint allowing the user to view the screen in the vertical or horizontal position; this will facilitate the use of the GPS capabilities of the iPhone 4.  The antenna has a magnetic mount that sticks to any metallic surface (preferably the top of the vehicle) and this connects to the cradle with a coaxial cable connection.  The DC adapter plugs into the DC port in your vehicle.The cradle allows the user to plug in their charging cable and the top of the iPhone is unobstructed to allow the phone to "Sleep".UseJust place your phone into the cradle and watch it work.  In just a few seconds, I watched as my "One Bar" 3G signal in a weak coverage area go up to "Four Bars".  That was impressive.  This weak coverage area that I drive through is notorious for dropped cell phone calls.  That could be the difference between getting a Tow Truck or walking a few miles in the dark with an LED flashlight in the middle of the night.  You get my drift?I took the cradle and brought it to work where there are lead walls in my department (Radiology Department) and there is poor signal ("Two Bars" Edge or "One bar" 3G). I took the DC adapter and plugged it into my DC to AC converter.  Again, I went from "One Bar" to "three bars" 3G!  As I moved the antenna from one location to another, I saw that it increased the signal to "Four Bars" 3G!This will surprise you but the sticker says that this is MADE IN THE USA!!!VerdictThis product works!Highly recommend it for the iPhone 4.
summary: This really works!  Boost your cell phone signal...Even for AT&T Service on the iPhone 4

reviewText: I was skeptical. All these glowing reviews? I bought it. It's wonderful! Now, buried in the heart of my big government building in downtown Sacramento, I can keep up on texts, email, and more. I love this product and heartily recommend it.BTW, I'm sort of a tech geek, and a computer programmer for a living. I associate with lots of electronics thingies. This one is outstanding.

Most of us that live in urban areas have become accustomed to the reliable nature of mobile phones.  However, if you asked mobile phone users from the 90's, how their reception was, you would undoubtedly hear how poor most coverage was.  This foul coverage gave birth to a product that forever stained the term, "cell phone signal booster."  Does anyone remember those odd looking stickers you were supposed to apply to your phone that would miraculously enhance your signal?  Yeah, those things.  Didn't work.  Wilson Electronics would have been wise to change the wording of their product to avoid the negative connotations because their products in fact, do work.PROS:- It actually works- Portable- Design works with most phones- Works indoors as well with an additional kitCONS:- Antenna only works when grounded to a metallic surface- Signal is boosted only when phone is sitting in cradleAdmittedly, my CDMA coverage is normally stellar so my use for the Sleek is limited.  However, I do on occasion trek to rural areas for the weekend.  It's a given that the campground or cabin will not receive cellular service so we're stuck with using land line phones.  My Android phone becomes useless for data services as well.In testing the Sleek, I took it to one of the few areas that I know I get spotty coverage in.  In a nutshell, it works.  I would use it all the time in my car except for the fact that I have to have an ugly wired antenna stuck to the top of my car.  It also happens to help inside an office or home via Wilson's home/office kit that basically suction cup's the antenna to a window, mounted on a metal frame.  The only handicap of the Sleek is the fact that it must be used while in the cradle.  This isn't a big deal for me because I have a Bluetooth headset located everywhere in case I want to make a hands-free call.I don't think the average mobile user will go through the trouble, but if you're in need of a device like this, then the Wilson Electronics Sleek is going to make a big difference.  It's reasonably priced, portable, and it just plain works.
summary: Sleek Works, But Will Need a Bluetooth Headset

reviewText: I am using this indoors in my home office.  I had to play with finding the best location for the very end of the antennae but once I did that it definitely works.  I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because it did not boost the signal to a high level in my case.  However, it does make it possible for me to use my phone when I could not before I installed this product.

Don't leave a lot of reviews for products as most are just fine, but this product inspired me to actually write a review. We have fairly poor cellular reception in our apt and this product solved the issues of dropped calls for us. My wife works from home and needs a consistent phone to talk with clients. This product solved the issue without having to buy a home phone line.The device is dead simple to use, simply plug it in and place your phone on it. (If you are using the device at home, the home/office accessory kit is a must). Place the antenna on the window mount kit and you're off to the races. At first we simply used the phone in speaker phone mode, but recently started using a bluetooth headset. Only issue with speakerphone mode is that some phones' speaker phone speaker is on the back and can be muffled. Solved this issue with a rubber band around the unit to hold the bottom part of the phone off the cradle just a bit. Bottom line - no more dropped calls. With a bluetooth headset it solved our issues.

Got this due to poor signal while driving in dead zones, and it does help. The phone needs to remain in the cradle at all times, of course, otherwise you'll lose the signal instantly. Overall, this will typically boost signal by one or two bars, which can make a difference in a call being dropped or not, albeit of a subpar quality. You need the antenna going out of the car window of course, but it's no trouble to do that as long as you don't mind a small antenna on the top of your car. Not pretty or too discreet, but you can't expect it to draw much signal otherwise.You will need a hands free or bluetooth headset to use your phone while it's in the cradle. The setup is easy, and the dock is sturdy. My father uses this with his HTC Evo 4G with a thick case(basically bulkiest cell phone possible), and it fits just fine. Impressive since almost every dock is too small for that phone.I would love to give this a glowing review but you are still limited to how good the signal can be in that area. We have Sprint, so that should say why we don't have a huge boost in signal. I give this 5 stars because of that, since it is not the cradle's fault.This is still worth purchasing and worth the money if you use it often, and much cheaper than other signal boosting options.
summary: Not a miracle worker of course, but it works and does boost signal

reviewText: Bought my first one and it worked for about two weeks. Not sure I messed it up or if it had a defect - but I contacted Wilson Electronics. What a great company! They sent me another one right out and even checked back to make sure I wasn't having any more problems. As for the product - it has been great. A huge increase in available signal when I'm up hunting. Usually the mountain terrain kills my signal, but with this, I was able to talk and go online where before I couldn't even get a signal. This is a must have product for anyone who ever travels in to weak or out of signal areas!

Improved my HTC Hero phone signal 2-3 bars  at home, where I had problems getting any service.  Makes phone awkward to hold and needs to be used hands free.  As I spend the winters RVing in the SW deserts should come in handy.

I have one location in the Ocala National Forest where we go that has almost nonexistent cell phone coverage.  Getting a signal there was always hit of miss.  I bought this booster to see if it would help, and it does.  Whereas I rarely got a signal before, I can now get at least two bars and sometimes three on my iPhone.  It also boosts the signal in areas where I would normally get three bars, but with this device a can get 4-5 bars.The antenna that comes with it has a nice long cord and is easy to mount on the roof of the car with its strong magnetic base.
I have used this item to boost more then one cellphone at a time as long as they are touching the booster. Went from having 1-2 bars to 4-5 inside the house. Great product!!
summary: Great to have cell service again

reviewText: I work in an area with a consistent 0-1 bars on AT&T...this thing gave me 3-5 bars almost all of the time...I do highly recommend this antenna Wilson Electronics Dual Band - 800-1900 MHz Magnet Mount Antenna with SMA Male Connector and 10-Foot RG174 Coax Cable Model 301125. It made a huge difference over the tiny antenna that was included with the Sleek...
Purchased this along with the accessory kit, and can't be happier! No dropped calls and MUCH improved signal. Bet the farm on this cheap investment!
I live by LAX and this device helps reduce the interference I get from the constant air traffic. All of these types of Wilson products are worth every penny.

This item works perfectly.  I purchased the sleek along with two home office kits.  I used a home/office mount to secure the antenna inside my vehicle with velcro.  it works superbly and I don't have an unsightly cable and antenna sticking out of the car. I get complete coverage at home and in the car...I highly recommend this product.  Wilson should offer a all in one kit with the sleek, two home window mounts & antennas and a few pieces of velcro.
Did absolutely nothing to give me better service. Didn't even give me an extra bar. I bought this along with the home kit. I will be returning both.

It works to an extent. There is a slight quality and reception improvement but no visible bar improvement. I do drop calls less often so that's good enough to keep it. The Antenna and home office kit I bought it with is the same situation. I think I just have to admit I live in too much of a dead zone for anything to help.

I own an iPhone, and I think any iPhone user can attest to AT&T;'s spotty at best coverage.  I've owned the iPhone for over a year now, and ever since I've had it I've had to deal with dropped calls, something I never had an issue with when I had Verizon.  While that situation is an entirely different review, I can say that after using this signal booster in a remote area it works extremely well!  I have used this in a few areas outside of town where I know the signal strength is low, and this booster increased from two bars to five bars.  Pretty impressive.  When I made a few calls the quality was strong, and there was no echo or delay which is something that happens with some regularity when I don't use this booster.  Additionally, my text messages sent quickly and painlessly from these remote areas as well.  When I try to text from these outlying areas without the booster the text messages will stall for a minute or two before they send, or in some cases not send at all.My first impression upon using this was annoyance in knowing that cell phone companies are unwilling to go out and build more towers so people wouldn't have to buy things like a signal booster.  Why shouldn't a phone just, well, work?  Obviously, the answer to that is "not really", making this signal booster a strong purchase for those who travel a lot and find themselves in varying levels of cell phone activity.  I cannot attest to this signal booster's performance with other phones, but it has made a huge improvement to my iPhone 3G.

I used this for my blackberry when I am on the go. Since I work close to the beach the service is lousey. Since using the the sell phone boost, I havent had any more problems with dropped calls. The service quality is a whole lot better, compared to what I had before. The set up was very easy. was on my dash in minutes. Used this also on a long drive , and it worked just great.Overall I do not have to switch carriers now love it.

I am very pleasantly surprised with this Sleek. I was getting zero reception in my new apt with multiple carriers and once I got this baby it raised me all the way up to 4-5 bars. I have not tried it in the car but I take a lot of road trips so I will try it soon. The only negative thing is that people were saying it prolonged battery life and I found it uses a lot more actually.Oh and I would not spend the extra money on the AC adapter if you have an ipod(or any other) cord that plugs into the wall with a usb port. I just used  and got an extension cord for more length. Saves $25 from buying the adapter kit.

I cant say enough good about the WilsonSleek signal booster..I bought one for my truckand with the external antenna, I ALWAYS get a good signal and No lost calls! I bought one for the wifes car and she loves it. I showed it to the emergency response team which can get sent to very remote areas, they are  buying some for the response trucks.I also bought the home kit which works just as well.

I've used this, so far, in my home and it works great.  I haven't had it out in the car yet, but going out tomorrow.  I live in hilly terrain and weak coverage areas on most of the country roads I travel.  I know some spots where I lose signal and where signal is so weak the calls break up and I will be traveling some of those tomorrow.  Will report back then as to how well I feel the Sleek performs. It certainly works great in the house.

First I must say, great price for this product. I'm in the Oilfield and have Verizon cell phone service as well as an iPad 2 with 3g and do not get more than 2 to 3 sometimes no bars at a time with either device. With this product I'm able to get five full bars and 3G as I have the iPhone 4S. Certain areas in south Texas are very remote and can get at least 3 bars of "edge" with this wilson sleek booster just incase I got to make a call. Would have been cool with a built in charging dock. Great product though. Also this product does not boost any other devices in the vehicle therefore it's only good for the phone that is in the cradle itself. If you want to boost more than one device such as your iPhone and an iPad or a friends phone then you might need to look into the $200 option of the Wilson electronics MobilePro which is a wireless booster. 5 stars an 2 thumbs up.

After playing around with this in the car for a few weeks, I decided that its a pretty good cell phone booster. It's not perfect, but there is some noticeable boost. I am not sure how many devices like this are out there, but I would recommend this one.Set up is easy. Plug into your car lighter, then plug in the antenna to the cradle and the antenna mounts securely by magnet on the roof of your car. Its a strong magnet so have no fear. When the little light turns green, you are all good. And then you just sit the phone on the cradle and thats it.Initially I went around town locally and it seemed to work ok. Nothing really noticeable. I am using an iPhone 3GS and I know there are "cold spots" where its almost inevitable that your call will get dropped.But then I decided to go into these areas and also further into other areas while using it and it seemed that I was able to get through those areas fairly successfully. Although once it did drop while using it, I noticed some enhancement.I am not sure about the battery life extension. One day I was going downtown into areas I am not familiar and using the GPS service and it I still noticed battery life being used up as normal. By the time I got home it needed charging. This is probably the only thing I noticed not really effective or not noticeable. Overall I do notice a signal boost, even data comes a little smoother.The cons to the device besides the one mentioned is that the cradle arms sticks out a lot so its a little bulky. Also there are 2 wires, but it seems like there are more in my car. I did not attach it to my dashboard because using an iphone in the car is cumbersome and attention needed to it, either to touch or otherwise. So its really not an optimal car device. Perhaps other phones work better with this phone and maybe in other areas it might work more effectively, but this was my experience. I like it and will continue to use it in my car for certain things, but I wont make it a permanent fixture. It should be noted that I dont use a blue tooth so you have an idea of what kind of set up I had.

I've used the Wilson Sleek cell booster for about three years now and it has exceeded my expectations. It can't make something out of nothing, but if you have a marginal cell signal it will make it usable to strong. I can't say enough good things about the performance of this product and Wilson Electronics' support. If you have reasonable expectations this booster will exceed them.
summary: This booster's been very, very good to me!

reviewText: I work in rural areas and it allows me to comple my loop which had no service to where now I have a minimum of 2 bars

I bought thus to working areas that I travel through where I would lose cell reception  I still lose cell reception I am disappointed  I have also tried moving the antenna to different areas on my roof  Any suggestions are highly appreciated
summary: I'M still trying to get good reception

reviewText: I got this booster and I set it up. I thought that it wouldn't work very well. Boy was I wrong. The bars on my phone were very low in my house. I got the power booster and I have a steady 3 bars anywhere in the house.

I was a bit worried since the description of the product was more for cars, but I used this at home.I get excellent signal. I was getting 2 bars and dropped calls in my room and now I don't have anymore. the only problem for me is that since I had a G1 it was a bit bulky to use the phone and you need to get a headset.The setup was easy and packaging was well done.

Like the title says, I wish I would have gotten the 4G model.However, this one is cheaper, and it covers the 2G bands that T-Mobile uses in my area. For that, it works GREAT.  While I am using this, I don't drop voice calls in the dead zone of my house anymore.I use this whenever I have to make a super important phone call.I just plug this in, set my phone on it, and turn speakerphone on; and BAM.No more having to call the cable company back and wait for another 45 minutes.

I am quite familiar with Wilson going back to my Amateur Radio days and advancing my communication skills thru the years. This was purchased as a whole house cell solution in one of several attempts. It is expected this is a great mobile product, but didn't help my home stationary needs. I had tried a number of systems and currently have a whole house solutions which I am quite happy with from Wilson, it's just not this one. If you are looking for a whole house solution, I would recommend calling the manufacturer and getting one specific to your needs rather than adapting a mobile solution.

I have an LG  Tracfone and live in a "dead" area and was hoping the Wilson Sleek Universal Cell Phone Signal Booster would solve that problem. I set it up in my car according to directions with the magnetic antenna on a metal surface on my car's roof (at least six inches or more away from the moonroof).  My Tracfone is small, so I exchanged the attached Sleek arms for smaller ones (three sets of varying sizes come with the unit), then plugged in the coaxial antenna cable and finally the DC power cord.  The green light came on as soon as I started the car's engine, but I still got a "service unavailable" message.  Moving up the driveway, I continued to receive this message until I came out to the cross street where the signal is strong enough to use a cell phone.  That is where my phone began to work.  Driving along the mountain ridge and down into the valley to the nearest town, service is spotty.  With the Sleek set-up and the phone in its cradle, operation was exactly the same as it is without the signal booster, so my experience was that the Sleek made no difference in cell phone signal strength.Apparently this is not the case for most users.  I was disappointed that it didn't work for me.I thought the hard plastic cell phone cradle was well designed and the antenna magnet powerful so not problem with it not staying attached. My car, a Volvo 850, does not have a spot suitable for mounting (an adhesive backing attaches the cradle to any flat surface), however this didn't affect my usage for review purposes.The Wilson Sleek Universal Cell Phone Signal Booster is USA made, a big plus for this reviewer.  I only wish my experience with this unit had been more positive.
summary: Did not work in my area.

reviewText: I bought this to use at home since my reception is shaky. I gave it an honest try for a few days and it just did not work. It didn't do anything.

I found a cheaper solution. For me it was free since I already had 2 of them... an HDTV antenna!! I had one out because the cable went out and I wanted to watch local over the air HD. The cable guy came and fixed the dish, and then I got an idea.We had been having problems with our cell phones. I looked on Amazon and other sites for boosters and it looked like I'd have to spend at least $70 to get something that would only give me 2 more bars. I wondered if I set the phone in the middle of the HDTV antenna, what would it do?I'll tel you... I got from an "iffy" 2 bars to a full 4!! I always use a bluetooth headset, so it doesn't matter that I can't carry the phone around. In fact, it even improved my bluetooth connection so I can go more than 10 feet from the phone without it getting crackly.The best antenna so far is one I got on sale at Radio Shack for $15. It is triangular with a big opening in the middle. My MyTouch 4G fits in the circular opening perfectly. Now I just need to find a way to fasten it so it can't fall out if someone bumps the antenna.

This case is great quality, fits the phone perfectly and I truly had no complaints. The pink color is nice and vibrant, but not a neon pink- in your face type, its just right. My phone has fallen so many times and I have never had an added scratch thanks to this case!

I got this phone case after i dropped my phone a couple times, this phone case works great just like most otterboxes and it protects ok, if you want a great protecting case i would go with the otterbox defender not the commuter. This case is nice fits well and is easy to get on and off.
Great protection. Grip is good & does not make the phone too bulky. This color scheme was great for my daughter.

had a short after 2 months....but unlike the other cheapo extenders, this actually lasted 2 months !! so it wasnt too bad.
