I needed a smaller jack to fit in to the case opening.This adapter fit the bill.  I bough a cheaper adapter, but that one cut out and provided poor sound quality.  This device works very well.  The sound quality is not negatively effected at all.It is slightly more expensive than other similar units.  But the nominal amount is worth it by the aggravation that you save.
Not worth it. Worked for 2 uses and then only works in one earphone only.  Save your money and don't buy.  I'm not sure why Mophie just doesn't sell replacements for their units.
summary: Two uses, and it stopped workign in both ears

reviewText: This is great to have - not just for apple products, but for any product that doesn't have much room for the headphone jack plug in.  My android phone has a case that makes this come in handy.

The theory - A+: It seems contradictory to trade in the cellphone for a regular phone, but that's the latest trend. It turns out that there might be something to all those fears of brain tumors and deafness while using the cellphone that close to our heads.Thus, products are springing up that bring back the handsets of old but use the Bluetooth technology to integrate with the cellphones. And if they look and function as well asNative Union MM03 Moshi Moshi Curve Handset and Weighted Base for iPhone, Blackberry and all mobile Bluetooth devices (High-Gloss Black)-- it's a very good thing.Appearance - A+: Moshi Moshi Curve Handset is stylish, sleek, and ergonomic. It looks perfect in any modern-designed home. The black is really shiny and thus looks great against any glass or wooden surface.Set-up - A+: It is easy to set up - follow the instructions in the manual and it will take you less than 5 minutes. Please note that any cellphone that has Bluetooth can be set up to use this handset. I have the Palm Treo III - a dinosaur by any cellphone technology standards - and I was able to set it up with this handset in under 5 minutes.Usability - A-: The process could be a bit more seamless if no additional buttons needed to be pressed between the switch between the cellphone and the handheld device. What I mean by that is that to dial out, press the phone number on your cellphone and wait for the other person to pick up and then switch to the Moshi Moshi. When you receive calls on the device, you have to inconveniently grab the handset and press the button in the middle. It's similar to how one used to pick up a phone handset but different from a rotary/regular phone which doesn't require the pressing of the "on" button.Reception - A++: Being one of the people who has gotten rid of the landline over five years ago, I have forgotten what phone calls should sound like. I'm so used to the cellphone reception static that I didn't even realize how bad it was until I used the Moshi Moshi Curve Handset. The sound is so much clearer both for me hearing others (even if the person I am speaking with is on a cellphone) and for the person on the receiving end of the line. The downside, of course, is that you are still required to use the cellphone when you are not at home.Range - A: The Moshi Moshi handheld only gets reception in a 10-meter radius. This means that you have to carry your cellphone with you if you have a large house and/or are going outside into the yard, onto the deck, etc. and the Moshi Moshi is deep inside the house. Generally, the 10-meter radius was enough to go onto another floor without having to carry the cellphone with me.Overall - A: This might not be the necessity of the year, but it's a fun, useful device that will come in handy (pun intended).
summary: handsets are back and sexier than ever

reviewText: Like many people, I long ago got rid of my land-line phone. After all, I already pay for unlimited calls on my cellphone, why pay twice? But if you are like me, you've probably noticed that there is a trade off. Cellphones just are not comfortable to talk on for long periods of time. I love my Android, and my friend loves her iPhone, but both of us agree that a classic-type handset is much more comfortable to talk on while sitting at my desk. (And no, I do NOT want to look like a member of the Borg 24/7 with an earpiece on.)I was very happy to find the Moshi Moshi Curve (MM03) handset. I had a similar product that I was very happy with, but it required a wire from the handset to my phone. The MM03 is wireless! Gotta love Bluetooth! As an added plus, when I'm not around my husband can use the MM03 because it can be connected to 2 Bluetooth devices!Speaking of cords (ie range) I was able to go about 20 feet away from my cellphone with no problems. I have a lot of walls and electronics in my house, so you might be able to get more if you have a clear line of sight from the handset to your phone.One of the main points for using this device was the "Radiation Reduction". I'm not a big believer that cellphone radiation is a problem, but why take chances? I wouldn't say to buy this gadget for just the Radiation Reduction feature, but hey, if you're going to buy it anyway, it's a nice bonus.Overall I'd say this is a great product. I'm not going to go carrying it around when I'm out of the office, but it is definitely nice change from holding blocky smartphone against my face.

The Moshi handset feels very well made, and comes in impressive packaging that one might more expect from an Apple product.One oddity is that the handset and base are almost perfectly symmetrical, and the points on the base that mate with the charging connectors are on the opposite end from where I expected then to be, resulting in the base and handset being set up upside down to begin with.Its setup and pairing process seem to work reliably with all the devices I tried, and while I don't consider the device perfect, it works as advertised, feels completely solid and manufactured to the highest quality standards, and it actually works (a plus for and Bluetooth device).If you're looking at this device and think it looks like it might be something you would like and use, then you're probably correct and should give it a try without worry.G.
summary: Works well, an interesting option for mobile devices

reviewText: MoshiMoshi solves a niche, pairing and answering calls on two different Bluetooth devices or a phone and a Bluetooth-enabled device (e.g. a laptop used for VoIP).What's good:* Easy to set-up; plug it in to charge and push a few buttons to sync it up.* Sound quality is consistent across different devices (e.g. iPhone).* Volume controls are easy to use.What's could be better:* Cell phones have a noticeable delay but the MoshiMoshi extends the delay to an annoying level.In summary, the main issue with the MoshiMoshi device is that it solves a niche problem. Unless you regularly juggle two or more smart phones and Bluetooth-enabled devices there is no need for the MoshiMoshi.The MoshiMoshi is handy If you frequently make VoIP calls and carry a smart phone (e.g. a home-based business); this wireless handset's value increases with the more phones you own and the more calls you receive.Rating: Four stars.
summary: Wireless handset's value increases vis-à-vis the number of devices you own

reviewText: Everyone raves about this thing, but the few times I've tried it, it was full of static and the person on the other end complained about hearing me. Not happy.

I have to admit that my first thought on seeing the Moshu Moshi was that it was another silly accessory for cell phones, like those old-style telephone handsets that plug into your cell phone. But it turns out that it's useful, too. Once it's properly configured, all you need to do is pick up the handset when your cell phone rings, and you're connected. And unlike the typical cell phone, you can hold this handset on your shoulder while you reach for a pen or type at your keyboard.Even more useful (for me) is the ability to connect it to your computer as a VOIP handset for use with Skype. Normally I use a microphone that sits on my desk for VOIP calls, but with the Moshi Moshi I can wander around the room or sit in a comfy chair away from the computer. Much nicer. The ability to configure it for two different devices is a big plus. (I have yet to see how it handles a cell call coming it while I'm on Skype. but I 'm guessing there's a way to switch back and forth.) Sound quality is good, and the microphone does apear to do a decent job of keeping out extraneous sounds.Downsides? Just one so far. As another reviewer remarked, the symmetrical design makes it impossible to tell which end is which without flipping it over and looking at the underside of the handset. But that's about the only problem I've seen. All in all a nice design and a convenient gadget for the tech-savvy user.

This French designed "Soft Touch" black MM03i handset and base are quietly stylish. The material feels like the skin on a stealth fighter--soft, invitingly tactile, non-slippery; and the curvy design is easy and comfortable for even a  young child to handle. I might expect hand oils to muss the finish over time, but not as yet. Instructions say to clean with a dry cloth. I like its feel in my hand and on my ear.  It does two major things. If your cell phone is Bluetooth, you can speak more comfortably with this handset than holding the cell. Second, if you have iPhone, it is a docking station that accepts external speakers if you put music on your phone.  The packaging is a nice Lucite case, which bears mentioning.The box contains:*Bluetooth wireless handset and base* Multi-country AC adaptor kit with 4 international plugs for the United States and Canada, Europe, UK, Asia and Australia.* Micro-USB /USB Cable to plug into your ' Apple computer to charge as other Apple devises, and to sync to your computer.*Two universal dock adaptors for iPhone 3GS and iPhone 4.* Instruction Manual; English is in the first 21 pages.The inside of the handset contains the single + and - control volume with the central control button nestled between; the central control performs all allowable functions.  There is no numeric dial pad, dialing is done normally through your cell phone.The inside design suits me; the universal radio/audio wave signal for the earpiece, and sound capture symbol of  ' concentric circles for microphone minimizes confusion on how to orient the hand piece (Regrettably Amazon will not allow my embedded symbols here to illustrate).  Even in the dark, I can feel and orient the sleek pair of charging contacts downward toward my mouth. The weight is comfortable and balanced; not so flimsy as to fall carelessly. The handset fits snuggly in the base with no play. When placed properly in the base a soft white light illuminates until the handset is again fully charged. You get aural and visual confirmation of connectivity and set on and off.FEATURES PROS/CONS:* The MM03i Bluetooth Wireless Handset & Base is made for the iPhone. Yes, you can use it with other Bluetooth wireless technology cell phones, such as our BlackBerry, which paired easily. But the base dock plug design fits only Apple's iPhone.* I like that I can pair the MM03i with a total of 4 phones--I can clear paired devises as needed. And although only two Bluetooth devises can be connected to the MM03i at the same time, you cannot take calls from 2 phones simultaneously. If you receive a call on a second phone while on the first, you will need to juggle by placing the first on hold to answer the second. This gets confusing because pressing on the central control once ends the call, while double pressing puts it on hold. To preserve cell battery life, turn Bluetooth off from the handset after your call.*  It is convenient for me to leave my non-iPhone charging within a yard of the base and walk away with the handset receiver. I just remind myself that the base is not a real landline phone. It's not going to ring loudly. I dial new numbers out from the cell phone. As the manual says, the handset gives me limited functionality to:o Reject incoming callso Control volume during callso Redial the last number calledo End the active call and accept call waitingo Hold active call and accept waiting callo Access "voice activated" dialing on devises that support this featureo Muteo Clear paired device listo Choose from 15 ringtoneso Automatically reconnect to the last 2 connected devises in memoryo Answer up to 2 phones with the headset (remember, if the second phone rings while on the first we're back to juggling).To save you "agita", be sure to read the instruction booklet before beginning. I freely admit MAJoR agita from NO phone support (minus a Star for customer aversion and some portion of a star for the little annoyances before mentioned); be aware that NativeUnion website directs customers to email, connect to Facebook and Twitter for service. The customer service/ community support section on the company website lists user problems and answers. Problems listed when I visited were: the unit switching off, VOIP not working and how to take an incoming call from the mobile phone rather than the MM03. All problems that I have not yet had but when I do, I'll be updating...For now, this is my best solution for using a cell phone at home with my VOIP or in an office environment where I don't want the cell static and lack of clarity. I get good range for my needs.  Admittedly, I expect to have the Bluetooth connectivity issue but then I know it's Bluetooth and not my phone or the receiver. Until something better comes along--this suits and it's PReTtY. I like and need pretty in my life.
summary: Call me Superficial, but Call me Please

reviewText: Wow!  I don't really think iPhone docks are really nice in general, but here's one you definitely need to take a look at.  The Native Union Limited Edition Curve is a great product.The form factor of the handset is a smooth curve that fits your face.  Likewise, it has a velvety touch that makes the handset enjoyable to hold.  It is evenly weighted so it balances in your hand and is relatively lightweight.  The base is about a foot long, so you will need some space on your end-table or desk.  However, you can mount the base on the wall with some clever engineering.  The iPhone (and the iPod v4) are held in the dock securely by the mount/charging coupling.The iPhone/iPod is connected through Bluetooth.  The headset can connect up to two different devices, although I'm not sure you really want to try it.  A soft muted white led in the headset flashes to let you know it's connected to your iDevice.The dock is supposed to be used as a charger/phone while you're at home.  One issue using it with the iPod is that although Bluetooth does connect, it cannot be used with a phone-type app.  Google voice (although it gives the iPod phone calling capability) does not work with the Curve.The Native Union Limited Edition Curve is a beautiful addition to your home in design and appearance.  It works well with your iPhone (and as a charger for your iPod too).  I wasn't able to test it with a Blackberry, but since this particular dock was for the iPhone, I assume the connector does not work with the Blackberry.  I highly recommend the Curve.
summary: Native Union designed a great iPhone dock!

reviewText: The Native Union MM031 Curve Wireless Bluetooth Telephone for the iPhone is a pretty neat product I have to admit. I was somewhat concerned after reading some of the negative reviews but I can honestly say connectivity and clarity have not been a problem at all for me. I am using it with my iPhone 4S. First thing I should mention that is packed and presently nicely in a very thick plastic box. The instruction book is extremely thick, but it comes in 10 different languages and the actual instructions to follow are only about 20 pages and that includes pictures. Comes with 4 types of multi country AC adapters in case you travel to foreign countries that use different type of voltage plugs. Two universal dock adapters and a Micro-USB/USB cable if you wish to charge the unit via your computer.The base has some weight to it and will sit securely in place. I got the soft Black Touch which is like a soft rubber and it feels soft and silky smooth and can easily be wiped cleaned. It stated in the handbook that it takes about 2 to 3 hours to charge the unit 100%, but it took about 1  until the white LED turned off telling me the handset was completely charged. Paring was a breeze - just press the MFB button for 2 seconds on the handset and go to your bluetooth menu on your iPhone. My iPhone found it and paired with the MM03i automatically with no code. You actually can program up to 4 Bluetooth devices according to the instructions, but it will only automatically reconnect the last devices connected in its memory.I use a case with my iPhone and do not like the idea of removing it. My phone fit perfectly fine in it's case and I had no connection issues if I used the base without a dock adapter. Using the "+" , "-" and "MFB" buttons pretty much allow you to use all the functions as you would on your iPhone. You can reject a call, control the volume, hold a call, redial last number call and even use voice command. I use Siri a lot and all you have to do is hold the "+" button for two sections and she will pop up and await your instruction.You also can choose a different ringtone. There are a total of 15 in all. Since I am using the handset in office, I set the volume at the lowest possible setting because some of the ringtones can ring quite loudly. In regards to clarity, I have had no complaints. Callers have heard me clearly and I have heard them fine. The handset feels comfortably against my ear and there is no hand or ear fatigue.I would like to mention that in the instructions it states the MM03i enables Bluetooth connection with any laptop, desktop (Mac or PC) to work with Skype, Google Talk or other VOIP services. I don't have Bluetooth Wireless Technology on my PC, but I thought it might be important to mention.The only negative feature is that it is hard to tell the difference between the receiver and earpiece, the both look identical. I would try to answer a call holding the wrong end to my ear. Sometimes instead of thinking the unit is charging I come to found out I put the wrong end where it is suppose to charge. Even though is will not sit perfectly flush when the right end is not in the right hole, it would have been nice to have some kind of marking showing the top of the handset.Overall this is a really neat product for Smartphone users. It is has the benefits of ergonomics and comfort-ability of old school phones but introduces Bluetooth Technology into the mix. Also makes a unique gift if you know someone who loves to gab!

Have been enjoying Native Union wired hand set for cell phones and now they move on to Bluetooth connection version also.VERY stylish as you come to expect from this company, designed for use with the new iPhones, but will pair with ANY Bluetooth device you have, and is backward compatible to version 1.1What functions you get to use with the Moshi Moshi 03i depends on your phone.Hand set and base looks good on the desk, might take a bit of time to get used to the feel of the shape when up to your ear though.  Nothing bad, just a bit different feel at first BUT is much better than holding your little cell phone up to your ear.  Plus if you are worried about microwave danger to your head, units like this will cut that down to almost nilListening/speaker end is opposite end from the charge pins and toward the cord end of the base...  hand piece design lets you have it upside down without knowing it, both ends look the same from the back.  Will also allow you to place it in the base wrong way around so you'll get no charge if not careful.AC adapter comes with a novel "insert" way to use any of the plug adapters that let it use whatever AC power plugs you have in any country, comes with all of them in the box and has a long six foot cord.Thought it was not charging at first, but note a change in the hardware that makes the instruction book wrong about where you will see the white LED blinking when it is on charge, the LED is on the back of the hand set and not on the base as it says it is.  Nice touch that the LED is under the plastic so you don't feel it in your hand.Paired with my phone very quickly first try and without any need to read past the quick reference card.  The 03i will memorize up to 4 paired devices and can connect with two at a time if needed.Don't let the thickness of the owners book scare you...  it repeats languages every 20 pages so there isn't that much you need to read to see all the features of the unit.Sound is pretty good, could use a bit more volume on max setting, but can hear and be heard just like a wired phone for the most part.Range seems to be the same as most Bluetooth items and the hand set will cut off when out of range and reconnect when back in.  Wish they could get more range with the better sound these days.3.5mm plug in the base lets you use external speakers to use your iPhone as MP3 player when it's plugged in to the base.The 03i will pair with Bluetooth on a PC for talking on Skype or whatever software/service you use for Internet phone calls if your PC/Notebook is equipped for BlueTooth.Also comes with 34 inch long USB cord to synchronize the iPhone with your computer but booklet states this will NOT charge you Moshi Moshi or iPhone.
summary: Native Union has done it again... nice design that works

reviewText: The whole shebang is a rather handy setup to have around. I feel like the sound quality on a headset is shaky, at best. I'm used to using a regular phone, however, and like the fact that the handset on the device weighs very little, and facilitates long conversations. I called my mother the other night, and we spoke for about 5 hours straight. No battery interruptions, no dropped calls, no nothing. I tend to wander around while talking on the phone. Unfortunately, it means that the iPhone will frequently drop calls when I walk into a cellular deadzone in my apartment. With this device, I'm able to rest the phone in one spot that I know works, and trust in bluetooth to sort me out.The dock on the base does not function to connect the phone with the handset. Instead, it's there as a courtesy, so that you can keep your phone charged while using the handset. The ring is plenty loud for me to hear across the apartment, with no problem. Setup was a snap. It took a scant few moments for the phone and base to find each other and sync right up.I'm surprised that nobody has come up with something like this before!The packaging includes plug adaptors for pretty much every country. It's also got a regular micro USB charger, and a micro USB cable to hook up the base to your computer for charging if you wish. It's got an adaptor to make it possible for the older style of iPhone to fit into the cradle. The manual is written in 10 languages. This is truly meant to be an international product.

At first this may seem like an excessively expensive iphone holder. But it really isn't. If you talk on your phone at a desk this device effectively turns your iphone into a desk phone--- in a good way. It charges while docked. The handset is very comfortable. In fact it is so comfortable I sometimes bring it home with me. With a full charge, the handset also charges on the base, it will last for many hours of talking. The bluetooth range is as good or better than a regular bluetooth headset. the sound quality, however, is far and away better than any bluetooth headset I've ever heard including, every product jawbone has ever made.highly recommend .

This Moshi Moshi phone is a pretty interesting device.Let's start with the pros:* Setup was ridiculously easy. Just connect your iPhone, press a button, accept the bluetooth signal on your phone, and it's ready to go. I had never set up bluetooth on my phone before this and yet the entire process took me less than 60 seconds.* The ability to place the base where your phone gets good reception is wonderful. I live in the hills and my cell signal is sketchy at best. With the phone seated in the base, the phone continues to get reception as I move around in my office chair or even as I walk throughout the house. Before the Moshi, any movement at all would have killed the signal so I would always have to sit perfectly still while talking. (Even then the calls would drop!)* The unit is pretty sexy looking and blends well with my other black office equipment.* The base weighted so it's heavy, which give the unit a substantial feel.* Two phones can be paired with it, so you and your significant other can both utilize it.* The handset is very comfortable compared to other home handsets. Compared to talking on an iPhone, it is exponentially more comfortable.* The unit also comes with various international plugs that work with the power-pack when you travel abroad.Cons:* The handset is (almost) perfectly symmetrical. This looks good, but when returning it to the receiver, I could see someone putting it on backwards, which would mean that it wouldn't get a charge. I have not had this happen myself, so perhaps it won't be an issue.Conclusion:Overall, I think this is a great device. It is probably a tad pricey for what it is, but it works well and it's stylish. If you'd like to use your cell phone as a home phone, this is definitely a great route to take.

Update:  After only having this device a couple of months, it all of a sudden became a very cool looking BRICK.  Nothing charges -- the handset does not charge, the iPhone while docked does not charge... it is dead as the proverbial doornail.  Unfortunately, it will wind up in a landfill and therefore WORSE than the doornail since it will take up much more space not to mention the potential toxicity of the internal piece parts of the unit.------------------Bang & Olufsen have long been known for the elegant design and exceptional function.  This has generally come at a significant cost premium.This handset is for anyone who has admired the B&O; aesthetic but didn't necessarily want to plunk down the amount of money on electronics that become obsolete at the speed of light.This handset works GREAT.  It pairs easily to my phone whether the phone is sitting in or out of the dock.  It looks slick as can be.  And the sound quality is excellent.  I prefer using this type of "retro" (yet futuristic looking) handset because I hate the sense of talking to a deck of cards.  I also love that it keeps my iPhone charged during the day at work without requiring yet another proprietary apple cable (this uses a standard micro-usb power cord).When my family was visiting this past month (all apple fiends) this was THE one gadget that all wound up rushing to purchase for themselves.  Docking states -- lot so f them out there.  But one that actually makes an iPhone into a "real" phone -- that is a great and rare find and should be on every apple's "must have" list of accessories.[NCJVR}
summary: BEWARE: does not last -- very cool looking BRICK!!

reviewText: It looks great, and is easy to use - press a button and it pair with up to two phones while one of them charges in the dock. Automatically detects the presence of those phones.The six-foot power cord system is designed to work in any country, via a clever design.It feels good, and those worried about brain tumors will appreciate not having to hold their iPhone to their heads. Assuming BlueTooth is safer, that is. You'll have to check you're holding the phone correctly, as it's almost symmetrical design makes it easy to confuse the two ends. Ditto for replacing it on the charger. Perhaps you can handle that by noting which end should be near the iPhone.Great sound and stylish design, with the above caveats.

The idea of having a more ergonomic and filled out phone for home or office use is fantastic. I've used a native union plug-in phone for years and I absolutely love the form factor and clarity of the conversation. The wireless & docking version however is just a bit shy of the seamless integration required for frustration free usage. The biggest drawback is that the docking connector doesn't work with the iPhone 5 and while adapters might help force the issue, it loses its ergonomic feel. This isn't Native unions fault (although perhaps they could have a more elegant interchangeable charging tip) but it's something to consider if you expect to move from the 4 to the 5 in the near future. The other main drawback is that Bluetooth for me (regardless of any handset maker) has produced mixed results and maintains a fair share of connectivity flaps.I would recommend this insteadNative Union Authentic MM05T-GRY-ST Travel Handset - Retail Packaging - Black with Grey Cord

I was initially very excited about the Moshi Moshi Curve Handset because we only have cell phones in our home and as such, sometimes we miss calls when our phones are not physically on us, such as when they are being charged. I was under the impression that I could leave this handset in the kitchen, for example, and be able to hear a loud ring from across the house as you would with a traditional phone, all using my iPhone. While the handset does indeed ring, it is not anymore audible than the iPhone ringer itself and so this did not fulfill my needs at all.Aside from that, the unit really is very simple to use and functions very well. It looks nice, it feels very durable and seems to be made of high quality materials. The handset rings when you're getting a call on your iPhone (or any phone that has bluetooth capability) and picking it up will answer the call, just like a traditional phone. You can also opt to not use the base, in which case you would push the multi-function button to answer or hang up. This is all very unique and novel at first, until you realize that you just paid a good chunk of change to have a wireless bluetooth receiver that isn't hands free. Then you have to ask yourself, why do I not just hold my actual phone in my hand at this point? Sure, it may be charging in another room and this essentially gives you the ability to use your cell phone from anywhere in your home while it's still plugged in, but there are much MUCH cheaper options for bluetooth devices that perform this same exact function just as well and with hands free to boot.Again, I really do like the novelty of the handset and I won't deny that it works very well, but I quickly got bored with the idea of it and went back to using the Samsung bluetooth headset I paid 15 bucks for. If you are just looking for something different and unique and you don't mind the price tag, this is it. If you are looking for a simple hands free bluetooth device that allows you to communicate via your cell phone while it's plugged in elsewhere in the house, this is probably not the right buy for you.

I received this unit as a demo to try it out and write a review. I wanted to first talk about the "blinking lights" since the only other reviewer that has a review for this product gave the device 1 star because of the lights.The blinking lights are NOT that bad. The lights are built into the base and handset and you can not see them when they aren't blinking. When they do blink it is obvious but it's not obnoxious. You could easily put a piece of white or black electrical tape over the part where the lights are to cover them, but personally I like the lights as they indicate1. If the unit is charging.2. If the unit is powered on.3. If the unit is paired to a device.Lights on this thing are cosmetic and should not mean it goes from a 5 star product to a 1 star because of them.As for functionality goes, it works. I paired this phone to a number of devices quickly and easily to see what did and didn't work. I tried a Blackberry Bold, LG Optimus V (Virgin Mobile prepaid Android Phone), and my laptop. All of these devices worked great and pairing was as easy as could be. Literally less then 10 seconds from start to finish.The only device I couldn't pair this device with was my iPad which I'm a little disappointed about. I use Skype on my iPad so this would have been a perfect handset to use. I can't even get the MoshiMoshi 3 to show up as a device when doing the "blue tooth search."  If anyone knows how to do this let me know!!Now for call quality, I made 2 calls, one from my blackberry to my work phone and left myself a voicemail. The call was clear just like if I was on the blackberry directly or using a landline. The second call I made was through my mac using Skype. The call had a lot to be desired. It had a lot of background static and noise BUT that could have been a a glitch with skype. I did test my network bandwidth and I had 15mb going up and 2 mb coming down in terms of speed so that should NOT have been an issue. I'll retest the skype piece later today and update this review if needed.Overall the phone feels well built. It comes packaged very nicely and would make an excellent gift for anyone with an iPhone but as I said I used it with my LG Optimus and Blackberry Bold, I just couldn't take advantage of the iPhone dock.The phone itself has volume buttons and a disconnect button so you can answer or hang up a call and adjust the volume as needed. I did find the volume was a tad weak for me when using it on my Mac with Skype but on the Blackberry and Optimus V it was just right.The only real complaint I have is the phone is shaped the same on both ends. I found myself putting the receiver on backwards when ending a call and the phone won't charge that direction.And the fact it doesn't work with my iPad so far is a disappointment, but I won't take any stars away from it for that since it doesn't claim it works with the iPad. I'm still going to try to get it to pair up, but so far no luck.
summary: So far so good, but does it work with iPad?

reviewerName: Joel Avrunin "Electrical Engineer who loves S...
reviewText: I received the Moshi Moshi to use with my iPhone 4 and also Microsoft Lync Communicator on my laptop.  While I do have an earpiece for my headset, it is often nice to have a real handset, and I was hoping it might sound better than my earpiece.The device exudes a feeling of quality with a weighted base, smooth glossy finish, and a well weighted handset.  I plugged it into the wall, charged the headset, and got some reassuring beeps letting me know the phone was turning on.  It paired easily with both my Apple iPhone 4 and my Dell Laptop so I could use it on both.  I called a coworker and he commented that I sounded clearer than I ever sound when on my cell phone, confirming for me that the quality of the audio is superior to both my iPhone by itself and my Plantronics earpiece.Regarding the blinking LED, I don't know why the other reviewers focused so much on it.  It is hardly noticeable in my office, but I imagine that on a nightstand it could be annoying.  Why would you put this on a nightstand?So why not 5 stars?  They make a Moshi-Moshi without a dock for the iPhone, and that is likely all you need.  They did do a nice job of including 2 different iPhone dock plastic inserts so that it will work with different phones snugly, it did not help me because my iPhone case is too thick to accomodate the connector.  I considered if it was worth changing cases to support the Moshi Moshi, but the manual clearly states that if you hook up the Moshi Moshi base to your computer, it will use the connector for synchronization only.  It cannot charge your iPhone or your handset through USB from your PC.  They should have added a 2nd USB connector to enable charging while the iPhone synchronized.  If both the iPhone and the handset can die while hooked up to a PC for sync, then I am still stuck swapping cables and it is not a complete solution.As a result, I still use my iPhone OEM cable for sync/charge, and I use the Moshi Moshi as a handset only, ignoring the iPhone connector.I rate it 5 for a bluetooth handset and 2 for iPhone integration due to the sync/charging issue.  Total rating is 4 stars.... I would recommend you get the version without the connector for the iPhone.
summary: Excellent telephone implementation but iPhone support is not stellar

reviewText: This is an attractive fun bluetooth handset.  Very comfortable and easy to use.  And it looks really slick.  It impresses anyone who sees it.The issue is they don't yet make one for the lightning pin connection.  I have the adapter and it works OK, but it significantly reduces the cool factor.  The sound quality is first rate.

I had first come across Native Union'sMoshi Retro POP Handset for iPhone, iPad, iPod, and Android Phones - Soft Touch - Black, and thought it looked like an intriguing idea... but not for me. But this more "traditional phone" designed to hold an iPhone looked perfect.Once I managed to break into the packaging (plan a good ten minutes for this), I found two iPhone adapters, and a set of international power adapters for the plug. The base is heavy, sleek, and rubberized.  The handset is so sleek, it took me two glances to figure out which end was the earpiece. The manual is just as minimalist as the design - figuring out the phone base and the correct plug up to the user.I don't like to use the phone for long conversations without using an earpiece (not because of cancer worries, but because it feels more comfortable), so I was willing to give this handset a try. The Bluetooth paired flawlessly with my phone.The iPhone 4S fits without either of the base plates (it has a very thin case), and charges while in the base. The base rings when calls come in, and call quality is reasonably good.  Charge time on the handset is excellent, and the range is good in the first floor of my home. I think the handset would be improved a bit of thickness or a curve that would allow the handset to rest on the shoulder - at least for a moment. The buttons could also be repositioned for a more ergonomic thumb use.Since my iPhone is my only long distance service, I tend to use it for long family conversations. My aging parents, who generally have plenty of complaints about the audio quality of my calls (they are so sweet, but it is never their hearing, it is always a "bad line"), have had no trouble hearing me over the Curve's handset. On my end, voices sound a bit muted, but I can hear even the smallest background sounds.There weren't any included directions for using Siri, but I found that by holding down the '+' for 2 seconds brought up the double-ding, and Siri's voice at the ready. This means you can also use the handset for any other Siri tasks; very convenient if you are using the handset away from the base.Overall, definitely earns the desktop space, even if it comes at a premium price.
summary: Great idea, needs a few tweaks

reviewText: My lady is a huge Apple fan with all the latest in Apple gadgets including the iPhone4 so, when I had the opportunity to review the Native Union iPhone headset, I gave it a chance by letting her try it out... and it didn't get much further than that.She plugged it in the wall outlet, quickly and easily synced up the Bluetooth from her phone and I gave her a call.  She picked up the headset and, after my customary greeting to the love of my life consisting of some suggestive phrases I shall not repeat here, she quickly requested I say it louder.  After repeating aforementioned suggestive greetings two more times it quickly lost its effect and she went right back to using her phone.We tried reading the manual and checking online to see if others had this problem to discover that many others have and can not figure out how to fix it.  This is the worst possible problem as, without the volume, what's the point.It was a great idea to have a sleek-looking Bluetooth headset for the house instead of lugging the phone around, but that noise issue really turned us off and, after trying to troubleshoot it for an hour, hasn't really seen any usage since.  If Native Union can come up with a better version with quality sound, I'd gladly consider getting it as I love the concept... just not how they put it into practice.
summary: Novel and Handy Idea but Lacks Approach

reviewText: A great product for office desk/home office desk use.PROS:1. Cool, beautiful design to look at and hold in your hand.2. Once paired, it sits on the desk and connects every time, without fail with my iphone.3. Great coverage - it works for about 35-40 ft even, and so within a small house, this handset will work. (I kept this in my office and it connects from the parking lot as soon as I arrive at office - a distance of about 50 ft!4. Clear voice (no change in tone unlike some bluetooth devices!)CONS:1. Not everybody needs it or can use it all the time. I only use it in my office (for the dual purpose, as an iphone charger and as the headset while in office). I can't think of using it at home as carrying the iphone is easier than carrying this headset.2. Too pricey!So, If you have a need for a desk phone that connects to your phone using bluetooth this serves the purpose admirably - a great product for this purpose.I haven't had issues with charging the phone (iphone 4S, Sprint) on this, though I must admit the connector is a little tight -so you have to carefully place it. I am using it for the last several months (iphone 3gs before this iphone 4s), and so far haven't had any issues with it.Sound quality is also good (there is a volume control on the headset) and the microphone does seem to pick up correctly at the right volume.
summary: A great product, but not for everyone...

reviewText: I wanted to get rid of my land line and this wireless Moshi Moshi Handset looked like the ideal solution.  I had my first twinge of doubt when I opened the package to find that the wall charger needed to be assembled with the proper plug (the U.S. plug is not automatically attached with international ones as attachments).  Nothing is labeled but it's easy to figure out which one to choose.  I snapped it on and plugged one end into the wall and the other into the Moshi Moshi handset.  I knew I was in trouble when no lights went on.  Not a good sign.  The included usb cable is only for synchronization, not charging.  I could not get this device to work.I did like the solid feel of the handset.  Others mention how the shape can easily confuse the talking and listening ends but if you look before using, you can easily tell the difference - the speaking end has circles and the listening end has a bowtie shape.  The base has images to match where each end belongs.  This device should make it super easy to talk for longer periods or while multi-tasking.  I hate talking on my iPhone when home, it's the only reason I keep my land line.Initially, you can only contact the company through e-mail (website is provided in manual) but they will provide a phone number when they respond.  Unfortunately, it is a Hong Kong number.  I have received responses within 48 hours through e-mail and while they have provided info to address my issue, they have not solved it.  End result - my unit still does not work.Although the idea of this wireless handset and all the benefits of having one appealed to me, receiving one that did not work was frustrating.  Not knowing if it really works as well as advertised, I am not likely to purchase near the $150 price tag.

Well, this is a rather sleek and expensive toy.The bluetooth connectivity to the phone is just one more place for the phone conversation to get static.The problem with high gloss black plastic finish is that micro scratches start to appear almost immediately, I have had mine just one day and already there are some unsightly micro-lines on it.For $149, I think you are better off buying a nice set of earphones from etymotics.  Of course, an expensive set of headphones, won't charge your iphone, or give you a sore next if you bend your head over to hold the Moshi Moshi in place for it be "hands free".Some of the selling points of the Moshi Moshi are just not unique to it: lower radiation, even less with a corded set of earphones; sync to Skype and iPhone, sure but Bluetooth is only 10 to 30 feet so you don't have that much flexibility aware from your iPhone or Computer.So, why three stars, well it charged really quickly (about 2 hours, not 3 as in the instructions), the pairing with my iphone was easy as can be, and it is true, once the connection screen on your iphone goes away you can use your iphone.Plus it just looks cool, so some kudos for that.  Also, the heft of the handset feels nice, for nostalgic reason perhaps, but nice.

This was my first experience with a Moshi Moshi handset, and I have to say I was blown away. It literally worked right out of it's box, required no set up and I'm a big fan of such products. This allows you to receive and make calls on it's handset instead of holding your iphone which gets uncomfortable after a while. It is also a charging station for your iphone and these are just some of it's features. The AC adapter that it comes with is also very innovative and includes a plug that you attach to it depending on which country you're in. They have included them for all countries and this is a big plus for travelers. As soon as I plugged it in and pressed a button, it located my iphone instantly. The handset itself looks very sleek and doesn't feel heavy to hold. You can connect external speakers to it for your iphone music. Also, there is only one correct way to charge the handset and you need to make sure the connectors are lined with the base otherwise it may not be charging at all. It's not a big deal since it comes once you're used to the product. Putting the iphone to charge is also very easy and they have given adapters for 3GS and 4. All in all, a very innovative product that is so easy to get used to. I love it!!

This is a product I will remember for many years to come.  Not that it is really great, and not that it is awful.  I just for the life of me can't figure out why a product like this, especially at such a high price point, would be appealing to the consumer market.  I mean, this product does everything it says it will do, and it does it all extremely well.  It looks kind of modern-retro stylish, and it even has a decent feel to it.  But I just can't understand why someone would pay such a lot of money for a product that you still have to hold in your hand while you talk.  Personally, I almost never hold my cell phone up to my ear.  I use a Bluetooth wireless headset.  Now I can have my cell phone charging, walk around the room (within the distance restrictions of the Bluetooth signal), and have my hands free to do whatever I need to do.  Does anybody really feel the need to actually hold something up to their head in order to talk on the phone these days?So aside from my personal curiosity about why this product exists, I found the Native Union Moshi Moshi Curve wireless handset to be well made, easy to setup, and extremely straightforward to operate.  It comes with a universal power adapter (with interchangeable plug tips for every country), which makes the Moshi Moshi Curve a great travel companion (but I don't know why one would ever want or need this while on travel).  The materials and build quality all seem excellent, and the sound quality of the handset (both outgoing and incoming audio) is definitely a big step above that of the average cell phone.  Native Union boasts that their product will greatly reduce the amount of radiation (by up to 99%) your melon will absorb during cell phone conversations.  OK, I guess if you are on your cell phone for hours and hours a day, then I can understand the concern about the radiation levels.  However, I still prefer a hands-free method of communication myself, vs. holding a device like the Moshi Moshi Curve up to my ear.Again I want to say that the Moshi Moshi Curve Bluetooth wireless handset is a well built device, which works well and seems to live up to the claims made by the manufacturer.  I used it a handful of times and it worked flawlessly.  But the fact is I was stuck holding this somewhat heavy, clunky handset up to my head during the entire conversation each time.  Other than an occasional quick call on my cell phone, which doesn't warrant me taking out my Bluetooth earpiece to use, I haven't held an old fashioned landline handset up to my ear in several years.  I even use a 2.4 GHz wireless headset for my home phone, just because it bugs me to have my hands tied up for long periods of time while I am talking on the phone.  The Moshi Moshi Curve just seems like a fashion statement for those that have a lot of extra money to blow.  Hey, I buy a lot of electronic gadgets that I sometimes don't need, but I don't think I would invest the money in this product for myself or anyone that I know.  The range of the Moshi Moshi Curve is standard for the Bluetooth technology that it uses.  I get about 15 to 20 feet away from the base before the audio starts getting garbled and frequently cuts out.  But this is the exact same range I get out of my little Bluetooth earpiece, which I hook onto my ear and often forget that I am even wearing.  So for those of you looking for a stylish, retro type phone handset to use with your cellular phone, then I can honestly say that the Moshi Moshi Curve (MM03i), by Native Union, will not disappoint you.  But I would really appreciate it if someone could let me know why they would spend almost a hundred and fifty bucks on a gadget like this, when you could by a decent quality Bluetooth earpiece for a fraction of that, and have totally hands free phone conversations.  Hats off to Native Union for producing a high quality product.  I just don't know why they did it, or why someone would buy it.  =o)

This MMO3i Handset has a beautiful form factor.  Less is more describes it perfectly.  It's sleek, with a low profile.  The base is weighted so it stays in one place.  One doesn't see lights unless the lights are on.  Otherwise, the whole unit looks uniformly black.The only lights that are visible when the handset is on the base is the tiny charging light and the equally small Bluetooth light, both of which are a soft glowing white.  They are unobtrusive at night.As a charging station for my iPhone 4S, it's wonderful.  It comes with a universal charging adapter for the iPhone 3GS and the iPhone 4.  What I like about this dock is I don't have to take my phone out of the case to place it on the dock.  To make it fit, I just don't use the adapters.As for the handset, sound quality is best when the phone and the handset are in the same room as the dock.  Separating either one too far from the dock and we get a lot of static or interference.  Even one room over can be a problem, so it's not as good as using a cordless phone.SOLUTION FOR SOME PROBLEMSThe manual was not very helpful for some of the problems I encountered, so I will share some of my solutions with you that worked for me.  Keep in mind, I have an iPhone 4S.  This may not work for everyone:iPhone NOT AUTO-RECONNECTING:1) Unpair the handset.2) Turn off the handset.3) Place the handset on the dock.4) While the handset is on the dock, press and hold the power button (MFB) until you hear a tone.5) Turn on the handset and pair your phone.HANDSET HAS NO SOUNDS:Go to settings --> general --> accessibility --> incoming calls --> choose "headset."I know the accessibility on my phone was initially set on "default" and that did not work.  Changing it to "headset" and then later switching back to "default" somehow did the trick so that I no longer have to worry about getting sound over the handset.CONCLUSIONI use this dock more as a charging station for my phone than for the handset.  The handset is more comfortable to hold than the phone, but I'm stuck using it in the bedroom (where the dock is), so it's not as convenient to use.  It is very elegant.  It looks pretty sitting on my nightstand.  I just wish it had more range.
Very easy in my opinion to set up from pairing to selecting your ringtone. I like that one usb wire charges both the phone and the headset and allows you to sync your phone with iTunes. Well built.

This is something I didn't think I would want or need until I got it, now I can't see not having it.  I don't have an i-Phone but it really doesn't matter, it works perfectly with my bluetooth enabled smart phone just fine.  Whenever I'm in the offie I keep my phone in a desktop charging cradle and have my wireless headset nearby.  But it is a hassle putting the headset on and off everytime I want to make or take a call.With the Moshi Curve (odd name for a product) my phone can remain in the cradle and I can make a call using a comfortable and familiar handset.  It is far easier to hold than a candy bar shaped phone and any radiation from the phone is far away from my ear.Since I don't have an iPhone I have found that the dock on the handset works perfectly with my iPod, it keeps it charged and there is a handy audio output to my computer speaker system.  It holds the iPod at the perfect angle and keeps it handy since the phone is close to me on my desk.I can't write this without commenting on the packaging the manufacturer used for this device.  Considering there is nothing really fragile about it, a normal blister card would have been fine, but no, it came packed in a box made of cardboard that is about 4x thicker than a normal box, with an intricately die-cut inner sleeve that has a piece of thick dense rubber surrounding the phone (!).  It was incredibly overpackaged, but certainly protected the device and gave the whole product an aura of quality.I read a review from someone who downgraded the product because of "bright blinking lights" and expected them to be visible and annoying.  In fact they are on the underside of the handset and not even visible in the daytime.  At night they put out a soft glow, not at all annoying.  I'm thinking most people who own this handset would use it at a desk or in their living area, not in a darkened bedroom, but if they did a little piece of tape over the light would take care of the problem and would be unseen so it wouldn't detract from the styling.  In my opinion, the status lights have nothing to do with whether this is a good product or not.So, is it a good product?  Yes.  It is extremely attractive and almost a piece of art (reminds of of Bang & Olufsen products).  The sound quality is better than the phone itself and it is substantially easier to hold for extended periods.  Personally, if there was a choice I would get the unit without the iPhone dock, but having it is not a dealbreaker.

I was excited to receive this "second generation" Moshi Moshi as I have very much enjoyed using the wired units that were released years ago. It's very attractive and the matte black finish works well with almost any decor as it shifts between "retro" and "contemporary" very easily. That said, I wish it docked in a more friendly fashion with my iPhone 4. I have an AmazonBasics Protective TPU Case with Screen Protector for AT&T; and Verizon iPhone 4 and iPhone 4S (Smoke) on my phone and don't find that the case hampers "docking" so much as the base just doesn't fit the phone very well. Pairing is simple and easy and I must say that when it's working, having the freedom to roam a bit independently of your phone via the Bluetooth technology is very nice. reviewText: The life of the extended battery is almost the exact same as the regular battery.  Hence, it is a waste of money

With the stock Droid battery during a normal day, I was getting 8 hours tops before the Droid shutdown. I now get between 24-36 hours between charges. Bottom line, if you consistently need to recharge and you don't always have access to power, get this battery.I don't know if I am a heavy or light user. Let me tell you how I use my Droid and you can compare my experience/usage with yours.My Droid is rooted and I am running CyanogenMod 6.1.2 with an overclocked 1100 Mhz kernel. I use set-CPU to keep the clock between 550 Mhz and 1100 Mhz with setpoints based on temperature to drop the speed to 300Mhz. I don't use any task killers at all (they are worse than useless, but that is a different story). I primarily use Wi-Fi for data.During the day, I use my Droid for data operations like Twitter (5 minute updates), video watching (maybe 5-10 minutes, sometimes longer), listening to music (a few hours), getting email using GMail (push) and Exchange using Touchdown (which is power hungry when using push), running the GPS and other activities like games. On a recent trip, I left my laptop at home and brought a Bluetooth keyboard with me. Even using that for hours at a time, I still had more than enough battery power to get me through the day.My normal usage would suck the stock battery dry in 6-8 hours. I ended up disabling a number of features to eke out maybe 8 hours of life from the stock Droid battery. I used to carry a spare battery with me, but that didn't help much plus I had to shutdown and swap the battery which is not terribly convenient. With the Seidio, I now get close to 36 hours or more.I did what others who have reviewed the battery did. I charged the battery for 10+ hours, ran it down to less than 5% (did a reboot to verify), and charged it back up another 10 hours. Works fine.The battery is a bit bulky but the cover fits snugly into the Droid body. I don't use a holster or cover, so I didn't have a problem with accessories. I did find that the batter pack did alter my use of both the hard and soft keyboard. It put me out of position just enough that it took some time to get my hands back in place.
summary: Two to four times more battery life

reviewText: I can't imagine a better case. I've tried various styles with other phones and they're always lacking in some way. I'm perfectly satisfied with this case for my N900. The fit is perfect - the design is very impressive - and it only adds a few millimeters to the size of the phone. Well done. I'll likely be looking at Otter Box for any future phone case purchases.

I think Otterbox makes some of the best phone cases, and this one is no exception.They have 2 lines: the High Impact, and the Commuter versions.The High Impact, which I have for my Nokia 5800, is all rubber. Very high quality, but also adds a lot of mass and bulk. And since rubber is non-slip, it can be a pain to retrieve out of your pockets while in certain positions (ahem, like while driving).So this Commuter version is a better alternative (I don't think they have a High Impact version for the N900 yet).This version is made of high quality plastic, which a thin inner rubber lining on the bottom side (opposite of the screen side), to protect the phone from short falls and small knocks.It fits into the phone very nicely and securely - very little creaks and give from loose spaces.In fact, you will find it very hard to pop it out when you have to replace a SIM card or battery (but there is a trick to get it to open easily, which is hard to describe, so you'll have to find it on your own).It doesn't add much bulk to the phone, and ultimately, gives you a great peace of mind, which is what it's all about.The only small negative about it (like any other case for phones with big screens), is that there is no way it can protect the screen side from falls onto bumpy or angled surfaces.

I've been using it for  3 months so far. Like it is stated it fits Nokia N900 very easily. It is equipped with silicone corners dissipate impact away from device. My main purpose was looking for bump & shock protection. I think I got it, but haven't had the opportunity to test it. Silicone plugs provide access to audio jack & USB portIncludes self-adhering clear protective film, cleaning cloth & installation card. reviewText: I've tried several holster cases for my Droid Bionic -- to which I've added the silicone sleeve and the Motorola extended battery (2700+). The ones I've tried include oversize -- most were too large so the phone flopped around inside or were difficult to pull out; the kind with a spring clip that you squeeze to attach to a belt -- these clips stab you in the side every now and then, and have a habit of popping off the belt; and the kind that requires you to use them as a system -- you must remove your silicone skin and replace it with their cover which then slides into a receiver frame.All of them had issues.This one fits perfect, without being too snug. And -- at first -- I thought the magnets were a bit too weak and that the flap would not fully close with the phone in this holster. After a week of wearing it, the material has "formed" to the phone shape a bit, the flap works just fine -- and the holster is very comfortable.Great holster for the price!Update 12/7/12...Biggest issue with this case is the finish does not wear very well. The "leather" or "vinyl" cover wore through within a very short time. I have since moved on to a Samsung Note II, but wanted to warn Buyers about this issue on this case.

The magnetic flap closure takes some getting used to as it is very stiff.  But that makes it just a bit more secure if you're jogging.The back has both clip-on clips so you can just put it on your belt or remove it without opening the belt.  And it also has loops to run the belt through so it's set on the belt and hard to grab or remove.The iPhone 4S fit with the thin neoprene cover.  It's tight, and a bit hard to pry out at a ring's notice, but that just makes it more secure.I do hope this same company makes an exact copy of this for the iPhone 6 upgrade I am hoping for.  The iPhone 5S wouldn't fit into this pouch -- but surely they must have made one for that size.

The amount of electricity used is similar to that of a non-powered USB port on your computer. For example, the USB ports on a standard Apple USB keyboard do not power devices; this charger uses the same kind of ports. Even plugging in one device at a time does not charge at full capacity. When I plug in my iPad 2 via its dock connector cable, my iPad displays "Not Charging" next to the battery indicator; worthless! When I plug in my Samsung Nexus S 4G via its USB charge cable, it takes twice the usual time to charge to full capacity. I did not notice any significant difference in charging my Kindle or iPod Shuffle than with their factory chargers.Overall, this USB charger is an awesome idea, but it fails to live to its expectations. It is round at the base of the pins and doesn't fit flush against the socket.  It has a tendency to rock when it is plugged in.  It should have been made flat.  Other than that, it does what it us supposed to do.
Kind of big and klunky for starters. Some of my USB device cables won't work with this charger - mostly Apple devices.
This product was shipped on time.  On a trip to Europe, it stopped working from a voltage converter.  I would question the quality of  this product.
This is great. When we travel this is good. I use this in conjunction with the iFlash High Output 4 USB Car Charger. One for the wall socket and one for the car port.

I should have read the tech specs closer. NOTE that all four USB ports  are 1 amp so it works for my iPhone, Kindle, Bluetooth Ear Piece, small Bluetooth speaker can but NOT for the iPad. At 1amp, it takes the iPad a really, really long time to charge. So, I have a lightning and three micro USB cords attached but have my iPad charger plugged in elsewhere. One 2.1A plug would have been great. Just one.
summary: I should have read the tech specs closer.

reviewText: this thing is a great little gizmo except that it looks like a squid growing out of your wall when all the ports are full of wires. it's convenient to have the ability to have several items charging as almost everything charges with a usb these days.mine is plugged in next to my bed. If I tug on it a little, as in using my nearly dead phone while it is charging with a long usb cord, it pulls out of the wall fairly easily. but that is my fault.it's not very powerful, this one is 2000mah. There may be more powerful ones out there, but take the total rating and divide it into the number of ports. In this case, 2000mah/4ports = 500mah per port. At that rate most items do not charge very quickly, some register as "not charging" because they are designed to have a higher charge rate at minimum, some devices were designed to charge at close to 2 amps... Some new devices like the droid max or ipad2 will need a whole lot of time to charge them up (especially when they got 3600mah batteries, but will  simply charge at a slower rate, often charging at or near full overnight.for example, if my ipad is at 5% and I plug it in it registers the connection but indicates 'not charging'. ultimately it will charge, when I wake up (7-8 hours) it usually will be up to 75% or so.when we rented a vacation home with friends or are out of town for the weekend with family it's a huge hit. less people lose or forget their phones, it's just convenient.you should try it. This one appears well made, looks good too. There are surely others out there that are good, and surely some that are junk, but i've been happy with this purchase.
summary: popular at parties and with the ladies

GeneralThe one I received looks a little different from the one pictured but it's pretty close.  For the price, I can't complain, as it appears to be made rather well with some nice features and blends well with my car's black interior.  I have searched for a while and found nothing at any price that would work for me.  This one works just fine.InstallationIt took a couple of tries and some moistening of the suction pad before I got it to stick to my car windshield but it is holding so far.  Temperatures here vary from the teens in the winter and 80s+ in summer, so I fully expected it to fall off at some point....but thankfully it has been holding on for months.  I use it twice a day, every day minimum.  I never remove it from the window....my husband just cleans around it.FeaturesThe long extension from the base can be bent & shaped in order to position the unit within reach.  I chose to make these adjustments before I locked on the unit bracket.  I was able to  position my Evo above the dash to the right of the steering wheel without it getting in the way of anything, including my view of the road.  I opted for this type of bracket as I did not care to use other types which looked very bulky/unsightly and could scratch/damage my interior in some way.  I have the unit in the lower center of my windshield and bent down slightly but not touching the dash.  I have the little feet extended out to hold the bottom of the phone and only need to use one hand to place my phone in the holder as I gently compress the cushioned side arms inward to secure the phone in place. I have used a couple of different cases and it holds solidly with case on.FunctionalityIf my phone is not in the holder, the unit is very stable and makes no noise, unlike reviews from others who purchased similar units.  When my phone is in the holder while driving, however, the weight of the phone seems to cause the unit to wobble a bit, but it's not terrible.  It does not make noise though, just goes from a slight vibration to a mild wobble.  (That's why I only gave it 4 stars.)  Since I never interact with my phone while driving anyway, it doesn't matter to me as long as my phone is in view and secure.  If I need to do something on the phone, I do it when stopped.  I have factory bluetooth in my car so I can now use more of the phone's features totally hands free and can easily see what's going on. I love that.  I have used my phone's navigation while it is mounted and can display it both in portrait and landscape positions, as the bracket rotates nicely clicking to those positions and more if desired.  Most of the time I use it in the portrait position.  I would say that it is made reasonably well and it is likely to last a while if used with gentle care.  It is mostly plastic, so rough handling/abuse may take its toll on the unit.  It has a small button on the back near the top which when gently pressed causes the padded bracket arms to release the phone into my hand for quick disconnect.Bottom line.....I like it very much.  It holds my Evo safely, looks nice and does the trick.  Time will tell whether or not it holds up to regular use, but I hope so, as I'm enjoying the convenience it provides.  I may even order another one as a backup just in case.Also, I would like to thank this and other sellers for making desirable accessories available at very affordable prices.
summary: Nice window mount for my HTC Evo

reviewText: When I received the unit I was impressed on how it looked but that is how far I went in liking it.First of all, the unit is hard on the ear. It's not as flexible. I was hoping that it would be at pliable so that it would bend for people with bigger heads. It does bend but after more than 2 hours of wearing it my ear canal would start to get irritated.Second, the silicon ear buds it would very often come off when I removed it from my ear. I guess I have to carefully remove it as not to knock it off.Third, the sound is really good if, I mean if it's wore it at a certain angled.Forth, when I use it for voice calls using my Nokia N8. I would always hear myself, not sure if it was echo but I always hear it during voice calls only.The only positive is it the battery last a very long time. I listen to music and talk radio (using internet radio) almost all day (about 6+ hours) and this thing will last all those time, that is if my ear don't get irritated first.Also, not sure if I got the wrong unit or color but, it doesn't look like it's ice blue, it's more like all white.

Have had a few months now.  Was concerned a little about how it fit when I first got it.  Does not fit tight to head like a sunglass's band that it resembles.  However, found this to be fine in terms of comfort and great in terms of not having to clean it from sweaty workouts.  The in-ear parts don't go too far in for me, which allows me to wear them while laying down with head on pillow.  Actually improves the bass a bit more.  I've been able to wear for hours without issue.Sound quality is much better than I expected.  I use a Nokia XpressMusic 5800 and after adjusting the bass to maximum, it really has pretty good quality for a bluetooth.  Plus it's fine for taking calls.  But don't expect to hear anything else as the in-ear fit seals off most outside noise.  I really don't use for phone calls unless I just happen to get one while wearing.  Don't get caught wearing these in a car as most states consider it illegal to wear full head phones that impair hearing, while you drive.Battery time is really great!  You can go several days without really having to charge it.  Your phone will die much quicker than this headset when playing music.  And the AC chargers for Nokia phones works with it.  Just can't listen while charging.Thought it might look a little too Star-Wars-ish, but not as bad as it looks.Simple setup (for phone) and buttons are great.  Volume and forward/back song selection rocker switches are a nice touch.  Hard to accidently change, easy enough when you need to.  Do have to press the answer and pause buttons a little hard to click on/off which tends to push the in-ear bud a little deeper that can cause discomfort.  Setup for PC not easy and I still don't have the sound quality set right.  I really did not get it for the PC, but proper setup is an issue for those who are needing it for such.  May take some serious tech skills to get right, and not mess with your other audio settings for other devices as did with mine.Overall am very pleased with product.  I had a Jabra with two pieces before to use for both calls and music and this is much, much better.

I wish i could return this product, but unfortunately I had to try on this product to discover it is completely the wrong shape for my head & ears.The hook above the ears is made of rigid plastic and is poorly shaped.  The design combination does not allow the ear buds to rest in or enter the ears properly (no matter what ear buds I use) which is a product killer for isolation type earphones.  The hooks' shape also acts as a lever, pushing the unit up and away from my neck and head.  Aside from the hook and ear buds, the entire unit never touches my head.  The item may not be heavy, but the resting point above the ears becomes very uncomfortable because it is the leverage/resting point for the entire unit.I could not even determine if the audio quality is of any value because the hook shape prevented the various isolation ear buds from entering my ear.I've tried to unload it to a friend for free, but it didn't not fit him either.
summary: Poor over hear hook shape kills isolation earphones

reviewText: My head is above average size, I guess. Often sunglasses are tight on me.This is very tight, I would say uncomfortable after only a few minutes. But I suppose this means it will be very secure. I can shake my head and the unit stays put. UPDATE: The comfort got better as I kept wearing it. Kind of like a new bike seat, it stopped hurting after a few days.There are 6 sets of tips. 3 sizes of the type that enter the ear canal, and 3 that sit outside the ear canal.By the way, the outside packaging says the unit is water resistant, but the instructions say not to get it wet. So I'm not sure how sweat resistant this will be. UPDATE: I sweat a lot. The power button became unresponsive twice during workouts. The unit behaves as if I'm adjusting the volume or pressing RW. It continues to play, but I can't turn it off. The first time, it "dried out" and started working again. Today when I used it, I even wrapped a baby sock around most of it during use, but the same thing happened. Sweat is entering the area close to the ears with the buttons.The sound quality is pretty good with the correct ear tips, but I don't recommend for working out. I may have to send it to Nokia for repair.
summary: Too small for larger heads, not sweat resistant

reviewText: these are definitely gonna take a bit of getting used to. They are not adjustable at all, which is kind of a negative in my view. The sound quality is a lot better than I'd expected for listening to music. I've listened to everything from a classical to pop to metal to rap to jazz and beyond, and have been pretty content with them. They don't provide the deepest bass hits, but they do a pretty good job. The treble sounds are pretty clear, and can hit painfully high pitches with clarity. As a pair of wireless headphones, I'm glad I got these.I was hoping these would be better for use with phone calls, but without a boom mic I can't be surprised. In a very quiet environment, they work fine. The slightest bit of background noise is picked up though and can make their use impossible. Sitting on my front porch, the sound of a small car driving by was all it took to drown out a conversation.Update 15Apr12: Ordered these in Sept'11, and they quit working this past week. They started to get static and weak signals last week (I think due to the humidity in New Orleans, never had that problem in colorado's arid climate), and then i bumped them just wrong and the left side snapped clean off, left hanging by the wires.While they lasted, they were great for listening to tunes~ nice on the bus, could just leave the iPod, Tablet, phone or whatever other device I was using in my backpack, and control everything without having to keep devices handy. For this use, I much preferred this pair of headphones most of my others. They are/were also much more comfortable than the pair from Motorola that I have.I'd definitely recommend these, but with warning:First, the weak spots just above the control buttons, where they are the skinniest, and also where the most force is put while putting them on/taking them off. This is where mine snapped, and there isn't really a way to fix this~ I've tried super glue, epoxy, tape, splint... Nothing decent has come yet.Second, these are really only good for listening, not for use as a phone headset. If you are looking for a stereo headset for two-way use, I'd recommend looking for something with a boom mic. This style of headset picks up every sound in the room except for your voice.
summary: Great for music, not the best for phone calls
