I have been a big fan of protecting investments such as the expense of a brand new smartphone for quite some time now (and yes, I DID manage to learn this the HARD way...) and after getting my HTC Incredible, I went ahead and STILL took my time getting one, knowing that by doing so, I was stalling the inevitable. My reasoning was simple: After a couple days, I figured I would be trading in my DInc for the Droid X as soon as one became available (those dang backorders!). But each day I slowly, but surely began to like my Incredible more & more. Before long I began to seriouly consider keeping it instead of trading up (although in honesty, the ONLY thing the X has on the Incrdible is a larger screen and more memory out-of-the-box, otherwise they are comparable in EVERY way--oh, and the X doesn't have Sense UI, so tie goes to HTC. With the 2.2 update, it now had Mobile Hotspot capabilities as well as HD video, so all-in-all they are pretty darned equal).Wouldn't you know it, within an hour of deciding to keep my phone I somehow managed to drop it (the story of my life). Not far, mind you--but when you've paid as much for a phone as these things typically co$t--even with my upgrade--it's almost weird how time really DID seem to stand still for a moment as I watched it fall. It really burned me, too--especially since I am such a staunch supporter of buying protective cases. Well I wasted NO time after this. I immediately went out and got my silicone gel case. It fit perfectly (oh, and BTW mine is a clear-ish version). It looks good, several times people have mistaken it for an iPhone. What I really like is how it protects and yet doesn't add unnecessary thickness to an already very thin phone. Even WITH the case my phone is about as thin as my old BB Tour WITHOUT a case (if not thinner).As another reviewer noted, this particular type of case tends to attract lint, hair and all sorts of miniature items you manage to accumulate in your pockets--along with tiny crumbs you may accidentally set your phone on top of. Weird, but its like a mini swiffer mop. Now in all fairness, I found that the similar manufactured EXPENSIVE case I used to have for my BB Bold did the exact same thing. I believe that silicone cases in general (which are by far my personal favorite) tend to attract these types of items, so accept it and move on. My other minor complaint is that when trying to retrieve from my pocket, the rubberized surface tends to want to *stick* to the inside of my pockets, sometimes annoyingly so. But again, this is the nature of almost ALL silicone cases I have ever seen. Not much you can honestly do about it, really. Once again, accept it and, well, you get the idea.In short, if you are looking to protect YOUR investment (and after spending $200 bucks, why wouldn't you?) this particular case works, fits and actually even looks nice. I'll definitely buy another (eventually).

I ordered this six-foot USB cable to use with my iPhone and iPad. The first picture on the amazon product page for this cable has what looks like a generic connector that you plug into the iPhone/iPad. That's the type of connector that looks bigger (fatter?) than the slimmer connector that you see on the current real Apple cables. I was pleasantly surprised to see that the cable that I actually received had the connector that was just like the ones you see on the more current real Apple cables. See the picture that I posted at the top of this product's amazon page for the cable that I received.I bought this cable from amazon marketplace seller 'The OEM Shop' for under three dollars with free S&H.; I received the cable very quickly in five days. I do NOT work for 'The OEM Shop' or for Amazon, but I mention the name of the seller because very few people seem to mention the name of the amazon marketplace seller who they bought a product from in their reviews. These cables are "generic" and it is often difficult to tell which seller sold the product that the buyer is either complaining about or praising in a product review. Also, a lot of buyers don't seem to realize that they can select a particular seller and not just take whoever is the seller who may be appearing as the "default" seller on an amazon product page. I don't know what determines who is the "default" seller, but I'm guessing that Amazon comes first if Amazon has the product in their warehouse(s), but if not, then maybe the other sellers are possibly rotated as the "default" seller on the page, and so on and so forth. Anyways, I think it is worth mentioning who is the particular amazon marketplace seller is in a review - especially if the product is generic like this cable and if there are a lot of sellers who are selling the product via the one single amazon product page.Anyways, the cable that I bought is indeed a nice long six-foot cable. It looks like the real thing. And it was new. I was able to charge my iPhone and iPad by using this cable when connected to a charger plugged into the wall. And I was able to sync my iPhone and iPad with iTunes on my macbook. The cable was also able to charge my iPhone via the USB on my macbook. For my iPhone, I've tried charging with both a real official apple power adapter and also a generic power adapter - and both worked. (Of course, for my iPad, I had to use the 10w charger that came with my iPad because you can't use anything else when charging from an electrical outlet in the wall.) I will be using this nice long six-foot cable for whenever I want to charge my iPhone or iPad for like when I want to use my iPhone or iPad when I'm in bed or if I'm sitting elsewhere like at the kitchen table and if I want to save the battery for later. (I would be keeping the shorter original cable that came with my iPhone/iPad for use with my macbook for syncing the iPhone/iPad.) I'm happy with this purchase and with this cable.

reviewText: This isn't exactly the OEM battery for the Incredible (since it's not orange); its actually the OEM battery for a different HTC phone but with the same specs.Perfect fit, and based on a month's use, possibly slightly better performance. I say "possibly" because it's impossible to use the battery exactly the same way each charge cycle; the life of a charge is very dependent on the services you're using, charging technique, and many other factors.  The Incredible really is incredible, but it's very powerful and very thin...  ...and under extreme usage (with all the things it's capable of doing simultaneously and with the very powerful processor it can be a horrendous battery-hog at times.  It's the price you pay to have a powerful phone and not being careful to turn off what you're not using.I've had a fully-charged battery go dead in less than three hours while using navigation (full-boogie GPS), WiFi and music on a road trip without the charger attached.I "super-charged" this battery using one of the many techniques found in the forums before using it the first time...  ...I was careful with the services I used, but used the phone "normally", and got over 36 hours of use (more than double the time I'd ever experienced before), so I'd have to say it's equal to or better than the "OEM" battery that came with my phone.  I couldn't be happier! My "test" was far from scientific and a lot of that test was stand-by, but I'm happy as heck with the performance.Many Incredible owners are investing very big bucks in high-capacity batteries and special larger backs to accommodate them; that makes the phone bulky and unable to be used with many accessories...  ...for what they're spending to do that, I can buy 4 or 5 of these and carry them around as spares (while still keeping my thin, light, phone. I now carry a charged spare whenever I leave home, and haven't been caught with a dead phone since.Save your money, folks...  ...if you're having battery-life problems with your Inc., just get one or two of these. It's a tremendous value.

There is also a pattern in the cast, look at the pictures of the back to see what I'm talking about, and there are small raised areas on the corners.  I actually like this as it helps me hold the phone when I am using it in a horizontal position.Overall this is a really nice silicone case for the EVO.  I am very happy with it and at $9.95 I feel it is a very fair price.  It fits well for a silicon case and gives me grip when holding my EVO.  Recommended.

reviewText: I'll be frank--the only real reason i bough this was to modify it to fit my 3500mAh Seidio battery.it worked/works.and for the price--it's a no brainer.the texture of it makes it great to have in the car--as it won't slide from side to side, and its elastic nature is really good at holding shape despite any instances in which you might leave it in direct sunlight. some cheaper cases i've purchased are really weak when it comes to sunlight for some stupid reason.it wraps around the phone really well, adding a little bit of a lip to the front of the phone so you can lay it face down and not really worry about any scratches. the power button is actually really easily accessible with this--but the volume buttons kind of become hard to find. perhaps it was from my modification--so i can't say for sure. all of the ports are adequately open and no problem accessing for anything.if you have the 3500 battery--get thisto make it fit= use a knife to cut a line directly from the dual flash to the hinge of the kickstand & a line directly from the speaker down to the bottom of the kickstand.it retains its shape remarkably well and doesn't stretch-out at all. i cut mine out in about 3 minutes and couldn't be happier with the result. the tech @ the Sprint store even asked if i bought the case specially made for it--then when i told her what i did, she remarked she wouldn't even had noticed if i hadn't pointed it out to her.also, if you feel more comfortable, use the outline of a credit card/drivers license to achieve more straight of a line.for the price--this is awesome. get it.

I've ordered numerous cases for my HTC EVO 4G, but this particular one really stands out when it comes to the simple silicone style. The shape is intuitive and extremely snug when compared to the typical silicone design, which is still adequate and a little cheaper; however, this case is well worth the extra couple bucks. The rubber feels a little thicker and less flimsy. The indented sides (as seen in the photo) are textured for the sake of grip, the power/volume buttons are covered without jeopardizing their functionality, and the extended/smooth central region makes it quite well designed for staying put and not wobbling on flat surfaces. The thickness of the case protrudes beyond the camera, thereby protecting the lens and other components. All things considered, it's a pretty great case for a pretty great price considering what you get - the only thing I'm not certain about is the durability over an extended period of time.*EDIT* (August 18, 2012) - Over a year later, this has been my case of choice and is rarely removed from my HTC EVO 4G. It hasn't stretched and still fits the contours of the phone quite snugly. It is still by far the best silicon and overall case I've put on my phone and every time I would seldom try something new, I immediately revert back to this. reviewText: When I first purchased the Evo 4g, I knew two things straight-away:1) The phone feels relatively fragile, hence the need for a case, and2) The cases that the Sprint store sells are overpriced crap.After reading some online reviews from the early adopters of the phone and various cases, I decided that the case that I wanted was theSeidio Innocase Active Case for HTC EVO 4G - Limited Editionbecause it appeared to offer the most protection for my shiny new toy.Unfortunately, at the time of my purchase, the Innocase was on back-order for almost a month.  I bought this Amzer case as a holdover (i.e. it was in stock and Prime-eligible) to protect my phone until my "real" case arrived.Immediately upon receiving this case I put it on my phone.  The fit and finish are pretty good for a sub-$10 case.  The case in no way interferes with the stand built into the back of the phone, which I was a little concerned with.  The case fits pretty snugly on the phone and offers protection to both the screen and the camera lens since it extends slightly beyond both.  I do wish that the fit was a little tighter (dust seems to find a way in behind the case), but I can't argue with the protection.I know the protection works because this weekend I dropped my phone from a decent height (around 5 feet) onto a tile floor.  The phone fell straight down on to the screen with a muffled thud.  I picked it up and wiped the screen off on my shirt, and noticed that there were no cracks in the screen.  Upon closer inspection, I noticed that I hadn't even scratched the screen.Bottom line is this -- do I think that this case is perfect?  The dust issue bothers me so I can't say yes.  Do I think that this case offers the protection advertised and is worth every cent?  Absolutely.  Whether you are purchasing the case for full time use or (like me) are purchasing it as a holdover until another arrives, I do not think you'll regret it.  Who knows -- I may even continue using this case once the Innocase arrives!

Me and my friend both purchased HTC EVOs around the same time so we decided to do some research on cases for the phone. Eventually we came down to two choices, the Seidio Innocase Active Case for HTC EVO 4G - Limited Edition because it look impressive and the reviews were great, and this case because it was cheap and looked like it was well built. Both came in around the same time and we compared them side by side, and to be honest this case is WAY better than the Seidio one. Even at more than half the price this AMZER case trumps the Seidio in flexibility, quality of build, overall feel, button accessibility, looks, well.. everything! Now my friend is returning his Seidio so he can get this case! When we first got the cases, the AMZER came in a plain looking package, while his came in some fancy shmancy packaging. I was beginning to think I had made a mistake, but once we had taken them out of the packaging it was pretty clear who had the winner.It isn't that the Seidio is a bad case, its just the protection just isn't the same. We tried drop tests on both of them and his sounded like a loud "CRACK" which made me cringe every time we dropped it from about 12 inches, while this one made a soft thud and obviously absorbed the blow much. much better. The buttons with the Seidio were difficult and uncomfortable to push, while the AMZER was smart and made the case a little bit softer where the buttons are which made for pressing them just as easy as if there was no case at all. The Siedio has a much less flexible material compared to the AMZER and is not comfortable in the hand at all, the AMZER feels like it is conforming to the curves of your hand every time you hold it and actually makes it much easier to hold thanks to the anti-slip grip that the Siedio does not have. Overall the AMZER trumps the Seidio in almost everything. The Seidio, however, is a winner when it comes to repelling dust. The AMZER does pick up a light amount of dirt/dust that is not very hard to remove but still can be an eyesore if not maintained. The Seidio seems to not pick up any dust.If I were to pick between the two, I would save my money and go with the AMZER for sure.
summary: Better than the Seidio Limited Edition case

I didn't quite skimp on buying a case for my Incredible but after reading the reviews for various screen protectors, I felt confident in buying this very modestly priced set of 3. I am completely satisfied with it.First of all, I found out the first weekend of owning my Incredible that the nature of the LCD screen coupled with the polarization of some sunglasses makes the screen appear completely black (as if it was off) when turned sideways (landscape). I was not a fan of this, as I always wear my sunglasses and I pretty much have to use the landscape keyboard to type. Well, this anti-glare screen protector took all of that away. The screen is still slightly dimmer, but definitely (and almost quite literally) a day and night difference!I had some trouble applying the first protector, and ended up ruining it as a result, but that was my fault for not being more careful to get all the dust/dirt off the first time. MAKE SURE you do this, as one little speck of dust will cause a bubble 10x as big around it. You do need to be very careful getting this on to not only avoid the bubbles but avoid other places it just won't lay down; in short, be careful when handling it and removing the cutouts for the indicator lights so as not to bend the protector at all, as it won't lay flat on the screen.As mentioned in other reviews, it has not affected the response of the touch screen in the slightest, and I don't really even notice that it is on the phone. The instructions said that there was a small plastic card to press the protector on and smooth out the bubbles, but mine didn't have the card. Not a huge deal, I just used a card from my wallet. Also, I ordered these at the same time as a case for my phone which had 2-day shipping, and this product arrived the day before that one, with standard! I will not hesitate to buy another set of these if needed, especially at this price!UPDATE 7/12: I'm just now moving on from the Incredible, but wanted to point out that this first 3-pack I bought when I first got the phone at the end of 2010 lasted me up until now, despite ruining the first screen as mentioned above. The one I initially put on lasted around a year until I decided to replace it with my last spare due to all the scratches and dings I'd accumulated over the months. The 3rd one was just as great as the last!

reviewText: I was lucky to have a screen protector on my Droid when I dropped it on a gravel road. The screen protector scratched, my screen stayed perfect. So I needed a new set of protectors and chose these.After removing my case and thoroughly cleaning the screen, I placed the protector as directed and it all went very well. This protector is great in that it covers the WHOLE screen and not just the touch part. It literally goes from top to bottom and fits in perfectly. It does not get in the way of the touch sensitivity either.There always seems to be a little bubble or two but they pushed out easily. It does not get in the way of my case and stays put.

This package comes with 3 screen protectors, two are clear and one is anti-glare.They cover the whole front face of the phone as seen in the photos.  There is a full circle cutout where the optical button is - the photos are ambiguous as to whether it's a full circle or separated at the bottom.It's not a bad deal for the price but there is a small issue with the quality that I've seen from other vendors of cheap screen protectors.There appears a sort of bubble around a small part of the circle cut area of the optical mouse/button that appears after installation.  I think it is caused by dull cutters that causes the material to bend out of shape a bit instead of being cleanly cut.  Then because the plastic is bent, it does not fit perfectly flat around those cut areas.This is a very minor flaw but something the thicker, more expensive screen covers avoid (Like the AT&T; vended ones for the iPhone which have a similar circle hole).Other than that, there's nothing remarkable about these protectors save for the price.  They are clear without noticeable distortion - even if you look for it.Bottom line:  If you can live with possible slight flaws around the optical mouse/button, I would recommend this product. If you attempt to install this and there is one spec of dust that gets underneath the film, well, that dust will be there until you change the thing.There are no instructions that come with it, but it's pretty easy to figure out the steps...turn off your evo, you will receive a phone call the instant you attempt to install thisclean the screen thoroughly - it should be shining and no fingerprints on the screenpeel the label that says "peel this before install" - at this point you have the world's best airborne dust attractor. My stepson lost his mother's cellphone. The phone, which my wife did not like much anyway, was on my family plan. My wife prefers clamshell phones so my plan to pass her down my IPhone 3GS was not met with any enthusiasm. So how did I get her a new cellphone, one she likes, put it on the plan, and not extend my plan by another two years?This phone is the answer. First it's a clamshell. Second it is priced right. Third, AT&T; will put in a new SIM card for her family plan number. Finally none of this extends my existing plan should I want to switch providers (and I am not sure I do since AT&T; is getting better).Now please note that by installing a new SIM card, this becomes a regular cellphone on my plan. It is no longer a prepaid phone.The voice quality is quite good. It has a camera, which my wife is unlikely ever to use. It has what it calls "Apps" was are a few limited and unimaginative mini-programs. It can text, another feature my wife won't use, and has a means to download a few MP3s.An iPhone it's not. My wife can use it, and we can communicate, and that's all that really counts.
summary: A solution-painless replacement of a lost phone on a family plan

reviewText: Bought as a back up phone for my husband because he is a phone killer. Great buy, excellent price. Phone doesn't do much but makes calls and texts just fine!

I have one of these. Initially bought back when my original AT&T; Samsung Impression went kaput. I have now been on a smartphone kick, progressing from the MB860 Atrix 4G to the MB865 Atrix 2 (This was actually a downgrade from the 4G unfortunately, it sucked) and now onto the MB886 Atrix HD.Back onto the subject oof the A107:Call quality was good-to-excellent:Never dropped a call, others heard me loud and clear, hearing them was loud and clear as well. If I recall, this does have a speakerphone through use of the ear receiver.Features were poor/lacking:It was able to call and text, I'm not sure I remember ever being able to connect to the internet on it however. I know it's not an HSPA/EVDO device (3G) but I should have still been able to pull up a single page on Google or Yahoo, however that was not capable even on the 1X data connection.Reliability was excellent:The phone still works to this very day, it's never bugged out on me or not turned on or made a call when I wanted & needed it to.Ruggedness was excellent:I am notorious for dropping my phones. I have dropped this thing numerous times but it functions perfect, the only thing apparent is the scuffs and marks on the outside of the case.Battery life was excellent:I remember using this phone for days with plenty of talk and text going on and not having to charge it very often at all. When I did charge it, I'd charge it overnight (8~hours) and use it until it was about dead again. It would last for days though, I am positive on that.*Not sure about if you're seeing this at the $27 price I am now, but I can honestly say I'd hold off on it for that price. I got mine for $19 + tax in Wal-Mart years back.

These are $10 +$2 S&H; at Walmart's online store, $3 more in-store.The only way I found to import my contacts was by copying them onto my SIM card from an old phone.  No  software available from Samsung, no iSync support - even from third parties, nothing from Google or Yahoo.  (Please add a comment if you come across anything@)TIP: If you don't want to get charged for Internet usage ever, call up AT&T;, get a Customer Service Agent and tell them you want to block all data/Internet access.  They'll warn you that this will also disable MMS (Picture/sound/video messaging) but since you can't send such messages anyway, this is probably not a big deal.  **Now I don't have to worry about being charged every time I press the wrong button and it starts.**  I use my Verizon MiFi with my MacBook Pro, iPod or iPad for mobile 'net access.Service:I recommend the $2/day plan.  You can use this as a backup phone - make most of your calls from anywhere over the Internet (via wireless hotspot and iPod touch, smartphone with WiFi - e.g. most Android, iOS or Symbian phones.)  It's best to use with Google Voice ; my GV # is my main phone # that I give out.  If the 'net connection isn't on, this lets me know if anyone calls, or texts, and then I can take the call on this phone or on another device.  Texting from an iPad is a GREAT experience compared to any cellphone.Cell Phone:The phone very cheap and yet it is quite sturdy.  It's about the simplest phone you can buy. This phone just lets you make calls and send/receive text messages, plus a few tools like alarms and calculators. No headset jack, volume controls, camera, crash-prone operating system,  No time-sucking learning curve.Final Word:I generally don't use more than $25 per 3 months.  Plus, you can buy $25 cards at a discount if you shop around. The phone serves my needs and I am very satisfied with it.  But, smartphones are getting cheaper and cheaper...
summary: Cost only slightly more than just a SIM chip.

reviewText: I bought this phone as a step in porting my land line phone to Google Voice. (For some reason Google can only port cell phone numbers.) So first I port my home phone to this cell phone and then to Google. Details of this process are all over the web so I won't repeat them here. I didn't intend to really use it for calls which is a good thing because the phone is really cheap.This phone is almost unusable for voice calling. Don't get the idea that this is a good choice for anything but a backup to your backup phone used only if you were stranded on a desert island. I suppose it could be used by kids who mostly text since that part of the phone is pretty standard.Setup was simple following the instructions in the box. It did take at least 10 minutes to activate. it turns out to be only $0.10/min and $0.20/text. Probably heavy text users would go for one of the /day or /month plans. They seem to charge for everything but calling 611. For example, it looks like even if the phone is forwarded they charge for the call time.
summary: Maybe good kid phone for text msgs, but not much for voice

reviewText: Have had this phone now for almost 15 months.  Using it on PureTalk network.  So far it has worked throughout all central states and two west coast states without any problems.  Retains charge for over a week.  Calls using the PureTalk network are clear and easy to hear.  I am using this only as a phone....not for any other uses.  I use my ipad3 or itouch5 for internet use etc.... Just ordered another one for my wife since her 'full function' phone just will not hold a charge and since we have these cell phones to actually just make phone calls this samsung a107 works just fine.POSTSCRIPT:  Since so many folks are having problems with this phone......and I have had none with my 15 month old phone.... I will update this review IF I see any difference in the quality from my old phone to the new one that arrives next tuesday.UPDATE:  Just received the phone one day early.  It looks identical to the one I have that has been working flawlessly for the last 15 months.  I took the puretalk sim card out of my wife's old phone and bam it works!  If you are like me and have access to WIFI almost everywhere I go you can use this phone for  what a phone is for.  calling people.  If I want to stream HBO GO, Netflix, access itunes cloud etc.....I can wait the 15 minutes it takes me to be back into a WIFI free connection zone.  Which is just about everywhere you go.Please note I purchased this from Amazon not a 3rd party.
summary: Purchased this phone over a year ago.

reviewText: I love my Sprint HTC Evo 4G. It is, in my opinion, the best smartphone made to date. However, even with all kinds of tweaking, you're going to need a second (or even third or fourth) battery because this phone begs to be used heavily.This Seidio charger allows you to charge one battery in the phone and another in the detachable tray. You can power it with 110 VAC or from a USB port. I can't see doing the latter because it would take forever.The unit is simplity itself a relatively small box with folding prongs. The removable battery tray I mentioned earlier. And a switch on the side for choosing between 110 VAC and USB. My unit came with a USB to microUSB cable.Pop a battery in the tray, another in the phone and in a couple of hours or so, youhave two fully charged batteries.The unit weighs only a few ounces and packs very nicely.If you have an Evo 4G, you want an extra battery (or two or three) and this charger,Jerry

Found this charger which charges phone and separate battery together so I should never be without my phone ever again. It's still compact enough to carry in my bag when traveling or even just around town unlike those older counter top battery chargers: it's the size of an older pager. So far, pleased with charger. On a side note, unfortunately the usb cord that came with does not fit plug on phone. It's too small. Not sure how that happens but I have a few extra of my own so wasn't a big deal for me.

I bought this because of the reviews and it lasted about 9 months when it started to malfunction. first it started to take to long to charge and then the indicator light started to remain red after several hours of charging. then when it turned green and installed the battery it should half charged. I have six backup  batteries to charge and this worked great at the begining but the slacked off. My son bought a cheaper model from another maker almost a year and a half ago and it still works fine. wont be buying it again.

Excellent, so may electronic products are made in China (no offense) & all are not of good quality.  I intentionally bought a product made by Seidio, because that is a name I have learned to trust.  Seidio makes excellent quality products, I buy as many electronic & phone items from Seidio, because they ship quality items, & as picky as I am, I want quality, even if I have to pay just a bit more to get it.  I want it to work next week, next month, or next year at a minimum.

A necessary purchase if you have a smart phone and more than one battery.  I keep one battery in my phone and before it runs down I have charged another battery in the charger.  You can also charge the battery in the phone at the same time if necessary.  It does not get better.  I'm very happy with this item.

I wanted a wall charger so I could charge my extra battery separately from the one in my phone (HTC EVO 4G). I want to have a backup battery ready if needed on days when I'm out and about with no chance to plug in the phone anywhere for a recharge.I tried a cheap AC charger, but returned it; the contacts were flimsy and after hours plugged in, the battery wasn't even fully charged.This unit looks and feels like much better quality. It's not blazing fast but after a few hours plugged into the wall, the battery is fully charged. Its finish and performance far outshine the cheap five buck unit I tried, and at about twenty-three bucks it was still not ridiculously expensive.I haven't used the USB cord or setting, and don't think I will because I have my phone's OEM USB/AC cord and plug.
summary: You get what you pay for

reviewText: I had to return the first one I ordered since it stopped charging my HTC EVO phone after about a week.  So far the replacement is working but time will tell.

I have the droid incredible and I've tried the extended battery but I really didn't like the extra bulk. I got a spare regular battery and pop one into this so I always have a fully charged spare battery with me.  It works quickly and holds the battery well.

I wanted to use this for my wife, who lacks a bluetooth speakerphone in her vehicle.  The idea of this product is to connect it to your keychain, and then use it as a phone leash and a speakerphone.  We didn't really need it for the leash/cell phone alarm function for when you walk away from your cell phone, but I was intrigued by the idea of having a speakerphone that connects to your keychain.  The description lists this device as a "full functioned speakerphone" but that is not really the case.This is my fourth cell phone blue tooth device, so I am familiar with pairing devices.  Even so, it still took me 45 minutes to get this device paired with my cell phone.  In any event, once I was able to pair the device, I connected it to my keychain and started testing it.  The ZOMM unit vibrates prior to ringing; I couldn't find a way to change that even though my phone is set to ring tones only.  This seems counterintuitive to a device that is marketed as a speakerphone.  This is an issue to because the vibrating first reduces the time you have to answer a call before it goes to voicemail.  Not a huge issue, but worth noting.  Once a call comes in you push the center buttom once, and now you can chat via the ZOMM unit.  The quality is obviously less than what you would expect with a headset, or a full sized speakerphone, but it is adequate,What I found surprising is when I tried placing a call with the ZOMM unit paired up and turned on.  My call would only go through my cell phone even though the ZOMM was on and paired.  I went to the website and did some research and it turns out that you must push the ZOMM button WHILE YOUR OUTGOING CALL IS RINGING to transfer the call to the ZOMM device.  Why is this function not automatic when the ZOMM is marketed as a full function speakerphone?  I have another bluetooth speakerphone, a Plantronics K100 Bluetooth Speakerphone, that clips to my car visor that handles both incoming and outgoing calls automatically - I don't need to "route" the outgoing call to the speakerphone, which seems to defeat the purpose of hands-free dialing, especially when the ZOMM is connected to the keychain hanging from my ignition.  I don't want to place my call, listen for the ring through my phone, then reach for the ZOMM at my keychain/ignition, all while driving.  The k100 sells for about 50% less than the ZOMM.  I would recommend it or any similar product over the ZOMM if your primary need for this product is a bluetooth speakerphone.The ZOMM is quite small, and comes with a belt clip and a keychain.  If you want a leash to help prevent you from losing your phone, and can live with diminished speakerphone functionality, I guess this product is OK.  But for what it costs, I can't really recommend it as a a good value.

The setup was a breeze including the small downloaded program on my computer. I tested the connectivity to my iPhone. Seamless hookup.The alert for 30' was nice and you can set that to other smaller sets if you prefer. It also connected when I was within range but outside of my home. I liked that.The panic alarm is hideous. LOL I suppose it is supposed to be though. I did not test the emergency call feature.My son called me to test the speakerphone. He said that I sounded much clearer than when on my iPhone's speaker. I am hard of hearing but he came through crisp and clear. If I moved the device too far away (more than about a foot) I could not hear him.I would recommend this device to those who fear a stolen phone of losing one. I am not convinced that the speakerphone function is as useful as it might be.

This review is for the ZOMM Wireless Leash, Bluetooth Speakerphone, and Personal Safety Device for Mobile Phones (Black). I give this product 5 solid stars for the idea, but only 3 stars for execution. Actually, I would say that the problem isn't the fault of the makers, but rather of Bluetooth technology itself. Making Bluetooth connections is always a hassle, and I wish that someone would come up with a solution for this clumsy way of connecting devices. Overall, I have to recommend that you steer clear of the ZOMM Wireless Leash, Bluetooth Speakerphone, and Personal Safety Device for Mobile Phones.
summary: ZOMM Wireless Leash, Bluetooth Speakerphone, and Personal Safety Device for Mobile Phones (Black)

reviewText: useful and good design, too many theft on iphones and othet smart phones. Can be very useful under many circumstances.

Ok, great ideal to create a device that can detect your phone when lost or replaced.  The bad is execution of this device.  So, i have a bluetooth earpiece that i use alot, and this ZOMM device can't be connected to both.  Which means, if i have my bluetooth earpiece connected, my phone won't connect to ZOMM, which defeats the purpose of this little device. Additionall, the distance between the device and ZOMM is too far.  I wish you can setup a distance for the alarm to go off.

My wife has a tendency to lose things, so I thought this might be a useful device for her. Turned out that it was more of an annoyance than a help.The device setup is pretty simple, and the package comes with a power adapter and USB connector. The device functions as a bluetooth speaker that alarms when out of range of the phone, pretty basic. The problems my wife had with the device spring from that basic functionality - she uses the phone in her car with the auto's built in hands free setup, the ZOMM does not appear to understand silent ring mode on the phone. Ultimately, these annoyances were enough for her to hand it back to me.Also, when I think leash, I envision a tether that I can use to find the distant end, i.e. I expect to be notified that I have forgotten my phone and get some help finding it, similar to a keyring leash that helps me find my misplaced keys.I'm sure the speaker phone use might be useful to those without other bluetooth headsets or setups, but for me I cannot use this device without continuous attention. P-)
summary: Bluetooth speaker phone, and phone loss notification

reviewText: I was pretty excited to try out this product.  I'm a tech junkie and love trying out new products. The ZOMM seemed like a cool idea - a "leash" for your phone so that when you misplace it, you'll be able to find it.  Couple that with a speakerphone and a panic button, and it seemed like a really good idea.Well, the idea is much better than the actual product. First of all, if you want to use this device, you need to have the bluetooth on your phone turned on at all times. For my phone (Droid Incredible), that cuts the battery life in roughly half. That makes it a major pain to use, as I always need to make sure I have my phone charger with me.The ZOMM works pretty simply - attach it to your keychain, connect it to your phone, and you're set. Walk about 30 feet away from your phone with your ZOMM, and it starts beeping very loudly (and I mean LOUD!). It also functions as a speakerphone. Just press the button on the ZOMM to answer a call and use it as a speakerphone. The quality is nice (great wind reducing technology), but the problem is that it's always connected to my keychain. So when I'm in the car, my keys are obviously in the ignition, which is like 4 feet away from my mouth. So people say they have a hard time hearing me because I'm so far away.It also functions as a panic button.  I tried it once, and it wasn't very loud (the newer versions being shipped now are roughly 4 decibels louder than the original models). It just didn't seem like a very useful feature to me.I know these devices are marketed at busy mothers, which is maybe why I didn't find it to be all that useful. You do need <some> tech savvy to get it working, but not much. I suppose it can be handy for some, but I just found it to be frustrating to use.

Very neat and definitely does what it isays it will do. If you are far from your cell phone it will beep to alert you to go back and get it. It can also be used as a bluetooth and answer and make phone calls.

The ZOMM is a great idea but needs some work.For those looking for something that will help you locate your phone this is not for you. It will help you avoid leaving your phone when you leave work  (for example). It is definitely small enough to keep on your belt or keychain.Set up was a piece of cake on my Mac. The Mac software was actually Mac software and not a Windows port and it worked great. I particularly like how the emergency number can be changed from 911 to any number. My main concern with that feature was accidentally have the ZOMM dial 911, although doing so would take a lot of having the perfect condition.As for the device itself, it is disappointing as a speakerphone. The speaker on the device is very disappointing. I had to hold the device up to my ear to actually here without struggling. The speakerphone on my phone is a lot louder and better. In a car, as you can imagine, the sound is virtually unusuable.So, take that for what  you will and decide if it will work for you.
summary: Has potential and useful depending on your needs

reviewText: I purchased this because I was feeling very vulnerable, and because I have regularly left my keys or phone.Unfortunately the other bad reviews are right:It isn't loud enough for an alarm. It should have 2 volumes, the alarm it sets off when the phone is too distant and a separate louder alarm for emergencies.Also this uses bluetooth 1, the range of that type of bluetooth is 30ft, that is where they get this 30ft range from... I definitely do not get 30ft from it and it looses signal if things cross between it and my phone. I use a bluetooth headset that works so much better at this.I never could get this set up on my computer or the app on my phone, it works fine basically but if I want to set up the emergency phone # I can't. I *think* that is really the only thing I'd want to access on the computer or my phone BUT if there was a way to set this up with Locale or Tasker so that it would be quieter in certain locations/times when it lost connection or so it could be switched to vibrate only that would be great.I stopped using it after a few days, I had a meeting where the thing went off several times in a row before I turned it off. My phone and the zomm were right next to eachother.

Not a bad little gadget if you're always forgetting your phone going hither and yon.  Keep this on your key chain or in your bag and once you are separated from your phone you'll get a tone message. Pretty cool actually.  So, if you admit you are a forgetful type, try this.  A little bit bulky, but manageable.

According to the manufacturer, the Zomm is the "ultimate accessory" for a Bluetooth phone.  As a wireless leash, it lets you know when you've left your phone somewhere.  It also acts as a speakerphone and an emergency device.Depending on what your needs are, it's kind of a unnecessary device.  I use my Plantronics headset often, both in the car and at home for general use, and prefer it to using speakerphone.  Since my phone already has a speakerphone option, as most phones do, I don't see the point in purchasing an external speakerphone.  Also, since a headset is better for road use (and safer), again, an external speakerphone seems useless.  The Zomm is not a bad speakerphone - but I prefer my headset.The wireless leash option is kind of cool, but again, I think buying the Zomm for that feature depends on your needs.  Again, I find that feature sort of useless, since I always carry my phone with me and am very aware of where it is at any given moment.  Finally, the emergency option is a good idea, but you can always dial 911 on your phone.Overall, the Zomm is a nice product if you like the latest gadgets (or are maybe a tad forgetful), but I think for most people, it's not really a device that will enhance your phone usage in any way.

It works as advertized.  I bought it for my mother so she cal call me in emergencies.  She had too many falls and I cannot afford the monthly service.  Tech and Customer supports are great and they helped me step through changing the emergency number to call my number.

Overall, we just didn't like this item. It sounded like it had great promise and we were excited to try it...but the love just never materialized. We had issues setting up (connecting) the Bluetooth and once we had it set up the sound was sketchy at best--certainly nothing I'd want to have a long conversation over. I set off the safety feature just being in my purse. And after a few weeks we realized it was gone and neither of us had even noticed.Admittedly, had we not received this item for free via Amazon Vine, we would have definitely paid more attention to its whereabouts and kept a closer eye on it...but while we were using it, neither of us loved it so I think it says something that we didn't notice it was even gone.
summary: We lost it and didn't care about replacing it.

reviewText: Was missing half of what was supposed to be in package including instruction booklet. Went to ZOMM website and followed instructions and could never get the thing to do ANY of it's purported actions including making a noise when away from phone. ALso would have been nice as a Bluetooth Speakerphone but, as I said, this thing did nothing. So disgusted just threw the thing away and not bothering to return it

I got this to see if it would work with anything other than a phone (this isn't clear from the manufacturer's info), but it doesn't. This is just a tricky hands-free set, which simply puts together a very mediocre hands-free function with a couple of alarm functions.Since I don't have a bluetooth capable phone at the moment, I as not able to test that function, and I would not ask anyone else to switch over to this unit, as it appears to take over the bluetooth function and is difficult to switch back.However, I will test it again in the future and see if there is some reason to recommend it.

I've got two sisters and, as adults, they're both great to have in my life. As far as males are concerned, both of them have, how shall we put this politely, memory issues. One of them is a complete ditz who is constantly leaving behind something: a cell phone, a digital camera, a purse, you name it.Although this functions as a Bluetooth speaker phone, I got it as a gift for the aforementioned sister because of the "electronic leash" function. When this and her cell phone are separated by about fifteen feet (not thirty as the manufacturer claims), the alarm goes off. And that's great for her. It's helped her avoid losing a cell phone several times already.PS One of the reviewers claims that the speakerphone ringer always goes off during meetings, but you can program this device so that the alarm goes off only when it and the phone are separated, and not when there is an incoming call.Five stars because the thing actually works as advertised and performs multiple functions. Yes, it does work as a Bluetooth speakerphone. Yes, it does work as a wireless Bluetooth leash. And yes, it does work as a manual panic button.
summary: Great Gift For A Ditzy Yet Loving Sister

reviewText: I would have liked it if the range in which it warns was only about 5-10' because a thief would be way too far at 30.  Otherwise it's a good device that works as advertised.
summary: Nice to have but won't warn until you're about 30 feet apart.

reviewText: I forget my cellphone at home all the time and, when I do remember to take it with me, often have to answer it while driving. Neither is a particularly good thing and if you have the same issue then the ZOMM sounds like a godsend.It syncs with your phone via the bluetooth connection (which means you cannot use another blutooth device) and functions as a speakerphone while driving, alerts you if it is more than a certain distance from your cellphone, allows you to call 911 at the press of a button and emits an panic alarm if you need it to.I was able to sync the ZOMM to my phone with no problem at all. Changing the settings of my device (turning off the panic alarm which seemed just to easy to trigger in a crowded bag) was a little harder since I could not access the correct place on the website for a while.Biggest cons:This is no more than a bluetooth on a keychain. The speaker phone aspect when actually driving (which means the Zomm is swinging from your ignition) is not so good. Scratchy at best, indecipherable at worst.This thing needs to be charged regularly. Even more regularly than my phone. So, there have been plenty of times that I have waltzed out of the door sans phone since my ZOMM has run flat and so failed to function as a 'leash'. If it has a warning beep for when it needs charging, I have not heard it. Perhaps the next model needs a battery that holds a longer charge time??The price is way more than acceptable, in my mind, for something that promises much and delivers little.Pros:As a personal safety device, I suppose it replaces an Onstar system in case of an accident. Press a button and you can call 911 - as long as you have remembered to charge it, of course.It is tiny and light and clips on to your keychain without turning it into a monster mess.So, in my mind the pros do not stack up so well against the cons. My husband has a Jabra cruiser speakerphone in his car and it is a dream. You can get it on Amazon for just over $60. You can use it to call 911 and I would highly recommend the jabra cruiser2 as oppossed to the ZOMM.As to the wireless leash reminding me to take my phone - I think I'll revert to the stone age and put a sticky note reminder on my steering wheel. :)
summary: Promises so much, delivers so little.

reviewText: If you're the type of person who can't get it together long enough to remember your personal items when you leave the house, this Zomm Wireless Leash can be of great benefit to you.  Like the title of the product itself, it's a leash, so if you liken your intelligence to a canine who can't keep a thought together for more than two minutes, the Zomm will be your holy grail of electronics.  Ignoring that, though, and focusing on the product itself, it does exactly what it says.The device beeps when you are at least 30 feet away from your items in the event you should drive away and forget.  It also acts as a speakerphone, so if you leave your phone in another room while at home it would prove useful in this way.  The speakerphone function is probably the best feature as the sound is pretty clear when used.  The bluetooth functionality works fine, but make sure you check the abilities of your phone as it must be able to handle multiple bluetooth accounts at a time.  The belt clip it comes with seems to work fine, and it's not too intrusive.While it does all of these things, it also proves to be useless and cumbersome in several ways.  Firstly, this thing isn't small.  The image you see here on Amazon's page is scaled to its actual size.  So if you plan on cramming this on to your keyring, forget it.  It's as thick as five or six keys as well, so unless you enjoy walking around with a bulge in your pants (I'm sure many men wouldn't mind) it's just too bulky.  Also, this thing will need to be charged everyday.  It seems to die in a heartbeat, and it goes off indiscriminately at times.  Perhaps I received a defective product, but it will just randomly beep when the phone is literally two feet away, thus draining the battery.  I'm guessing that the people who are distracted enough to forget their phones on a regular basis are the ones who will want this thing, and those people aren't going to remember to charge items when they need charging.This is one of those products that will only speak to the right type of person.  Personally, this Zomm Wireless Leash is absolutely worthless to me.  Then again, I'm a thinker, and I don't forget important items when I leave home.  Additionally, I don't see a lot of purpose in this device.  The speakerphone function works, and the volume is clear, but do individuals really need yet another device to distract them when they're driving?  Is the Zomm really that important in situations like that?For those of you who need constant reminders to function through your day, and are specifically looking for a portable and sleek looking version of a cowbell for your phone, the Zomm is your answer.
summary: Usefulness depends on your own density

reviewText: This item is a neat little contraption.  I'm using it with an LG Voyager.  What I've discovered is that when it wants to notify you when your phone is out of reach it is very loud.  I gave it a 4 because calling it a speakerphone is stretching things a wee bit.  I found it to be irritating. Personal safety device?  Eh....that's stretching it a bit too.I can't say I'd suggest buying this unless you lose your phone a lot and think it might give you some peace of mind.

If you are forever forgetting your phone, this is the product for you.  When the leash feature is activated, the device will vibrate and sound an alarm when you & your keys get a prescribed distance from your paired phone.  Even when the leash feature is off, you will get an audible tone when it gets out of bluetooth range which is a less obtrusive way to do the same thing.When I am driving this allows me to answer the phone and talk through the speakerphone from the Zomm hanging on my keychain.  No more digging in my purse and risking a ticket or accident!I love the security of knowing I can either sound a panic alarm or initiate a 911 call from my car keys.You can charge the battery with the wall charger or from a USB port.  If you have a USB-cigarette lighter adapter for your car you can charge it on the fly too.  Zomm sells a car kit that includes such an adapter.What I'd change if I could:1.  I wish the leash could be turned on or off through the device.  Instead you have to plug it into the computer where you registered it and activate the change there.2.  I wish it used a mini USB rather than a micro USB connection so the fistfull of spare cables I have from other devices would fit.3.  Somehow put the speakers either on the side or on the top rather than the back.  If you hold the device to push the button, you tend to cup it in your hand and cover the speaker on the back.  You have to make a conscious effort to hold it by the chain or the sides to avoid completely muffling the audio.If the phone and Zomm are out of range briefly, they will disconnect and then reconnect when back in range, with a beep each time to let you know what your status is. If they are out of range for a long time (say I go for a walk and take the phone but not my keys) I will likely have to re-pair the bluetooth when I return.  This also happens if either the Zomm or my phone battery runs out.  The blue lights on the Zomm flash in various combinations to notify you if it is properly connected to your phone and it has an audible tone to remind you when the battery is getting low.All in all, it is a totally cute and useful device that is the envy of all my friends and co-workers.
summary: I wish my boss had one of these...

reviewText: When you see the ZOMM Wireless Leash in its box, it looks really cool and sleek. When you open it up, handle it and start to configure it, you realize it's pretty flimsy and overpriced for what it does.It works the way it says it does. If you end up more than 30 feet away from your phone, the ZOMM starts losing it's cool to let you know. It would be nice if the distance was customizable - for instance, I'd rather have it set up to go off when I get 50 feet away from my phone, rather than 30. Not a huge deal, but just know that it's not customizable at all.As a Bluetooth speakerphone, it has worked as intended thus far. The sound quality isn't the greatest, but it works. There is also a personal safety function where if you hold the Z button for 9 seconds a loud panic alarm sounds, and if you keep holding it, emergency services are called. Thankfully we haven't had to try this feature out, so I cannot tell you if it works as intended. It is a nice "peace of mind" feature to have. Again, I wish this was customizable. If it were up to me, I would lower this to 5 seconds before the panic alarm sounded, as sometimes you don't have 9 full seconds to wait in an emergency situation.My other main problem with the ZOMM is it just doesn't seem to be built to last. I don't feel overly confident carrying this on my keys, as it seems like one hard bump and it will stop functioning. Still, it has worked as intended thus far. At the current retail price, the ZOMM should be more customizable and less flimsy. Still, if you need it, it seems to work as intended.
summary: Functions, but flimsy and considerably overpriced

reviewText: Broke after 3 days.  Got it replaced.  Broke after 2 days.  Trash.  Just don't buy it.  Oh... it looks cool!

I was ready to totally pan this device in my review and then they came out with a new companion app for Android. This app fixes some of the major shortfalls. You can now change the device settings and mute it for the times when you are someplace that you need the device to remain silent. You can also look on a map to see the last approximate location that the Zomm was still connected to your phone via Bluetooth. It still has some limitations that you can go read about but these are good improvements. There is still one thing that I don't like about the device and that is the sound quality. People tell me I don't sound good and they don't sound good to me either. This is probably more of a size / power limitation inherent to the device. Maybe the Zomm 2 could be a little bigger and improve things a bit. So with the recent app and all this might be a device that is worth checking out if it meets some of your needs. I have to give them credit for working to improve things. I just wouldn't use it as a primary speakerphone type device.

Honestly, I'm surprised that the Zomm is getting so many bad reviews. It is a pretty straightforward device that does exactly what it says in the description.Setting it up with my phone was straightforward. You press the main center button for a bit until it blinks and then tell your phone to find it. If you have ever set up any BT device, it's pretty much the same. After that it's "mated" with your phone.I think the best way to review it is a simple list of pros and cons:Pros:If the Zomm and your phone are separated by more than about 30' the Zomm sounds a *loud* *annoying* alarm. You will know that your phone is not nearby.Set up is easy, like any other BT device.Has a standard microUSB charging port so it will be easier to find places to charge that. (see Cons)Cons:Battery life only lasts about two days (max). If you're the type that always forgets your phone in places, hopefully you're better at remembering to keep things charged.If your phone doesn't support multiple BT devices and if you also use a BT headset, the Zomm won't be able to work with your phone too. Fortunately, many (most?) modern phones support multiple connections. You should check yours before purchasing though.The panic alarm function works and is loud but if you have to hold down the main button for a long time. If you're in an emergency and have enough time to wait then you're probably not in a real emergency.______________________________________________Some other customers said that they had problems with the Zomm going off even if it was in their pocket and only separated by their body. I did not experience this. Perhaps it has to do with the strengths of the phone's BT signal?Unfortunately, I have not had the need to really test the speakerphone feature. It worked well enough in a quiet room but I haven't had a chance to test it in a vehicle.As I mentioned earlier, the alarm is loud and annoying and abrupt. I wish it had a graduated volume that increased every few seconds.If you leave separate your phone and the Zomm intentionally, a simple press of the Zomm's button mutes it until it detects your phone again. Since my keys and phone rarely are separated this is nice for me. If you are constantly finding your keys in one place and your phone in another, it might become too much of a habit to just mute the alarm when you really have forgotton your phone.
summary: Does what it says but is it what you need?

reviewText: The Zomm has a lot of potential to make a great niche device.  Speakerphone is decent for the size of the device and could use it my car as a speakerphone.However it does not trigger voice commands via Bluetooth on my android ver. 2.2 device or my iPhone device so you cannot use it to make voice activate calls from the Zomm. Some phones will allow multiple pairings of BT devices but not simultaneously connections of identical profiles without actively switching between the Zomm and your BT headset in the phone's menu system.  So, Zomm really needs to make this device capable of initiating calls via bluetooth if you cannot use a BT headset simultaneously.I also found that many times if I chose to use the device a speakerphone particularly on a call I initiated it would frequently drop connection with my phone and I would have to reconnect by making a single depress of the Zomm button.  Generally after two BT connection drops the Zomm would then stay active during the call, however the individual on the other end maybe irritated with you by then.I rating this device 2 stars because it has some quirks that make it difficulty to adopt usage consistently.  And the time when you cannot use this device because you need a bluetooth headset capability to initiate reliable phone calls will be the time you misplace your phone.

I am always forgetting where I put my phone down or forgetting to take it with me, which is why I was very interested in theZOMM Wireless Leash, Bluetooth Speakerphone, and Personal Safety Device for Mobile Phones (Black).  However, this product simply did not meet my expectations for the following reasons:1. I often turn off my phone when I am at home or when I lose my phone the battery often goes dead. The ZOMM only works when the cell phone is on.2. When I am at work I don't want to take both my phone and keys into a meeting. As soon as I leave my office, the ZOMM alarm starts sounding.  I want something that alerts me only when I want to be alerted.3. I don't want to use a speaker while  on my cell phone. You think people look strange talking into a bluetooth headset, what do you think they look like speaking and listening to their keyring?4. With four kids and a very full purse, I am just sure the "emergency button" is going to be pushed unintentionally and 911 will be called.For all these reasons I found this product to be unusable.

I've had this device for several weeks now, and I really wanted to like it. I wanted this device to shift from the gadget role into something handy and more mainstream, but it falls short. I'll talk about the good first. The "leash" role works pretty well. If you walk away from your phone, it goes off and it's a pretty loud sound too. It was fairly easy to setup on the computer and connecting to my phone which is an LG banter touch.Now onto some of the issues. The first is it sucks as a portable speaker/headset. People can hardly hear me, and I can't really hear them either. It's just awful in this area so this dual role is pretty much useless. It has a habit of setting off the alarm multiple times even after I basically told it to stop which brings us to the next part of the problem, it's one button design. It just doesn't work. Maybe after a year of solid use, using the push once in this situation and push twice in that situation will become second nature to me, but for me, this device is not meant to be used that often because, as I said above, the headset functionality is terrible. They should have just added another small button or two and just simplified the process. Another problem is the battery life. I don't know if it ever does anything besides stop "beating" when the battery is dead. You can glance down and check the lighted "N" to see if it is connected and working with the phone, but during a busy day or even week, I'll forget to look. When I do look, it's dead. I have no idea how long it's been dead, but the battery life seems pretty poor.I think this was an interesting idea, especially the leash part which works okay, but it falls short for the mainstream crowd and is really only something I think the gadget persona is going to love. I like gadgets; I do, but I am not so into gadgets that I collect a lot of them so this was just not for me.
summary: Half the Advertised Features Fall Short

reviewText: My husband was woken at 2 a.m. because this thing was going off.  A week later the same thing happened to me.  I tried testing this in the house but it wouldn't go off when on the same floor.  I am a forgetful person and will obsessively check my pockets, hands, wallet for missing debit cards, IDs, and my phone when leaving anywhere while I'm out of the house, so I thought this would be perfect for me.  It doesn't go off for me right away and I worry someone will snatch my phone in busy areas before the device goes off and I have a chance to go back.  Thankfully I haven't needed this things help much at all because I obsessively check multiple times.
summary: Don't separate this from your phone at night!

reviewText: These make great gifts as they are "gadgets." They do everything as described and quite well I might add, people who received them said that they loved the function. It has helped one of them who almost left the house without their phone, another who misplaced their phone in the shed. The bluetooth speaker function also works quite well in the car while driving. I bought 4 total, two white and two black.

Anyway I was able to replace it at the cost of 699 and was looking for ways to protect my investment (and no I have not had dropped call issues on my phone) ... So I went with the best buy 15 dollar a month insurance .... Which covers pretty much everything but a lost phone .... While the geek was setting me up for that I spotted this on the rack and asked him about it ... Anyway he really didn't know how it worked so I went home and checked it out ... It's pretty simple a Bluetooth speaker that beeps loud when it looses it's connection (which is why you can not set the distance for the alarm) ... It works well and has reminded me a couple of times that I was leaving my phone at home when leaving for work .... Overall a pretty nifty little thing worth it if you have dropped some bucks on your phone ...UPDATE - i hate this thing - it starts beeping at any random time ... ie the MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT ... WTF???

reviewText: The Zomm device sure did sound great on paper/website. A tether alarm for my phone or other mobile device, and the added benefit of a speakerphone and safety device. All of the features work as stated. But I've found it to be more hassle than anything. Keeping it charged. Running upstairs with my phone (but without my keys) causes the alarm to go crazy unless I turn it off. The safety feature requires long presses of the button, so it may be too late. And my main complaint is the lack of ability to edit settings - distances from device and button press activities. Hopefully Zomm improves upon its device and software, but for now, I find the device to be a nice keychain and not much more.
I had this for about 3 month. Then I drop my keys and it Brock. It nice and it worked good. but once u drop it. that the end of it.

I love the case but like the other reviews the picture is misleading. The color on the phone shows like a greyish brown, looks nothing like this pic. I think that maybe the white or "clear" argyle cover would resemble this pic more. The case is sturdy and not bulky, my favorite of the three I ordered on Amazon. All in all a great buy just don't get it for the "fashion" aspect as the color my not look like the picture.
