You can probably buy batteries with a higher capacity.PROS: camera, features, speed of 3g/4g, network seems strong, screen size, phone size, kick stand, hdmi port, charger doubles as a usb data cable, camcorder, dual flash that doubles as a flashlight, you can get flash on the internet, memory card is included, access to 50,000 plus appsCONS: battery life, phone seems slippery to me, $10 premium for 4g weather or not the area you live in has it.

This is a beautiful phone, both physically as well as the User Interface. I would even go so far as to say it is THE best looking and functioning Android phone available on the market today from any carrier. And yet I am returning this handsome beast this week and switching to an uglier (in my opinion) Droid X with its clunkier Moto-whatever cartoony interface.All because of one culprit - battery life. Not once in the last 3 weeks that I've had this phone has it lasted a whole day on a single charge. I tried everything; Juice Defender, Advanced Task Killer, manually shutting off services when not needed, wiping out all of my home screens, turning off account sync, never using 4G, turning down brightness until I can barely see anything, etc. Everything short of getting an extended battery (which are currently too bulky/ugly in my opinion). Its not like I got a dud, since my wife got an Evo too (I went Black and she went White), and the experience has been near identical.If you have the luxury of always having an electric outlet at your disposal (even while on business trips, conventions, conferences, vacations, etc. when you actually find yourself using your smartphone the most), or, if you don't mind getting a bulky/ugly 3500mAh extended battery, then there really isn't any excuse not to get this phone. Neither works for me, so I'll have to say goodbye.Pros and Cons follow.Pros:1. This phone is beautiful. And that's an understatement. All eyes on you when you're using it in the office or in public transit. Curves are all in the right places (no humps like the Droid X). Nice smooth expanse of glass in the front (no plastic buttons like the Droid X). Nice touches of red. Many a time I've stopped what I was doing to just pick the phone up and admire it.2. HTC Sense UI is fantastic. Smooth flow, pleasing fonts, beautiful colors and shadows. Excellent collection of good-looking widgets. I generally mod my smartphone themes extensively since I'm rarely happy with the out of the box experience. But this thing is just beautiful. I played around with the Droid X at the Verizon store, and its interface pales in comparison. It looks cheap and cartoony. I understand that the Moto version is closer to stock Android, but I'm not so much a purist as I am someone who likes things to look good. I do suspect that Sense has some not-so-small role to play in the battery life on the phone. A lot of folks have reported insane improvements to their battery life by custom-romming their phones. But then Evo owners in general tend to overstate their actual battery times, so take anything you read from them with a pinch of salt.3. 4G speeds are insane. I have a very strong 4G signal at home (Burlington MA), and downloads just whiz past at 3Mbps. But I did find myself using it less and less (see Cons below). 4G would be invaluable if you have a strong connection at home and are considering tethering it to a PC / laptop to make it your primary internet connection. Provided of course that you live alone (since anyone else would be disconnected when you aren't home), this would totally work.4. Video calling. This isn't mature yet in my opinion, since my few attempts with Qik have been far from satisfactory. Half of the calls one of us had no audio (both using Evos), and it was very poor whenever one of us had no 4G. This is just a software issue I imagine, and should soon be rectified by better apps. But at least the hardware (front-facing camera) already exists should the right software come along.5. SWYPE! Yes, this gets an entire bullet point. The latest software update brings Swype to Evo handsets. Its made my decision to leave the Evo even more difficult (though Droid X has it too). Try Swype and you can never go back - it truly changes the way you type.6. 8MP Camera and 720P Video recording. I don't count MPs as indicators of camera quality. My actual experience with video recording has been good, and still photos 'OK'. I find phones inching closer and closer to point-and-shoots in quality, though they're not quite there yet. I carry a DSLR with me whenever I plan to take photos, so I'd never use a phone for still photos anyway. For video recording, its pretty good, and can easily replace a digital camcorder.7. Screen size at 4.3-inches is perfect for most things you'd use a smartphone for. Web browsing is very good in landscape mode. You can also actually start to enjoy videos at this size. I feel that 800x480 is the perfect resolution for a device of this nature.8. Its an Android device! I saw a remote desktop application called PocketCloud in the Market and my love for this device instantly doubled. I have to go through a complicated Corporate VPN system to access my mail and other work systems, so this gives me so many more situations where I can just leave my laptop hooked up at home or at work. 800x480 is also a very workable size for RDP. Its like having a tiny laptop running XP in your hands. 4.3-inches of real estate is also essential for using the virtual mouse that comes with PocketCloud. Of course, I don't stay connected longer than 5-10 minutes at a time for fear of draining out the battery on the Evo, but its still a big deal.Of course, there are dozens of other pros with this super-phone and I could go on and on. But a lot of others already have. So I'll stop here and switch to the Cons.Cons:1. The Battery life sucks! There's no nice way to say this. Coming from a Nokia XpressMusic 5800 that was also capable of full-GPS and 3G web browsing, but could still last 2 days with very heavy use and a week(!) with moderate to low use, to say that the battery life on the Evo was a shock is an understatement. When I use this phone heavily I need to charge it THREE times a day. If I don't use it at all, it still threatens to shut down by nightfall. Short of custom-romming the phone, I've done everything in my power to extract a few additional hours from this phone, and failed. I knew of poor battery life before going in, but the scale of poorness was still not expected. I also see a lot of Evo owners misguiding others by quoting unrealistic numbers ("I got 27 hours with moderate use!", "I rarely use the phone and I can get by 3 days without a charge"). After combing through the forums and following every advice I found on both my and my wife's Evos, I must say that these people either got experimental super-batteries, or they're just making things up to evoke envy. Also, the Evo's battery charge indicator isn't perfectly linear. It stays most of the time between 30% and 70%. It drops quickly from 100% to 70% and very very very quickly from 30% to 5%. The phone shuts off within 15 minutes of the 5% warning, even if you do nothing to the phone. I really love this phone, but I could not imagine spending the next 2 years constantly worried about being stranded somewhere with a dead phone whenever I check e-mail or use the GPS. That's a deal-breaker in my book. Super-phones need to come with super-batteries. If HTC came up with a battery with 50% more juice without altering the form factor too much, I'd switch back.2. The camera makes contact with whatever surface you place it on. This makes it essential to get a case. Fortunately there are several good looking inexpensive cases out there for the Evo. The camera also adds to the unique looks of this phone so much that I probably wouldn't change anything even given a choice.3. One of the side effects of combing the forums looking for battery extending tips, was the finding that a disproportionately large number of people cracked their Evo screens or the plastic at the top of the phone, by seemingly minor falls. I can imagine how I'd feel if my $500 phone slipped from my hand/pocket on to the carpet and shattered its screen. User reports indicate that the Droid X is much more resilient to drops. The first few days I had the Evo I did not have a screen protector yet. So I was very careful not to put coins or keys in the same pocket. Only once I forgot and dropped a key into the same pocket. The result was a tiny (4mm) hairline scratch. Not very noticeable, but its there.4. 4G implementation on the phone is far from ideal. If you need to download something specific quickly, or if you need a short tethering session, that's great. But if you use 4G longer than an hour, the handset starts heating up very quickly, and the battery drains out completely within 2-3 hours. I suspect that the heating is related to the rapid battery drain rate, but its disturbing nevertheless.5. I don't have 4G coverage at work, and even the 3G coverage is spotty. They're both very strong at home, but one of the main reasons for wanting a smartphone was so I could access my personal mail from work. This is nothing against the phone though. It doesn't even say anything about Sprint, since I'm sure Verizon has some spots where Sprint is much stronger too (I believe this is more so in the west). It just means that for my particular situation, Verizon 3G is probably better than Sprint 4G.Returning this phone is one of the hardest decisions I've made in a while, but one that I believe must be made. My wife even reported feeling envious of the last longing looks I've been giving the phone the past few days :)If you're on the fence between an Evo and a Droid X, I suggest you try the Evo first. Sprint has an amazing 30-day return policy. So amazing in fact, that I'm actually feeling guilty about taking advantage of it.Since the phone is married to Sprint, I think a few notes about Sprint are warranted as well:1. My relationship with Sprint got off on a bumpy start. I ordered through the online Sprint Store (so I would have control over entering coupon codes like SAVE50, and so I could easily apply employee discounts as well). I expected the plan to start from my activation date. But I was surprised to find it actually starts from my order date! So though I ordered on 11/22, received my phones on 11/29 and activated them on 12/1, my billing started from 11/22. For a $130 monthly bill, that represents an unnecessary loss of at least $32.50. However, in Sprint's defense, I chose the wrong time to order - the Tuesday before Thanksgiving. If you order by Wed morning during a typical week, you should get the phones within 2 days. Also, Verizon just did the same thing when I ordered through them (i.e. starting billing from the order date). But they shipped overnight, so I only get billed for one extra day.2. Sprint ported over my wife's number several days before her phone got here, meaning she was left with no phone for a few days. This was more than a minor inconvenience, since she was expecting several important calls. We later found that this happens fairly frequently and the best bet is to order the phones as new lines and port them after they arrive.3. Except for poor 3G/4G connectivity at my workplace on the 16th floor, I've had no other issues regarding connectivity. Voice calls were never an issue.4. Cancelling the account with Sprint was super easy. No one caused any trouble. We weren't even asked why we wanted to cancel. Just remember to both cancel your account and initiate the return of your phones within the 30 day period (which starts from your order date). If you miss either step, you might find yourself with a bill for the ETF.5. Overall, Sprint represents tremendous value. Especially when you get a discount through your employer, but even if not. The fact that you have unlimited mobile-to-mobile calling irrespective of the called-party's carrier is a big deal. Even after paying an extra $20 for 4G (two of us) we were still hard-pressed to find a plan from any other carrier at the same cost for similar benefits.
summary: Best phone I ever had - But I had to return it

reviewText: So I have had this phone for about a month now.  I haven't even touched most of the functions b/c I just use it for internet access and music during commute times etc.  However, my son loves watching Phineas and Ferb on it even though we have a giant LED tv at home.Overall, very easy to use and responsive.  I live in SF so we don't have 4g yet but to be honest, downloads and uploads are pretty fast regardless for someone like me.  Screen is very responsive and I like the 7 customizable home screens and folders etc.  Froyo has made start up about 50% faster as well.My only complaint is what everyone else says, battery life.  I am lucky to get a full day out of it.  I was hoping Froyo would help prolong battery life but oh well.Overall, great phone, I like the screen and functionality.  I am anti Iphone b/c I don't like that everything they do is proprietery.  This is a better phone regardless (Check out Cnet's comparison)

I took a risk from jumping from the iPhone 3GS to the Evo.  I really thought the iPhone was an excellent phone, but it pales in comparison the Evo and to the Android OS in general.  While most settings in the iPhone are set in stone, the Android powered Evo allows the user to make the phone extremely personalized in each and every way, from custom operating systems, to different keyboard layouts, one-touch navigation directions, video chat over cellular network, custom widgets, and on and on.  One could write a book on advantage of Android vs iOS, but in short, the iPhone OS is simply a page of apps, whereas the Android's OS is so much more, making the phone experience more personal, more fun, and more productive.  Two key disadvantages in the iPhone vs EVO battle: The clarity of the iPhone's retina display is purely unmatched.  When you zoom in on HD pictures and take a close look, the iPhone is by far clearer and sharper than any other device.  The 2nd disadvantage is battery life.  Evo's battery drains fast due to the more complex Android OS and the Evo hardware power requirements.  While the iPhone can stay charged during normal usage for 2-3 days, count on recharging the Evo before the end of your 8-hour day.If you are comparing the Evo to other Android powered devices, you'll want to consider both hardware and software specs.  The key competitor between the Evo and other Android phones is Verizon's Motorola Droid X.  In terms of hardware, the Evo's huge 4.3" HD screen is unbeatable, and only matched by Motorola.  This larger screen makes typing on the virtual keyboard much more accurate and easier to use than smaller screens.  A very similar typing experience to the 4.3" screen of the Moto Droid X, but because the Evo's shape is smooth and continuous, unlike the glaring protrusion of the camera on the back of the Droid X, the Evo both looks and feels better in this department than the Droid X and any other phone.  The Evo also has the awesome 8.0 MP camera, capable of taking the most stunning HD pictures, turning you into a semi-professional photographer.  The 1 GHz processor and 512 MB of memory makes the Evo a very sharp, crisp, and lag-free phone.  Of course, if you wanted more power, the Android OS lets you unleash the nerdy side of you, and work on things like custom operating systems and overclocking.Comparing the software side of the Evo to other Android devices, the key ingredient here is HTC's home screen launcher they call HTC Sense.  This home screen launcher is what sets HTC devices apart from other Android phones, in terms of look and feel of the phone.  I have compared HTC Sense with the likes of Samsung's Touch Wiz, and the custom Launcher Pro.  Overall, I adore HTC sense because of it's extremely useful, simple, and well decorated widgets, and dock at the bottom of the screen.  Again, thanks to the open-source of Android, you can always tinker and play around with home screen settings and different home screen launcher apps to make the experience exactly fitting to you.As for the Sprint network, I personally have been extremely satisfied overall.  One thing that is hard to swallow is Sprint's $10/m charge for 4G, even if you don't use it.  Right now, 4G is so spotty, that unless you are in a well covered area, the 4G actually DECREASES the phone's speed because it gets bogged down with trying to retain a weak connection.  However, in a well covered area, the speeds area amazing at around 4 mbps and under 100 ms ping times.  When 4G isn't available, the 3G coverage is reliable and fast.  When I was making the jump from AT&T;, I considered Verizon and Sprint, and ultimately chose Sprint because of much better pricing.  Under their family plan, you can select 2 lines for $129.99 and be sure that you will never go over thanks to unlimited mobile-mobile calling, texting, and web data.  Of course, that doesn't include the $10/m mandatory extra charge for 4G.  Even with that, Verizon's plan would set you back around $170/m if you were to get unlimited calling among 10 favorites, which is almost a must to have since their included minutes are so few.For me, I am glad I made the switch, and I am much more impressed with the Evo than I ever was with the iPhone.
summary: Switched from iPhone and not regretting it

reviewText: I've had my EVO for a couple of months now.  I had my land line disconnected and bought a Bluetooth device (Nuvelli) that connects all my former land-line phones to my EVO so I can answer my cell from any regular phone in my home regardless of where the EVO is.  I am also using the Hot Spot for all my WiFi devices, including my TV--Netflix streaming is seamless with the 4G network and I've never see it stop to buffer as it occasionally did with the DSL modem.  In Chicago, I was paying more for my land line + DSL modem than I am now paying for my EVO with Hot Spot (plus I have all the phone options like caller ID, call-forwarding, voicemail, etc., for free with the EVO).  I loved saying "Goodbye" to AT&T.  The EVO is still amazing me after two months.  I use the TeleNav system and it is far better than the GPS system I was using (it needed a costly upgrade to be up-to-date, so I saved on that, too); my older system did not have real-time traffic warnings, nor did it show me the speed limits of every road I was on, nor did it warn me when I was approaching a traffic camera).  The ability to use the Internet to find a place that is not listed in the usual "Places" listings, click on "Map It" and have the option to use the TeleNav system to route me to the place I just found on the Internet is amazing.  The EVO has replaced two other, more costly and less efficient, devices I was using:  MiFi and Internet access using Sidekick.  With MiFi, I had to constantly check the number of MB I had used to be certain I had not gone over my monthly limit.  The Internet access with Sidekick was an inferior platform that was 3G slow.  The Internet access with EVO is fast and it does everything I can do with Windows--including the use of multiple windows.  The camera takes pictures that are every bit as good as my 10 megapixel digital camera, it takes great video, and it is so easy to send pictures from the EVO.  I also use a free app for my grocery list, keep track of all those little key ring cards with another free app that replaces those tags altogether, and can download coupons to my grocery card while I'm shopping--when I check out and they scan the card (on my phone), all the coupons automatically show up on my register ticket.  I also schedule my TV programs from a DirectTV app and can order the pay-per-view using the same app without having to call.  Everyday I find something new to love about my EVO.  This is the first device that has made me feel like I really am living in the 21st Century.  With the Bluetooth connectivity, who knows what it will be able to control tomorrow?

The HTC EVO 4G from Sprint is one of the newest phones to come with the Android Platform. With a 4.3" LCD and the coveted 1Ghz Snapdragon processor, it is a hefty competitor in the smart phone market. With over 15,000 apps to choose from you can rest assured that the giddy feeling you get from a new device will not end soon. Having owned the phone for almost two weeks, I can provide a good review on what to expect from the HTC EVO 4G.PROSIt has 4G: This is a first in the smart phone industry. Sprint has been touting its ever expanding 4G network but has never had a phone enabled with 4G to use it with until now, and let me say that the differences in speed are enormous. Downloading on Sprints 3G network hit around 1.0 mb/s, Upload 256 k/s. Downloading on Sprints 4G network hit around 3-4 mb/s and, Upload 1-1.4 mb/s! I took a pic of one of my Speedtests, you can find it in customer images.It's huge: With the 4.3" LCD display taking up most of the face of the phone, you will be surprised on how big the phone is. Tons of room to work with and movies look great. I can also add that the phone is a little thick and has a very firm and heavy feeling. (Good build quality)Responsive: Out of the box you will see that the phone is extremely responsive to even the tiniest touches on the screen, but seems to block out accidental tabs with the edge of your finger which actually makes the phone a lot more easier to use. Apps load in less than a second and the pre installed apps almost always load up instantly.8 Megapixel Camera: The camera is great. See an example picture in the customer images that I posted (Look for two geckos!)Front Facing Camera: The front facing camera takes fantastic pictures and has a very good looking video quality when used for video chat.720P HD Video: Recording at 720P at 25FPS, it takes surprisingly good video for a camera phone. Check out YT for a plethora of example videos (If you type in "htc evo test video spacebears" in the searchbar and view the first video that is a fantastic example of the video quality)Video Chat: The video chat is simply great, it can be used over 3G or 4G and is very responsive and not sluggish at all.Mobile Hotspot: For 29.99 a month you can turn your phone into a 4G hotspot. The data speeds are extremely fast and you can connect up to 5 devices at once.Kickstand: It's AWESOME. Doesn't let the phone fall over and is very sturdy. Don't expect it to break off.The monthly plans are cheap(er): Ranging from 69.99 to 99.99 for the Simply Everything Plans, you will most likely pay less over other carriers with similar features. But don't forget the 10 dollar premium data fee.CONS4G not in all areas, premium data fee mandatory: Currently Sprints 4G network is limited to around 25 major cities, but it is expanding continuously and hopes to cover 120 million people by the end of the year. Also if you order the HTC EVO 4G you will be subjected to a mandatory ten dollar premium data fee even if you aren't covered with 4G. Supposedly the funds are going toward improving and expanding the 4G network.The microphone sounds bad: The audio sounds like it is in mono and picks up a lot of background noise. No external mic port. Don't expect to be Vlogging with this anytime soon. (Firmware update may improve sound)UPDATE: Due to recent ROM updates, battery life has improved tremendously!Battery Life: Simply put, it sucks. You will need an extra battery if you are a road warrior. I can get through the 9-5 day without having to charge but I almost immediately have to plug it in by 6-7 o clock with normal use. Expect around 4-5 hours of HD video and around 12 hours if you use the phone simply for calls. Normal use you can expect around 8-9 hours. The good news is the knock off e-bay batteries are cheap.It's waitlisted: This phone has been waitlisted ever since it came out so good luck finding one!The HTC EVO 4G is simply a great phone and should be seriously considered if you are in the smart phone market :D
summary: Best 4G and Android phone on the market

reviewText: Ok, first off if your about ready to buy this phone and your coming here for Amazon's reviews then do yourself a favor and buy it right here after you've read the reviews.  I purchased mine here and was amazed at the price and service.  I ordered it at 4:00 pm on a Wed and had it Fri with no issues.  I don't know why people continue to buy phones from the providers especially the ones like Sprint who continue to insist on making the customer deal with mail in rebates to get to their special price.  Like I told the Spring store guy, I can go down the road and buy it at Best Buy and get it for the final after rebate price or I can go online and get it even cheaper.So I am moving over from AT&T; and an Iphone 3G.  You really have to go up to an Iphone 4 before you can really compare to an Evo but while the Iphone 4 has some new features and better hardware the overall experience is exactly the same.First off the main reason why I'm switching is AT&T.;  They have the highest prices of all carriers and the worst service.  With the move to Sprint I'm dropping my cell phone bill by about $30 and getting more minutes.  AT&T; banked too much on their exclusive Iphone contract.  Yes they have a millions of people locked into contracts but we will see how the Verizon Iphone affects their business in the long run.  Hopefully Verizon doesn't make the same mistake, AT&T; never really addressed the network issues that arose from the millions of Iphone that suddenly got put on it with unlimited data (broadband speeds my butt).Apple, well they designed an amazing device and if it weren't for Android there still would be nothing in its class.  The only other maker that really took a poke at them as far as I know was Palm with the Pre and it was a poor attempt from a failing company.  The software was poor and the hardware was junk.  Oh, I guess maybe Blackberry with the Touch but it was only the look, it was still more of a business phone.  The thing that always bugged me about Apple was that they didn't want to let me do with what I wanted with the phone I purchased and owned.  Thanks Steve, but I can really take it from here.  I also didn't like the whole Iphone 4 signal fiasco.  There is no problem with the phone, your just holding it wrong, here is a free case to protect you from yourself.  Have another drink of the coolaide, everything is fine, you love our stuff.Ok, on overall polish the Iphone has the Evo (really Android) beat hands down.  Apps from the same company like Facebook are just done better on the Iphone.  Maybe they just need time like they had on the Iphone, who knows.  Since I have released the Iphone from the case that has protected it well over the last 2 years it just feels good in your hand.  The Evo is a little big, granted it went straight from the box to a case of its own.They Iphone from day one was just slow on data.  Even on wifi on blazingly fast broadband it was just slow rendering pages and getting data.  I never understood why, but tethered to a laptop the speeds were more what I would expect.  For that reason I never used it much for web surfing, it was quicker to fire up the laptop.  The Evo doesn't have that problem.  While still not as fast as a computer, its pretty darn fast.Here is where I am different from everyone else.  I have had no issue with battery life.  The Evo has been off the charger for 9 hour now.  Granted I have not made any calls but I have been playing with it and installing apps non stop and it still has 50% charge left.  Mine shipped with Android 2.2 which I have heard is better on batteries.  I did not change any factory settings, it came with bluetooth, 4g and wifi off.  I turned wifi on but thats it, there isn't 4g within 100 miles of here.  I think it may be better on the battery than the Iphone 3g.  I do think the Iphone 4 has some pretty significant battery life.Overall I am just very impressed with the Evo, its fast, there is no wait while an app loads, its just there.

I bought this phone with some concern about it being another one of those ...trying to catch up with iPhone products.  I went through a good number of MP3 players before I finally purchased the iPod back in the day.  I liked my iPhone but had a number of concerns:1)  Steve Jobs - very controlling and slow at releasing updates to the iPhone which make it do what other phones have been doing forever..(come one...the 3G can't record video are you kidding me....can't send MMS messages until recently?...really?)2) Wasn't sure I liked the whole touch screen keyboard experience.  My text messages were horrible unless I slowed WAY down....misspelled words all the time.3) iPhone camera software stuck with shutter closed and apple says it was a "hardware" problem and wouldn't fix as out of warrenty (thank God my Geek squad plan covered it.)  But disappointing performance from Apple on this....a HARDWARE problem because an APP had the screen shutter stuck on closed?...maybe but didn't seem right.That being said I still wasn't sure about this whole android thing.....wow I was in for a suprise.  This phone rocks the face off of the iPhone.In addition to having the unnecessary but still cool "Wow!" factor...this phone does everything.  I can browse the internet and clearly read the web pages.  If I have to zoom in the text on the page "word wraps" the text so I can still read it without scrolling left--->right.The screen is awesome....nice colors, great resolution...awesome.The speed is great.The keyboard is bigger....but the really kicker is the SWYPE program which quickly made me forget about how much I loved my work Blackberry Keyboard (but hated everything but email)I had concerns about moving to Sprint as I had them about 5 years ago and hated their customer service and service.....they have obviously changed somethings.  Customer service is as good as ATT or better....more importantly...no dropped calls....great coverage....high speed ....AND I get unlimited EVERYTHING (except calls to landlines-450 min during peak)for $79.99....unlimited text included (ATT - $20) unlimited data (ATT  $30)unlimited mobile to ANY carrier included (ATT to ATT only)...ATT well over $100.I could go on but this is an awesome phone.....Oh yeah if you are worried about the number apps....don't.  Apple may have the numbers for now...but seriously how many "tip calculators" do you need to choose from...plus the Amazon Marketplace allows for some more "colorful" apps as Steve Jobs isn't dictating what you should or shouldn't do.  Also, there is still an app for almost anything you can type in the search field.Great phoneIf you are a "small handed" person you may want something more along the lines of the HTC Droid Incredible or the HTC Hero (maybe).  Hopefully Sprint will come out with a smaller phone like the incredible for those who mind the big screen (The incredible is basically this phone without a front camera and smaller - awesome phone).  But Sprint's plan kicks Verizon and ATT's proverbial A@*.
summary: Bye bye AT&T and iPhone for me

I just received my HTC EVO 4G and haven't really had enough time for a full review other than to note that the system seems pretty speedy even when stacked against my Droid X and Incredible.Unfortunately my first experience with the EVO was marred by a call to the Sprint activation number. Apparently there's a PIN and secret question that you fill out during ordering. I couldn't recall having to fill this information out. And for some reason phone companies believe that we all have memorable facts like the model of our first car embedded into our brains.Needless to say I could remember neither a PIN that I supplied during checkout or the secret question answer. Therefore during activation the customer service would not provide me with any information pertaining to my plan, etc.STOP.Yes, I do realize that Sprint implements these security measures to counter fraud.It seems however to be excessive to make a new subscriber walk a gauntlet of questions as they're trying to activate their phone. It was a most unpleasant experience and I'm not entirely sure if I'll be keeping this phone after the nasty interaction.My tip -- if you order this phone at Amazon -- or elsewhere -- be sure to WRITE DOWN any pin or secret question that you'd asked to supply. You'll need it to do ANYTHING with the phone once you get it.October 24, 2010I've run into what I consider a show stopping bug on my EVO 4G. When I am on pure 4G (not Wi-Fi or 3G) the phone won't connect to GTalk Instant Messaging. This is important because Android uses this connection to authenticate your market purchases. Without a GTalk connection you will be unable to purchase or download any applications.Since I've owned the phone my ability to connect to GTalk via 4G has been basically non-existent. I can make a connection from WiFi. I can connect from 3G.  When I switch on the faster 4G speeds (for which I'm charged an extra $10 per month) the GTalk connection times out with an error.I phoned Sprint technical support and was passed along to "advanced support" who quite incredibly (and wrongly) explained that the reason that the GTalk connection was not working was that it wasn't compatible with Sprint's 4G service (totally wrong).Use caution with Sprint - I'm still evaluating but so far the EVO 4G hardware is holding up ok (as soon as I figure out the GTalk connection issue). Sprint customer service and technical support are quiet a different matter.October 25, 2010Problems continued to persist with the Sprint EVO - primarily that the required GTalk component would not connect when I had 4G turned on. The helpful Sprint support staff ran the gamut of telling me that GTalk was incompatible with 4G and that the 4G service which was clocking 8 to 10 MB downloads on my EVO wasn't in fact active in my town.I completely wiped the device (twice) and tried another Google account. Neither worked.Sprint's clearly on the defensive as well about their added $10 per month for the privilege of having an EVO 4G which they quickly claim (wrongly) isn't compatible with their 4G service.I love that they answer their help lines touting their not ready for prime time 4G network too.You've been warned...
summary: Favorable Phone - Sprint Customer Service Is A Pain

reviewText: Me and the wife both have evos.  We both have chargers. I have 2 of these cables - one for home and one for work. During a trip, her charger got this cable as opposed to the stock cable.  I didn't think much about it but we started having issues with her phone charging to 100% over a couple of hours, but if we left it on overnight it was down to 60-70% when we woke up.I installed juiceplotter / juiceminder / juicesomething (free from the marketplace) and looked to see what was going on and sure enough it would charge to 100%, sit there for a bit and then stop charging.We swapped her charger and cable to another one, it worked fine, I assumed the charger was bad and put it aside for the next time I headed over near the sprint store.I've been having some issues at work where a USB hard drive kept dying.  I swapped the drive, same issue. Swapped the drive case, same issue.  Weeks later (today) was doing ok and copying 200 gigs from one USB drive to another, plugged in my phone to the USB hub and noticed the USB drive that has been working fine died.  HD light on solid, drive disappeared, and computer started running badly.  Unplugged the cable from the USB hub and bam, everything starts working again.Now, this could be coincidence.  There could be something wrong with her USB charger and something wrong with my evo and the way it talks to a USB hub at work (I have the exact same everything at home) but I think it's the cable.  I noticed with the other cable that it was not suitable for syncing - it did charge (for a while) but if I put the evo in HTC Synch or disk drive mode it never came up.So, as soon as I can find a USB diagnostic program I'll post the results, but for now I'd say spend a couple more dollars and get something else--- ok, quick USB diagnostic took a month to get to.Batterymonitor widget reporting these numbersReal HTC charge cable 395ma positive (maxing out at 438)Off-brand car charger 312ma positiveThis cable 2ma positive - I moved it from a powered USB hub to the computer thinking perhaps there was something afoot.  Same after 10 minutes 2ma with the screen off and 80% charge.

Wilson recommends 3" or so for this antenna, but I'd say you want at least 6" on metal around it for best performance.

reviewText: Okay, first you have to have some outside signal to benefit from this. I'd say -98dbm to -100dbm voice and even a little worse for 3g.Mounted the inside antenna to the ceiling in my living room, which is at the back of the house and 8 feet from the floor, I know have usuable signal inisde my entire house. The ground floor is around 1000 square feet.  In the lving room which is around 400 square feet. Signal Varies from -56dbm to -80dbm for voice and data, so plenty for calls. So great buy, super happy.

Went from nothing, in the dining room, to 3 or 4 bars of 3G nearly throughout the house. Signal seems to be constant, so far. The lowest was one area of the hall, that was down to only 2 bars of 3G,but compared to what we had we are very satisfied.I put the outside antenna on a ten foot pole at the peak of the roof and aimed it using the Open Signal and Signal Finder apps. The inside antenna is in the attic, against the other side of the dry wall, on a high wall, in the dining room.

Took this to an almost completely dead area (in East Sparta, Ohio). My phone gets 1x or no signal at all there. Put this in and managed to use it to get 3G in the house and even attach a 3G hotspot to it and broadcast wifi in the house. Went from no Googling to Googling anywhere in the house and even in the yard.It's not like living in the city where you get crazy fast connection everywhere.. but it's better than not being able to communicate at home! By a lot.Using my iPhone, before installation it was at -110 db or whatevers, and after it fluctuates between -70 and -80. This is a MORE than tolerable range.Admittedly, we do not have it mounted right. This could cause for the ridiculously tiny little bubble that it emits good signal in... but with the WiFi repeater, it's usually not a big deal. Just connect phone to WiFi and good to go. Just can't make calls unless you stand in the little repeater bubble... or get a VOIP app.

reviewText: We have a client located in a near cellular "black hole". Odds of a cell phone ringing there are worse than a coin toss. The Wilson DB-Pro with directional antenna brought the signal in the building up to 3 or 4 bars with clear reception.The directional antenna is located on a outdoor mast and the amplifier is located with 15ft. of the outdoor antenna. The indoor antenna is at the far part of the building and the directional antenna is pointed away from the indoor antenna. All these are best practices with this unit.An important consideration when using the directional antenna is to Google-up a map of cell towers overlaid with a topological map. Being able to accurately aim the directional antenna from the map will save time and perhaps some ladder climbing.It was pretty easy to install (except crawling in attic space!) and when accurately aimed it provided a great boost and clear signal.Bottom line is it works well for us and gets 5 stars.

I have several installations with Wilson equipment and at each the product works perfectly. Most are remote cabin sites 5 to 10 miles from the nearest cell tower. Cell signals are -105dB to -110dB. With this product you simply point the outside antenna at the nearest cell site and turn it on.I get a boosted signal inside my cabin of -70dB to -80dB. Data rates of 3MB/s to 5MB/s (benchmarked with OOKLA). No dropped calls either. Very reliable ATT service with this booster.Same thing at home. I live in an urban location Orange County, CA but I can not get a good ATT signal in my home. I have the yagi version of the outside antenna pointed at the nearest tower which is only 1 mile away. Inside I use the DBPRO amplifier and two of these panel antennas. I split the signal and put the antennas at different ends of my home.With that config I get excellent, reliable ATT in my home when before I could not hold a phone call on the cell phone.
summary: Read any of my previous reviews of this company or their products. It is a "no-brainer"; hook it up correctly and it will work.

reviewText: I had tried several models and a couple manufacturers of repeaters. After calling on Wilson technical support, I was advised to purchase this model for my needs. I am located on a small hill between a couple of Verizon towers, so there is no real line of sight. Our signal would vary from about 1-4 bars on 3G, and if near a window on the far side of the house, get a couple to 3 bars on 4G.The problem is my office is on the other side of the house where the signal varies and rather low. I have recently been using 2 cell phones, one as a portable for my business and the other for a home line. I got tired of the Comcast and VoIP functionality together. I had fought with 8 VoIP carriers in an 8 year period, along with Comcast, never having what I would call solid performance.Anyway, purchasing the DB Pro with the optional directional antenna made the signal solid on the other side of the house and improved a bit on what was the best signal before the purchase on the "good side" of the house. Although I have apps to check on the signal, for the most part they are all trying to check the 4G signal in performance. This system is not designed for 4G. So, it may not be apparent that a signal increase has been accomplished if you are just reading the bar graph on your phone. Even with some cell phones that make the status available, you would have to be sure the app or the phone are recording the 3G signal.It has made my signal solid and have no issues with conversations that I experienced with VoIP or using the cell phone without the DB Pro.
summary: The DB Pro stabilized my signal

reviewText: Our neighbor vacationed in his 5th wheel in Oregon all last summer and he was not able to get a signal from the RV space he was in. reviewText: I would have given this 5 stars if the "holder" it self was a little more flexible in terms of adjustments for various size phones. My Note II displays -107dBm 35asu and wasn't able to pick up a carrier signal half the time.With this booster plus the larger magnetic antenna (301125), my Note II is registering -85dBm 49asu with a full 4G LTE signal -- speed tests @ 8879/2196kbit, 4 bars.Pretty slick!

Definitely boosts my signal with my Samsung Galaxy S4 on ATT with LTE.  The antenna I bought was:  Wilson Electronics Dual Band - 800-1900 MHz Magnet Mount Antenna with SMA Male Connector and 10-Foot RG174 Coax Cable .  Note: this product comes with a 4 inch antenna, but I wanted the full-experience 12 incher (that's what she said?).  EDIT: I also have used this with a "CA24M" 24" antenna (requires a male FME to male SMA adapter).  Amazon doesn't sell this, but Google it and you'll find the place that sells it (CellAntenna Corp.).  In the mail I have the 40" antenna "CA40M" just to see what a ridiculously-long antenna can do.I installed the antenna on my trunk and I see an increase in dBm (signal strength) as well as download speeds (24Mbps -> 31Mbps).  I haven't had a chance to test it's "max-range" in the middle of the desert yet, but what I see from in-my-garage testing shows promise.The product also fits my S4 well. reviewText: I bought this with the 4G-V and am glad I spent a little extra to get it. The stand is the centerpiece here, and it is very well designed. One caveat with this particular phone is that with the touchscreen using almost the entire width of the phone, the curved restraints sometimes inhibit the far right and left hand characters on the virtual keyboard. It's easy enough to unplug the phone and slide it out if you have to answer a text or e-mail. but it bears mentioning Other phone likely won't run into this issue. The window antenna holder does a nice job of adherring to the glass, but I found I don't really use it at my house since the magnetic antenna itself that came with the 4G-V clamps to the metallic housing on my blinds like a champ. If you're going to get a 4G-V I strongly recommend you get this kit to complement your purchase.

Bought this to go along with my wilson sleek, works great love the little window kit, and the table top suction cup holder. Buy this im sure you wont regret it.

reviewText: Where I live i am bouncing between 3 bars 3g and 2 bars 4g service. My iphone 5 does not let me force it to stay in 4g so watching long videos is great if I can keep 4g but if it decides to drop to 3g the stream is interrupted an i have to start over :( I bought this item in the hope that it would boost the 4g signal enough to keep me in steady 4g coverage. I also used the cradle with my moms iphone 4 and it works well with it too (3g only)speed test speed results:3g no cradle:  .4mb up  .3mb down4g no cradle:  7-12 mb down  3-5 mb up3g with cradle (iphone 4 & 4s) .8-1 mb down and .8-1 mb up4g with cradle 15-25 mb down  6-14 mb up.I took a trip recently where there was only 3g coverage and the booster worked well for making a limited 3g signal steady and stronger.The home kitWilson Electronics Home/Office Accessory Kit for Wilson Sleek, C-Boostis well worth the price. The antenna mount is worth the piece by its self. I tried to make my own and had poor results. the desk stand is helpful but has a few issues (see issue two below). the home kit has a nice bag that fits the whole kit in one nice package.I have had two issues with the cradle over the past 3 weeks. First, the side plastic things (hands) that hold the phone are not sized right for the thin iphone 5. it will work but the smallest plastic hands on the farthest in setting hold the phone but they bend in enough to make the outer 10% of the screen hard to touch. I have no case on my phone but using one should help this. I could also just cut the plastic tabs shorter. My moms iphone 4 in a hard case had no issues so bigger phones are fine.Seconds issue is with the home mount kit. the attachment point for the cradle to the gimble base is loose and works well in vertical mode. put it into landscape mode off balance the whole thing and it tips over. the Iphone 5 is one of the lightest phones out there so bigger phones must have it worse. I bought this to help boost my home reception, since I live on the outer edge of the range of our local 4G tower. Before the 4G-V, I was getting about -116db of signal on a really good day, with typical readings in the range of -120 to -125db. My data throughput was about 1Mbs typically, with 1.5 on a really good day. Total data dropouts were common. Since I got this device, my signal is a rock solid -85db. That's a difference of 1 bar to 4 bars on the phone's display. I typically get throughput measured by Speedtest.com between 6 and 8Mbs, and up to 10 in bursts on a good day. Drop outs are a thing of the past, although I notice that sometimes I'll get a data rate drop down to about 4Mbs during times the tower is likely to be getting hammered with traffic. That's not the boosters fault. My guess is that if your signal is already ultra-weak (< -130db) or fairly strong (-80 db or better) then you might not get much difference using this device. But if you are in the sweet spot, this booster is going to worth every penny you pay for it.

It takes my Sprint and ATT phones from almost no signal, to one or two bars. If there is a signal, I will see 3 bars. My recommendation though, is to get the larger antenna. I work in a building on a military installation that has no signal at all inside and one bar of 3G outside.  I bought this to hook up to a military OE 254 antenna (RF antenna).  This take no bars and give me a solid 3 to 5 bars of 3g indoor.  The only real complaint I would have is the rail that hold a phone onto the booster are not meant for a GS Note 2 with a otterbox defender case.  That said, this product has made my 24 hour staff duty shifts easier by giving my consistant signal to serf the internet and watch movies or stream music.  I would gladly buy this again.I was a little uncertain about the use of an RF military antenna and thought that it would not really work because an OE 254 is meant for lower spetrum RF signals.  That said, the antenna does get 3G... and the little antenna that comes with it will get 4G if I put the antenna in the right place.  3G suits my needs though.Those that say it does not work need to get a better antenna or are working a in completely dead zone that has no signal.  You need at least some signal to get this to work.  Signal theory explains it all.  Look it up.  Ask me if you have any questions.

First, make sure you get the correct booster for your 4G phone.  This particular model can be used for AT&T; and Verizon.  It has a switch to use depending on the phone / towers.I travel to remote parts of Montana every year for two months.  This year I tried the booster for the first time.Pro's:  It really does boost your signal and It is very easy to install.--In places where I had an "E" on my iPhone 4s display, it would often boost it to 4G.--In places with no signal, I would often get one to two bars.--in places with 1 bar of 4G it would boost to 3 or 4 bars 4G.--In valleys where I would normally drop the tower, it often kept me connected.Is this thing a panacea?  uh,no.Con's:-- you can't take it out of the cradle if you need the boosted signal; bluetooth remote is advised for answering, speaking, etc.-- you should NOT be texting when driving anyway unless pulled over, having said that it is a pain to text in the cradle.-- Be careful not to touch where the external antenna plugs into the base!  the metal connector gets hot!-- Position of the cradle is important, make sure you place your cradle high in the car even though it has an external antenna- it will aid in reception, trust me.-- sometimes, a few feet forward or backward in your vehicles location will make the difference between signal and no signal in remote areas but this is to be expected.I would definitely buy this again because it does work.  Expect one to two bars improvement on average and many times will give you 4G connection verses "E".
summary: It works, proven in remote parts of eastern Montana

reviewText: this booster works in AT&T and Verizon, then good for sale when I no need, now I have 2 of this item, working well for my office and dormitory.

Now i'm able to stream all my movies on netflix and amazon off my roku player & browse the internet on my work computer without a single hiccup. reviewText: Email support is awesome here, that adds a starprice at about $150 = well worth it in fringe areascompatibility with carriers; read the specs before you buyflexibility: buy another $20 antenna and use it at home toocar mounting hardware: easy on, easy off. adjustablemeasuring how well it works: there is an app for that, your number of "bars" don't mean nothin.cons: phone mounting hardware. Your phone antenna needs to be ON this unit, as in face-to-face. For the Samsung Galaxy Note 2, it is a bit larger than normal so I was only getting about a 6db bost when mounted as recommeneded. After installing a proper app to properly measure changesin signal strength in dB, from testing I noticed that mounting sideways )no mounts provided to do this with any amount of stability) gave me ~20 dB of boost!con: interference with FM radioTips I have read about online from forums: mount your antenna far away from the phone as possible, to avoid feed back loops/interference with your phone's built in antenna. Try decoupling antenna from the car ground by placing the antenna magnet over a piece of cellophane or similar insulator. Also,mount vertically per instructions and principles of radio wave physics. Paired with bluetooth headset the experience is seamless, try using an NFC tag to quickly toggle bluetooth when you enter/leave the automobile to save battery power if desired.In sum: test your phone position/boost result using a proper dB scale app, find out location of your internal antenna and get that as close as possible to the sleek (ultimately just test and try it in different positions), mount external antenna up high and far away and perpendicular to the earth, get a cheap second antenna for easy use in your home if needed.Note: uses a micro USB connector for power. Runs hot, measured mine at 124F with 65F cabin temps. Optional antennas with more gain necessarily have a narrower "beam" that they pick up in - this is physics and unavoidable.  6db minimum boost is 2x the power as it is measured in log scale. Note that mount can EASILY be modified to suit internal antenna jiving with the sleek with less than $10 worth of instamorph: http://www.amazon.com/InstaMorph-Moldable-Plastic-12-oz/dp/B003QKLJKQ and you can even color the plastic to suit. Instamoph is magical space-age food-grade mold-able and remold-able plastic and should be in your toolbox anyway so just buy it already, if only to amaze your friends.In sum; price/performance/support deems five stars but it isn't magic because physics..Just be grateful someone is offering this product at this price with REAL support.Any questions call/email support  as they are super helpful.

I've used one of the old versions of the Sleek to help reception with past Verizon smart phones, and it worked pretty well, though not perfectly.  Well enough, though, that when I got the new BlackBerry Z10 on T-Mobile, and found so many new and different dead spots in cellular coverage (T-Mobile does NOT stack up to Verizon for coverage in my area), that I bought this unit and the bigger antenna -Wilson Electronics Dual Band - 800-1900 MHz Magnet Mount Antenna with SMA Male Connector and 10-Foot RG174 Coax Cable- to try and help.  My expectation was that this unit would improve signal reception to the point where many dead spots would be usable, but I did NOT expect it to fix every cell coverage/reception issue, i.e., my expectations were moderate based on my experience with previous units.Net, it is helping in my highest priority location, which is a dead zone as I pull up to my house.  Signal strength has gone from 0-2 bars and no effective voice or data connection at times up to 3-5 bars and consistent voice and data connections.  No 4G, but went from unusable to usable, a critically important improvement.  Much more usage is needed to see how well this unit works overall, but a good start.Pros+Made critical improvement to voice and data signal in key dead zone+Easy to setup and use+Works well as holder in car+Works with T-Mobile to improve basic voice and data connection speed/reliability (but have not seen 4G help yet).+Designed to work with all major NA carriers, helpful vs. having to buy the carrier-specific versions.Cons-Gets really hot-Suspect would drain car battery if left plugged in and car is not run due to heat this thing puts outRecommended if you need a bit more signal on the road.Will update as I get more experience with this unit.

My wife and I have been using the LG420 flip phones, from Tracfone, for a couple of years now. With our following pre-paid cards, we have now well over 1,000 minutes on each phone. Also, we purchased the phones at Wal-Mart for about $15, with wall and car chargers and belt clip included. Not sure if it comes with those accessories here.For text messages, we noted that our e-mail address for our phones is AT&T.; And since this is a GSM phone, I suspect that this runs on AT&T;'s network.Also, to note: Ok camera on phone. Voice mail seems to work fine. We also ported over our old Verizon cell phone numbers to them. Worked great!Overall, great deal! I recommend this phone and plan.

I've been with Tracfone for several years now, always using a new phone model when an older model dies, which seems to be 10-16 months.  This LG 420G has been my favorite so far in terms of aesthetics, use and function.  It's a basic phone with web access and camera, although I use neither.  Unlike the photo depicted here, mine is nearly all black.The nice thing about the LG420G is that for under $20 you get a carrying case and a car charger with this (along with the standard wall charger).  You also get "Double Minutes for Life," a benefit that for older models has been an extra charge.  The carrying case is a clip-on vinyl case that is attached to the belt loop.  One has to use careful force to turn the swivel from a vertical position to a horizontal position.  The fasterner is a flimsy magnet.  Twice now I've lost the phone while sitting down.  Luckily both times I found the phone stuck deep in the couch.  I now wear a brown hair band around the case to keep the handle from popping open and to provide added security.The phone itself is well-made.  I recently left it in my jeans pocket and it was submerged for about five minutes in hot water during a wash cycle.  When I realized the phone was in water, I immediately fished for it in the barrel, dried it out, removed the battery and placed it in indirect light.  A few hours later it was working again with no signs of water damage.  Whew! My Sprint phones were never this good.Activation is easy and fast.  I prefer to do mine over their website.One nice feature is having a voice recorder on this phone.  It's not high quality but it's great for leaving myself notes.  There's also the standard stop watch, calendar, quick dial settings, an alarm clock, notepad, "secret notes," calculator, world clock, stop watch.My one complaint about Tracfone is that whenever you buy a new phone and want to transfer your number, you have to call their customer service number and talk to some Indian guy with a heavy accent.  The last one who worked with me on transfering the number was downright rude.  It also took me three days to get my number activated from another phone that had died on me.  (On a previous number transfer it only took me a day.) Luckily I was able to get by with my other phone that I keep handy for these emergencies.I could have transferred my number on-line via the Tracfone website but the last two times I tried that I noticed that not all my minutes were going to transfer over.  I didn't want to lose 500+ minutes so I had to endure that rude guy from India.  Hopefully this phone will last me a year so that I don't have to keep calling India whenever a phone dies.  This long ordeal is my one complaint about Tracfone.Other than customer support being questionable at times, I do have to praise the company for offering budget plans for the frugal-minded.  I get by with under 200 minutes a month so my 60-minute cards (which are doubled, remember?) usually last me.  The 60-minute card, however, only gives you 30 days of service.  I can handle that for $12/month and not have to worry about an outrageous Sprint bill every month, an experience that turned me off to Sprint and on to Tracfone.  I can add minutes with a quick visit to the website, or I can buy time via my phone.  Because I have been a loyal customer for several years, I also get additional deals via email for reduced minutes, etc.For no additional fee I also have international access so I can chat with my brother who lives in Germany.I live in SE Arizona and have no problems with reception at home or in town.  Although Tracfone shares towers with Verizon, I don't always get service in remote areas, but that's OK with me.  There are only two things in life that require my immediate response and chatting with friends or co-workers is not one of them.Overall I am very pleased with Tracfone and their products.  I like this LG420G model as well.  I dinged the company a star for their unfriendly (at times) customer service.  But for anyone looking for a bargain, someone who doesn't chat much or who hates being tied down with an outrageous monthly cellphone bill, who's not much into texting, you may want to check out Tracfone.  You can check for local availability via their website.
summary: A bargain phone for the casual user

reviewText: My wife just started using this phone yesterday, but so far it seems that there are no problems with this. Easy to use menus that take a little adjustment after using the Samsung Flight II, but she'll get used to it. My only complaint and the reason for not giving it 5 stars is that the wall charger did not have a usb cable incorporated. We happened to purchase an accessory bundle with case at the same time which just happened to arrive on the same day, so we have connection to our computer anyways. Aside from all that, this phone seems to be a great buy for the price compared to Go phones in stores around the same price. My wife seems happy, and that's all I need.Edit 5-20-12!!! We ended up having to return this for a refund and reorder the product for $5 more, even though the product was fulfilled by Amazon. They explained that even though the product was fulfilled by Amazon, it was shipped out by the seller. It turned out there was a minor moisture bubble in the lcd display upon receipt, so we had to return it to an AMAZON RETURN CENTER, and when my wife gave me the phone and wall charger to return, she forgot to remove her micro SD card. After contacting Amazon about the issue and a 3 day research time, I was informed that they were unable to find or retrieve the micro SD card, but that I could order another and they would reimburse me for the price (which was only $6.99 fulfilled by Amazon for a 4GB.) BE WARNED THAT IF YOU DO NOT HAVE A MEMORY CARD, THAT YOU CANNOT TRANSFER ANYTHING TO OR FROM A COMPUTER WITH A USB CABLE connected to this  phone; SO NO CUSTOMIZED MP3 RINGTONES AND NO REMOVING PICTURES. I can't tell why this is since there is internal storage, but since Amazon is more than handling the problem they retain the 4-star rating for the phone. As I noted before, my wife had the Samsung Flight II prior to this phone, and they take the same memory card, but for those of you purchasing this as a new phone and  who would like customized mp3 ringtones or to transfer pictures off the phone, it would be a good idea to purchase a usb cable compatible with the phone and either a micro SD card or micro SD card with SD card adapter if you have an SD port on your computer. Oddly enough, we still have the adapter and case for our old micro SD card, but Amazon is replacing the whole adapter kit at their cost, so yet again Amazon exceeds to please with their customer service.

I bought the blueant s4 at the local electronics superstore in case I wanted to return it afterwards.  This was going on my dad's sunvisor and being paired with a motorola maxx ve.To make it quick here are the hot and not so hot spots about the S4HOT : Audio quality.  How many times have we been saying take off that bluetooth earpiece and toss it?  Well the blueant sound quality is impeccable (see number 2 below)HOT : Because of the superb audio quality the blueant must use the phone's internal voice recognition system.  The good news here is the sound is so good the phone can recognize speach over bluetooth - something I could not do before with bluetooth headsetsnot so hot: on my dad's setup - a motorola maxx ve (derivative of the razr) the blueant could not download his phone directory - but the ability to talk clearly to the phone made using it "normal" as using the phone without bluetooth.  Most BT headsets screw up the audio so much the phone can not understand its built in voice commands but they all worked on the blue ant.HOT : people you call on the H4 can't tell either A) you're on a speaker phone or B) you're on a bluetooth device.  They got it totally right on this setup and I'm very happy.In the end, we could not transfer the up to 2000 contacts into the blueant from the phone over bluetooth (thats more for smartphones) but the good sound made the blueant usable as a remote speakerphone to the handset in his pocket to abide by the california 'cant use your phone in the car' laws (except speakerphones)Personally i've used alot of speakerphones like conference room speakerphones from polycomm costing $1K and the sound quality out of the blueant is as good if not better - people are full duplex so you can break into a conversation if need be.Because of the great performance, despite its not working as planned on my dad's older model phone, I'lll give it 5 stars.  People calling him in his car can hear clearly, it comes with a car charger (cig lighter to mini usb), and is easy to use.  It seldom falses on a command (most commands begin with "blueant!" so it knows when it's being called upon)We also tried it indoors in a conference room where the polycom would normally go and people thought it sounded better as a speakerphone so the technology inside the blueant is top notch, hence the five thumbs up.  I almost made it a 4 star, but my dad's trusted phone is so old that I'm surprised it works at all with it. And that is talking to the cell phone via bluetooth with 100% success - unheard of before.Overall - I'm very happy - I would have saved 20 bucks buying it on amazon but I was not sure how good/bad it would be so I used the store with the real easy bring it back for any reason policy just in case.  I'm glad we're keeping it in the house/car now, and If I were to buy one for my droid, I'd buy it on amazon for the lower price.
summary: a few glitches on some phones, but otherwise GREAT sound!

reviewText: I really wanted to like this product.  I spent a long time researching what was available, without having to change out the entire stereo in my car.  It all started fine. Turned on. Synced with my phone. Contacts etc.  But the part about hands free voice control was below par.  I know, some might think it's my voice, or the way I speak.  But I used the voice activation on my phone by itself and it worked perfect.  I spent about 2 hours playing with this unit, and not once could I get it to call the right number.  I even did the software upgrade.  Didn't help.  I returned it.  Too bad really... It was a nice looking unit and the speaker worked well.  But the voice recognition was the most important feature I wanted.

In the past used a plantronics bluetooth, and I have two of those for use in the house etc. But the Blueant is great in the car.  Not perfect, takes some getting used to... the "Blueant speak to me" usually works but sometimes is clueless, usually because it hasn't reset after hanging up a call, but can always just touch the unit and get it back into command mode.  Battery life is awsome. It is certainly loud enough and does what it says.  Completly hands free when I do the "speak to me" thing right.  Also nice when someone else is in the car. People don't know I am on a car speakerphone, think I am just talking into phone normally. I recomend it highly. Haven't used any other car speakerphones but this one is perfect for me.Update: Have been using this over a week... brought it into the house to charge, it was only medium charge after a week of heavy usage, slipped it into my shirt pocket, was dumping some doggie poop into the toilet and... you guessed it... it FELL INTO THE TOILET, UCK .... grabbed it out... hey it is my Buleant... you woulda too... hahaha.... drained it, blew air on it with a hairdryer on low, put it in a bag of uncooked rice... that's what people recomend on the NET... next morning plugged in the charger... TADA!!!!! It came back to life... "BLUEANT SPEAK TO ME"... "Say a Command" said the Blueant S4. haha. This is a tough little poopie cookie. Been working perfectly since the incident.update2.... still going strong. ordered on for my daughter for her birthday. still loving it.  Not perfect hearing me say "blueant speak to me" but can always just touch it and get command mode.  not using an ear bluetooth anymore.  People can hear me on the unit just fine.
summary: really like it, even works after I dropped it into the toilet.

reviewText: The Breffo Spiderpodium mount for smartphones is a great concept of a mount that can fit any kind of phone as well as allowing you to place it in any orientation. Plus, being able to use the “spider-like” legs of the mount can allow you to use it in things like car vents. This review is meant to find out if the concept translates into real functional use.The spiderpodium mount has an interesting look with its multiple arms/legs which wrap around your device. It’s not the most attractive design in my opinion, but it’s meant to be eye catching and flexible, both in terms of appearance and functionality, which it certainly is. In using this mount at school as well as in a local coffee shop, I received a lot of comments and questions from many people. It’s definitely a head turner.The mount has a nice rubber feel, and it wraps around devices well, whether they have cases on or not. The arms are extremely flexible, but they are not so easy to move such that your device will fall out of the mount, nor will the legs propping up the device flatten out. Each of the arms has little grooves every so often across the length of the arm so that you have a rough idea of where you need to bend it. However, it’s important to note that this isn’t the only place where it can bend; it can bend across the entire length of the arm.In using the mount, I found it was difficult to figure out the best orientations to place each arm in for the desired orientation of the holder (landscape, portrait, different viewing angles, etc). Luckily, on the box itself, there’s pictures that show a lot of the different orientations you can place the arms in to get your desired hold of your device. And if you’re the creative type, I’m sure you can come up with even more orientations for the arms. I did have some trouble getting my spiderpodium mount to look exactly like the arms in the pictures in the box. After all, each arm moves independently of the rest, so it’s difficult to get it to be level with the other arms propping it up, etc.Overall though, it’s a great concept item that delivers with functionality, and I couldn’t find any major issues with it to warrant anything less than 5 stars. If you have many devices of different sizes, or are looking for a mount/holder that can work in multiple scenarios and environments, this is the mount for you.Incidentally, Breffo gave me a discount code for anyone who reads this review to use on their website. The code is REVIEW20, and gives you 20% off anything on their website!I was provided with this item as a sample in exchange for my fair and honest evaluation. If you have any questions, feel free to comment below or contact me in my profile.
summary: Great flexible mount that works in many different scenarios

reviewText: Wireless charging is one of those things you wouldn't expect to be as comforting as it actually is. It kills me how this isn't more widely available yet. Great device, unfortunately I am moving on from my Palm to an android phone. I will miss the touchstone, unless I can figure out a hardware hack for my new phone :)

I got the Touchstone back for my Palm Pixie Plus, so it was only natural that I would have to get the Touchstone Charging Dock so I could charge my phone.  It is a great fit, but you have to be careful that you sit the phone in the center to the Touchstone or the magnets won't latch and it won't charge.It looks nice on my desk and it is small enough that I can move it around depending on what is on my desk.  The cord is long enough that it reaches from my surge-protector on the floor to the top of my desk.  I like the way they have the AC charger with the USB plug going into it for charging.  On the Touchstone itself, it is a little difficult to put the USB plug into the Touchstone charging receptacle - I had to put it under a light so I could see where it was located.All in all, the three pieces fit well together and make up a great dock for either portrait or landscape viewing.

If you have an older Palm Pixi or Pixi Plus, this is a great charger. Please note you will need the Touch Stone back plate to make full use of this product. Palm was way ahead of the curve with this product. Still absolutely love the Web OS and the Palm devices. Too bad they went away :(

reviewText: The defender case almost doubles the thickness of my bold and adds a little to the weight.  But the protection it provides is well worth the extra mass.The case comes in four parts:  plastic keyboard cover to keep dust out of the keys, front hard cover that integrates a screen protector, hard back cover that snaps securely to the front cover, rubber skin that give the phone a good grip and provides dust covers for the buttons and ports.The included holster firmly holds the phone in place at whatever angle you rotate it to.  It took a bit of wear before the phone would easily release.  But even after four months of continuous use the holster holds firm.The one problem I had with the case is that it has a gasket around the bottom microphone that can fold over when you are installing the phone.  This blocked the mic so everyone I talked to complained about the quality.  Once I straightened the gasket the quality complaints ceased entirely.

reviewText: I bought this case to keep my headset in. It keeps it from getting tangled, and it makes it easy to take the headset along. It has elastic storage areas on the inside of each flap. Another brilliant idea from BlackBerry!

I purchased this case to use for my Plantronics Backbeat 903 Bluetooth stereo headset, after I lost the trouser-pocket-pouch that originally came with that device.As comfortable as the Backbeat headset is to wear, being light and comfortable enough that I forget I'm wearing it, it bothers people. They look at me like I'm a martian, and wonder aloud if I'm going deaf and wearing hearing aids. Thus, when I enter into society, as a matter of decorum, I frequently remove the headset and stick it in a front pants pocket; --whence I have learned that the Backbeat headset does NOT play well with pants pockets! I have broken at least three of these expensive headsets in my pocket, so I started using the little carry pouch that came with the latest headset, to provide some protection, and boost survivability. It clearly helped. The headset stayed fresh and whole when I had the pouch, while in the short couple weeks it took me to get around to ordering another case, my pocket somehow broke a piece off one of the headset control switches (though it still works perfectly), and it started looking dusty and ratty.It took me a lot of time and effort to pick this case out, because it was VERY difficult to ferret out a case that might fit. Plantronics doesn't offer JUST the pouch for the Backbeat (they only include one with the set), and many of these types of carry cases offered on Amazon don't give details as to the size; --nor is it easy to be sure the thing is a good fit even if you have the dimensions. The fit is very important in that it not only has to be big enough to accommodate the headset, but small enough to fit in a pants pocket without being an unsightly, uncomfortable lump.As it turned out, my hour (or two) of searching and agonizing, and my best-guess purchase of this "Blackberry Premium Zippered Leather Carry Case Pouch", resulted in a pretty much perfect solution. It is JUST big enough to fit the Backbeat 903, with room I think, to squeeze in a USB-to-mini-USB connector (I lost the one I had when I lost the last pouch I had, and still have to order another). This new pocket pouch is a man-friendly black, and while I'll have to take their word that it's leather, it does seem to be sturdily made and of good quality. It is smooth and flat, with no sharp edges, and it's sides are rigid, but with some flex, so it's compact and comfortable-in-pocket. I expect the rigidity of this new pouch (my old pouch was soft) will significantly enhance the protection afforded to my headset.I have yet to mention that the $4.50 price, with free shipping, is so low that it's almost like they're paying ME to own this practically perfect solution! I just ordered another one to keep on hand in case I lose this one.
summary: Perfect fit for my Backbeat 903/905 bluetooth stereo headset, pants pocket, and wallet!

First things to do when you get a touchscreen smartphone; find a good case and find a good screen protector. Seidio makes some very decent and inexpensive products, and this screen guard is a good example. It was very easy to apply and left no air bubbles that couldn't be pushed out, and I have a backup in case anything happens to the one I'm using. Very happy with the product.

OK, so I don't listen to or follow directions very well, and didn't on this, still got it on my phone.
