Fits the phone great and easy* to install.shipping was a nightmare, but I ordered Thanksgiving week, and all of my packages for all sellers got delayed.

I purchased two other screen protectors and compared it against the Seidio Ultimate Screen Protector for HTC EVO 4G, 2 Pack (Crystal Clear).In addition to the Seidio, I also tried the SGP STEINHEIL HTC Evo 4G Sprint Screen Protector (Ultra Crystal), http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003TML0V4/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_titleand Three LCD Screen Guards / Protectors for HTC Evo 4G, http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003TW9BEM/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_titleThe Three LCD Screen Guards were a cheap version and clearly made the screen resolution (pixels) look less clear.  Ironic choice of words huh?  Yes, it made the EVO's beautiful screen look less clear, as if turning an HD TV back to non-HD, not to mention the rainbow colors it showed on the center of the screen.  I quickly removed it and tried the other two brands.  You get what you paid for.Between the Seidio and Steinheil screen protectors, I'd say they are about on par, except the Steinheil Ultra Crystal had a brighter effect (it allowed more light from the EVO to reach your eye balls), and the feel against it had less friction than the Seidio.  If I had to choose, I'd definitely go with the Steinheil again.  Just don't make the mistake of what I did by first putting on the screen sticky by accident, and then realizing I needed to use the thicker screen protector.My wife also noticed the same thing too.  The Sedio clearly wins over the Three LCD Screen Guards.**** TIP 1: Do not use the stupid squeegie/plastic thing that comes with the product to smooth/remove air bubbles.  It will leave scratches on your screen protector.  Instead, use your thumbs by pressing down on the film against your EVO screen to smooth out the air bubbles as you lay down the protector cover.**** TIP 2: If you notice that there are particles underneath the protector cover after applying it already, get good ol' trusty Scotch tape.  It's good enough that it'll stick to the cover so you can peel the cover from the EVO screen easily (as the tape will stick to the cover) and will be able to pick up particles, and weak enough that it doesn't leave any messy residue.  For best results, have a 2nd person help you.If the protector cover is already laid down on the EVO screen and you want to grab a particle that's stuck underneath, you (the person holding the phone and applying the cover) take a piece of scotch tape and stick it on the protector cover so you can peel the cover up slightly.  Your partner in crime will then take another piece of scotch tape and stick it against the under side of the protector cover (right on the cover itself since the particle would have got stuck on the sticky side of it) to pick up the particle.  Once this is done, you can slowly release the protector cover back down and you should notice the particle is now gone.  I did this like a dozen times to remove small particles and it worked like a charm.  It's also best if you do not position your head directly on top of your phone when performing this, as to not cause additional particles from falling down.  If you don't have a partner in crime, you should be able to do this yourself if you're careful.  No liquids required!
summary: Good, but not as good as the Steinheil Ultra Crystal protector

This is my second time buying an extended battery and the same results.  So I am sticking with my stock battery that I got with the phone which I am getting almost 18 hours on a charge with normal use of my HTC EVO.  I would recommend buying another stock battery with a charger.  That is what I have done and it works great!

reviewText: I GOT IT FOR MY SAMSUNG NOTE 2 ANDROID PHONE,ITSTHE SEIDIO INNOCELL 1750MAH SLIM EXTENDED LIFE BATTERY FOR HTC EVO 4G SEIDIO.

reviewText: This battery makes this great phone only better. It lasts me an easy day and sometimes a day and a few hours in change. If I am using it extensively it will possibly last me 18 hours. There are days when Pandora plays on a medium volume for about 8 hours and when I look at my phone and am ready to go home from work, it still says 47% remaining. Mind you, I am constantly checking four of my email accounts, browsing facebook, making atleast an hour worth of calls during this time. The display consumes the most battery on the Evo, I keep mine on 50% ... Even when I have just 19% remaining, i know the battery is going to last me atleast a few hours.using the regular battery which came with the phone, I managed about 7 hours. This battery is at the very least atleast three times as good. It doesn't require an extra case and easily fits. I also no longer put my phone on airplane mode when Im using the public commute cause phones tends to look for signals when you're underground.The Htc Evo is a great phone and it should be used without any reservations. If you are using the Stock battery and telling yourself its doing a fairly decent job for you, then good for you but for people who hate this marvel of a phone and think twice before switching the GPS on or watching youtube for videos or browsing the internet... or whatever the case maybe, this is the battery, look nowhere else.Charging time required - 3 hours

I pre-ordered this battery before the Sprint HTC Evo 4G was even available. From past experience with four previous HTC smartphones, I knew that I would be wanting a second battery - if not a third and maybe even a fourth.I've owned Seidio after-market batteries for each of my earlier HTC phones and, to tell you the truth, I have never been able to determine if they supplied any more power over a longer period than the stock battery. Personally I am not convinced they do. I don't know of any accurate tests of battery life for the consumer. I do know from my own experience with Seidio batteries on the HTC PPC 6800, Touch Pro and Touch Pro 2 that I didn't get any longer operating times than with the stock battery.So far in a week of alternating the Seidio battery with supplied battery for the Evo, it has been the same experience: I don't see a longer operating time with the Seidio. Admittedly, my observations are not at all scientific. I inquired of Seidio once before with an earlier battery if they had any lab tests or something similar to back their battery capacity claims - and they did not.In any event, the  Seidio battery does last as long as the original and Seidio does stand behind their products, so at the end of the day I remain a customer, even if a suspicious one.Jerry
I bought it.  I works Great!  I would buy another if I needed to get one.  You should buy one too!
This is a great battery, not really much else to say. Got one for my mom, she's still using it, makes the phone last slightly longer than the origional does.
summary: Great battery, what else is there to say.

reviewText: I'm still conditioning this battery, but so far, it's done what it says.  Even when it was new, my Evo battery would not get me through an entire day - I got so I would leave it plugged into a charger while at work.  I am a moderate phone user (a couple short phone calls, several texts and email reading and sending throughout the day, some web surfing, Bluetooth while in the car).  I charged this new battery overnight since it said to leave it in the charger for a couple of hours after it was charged.  I had it in the phone for two days and finally had to turn on the 4G antenna and set the screen to "always on" in order to run it out completely.  I currently have it in the phone and I stuck it in there yesterday morning.  It's now 2:30 p.m. the next day and the battery is still showing 50% left.  I'm starting to wonder if I'll ever get through the conditioning stage!After reading the negative reviews for this one, I was a bit nervous but...I have the Seidio cradle on my nightstand and it has been awesome so I thought I'd give this a try.  I wasn't disappointed in the least.

I've had this battery for about 6 weeks now. I chose it because of the form factor. It's the same size as the OEM battery, so I didn't need to buy any additional parts - new back cover and a new case. I like my Otter case and frankly my EVO phone is already big enough, without adding more bulk to it.I carefully followed the advice to drain and fully recharge the battery five or six times after installing it. I've been rewarded with some pretty amazing battery life hours.Two things to bear in mind about this phone and this battery. First, at 1750 mAh, it's going to take longer to fully recharge than the stock OEM 1500 mAh battery. And I have read that the phone is calibrated to indicate a "full charge" when the battery reaches 1500 mAh. If that's true, then you should always let the phone keep charging for awhile after the green light comes on and the battery indicator reads "100%." How long? I have no clue, but I usually plug the thing in at bedtime so by the time I'm ready to unplug it, it's had a few hours past the first green light, to build up a charge.Also, I happened to walk by a Sprint kiosk at a local mall, which was decked out with signs promoting the EVO. I spoke to the young man who was staffing it, mentioning that I liked my EVO. He was eager to help me change some settings to enhance the battery life. I hadn't had time to tell him I had a new, more powerful, battery, so I just smiled and let him get on with it. He tweaked a few settings and I think it helped. I'm no expert, and I recommend consulting with Sprint staff about your phone settings, if you find someone as helpful as I did.Overall, I'm pleased with this purchase.
summary: Definitely an improvement over the OEM battery life

reviewText: must have. This battery just barley gets me through the day but it does it. Its a must have if you don't get the bigger battery with a bigger back. Personally I like the slimmer phone but my wife has the Seido 3500mAh and is happy (lasts 3 days.

I followed the instructions to the tee, however this battery didn't work any better than the original.  Initially it worked 18hours and that was with shutting down as many running apps as possible.  Within a month it was down to barely 10hours.  Don't waste your money.

So I must've spent about $80 worth of worthless cases so far. Either they make my EVO too bulky (those Otterboxes truly add bulk to your phone), are lint magnets and make it a chore to pull the phone out of your pocket, or are flat out aesthetic and provide little or no protection at all (Barely There case for EVO = Barely Any Protection from a simple drop - I dropped my phone with that case on it and it plopped right off like a cheap piece of plastic). Then I got the Seidio Innocase II. Holy cow. What the heck was I holding back on? It doesn't add much bulk. It's actually quite easy to snap on and off once you figure it out. It's got a matte finish so the gripping is actually better than slippery cases like TPU cases. It's actually quite good. My only gripe is it's a little tricky to hit the power button (takes a little getting used to, but it's easy once you get the hang of it) But as for the 'squeaky' or 'creaky' sounds? I guess if you really squeeze the case hard enough, you'll get some sort of squeaky or creaky sounding effect. But aside from that, this is basically all I could ask for. A case that protects your phone from oopsies on the ground. It's not a lint magnet. Decent gripping, and overall, worth protecting your $500+ EVO. I give it a double thumbs up.

reviewText: I bought this case from Seidio before I even received my EVO, just to be prepared.  It was about the only case I could get prior to the EVO's launch.  The case looks nice and is slim but after putting it on an using it for a few days it was creaky, i.e. not fitting as close as it should, on the back.  Also, I noticed when I took it off it trapped a ton of dirt/dust under the edges where it goes over the screen.  On the plus side it is slim and definitely looks cool but the cons were too much for me.  I now have an Amzer silicon case which will probably be on the phone until Otterbox gets their EVO case out.  Maybe I just got a lemon on this case?  I don't know.  While not a seriously flawed case it just wasn't for me.

reviewText: This is basically a shell composed of two parts that fit over the Evo. There is a rubber kind of sheet inside that may perhaps provide some additional shock protection.The shell is just thick enough to keep the rear camera lens protected when the unit is placed on a flat surface.The build quality is high and all the sockets and connectors remain easily accessible.If you use a second battery, the case is a pain because the two sections join together tightly and are a hassle to separate.My opinion is that the case offers little shock protection and its value is in acting as a cover for the phone to prevent wear marks on its surfaces. As such, I think it overpriced. By the same token, with a good screen protector and this case, I feel pretty comfortable carrying the unit in my pocket.Overall, this will for the moment, but I'm keeping my eyes open for a more durable solution.Jerry
A lot better than the rubber one you can pickup in the Sprint store.  Nice matte black/rubberized finished ala classic Thinkpad laptops.  I would highly recommend this.

First off, this is a very good case with a kind of felt material on the inside of the case.  It does have a tendency to let in dust between the cover and the phone but, that's not much of an issue if you take the case off occasionally and wipe the phone and inside of the case.  My case developed a crack on one side of the hole where the kick stand is located.  I contacted Seidio about the crack and apparently all their cases made prior to January 2011 only come with a 180 day warranty but, those sold after January 2011 come with a 1 year warranty.  My case was within a 1 year warranty but, sadly it was purchased before January 2011.  I bought an Otterbox Commuter and it protects the phone better but, I wish it had a rubberized coating on their hard plastic cover like Seidio.  I hated to give Seidio any more money since they didn't stand behind their product.

Pre-Intro: Seidio Inc was founded in 2002 in Houston Texas. They first started as a company that designed unique and quality products for PDAs, which slowly evolved into Smartphones. They has a passion for innovation and this lead them to become the leading manufacturer of Smartphone accessories.They are also very well known for their rubberized cases. Many online forums and review sites have reviewed and vouch for their products. Their products are known to be built for quality and endurance.Currently they are carrying a variety of cases for the Sprint HTC Evo 4G, Ultimate Screen Guard Protectors, Spare Batteries, Chargers, Cables, and many more. You can visit their site here for all the details and see a list of their products (Seidio - Your Single Source for Premium Smartphone Accessories).Specs of Innocase II for EVO:Quote:Innocases have quickly become one of the most popular products Seidio manufactures. Crafted from a hard yet flexible material, it provides an amazingly thin layer of protection without adding the excessive bulk of other cases. The Innocase II consists of interlocking top and bottom pieces that fit your phone snugly, and Seidio's signature soft touch finish provides a great feel and better grip without attracting lint. It is also available in a combo, which includes a matching holster.- 1mm thin case provides scratch protection without adding much bulk- Designed from a hard, yet flexible material with Seidio's signature soft touch coating- Unique slide-in design consists of top and bottom interlocking pieces that fit your device snugly- Precision cutouts for ports, controls, and kickstandFirst Impression:HOLY!!!, I GOT IT, I GOT IT!!!!! I GOT IT, I GOT IT!!!!!The little brown square/cubed box arrived at my door early this morning. I was like "wow", quality service from Seidio. It was very nice of them to send me a review unit early before shipping date. I must take my time to thank them once more.As I took the products outside of the packaging, I saw the plastic looking case for the Innocase II. The product showed very well through the plastic container. It was definitely screaming at me to put it one. But before I did that, I took my dSLR camera out and started to snap some shots with my camera.One thing that I thought I would do better is move Seidio's Logo a little high above the inside background. You can't really see the Seidio logo from the packaging.Build Quality:Definitely not cheap. The build quality of the thing was hard. I wouldn't say hard as a rock, but it's definitely hard plastic. It was harder than those cheap eBay cases that you can get for 10 bucks shipped to your door. The rubberized feel of the case was also very good on your hands. It felt smooth and prevented the phone from slipping out of your hand.There was no sharp edges around any corner. or on the inside of the case. The inside of the case was very well thought out. They put some felt cloth in the backing so that it will prevent the back cover of the Evo from being scratched up.I also tried to double check on their advertised specifications by using a mm gauge to measure the overall thickeness of the phone before and after installing the case. You can find those pictures below.Fitment:I slipped the case and the Evo and it clipped together nicely and firmly. The right side and the left side of the case fit snuggly together and it fits the Evo flush on both sides.The cutout for the LED, Camera, and Speaker is perfect. There's enough space for the all three hardware specs. The camera glass is now protected because the case brings up the level to a point where the camera is indented inside the cutout location. No more worrying of scratching the camera lens when you put it on the table.I've also took specific pictures of each cutout location around the case to show you how they go around the buttons, insert holes for the charger, HDMI, power button and volume button. All those edges fit without gap in between and have been well covered with the rubberized layer to protect the phone.Forgot to mention, it covers all screen leaks from the edges.Protection:With the pictures showing 1000 words. I don't need to say much abut protection. They thought out every aspect of the phone do the point where there's felt inserts on the backing to protect the back cover. I wish they did one thing with the inserts though. They should have put the felt cloth all the way wrapping all aspects of the inside including the curved edges of the phone.Conclusion:In conclusion, the case lives up to the standard of innovation. They really did make a case that protected the phone real well. The design is slick and they did not have to include a bunch of artwork to make it attractive. It also keeps the phone low profile and gives the Evo a high class look while your on the phone or when the phone is sitting on your table.People always complain that getting a case at a high price isn't worth it. Or they complain that they want their phone naked. I think the reason they say it is because they can't get themselves to click the buy button. Some people settle down with cheap cases from ebay. But if you want a cheap case, that's your decision. If you want a high quality case built with precision and design to innovate, this is definitely the case to buy. Buying a cheap case from ebay would make your $450 phone look cheap also.They offer many different colors, so go to their site to check it out!The only thing I wished I had the honor of reviewing was the accessory that came with the case, "The holster". I didn't get a chance to get the holster so I couldn't test if the holster made the case even better. I'm sure the holster would give the case additional points!

Paying $30.+ for a couple of pieces of plastic to carry and protect your mobile phone can be hard to swallow.  But, after using lots of cheap hard cases bought on ebay over the years, and after finally getting a Seidio (sold at my local Sprint store) for my Treo Pro, I became a believer.Good fit, slightly grippy texture, and a solid belt clip are hallmarks of the Seidio Innocase Holster Combo.I loved and trusted the case so much when I had my Treo Pro, that I immediately ordered one for my EVO 4G when I got it.  (I actually bought the Best Buy label case which is identical and made/supported by Seidio.)My first one was a tiny bit loose--I read that this was a problem with some of the initial batch made--so I returned it and bought the Seidio from Amazon.  About the same price, came fast, and fit even better.I've convinced a friend to try it and he's satisfied.And, my old Treo Pro case is still being used by my wife who is now using that phone.I'll keep outfitting my phones in these cases unless someone comes out with a better product at a similar price.

reviewText: This is my favorite screen protector for my Incredible. I've tried SGP, Anti-fingerprint, Boxwave, and Verizon. To me this is the closest to the natural feel of the screen itself. I put it on in the bathroom first running the shower for a few minutes to steam it up and then cleaned my DInc with a eyeglass cleaning cloth, microfiber and finally running a piece of tape across the screen to pick up any remaining little pieces of lint. The very first time I put it on I misaligned it big time but it was easy enough to try again. Having 3 cats, lint travels with me wherever I go! When I did get it alinged there was to much lint for me to individually pick out but Seidio's are washable so I rinsed it off with a little soap and water, shook it off and started again. This time the alignment was correct and the few bubbles came right out by smoothing with the included card. There is a cut out for the optical joystick and speaker which I know is hard to see in the photos. These are usually backordered here but I only had to wait a few days before I got an email saying it was on it's way! Seidio Ultimate Screen Protectors have kept my screen free of scrapes and scratches from being kept in my purse, and I would recommend them to anyone.

This is a great case for the Droid Incredible. I was having a hard time holding on to the phone without a case because it is so thin. This added just enough to the thickness and a good sticky grip so I don't drop my phone. Easy to install and take off and feels like it will protect the phone well if dropped.This is much better than those flimsy gel grips.

My only complaint is that it is a little bulky, which is a problem if you have the car mount.  An Incredible using this case will no longer fit on the car mount-you have to remove the case.  Not too big a deal though-the mount is only worth using if you are driving a long distance or don't know where you are going, so you take it off then, and in short or routine drives you just put it on the console or the passenger seat.  The buttons and the headphone and charger ports are well exposed so that isn't a problem.  All in all I recommend this case if you want to have a case for your Incredible.  With that said, if I find a case that does the job as well but allows me to still fit it on the car mount, I'm going to switch to that.

reviewText: This is a very nice case, exactly the style and quality I've been looking for. I've been through many other cases for my HTC Incredible including the OtterBox Commuter. All others were either too bulky and had exposed silicon that attracted too much lint(OtterBox), or just too cheaply made that snapped together from back and front pieces. The Seidio Innocasse II has a nice matte black finish that allows you to grip the case with no silicon to attract dust and lint. It consists of an upper and lower piece that slide and lock together instead of the other top and bottom style pieces that snap together, look cheesy and never look clean along the edges. At this point I highly recommend this case! Will return with an update in a few month's with my verdict.

I have had this case on my phone for about 8 months now and it has been great.  The only problem is that I dropped my phone from a height of about six feet onto concrete and the case itself has started to crack.  I can't be upset about it though because the phone was left completely unharmed and the case did it's job.  One of the things I like about this case is that it has a little bit of rubber tackiness to it.  The stock phone is difficult for me to hold on to without it slipping out of my hand.  Also, I like that it adds some thickness to the phone because it is so thin it is difficult for me to hold on to.  The only annoyance is the edge of it above the speaker hurts my ear if I hold it there for an extended period of time.  Once this one cracks I will probably buy a new one.

This is a sexy design, and the way the case connects in the middle provides excellent protection and ease getting to the battery if needed. My mom has dropped her Incredible numerous times, and this thing has performed with aplomb. I don't see a reason to get any other D. Incredible case: this one is excellent

reviewText: I've had this case for almost a month now. I did some researching for a couple days following my purhcase of the phone and decided that this case sounded like the way to go. I couldn't be happier with it. In all the phones (and other electronics) I've had and all the clips, skins and cases I've had for them, this tops them all.Everything everyone has said about this case is true; the way it very, very snugly slides over the phone, just barely over the edges of the face of the phone so that it keeps it securely in, but you won't lose a bit of the screen surface. The feel of it is great; smooth and sturdy but with that neat rubbery kind of feeling. Problem with silicone-type skins is that they don't slide into your pocket very well. This product retains that ability. And also the design of it makes it look like it's just a part of the phone. I don't even realize that it's a case. reviewText: I have always liked Innocase cases - very durable and nicely designed.Like a previous reviewer I tried most of Verizon's cases and was not happy with them. This Innocase is excellent. The two piece top/bottom design offers much more protection than a front-back design which will pop off if you drop the phone - defeating the purpose of a case.Not much more to say than this is an excellent case. Also fits great into my Mivizu leather holsterMivizu Premium Luxury Genuine Leather case cover for Verizon HTC Incredible Droid phone belt clip holster.

The Innocase II for Droid Incredible is a great case for a great price. It doesn't add too much to the size of the phone and protects it really well. The only negative thing I can say for it is that it sometimes move the Invisishield I have on, creating an air bubble, usually the corners. This is probably due to me installing the Invisishield wrong. All in all, this is a great case that all Incredible owners should own.

Having read the many excellent reviews by others I ordered this case to cover my new 3500 mah Seidio battery and cover. It works great together. I'm not quite used to the heft of a 3500 battery but as one who just upgraded his data usage to unlimited I found it almost funny that with constant use of the phone for about 40 hours, including two night shifts where I have some extra time to check the weather, order cat food via Amazon, read political commentary, check the weather again, text my coworkers, send out a couple of emails -- that this monster battery holds its charge really, really well. Above all else, the fit of the outer cover is unbelievable. The tactile feel is a little less grippy than I would like, but it also slides into my horizontal belt holster all that much easier. I had Body Glove covers for years and love that rubbery, non-slip surface. That is the only reason I give this 4 stars. That said the phone does fit very well in the palm of either hand and allows one thumb input through the Droid Incredible's great front screen. Obviously, this cover will not protect in case of a drop as well as a thick, rubberized front and back Body Glove style, but that's a tradeoff for an excellent product. It also does not come in aqua marine or midnight blue and it doesn't have a tracking chip embedded in the body, nor does it glow in the dark....But that's more a function of how spoiled we have all become in this golden, golden age of affordable, high-tech electronics.

reviewText: I purchased this case and have had it on my HTC Evo for over six months at time of review.At the time that I purchased this case, there were fairly limited options for protecting the HTC Evo.  I had previously purchased (and reviewed) theAmzer Silicone Skin Jelly Case for HTC EVO 4G (Black), and was hoping that the Innocase would be the last case purchase I would make for my new phone.  This case appeared to offer substantial protection with a form-fitting design.  I was drawn to the fact that this case has a plastic exo-skeleton which helped keep the rubber surround snug on the phone.  Early reviews for the case were also extremely favorable, with many users reporting things like a "fit like a glove".Six months of use has given me a good perspective on what this case does well.  I'm not sure if I have butter fingers or what, but I swear I drop my phone at least weekly.  This means that I have probably dropped my phone from decent heights 25 times or more in this case.  I am happy to report that my phone is no worse for the wear despite this relatively rough handling, and has nary a scratch on it.  The case is indeed snug because of the exo-skeleton and does a great job keeping dust and other grime away from my phone.I do have a few gripes with this case.  I first off do not like the added bulk that this case adds to my phone.  This added bulk combined with the larger surface area of rubber causes the phone to "stick" somewhat when I put it in or pull it out of my pocket.  "Stick" isn't really the right word, but that extra amount of rubber does create a sense of friction when pocketing my phone.  If this was the only drawback to this case, I would wholeheartedly recommend it simply because of the superior protection it provides.  Unfortunately, I have also noticed diminished reception with this case.I work in an area that has "fair" phone coverage according to Sprint's phone map.  On my phone, this translates to three out of six bars of coverage.  Shortly after putting the case on my phone, I noticed that my phone began dropping calls at work.  I called Sprint several times in an attempt to troubleshoot my phone, and nothing seemed to help.  I didn't even suspect that my new case was the culprit, so I just learned to live with the new worse coverage.  One day at work I went to swap out my battery with a backup I had purchased (one of the major drawbacks of one or no bar coverage is the fact that your phone switches to roaming a lot and eats your battery), and I noticed that after swapping the battery and setting the phone on my desk that the reception had improved back to three bars.  I further noticed that upon putting the case back on my reception dropped back down to one or no bars.Somewhat incredulously I repeated this exercise many times over the next few weeks.  Furthermore, I used the Speedtest app available in the app store to take 3G internet speed tests during random times of the day.  By simply removing this case, I averaged speed test increases of almost 150 kbps over those several weeks.  It became clear that the case had a definitive and repeatable negative effect on my phone's voice and internet reception.Because of these faults, I cannot recommend this product.  I bought the HTC Evo to be able to use it, and this case effectively renders usage difficult at best in areas with less-than-stellar coverage.  I have since gone back to using the Amzer case referenced above.  While the Amzer case may have issues with dust, it provides decent protection without negative reception effects.  If you are considering purchasing this case, I would strongly recommend that you pay attention to your reception levels throughout your day.  If you see three or less bars of coverage in an area that you frequent, this case is probably not the best choice.
summary: Nice Case with one MAJOR flaw

reviewText: Pre-Intro: Seidio Inc was founded in 2002 in Houston Texas. They first started as a company that designed unique and quality products for PDAs, which slowly evolved into Smartphones. They has a passion for innovation and this lead them to become the leading manufacturer of Smartphone accessories.They are also very well known for their rubberized cases. Many online forums and review sites have reviewed and vouch for their products. Their products are known to be built for quality and endurance.Currently they are carrying a variety of cases for the Sprint HTC Evo 4G, Ultimate Screen Guard Protectors, Spare Batteries, Chargers, Cables, and many more. You can visit their site here for all the details and see a list of their products (Seidio - Your Single Source for Premium Smartphone Accessories).Build QualityThe build quality of this case is pretty different compared to the Innocase II that everyone is accustom to. It isn't hard plastic. Instead, it is made from soft silicon and plastic. The case is still two piece like most Seidio products (main piece is silicon, the second piece is a clip on of thin hard plastic that holds the phone and the case tightly around all edges). It also has the rubberized feel that everyone is used to.Upon putting on the case, I held the case in my hand without the phone in it for couple seconds. The texture is definitely nice. It's not like any of those cheap silicon cases that you can get for couple bucks on ebay. It's build to perfection.I loved how they put curvature on the case for where your fingers are. it gives you a sense of security when your holding the phone.Fitment:WOW! Fits perfect. When i mean by fit's perfect, it means that there isn't any space on the inside. It's almost like putting the phone into a high end pair of socks. It fits tight and smooth. Since the case is silicon, you don't have to worry much about the case on the inside. There's no sliding of individual pieces to put the case on, therefore you don't have to worry about scratching the phone.Seidio also once again did a perfect job when it comes to cutout on the backing and the back cover of the phone. The camera, speaker, and LED are all cut to perfection. Nothing is blocked in anyway. Also you don't have to worry about anything touching the camera lens. Kickstand is also the same. The bottom of the phone also gives easy access to the HDMI and the mini USB port.One thing that I feel weird about is the power button and the volume rocker being covered by silicon. Basically your pressing on the case to access those three buttons. BUT! they did give some embossing for those buttons so you can easily find them with your fingers without looking at the buttons.Protection:There's no possible way to scratching the inside of the casing when you have the phone on the inside. They are well thought out, including simple things like an indent on the top clip so it doesn't press the Evo power button as it slides over the top.  The top clip is also offset, leaving the headphone jack in the clear.  Having a face-in design protects the screen from walls or other bumps and scrapes. The USB and HDMI ports have plenty of clearance for use when the phone is in the holster.The holster will NOT work with the phone face out, so you can't use it as a video stand (besides, the Evo has a kickstand). The Seidio Spring-Clip Holster for an uncased Evo has design, quality and engineering that make it 4G is the best item of its kind on the market. You would have real problems improving on it or finding a better one.The Good:Great (and possibly brilliant) design, engineering and implementationHigh-quality materials, good attention to detailThe Bad:I have large hands and for my personal tastes, they could have made the springs in the clip just a shade stiffer.The Ugly:Not a thingThe main idea with clip holsters is convenience. With most clip holsters, when you need your phone you reach for it, disengage a clip and pull it out. Seidio does this idea one better and then improves on its implementation with several intelligent refinements.First, the Seidio clip-on holster is a 'face-in' design; which means it keeps the touch-screen pointed inwards towards your body and in contact with a piece of velvet-like material to protect it. This idea is so simple and so powerful that you don't know why every holster-maker on the planet hasn't adopted it yet.Your screen is the most delicate, delicate and hard-to-replace part of any smartphone, the Seidio holster treats it that way.Second: most clip holsters require an upwards motion to get your phone into your hand making them hard to use when dressed in winter clothing or business attire. The Seidio Spring-Clip holster eliminates the need for the 'gun-fighter' motion by stabilizing the phone at only three points--at two fixed corners and by the spring-loaded clip that grips the top edge of the phone at an optimally secure angle so that it is stable until the clip is raised.This means that your phone is safely locked into the holster so long as you don't accidentally move the clip or snag it on objects and with a little practice, thumbing the clip and letting the phone drop into your hand for use becomes second nature and you forget you're doing it--as someone who once fed $400 worth of smartphone to a seat in a movie theater and had to buy a new one, I have big reasons to love the Seidio.Third: Most clip-holsters are so badly engineered and so insecure that clerks in stores that sell phones will warn customers away from them saying that they're bound to lose their phones.  This is far less likely with the Seidio than with any other clip-on holster I've ever bought.Unlike other case/holster makers, Seidio makes their holsters using a good, high-strength polymer and they display an attention to detail and quality control that simply makes their product better. The tongue on the end of the clip that secures the holster to your belt has a sharper angle to it than others do; the mechanism that allows you to rotate the holster on your belt to the optimal position for you demonstrates a good, positive lock that you simply don't see elsewhere.All in all, the Seidio Spring-Clip Holster for an uncased Evo 4G has a lot to recommend it. It is my go-to solution for carrying around and maintaining quick access to my phone and keeping it safe. In fact, this review is of the second one I bought for this model: the first was destroyed at my workplace but the phone itself ended up just shy of being pristine. All in all, Seidio can be said to have worked with an all too rare business model: they decided to make money by making something good.*** Update: Sept 1, 2011***Wrecked my third holster--this time while getting into a car and snagging the back end of the clip on the door-frame, breaking the swivel joint that holds the holster to my belt. The phone fell to the ground and was completely unharmed. These things are great and it is time to order case number three.

Got this bluetooth to make hands free calls on a long commute. It seemed to work okay at first, after a few months I've noticed some problems with it.1. Finicky Communication - Works okay for the first few minutes of the call then unexpectedly cuts off and the caller is left thinking the call was dropped, when in fact there is a problem with the bluetooth connection. Only happens periodically.2. Lack of True Handfree integration (for the Motorola Atrix at least) - I have not been able to interface the bluetooth to make a call through my handset using only my voice. Even though I can start the process with a click to the headset followed by a voice command, I have to go through 2 sub commands before I can make a call. This coupled with the spotty voice recognition makes voice dialing an option I never use.3. Low Mic Volume - I have had multiple people tell me while talking to me that the call volume on their end was low. This, coupled with the experience of owning another bluetooth headset where I didn't have this problem, leads me to beleive it's the Blue Ant's fault.Things I Liked1. Battery Life - Seems to stay solid, even when left in the car and used periodically over the week. I can usually go a week without a charge, this is with light use during the week though.2. A2DP - Being able to stream music and podcasts wirelessly is great, I really like this feature, and it's one that I'll look for in my next headset for sure. Though it does tend to drain the battery.3. Micro USB Charger - Having the same charging port as my phone makes it possible to have only one charging solution in my car, which is very nice.Overall I can't recommend this headset. If you get it at a really good price it would be serviceable, but to pay a premium for it doesn't make sense. I've owned a number of Plantronics bluetooths and most of the problems I've had with this unit have been non-issues with the Plantronics ones. It has been time for a new headset for a while considering the time spent in the car. We have several headsets in the household: an ancient Motorola bluetooth that's not able to work well in our noisy ScionxB car; the new-ish Motorola H850 started sounding tinny; and a very disappointing performance from the Jawbone Icon.After Googling for "the bluetooth for Blackberry" I was faced with a list of brands and models. Some of which I'd heard of Motorola, Jawbone etc. But what of this Blueant? Yes, I'd heard of it, but no one I know has one. But the reviews on Amazon looked fine. After charging the headset I noticed the odd rubber ear piece (like the Jawbone Icon) but luckily an earhook is available to support the gadget. The Blueant is very easy to set up - the voice instructions are like a sci-fi film. And really useful. I paired to Blackberry, then to Samsung Epic (Android) and both tests were great - clear, loud and the noise filtering didn't affect the voice sound too much. If there's background noice Blueant will fade the noice which does affect your voice a bit, but still makes the conversation heard. (Out of curiosity I paired the Jawbone Icon to the Blackberry and that was not so good - the usual reported excessive fading in and out, the rustling sound and cut outs were all apparent.)So, after pairing and unpairing pretty easily and testing on Blackberry and Samsung Epic I am happy to say that this bluetooth might actually live up to its claims. I've just to try it with 22mph winds, but I am glad I've been able to get a great headset for less than $50. Highly recommended. Pity I had to gave this to my lady. A quick summary of this product before I get into the details:Likely great for dedicated Apple device users that has all the power it claims (simultaneously 2.1 Amps on one port with 1 Amp on the other for a total of 3.1 Amps output combined, but under performs DRAMATICALLY for non-Apple devices due to protocol issues for USB chargers.  It gets 3-stars because all it claims to support is Apple devices.Now for more details...A little background on USB charging for those who don't know:The USB power spec is for 0.5 Amps at 5 Volts... or 2.5 Watts.  This was great up until the last couple years when devices have gotten really power hungry, particularly smartphones and tablets and to a lesser extent dedicated GPS's.  Some of these devices use over 2 Amps, particularly the tablets like the iPad (or in my case the HP Touchpad).Manufacturers of these devices therefore had a dilemma.  If they had their devices pull more than 0.5 Amps, they risked damaging the power source, which could be a computer, that was only prepared to source 0.5 Amps.  Thus the manufacturers have used tricks to determine whether their device is connected to an unknown source, at which point they purposely only draw 0.5 Amps, or to the dedicated charger that was provided with the device, where they can draw all the power they need.There seem to be two common tricks used.  The first is to short the two data-wires together in the charger.  This is what most non-Apple devices do.  Since a computer or older device wouldn't have done this, the device can assume it is safe to draw all the power it needs.Apple seems to have taken a different approach, one that I don't fully understand but know can be seen by the fact that the data lines are neither open nor shorted when the charger is plugged in, and is more sophisticated and probably superior, because I suspect it allows the device to know exactly how much power it can use.While Apple taking a better approach might be nice in concept, it's created chaos in the USB charger product category.  What is the non-specific charger to do?  They can't support both.Kensington chose to go the Apple route for the 2.1 Amp port.  I don't own any high-power Apple devices, so I can't say for sure, but I suspect this unit performs well with Apple devices.  Using electronic equipment I was able to draw 2.1 Amps when putting a fixed load on this USB charging port.  However, when I connect any of the 3 high-power devices I have (HP Touchpad (2 Amps), Motorola Triumph Android phone (0.85 Amps) and the LG Optimus Slider (0.7 Amps)), none of them drew all the current they could have, because they were expecting a shorted set of data-lines.The 1 Amp port on this device is a bit of a quandry however.  It didn't have the signature on the data lines of either the Apple protocol or the shorted lines.  It appeared to have them open... which was a surprise and I believe a mistake (although I can't be certain with Apple products).  The results for my 3 devices however were identical to that of the 2.1 Amp port.To highlight the positives, I can say this, I was able to draw all the power the product claims it can source using fixed loads.  As my above explanation makes clear, it is the DEVICE, not the charger, that chooses not to make full use of the available current (Amps).  So by using power resistors I could test the actual capacity of the device without dealing with the data-line issue.As such, I was able to draw both 2.1 Amps from one port and 1 Amp from the other, simultaneously.  I can not say the same for the other charger I have tried (and I have two in shipment to test).Thus this device gets 3 stars because it only claims to support Apple devices and without any to test I have to assume it would work great for them.  It also can deliver the current it claims.  It is likely a 5-star product for sole apple users.However, for non-Apple users, I STRONGLY encourage you to look elsewhere for your Car USB power needs.  The other device I've tried is the "PowerGen Dual USB 2A Heavy Duty Ouput Car Charger" (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00622AG6S/ref=oh_o05_s00_i00_details).  It has other problems (the 2A port doesn't have the data lines shorted and it only sources a TOTAL of 2A, not 2A on one port and 1A on the other), but at least one port (the 1A, which can really do 2A by itself, see my review over there for more details on that) on that has the data lines shorted to get the full power with non-Apple devices.I've ordered two additional devices:- "Ultra Compact High Output Dual USB Car Charger - 2.1A Output" (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00470C35E/ref=oh_o01_s00_i00_details)- "Bracketron Universal Dual USB Car Adapter (UGC-298-BL)" (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0056VNVV8/ref=oh_o00_s00_i00_details)Hopefully one of the two of them will be able to deliver to their specs for my devices.

Don't get me wrong it IS clearly marked on the front face but if you are an avid traveler renting various types of cars you'll know that some of the DC adapter outlets are located inside armrest consoles, tucked in the lowest parts of the center consoles in the front or back seating areas depending upon make/model/year of the car. I know Amazon prices fluctuate far more rapidly and widely than other online retailers. but the tale of this charger is whackier than most:On December 7, 2012, I see this for $9.99 here on Amazon and order TWO. It's a no brainer! Kensington at "no-name" pricing, dual power slots at "single slot" pricing, 10 watts at 5 watt pricing. It's sold direct by Amazon, not by a 3rd party vendor closing out on over-stock.Did I mention it came with an original style cable, which seems sturdier than the Apple which is prone to fraying at the juncture with the connectors themselves?So I dutifully come back here on December 24, 2012,  to review it, and suddenly it is $24.96! Not a buck or two more expensive, almost THREE TIMES as expensive.Now at $9.99, that's a cheap price for a name-brand cable, let alone for a dual slot power supply, with one of them delivering the full 10 watts preferred by the old iPad 3. But at $24.96 the decision is much tougher - go with this one, or with a no-name for half the price? Do I really need an extra cable (at this higher price), or would a no-name without a cable be ok? What about a no-name that is reviewed as being able to deliver 10 watts but only if the other slot is unused? What about a no-name that can only deliver 5 watts, enough for my phone but not for an iPad? See, I got the first class, feature-rich charger, WITH cable, for a stripped, generic device price. Yay! But - why the pricing difference? Is it still worth it?See, products don't have "absolute" value. They have value relative to their price.The new model of online pricing - varying prices daily, or even hourly - is making it really hard to shop.This isn't limited to Amazon, the NY Times did an article this holiday season about how Target, Best Buy, and WalMart, among others, varied prices day by day this holiday season, post-Black Friday, to match or beat their competition, and which store had the most consistently low prices - which wasn't consistent across all products. I just read an article that another retailer, Staples, even delivers different online pricing depending on your zip code and nearness to one of their identified competitors, like Office Depot.So this review is a little different from my other product reviews, and different from the other product reviews of this particular product.For the best insights on performance of this product, read the two top-rated reviews here - I believe those two are honest, objective, and insightful. The only thing I would add, is that I have three Apple cables that are frayed at the junction with the actual connector - the flex portion wasn't well-designed. From the looks of it, the flex portion on the Kensington cable is longer and thicker - which should extend the cable life at this critical juncture where more stresses occur. The first top rated reviewer has actually used this for over two years and reports that, yes, the Kensington included cable does last longer, so that is a nice bonus. Secondly, and don't laugh, now that Apple has released the new Lightning Connector, I like the fact that Kensington departed from "Apple white" to make their connector in black - why? - because it's a lot quicker to grab the right device cable when black means old style and white means Lightning. Yes, this comes up, since I have devices with both styles of connectors and travel with both. It's just one less thing to be annoyed by, when trying to charge them.In terms of pricing strategies, good grief, stay on your toes! Amazon USUALLY has very competitive prices, if not the best, but now more than ever it pays to comparison shop, even to open an "Incognito" browser tabe in Chrome to see if searching cookie-free returns different pricing. Above all, comparison shop, and if you don't like the prices today, bide your time, and post buying, monitor the prices for the first month so you can ask for a price adjustment if things get out of whack.
summary: At 9.99 a steal. Cable alone worth the price!

reviewText: This thing is perfect. Not only can you charge an iPad at full power with the thing, but the secondary port outputs 1A which will charge your phone faster than usual. Having your devices too low on power when you get out of the car is really not fun, especially when they're drained before you can even make it back to the car. Two high power USB ports in one cigar outlet is a major advantage because most people don't have more than one or maybe two cigar outlets in their car. Even if you don't normally need two USB power ports, trust me... you will be happy you have the extra one day when you do need to plug something else in. And eventually you will.Buy a cheap adapter for $5 or something and one day the extra $15 you should have spent will feel like nothing when your battery is dead in some critical situation.

reviewText: For under $5 I was able to buy this silicone case.  It fits nicely and has a nice feel to it.  It certainly gives me the impression that it will not slide around on a slick table. I was a huge fan of the InvisibleSHIELD for iPhone 3 series phones. When properly applied, they were awesome: crystal clear, completely stationary (no sliding, no peeling, no emerging bubbles), and shock resistant.The iPhone 4 era InvisibleSHIELD, however, suffers from a serious manufacturing defect: roller lines. The machine rollers in their manufacturing process are leaving perfectly straight vertical lines on InvisibleSHIELDs coming off the line these days. You won't notice it at first; it will only become apparent once the shield has had 24 hours to dry and the bubbles have all disappeared.You will then find perfectly straight, well-defined "rainbow lines" on the shield that refract light, particularly when your phone is showing a white screen. By holding the phone and shield up to light and turning them back and forth to see the protected screen at different angles, you will notice that there is a line running the length of the shield from rollers during manufacturing.I have always applied InvisibleSHIELD protectors for family and friends and can do a perfect job each time and every time. This is not installation error; you can hold a ruler against the lines and see that they are perfectly straight and of precise width.Of the six iPhone 4 protectors I've installed from Zagg, FOUR have had "rainbow lines" in them, one of them with TWO perfectly straight parallel "rainbow lines" running the length of the screen about a centimeter apart. (Search Google for the term "rainbow lines"; it's a well-known problem.) Zagg won't honor their lifetime warranty for affected protectors, instead saying it's a normal artifact of their manufacturing process (while some other reps will just tell you you've done a lousy job installing the protector).So now it's "normal" for Zagg InvisibleSHIELD users to have prominent lines that look like screen defects running vertically across the screens of their iPhones. So much for "invisible."In fact, they're extremely distracting and I'm currently looking for a similar wet-applied, soft-protector alternative that has better quality control.Until Zagg acknowledges and fixes this quality control problem, I can't recommend dropping $20 on a product that will leave you wishing you could still read your pristine iPhone screen. It's a shame, because during the iPhone 3/3GS years this was the ULTIMATE in iPhone screen protection.No longer.
summary: Not as good as it used to be.

reviewText: After buying this product for several phones I would like to consider myself somewhat of an expert in installing these.  This by far excels the no name brand knock off versions that are sold on Ebay.  Amazon is much cheaper than in the store and the product is very durable.

The main appeal for the Zagg products is its 'guarantee' but realize with this guarantee you've to pay $4 for shipping and handling of a tiny plastic sleeve and you must ship back your original product which is aobut another $1 when you figure postage and envelope.So in other words you spent $5 on shipping fees for a $10 product.  Doesn't sound like Zagg has much confidence in their product after all--if they did they would pay for the bogus shipping fees instead of leaving you on the hook for them.Nonetheless, I got the product at Best Buy, since apparently Best Buy cut a deal with Zagg and will only offer Zagg products, and then Best Buy whacks you another $8 to put the product on.  So by the time you're said and done it's about $30 for a tiny plastic screen protector--a total ripoff!To add insult to injury in a few weeks my screen protector cracked and warped. really easy to apply and its  been a couple months and it still looks good. we'll see if it really lasts for the life of my phone. my screen is super protected.  I say it's a good buy.

reviewText: A naked iPhone 4 has too much exposed fragile glass, thus prone to scratches and breakage.  I also find the sharp edges uncomfortable on my hands when compared to the rounded edges of the previous iPhones.My ideal case is one that does not add bulk, protects all surfaces, is comfortable to hold, allows for access to all bulky chargers and docks, and fits loosely inside my belt case.  After physically comparing 7 other cases and 3 bumpers, and researching tens of other cases, I have not yet found my ideal case, but this is the case I currently use exclusively for my iPhone 4.It adds little bulk to the iPhone 4 (good).  It protects the back and the camera lens (good).  When laid upside down on a flat surface, the front of the phone will not touch the surface (good) (see picture above).  My bulky chargers and docks connect to the 30 pin connector without needing to remove the iPhone 4 from the case (good), which is a problem with many other cases and the Apple Bumper.  It is more comfortable to hold than a naked iPhone 4 (good).  My belt case can accommodate the iPhone 4 inside of this case without much fuzz (good).  However, I deducted a star due to some sharp edges (see picture above) that made it not as comfortable to hold on my hand.
summary: Not perfect, but it is my favorite iPhone 4 case

reviewText: I have owned the iphone 3GS and now the iphone 4. Between the 2 I have purchased 3 different cases for the iphone 3GS and this is my second case for the iphone 4 (I also have the Apple bumper). The cost of the various cases I have bought have ranged from $20-$50. Here is my basic impression of how the Sonix case stacks up:1. Build quality: This is a very thin and lightweight case. If you want a case that will protect your phone from drops, the Apple bumper may be a better choice. In fact I did drop the phone with the bumper and there were no scratches. Zero. Haven't had an accident with this one, but it's a nice quality case, with a very nice grip but it's main function is to protect the phone from nicks and bruises in daily use. I have switched to using this as my default case.2. Design: This is the best 'looking' case I have ever owned! It is very slim and light and compliments the iphone 4 beautifully. Whereas with the Apple bumper you completely lose the metal looks of this band, this one keeps enough highlights of the aluminium band that the phone does not lose any of its attractiveness. With ANY other phone I would not care about cloaking the phone in a case, but the iphone 4 is a thing of beauty! You just need to see it and hold it to know what I mean. This case is unique because it does NOT change either the balance or the looks of the phone. It compliments it very well.3. Impact on antenna issue: Frankly I have had no dropped calls with my iphone 4. It is better than my iphone 3gs in very way in terms of call quality. In fact I was in the Outer Banks recently and  while my wife Sony Ericsson C902 phone had a hard time keeping a signal for a call, the iphone 4 had no issues. I do have the issue where the bars will drop when you hold the phone a certain way, but it has no impact on my call quality. This case, like the bumper helps in not dropping the bars compared to holding the phone, but it does not help or degrade the call quality. So, if you are looking to get this case to help with call quality I am afraid my experience in both the Washington DC area and the outer banks and places in between says it won't help or hurt...4. Value: At $19.99 this is a no brainer really. You get the best looking case that is very functional and elegant. I don't really use the screen protector. The screen on the iphone 4 is already pretty glare resistant -  more so than the 3GS, so the screen protector can help with scratches but not for glare. For what it's worth I used my iphone 4 as a GPS for our trip to the outer banks. The screen on the iphone 4 was completely readable even in the brightest and direct sun light. The screen on the iphone 4 is fantastic and covering it up with a protector doesn't seem like a good idea (to me at least).Overall, I am really happy with this case and would recommend it to anyone.

This is my first case for my iPhone 4 (my first iPhone, as well).I wanted a case that didn't take away from the sleek look of the iPhone 4, and preened diligently through Amazon.com.  At first, I wanted a temporary cheap-o case 'cause I planned on purchasing the Otterbox Impact when it finally released.  I don't remember exactly how I stumbled upon this one, but after being discouraged by the plethora of knock-offs on eBay, I wanted a decent-looking one with somewhat of a return policy, so I ordered this one.It's a great case, and the material doesn't have much of that "rubbery" feel that I've encountered on other silicone-type cases.  The only other case I own for an Apple portable gadget is the iSkin for my iPod Video, and, though it's a fantastic case, the material makes it so it's a hassle to get it out of my pocket.  Not so with this case.It has a slight stick to it, but not where I have to slide my whole hand in my pocket to remove my iPhone.  The argyle pattern is very nice, and only adds to the design.  To be honest, I think it makes my iPhone 4 look even better.In terms of protection, I don't really expect this to hold up against nasty drops.  I haven't dropped my phone yet, but the case is pretty thin and I'm afraid it won't hold.  Only time will tell.The only other issue I have is that the nibs for the volume and hold buttons get a little indented, but it's really not that big a deal.  The case covers all but the dock port, speaker/microphone, headphone jack, silent button, and rear camera and flash.I'm still considering ordering the Otterbox, but this case makes the aesthetic that much more wonderful that I'm reconsidering making this my primary case.  I've already gotten compliments on it, and may have inspired some others to make this one of their iPhone 4 case purchases.

reviewText: Didn't work.  Unit was producing 12V DC output (note - this is way too high to charge a phone - they need 5V)I'm an electrical/software engineer - I looked up the microchip they're using in it (MP1410) and compared it to the circuit board - here is what I found:- Solder blob shorting pins 1 and 2 (input pin and boost output)- Giant solder blob at the feedback pin (5) and feedback voltage divider- No landing pad under the enable pin (7), with a live trace under it!- No landing pad for pin 8- Burrs on nearly every solder joint for the surface mount parts.- Missing ceramic output bypass capacitor- Cracked solder joint on inductor leadAfter fixing all of the above issues, the output voltage was a little low (4.7V), but it works.  So - if you're in to electronics and have $300 of electronics test and repair equipment, including a reflow kit, this is an awesome hobby project.  Just don't plug it into your iPod until you've verified that the output voltage is correct!

Good enough for me.9/19/11 update: I liked these enough (and they're cheap enough) that I ordered two more sets.  I know I'll lose some, so this way I'll have spares on hand.  Now that I've got nine to try out, I'm starting to see the problems others are having.Of the nine, six are OK.  They've been scattered around the house so one is always handy no matter where I am.  Two are fantastic--they work with a feather touch.  I put those in places where I do critically important work.  (*COUGH*games*COUGH*)  One stylus is terrible. It has been strategically placed in the trash can.But these things are so cheap that one bad stylus out of nine isn't enough to make me regret buying them. It has a reptilian feel to it, rather than being smooth.  This texture is visible when you're looking at the display, and it negates the Retina display quality.  However, the texture *does* make the back of the phone easier to hold onto.If you want something that'll make the back of your phone easier to hold onto and grip, that will get rid of the slippery feeling of the bare iPhone, and will protect the back of your phone from scratches without changing the look of your phone much, then grab this and just apply the back portion.  The front will likely bug the heck out of you, though. :)

reviewText: First let me start by saying that I have used Zagg invisishield on my previous iphone 3g and 3gs. Both were very superior to this crap they're pushing out now. I,ve applied the invisishield to all my kids iphone 3g's and mine and was very pleased with them. They took a beating before they showed any signs of wear. Not with this iphone 4 shield. I applied the full body protection to both my iphone 4 and my son's. They went on easy, no bubbles, the problem is the adhesive is obviously not string enough or never dries. Whatever the reason, they silde off with the slightest movement. Forget about putting the phone in your pocket or a case, because the shield will peel right off.Now for the sad part. It seems Zagg is following in Apples foot steps claiming there is no problem with the shield, and blame it on applying error. That is just BS. Sure they'll replace it for free, but you have to pay for the shipping, packaging, gas and time to take it to the shipper, etc. In other words, they know they're getting very few back. The cost to produce these has to be next to nothing when you poduce in the volume they do. They can easily send you a replacement free without any of the above hassles.While they did respond to my e-mail, because like another reviewer said, you won't get them on the phone, they agreed to a ONE TIME REPLACEMENT!, providing I followed the above procedure. That's mighty nice of them isn't it.I got news for them, with they're CS and lifetime guarantee policy I'll stick to the silicone case for $5.00. It won't peel, won't scratch and will last a lifetime.Save your money and stay away at from this Zagg product. I would have given them a -5 star review if it were possible.

I used to love my old Zagg InvisibleSHIELD on the back of my 3GS. The invisibleshield material sticks so well to plastic, it's almost impossible to get it off (apart from the poorly-cut corner pieces, which do get dirt under them and lift up over time).The problem with the invisibleshield/iPhone 4 combination is that the iPhone 4 isn't plastic.  This stuff does NOT stick to the oleophobically-coated glass (front or back).  It is incredibly easy to separate this film from the screen.  Those people that gave five star reviews - just wait a few more days (weeks if you're very lucky) and you'll see exactly what I mean...

It just needs some other method that would be more effective on the long term.Alternative screen shields should work better than this particular product.Not Recommended for the iPhone 4.

reviewText: I have purchased a Zagg screen for 6 different devices over the years. This is a product where it is absolutely essential that you read and follow the instructions completely. Most of the negative comments are related to not following the directions or not waiting a few days before judging the finished product. Also, it isn't completely invisible - but it will look better in the end than a device with all kinds of scratches on the glass. Consider the alternative to not installing one.1) Install in a dust-free clean area (i.e. clean things up first with an air-can if you have one)2) Wet your fingers gernerously with the spray provided.3) Wait. Once installed it takes a few (2-3) days for the air bubbles to disappear. It will be worth it in the end.4) If you purchase the front and back cover. Install the back first. It will give you some experience when installing the front.5) Enjoy. I sold a device on Ebay and I cannot tell you how perfect the screen was when I ripped the Zagg off. It looked brand new.6) Touch is not significantly affected. I use a stylus tip and my finger with no problems. A little oil from your finger reduces most of the friction.
summary: Follow the Instruction and you'll be fine

I purchased this from The OEM planet for $0.75, and am quite happy. I bought it to replace the Invisible Shield style product that I got from gadgetshieldz because I had ripped it (I don't even know how). While this is cheaper, the gadgetshieldz is a full body shield. I left on the rest of that, and only replaced the protector covering the screen.Comparing the two, this screen is a hard, slippery plastic (rather than the rubbery material that the gadgetshieldz is made out of). I don't expect it to last as long or be as scratch resistant, but I did get 3 of them. Which brings me to my next point: one of them was damaged/not perfect. At a quarter a pop, I don't really care.The product comes with no application instructions and a polyester cloth that removes your fingerprints, but will be sure to leave a mess of cloth fibers in its place. Don't use it. Use a microfiber cloth, of even your cotton t-shirt. Anything is better. Just make sure that all fingerprints and dust are gone before application.To apply this product, I followed the same wet application instructions that I used for my gadgetshieldz. Just grab a plate, put a couple drops of dish soap and clean water in it. Make sure the solution is well mixed (mix it with your finger). The solution should be soapy, but not bubbly. If there are suds, you used too much soap. All we are trying to do here is make the solution somewhat sticky.Then remove the protective backing on the shield, and dunk it in the solution (totally immerse it). Plop the shield on your phone now and arrange it till it is perfect. Take of any excess water (rearranging it if needed), and leave it be overnight. If you mess up at any point, you can simply lift up the protector, dunk it in the solution again, and start over. When you come back the next day, it'll be set enough for you to use. Just peel off the front backing, and you are good to go.There is pretty much no risk of damaging your phone, but if you want to be extra careful, you can turn it off and remove the battery.To those that complain of bubbles: ANY OF THESE PRODUCTS WILL HAVE BUBBLES UPON INITIAL INSTALLATION. Over the next couple of days, the bubbles will go away.If I could do this again, I would just get a gadgetshieldz instead. While this product is nice, it is too slippery, attracts fingerprints, has too much glare, and won't last as long. If you want a shield that you can just set and forget for the next year or two, then get something else. There is likely a good reason why this product comes with 3.

I do a moderate amount of running, both outside and on a treadmill, and was looking for a new armband for my iPhone 4.  My old iPhone 3GS armband was worn out and didn't hold the 4 very well.  I researched armbands at various exercise/running sites and most people liked the Fast Fit.  I found Amazon had the best price so I made the purchase.My initial impression was that the product is well-made, sturdy, and would not be affected by sweat, rain, or heat.  The armband is a vinyl-like material that doesn't stretch.  You need to find a good size setting to prevent the armband from sliding down your arm during a run but not so tight as to cut off circulation to your arm.  So far, this has been my biggest complaint with this product.  I can't find a good medium between holding the phone secure on my arm and my arm turning blue.  I find I'm accepting of a little arm slippage rather than arm tingling and blood supply cut-off.The other minor item is the velcro connector that holds the phone in place.  The phone is inserted from the bottom of the holder.  There's a velcro strap that's about 1.5 inches wide that wraps from the front of the phone to the back.  You can see in some of the product pictures that this holder sticks out a little, about 1/4 inch.  It holds the phone securely in the pouch, but it also rubs on your arm with every step, causing slight discomfort.  Shirt sleeves lessen this discomfort but don't eliminate it.You can't use a case with this pouch, at least not initially.  I have a very minimalist case from CaseMate, very thin and form-fitting around the phone, and I can't use it with this armband.  The phone pouch is still too tight and the iPhone doesn't slid in or out very well with the case on.  I'm hoping the pouch will stretch a little with time and use.  Until then, I have to remove the case prior to inserting the iPhone.  The plastic screen cover is a bit touchy to use, it doesn't always register finger presses/swipes, but once I start an exercise, I don't usually touch the screen again until I'm finished.  So that item doesn't bother me.  If you find yourself using the screen often, it will take some time getting used to.Apart from those issues, I'm pleased with the buckle system, it goes on and off quickly.  The cord holder is nice touch if you have dedicated headphones; I don't so I don't use it.  Based on my first impressions and the price I paid, I'll keep using this armband at least through the summer to see how it holds up.UPDATE 6/24/11:  I've used this armband for several weeks now.  My initial impressions remain the same but I have found increasing displeasure with the armband slipping down my arm as I run.  As I mentioned in my review, the strap is not elastic so it's difficult to find a comfortable setting for keeping the armband in one place above my bicep while at the same time not cutting off the circulation to my arm!  The longer I run and the more I sweat, the more apt the armband is to slide down.  I still haven't found a comfortable adjustment yet, but I keep trying.  Other than that, the case keeps my iPhone dry when I'm running and it starts to rain and the plastic screen cover, though it attracts a lot of finger smudges, accurately tracks my finger across the screen.
summary: Good attempt, but a few flaws hold it back

I wanted something to hold my iPhone 4 when I take the dogs for a walk/run.  I've never used such a contraption before and my other half purchased the Belkin DualFit armband, so I've been trying it out.The Belkin DualFit armband, weighing 1.5 ounces, is a simple lightweight device used to store an iphone on your arm.  The hand washable armband is sized by a Velcro strap and two slots.  A larger enclosure holds the iPhone securely in place and fully covered.  A clear plastic sheet encircled by a reflective strip protects the front of the iPhone while allowing the user to see and use the encased iPhone.  A small pocket next to the larger water resistant enclosure is large enough to hold a house key or excess earphone wire.There seems to be confusion about how to use the DualFit armband.  When I first saw the armband, I thought I was to thread the strap through the inner slot, and loop it back through the outer slot.  This just seems logical; however this method will size the armband between 9 to 11 inches.  For larger arms, one should thread through the outer slot (as shown in the product image) which allows sizing between 11 and 15 inches.  My initial confusion and comments from others indicates Belkin does a poor job of explaining how their product works.The iPhone 4 fits in the DualFit's larger enclosure, but doesn't fit snugly.  This is more of a visual issue than anything else.  The iPhone4 is still protected from the weather, and fully functional.I haven't bought my own armband yet, as sharing hasn't been a problem for us.  When it becomes a problem, I will definitely consider purchasing this armband.  If your looking for a weather resistant lightweight armband, the Belkin DualFit armband is worthy of consideration.PROS:Extra small pocketTwo slots for the perfect fitWater resistant and lightweightComfortably fit up to a 15 inch armCONS:Poor description and instructionsFit for the iPhone 4 is a little sloppy
summary: It Fits Me: A Belkin DualFit Armband for iPhone Review

I've noticed no signs of adhesive deterioration or any other issues with the velcro though.For $20 this is a well designed, nice looking, armband for your iPhone (or other device of similar size.). I'm sure there are much more sophisticated, higher quality, armbands out there. But, with this, you're getting an average armband for an average price. As I stated, I had no issues with the velcro separating from the rest of the armband, but I have not used this extensively. Although the times I have used it, I was sweating thoroughly and it didn't seem to deteriorate the velcro at all.

Pros:confortable materialnice opening for headphones and lock buttonCons:plastic screen cover doesn't touch the glass, so you have to push harder for the phone to respond to touchruns small; probably not great for men or bigger arms

reviewText: This armband is far too much trouble for me to actually use. First, I must remove the bumper case from my iPhone 4. Next, the phone must be squeezed into a very tight armband compartment. For those who need to have their iPhone display in full view (at least for passers-by) throughout a run, this may be necessary, but that is not a requirement for me. The iPhone's audio beeps and rings, along with the Nike-GPS app's announcements of pace and time at half mile intervals are all I need or want. I get this by carrying my phone in the pocket of my running jacket in the winter, but need a solution for the summer when there are no pockets. All the products that I see on Amazon look like they would have the same problem. Any suggestions would be appreciated.UPDATE: My solution is the Small Personal Item BeltSPIbelt - Small Personal Item Belt - Great for Runners!, Blackalong with a ziplock snack size bag for waterproofing. It easily accomodate my iPhone with bumper case and is inconspicuous under my untucked running shirt.
