reviewText: Using this with an iPhone 4 (GSM).This armband is perfect for our runs around the park. It fits snug, has a slot for your house/car key (not a keyfob), and seurely holds the iPhone or iPod Touch (no room for a bumper; just the device). It is pretty bright in color. Not my favorite color, but it makes it difficult to lose. The screen protector is not as smooth as glass, but does not negatively impact the touch screen usage.Some are complaining that it is only for those with larger arms. It should fit most arms. While the description says it fits 12.6" to 15.8", the one I received seems to more realistically fit 10" to 15" arms. Here is a  trick for those that pick this up and can't get it to fit smaller arms. This is difficult to explain in words, so hoping it is clear. With this armband, you typically slip the strap through a slot on the opposite side, and then wrap the strap back around to stick the velcro. If you have smaller arms than this permits, you can slip the strap farther through the slot, and just fold the strap and stick the velcro on the outside of the slot. So instead of wrapping the strap around the slot and attaching the velcro, just fold it and attach it on the other side of the slot than normal. You'll have a little loop of the strap dangling, but at least it will fit snug. With this method, you could get it to fit tiny arms.We do wish it had more of a lip at the top to cover the iPhone, so the top of the device has at least some mediocre protection from the elements (e.g., water/sweat trickling down the arm). The back of the armband pocket can get moist too, which also means the back of your device will get wet too. Not sure why Belkin did not add a plastic liner to the back of the pocket, I guess we could add our own plastic back out of a sandwich bag or something, but it definitely seems like an oversight.In addition, we've had some issues with Belkin's armbands in the past where the glued seams do not last long. This armband has similar seams, so we are hoping we don't have similar issues. So far, all is well. Just be careful inserting your device. Don't stretch the seams too much. Be careful with the velcro strips too. Easy does it.In any event, it is a worthy armband and we'll keep using it and abusing it.

reviewText: This is a really great screen protector for the iPhone 4. Once properly applied, it is crystal clear and feels better than the iPhone's glass screen.  You still get fingerprints on the screen.  However, I haven't seen any crystal clear (as apposed to the matte finish) screen protectors that truly are oleophobic.  Very happy.Now the application is a bit of a challenge, as is with any screen protector.  I installed it in a laminar flow hood (i.e., dust-free cabinet), and I stilled managed to get 2 piece of dust near the outer rim (These must have been transferred by the nitrile gloves I was wearing).  No biggy; I was able to peel up the corners and pull the dust off using the sticky sheets included with the screen protector.My advice, use the wet application method. I used wet solution included with another screen protector.  However, you can make your own by adding a tiny bit of mild soap (unscented, uncolored) to deionized water (buy some distilled water from the grocery store) and putting it in a spray applicator.  You can read instructions on the wet application method elsewhere online.  But by application a liberal amount of solution to the screen and the iPhone, you can slide the protector for a few seconds to position it properly before it adheres.  Also, I think it helps prevent dust.  Don't freak out if it looks like there are tons of bubbles.  These dissipate within a day or two.

This is my personal choice for screen protectors. The included accessories are the best part: a large and high quality microfiber cloth and 2 dust/particle removal strips. This is the easiest solution to get a perfect application of screen protection for the front and back of your iPhone.

reviewText: This Kensington "Universal Windshield/Vent Car Mount" is one of the handiest gadgets I have come across in a lone time! Here are my observations:+ Good Materials; while mostly plastic, this is well made and heavy enough to give me confidence to trust my expensive equipment in it+ Long Neck on Window Holder; gives the ability to position it at an optimal viewing place, even on deep windshields (like on my van)+ Strong Suction Cup on Window Holder; this draws a good, solid vacuum and resisted my testing attempts to pull it off+ Handy Vent Mount; included for states where window mounts are not legal (California and Minnesota are listed in the instructions), but I like it because it is fairly small can be easily carried in my PC case for use in rental cars when traveling+ Rotatable; both mounting options allow the device to be rotated 360 degrees, which is handy when using the EVO as a GPS+ Fits All of My Devices; my EVO, BlackBerry, and iPod Touch fit well, even in their casesI was lucky enough to pick this up on a "Gold Box" sale but am seriously considering picking up a second one, even if it is full price.Highly Recommended!CFH

reviewText: I bought the dash mount version of this item, but the holder is identical. reviewText: These work fantastic but i noticed that almost everyone who buys suction cup thingies complains that they eventually fail (they usually do).  If you don't have window tinting on the inside, i have a tip that will make the suction cup stick forever, just drop a dot of glue on there (crazy glue is best).  yes, I know what you're thinking but actually getting crazy glue off glass, should you ever decide to remove it, is not difficult, it scrapes right off with a razor - provided of course you don't have window tinting on the inside.  To test  that if you're not sure, just find a discrete location on the window and gently poke at it with a sharp point - if there's any resistance, you have plastic film tinting on your window and therefore it's a NO GO.  If the razor or pointy thing will NOT bite into the window, it's glass, and you're not going to scratch it with a razor blade (use a new razor blade - I suppose it's possible to scratch it with a useless old and dodgy one).  Razors are what glass people (glaziers) use to clean windows so, there's your tip.
summary: a tip to make suction cups work forever

reviewText: In southwest Ohio, it's not unusual for winter temperatures to be in the 10 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit range.  I keep this Kensington windshield mount in the car during those times, and find that it won't attach to my windshield when it's too cold.  I suspect that the problem is that the suction cup material is less flexible in cold temperatures.  A solution could be to keep the mount indoors until I'm ready to use it, but I have a hard enough time keeping track of my car keys, so I don't think that option will work for me.  Another possibility is the included vent mount.  I found the mount to be awkward and obtrusive in our car (2009 Subaru Forester)...I had difficulty mounting it...and besides, I really purchased this for the windshield mount.When the temperature warms up, the windshield mount works extremely well.  I find it to be very stable, and very easy to secure and remove my iPhone, and to attach it to a charger.  It works well as my GPS device in both portrait and lanscape orientations.  The price on this was really good, so I'm happy to have it for 9 months of every year.

These chargers do not short the D+/D- signal lines to tell the device being powered that they are chargers rather than data connections, so a modern device like an iPhone or Android phone will not take the full available current from the device. So they are limited to 500mA rather than 900mA so they power but will not simultaneously charge a modern smart phone.From the Wikipedia page for USB: "The Dedicated Charging Port shorts the D+ and D- pins with a resistance of at most 200 '. The short disables data transfer, but allows devices to detect the Dedicated Charging Port and allows very simple, high current chargers to be manufactured."When I power a Samsung Galaxy S phone with this it sees it as a data port and offers to connect as a mass storage or media device, as expected for an incorrectly wired charger.

I took some fine sandpaper, placed it flat on a table, and then ran the top and bottom surfaces for the iPhone connecter (the wide surface, not the smaller side surfaces) until it fit through the case properly.  Took 2 minutes, there is plenty of plastic on the connector so this does not cause problems.NOTE ABOUT SANDING... you will sand off the little icon which tells you which end up to insert into the phone, to address that I just scratched a little triangle into the surface where the icon was with a knife... actually a better solution than the printed icon because I now know without looking which end up goings into the phone.One caveat to note about this cable, the charger piece that plugs into the lighter does not stick very far out from the lighter, it is a bit difficult to remove this piece from the lighter socket.  if Kensington made the edges a little rougher, or hard ridges of some type, it could be easier to grip when removing.Enjoy!

But with the stones on it, it actually helps improve her grip on the phone because it has texture and prevents it from falling out of her hands as easily as some of the smooth cases.  It fits the phone well and has held up fairly well. The stones are large and easy to spot when they fall off so a dab of krazy glues easily holds them back in place. reviewText: I love this battery!  It gives me 8-12 hours extra life over the standard 4-8 hour battery.  Typically I get anywhere from 8-10 hours extra over an 8 hour period. That is playing games, surfing the web, emailing, and occasionally navigation,  BLUETOOTH stays on.  before I had an app killer and got maybe 5 hours of use before it DIED!

Not sure what happened but I bought this battery just a month ago. First 2 weeks was awesome, didn't even have to charge for 2 days and that's watching videos with my little one. The last week has been horrid!! Won't hold a charge any longer than the stock battery, drops to like 50% after a couple of hours of doing nothing with it AND all of a sudden, my network is busy, dropping calls left and right. My phone was working perfect before I installed this new battery. I am definitely disappointed and felt I wasted $57.00 :-( I am waiting for the seller to approve my return and I'm just going to have to deal with the stock battery rather than throw away my money. Not recommending - sorry!
