reviewText: Ran this thing for almost two years I guess on my Evo4G, it's a tank.  It lasts forever.  It MADE that phone.Unless the size really, really bugs you, you'll wonder why the heck you didn't buy one sooner.
This battery gives me 3 days of power with simple use. With full load, at end of day I'm still showing 50% power.  Much better than the 6 to 10 hours on the standard battery.

Finally got my Seidio 3500 mAh for my EVO. I have small hands but the extended back never touches my palm when I hold it. I had it off the charger for 10 hours and I have 62% battery life. I was on the internet with 4G, sent texts, and watched some video. I haven't conditioned the battery yet just charged it for 8 hours then let it charge for 3 additional hours. The battery discharges about 1 to 2% an hour on standby. Oh the back extended cover fits tighter than the original.When the light on your EVO turns green remember "Green means Go a little longer" if you have the time you should continue to charge the battery for an additional 2-3 hours to get the full capacity of your battery for that day.Seidio said the battery performance will increase even more after 5 to 6 full charges. Now 10 hours and 13 minutes and it is still at 62%. I am  using the Athene Task Killer from Andriod Market. So far the battery does what I want it to do keep my EVO running longer. If you have a facebook account look at HTC EVO fan page for tips on your phone.
summary: Green means Go a little longer

reviewText: Just got this battery yesterday. I was running a $9 version that I was unhappy with. I guess you get what you pay for. The stock battery would charge from empty in about an hour and a half. The old extended life battery took about two and a half hours. This battery took a little over five hour last night, and it wasn't fully discharged when I plugged it in. So far today I've had 4G on all day along with streaming music with Pandora to a Bluetooth headset for about five hours. I unplugged the phone at 6am and it is about 10pm now and I'm still at 60%  seems to be about twice the capacity of my old battery. I bought it along with the clip case and I'm also quite happy with that so far. The clip almost doubles the size of the phone, but its an EVO. I wasn't exactly looking for a small phone.Edit: so my phone finnally gave out and shut down.  At 745pm.  On the second day.  37hours 45 minutes!  that is easily twice the runtime I was getting out of my old "extended life" battery and almost 3 times the stock battery.  I was again today running my bluetooth all day, streaming pandora, and using the phone for about 30 emails, 10 texts, and almost 2 dozen phone calls.  I am blown away at the increase in performance.  Now Sprint needs to start shipping the phone with this battery as an upgrade at least if not just the factory battery.Second opinion on the case : not sure I will keep using it.  its HUGE and the part that catches the clip is rubber.  I've had a lot of bad luck with the clip poking in between the rubber and the phone.  It holds the phone fine that way, no dropping the phone to complain about.  But as soon as the clip is under the rubber its a pain to get it untangled from the phone and off of the holster.

This is a review for the HTC EVO - Seidio does make batteries for other HTC devices.What this battery brings to the Evo is remarkable - it makes this device immensely more useful.  Everyone knows the Evo battery is dead within eight hours with normal usage.  In the morning, when I take it off the charger, it's down to 80% before I get to the office with just basic usage.  Throw in calls and 4G and some emails and the phone is getting hammered.  The 3500 mAh battery is what the phone was designed for, and vice versa.  My battery monitor tells me I have an estimated 18 hours of use at 85% charge - before this, my monitor was never able to estimate more than nine hours usage!  Truly a huge improvement.Now's the time to get this battery, too.  A couple months ago it was nearly $70 - now it's less than $50.  Quite frankly, Sprint and HTC should be offering this battery as some kind of upgrade when you buy the phone for like another $25.  Selling the Evo with the stock battery makes no sense.  This is a monster phone with speed and brains and extended capabilities - it's needs juice and the stock battery is not up to the task.One thing to keep in mind when you get this thing is that it's not at full capacity right away.  You do have to charge it a few times, use it, charge it again and use it.  After a couple days you'll notice your battery monitor reporting the proper estimated usage.  Even the documentation mentions charging the battery completely a few times to get the max capacity out of it.Another thing is there aren't any other third party cases out there for this size battery.  Pretty much gonna have to use this thing naked when you get it, unless you want that expensive case Seidio sells for the extended battery.Recommended!UPDATE:I am using Batteryminder 2.7 for the phone - even though it's the best app Ive found for what I want - I hate the widgets - I am not sure it's reading the new battery as precisely as it could.  Just a hunch.  Battery indicator seems to show a percentage that draining quickly although it will still say I have 18+ hours usage left.  Still evaluating.
summary: Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended Life Battery

reviewText: Considering that I had to charge my phone twice a day with the standard battery and now only once a day with this one, I'm a happy guy. I'm using the Laza case with this as well and it has been great so far.If weight or bulkiness is an issue for you then don't get this because it's both of those. It's not an issue for me though but something to consider.

I'm still in the process of conditioning my extended battery, but oh my god, it's only been 3 days so far, and the battery is slowly starting to improve ALOT!!!Today, I spent just about over 12 hours of just playing around with the phone, facebooking, heavy internet browsing, and wireless tethering for a friend's laptop, while he surfs the internet, and I left my GPS on (not if that makes any difference to everyone else) but MAN!I love it!

I've had my evo since launch day and due to all the internet surfing, slingbox use, games, etc. my battery usually didn't last until the end of the day.  I bought this Seidio Innocell 3500 hoping to fix that.  It has worked as advertised and exceeded my expectations.  Now I can easily get two full days of power while not worrying about what I do.  Sure if I stream Slingbox for hours it depletes faster but it is so much better than the stock battery!  I was skeptical as I had never bought a third party battery before for a phone but this battery is just top notch.  It does add a little size to the back but it was not nearly as bad as I thought.  I don't mind the extra size at all as the tradeoff is more than worth it.  The battery cover provided with the battery is actually very nice.  I actually like it better than the stock cover as the Seidio cover is more rubberized and easier to grip.  Overall if you have the EVO I highly recommend this extended battery!
summary: This battery is the real deal!

reviewText: its key to follow the instuctions upon installing the battery. this battery last at 5-6 hour more and that's with heavy talk text and web use and some lite 4g use. it charges in the same amount of time as standard battery. only con is it makes the phone bigger and heavier. not really a care of mine.
summary: Good investment if you're on the go.

reviewText: This Seidio "3500mAh Extended Life Battery" works much better than expected and actually contributed to my decision to keep my EVO. While I really like the EVO, particularly it's MyFi (sharing Internet) capability, the limited life of the stock battery made it impractical to use on long trips if an outlet to plug the charger into wasn't available. With the stock battery, it was lucky to get three hours or so out of casual use out of it and far less if an App kept the screen on (like a game or GPS). This Seidio battery lasts much longer! Here are my observations:Pros -+ Long Battery Life; the only one that really matters - I have kept the screen on for over four hours straight and the EVO still showed 25% charge remainingCons -- Size; this is much heavier and bigger than the stock battery so it requires changing out the EVO back with the included replacement- Standard Case Will Not Fit; due to the increased size, I needed a new case (Seidio Innocase Extended Case for HTC EVO 4G (for use with Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended Life Battery))Misc -* The instructions advise that the battery will perform best after it has been recharged 5 or 6 timesThis battery allows me to use the EVO like it was intended to be used!Highly Recommended!CFH
summary: Seriously Long Lasting EVO Battery - Highly Recommended!

reviewText: I guess for all the 5 stars folks, they've said it all. Awesome battery life! With the 1500mAh OEM pack, it just does not do it. I have this thing running getting acquainted with the phone and about 3 hours, I blinking for more juice.The seidio just rocks. I had this thing about probably 6 hours including a 4G encounter and I must say I was very impressed. The quality for the case was way above par. The biggest gain is the protection of the camera lens. The OEM just had the lens rests on the surface, which is prone to scratch. A bit heavy but it feels like you are holding something very solid. As for the solid battery life, see the preceding comments as I have similar experiences. Now, I just wish they make a leather case for this thing. One happy Seidio customer.
summary: The king of Batteries is finally here

reviewText: Sure it adds bulk and weight to the phone, but the battery life nearly doubled! So pleased with the results.

This product speaks for itself. Before this battery i used to get about 8hrs of battery on my EVO, upon installing this battery i would get anywhere from 2-3 days of battery life before i would have to plug it into a charger. The 2 - 3 days are with moderate to heavy usage of the phone, that is with WI-FI on, bluetooth on, playing music for about 2-4hrs a day and browsing the internet and email. This battery is great i would definitely recommend it, i was actually recommended this battery by my friend
summary: Real definition of an extended battery

reviewText: Battery door fits perfectly, everything was easy to install.  The battery door is more difficult to remove than the stock...it's a very good nice tight fit and I don't think it's going anywhere.  It also has a rubbery feel so it doesn't make you feel like the phone is going to slip out of your hands.  The edges of the door come out on 3 sides around the camera so the camera is also protected when you set the phone down on the back.At first the battery didn't last noticeably longer than stock but after a few recharges I noticed a pretty good increase in the life.  I bought this a little over 3 months ago and didn't write any review then. The reason I'm writing now is because the battery cover is starting to wear down.  What's happening is the rubber-like texture on the back is wearing down to a slick plastic. It started with the edges but now it's getting to the point where every time I remove it from my pocket there are tiny bits of that rubber-like material all over the back of the phone.  It's pretty annoying and will get to the point where I'll just have to scrape it all off.As far as weight goes, it's already a pretty beefy phone so what's a couple extra ounces??Other than that this battery and door set is awesome and serves its purpose well!  I would definitely recommend it if you're looking for longer battery life.If you can get a case to fit over the the phone while the extended battery is installed (Seidio makes this as well) then put that entire fitting in your pocket or on a holster, it would most likely protect the condition and extend the life of the battery door. If I could do it again I would have purchased the case to go around it all as well.
summary: Overall great product for a good price

reviewText: The battery that ships with the HTC EVO is severely too small.  I would get anywhere from 4 hours to 8 hours of battery life (yes, I had GPS, WiFi, 4G, Bluetooth, all enabled---What's the point of having a smartphone if you can't enable all of it's features).  With the 3500 mAh battery from Seidio, I can now go all day, 7AM-midnight without needed to charge. (sometimes it gets as low as 8% but for 17 hours of use, that's pretty good)  I would recommend this to anyone that is concerned with battery life on their HTC EVO.  It is worth the money unless you are tied to the charger 3 times a day, or don't mind shutting down all the services that make your smartphone work.  If you are looking for an extended battery, this is the one to get.

Works incredibly well; whereas with the original battery I had to recharge it mid day, this one last. I unplug it from the charger at 6:00AM in the morning, and by 11:00PM the same evening, the battery meter still shows 65% remaining with this battery. The weight is barely noticeable and in fact, extra bulge makes it more easier to grip.Only complaint I have is the price for this. Other manufacturer sell similar product in the $35 to $45 range.
summary: Great Product; wish it was cheaper.

reviewText: I initially bought the inexpensive extended battery for the EVO 4G, and thought it was OK, but wasn't very satisfied with the charge it held. I tried draining and fully charging it multiple times but after a month of heavy use it seemed to just get lower and lower in battery life. I could watch the level going down percentage by percentage on the battery widget I have. So I bought the Seidio battery instead and am much, much happier. I use my EVO a lot, with every feature full-on and the Seidio lasts a full day easily. Go for the name brand and you can trust the quality.
summary: You get what you pay for

reviewText: Yep battery life is a problem with most PDA phones.  The solution for most people with a standard battery is to modify their phone settings and limit use.  For those of us who do not care to limit use there is this honking battery.  I charge my phone every night and now I never have to worry about it during the day.I'd like to know if there is a charging pad that will work with this bad boy, that'd be sweet (huh huh huh!).

The look of this product installed is not that bad. Not super sleek, but the increased battery life is worth the looks and much more! I followed the instructions fully draining the battery and charging it over night 5x to get max life from the battery. This was not easy because the battery was very difficult to drain right out of the package. Definitely worth the trouble though. My phone lasts almost 2 full days on a single charge. I never need to go that far because I also got the innotraveler car dock which charges the phone while looking sweet and holding your bump-back EVO perfectly secure. I also have the innocase cover,which may not cover the top and bottom of the phone, but still protects and fits in the dock perfectly. This whole outfit is almost as cool as the EVO itself! Worth it's weight in gold!!!
summary: Stock EVO battery sucks...this 1 dose not!

reviewText: I received this battery about four days ago. The first day, it drained very fast and appeared to offer no more charge than the standard battery. I contacted Seidio customer service and they confirmed to let this battering drain to the point where my device will shutdown automatically, charge again and repeat two times for a total of three cycles to condition the battery. PLEASE NOTE: some reviews have said NOT to do this but this is wrong information. Seidio says TO DO this for three cycles. Today, I am on 60% and the battery has not been charged for 24 hours! MAGNIFICENT! Buy this battery! If you have poor performance at first, let it drain down funtil your evo powers off automatically and recharge three times and then it should start working very well. I am on 3G, Mobile Network Data, GPS Enabled. I have listened to music on it for about a half hour yesterday, watched a few youtube videos averaging about 10min, use gps navigation for about 30 min as well as constant use with tweetdeck notifications all day and texting -and internet browsing for a total of an hour. I talked a total of an hour and a half as well on the phone. Not shabby.UPDATE 9/28/10After weeks of use this battery gets better and better. I can use this device heavily all day and get two days out of easily. When I am using it moderately, it lasts three days. This is will GPS on. Network Data on, Screen is at Automatic and Bluetooth on. My screen is set to timeout at 1 min and I do run live wallpaper. I talk and text all day on the phone. I just looked at the battery time and it has been unplugged now for two days, two hours and twenty seven minutes and has 55% left. I browse my web, and use the facebook and twitter all day on this phone. Stellar!
summary: Working great but needs a few cycles to get up to speed b patient.

reviewText: This saved my EVO. The phone was worthless without the extended battery.  Seiko makes the best phone products there are.

So this shipped like OVERNIGHT .. NEXT DAY .. I got it in the evening.  Stuck it in the charger around 9:00 PM.  Awoke and put it in my phone around 8:00 AM.  Around 7:00 PM today I am like 75% so I turned on WIFI, 4G, GPS and Bluetooth to try and drain it.  8:30 I am still at 62%.*** One week later ***  They say you should drain this completely and recharge fully to get the best performance.  I have a hard time draining it.  In a whole day, I leave on GPS, WIFI, Bluetooth and 4G ... the phone is still at 70% as I'm ready for bed.I used to carry around TWO spares, one of them a SUPPOSED "extended life 3500mAh" battery I bought here for six bucks or so.  I felt embarrassed at customer sites asking for a charge during meetings.  I would run up and down Amtrak cars looking for a window seat so I could charge my phone.NO MORE !!!!  This battery changes my relationship to my phone. It changes my life for the better.

THIS BATTERY IS IT.WHEN I FIRST GOT MY EVO I HAD EVERYTHING RUNNING.YOUTUBE,ETC.I DIDN'T CLOSE APPS SO MY BATTERY WOULD DIE IN 3OR 4 HOURS.WHEN I LEARNED ABOUR APP KILLER IT GOT BETTER.SO I ORDERED THIS BATTERY AND ALL IS RIGHT WITH THE WORLD.I LISTEN TO MY LOCAL RADIO STATIONS IN CLEVELAND OVER THE INTERNET FOR OVER 8 HOURS!!!! MAN THIS BATTERY BRINGS OUT THE BEAST IN THE EVO.AND IT CAN STILL FIT IN MY POCKET.SO DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND GET ONE AND ENJOY YOUR EVO.JUST DONT FORGET TO GET A APP KILLER
This made my phone tolerable by doubling the time I could be on battery vs. the original battery but also doubled the size of the phone which was annoying but also made the phone easier to hold.

I'm a firm believer that this phone needs a car battery in order to get a good amount of use in a day out of it.  Please don't take this wrong, the phone is AMAZING, its ahead of its time (and that in turn is its main problem).  The batteries today just cannot power such a powerful phone.  Why should I have to power off Bluetooth, 4G, screen brightness, etc to make the phone last longer?  Doesn't that take away from the use of the phone.To preface, the battery DOES help.  It makes the phone look ridiculous, but it helps greatly.  On standby, this battery works great so long as the phone doesn't heat up.When I realized the battery couldn't handle the phone:On a trip about 2 hours away, I used it to listen to music stored on the phone (not Pandora) had 4G off, Bluetooth off, and GPS & WiFi on.  About an hour or so into the trip, the phone had dropped to 43% (we left at 6:30 and by 8:00 the phone's battery was more than 1/2 drained).  I stopped listening to music, but got the occasional text message.By 12:00 I needed to turn the phone off to preserve any battery left for emergencies.  I turned it back on at 6:00 to have less than 10% left in the phone.If you need a phone off the battery for most of the day, I'd keep a spare with you (or consider a different phone).  If you can be near a car charger or wall charger during the day, then you should be fine.Again, its really too bad that this phone is so great, but battery technology really isn't there yet to power such a power-hungry device.
summary: Its not the battery, its the phone...

reviewText: I am lukewarm toward Seidio's batteries and, more importantly, their claims about battery power. I have their earlier, lower capacity extended battery and didn't think it offered much, if any, better performance than the stock Evo 4G battery. With earlier HTC phones, I noticed the same thing.I gave this battery its first real workout on an out-of-town trip on which I was constantly using data and voice. It worked well. At the end of a long, hard day, the Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended-Life Battery was showing about 40% capacity remaining. My regular and lower capacity Seidio batteries would have been dead earlier in the day.So, for the moment, I am moderately pleased with this product. Still need to work it hard for a few days with playing videos, streaming music  and such to give it a real workout, but so far, so good.The extended battery door  feels a little on the flimsy side. It ss surprisingly difficult to remove and I was afraid I'd snap off the two retaining pins at the bottom. So far I haven't, but I suspect it won't be long before I do.As it is with most Seidio products, I feel that this battery is overpriced, especially when you look at other lesser-name vendors. But that's simple enough: I'll try one of the cheaper batteries and compare the two. Can't ever have too many smartphone batteries, can you?Jerry

I've had this extended-life battery for over a month now, thinking now would be a good time to share my experience.  It's been great!.  My stock battery would last about 24 hours with minimum use, but this extended life battery has gone over 3 days on a single charge, and battery indicator is still showing 50% available.  I'm not what people would consider a real power user, but it's constantly checking and updating my g-mail account, exchange mail, and all the other typical HTC syncing applications.  In my 3 days of use, I've read several blogs and newspaper applications, popped the browser several times, updated apps daily, checked the weather conditions including radar maps/maps in motion, sent several text messages, read and responded to e-mails, scheduled appointments, writing back to the exchange server, and played a few games.  Oh yeah, even took several phone calls in and dial outs as well.  I've added a picture to prove my statement in this review.  If you've had battery longevity issues like I had, buy this battery, follow the 10 hr by 5 time charging recommendation, and I'm sure you'll get it too.

I read just about every review of this before purchasing, and I can tell you after a full day of use that there is no debate. If you own a EVO you should own this as well. I am running everything (WiFi, 4G Bluetooth, etc) and 7 hours later I am still at 83% battery. AMAZING!
summary: The reviews are right, this thing is the real deal!

reviewText: just got mine today, quick question did anyone else get there battery with like 75% of battery charged, cause the instructions say to charge for 8 hours but if i charge a already almost full battery for 8 hours wont it break? well please answer somebody cause i would like to know if amazon sent me a used product because the packaging put this product at a dis advantage because there easy to open and reseal without damaging the casing. so im just curious if someone got this product for a while decided to return it saying its unopened and just packaged it the same and then i bought it! so please let me know if any of you got yours with that much charge. thank you.  p.s. be back in a week or two with a full review 5 stars for now :D
Great product, it really did increase my phoone life by a whole day. The cover was not that large that it couldn't be dealt with.
summary: Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended-Life Battery for HTC EVO 4G - Black

reviewText: I have only had this battery a week but I was so impressed that I wanted to post a review. I took the battery out of the box and charged it to full overnite on the 1st nite I got it in the mail. I used it the next down and drained it all the way down. After that I charged it overnite while fully charged and the next day it was giving me double the battery life that I was used to.I use my phone during the day for texting, internet surfing, email, and as a mobile WiFi spot. The mobile WiFi was killing my battery in 4 hours or less and I was running from charger to charger. Now I can use my phone without hesitation and get a full days use on one charge. I use Google maps with the navigation feature and mobile WiFi a lot and those things seemed to drain my battery in no time. Now I don't even use my car charger and this battery is on pace with the 10 hours my iPad battery gets on a single charge with heavy usage.The only negative and reason it didn't give it a 5 star review is due to the bulk of the battery. It took me a few days to get used a big phone getting even bigger. The extra battery life is worth the bulk but I must be honest and give a full review.

Product worked as advertised at first, nearly doubling the battery life, then I experienced a sharp dropoff in battery life to where I was at the same charge levels at the end of the day as with the OEM HTC battery. Returned it.I'll stick with carrying a charger around with me from now on, this just isn't worth it.

With everthing turned on: GPS, Wifi, BT, 100% screen, sync etc... I still have at least 75-80% after 8-10 hours. My only beef is that cases becomes very difficult to find. I have an Amzer rubber case for it before and I had to cut out a rectangular shape from the back to make it fit. It works great! Its like bumper for the iphone, i now have it on mt Evo.Great battery. Don't hesitate if you're debating on getting one. I sold the original battery on eBay for $23. I got lucky on this here at Amazon. I purchased it a week before it came out for $53 with shipping. But even at $60+, it's really worth it.Update 11/18/11:I bought this 4 months ago and now, this battery just last the same time as the OEM battery. It was great at first but now, I'm back to the OEM battery. I don't know if anyone has the same problem.
summary: Great battery! This should have been the standard battery.

reviewText: This is a great product. Made my phone usable past 12pm. The only con was it made the phone very bulky and heavy.

I was cautious to get this battery because of the added bulk and weight to my Evo.  I have had the Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended Life Battery for HTC EVO for 3 days, and it's great to not be concerned about carrying around a spare battery (or two), an AC charger, and car charger.  So I'm not really bothered by the extra weight of the extended battery, since I don't have to carry a bag of supplies with me to keep this beast alive!I'm  a new smart phone user, and a geek, so I'm still  getting to know my  phone.  I've got it all turned on:  WIFI, GPS, 4g, Blue-Tooth, while downloading and installing/uninstalling new apps to try.  At the end of the day, the Seidio Extended battery still has a 40%-50% charge.For the past month, I tried the stock HTC battery w/ a couple of spares and chargers, and found it to be high maintenance to  keep my eyes the battery gauge, only to watch it run out after 6-7 hours. I tried turning things on and off (as researched and recommended by the Evo/Droid websites), but even just having the Evo sit around without use, the stock battery drained dry anyway.I bought the Evo to use everything all at once. I'm  paying for unlimited voice and data, and don't want to have to monitor what I'm using, and juggle turning things on and off all day to preserve the battery.Well worth it. Also purchased Seidio Innocase Extended Rugged Holster Combo for HTC EVO 4G, which I really like.-------------6 month updateThe battery is starting to lose juice.  It's not lasting as long as it once did, which is fairly expected since I'm a heavy user, but 6 months?

No complaints about the battery itself. It last all day w/o any problems. I personally think it's a bit pricey for a backup battery. One thing I didn't like was the form factor of the cover. It protrude out at a 90 degree angle where the battery sticks out. The sudden protrusion can be kind of annoying because it doesn't seem as smooth of a curvature and very noticeable when you are a guy wearing jeans and taking the phone in and out of your pockets. [...]This may sound a little too involved but it's a big deal if you are wearing jeans and trying to keep this in your pocket all day. The phone is big enough as it is. But if you don't care about form factor or cost, than the Seidio is fine and will do the job.
summary: good for the phone since stock battery is terrible

reviewText: its a great battery. I've had it for two years now and it still works fine. I use it on and off because it is bulky, but nonetheless this gives you a ton of extra battery life. If you keep your 4g and gps off, this will probably go all weekend without recharging.

I get almost 2 full days of charge with my Evo with this battery.I used to have to plug it in @ lunch time with the stock battery because it wqould already be down to 60 or 50%, but with this new battery it is still in 85-95% charge @ lunch time.This is a must buy + the battery cover protects your camera lens, makes it easier to hold when you are talking on the phone, and is more sturdy than the stock battery door.

I've decided to remove the 3-page long review I had.  Here's the short of it.  This battery will last approx 2.5-4 times as long as the default battery. I do not know how people claim to be getting days of use out of it, I can squeeze a day of decent use out of it.  This is all I needed it to do since I charge at night anyway.Some things to note for battery life - I've been told by Seido online tech support (the chat client) to just charge it and not let the thing discharge completely, that the thing has no "memory" so, that combined with what other people say, do as you will.Charge the thing up 8 hours if you can to begin with.Learn some battery-saving tips that are counter-intuitive3g data transfer seems to take the most juice by far (of my tests)turn on wifi if you have it available.  Data going over wifi uses much less power than data over 3g (transmittiing 50 feet as opposed to a quarter mile). If you're not doing email synch and downloading stuff and syncing with FB/Twitter you can probably leave it off.turn off automatic task-killers - they don't help.  I suggest you do have a task killer, but it not be running.  Most programs behave in the background and unless you root your phone you're not going to be able to remove the sprint bloatware.4G - no idea, I cant tell if it drains the battery significantly or not - I pay $10 extra a month for 1 bar of 4g that goes out when the wind blows.GPS - leave it on, leave it off, you're not going to notice any difference except when a program needs GPS coordinates.Haptic feedback (vibrating when you press a key) - turn it off for texting - if you don't know if you pressed the key or not by looking at the screen it's probably not helping you much anyway.  I do not know how much juice this saves, but that's a little motor that spins to vibrate your phone, gotta be something.With wifi off, 4g off, gps off and playing around - movies, angry birds, word feud, texting, twitter, email sync, I get about 12 hours before I notice the thing's in the 20's.With GPS on, wifi on, 4g off (it really sucks in my area so no reason to have it on), a 5 minute call every hour or so, tweeting, facebook, email sync, couple of youtube videos I get an average battery drain or 4% per hour. or roughly 25 hours of use.Your mileage may vary, I would love to know how to get the battery life the #1 reviewer has - I turned everything off, even airplane mode pulls ~3% an hour which is nowhere near the days worth of life claimed.For the record I've tried auto task killers, they seem to help when the thing is sluggish, but not help any on the battery.  I've tried Juiceminder, which gave me ~20% more battery but no longer works (for me, probably will for you - long fun story) and was causing the phone to be sluggish for 30 seconds after waking up (it was worth it).So yeah, I'm leaving GPS and wifi on all the time when I'm at home or work and not charging the thing except at night.  When I'm out not around an access point I turn wifi off (not sure how much that helps).  GPS applications seem to drain the battery the fastest (google maps / earth in sat mode use an buttload of data, which usually is going over 3g - so put them in non-sat-view mode)
summary: An ongoing review of the powerhouse

reviewText: So the reason I bought this was because my rear cover was already cracking.  I notice this is more apparent on the white evos than the black ones.  I also want to go a whole day of heavy usage w/o charging.  I figure this is a great combo and I don't mind the size or weight.  I can basically last a whole day of using 3g data / texting (about 40) / and listening to mp3s (4 hours on average), this is all on OEM rom.Pros: longer battery life.  I will say my OEM battery was near the end of its life.  Also the back is much like the black evos so it's got a rubbery texture with it.  Everything still works as a normal oem cover (kickstand, LED, and camera).  This also helps protect the camera more. This also works with the seidio car dock for the evo 4g w/o modification. That last part was one of the biggest selling points.Cons: Doesn't come in white (I guess that's more of a personal preference). It's obviously heavier and makes your phone almost twice as thick.  The cover is also very hard to take off.  It feels as if it's about to break so I don't remove the cover and clean the phone as much as I used to.Overall a great product but I feel like most people will probably have a new phone or buy spare cheap OEM batteries.
summary: Great if you want longer battery life.

reviewText: this battery lasts 2 days with a full charge with me. compared to the factory battery that i can only get 3-4hrs max out of. very happy with the purchase i made. this battery really makes the evo come alive and i like the back cover too. fits very nicely on the phone and looks oem. i've had this battery in my phone for a month now and i have no complaints. very well made battery.
ok, this battery is fine but i found one that is exactly like it (with a better looking back cover) that is significantly cheaper.[SHIPS FAST!] HTC Evo 4G 3500mAh Extended Battery + Cover
summary: way too expensive! cheaper alternatives available

reviewText: It worked well for me. I never noticed it discharging quicker than when I first bought it. Battery would last me all day with moderate to heavy use and still go on the charger overnight with about 15% left. I upgraded to a new phone and had to retire this one.

I recieved this battery about a year ago. worked great till about 3 months ago, When it was new it kept a charge for over 48hours, now it bare works for 4hours. I cant find a way to get in touch with the seller, so it looks like im S.O.L.

The only flaw I have found with my HTC EVO 4G has been battery life. On a normal day (working in the office), I have to plug my phone into a charger on the desk to top it off so it will make it through the day. When traveling, I have to bring a spare battery. No big deal, it's worth the sacrifice, but without recharging or changing batteries, my phone would only make it through the lightest of days.This battery changes everything. I made it through the entire weekend last weekend (granted, light use). And halfway through the day I am at 84% on a light day today. Normally I'd be below 40%.The back does look flimsier so I'm going to leave it on as much as possible -- hopefully, light handling will mean long life. But it's still comfortable to hold, fits into my holster case, and works like the phone should.If you're even looking at this battery, you're questioning the battery life you're getting with the standard battery. Stop reading, hit the "buy" button, and get on with your life. This one is a no-brainer!

The battery is almost an essential with the HTC EVO - battery life on that phone is simply terrible.  But even with the extended life battery, the phone can barely hold a charge for a day.  The Seidio battery worked just as it was supposed to, but after a year, the battery life was noticeably shorter.  I understand this is normal for a phone battery, but I thought I should mention it.
summary: Life of phone is still short

reviewText: This is a wonderful battery.  It works as advertised and maybe even better for me.  Customer service was great because I had a few questions about how to use the product and the website had an instant messaging chat feature.  I would recommend this battery to anyone that loves staying unplugged for long periods of time but does not mind the extra bulk that it adds to the phone.  For me, the bulkiness is really not that bad.  I like that I do not have to charge my phone for 3 days on light to normal use and about 1.5 days for normal to moderate use.  The battery is really worth it.  Make sure to read up on how to calibrate and charge the battery to maximize its capacity.

I recommend every Evo user to buy Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended-Life Battery. Battery does exactly what it says it does. I've also noticed that if i drain the battery once a week and fully recharge it; it last longer.
summary: Must buy for all Evo users

reviewText: It provided extended life for a few days only.  After that it functions about the same as the stock battery.  A waste of money.

i get 2 full days of full use. no more rationing my battery one bit, ive had it for almost a year, and i find that once it says battery full it really needs a few more hours to last for 2 days. but if i give it a full charge and charge it every night i never have a dead phone. but to b honest most nights i dont even bother plugging it in, this battery has made me lazy. this is a MUST if u hav an htc evo.o i should also add that the back fits my phone perfect, and actually feels more comfortable in my hand especially in landscape position. and fyi, my son dropped it from about 4 feet, it landed on the corner of the phone, screen shattered but the back didnt even pop off. although i do advise u be careful when removing the back if u ever need to, the clips do seem sensitive.loved it so much i bought one for my wifes epic
summary: i just wish it was more attractive

reviewText: This beats the battery that comes with the phone, that is for sure.  But mine is down to 60% charge after 5 hours on standby not doing anything.  That seems pretty retarded. And yes no other programs were running.  This phone only lasts about an hour and a half playing 3d games on my Evo.  So, it is "extended" from the original battery but I would have thought in this day and age that a battery company could do better than this.  Especially for over $50.  And the battery causes my phone to run hot.  Pretty darn hot actually, when I am using it.  I am still on the lookout for something better.
summary: It's alright but not as good as expected

reviewText: I bought this so that I could last the whole day without charging.  I would typically charge overnight and then disconnect at about 7am.  With medium to heavy use the phone would be at about 30-35% when I plugged it back in 16 hours later.  This went on for about 13 months at which point things went downhill.I would get a very big drop in power in less than an hour after unplugging and 12 hours after disconnecting the phone I would need to plug it back in as the charge would be at 15%.I do understand that these things have a certain life span but I was hoping that I could get more use out of it.This battery is too expensive to get another one for a phone that I may only keep for another 6 months as I am do for an upgrade though this phone still works great for me.My next decision is do I get a cheaper version of this battery which may not be as good as a product, do I get a two smaller batteries and swap out or do I get a powerstick that I can use for the EVO 4G or any other device I wind up getting in a few months.

I've loved my EVO 4G for over a year now, and the *only* real gripe I've had with the phone was its sub-par battery life.  This completely eliminates me having to plug in the phone for a battery freshening during the day--even with heavy email usage and travels around low-signal areas.Adds a bit of bulk, yes, but overwhelmingly worth it.  If you're right pleased with your EVO 4G and don't feel like upgrading to an EVO 3D just yet, don't pass up on this upgrade!

*Update* 5/1/2011The battery still works fine, but I now use it only when on extended trips. HTC has pushed out quite a few updates that have improved battery life tremendously, so I now use the OEM battery for everyday use.*Update*I followed the manufacturer recommendations and charged this 6 times to get the maximum amount of battery life. After a few days of testing using Battery Monitor I found I could get 24+ hours with 4G/GPS/Highest brightness on and 38+ hours with 3G/GPS/Highest brightness on before reaching the 5% warning.Original Review:I had been waiting for this battery to be released by Seidio for such a long time. To be honest the battery life of the OEM battery was horrible and I could only get around 8 hours of solid use out of my phone before my "5% until empty" warning came up. Now that I have this battery, I don't even worry about running out of power! I can have 4G running at all times and still get double what the OEM battery got and with 4G off the phone will last for days! The battery itself adds minimal weight to the phone.5/5 for the batteryThe backing that the battery comes with has the same soft touch coating that the OEM backing has, and has "SEIDIO" imprinted on the back. It adds about 3MM of thickness and it actually doesn't make the phone seem much more bulkier. In fact, texting is easier now with the extended backing because I can wrap my index fingers around it and stabilize the phone much better. The flash LEDs are not covered at all, the camera lens sits perfectly center, and the holes for the sound are sufficient and don't degrade the quality of sound when I play music.5/5 for the backingTo the person that said when taking a picture with flash it causes a washed out lower right in the picture, I tested this out in numerous conditions and never saw any washing out so you may have had your backing not on tight enough. Make sure that all the latches are snapped in around the case before you take pics.All in all, the extra thickness is worth it! Don't waste your money on the 1750 mAh "extended" batteries, they suck! Just get this one and you won't have to worry about running out of juice during the day ever again!Thanks for reading my review! Be sure to check out the customer images, I posted a handful of pics of the product!

Magnificent. I was ready to just flat out buy the newer phone sprint released and take a dive on size and 4g due to my stock battery life.I have had the new battery for about 48 hours now and have charged it once, when I installed it.Followed the directions and got about 12 hours out of it today, watching videos, texting making calls and had 4g and wifi on the whole time.Feels better in my hands, much more ergonomic that stock.I would recommend this to ALL EVO users. I have already had three friends order theirs today after spending the day shooting and uploading vidoes to youtube without the battery dieing shortly after.Now if there was just a gel case that covered the whole phone..

Initially after purchasing a EVO, I was very excited to find this extended life battery on Amazon.  I had used Seidio before with my blackberry Bold 9650 and that phone lasted for dayyyysss.  Unfortunately, I cannot say the same any longer with this battery.  For the first few weeks I was experiencing the great battery life as described but now after about 6 months of owning this battery I get down to about 70% after about 2 hours of my phone being off the charger.  I don't use it that much either really...I have gps and wifi turned off most of the time, wi fi is on at home usually.  I play minimal amount of games, do not watch much video on it and mainly just use it for facebook, email and the occasional news/sports scores updates.  I contacted the company months ago to see if I could get some sort of feedback as to why the battery was suffering from poor performance so soon after purchasing it but never got a reply from anyone.  I usually do not write reviews here but as an avid technology freak and educated consumer, I felt the need to share my experience of this product with other fellow consumers.By the way....I conditioned the battery exactly as instructed and I never let my phone sit on the charger overnight so from the time it was purchased the battery was treated properly.

I have had this battery for over a year now.  This battery is much better than the stock one.  The stock battery is a joke, there is no way HTC could have expected that battery to last more than a few hours with all of the features that the Android phone offers.  It is ridiculous that you have to turn most of the features off, find battery optimizer programs, and task killers, all in an effort to make the pathetic stock battery last for part of a day.  Now I can turn on everything on except for the live wallpaper, and have the phone easily last all day, even a year later.  I don't text excessively, but I do like to play games, make a few calls, check facebook and email, and just play with the phone part of the day.  Now it does add a little bulk to the phone, but it actually allows you to enjoy your Evo once again.  If you are tired of keeping your Evo tethered to a charger, get this battery and start enjoying your phone.

im sure im making a Review to soon. but so far it adds allot of life to the phone and I say so far because I hear allot of stories about them going bad after a while.  I don't think so but hope amazon allows more than one Review.  but all that said I can go two days of use and about 3 to 4 days standby Just doing nothing things like checking the mail.  I would say it only turns it into a normal phone as it was ment to be. im kind of old school the next phone I get will be a smart phone with a physical keyboard and nice and small. one I wont have to turn into a brick by adding a extended battery.

The life on this battery is just amazing. My wife has this battery and I have the 1750mAh. Her phone can go 3 days on one charge and I have to charge mine every night. My wife also likes the heavier wight and bulk as if feels more natural to holding her phone. Who know size really does matter?

As others have stated it worked good for a about a year, then slowly started to die on me very fast. It does add a lot of bulk to your phone so be prepared for that. Overall it was OK, but for the price I would have expected it to last at least the life of the phone.

We all know the obvious flaw and the most annoying one is the battery life. I knew that all too well because my battery reached half of it's capacity close to noon at school on Mondays and Wednesdays. I hate the fact that I had to bring the charger with me. Then, I wanted to go for a better battery and I decided to get the Acase despite having conflicting reports, but half the price of this battery. As soon as I got it and after about a week of use with it, I saw very little improvement and I felt disappointing with it because not only did the case bumped up the battery area, but the entire back! That was really annoying and I gave the Acase to my dad who found use of it for his Incredible and went back to the original stock battery after ordering this one. I was rather excited to see what this baby can do after reading all of the positive reviews for the Seidio. When I got it, it was much better packaged and more presentable than the Acase. I started to see it was a little better than the Acase, but was still disappointed. Then it started getting better and it still is! I really haven't let it die below 15% battery life yet. I really need to do that sometime to get better results. But I've left it on the charge over night and it does a great job. Yesterday, I went out to wifi on my laptop and had my phone with me. I checked texts and emails regularly and it went from the 84% to 70% within 4 hours. It tends to last the longest after getting under 90%. That's a lot better than the Acase or the stock battery. This phone doesn't stay at in the 90's range so much so you can forget about that, but I don't know yet because I still have to let it die down and charge it the more proper way. I'm sure it will last a lot longer if I do that. I also try to keep the wifi, bluetooth, etc. off on my phone whenever possible. I'm pretty confident I can get through the day without charging this phone now.I also know about the issue about not being able to fit a regular case on to the phone due to the extended battery. I ordered a blue Seidio Active case to do this hack I saw online where you can cut out the back on it. ;) I'll post pictures on here if I can so I can show you how it turns out. I'll also keep you updated on how the battery is doing, but so far, it's worth it to me =)Update: I'm happy to announce that i managed to keep my battery in the 90s for nearly 4 hours! Not only that, I can actually last little over half a day without charging! I'm really confident to ditch the charger and leave it at home. I only keep the cord with me in case I want to share things between my phone and my laptop. One secret I discovered which us from one of the reviewers is that you should power your phone all the way down. Running applications and the operating system itself will prevent this battery from reaching its full capacity. Also, if you see it charged with the green dot at the top while its on, its not really charges. I think its due to the fact it only recognizes the original stock battery. As soon as you power it down, that green light will turn orange, showing you that the battery itself is not entirely charged. Just power it down overnight. That's time for sleep anyways. By the time you wake up, the diy should be green and you can turn it on to enjoy a long lasting battery. Try killing apps that you aren't using to save battery life. An advanced task killer will help, but you'll have to actually force stop apps that come back on after its been already killed.I also managed to get a case and make some modifications to it to give it some personality. Hopefully, I can post a picture on here to show you guys. Its best if you get a plastic or rubber case so its easier to cut through for the modification =) I hope this was helpful!
summary: Don't get the Acase! This one kicks it to the curve!!

reviewText: The first thing I noticed about my new Droid Incredible was that it is a powerful little computer. The second thing I noticed was that I drained the battery in a single afternoon.That brings us to the Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh battery. The 3500 mAh battery almost triples the standard 1300 mAh power available to the new Droid owner. It allows the active talker and surfer to work all day and all night on a single charge. Typically, I have between 55% to 65% power left after 16 hours using the Incredible as an e-book reader with moderate internet surfing, GPS on, Wi-Fi on, sync on, and even the occasional phone call.The included case cover looks similar to the original cover, just a bit thicker to mold itself around the larger battery. (I uploaded several photos). I find that the precision cover with its slightly thicker form makes handling the phone a bit easier, does not interfere with the flashlight, and provides some badly-needed protection for the camera lens.Pros:1. Surf and work all day and night on a single charge.2. Identical looks, just slightly thicker. Still lays flat on surfaces.3. Easier to handle phone.4. Protects camera lens.Cons:1. Might need to buy a different holster (I don't use 'em). Standard-sized replacement covers will not fit.2. Thicker body might offend the "my phone is smaller than your phone" purists. Makes phone slightly heavier.This product is not an option; this battery SHOULD be standard in the Droid Incredible.

Was loving my new Incredible but after coming from Nokia phones for years, was appalled by the poor battery of the HTC Incredible (honestly the only thing not to love about it). It never made it through a single day with heavy use, sometimes not even half a day! Ordered this replacement battery and WOW!!! I can now safely make it to the very end of the day without any problem whatsoever. It's great to not worry anymore. However, you do lose the slimness of the phone. The extended back is nice to grip but to me the front of the phone now feels too exposed. I have decided to use the old battery and original backing so the protective case I bought for it can keep it from harm & I just charge the phone everytime I'm in my car. I'm hoping a case comes out for the extended battery soon as I miss the worry free charge this extended battery offers. Great purchase and you won't be disappointed in it!

I love this battery. After the first charge (following instructions to charge past green light), I got 46 hours of battery life. This was with me playing games and listening to Slacker radio. I also used wifi a lot and bluetooth some. I'm on my second charge now. Has been running for 26 hours and have over half of the battery left.The battery does add a little weight and sticks out from the back, but I like this as the phone kept slipping out of my hand before, but not now. Also the battery is about a 1/4 of an inch to short, so I tore off a piece of the instruction paper that came with it, folded it 3 times and shoved it in the gap and it stays fine.Though it does have a couple of minor issues, this battery still deserves 5 stars. I  used to charge my battery around noon every day then again at night. Now I can easily go a couple of days on one charge.

I would give it 5 stars if the price wasn't so outrageous. Other than that it is a wonderful battery which will last several days as long as you don't use your GPS and Wi-Fi, in which case it may last 24 to 48 hours of constant use. Very good, I am impressed by Seidio.Not too impressed with the lousy battery Verizon included with the original HTC phone.

Yes, it makes my Droid Incredible a bit thicker. I admit that concerned me when I first though about buying this. But actually, that does not bother me at all. In fact, it makes the phone fell even more solid and easier to hold. Not an issue as far as I am concerned.But what I love is that I can use all the features of my phone, as much as I like, and never worry about the battery. Never.With moderate use, it will last days. Not hours, as with the original battery, but days.Texting, using the phone, watching video, playing games, reading books...whatever...and still lots of battery left at the end of a long day.

I was so excited when I added this battery to my Droid Incredible.  I was able to go a full day & then some off of a single charge.  After about 4 months my battery started to decline.  I thought it was a 3rd party app draining my battery so I decided to do a clean wipe & not install 3rd party apps to test.  After a clean factory install, my battery was still draining fast.I decided to take it out and put the original OEM battery back in.  I was getting far better battery life with my original OEM battery than I was with the 3500 extended battery.  You'll most likely get great battery life for about 3 or 4 months, then it will begin to decline there after.  I went to Seidio's warranty page & it states that their warranty policy is 180 days.  Go figure.  That's just about how long I got good service from it.
summary: Battery is great... for about 4 months :( (Buyer Beware)

reviewText: Like other reviews, I'm only noticing a 25-50% improvement over the original 1800mH battery.  But, I'm still happy for the extended life (thus 4 stars).  With an extended cover and case, it feels like a real phone and not something from zoolander.

reviewerName: Chris R. Hotz "Real reviews.  No fake 5-star"
reviewText: Like most Incredible users, I was disappointed with the stock battery so I bought this one based on the reviews.  The battery definitely lasts a long time, but after about 9 months of use it started getting weird on me.  For example, sometimes it would last for two full days, other times it would drain in literally a few hours.  Odd.  My phone started powering itself off, at first once in a while, then up to five times a day.  I took it to Verizon and they said that is usually the fault of the battery.  I didn't believe them (they tend to blame your problem on something else if they can), but I went back to the crappy stock battery and sure enough; they were right.  No more powering down problems.Anyway, I e-mailed Seidio and they said it's been too long and there is nothing they can do.  I'm not upset, because the battery IS out of warranty, but I thought potential buyers may want to know that you might have to drop another $55 in less than a year on another one.  I'm a little  surprised they didn't shoot me out a new one, so just understand this isn't one of those companies that bends over backwards once the warranty is up.I'm now using an extended HTC battery I got through Verizon.What I'm really doing is waiting for my upgrade so I can get an iPhone V, because as much as I love the flexibility of the droid platform, free apps, etc., there's just too many quirky things this thing does that my wife's iPhone never does.
summary: Great battery, but started have trouble and got no help

reviewText: I have the factory battery as well as the 1700mAh battery from Seidio (which lasts about 7 hours) over the OEM battery's 5-6.  I've only been using this battery for 32 hours, and haven't charged it yet and it still has 60% left.  So it looks like this battery should last 80 hours (3.3 days).  Not bad!  I'm running with just the email sync on (no wifi or GPS).Physically the batter is just a bit bulkier than the original.  Interestingly, I find that the shape of the battery actually makes it a little easier to hold the phone and "cup" it in your hand, though it does make it bigger and a little harder to fit in your pocket.Also, I no longer have a case on my phone as the other cases I own are not shaped to hold the new battery cover.** Update, the battery lasted 66 hours before the phone asked to be plugged in.

The HTC Incredible - is incredible when it has power.  The problem is that the battery that came with it is worthless.  Of course, the under-powered battery helps to make the Incredible slim and lite.  But the battery is insufficient for the requirements of the phone.  Making the problem worse, it does not fully charge while the phone is powered on.Before, I had to recharge my phone 2-3 times per day.  I had to keep all of the features that make the Incredible 'Incredible' turned off.  No GPS.  No live wallpapers.  Dim screen.  Whatever I could turn off I did.  I had to plan when I could recharge the phone to keep it running.Now, I just use what I want to use.  I don't run out of power!  I can enjoy live wallpaper!  I can even turn my GPS on!  I can use all of the special features that make the Incredible such a nice phone. With power to spare!After a full day of calls, music, reading books, and even playing games - there is still 50-60% battery remaining.Adding the Seidio Innocell 3500 mAh Extended Life Battery makes the Incredible fat and 'not' lite. Also, there are not any useful protective cases.The tradeoff is good.  This battery makes the phone whole.

I purchased this battery about a month ago and it's been a lifesaver.  I recently had a significant flight delay and no power outlet at my seat.  I watched a 2 hour movie on my HTC Incredible and only used 1/3 of the battery.  When I landed I had to pick up a rental car and drive 100+ miles to a rural area that I've never been in.  Of course I'm going to use the GPS in the Incredible to guide me.  About 15 minutes into the drive, I notice that the car charger is NOT charging. Apparently the outlet in the rental car was dead. But, it didn't matter, I made the entire trip on battery power.  For me, this was as difficult a test for a battery to pass that I could give it.  I highly recommend this battery.
summary: Juice to work with and on and on

reviewText: I swear I already posted my review but here we go again..... I got about 1 full day on the first charge with this and now I get around 30hours (mainly text and internet use is all I do... I'd like to know what some of the users have their phones set to that they claim they get 2-5days of use out of this battery because I've got screen brightness down, synching set to 1hr+ and I'm not using Pandora and GPS like many of the reviewers claim they are doing. Still this battery is cheaper then the extended one from HTC/Verizon and it lasts quite a bit longer. I got the wall charger so I can always charge my stock battery while using the extended and therefore always have a backup. It's not that bulky, and the case fits perfect (something I was worried about from some reviewers saying otherwise) so either they can't put a case on or the design was improved... A battery with this much life is what should've came with the phone in the first place, they just need to start making them this powerful in the normal size.
Works great!  I easily make it thru the day on a single charge while connected to 3g, heavy texting, wi-fi, etc.
Well this battery is better then the original battery the phone came with it dose last so I guess its a ok battery but I was not to happy with my purchase but customer service is great thank you.
The battery that came with my Droid Incredible just barely would last 2 days.  This one has been lasting almost a week.  This is a great product!!!

I tore through the default 1300 mAh *and* the upgraded 1750 mAh batteries looking to have a phone which would last > 5 hours on a charge.I wasn't a fan of bumping out the back of the phone, but it ended up being a blessing in disguise. I have found that it is more comfortable for long calls, and Seidio has done a great job making the surface match the HTC original exactly.And now, even without using Juice Defender, or AppKiller on my phone, it can run most of a business day doing all the wonderful things I actually bought it to do.It doesn't last as long as my Blackberry used to, but considering all the new capabilities, I am very happy with this battery and what it offers.
summary: This made my HTC Incredible usable

reviewText: I love this charger, it charges both the phone with a battery and a regular battery by itself. It does extend out a little more than I'd like but can't complain. The cable included though does not act as a data cable, charging only.
summary: Great dual charger, extends out a little to much

reviewText: Read other reviews and was very excited about this battery. I was too the point where I was charging my phone every 3-4 hours. Recent trip, phone couldn't make it through one flight, one layover, one car ride. I use this phone as my datebook, shopping assistant, mp3 player, game console, internet browser, gps, pretty much my everything. Got battery yesterday and charged it for 8 hours while at work with Seidio Multi-Function Battery Charger. Extended battery has been in phone for 8 hours now and with my regular uninhibited use I am currently at 89%. Seriously? I'm in heaven. Such a wonderful powerful device should not be limited because of short battery life. I have the other battery now for backup and I'm a very very happy camper.Drawbacks: Battery does add bulk. Other reviews said it was not that noticeable but to me it is. My phone is no longer very sleek. The trade off is worth it to me but it slightly depresses me.Secondly, I cannot find a case to fit new girth that does add even more. The few cases I saw were not feminine by any means.Alas, not the end of the world.

A lot of folks have claimed to have tested this battery to it's limits... and now I'm going to make that same claim.  The greatest drain on any cell phone battery is when the phone is "searching for a signal."  I live and work in a rural area and couldn't wait to take my new Incredible to work to put the Seido to it's ultimate test.  I work a 13 hour shift and the day I took my phone with me was one of the days that I either didn't have a signal or was in an area where the signal is very poor.  After 13 hours of my new phone searching for a signal I still had 30 percent of the battery left!  I couldn't believe it.  I've had two other phones that would have been dead within 6 hours.  Add to the signal searching, me playing a game for awhile on breaks, constant waking the phone up and learning it's features, etc.  I couldn't kill this battery! If you own an Incredible you must own this battery too!  The extra thickness of the phone doesn't bother me at all.  I like the added weight and the thickness makes the phone much easier to hold by the edges. It's been a few days now since I bought the Incredible and this battery to go with it and I am very pleased with them both.

Finally I found an extended battery that provides enough power to support the Droid Incredible under heavy use for longer than a day. The added size and weight are inconsequential to the comfort and convenience when using the phone. The added size, however, may not be compatible with 3rd party cases and docks.

In the course of my daily work activities i often need to use my phone as a 3G hotspot for a couple hours, use the GPS system in conjunction with google maps to find satellite views to navigate to hard to find work sites, make several phone calls and look up information from either email, spreadsheets, or both. This battery gives the Incredible the kind of usable life i need to not have to charge it at every opportunity.Very Pleased

This is a great battery lasts for days and the extra size and weight isn't an issue.And the back cover fits like the original.One of the most worthwhile products I have bought this year.Fast shipping and in great shape. Would buy from this vendor again...
summary: This is a great deal lifesaver.

reviewText: I bought this battery so I could use my phone as an ereader and to watch netflix.I can finally last til 10pm without plugging in at 5pm and use the phone the way I want. If I'm careful w usage, I can get 2days out of this battery!

Pros : It extended my phone life to atleast 100% from 1750mah seido battery. Now I am able to watch netflix movie, browse net, use bluetooth, gps without worrying that my phone will die in 6-7 hrs.Cons: Phone is definitely heavy and looks odd with a hump.I choose functionality over cosmetics.

I purchased this phone to replace my phone that wasn't working well since my contract with AT&T; wasn't up yet. Installation of the SIM card was easy and that's about all the good I can say about it.I have tested and played with many touch screen phones lately as I was counting down the days until my contract was up. Out of necessity I had to make this quick decision. The layout of the menu is not very user friendly. But the worst part is attempting  to actually use it. I cannot scroll through the contacts without accidentally calling someone. Moving my finger up the screen will scroll sometimes but 'select' another, causing a panic looking for the cancel button. One time it was in my pocket just sitting on the couch and my child's phone rings and it's my phone calling. I looked at my phone and it showed 37 outbound calls within the last minute to their phone.I got rid of it real fast and I would not recommend this phone... to anyone.

......for someone who has never owned a `touch screen' phone. This is a veritable bargain at $99.99 or less, and I couldn't resist getting it to initiate GSM service with AT&T.; I liken going from a conventional flip phone to this touch screen to putting someone in a stick shift car that's driven an automatic for the last 40 years.  The  munchkin sized owner's manual is the worst I've ever had the misfortune to try to use. No meaningful index, very vague tutorial on features, pictured icons (in the manual) so small as to be illegible. Sadly, there isn't (yet?) an online manual which one may print out..Still....I think I'm going to really like this phone. (naww[...] update) FM radio with or without a wired headset, very good volume in ALL functions including speakerphone, a whole bevy of  intriguing  foo-foo  features.  Bluetooth wireless headset stereo capability on music IN the phone, FM radio wired headset only (or no headset)..I was able to assign this phone to the standard AT&T; minutes plan rather than their prepaid "GO" plan. Strangely, about half of the AT&T; and independent stores said it HAD to be a "prepaid GO phone", half had no problem using it with a conventional plan and SIM card. Happy days! A conventional plan, month-to-month WITHOUT a contract. I'm thrilled..I'll shoulder most of the blame for the problems I'm having with the touch screen.  I don't think it's the most user-friendly touch screen (particularly compared to my GPS units), but I'm learning..This LG Prime LGS390 phone has (at least initially) had the most favorable feedback from users of ANY cell phone. IMHO it benefits in quality from being made in Korea (LG is Korean) rather than China. Just an opinion..I find it interesting that LG initially stood for "Lucky Goldstar" for years. Now it's either "Lets Go" or "Life's Good".  Sounds more `Western', I guess..A good phone.  Go for it.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>ADDENDA: A few disappointing qualities have arisen since my initial report. This phone WILL NOT work with a (blue tooth) "X Link". THIS IS A BIG ISSUE FOR ME!!  First phone EVER that wouldn't.  X Link even has a downloadable  "LG patch" to correct problems. This with the latest X Link software is of no use. And the $50 credit (which expires in 90 days) makes this phone only $30 dollars here on Amazon.First of all, you can use a standard Micro USB cable to connect to PC, and attach a standard 3.5mm headphones to listen to music. No adapters needed. You also get FM radio, Bluetooth, an MP3 player, MicroSD reader, etc, etc. I mean it's worth the $30 just for the MP3 player capabilities alone.Second, when you connect this device to your PC, you are able see and copy any data files to the internal memory or the MicroSD card. None of the Virgin Mobile phones I've used in the past gave me this option.You can add Java ME applications with zero hassle. This is a major plus. There are thousands of free Java ME applications on the internet, which you can download using your PC and send them to your phone. For example, to install Opera Mini, you go to their website on your PC, download the full .jar file, and copy it to your MicroSD card (or the phone's internal memory). Next, disconnect the phone from PC, go to main menu, select "My Stuff", and finally select "Memory Card". You .jar file will be shown. If you tap the file, it will automatically start the installation process (fast and simple). No application restrictions, and that's definitely awesome.Everything else works great too. Screen is responsive. This is a small phone however (smaller that the iPhone). I also have no issues with the screen lock during calls. All you have to do is press the unlock side button and the screen in immediately unlocked.Additionally, AT&T; new rates are 10 cents per minute with no daily access fee (down from the original 25 cents). That's half of what  Virgin Mobile is asking.Overall I love it. I had high expectations when I ordered this, and wasn't disappointed with I received it.

I've tested a lot of screen protectors for the iPhone 4, and this is easily the best available. It's precisely cut and seems even more oleophobic than the native iPhone 4 glass.  After first installing it, I did notice a small amount of friction on the surface, but this may have just been residue from the protective film it came in.  After a small amount of use, it looks and feels just like the regular, naked iPhone 4 screen surface.  If you install it well, you won't know it's there.  Also, the Apple bumper won't cause this film to peel up at the edges (unlike the InvisibleShield).  Yes, installation can be difficult and needs a steady hand; a few recommendations here: 1) install in a steamy bathroom to minimise the amount of dust that gets under the film. 2) Be prepared to lift the screen protector and re-apply it if you don't get it perfectly aligned the first attempt (on average, this will take me 4-5 attempts to get perfect).  3) Once it's aligned perfectly, use two pieces of tape to remove any dust or bubbles under the film.  (One to lift the film, the other to remove the dust, which will stick to the tape, rather than the underside of the screen.)I have only one complaint about this product: it does not come with a rear-screen protector.  If they made one of those out of this same material, I'd buy it in an instant.
summary: Easily the best iPhone 4 screen protector

reviewText: **this is an initial review.  ive only had the film applied for a few days.**ive been a zagg fan for as long as they have been putting covers on phones.  ive had a zagg on every phone my wife and i have had in the past few years as well as both our ipad 2s, and ive promoted their products to friends and family.i had a friend tell me he tried one of these on his wifes iphone, and after reading recent zagg reviews i decided to give this a try.  its 12 bucks for two.  you cant go wrong just to give it a show.the install wasnt what i was used to.  these just simply get applied.  no solution spray and no flimsy film.  this cover is a hard, taught cover.  the install was easier than the zagg overall, but as other said here you will have fuzz and lint.  i applied this to a brand new, fresh out of the box phone.  i took the other protective film off and directly applied this one and i still had a couple of pieces of dust after repositioning a couple of times.  the little dust stickers they provide is a great idea and being careful i was able to remove the dust.after getting it applied just right it appears that the film is cut just a tiny tiny tiny bit too big for the phone.  maybe mine wasnt cut right, but on both sides there are spots that are apparently touching the inside edge of the front phones lip and it wont lay down perfectly.  all the air has been worked reviewText: This was the third screen protector I tried in less than a month and got very happy with it! Although it comes with a plastic card for bubble removal, I could apply it without any bubbles at all!Its oleophobic properties are very good. Not as good as iPhone screen itself, but you can swipe most of the fingerprints with your bare fingers. Of course, to get a perfectly clean screen, you still have to use a cloth.It is thicker than the others I tried. Inspite of that, you just notice there is a film on your screen when you look around the front camera/earpice and home button opennings. I mean, you can't "feel" it with your fingers. Being thick helps a lot during application because, as it progressively sticks to the surface, it doesn't fold, wrinkle or make bubbles. And being thick must add some protection too.It comes with some stickers to remove the fingerprints from the film in case you accidentally touch the sticking surface while applying it. Some days ago I ruined a screen protector from another brand because I touched it when it slipped off my fingers during application.It is a bit expensive, but the pack comes with two pieces. And judging by its quality, I won't have to replace it any time soon.

It's just not oleophobic, and it claims it is. Is it a little tiny bit better than the one I was using before this? Yes, just, but that's not really saying much. Save your money and buy something else.

*****Five starsSimply the best that I ever used. I had both the zagg which was protective but not smooth and always reminded you of its presence and the bodyguard which used to be my favorite but was so thin you had to be careful what case you used because it peeled off my screen (lasted less then six months). This one is protective and clear as glass. It feels natural to the touch. I would take the advice of a previous reviewer and put it on in a bathroom after running the hot water in the shower for a few minutes to minimized the dust in the air.
This really works. When my son removed it from the phone, there was so much grime on it. The phone was nice and clean and it was easy to put on.

I purchased the same Steinheil protector for my HTC Inspire after reading that other people were very happy with theirs. Now that I've been using the protector for several weeks, I have to wonder if the company that makes these screen protectors just paid for a bunch of false reviews! I don't like this screen protector for several reasons:1. The film is very, very difficult to put on. This was my third or fourth item to put a protective screen on. It was by far the hardest to get on without bubbles or dust. Bubbles seem to crop up from nowhere after the film has adhered. They won't be pushed out with the squeegee. You have to start over. Dust particles are literally attracted to the adhesive. In a room without A/C or a fan, on a large cleared surface that has been practically sterilized I don't know where dust could from but it'll find its way under the film. You'll use the little strips of dust remover but end up sticking a particle somewhere else. Then you'll have to start over. You'll probably have to trash the first protector and maybe even the second too.2. The Steinheil screen gets oils on it more than any other I've used, even the cheapest ones that came with cheap cases. You'll notice the screen looks horribly grimy and wipe it with your shirt. Voila - you've smeared grime everywhere. It's gross. I've made it a habit to wash my hands frequently (maybe compulsive but it's always worked for me), so there shouldn't be many oils on my hands. The cheap screen on my iPod touch gets sparkly after a good wipe, the Steinheil gets more smeary. Even after I used an expensive microfiber made for camera lenses, the screen still looks oily and gross. I wonder what kind of residue was transferred to the cleaning cloth. Ugh.3. Touch capacitance has decreased. I verified this by using a phone without a screen protector on it at the same time as using my phone with the Steinheil screen protector.4. Nothing special to make up for the above faults.5. I contacted the company twice to get advice/comments and haven't heard back.So, I'm replacing the Steinheil screen protector and I'm looking for one that'll do a good job.
summary: Not as good as its marketing
